english: Is it a good idea for me to plant corn alongside my young cocoa trees on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ cacao tsei bibii ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting quick crops like corn or cassava alongside young cocoa trees provides temporary shade to protect the cocoa and gives you food or income while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Enɛ, kɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ baaha oná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni baabu cocoa lɛ he, ni eha oná niyenii loo shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni cocoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks, or simply because the tree naturally produced more flowers than it has the energy to feed.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa lɛ Aloo eji akɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ hewɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil, which it needs to stay green and build healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ enɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmei ni mli wa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests of crops every year if I plant on it continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii daa lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest a crop, it takes away valuable nutrients from the soil; without giving the land a rest or adding fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaagbala niyenii ni jara wa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaaa ejɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaafite.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer to my farm right when heavy rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa pɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer away into water paths or washes it deep underground before your crops' roots can absorb it, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ nu gbɛi amli loo shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Shika ni afiteɔ

english: Why do black spots spread so quickly across my cocoa pods during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in cold, wet weather and spreads rapidly through splashing raindrops, high humidity, and unpruned branches.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo, kɛ tsei niji ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when there is too much rain near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain leaves the soil waterlogged, depriving the root tubers of air and creating ideal conditions for rot-causing fungi in the ground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifã lɛ mli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off unnecessary branches from my cocoa trees if I want more yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni he ehiaaa kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni maná nibii babaoo?

english: Pruning extra branches lets air and sunlight flow through the tree, prevents disease, and ensures the tree directs its energy into producing pods instead of excess leaves.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli, ehaa helai baaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to stay small even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ feɔ bibioo yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, starving the crops even if weather conditions are good.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ hi moŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or are sitting in waterlogged soil. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or urea early in the plant's growth helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii yɛ shishijee be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up and stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a virus, or by extreme dry heat. Spraying with recommended neem oil or organic insecticides helps keep whiteflies away so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni mli egbi waa mli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ akabote mli bɔni afee ni baai heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the weather is too hot and dry, or when sap-sucking insects like capsids (mirids) attack the buds. Keeping shade trees on your farm and spraying against capsids at the right season helps flowers turn into full pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids (mirids) lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ capsids lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when wet soil traps too much water around the roots, allowing fungal diseases to grow. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps rain water drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mɔ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for growing big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they catch plenty of sun and stay safe from rot and soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa aba. ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ fitemɔ kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe

english: Is it good for me to plant beans or cowpeas together with my maize on the same plot?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful because bean plants take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally feeds your maize crop and improves the soil for future seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha o-corn tsei lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and your crop is growing fast—usually 2 to 3 weeks after planting, and again when flowers start forming. Never put fertilizer on dry soil or right before a heavy rain that will wash it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida oya, bei pii lɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Ni ekoŋŋ beni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ. Kaaha ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo dani nugbɔ ni naa wa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwie shi lɛ aba.

english: Plantains have shallow roots, and microscopic soil worms called nematodes can eat those roots and weaken the tree's hold in the dirt. Planting clean suckers and using wooden props to support fruiting trees prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aye nakai shishifãi lɛ ni amɛha sũ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ afee mlɛo. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi.

english: Extreme heat causes pepper plants stress, making them drop their flowers to conserve water. Watering early in the morning and providing light shade during peak heat months helps the plants keep their flowers and produce more peppers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni nu akafite. Kɛ́ awo tsei lɛ nu leebi ni aha amɛ hulutsoo yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Weeds are native wild plants with strong roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil food much faster than farm crops can. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks of planting gives your young crops the advantage they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my farm regularly to check my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa koni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Walking through your field allows you to spot early signs of bird damage, water pooling, or crop disease so you can take action before the problem spreads across your whole farm.
ga: Kɛ́ onyiɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ okpoi efite, nubui, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela mra koni onyɛ ofee nɔ ko dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if rainwater is damaging my growing maize cobs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ nu miifite mi-abele ni miida lɛ?

english: Look out for soft, soggy husks, dark or moldy spots near the tip of the cob, or a sour smell coming from the corn stalks while you inspect.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ. Hei ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naagbee he. Aloo ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli beni okwɛɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: What specific things should I check on my maize after a period of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔi krɛdɛɛi esa akɛ makwɛ mi-abele lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be ko sɛɛ?

english: Check whether water has settled inside the leaf wraps or damaged husks, and look for torn covers where rainwater might have penetrated into the grains.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji nu yɛ baai loo ŋmãa ni efite lɛ mli. Agbɛnɛ hu, taomɔ hei ni etse ni nugbɔ nu baanyɛ abote ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do cobs pecked by birds rot so much faster than undamaged ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni okpoi shwieɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya fe nɔ ni efiteee lɛ?

english: Birds tear open the protective outer husk, leaving an opening for rainwater, dirt, and airborne mold spores to get inside the cob and cause rapid decay.
ga: Loofɔlɔ lɛ gbálaa esɛɛ fã ni buɔ ehe lɛ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu, muji, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛhaa egboɔ oya.

english: Does leaving bird-damaged maize on the stalk bring more problems to my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni okpoi efite lɛ ni mashi yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛ naagbai babaoo baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, open and damaged grains release sweet smells that attract secondary pests like beetles, insects, and rodents, which will then attack your healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni agbele ni efite lɛ jieɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ko ni gbalaa kooloi bibii ni ji enyɔ tamɔ ladybugs, kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii. ni baatutua oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: How does the outer leaf cover protect my maize while it is growing?
ga: Te kponɔgbɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ buɔ mi-ŋma lɛ he be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The husk acts like a natural raincoat and shield, preventing rainwater from entering the cob and keeping birds and insects away from the soft grain.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ atade kɛ adebɔɔ mli gãimlibi. Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu naa koni ekabote cob lɛ mli. ni otsi okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize cobs start rotting on the stalk when water gets inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nu bote mli lɛ?

english: Trapped rainwater creates a warm, damp environment inside the husk, which is the perfect condition for fungi and mold to grow and destroy the corn.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ ni mli edɔ baa ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni baakwɛ̃ ni efite ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why should I remove spoiled maize cobs from the field while the crop is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmãa ni efite lɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Removing rotten cobs stops crop diseases from spreading to neighboring healthy plants and keeps mold from multiplying in your farm.
ga: Kpoji ni egboi ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa tsei ahe helai agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. ni otsi ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: What is the best way to dispose of the diseased corn cobs I pluck off my plants?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ ŋmãa ni hela emɔ lɛ ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Carry them far away from your farm to burn or bury them deep in the ground so wind and rain cannot spread the mold spores back onto your healthy crops.
ga: Okɛ amɛ aya he ko ni kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ koni oyashã amɛ loo ofu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ akagbɛ fungal spores lɛ ashwã onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do insects cause more crop damage during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Insects bore holes into the plant tissue, which allows rainwater to seep deep inside, leading to mold and internal rotting that destroys the crop.
ga: Kplukai shwieɔ bu yɛ tso lɛ fãji amli. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baa.

english: Can plant diseases move from my neighbor's farm to my yam farm on my hands or boots?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ajie tsei ahe helai kɛjɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli kɛya sweet potato ŋmɔ mli kɛtsɔ nine loo bɔɔtu nɔ?

english: Yes, plant pathogens like fungi, bacteria, and microscopic worms can easily hitch a ride on dirty hands, footwear, or clothes. Moving directly from an infected field to a healthy crop field without cleaning up can spread diseases fast.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai tamɔ ŋmeii, helatsɛmɛi bibii, kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa lɛ baanyɛ akpɛtɛ niji, tokotai, loo atadei ni he tseee lɛ ahe oya. Kɛ́ mɔ ko fã kɛjɛ hei ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtee hei ni shweremɔ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ ni asaaa he lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela lɛ eshwa oya.

english: Why do some yam farmers get worried when visitors walk straight into their fields after visiting other farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato okwaafoi komɛi haoɔ kɛ́ shisharalɔi bote amɛŋmɔji amli beni amɛsara ŋmɔji krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Farmers fear introducing outside infections. Visitors coming from other farms might carry invisible crop diseases or destructive pests on their skin, shoes, or tools that can destroy healthy yam plants.
ga: Okwaafoi sheɔ helai ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ gbeyei. Ekolɛ saralɔi ni jɛ ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ baaná tsei ahe helai ni anaaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii yɛ amɛhewolo nɔ, amɛ tokotai, loo amɛdɛŋdadei ni baanyɛ afite sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is washing my hands with plain water enough to keep my crop plants safe from rot?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛbaafɔ miniji ahe lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite?

english: Plain water removes loose mud, but soap or disinfectants are needed to kill the invisible bacteria and fungi that stick to skin after handling infected plants or tubers.
ga: Nu lɛ baajie muji ni etse ehe lɛ. Shi samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ helai ahe miihia koni akɛgbe helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni anaaa ni kpɛtɛɔ hewolo he beni mɔ ko eta tsei loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do some experienced farmers make visitors wait at the farm edge before letting them walk among the crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ haa saralɔi mɛɔ yɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ anaa dani amɛhaa amɛnyiɛɔ amɛŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This gives the farmer a chance to ensure visitors clean off any contaminated mud or plant debris from their feet and hands so they do not accidentally bring diseases into the clean farm area.
ga: Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ náa hegbɛ koni amɛkwɛ koni saralɔi lɛ atsumɔ muji loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ amɛnaji kɛ amɛdɛŋ lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji koni akakɛ helai aba ŋmɔji amli hei ni he tse lɛ amli yɛ oshara mli.

english: Does touching young, tender yam tubers with my bare hands hurt their growth?
ga: Mikɛ miniji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko taa sweet potato ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe Ani eyeɔ edalɛ awui?

english: Rough handling or touching soft tubers with dirty hands can bruise their delicate skin and introduce rot-causing germs, which leads to decaying tubers or poor growth underground.
ga: Ni akɛ niji ni mli ewo muji baatsu ŋmeii bibii ahe nii loo akɛta amɛhe waa Enɛ baanyɛ afite amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ekɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ aba. Enɛ haa tuber rot loo shikpɔŋ shishi dalɛ ni ehiii baa.

english: Should I clean my cutlass and hoes before moving from one bed of yams to another?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsumɔ mi-knibii, mi-fɔk, kɛ mi-spade lɛ mli dani majie amɛ kɛjɛ sweet potato saatso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ?

english: Yes, farm tools can spread germs like a dirty blade. If you cut an infected tuber or root and then use the same tool on a healthy plant, you pass the disease directly into the healthy crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii baanyɛ agbɛ helai ashwã tamɔ ŋmeii ni he tseee pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji ofolɔ tsei loo shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, okɛ nakai dɛŋdade lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Obaatswa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does dirt stuck to my boots or feet affect the soil in my crop field?
ga: Te muji ni kpɛtɛɔ mi tokotai loo minaji ahe lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Mud from other locations often contains parasitic worms, harmful insect eggs, or weed seeds that can invade your soil and attack the roots of your healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yɛ klon ni jɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ amli. Kplukai ni yɔɔ oshara loo jwɛi dumɔwui ni baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my yams start rotting in the ground even before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Underground yam rot is usually caused by soil bacteria or fungi that enter the tuber through small cuts, insect bites, or wounds made by dirty farm tools during weeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ loo ŋmei ko ni tsɔɔ ŋmei bibioo ko mli ni eboteɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa. Kplukai loo pilamɔi ni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni he tseee kɛbaa yɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ be mli.

english: Why do yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbala shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb to catch more sunlight to feed their growing tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off damp soil, which improves air flow and protects the foliage from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛha bulbs ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How can I tell if a seed yam is carrying a rot disease before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ egbo dani madu amɛ?

english: A healthy seed yam should feel firm and look smooth. If it has soft spots, cracks, a bad smell, or dark patches, it is infected and will contaminate your soil if planted.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji amɛyɛ hei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ŋmeii, ŋmɔlɔ fɔŋ, loo hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ, no lɛ hela emɔ amɛ ni amɛbaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ.

english: If I plant many maize seeds together in one hole, will I get more corn, or should I remove some of the young plants?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa Dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli Ani maná ŋmãa babaoo? Aloo esa akɛ majie tsei bibii lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Crops need enough space, water, and soil food to grow strong. If too many seedlings grow in one spot, they fight each other for nutrients and stay small; removing extra seedlings leaves fewer plants that grow bigger, healthier cobs.
ga: Tsei hia gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ dara babaoo yɛ he kome Amɛyeɔ niyenii he akaŋ ni amɛji bibii. Kɛ́ ajie dumɔwui ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tsei fioo komɛi pɛ abadara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Does cutting off some extra leaves from my tomato plant help it grow better fruit, or am I damaging the crop?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mifo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai krokomɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ? Aloo miikpãtã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Removing extra or old leaves helps the plant save energy and improves airflow. Instead of wasting food on keeping useless leaves alive, the plant directs its nutrients into making bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni fa fe nine loo egbɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ he ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafite niyenii koni baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahi shi lɛ. Tsei lɛ heɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can giving my cassava crops too much water actually spoil them, or do plants always need as much water as possible?
ga: Ani nu babaoo ni akɛhaa ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ aha efite diɛŋtsɛ? Aloo ani nu he hiaa tsei fe fɛɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Cassava roots rot if they sit in flooded, waterlogged soil for too long because root tissues need air to breathe. While plants need water to drink, excess water chokes the roots and rots the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Yɛ be mli ni tsei he hiaa nu ni amɛnu lɛ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ ni ebaaha tso lɛ agbo.

english: If I put a very large amount of chemical fertilizer on my crops, will they grow twice as fast, or can it hurt my plants?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baakwɛ̃ oya shii enyɔ loo ebaafite tsei?

english: Too much chemical fertilizer can burn plant roots and draw moisture out of the plant, causing it to wither and die. Applying just the right amount feeds the plant safely without damaging the soil or roots.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni ejie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ɔ ma nyɛ ma ha nɛ e gbi nɛ e gbo. Kɛ́ akɛ falɛ ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii shweshweeshwe ni amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ loo amɛshishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen food in the soil. To survive, the plant steals food from its older lower leaves and sends it to the younger top leaves, causing the bottom ones to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni ehi shi Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli ni ekɛmajeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and pale even when rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by stealing light, water, and soil nutrients before your crops can reach them. Without those essential foods, your crops starve and lose their dark green color.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ baaje amɛŋɔɔ.

english: If I cut off diseased black pods from my cocoa tree immediately, will that protect the healthy pods?
ga: Kɛji mifo cacao tso lɛ mli ŋmeii diji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Ani ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Removing infected pods stops sickness from spreading to healthy pods through rain splashes and insects. Cutting away the bad parts early keeps the rest of the tree and farm safe.
ga: Pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu kɛ kooloi bibii anɔ. Hei ni ehiii lɛ ni afoɔ mra Ye obua ni tsei lɛ kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crop yields keep reducing if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Maize sucks specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly on the same land drains those specific nutrients completely, leaving the soil exhausted until you rotate crops or let the land rest.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaatsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need plantain trees planted next to them for shade, but mature cocoa trees prefer direct light?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwu yɛ emasɛi lɛ? koni ekɛha hulutsoo Shi kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ sumɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under hot direct sunlight. As the tree grows older, its roots deepen and its trunk strengthens, allowing it to handle full sunlight to produce heavy cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ ni eshishifã lɛ daa waa. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛfee kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of growing flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu lɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much sunlight as possible to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the vines high into the sunlight and prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and dying when I plant them in an open field without any plantain trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni dumɔwui bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like a canopy, protecting the delicate seedlings from scorching sun and preserving moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or adding well-decomposed manure will restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmei ni efite jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ ahe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller maize harvests every year when I plant on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baa shi daa afi be mli ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients without giving the earth time to recover. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and keeps it fertile for future crops.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ dumɔwui.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn plants and leaving dark droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ su diŋŋ yɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the soft center leaves of corn. Regularly inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can protect your crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra kɛ daa Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the soil becomes waterlogged and starves the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nu ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my corn seeds very close together to fit more plants in my field?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely actually reduces your harvest because the plants fight with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and tiny cobs. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow full, healthy, and yield larger ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei baawuu kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Kɛji akɛ gbɛ ni sa ba tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ, amɛhe awa ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers under the ground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni akɛtsi baai helai anaa.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Mulching around the roots to keep the soil cool and moist, along with proper watering, helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛfata nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he jogbaŋŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shi.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and root space directly from your plants. Clearing weeds early within the first few weeks of planting ensures your main crop gets all the nourishment it needs to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ ha onibii titri lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if it is safe to sow my seeds after the very first rain of the year arrives?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Sowing seeds right after the single first rain can be risky because dry hot spells often follow, causing germinated seeds to dry out and die. It is safer to wait until the rainy season fully settles with consistent weekly rains before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara. Ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, okadi ko yɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ fe nine. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ be lɛ aba naagbee kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa otsi lɛ dani odu.

english: Young cocoa leaves curl and turn yellow when exposed to direct sunlight and high heat without enough shade. Planting nurse crops like plantains or shade trees protects young cocoa plants by keeping the air humid and blocking harsh sunlight.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli lɛ mli. Nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cocoa tsei bibii ahe kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ehaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that eats maize leaves and hides inside the central shoot. Applying recommended biopesticides or neem extract early in the morning or late evening when caterpillars are active helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmei baai ni ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Which direction should I push my cassava cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ ashɛre ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted with the buds or 'eyes' pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the plant to waste energy turning around underground, leading to weak growth and poor tuber yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ daa ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ, efiteɔ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbɔleɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he, ni no haaa tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ bulb lɛ wooo jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop dark spots on the leaves and rot from the bottom during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is often caused by fungal diseases like blight, which thrive when rain splashes muddy soil onto the leaves. Spacing plants properly, tying them to stakes, and mulching the base helps prevent fungal spores in the soil from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fungal helai tamɔ baa tsɛŋemɔ, ni daa kɛji nugbɔ shwie muji yɛ baa lɛ nɔ kɛ enɛ baa. Tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei ahe Ni akɛhaa shishigbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni fungal spores ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my stored seed yams sprouting too early before the land is ready for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ miikwɛ̃ oya tsɔ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu lɛ?

english: Seed yams sprout early when stored in warm, humid conditions with direct sunlight. Keeping yams in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded yam barn allows them to stay dormant until the main planting season begins.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Sweet potato ni akɛtoɔ sweet potato ŋmɔ ni mli ejɔ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ jɛmɛ. Ni hulutsoo yɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi. kɛyashi be titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ baaje shishi

english: Why does my maize crop look pale yellow instead of dark green even after rain has fallen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ moŋ?

english: Pale yellow maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the crops the nitrogen boost they need to turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baa lɛ dalɛ. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná nitrogen kroko ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring regular watering during hot spells and avoiding over-fertilization helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo bɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kpo lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains the same specific nutrients every year and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kpo afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Rotate ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: How do I know which plantain suckers are best to cut and plant on new land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male plantain tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afo ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: The best suckers to plant are 'sword suckers,' which have narrow, sword-like leaves and a broad base. Avoid using 'water suckers' with broad leaves, as they grow slowly and produce small fruit bunches.
ga: Sucker ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akwɛ̃ ji ‘sword sucker’, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ klante kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘suckers’ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ he, ejaakɛ baai lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii akui.

english: Why do my lowland rice plants turn yellow when the water level on the farm stays too deep for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When water levels are too deep for extended periods, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to rot and turning the leaves yellow. Maintaining controlled water levels—just a few centimeters deep—allows roots to breathe and absorb nutrients efficiently.
ga: Kɛ nu lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nu ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ—ni mli kwɔ sɛntimitai fioo pɛ—haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the difference between buying a grafted mango seedling and planting a mango seed directly from a fruit?
ga: Mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ ahemɔ kɛ mango dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ aduawai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ Te amɛsoro amɛhe amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Grafted seedlings produce fruit much faster—usually in 2 to 3 years—and are guaranteed to yield high-quality fruit identical to the parent tree. Planting directly from a seed takes 5 to 7 years to bear fruit, and the fruit quality can be unpredictable.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ akɛ ebaawo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaahe afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani ewo yibii. Ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ bɔ ni aduawai lɛ hi ha.

english: Why is it important to leave plenty of space between fruit trees like mangoes and avocados when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi gbɛ yɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii, tamɔ mango kɛ avocado ateŋ kɛ́ oodu nii lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, air circulation, and ground nutrients. Planting them too close makes them compete for resources, leading to smaller harvests and a higher risk of diseases spreading between branches.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi, ni helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei niji ateŋ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: How long will it take for a newly planted avocado tree to start producing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani avocado tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: If you plant a grafted avocado seedling, it typically begins bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years. Trees grown directly from seeds take much longer, often 7 to 10 years, to mature enough for harvest.
ga: Kɛji odu avocado dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ Amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli. Tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baahe be babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani edaa bɔ ni sa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Can I grow food crops like vegetables or legumes between my young avocado trees while I wait for them to mature?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ aduawai loo ŋmãa. Ani manyɛ madu yɛ mi-avocado tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping short-season crops between young trees is a great strategy. It covers the bare soil to prevent erosion, suppresses weeds, and gives you food and income while your main fruit trees grow.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, be kukuoo mli dumɔ yɛ tsei bibii ateŋ. Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji ŋaa kpakpa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ koni ŋshɔ lɛ akaho. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ehaa bo niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni oyibii titrii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land has the right soil for growing avocado and mango trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha avocado kɛ mango tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Both avocado and mango trees need deep soil that drains water easily. If water stays pooled on your land for days after rain, the roots may rot; adding organic compost helps improve soil texture and drainage.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia avocado kɛ mango tsei. Kɛji nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ hu baanyɛ agbo. Kɛ́ akɛ organic compost fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni nu lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How often should I water my young fruit seedlings during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-fruit dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Newly planted seedlings need deep watering 2 to 3 times a week during dry spells to help their roots travel deep into the ground. Once trees are well-established after a couple of years, their deep roots can survive longer periods without extra water.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ he miihia ni awo amɛ nu waa shii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ otsi mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni eye ebua amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni tso lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ yɛ afii fioo komɛi amli Tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nu kroko fataaa he.

english: Why should I cut off some of the branches on my mango tree if I want more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi mango tso lɛ niji komɛi kɛji miitao aduawai babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or overcrowded branches so light and air can reach the inside of the tree. This directs the tree's energy into developing stronger branches that produce larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, hela emɔmɔ amɛ, loo ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ewo niji ni he wa ni woɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I protect my newly planted fruit saplings from high sun heat and stray farm animals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-fruit dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni elaaje lɛ ahe?

english: You can erect temporary shade screens made from palm fronds to protect young leaves from harsh sunlight, and build simple wooden or wire cages around each sapling to keep grazing animals away.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni akɛ ŋmei tsei fee koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni oma tso loo waya ŋtayaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni obɔle he. tsei bibii aŋkroaŋkroi koni akɛha kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ akashɛ amɛhe

english: Why do the flowers on my mango tree drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mango tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flower drop is often caused by fungal diseases like anthracnose, insect pests like thrips, or sudden dry spells. Keeping the area under the tree clean and providing steady moisture during flowering helps hold fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips, loo hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ aha he ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ he tse ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli daa yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young avocado plant turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi avocado baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is either receiving too much water—which causes root rot—or is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, which gives leaves their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting cashew trees before I can harvest nuts?
ga: Kɛ́ midu cashew tso lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani manyɛ makpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cashew trees typically start producing a small harvest around 3 to 4 years after planting, with full production starting between 7 and 10 years depending on rainfall and soil health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei jeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ashishi yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ afii 7 kɛyashi 10 teŋ, ni enɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cashew trees drop their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during the dry spell is a natural survival defense mechanism for cashew trees to save water and keep their roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛha cashew tso lɛ wala. Koni akɛ nu akafite ni akɛbu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do some crops yield heavy fruit in forest regions but struggle in dry transitional zones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi tsuɔ nii waa yɛ hei ni kooi yɔɔ lɛ shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be tsakeɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Crops react heavily to air humidity and rainfall; transitional zones have longer dry seasons and higher heat, which stresses moisture-loving plants unless drought-hardy crops like cashew are planted.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he waa. Tsakemɔ hei lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ dɔlɛ ni fa babaoo. Enɛ maa tsei ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ mi. ja aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ cashew ŋmeii

english: Does a cashew crop require rich soil and heavy watering to give a good yield?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ nu babaoo he miihia cashew tsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Cashew is a resilient crop that can survive in sandy or low-nutrient soils, but watering young saplings during their first dry season helps them build strong roots for better yields later.
ga: Cashews ji tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting cashew trees so far apart from each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cashew tsei yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Cashew trees develop wide, umbrella-like tops that need full sunlight to produce flowers; planting them too close together creates shade that reduces nut yields and breeds pests.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni tamɔ umbrella ni he hiaa hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni amɛfɔlɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa, ni no haa ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: Can I grow food crops like groundnuts or maize between my cashew trees while they are young?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Ani abaanyɛ adu yɛ cashew tsei ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first 3 to 4 years when cashew trees are still small, intercropping with legumes or maize provides food and income without damaging the young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli beni cashew tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa anáa niyenii kɛ shika ni eyeee dumɔwui lɛ awui.

english: What is the benefit of planting grafted cashew seedlings instead of planting raw seeds directly?
ga: Cashew nut dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ ni aaadu yɛ dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ najiaŋ Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ he?

english: Grafted seedlings are taken from proven high-yielding mother trees, meaning they fruit much faster (often in 2 years) and produce larger, uniform nuts compared to trees planted from random seeds.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ nyɛ tso ko ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ ewoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii mra kwraa (bei pii lɛ yɛ afii 2 mli) ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ekome kɛ akɛto tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui ni afeee nɔ ko nɔ ko mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I try a small demonstration plot on my land before planting a large cashew farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko makwɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu cashews wuji?

english: A small test plot allows you to observe how the crop responds to your specific farm soil and weather conditions without putting all your capital at risk.
ga: Kaa shikpɔji bibii haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii amɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ni okɛ oshika muu lɛ fɛɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Why do cashew flowers dry up and drop off without developing into nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔko ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers often dry up and fall due to pest attacks like tea mosquito bugs or sudden hot, dry winds that dehydrate the sensitive blossoms before pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Aedes ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbiɔ trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli nu sɛɛ foɔ dani amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the lower branches of a growing cashew tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ cashew tso ni miida lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning lower branches directs the plant's energy toward growing a strong top canopy, improves airflow beneath the tree to stop diseases, and makes harvesting easier.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ aya hiɛ koni helai akabote mli. ni eha nikpamɔ afee mlɛo

english: If I get access to dam water on my farm during the dry season, can I grow maize all year round?
ga: Kɛji miná nu kɛjɛ faa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, with a steady water supply from a dam, you can grow maize even in the dry season. Maize needs consistent moisture to produce healthy cobs, so having stored water allows you to plant and harvest without waiting for the rainy season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ nu ni jɛɔ faa lɛ mli ni baa daa lɛ. Obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po. Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa anyɛɔ aduɔ nibii ni akpaa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Which vegetables grow best on my farm if I only have access to water for a few months during the dry period?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji miná nu nyɔji fioo pɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Fast-growing vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, okra, and garden eggs are great choices because they mature quickly within three to four months, allowing you to harvest and sell before your water supply runs low.
ga: Aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, okra kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ji nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ni ohɔ̃ɔ dani nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and droop when the weather stays dry for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water in hot weather, they lose moisture faster than their roots can drink it up. Drooping and yellowing are the plant's natural ways of cutting back energy use to survive until it receives water again.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ehi shi kɛyashi be mli ni enine shɛɔ nu nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before forming fruits when the ground gets dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers as a defense mechanism during water shortages. When the plant senses there isn't enough water to support developing fruits, it drops the flowers to save its remaining water for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni faaa lɛ naa. Beni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ. Ebaashi efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Is it better to water my crops early in the morning or in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water your crops early in the morning when the temperature is cool. This gives the soil time to soak up the water before the strong afternoon sun causes it to evaporate.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha otsei lɛ nu leebi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛmuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa efoɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much water from the irrigation channel?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ mi-irrigation gbɛi lɛ amli?

english: Crops getting too much water will have pale yellow leaves, soft or weak stems, and water sitting on the soil surface for days without draining. Overwatering suffocates the roots and causes them to rot.
ga: Tsei ni nu babaoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsoi bibii loo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni nu hoɔɔɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha amɛgboi.

english: Will adding more water to my cassava farm make the cassava tubers grow bigger?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛbaafata mi-kassava ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaha cassava shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Cassava needs water when it is young to establish good roots, but too much water later in the season can actually cause the tubers to rot underground instead of swelling bigger.
ga: Nu he miihia cassava kɛjɛ egbekɛbiiashi koni shishifãi kpakpai aba. Shi nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛfuu.

english: Why does water soak into the ground quickly on one side of my farm but sit on top of the soil on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ ni ooota yɛ afã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This happens because of different soil types on your farm. Sandy soil has large spaces that let water drain away fast, while clay soil is tightly packed and holds water on the surface for longer.
ga: Enɛ baa mli yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ hei wuji ni haa nu hoɔ oya. Shi shikpɔŋ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ fee lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does having water available near the surface affect how deep my crop roots grow?
ga: Te nu ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ saa bɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When water is easily available near the surface, crop roots stay shallow because they do not need to search for moisture. If the topsoil dries out, the roots grow deeper into the ground to find water hidden below.
ga: Beni nu yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ejaakɛ ehe ehiaaa ni atao ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli egbi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni anaa nu ni akɛtee shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin instead of strong and bushy when I plant them close to the water path?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji beni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu gbɛi lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and room to grow. They stretch upward as fast as possible to catch light, making them tall and weak rather than sturdy and productive.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la kɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛgbala amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛhe waaa moŋ fe ni amɛaafee mɛi ni he wa ni amɛhe wa.

english: How can I tell when my plantains are fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantains lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Plantains are ready for harvesting when the individual fingers plump up, lose their sharp angular edges, and become rounded. Additionally, the dried flowers at the tips of the fruits easily rub off, and the top leaves of the plant begin to turn yellow.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji nine fɛɛ nine shwie shi. Elaajeɔ ŋwɛigbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebatsɔ ŋwɛigbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Kɛfata he lɛ, fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Ni tso lɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What is the proper way to harvest a bunch of plantains without damaging the crop?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa plantains ni afiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: To harvest plantains properly, make a partial cut halfway up the main stalk so the weight of the bunch gently lowers the plant toward you. Then, cut the stem cleanly with a sharp cutlass, keeping the bunch off the bare ground to prevent bruising.
ga: Bɔni afee ni akpa plantains lɛ jogbaŋŋ Feemɔ ŋmeii komɛi kɛya tso titri lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ aya ŋwɛi fiofio. Okɛ tso lɛ aba shi kɛba oŋɔɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ kakla ni naa afo tso lɛ he. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔlɔ naa.

english: Why is it recommended that I start my daily farm work early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ mije miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ shishi mra daa gbi lɛ?

english: Starting work early in the morning allows you to avoid the extreme afternoon heat, which conserves your physical strength and helps prevent heat exhaustion. It is also the best time for activities like spraying or planting, as soil moisture and humidity are higher.
ga: Kɛ́ oje shishi mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ hiɔ shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe yɛ latsaa mli. Eji be ni hi fe fɛɛ hu kɛha nifeemɔi tamɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsei adumɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain plant turn yellow and dry out as it grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Lower leaves naturally turn yellow and dry up as plantain plants mature because the plant redirects its nutrients and energy upward to support the growing stalk and heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ mli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua tso lɛ yibii ni miida lɛ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ.

english: How many suckers should I leave growing around a single plantain plant?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi ŋmeii enyiɛ mabɔle dumɔwu kome he?

english: You should leave a maximum of two to three suckers per stand: the main bearing mother plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot. Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight for nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Esaaa akɛ oshiɔ ŋmeii ni fe 2-3 yɛ shidaamɔ kome mli: tso nyɛ ni yɔɔ prune titri lɛ, ŋmeii kome ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ ŋmeii bibii kome. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why does my plantain crop perform poorly when I allow weeds to cover the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miha jwɛi ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's shallow roots. Keeping the space around your plantains clear ensures all the nutrients go directly into growing large, healthy fruits.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la ni he hia, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ashishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Plantains lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I store my harvested plantains so they do not spoil before I take them to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ ato koni amɛkafite dani mikɛya jara nɔ?

english: Store your harvested plantains in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded shelter away from direct sunlight. Stacking them on dry palm fronds or soft leaves prevents bruising, which delays premature ripening and rotting.
ga: Kɛ plantains ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to ŋmei tsei ahe tsei ni egbi loo bibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee nɔ ni shwieɔ mɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaha amɛshwere ni amɛgboi mra.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during rainy or windy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have soft, water-filled stems and shallow root systems, making them top-heavy when carrying a heavy bunch. You can prevent falling by using strong wooden bamboo poles as props to support the stem under the weight of the fruit.
ga: Plantains yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ tsii kɛji amɛmiiwo ŋmeii ni tsii. Obaanyɛ otsi shigbeemɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei tso ni wa ni okɛbaatsu nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi yɛ tso yibii lɛ tsiimɔ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: What type of soil is best for planting plantains to get a rich harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ sa kɛha plantains ŋmɔshi nibii koni ená yibii babaoo?

english: Plantains thrive best in deep, fertile, loamy soil rich in organic matter that drains well. Soil that traps stagnant water rots the roots, so well-draining soil mixed with decomposed manure gives the best results.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni hiɛɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ efutu mli lɛ haa yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: How long does it take from planting a plantain shoot until I can harvest the first bunch?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani anyɛɔ akpaa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Under good weather conditions with sufficient water and soil nutrients, a plantain sucker takes about 11 to 15 months to grow, produce flowers, and fully mature its fruit bunch for harvest.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai ni nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shishi. Plantain suckers lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛdaraa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai akui ni akɛkpaa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their young leaves dry out quickly. They require shade trees or fast-growing nurse crops like plantains to shield them from the sun while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ema shi shiŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with plenty of green leaves, but give me very small roots at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ehaa shishifãi bibii waa kɛji akpa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, cassava puts most of its food energy into growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of storing energy in underground root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava heɔ eniyenii hewalɛ lɛ fa ni ekwɛɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I spread chemical fertilizer on my maize field when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ mi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so that plant roots can absorb the nutrients. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots and cause leaves to dry out instead of helping the crop grow.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã ni baai lɛ agbi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua tsei ni amɛdara lɛ

english: Why are there tiny holes in my young maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibioo ko. Ani akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which lay eggs on leaves. Once hatched, the worms eat the leaf tissue and hide inside the central funnel of the plant to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ amɛfɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baai lɛ ahe fãji ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on leaf juices, or by viruses carried by these insects that disturb normal plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear the extra shoots coming out from the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain stem for water, light, and soil nutrients. Keeping only a few strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, healthy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo (tso lɛ) kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei bibii fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants stop making pods when I pick too many green leaves for cooking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ beni mikpaa baai eŋɔli babaoo ni mikɛhoɔ nii lɛ?

english: Leaves are the factories where plants make food using sunlight. When you pick too many leaves, the cowpea plant lacks the energy needed to produce flowers and fill out pods.
ga: Baai ji tsei ni tsei kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii. Kɛji okɛ baai babaoo shwie shi lɛ, Cowpea tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmeii amli.

english: Staking gets yam vines off the ground and spreads out the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to manufacture more food to send down into the growing tuber.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato wain tso lɛ ateshi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa bulb ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or poor pollination, causing the plant to shed flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ shwane mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo pollination ni ehiii Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why does my groundnut crop need loose soil around the base after it starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he beni ebɔi fɔfɔii lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow long stems called pegs that bend down and push into the soil to form nuts underground. If the soil is hard, the pegs cannot enter and nuts will not form.
ga: Beni amɛwo ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen sɛɛ lɛ Amɛyɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs. Efoɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa lɛ, pin lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli ni nut lɛ hu efeŋ.

english: Leaves curling and turning yellow usually means your tomato plants are under stress from heat, irregular watering, or being attacked by tiny insects like whiteflies. Keeping the soil consistently moist and spraying organic neem oil can help protect them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ latsaa he haomɔ shishi. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni tutuaa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ organic neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Tomatoes split when there is a sudden change in water supply, such as a heavy rain after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, so regular and even watering helps keep the skin smooth.
ga: Tomato baatswa kɛji nu lɛ tsake trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ he daa kɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewolo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if my maize crop is not getting enough water during the hot dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: If your maize is thirsty, the leaves will roll up tightly like pencils during the hot afternoon to save moisture. Giving them extra water during the flowering stage is key to getting full cobs.
ga: Kɛji kumai miiye o-abele lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nu ni akɛfataa he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ titri ni haa anáa ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin, tall stalks that fall over easily and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii baa. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Do I need to buy a lot of chemical fertilizer if I want to plant soya beans?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni madu soybeans lɛ, ani esa akɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo?

english: Soya beans actually feed themselves and the soil! They take nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots, so they require much less commercial fertilizer than crops like maize.
ga: Soybeans baanyɛ aye amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ! Amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe tsei tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How can I tell when my soya bean plants are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-soybean tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Your soya beans are ready when the plant leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving brown pods. If you shake the plant and hear the seeds rattling inside the dry pods, it is time to harvest.
ga: O soybeans lɛ efee klalo beni tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Kɛji okpokpo tso lɛ ni onu dumɔwui lɛ ni miihoso yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni abaakpa nii.

english: Does all rice need to be grown inside a large pool of standing water?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmãa fɛɛ yɛ nu agboi ni damɔ shi lɛ amli?

english: No, not all rice needs flooded fields. Upland rice varieties can grow in regular rain-fed soil just like maize, without needing standing water.
ga: Dabi, jeee ŋmãa ŋmɔji fɛɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli. Omɔ henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa tamɔ ŋmãa pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni akɛ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ tsuuu nii

english: Why are weeds such a serious problem for young rice plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ji naagba ni mli wa waa kɛha ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young rice plants grow slowly and have thin grass-like leaves, making it easy for fast-growing weeds to shade them out and steal their food. Clearing weeds early in the first four weeks is critical.
ga: Omɔ tsei bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛyɛ baai bibii ni tamɔ jwɛi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ akɛ amɛaatsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni amɛju niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ he hiaa waa.

english: Why is it good practice to divide my farm land into separate sections for different crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aja miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awo fãi amli lɛ? kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi No hewɔ lɛ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa.

english: Dividing your farm into distinct blocks makes it easier to give each crop type its specific fertilizer and water needs. It also helps prevent pests and diseases from spreading across your entire land.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mlijaa yɛ blɔkii amli Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oooha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ kɛ nu kɛha tso henɔ fɛɛ tso. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ amɛshwã oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: How do I decide how many acres of land to clear for planting before the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ acre enyiɛ ni esa akɛ mafo dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi?

english: Base your farm size on the amount of seeds, labor, and money you have available to maintain the land. Clearing more acres than you can properly weed or harvest will lead to wasted effort and lower yields.
ga: Too bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ ji lɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ dumɔwui, nitsumɔ, kɛ shika ni oyɔɔ ni okɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie shikpɔŋ babaoo fe bɔ ni obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi loo kpamɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni efite lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I clear my weeds without burning the bush before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi lɛ ni mishãaa jwɛi lɛ dani midu?

english: Burning destroys valuable nutrients in the topsoil and kills beneficial organisms like earthworms that help aerate the land. Leaving cleared weeds to rot naturally creates organic compost that feeds your crops for free.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. ni egbe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni atsuu he lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ yaka ni akɛhaa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ.

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs ni mli wa ni mli wa baa.

english: Why does my land give me smaller maize harvests when I plant maize on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize consumes specific nutrients like nitrogen heavily every season. Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those soil nutrients, whereas rotating with beans or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
