ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ nitrogen waa daa be. Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow and showing ragged holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni buji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes with yellowing leaves are usually caused by fall armyworm caterpillars feeding on the central growing point of the leaf. Treating the leaves early prevents the pest from destroying the plant's food-making process.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni yeɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni ekumɔ kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Baai lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite tso lɛ niyenii feemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates rapidly between dry and wet. Maintaining regular watering and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my crop roots burn and die when I place fertilizer right next to the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts. Placing fertilizer directly touching the stem pulls water out of the roots instead of feeding them; putting it a few inches away allows roots to safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛwo shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛkpe inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Will trimming excess branches off my cocoa tree hurt the tree or help it?
ga: Ani niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso mli lɛ baaye tso lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua lɛ?

english: Trimming excess leaves and dead branches helps the cocoa tree by allowing sunlight and air to pass through the canopy. This reduces humidity that causes black pod disease and encourages more pods to form.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehaa eboteɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ pods babaoo hewalɛ koni amɛfee.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant in the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give high yields only in their first generation. Saved seeds from a hybrid harvest lose their original strength, leading to uneven growth, smaller cobs, and poor total yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛshishijee hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ ehiii

english: Why does my harvested maize get covered in white powder and tiny holes while stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powda yɛŋ kɛ buji bibii ehà mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ nɔ lɛ? Be ni akɛtoɔ kotoku mli?

english: White powder and small holes are caused by maize weevils eating the grain from the inside out. Grain must be dried completely to safe moisture levels before storing in airtight sacks or treated bags to stop insect eggs from hatching.
ga: Powda yɛŋ kɛ buji bibii Nɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ mli baa. Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ kwraa kɛyashɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. dani akɛwo vacuum kotokui loo kotokui ni atsa mli koni kooloi akui akafɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow from the middle instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure helps restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts naturally puts nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my cassava help my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni akɛfataa ŋmei he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer for your cassava while the cowpea leaves cover the ground to stop soil from drying out.
ga: Cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-cassava lɛ. yɛ be mli ni cowpea baai haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide vital shade and moisture, protecting the young cocoa trees during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Is it better to plant my cassava stems slanting or straight down into the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanting angle of about 45 degrees helps the roots spread out comfortably, producing more yield and making the tubers much easier to harvest later.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ aaafee digrii 45 lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to build energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping tubers grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars keep hiding inside the middle funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack the tender young leaves inside the funnel where they are hidden from birds and rain. Early detection and spraying recommended organic or chemical pesticides early in the morning kills them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa baai bibii yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni akɛtee ni okpoi kɛ nugbɔ nyɛɔ lɛ anɔ. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ ana tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mra ni afɔ amɛ nɔ. Leebi lɛ, gbemɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my pepper leaves when I splash them with water late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu shwie shi gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Watering leaves late in the evening leaves them damp all night, creating the perfect conditions for fungal diseases to grow. It is better to water directly at the roots early in the morning so the leaves stay dry.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo baai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii adalɛ baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ leebi koni baai lɛ akagbi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough regular water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose a lot of leaves during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei lɛ ahe baai babaoo fiteɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves during dry weather to save water and keep themselves from drying out completely. Adding mulch around the tree roots and keeping shade trees on the farm helps moisture stay in the soil through the dry spell.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛkagbi kwraa. Mulching ni akɛbaabɔle Tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe kɛ hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective covers, keeping the air cool and the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Will I harvest more cassava if I plant my cuttings very close to each other?
ga: Ani makpa ŋmei babaoo kɛji midu ŋmei ni afolɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa?

english: Planting cassava too close together forces the plants to fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to thin plants with very small tubers instead of a bigger harvest.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulbs bibii waa baa yɛ yibii babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii?

english: Beans, groundnuts, and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for your main crops without needing extra chemicals.
ga: Beans, peanuts, kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei titrii lɛ ni tsofai krokomɛi ahe ehiaaa.

english: Heavy rain creates high humidity, which helps the fungus that causes Black Pod disease spread quickly across wet pods. Trimming extra branches helps air flow through the trees to dry the pods faster.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni no haa ŋmei ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ pods ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, dry soil, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ lɛ mli.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry period that can dry out the upper soil and kill newly sprouted seeds before the main rainy season fully arrives.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ kwraa.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the size of my crop harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors; their roots suck up water and nutrients from the soil and their leaves block sunlight, starving your crops of what they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa, ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the extra shoots growing out of my cocoa tree trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extra shoots consume the tree's energy and food, leaving less energy for the tree to produce flowers and healthy pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ tso lɛ náa koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during digging or if they are stored in hot, damp conditions. Storing them off the ground in a cool, well-ventilated space helps keep them fresh.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa yɛ be mli ni atsaa loo akɛto he ko ni edɔ, ni edɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves lose water faster than their young roots can absorb it. Planting shade crops like plantains gives cocoa plants the shade and humidity they need to survive until their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ amli baawa.

english: Why does my plantain farm grow smaller fruits when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The young shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away excess suckers allows the main plant to direct all its food toward producing a large, healthy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves indicates that the maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the newer top leaves, signaling that your soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or compost.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does the top flower of my maize open before the silks appear on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ dani siliki jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The top flower releases pollen into the wind, while the soft silks on the cob catch that pollen to form seeds. The plant times this growth so that pollen is actively falling right when the silks are ready to receive it and form full corn kernels.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jieɔ pollen yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Yɛ be mli ni siliki lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ On the cob lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nakai pollen lɛ koni ekɛfee dumɔwui. Tsei kɛ be haa nɛkɛ dalɛ nɛɛ bɔni afee ni pollen lɛ aba shi kɛji siliki lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ lɛ pɛ ni ekɛ ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with big leaves, but the tubers under the soil remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or grows in rich soil without enough potassium, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of storing food underground in the tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ebaafite hewalɛ fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ oyitsoŋ lɛ

english: Yam vines climb to lift their leaves up toward sunlight so they can make food efficiently. If left on the ground, the leaves get shaded and damp, leading to smaller yam tubers and higher risk of leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he koni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara waa kɛha foliar helai.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing any tomatoes during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air dry out tomato pollen, preventing flowers from being fertilized. When the plant senses it cannot form seeds properly under high heat, it drops the flowers to conserve moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo fɔmɔ Kɛ́ tsei nu he akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ yɛ la ni mli wa shishi lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or viruses spread by them. As the insects suck juices from the young leaves, the leaves distort and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa be mli ni kooloi bibii nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers grow above the ground but then bend down and push into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi amɛkotoɔ shi koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but once the flower is pollinated, it forms a growing stem called a peg that pushes down into the soil. The actual peanut pod then grows and matures safely under the ground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen lɛ Efeɔ tso ko ni miida ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanut pods lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants keep growing leaves during the main rains but only start flowering when the rains begin to reduce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ amli lɛ? Shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ bɔi shibaa pɛ kɛkɛ ni ebaabɔi fɔfɔi.

english: Many traditional cowpea varieties respond to day length. They use the long rainy days to grow foliage and wait for shorter days at the end of the rainy season to trigger flowering and pod production.
ga: Kusum cowpea henɔi babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ gbii kakadaji tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai ni amɛmɛɔ gbii kukuji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee koni amɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ podi afeemɔ he hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that easily dry out under full, direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides essential shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa bushes are mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient needed to build healthy leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the strength to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller crop yields when I plant maize in the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year without giving it time to replenish. Rotating crops like maize with legumes restores nutrients naturally and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ, haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting groundnuts or cowpeas improves my soil for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the dirt. When the plant roots decay, they leave this free fertilizer behind for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite Amɛbaashi nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling after just two or three days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ duŋ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lack a protective outer shell, so once pulled from the wet soil, they react rapidly with oxygen in the air and break down. They must be cooked, sold, or processed into products like gari immediately after harvesting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ kponɔgbɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie Cassava shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii oya ni amɛfiteɔ. Esa akɛ ahoo amɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ loo afee amɛ nibii tamɔ gari kɛji akpa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains and strong winds hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that struggle to hold up heavy bunches of fruit during storms. Propping the stems up with sturdy wooden Y-stakes gives them the extra physical support they need to stay upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔmɔ aduawai babaoo yɛ ahum be mli. Tso ko ni tamɔ Y ni akɛ tso ni wa fee lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa yelikɛbuamɔ kroko koni amɛhi shi jaŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus causes stress to tomato plants, making them shed their blossoms to save energy. Consistent watering and mulching around the roots help stabilize the soil temperature and prevent flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ daa Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yaa nɔ daa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Weeds are native plants that are naturally adapted to the soil and weather, allowing them to suck up water and nutrients much faster than domestic crops. Regular early weeding removes this competition so your crops can grow big.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Daa lɛ baaye abua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants suddenly full of ragged holes with tiny caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: This destruction is caused by Fall Armyworms, which crawl inside the central funnel of young corn plants to feed on delicate leaves. Applying recommended neem-based treatments early kills the caterpillars before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni akɛ neem fee lɛ tsuɔ nii mra. Egbeɔ ŋmei lɛ dani efiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck sap from the underside of leaves and transmit plant viruses. Spraying soapy water or bio-insecticides helps control these pests and protect new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli ni ekɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ baa Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ebuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei ahe.

english: How can I tell that my yams are mature and ready to harvest underground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ akɛtoɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yam plants tell you they are ready above ground; when the vines and leaves naturally turn yellow and start drying off at the end of the rainy season, it shows the plant has stopped growing and transferred all its energy into the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ etee shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling just two days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboi beni akpa gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once dug out of the ground, cassava roots lose their natural defense system and react with oxygen in the air, which triggers rapid cell decay within 24 to 48 hours.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa wala yibii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing shoots and sprouting even when I keep them in a dry place to sell later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ kɛ shweremɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ makɛto he ko ni egbi koni mahɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli moŋ.

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally break their rest period after a few months, using warmth and moisture signals in the air to start growing a new plant from their stored energy.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni fiteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo he okadii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛjeɔ tsei heei akwɛmɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested cocoyam leaves wilt and shrink so fast before I can reach the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baa ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ oya dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Broad leafy greens continuously lose water through invisible pores on their leaves; once cut from the root system, they can no longer draw up moisture, causing them to lose water and go limp quickly.
ga: Aduawai ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ afo amɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nu dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli oya ni ehaa mɔ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize farm roll up into thin tubes when the sun is hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awoɔ tsɔji bibii amli lɛ? Beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick where the maize plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun to protect itself from losing water too quickly during heat.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji teemɔŋ sane ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi. Abɛi haa ebaai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from environmental stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or nutrient shortage, because they lack the energy to feed developing pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ he amanehulu. Nɔ ni ha ebalɛ nakai ji hewalɛ ni bɛ ni akɛbaahã ŋmɔtɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the farm right when they are turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ etsɔ tsuru lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack when heavy rain or sudden watering follows a dry spell; the plant absorbs water rapidly, expanding the fleshy inside faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu ho trukaa yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ. Tsei shwieɔ nu oya. Enɛ haa mligbɛ fãji lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree branches during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous moisture allows fungal spores that cause Black Pod disease to float in rain droplets and attack the outer skin of the pods, quickly rotting the fruit inside.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei ni haa black pod hela lɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli ni amɛtutuaa pod lɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ. Enɛ haa yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over by themselves just when the fruit bunch becomes heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shi beni jwɛi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad roots that stay close to the topsoil rather than deep taproots, making the heavy top-heavy tree easily overturn in moist soil under heavy fruit weight.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shwiili ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ shishi.

english: Why do some of my yams become soft and watery inside while still in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: When soil gets waterlogged and lacks drainage, it starves the roots of oxygen, allowing water-loving soil bacteria to invade and cause wet rot inside the tubers before harvest.
ga: Be mli ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Ha sũ mli helai ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ ababote mli ni amɛfɔ bulbs ni egboi lɛ anɔ dani akpa.

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the central shoot (the whorl) where it is moist and dark, feeding on tender new leaves before the plant can mature and grow ears.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Asraafoi ŋmeii. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. (fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ) ni mli edɔ ni ehiɛ edɔ Ye baai heei dani tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛ toi.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by microscopic insects like thrips, mites, or aphids hiding on the underside of leaves and sucking out plant juices, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and burn when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They need shade from taller crops like plantains or shade trees to shield them from high heat while their root systems establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he beni shishifãi lɛ miibua amɛhe naa lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting underneath the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually mature at 9 to 12 months. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, and the soil at the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca shɛɔ dalɛ he beni eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 lɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers fall off without producing any pods when it rains too heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall can knock pollen off the open blossoms, waterlog the soil so roots cannot breathe, or create high moisture that causes fungal rot, leading the plant to drop flowers from stress.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha pollen lɛ ajɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he aahu kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Aloo afee hulutsoo ni fa ni haa ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ haomɔ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow starting from the middle tip in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ naagbee lɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing that moves from the tip down the center vein of older leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is the main food plants use to stay green and produce strong stems.
ga: Yellowing ni jɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my ripening tomatoes turn dark, flat, and rotten before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ, efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egboɔ dani manyɛ makpa lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. It often happens when watering is irregular—such as letting the soil dry out completely and then flooding it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ejaakɛ calcium ni bɛ lɛ shɛɔ aduawai lɛ ahe. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ahaa egbiɔ kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ nu afua.

english: Should I let all the small shoots that grow around my main plantain tree keep growing?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃? growing around Ani midumɔwu titri lɛ baaya nɔ eda?

english: No, you should remove most of them and keep only 2 or 3 strong shoots (suckers). If too many grow around the mother plant, they compete for nutrients and water, resulting in very small plantain bunches.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ojie emli babaoo ni okɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi shi kɛji oodu yɛ he fɛɛ he. Nyɛ tso babaoo Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early instead of waiting until my crops get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, light, and soil nutrients during the early critical weeks. If you clear them late, the crop has already lost the energy it needed to make a strong yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishijee otsii ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Kɛji ojie sɛɛ mli lɛ Ŋmãa lɛ efite hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Why is it important to support my yam vines with wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsei lɛ afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the air to catch sunlight, which powers root growth, while also keeping leaves off wet soil where fungal diseases quickly spread.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baa lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni emɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ adara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa sweet potato baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source plants need to grow. The maize plant moves its remaining nitrogen from the older bottom leaves to nourish the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛwo ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ hewalɛ.

english: When the sun gets extremely hot or the soil dries out quickly, tomato plants get stressed and shed their blossoms to save water and energy rather than forming fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi oya. Tomato tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: What is making my pepper leaves curl up into tight rolls and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from the leaves, or by viruses carried by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ

english: Why do white powdery patches cover the leaves of my pumpkin and cucumber plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni ha mi-pumpkin kɛ kukumba baai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: This is powdery mildew, a fungal infection that spreads when plants are crowded together with warm air and damp leaves. It blocks sunlight from reaching the leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji powder mli ŋmei. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ tsei kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ baai ni mli efɔ ebɔ he. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct heat. They need temporary shade trees, like plantain or shade-providing forest trees, to protect them while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni abu tsei ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ

english: Why is it important to weed around my cassava stems regularly during the first few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔjie jwɛi ni bɔle ehe lɛ? Cassava tsei ni aduɔ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 2-3 lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow faster than cassava and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your cassava cuttings need to establish strong roots and tuber growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ŋmei ni ofoɔ lɛ he hiaa koni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ ŋmei shweremɔ aba.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not reach deep into the earth. When heavy bunches grow, the tree becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wet soil and wind to pull the roots out.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni eshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji tso lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baaná nɔ ni tsii fe fɛɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do black spots turn my cocoa pods dark and rotten during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, a fungal sickness that spreads quickly in cold, wet, humid weather. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air flow to dry out the farm and prevent the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, hulutsoo be, kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes through the middle leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu bibii kɛtsɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are armyworms or stem borers, which hatch from eggs laid by moths. They crawl into the center of the maize plant where the fresh leaves grow and feed on them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo stem borers. ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ Amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ he ni baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn soft and rot underground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yam rot happens when water gathers and stays around the roots in poorly drained soil, which allows soil fungi and bacteria to enter damaged tubers and decay them.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu shwie shi ni ebɔle nu lɛ he. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii ni efite ni miifite lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in strong, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees shade and keeping the soil moist while they build strong roots.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni otswaa shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting before my cocoa trees start producing pods?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du nii sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani cacao tso lɛ aje shishi ewo ŋmeii?

english: If you plant modern hybrid cocoa varieties, they usually start bearing pods in about 2 to 3 years. Older traditional varieties take longer, usually around 4 to 5 years.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrids Bei pii lɛ Amɛjeɔ pods feemɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli. Kusum nifeemɔi srɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ baahe be babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to pass freely through the tree canopy. This helps trees grow stronger, reduces fungal diseases, and helps pods grow bigger.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ mli ni amɛfee nɔ ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli waa, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: Dropping leaves is the tree's natural way of surviving dry weather. By shedding leaves, the tree conserves water in its trunk and roots until the rains come back.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ nu toɔ eshishi kɛ eshishifãi amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are some of my green cocoa pods turning black and soft before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads easily in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Keeping the farm weeded and pruning branches helps air dry the trees and prevents the rot from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi jwɛi ni egbo lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: What causes the leaves on my young cocoa shoots to look burnt and dry up suddenly?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ?

english: This damage is often caused by mirids (also called capsids), tiny insects that suck sap from young stems and leaves. Spraying recommended treatments during peak pest seasons helps protect fresh growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirids ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. (Atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ capsid) ni ji kooloo bibioo ko. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai amli lɛ Tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tsɛŋemɔ helai heei ahe.

english: Why do so many tiny flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi enyiɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only tiny midges (insects) can pollinate them. Unpollinated flowers drop naturally, but maintaining a damp ground cover helps midges breed and pollinate more flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kooloi bibii pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Amɛ pɛ ji mɛi ni baanyɛ afee pollin. Fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ pollen lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi kɛ́ aha he ni akɛ sũ ewo mli lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua dwarf lɛ ni efɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni ekɛ pollination aba.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need fertilizer to produce more pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: If your trees have pale yellow leaves, slow growth, or produce very few pods despite flowering, the soil lacks nutrients. Applying specialized cocoa fertilizer replenishes potassium and nitrogen needed for pod formation.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo, loo eyɛ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ eewo fɔfɔi moŋ. tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha potassium kɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa kɛha pod feemɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their color changes completely—usually from green to bright yellow, or reddish-brown to orange. Harvesting pods when fully yellow ensures the beans inside have maximum sugar for quality fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su etsake kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. loo red-brown kɛyashi orange Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛji ŋmeii kwraa lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa sugar babaoo kɛha ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must I cover cocoa beans with plantain leaves to ferment them after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ plantain baai aha kookoo yibii lɛ ahe koni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans to kill the inner germ and develop the rich chocolate flavor and deep brown color. Plantain leaves trap heat and natural yeasts, allowing proper chemical changes to take place over 5 to 7 days.
ga: Fermentation haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ koni egbe helai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni ehaa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ waa Plantains mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tsofa tsakemɔi baa yɛ gbii 5 kɛyashi 7 mli.

english: Why do some farmers plant mushrooms or crops in plastic bags instead of putting them directly into the open ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii loo nibii krokomɛi yɛ plastic kotokui amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in bags allows you to easily control moisture, protect delicate roots or spores from wild soil pests, and move the crop around to avoid harsh weather.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛɔ yɛ kotokui amli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ hulutsoo be lɛ oya. Ebuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛɔ sũ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ahe. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aya he fɛɛ he Koni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa akafee nɔ ko

english: Can I take a mushroom I find in the bush and plant it directly in my farm soil to make it grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii ni anaa yɛ jwɛi amli lɛ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛkwɛ nɔ?

english: Most wild mushrooms need very specific shade, decayed matter, and moisture to survive, so simply moving them into open farm soil usually causes them to dry out and die unless you recreate their natural environment.
ga: Koo mli ŋmeii babaoo biɔ hulutsoo. nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ hulutsoo pɔtɛɛ ko koni ehi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ, ehaa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Ja okɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ lɛ fee ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to cover my planted seeds or crop material with a light layer of soil or sand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋã bibioo ko baaha midumɔwui loo nibii ni miduɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: A light layer of sand or soil keeps the planting material moist, protects it from burning under direct sunlight, and prevents insects or birds from eating it before it sprouts.
ga: Ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni otsi kooloi bibii loo okpoi anaa koni amɛkaye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I choose between different varieties of the same crop when buying planting material at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ mihe nibii ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Different varieties are bred for different conditions—some produce harvest quickly, while others resist common local diseases or survive better during dry spells, so you should pick the type that matches your land and weather.
ga: Akwɛɔ kooloi srɔtoi yɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli. Henɔi komɛi haa nɔ ko baa oya. yɛ be mli ni henɔi krokomɛi Eteɔ shi ewoɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ loo ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ohala tso srɔtoi ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ.

english: Why do some crop seeds sprout within a few days while others take weeks to push through the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii fioo ko pɛ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ otsii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seeds have different coat thicknesses; seeds with hard outer shells take longer to absorb water and break open, whereas soft seeds sprout almost immediately when moist.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔi srɔtoi. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba.

english: Why do my plant roots start to rot when the ground stays soaked with water for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do; when soil remains flooded, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with weak stems when planted close to large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ahe lɛ?

english: Plants stretch upward towards sunlight when they are shaded, consuming energy to grow tall rather than developing thick stems and strong roots.
ga: Tsei baagbala amɛhe kɛya hulu lɛ he kɛji amɛyɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ moŋ fe ni eeehiɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: What causes young crop leaves to turn yellow and wither during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni haa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Young plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their small roots can pull water from the ground, causing them to wilt under intense heat.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ Nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ lɛ, amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do crops grow much better in soil mixed with decomposed leaves than in plain red dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baai ni egboi efutu mli lɛ nɔ fe shikpɔŋ tsuru folo nɔ lɛ?

english: Decomposed organic matter acts like a sponge to hold moisture while releasing rich natural food that plain dirt or sand lacks.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa, ni muji loo ŋã folo bɛ mli lɛ kpo.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots and leaves fight for the same water, nutrients, and sunlight, leaving less energy for fruit production.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ yibii lɛ faaa.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tip usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishijee ŋmɔŋ ni baa yɛ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rains stay on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits on the field without draining, it drowns the roots and creates the wet conditions that fungi need to rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni he hiaa ŋmei lɛ koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the tree branches without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, attacked by insects like capsids, or lacking nutrients. Giving the trees partial shade, protecting them from pests, and keeping soil moist helps flowers stay on and set pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ, kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei ni akɛhaa amɛhe hulutsoo Buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui ahe Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull water from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect the plant from drying out, and they usually bounce back once the afternoon cool arrives.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa ekoŋŋ kɛ́ shwane kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ ba.

english: How does breaking up hard soil before planting help my yam tubers grow long and straight?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akuɔ mli dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow directly downward into the earth. Loosening hard or compacted soil gives the soft tuber room to push down easily without bending or splitting against underground barriers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tuber chamber ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ashɛ shi mlɛo ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nibii ni tsiɔ gbɛ lɛ agbalaaa shi loo ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do my maize crops grow stronger when I plant groundnuts alongside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa waa kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil, providing free natural food for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do armyworms feed on my maize leaves mostly at night instead of during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms yeɔ mi-corn baai lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Caterpillars hide in the central funnel of the plant or in the soil during the day to avoid dying from hot sunlight and being eaten by birds. They come out to feed at night when it is cool and safe.
ga: Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbi mli koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbo amɛ ni okpoi akaye amɛ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop seeds right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very tough seeds already sitting in your soil, designed by nature to sprout instantly and capture light and soil water before your planted crops get a chance to establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni wa waa ni afu yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee amɛ koni amɛje kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛhiɛ la kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi aba.

english: Why do my stored maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If seeds are stored in a place that is warm or damp, small insects or moisture slowly destroy the tiny living embryo inside the seed. Storing dried seeds in cool, tightly sealed containers keeps them alive for planting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni hulu tsoɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kplukai loo nu fioo ko baafite ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ fiofio. Dumɔwui ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ tsinsii ni mli ejɔ ni atsĩ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why should I wait until my seeds sprout before putting fertilizer near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo dumɔwui lɛ ahe?

english: Seeds without roots cannot drink fertilizer nutrients. Applying fertilizer too early wastes your money because rain washes it away before the young roots grow deep enough to reach it.
ga: Dumɔwui ni shishifãi bɛ amɛhe lɛ nyɛŋ anu ŋmɔshi nibii amli niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ofite shika ejaakɛ nugbɔ baaho lɛ dani shishifãi bibii lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛ he.

english: Why should I use chemical weedkillers instead of only clearing my farm with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ dade pɛ baajie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing with a cutlass only cuts the tops of weeds, leaving the roots alive to quickly sprout back and steal nutrients from your crops. Applying the right weedkiller destroys the roots completely, saving you labor and giving your young crops clear space to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ, efoɔ jwɛi lɛ ayiteŋ pɛ. Shi shishifãi lɛ ahi shi koni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ kwraa. Ye obua bo ni okɛ nitsumɔ ato Ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Will spraying weedkillers on my land destroy the soil for future crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ ni akɛbaadu wɔsɛɛ lɛ?

english: When used in the correct quantities and at the right times, chemical weedkillers break down safely without ruining the soil. However, using too much or applying the wrong chemical can harm beneficial soil organisms, so precise application is essential.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa kɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ shweshweeshwe ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine loo tsofa ni ejaaa lɛ baanyɛ aye sũ mli nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ nitsumɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ he miihia.

english: Is it better to burn cut bushes or leave them on the soil after clearing my land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaashã jwɛi ni afolɔ loo abaashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving cut bushes to rot naturally on the soil creates a protective blanket called mulch. This keeps the soil cool, holds rainwater longer, and slowly decays into rich organic plant food, whereas burning kills good soil nutrients and dries out the land.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ajɔ. Ebua nugbɔ nu naa be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa. Yɛ be mli ni shãa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ lɛ.

english: How does buying fertilizer actually help my crops yield more food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahemɔ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer works like food supplements for crops. Continuous farming empties the soil of natural minerals, so adding fertilizer restores key nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that plants need to build strong stems, green leaves, and big harvests.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ ejie adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei akwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa, baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I put all my bag of fertilizer on the crops at once when I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and cannot absorb a full season of fertilizer all at once. Applying it in smaller portions over time ensures the plant gets fed as it grows, and stops heavy rains from washing away your expensive investment before the roots can take it in.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ be muu fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ fioo mli Yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, enɛ baaye abua ni aha tso lɛ niyenii be mli ni edaa lɛ. ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ oshika ni jara wa ni okɛwo mli lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ abote mli.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant produce chlorophyll, which turns the leaves green again so it can process sunlight into growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ klorofil. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛtsake kɛjɛ hulu la mli ni amɛdara.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one hole, their roots choke each other fighting for the same small pocket of water, sunlight, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each crop its own area to grow tall and produce large fruits.
ga: Beni dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ sũ kotoku bibioo kome mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ ni ekɛda ni ewoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Why is it important to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo niji krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cutting off dead or overcrowded branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the whole tree. This reduces fungal diseases and forces the tree to direct its energy into growing bigger, healthier pods instead of useless leaves.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and stop expanding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmli eshwaaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck plant juice and spread plant viruses. Treating the crops with targeted pest control prevents these insects from ruining the plant's ability to grow full tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ koni akɛgbe ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs ni eyi obɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my crop flowers drop off without turning into fruits when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water during dry spells, they drop their flowers to conserve energy and save themselves from dying. Providing shade crops or mulching keeps the soil moist so flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ Amɛbaashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhere amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo mulching ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ akpɛtɛ he ni aduawai aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that your maize lacks nitrogen or is sitting in waterlogged soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves regain their green color and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: What makes my cassava leaves curl up and grow tiny and twisted?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Curled and twisted cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. You can prevent this by planting improved, disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings.
ga: Kasava baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kasava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ yucca tsei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves suddenly even when the weather is warm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baa shwieɔ shi trukaa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ po lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their leaves when their roots are trapped in waterlogged soil or infected by fungal rot. Ensuring your soil drains water well keeps the roots healthy and leaves intact.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ emɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni baai lɛ hu akafite.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can trap direct sunlight, which fuels the growth of large tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ daraa Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of pollinating midges. Providing light shade and feeding the soil helps flowers set into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: How do I choose which small plantain shoots to cut away from the main plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala banana tsei bibii ni esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli?

english: You should remove 'water suckers' with broad leaves because they are weak. Keep 'sword suckers' with narrow, pointed leaves, as they have stronger roots and will yield heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ‘suckers’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ejaakɛ amɛhe waaa. Ha ‘klante-suckers’ ni baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni ebaawo plantain ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Tomatoes split when heavy rain or sudden heavy watering follows a dry spell. The inside of the fruit grows too quickly for the skin to stretch, so keeping soil moisture steady prevents cracking.
ga: Tomatoi tswa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni hoɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why do my garden eggs stay small and bitter instead of growing big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs become small and bitter when the plant lacks sufficient water or essential nutrients like phosphorus. Regular watering and healthy soil produce larger, sweeter fruits.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa baaha aduawai lɛ adara ni amɛmli ajɔ.

english: Why is it bad to place fertilizer right next to the main stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's skin and young roots. Spreading it a short distance away in a ring allows outer roots to drink the nutrients safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli yɛ hei kukuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts between their maize rows instead of growing only maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ŋmeii kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air into the ground, which naturally feeds the neighboring maize plants. They also cover the soil surface to shade out weeds and retain moisture.
ga: Akpɔlɔi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu koni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: This yellowing usually means your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which frequently happens when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when crops are grown continuously on the same land without manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ laaje. aloo kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air into the soil through small nodules on their roots, leaving behind free plant food that feeds the crops planted after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ, ni amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii koni amɛkɛye tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants filled with ragged holes and small brownish droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ eyi kɛ buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is a typical sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which crawl deep inside the central shoot of the maize plant to feed on tender young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ateŋ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus carried by whiteflies, which damage the leaf tissue and prevent normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛji hiɛ ni fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni haaa baa lɛ adalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil fills all the air spaces with water, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal diseases to rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ mli hei lɛ eyiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain usually warms the dry soil without soaking deep enough, creating a hot, wet environment that cooks and rots the seeds before steady rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ mli bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, delicate leaves that dry out easily under direct sunlight. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo tsei ni hiɛ ka yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Staking lifts the yam vines off the ground so the leaves can spread out and catch full sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more energy and grow larger tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ehaa bulb lɛ daraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any tomatoes during very hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too hot, the pollen inside tomato blossoms dries up and cannot fertilize the flower, causing the plant to shed the blossoms to conserve water and energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔmɔ nii amli. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I trim off the roots and outer dark skin of a plantain sucker before planting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛhewolo ni tsuɔ yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ dani madu?

english: Trimming the base removes hidden banana weevil eggs and microscopic worms in the roots, ensuring you do not transfer pests into your new field.
ga: Base cutting lɛ baajie banana ŋmei ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baaha okɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akaya shikpɔŋ hee nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds when the rain starts falling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?
