english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath might still be too dry. Wait until the rains become steady—usually after two or three deep rains—so the soil holds enough moisture for seeds to germinate without drying up.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lolo. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ—koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface exposed to heat and wind, preventing water from evaporating too quickly during hot spells.
ga: Abɛi baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Tsei haa he ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from the district office instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni kpokpaa nitsumɔhe lɛ ewo he odase lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaahere dumɔwui kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to produce higher yields, resist local diseases, and grow uniformly. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose these strong traits over time, leading to smaller harvests and a higher risk of disease.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ daa Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi fioo, ni helai hu baa.

english: What causes my cassava stem cuttings to rot in the soil after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems rot when planted in waterlogged soil or when infected by soil fungi. Planting stems at a slight angle on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the stems healthy.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ emɔ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Is it better for my soil to plow my field with a tractor or just clear it by hand with a cutlass?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ trakta baatsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nine baatsu nii kɛkɛ?

english: Plowing with a tractor loosens deep soil quickly, making it easier for roots to spread and absorb nutrients in large fields. However, for sloped or fragile land, gentle hand-clearing prevents the good topsoil from washing away during heavy rains.
ga: Trakta ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaajara nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli ni amɛŋɔ. Shi, kɛha hei ni shwieɔ shi loo hei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ, nine ni akɛtsuɔ nii blɛoo lɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ naa koni ekaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and healthy in one part of my farm but turn yellow and stay small in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ bibioo lolo yɛ fã kroko mli.

english: Soil nutrition and water drainage vary across a single farm. Crops turn yellow and stay small where the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or where water collects and chokes the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ hei ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo hei ni nu buaa ehe naa ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam tubers become small and bent when planted in hard, rocky, or shallow soil that physically blocks them from growing downward. Planting in deep, loose mounds gives the tubers space to grow smooth and long.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɔ, ni no haaa amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛshishi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha bulb lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: If I am farming on family land for a short period, what crops can I plant that grow and yield fast?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ miweku lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii be kukuoo ko lɛ, Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ makwɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya?

english: Short-season crops like cowpeas, tomatoes, and pepper mature within two to three months. These allow you to harvest quickly and clear the land without making long-term changes to family property.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ tsina ŋmei, tomato kɛ ŋmei baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii oya ni otsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ofeee tsakemɔi ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ oweku lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my bean plants growing plenty of green leaves but producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes bean plants to focus energy on leafy growth instead of flowers and pods. Using fertilizers higher in phosphorus encourages the plant to set more flowers and produce full pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How will planting trees along the boundaries of my farm help my food crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Boundary trees act as windbreaks to protect delicate crops from strong storms, drop leaves that decay into rich natural fertilizer, and help retain soil moisture during dry periods.
ga: Husu tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ahum ni naa wa he. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect them from direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside cocoa keeps the leaves cool and prevents sun scorch while the cocoa trees establish roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni cocoa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ maa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall sticks instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb stakes so their leaves receive maximum sunlight to produce energy. Lifting the leaves off the ground helps the plant grow larger tubers below the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my plantain stem die after giving me one cluster of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbo beni ekɛ plantain ŋmɔ ko ha mi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A plantain stem naturally flowers and fruits only once in its lifecycle. After producing fruit, that main stem dies so the root system can send its energy into the young sucker plants growing around its base.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ ewala be mli. Beni ewo yibii sɛɛ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baagbo. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aha hewalɛ aya tso bibioo ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking phosphorus or that cold, wet soil is preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients. Adding phosphorus-rich fertilizer or improving soil drainage helps the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ tso lɛ mli loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers recommend planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow strong, so planting them together enriches the soil naturally.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young corn look like holes were eaten in them with dust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu ni sũ eye yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central leaf funnel of the corn plant. Applying targeted organic or chemical remedies early protects the growing tip of the maize.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmãa lɛ naji ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants wilting and falling off after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess rain causes waterlogging around pepper plant roots, which suffocates the roots and encourages fungal root rot. Planting peppers on raised ridges helps extra water drain away from the plant roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu feɔ ekome kɛbɔleɔ he. pepper tso shishifãi Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the air gets too hot or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing partial shade during hot periods keeps flowers healthy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when its lower leaves turn yellow and drop off. You can also dig carefully around the base of one plant to check if the tubers have grown to full size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii kɛbɔle he hu. Tso ko shishi koni akɛkwɛ kɛji yitso lɛ eda kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds growing near my young crops make my crops stay short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ haa midumɔwui lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow tall and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Ehe hia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for growth, or that the soil is too waterlogged, which stops the roots from absorbing nutrients from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops rot at the roots when heavy rains fall for several days in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and creating a damp environment where soil fungi can quickly grow and rot the root system.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ adara oya ni efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes into my young maize leaves and leaving powdery waste in the stalks?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central whorl of the maize plant and feeds on young leaves before the cob forms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmei mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees during the maintenance season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let sunlight and air circulate. This reduces humidity around the pods, preventing fungal diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni ehaaa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Very high temperatures cause heat stress, which destroys the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot form fruits, causing the unfertilized flowers to dry up and drop off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. ni fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ no hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ ekɛ nɔ ko aba Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to dig up since they grow hidden under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko eshɛ he ni esa akɛ atsa ejaakɛ ekɛ ehe ewo shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is generally ready between 8 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, and cracks start appearing in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ni ŋmeii bɔi baa yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: What will happen if I plant my pepper seedlings very close together to fit more into my plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting too closely forces the pepper plants to compete for soil nutrients and light, resulting in tall, thin stems that produce very few and small fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha pepper tso lɛ abɔi niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ la lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsei lɛ kɛlɛɔ, ni amɛhe tseee, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai fioo ko pɛ.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high in the sunlight to produce energy for the tuber below, and keeping the leaves off the damp ground prevents them from rotting.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last maize harvest yield smaller crops than the fresh packaged seeds I buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo kotoku mli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds lose their strength and high yield potential after the first harvest, so planting seeds saved from that harvest leads to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛwo yibii fioo.

english: Even small weeds steal nutrients and water from the root zone of your crops, and they also shelter insects that can carry diseases to your plants.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ashishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa kooloi bibii ni kɛ helai baa lɛ hu náa wɔɔhe.

english: Why do my groundnuts grow well without me buying expensive fertilizer, but my maize always fails without it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ? Shi mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be kɛji ŋmãa nɛɛ bɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, meaning they have special roots that trap natural plant food directly from the air and put it into the soil. Maize cannot do this and relies heavily on fertilizer or rich soil nutrients to grow.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi nyɛɛɛ afee enɛ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa babaoo lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: What crops can I plant on my farm if I don't have money to buy starter fertilizer this season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Kɛji obɛ shika ni okɛbaahe shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: Crops like groundnuts, cowpeas, and bambara beans are great choices when fertilizer is scarce because they make their own nutrients and actually leave the soil richer for your next crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei kɛ bambara ŋmei ji nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji ŋmei faaa ejaakɛ amɛfeɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: If I plant maize without applying fertilizer right at the start, will the crop still grow?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa wooo mli kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ, ani ebaakwɛ̃ lolo?

english: Maize seeds will sprout using the food stored inside the seed, but as soon as the young roots spread, they need heavy nutrients like nitrogen to keep growing strong, or the leaves will turn yellow and growth will stop.
ga: Niyenii ni akɛto dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui. Shi kɛji shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ amɛshwã pɛ kɛkɛ ni niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ nitrogen hu he miihia amɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara waa. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdalɛ baakpa.

english: How does growing groundnuts help the soil before I plant maize on the same land later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani sɛɛ mli lɛ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts naturally drop leaves and leave root nodules behind that add nitrogen to the soil. When you plant maize on that same land afterward, the maize uses those leftover nutrients to grow better with less added fertilizer.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛshiɔ shishifãi ni kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ ŋmãa kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ baatsu nii koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmãa fioo.

english: Why do groundnut plants need less food from the soil compared to heavy-feeding crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei biɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Groundnuts work together with friendly bacteria in the soil to feed themselves nitrogen gas from the air, while maize relies entirely on nutrients already present in the dirt or added by you.
ga: Peanuts kɛ naanyobɔɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛye nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli momo loo nɔ ni okɛfataa he lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when the soil runs out of nutrients?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is its main food for making strong stalks and green leaves; without enough of it, the plant cannot feed itself properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmãa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmãa ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛji akɛ eshɛɛɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it true that harvesting groundnuts leaves the soil better than it was before planting?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmei ni akpaa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe dani aduɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, because groundnuts fix nitrogen in the ground, leaving their roots and decaying leaves in the soil acts like natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant in that spot next.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmeii saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Shishifãi kɛ baai ni ashiɔ koni amɛgboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ he ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: How can I tell if my farmland already has natural nutrients before spending money to bring in outside inputs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii momo dani mawo nyɔmɔ koni mikɛ nibii ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ aba?

english: Look at the wild plants and weeds growing on your land—dark green, thick plants show fertile soil, while pale, thin vegetation means the soil lacks nutrients and needs organic manure or compost.
ga: Kwɛmɔ koo mli tsei kɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ fɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe tseee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I use local farm manure instead of commercial chemical fertilizer when planting my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ jarayeli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ kɛ́ midu tsei?

english: Yes, well-rotted animal manure and compost slowly release nutrients into the soil while improving its water holding capacity, giving your crops a strong start without commercial chemical fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaya hiɛ fiofio. jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ha onibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: What natural nutrients are already present on my fallow land that my crops can use?
ga: Mɛɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii?

english: Unused land usually accumulates organic matter from rotted leaves and wild bush roots, which holds moisture and slow-release nutrients that light-feeding crops can easily feed on without added inputs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ buaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ koo mli tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni egboi lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni tsei ni bɛ la babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye lɛ toɔ mlɛo ni ekɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ eyaaa hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight and extreme heat. Without shade trees or plantains planted nearby to shield them and keep the soil moist, the cocoa trees get stressed, turn yellow, and drop leaves to survive the dry heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, dumɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha edɔ. Kookoo tso lɛ miihao. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ koni ehi shi yɛ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ mli.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long hot spell before the regular rains truly begin. If you plant immediately after that first rain, your seeds will sprout, but the young seedlings will quickly dry up and die from the scorching sun before the next rain falls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni naa wa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ Odumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ nɛɔ.

english: Why is my maize crop staying small and turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ ji bibioo ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn pale green or yellow starting from the leaf tips, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient maize needs to grow tall, build strong stalks, and keep its leaves healthy and dark green.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa akwɛ̃. Bɔɔ tso ni mli wa ni oha baai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ

english: Why do extension officers advise me not to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot year after year completely drains the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why will my crops produce a smaller harvest if I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmaa bibioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food or light, they all grow weak and produce smaller fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa enaaa niyenii loo la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ aduawai bibii loo ŋmeii.

english: Why do I need to use wooden poles to stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso atsu nii koni mikɛtsi sweet potato wain tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves in direct sunlight to make energy for growing big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, keeping them healthy, capturing more light, and preventing diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ha baai lɛ mli awa Na la babaoo ni otsi helai srɔtoi anaa

english: Extra sucker shoots growing around the base steal water and food from the main plantain stalk. By pruning away all but one or two strong suckers, you ensure the main plant gets all the energy it needs to grow a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi krɛdɛɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Shishitoo lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain tso wulu lɛ mli. Afoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ, ja eko loo enyɔ pɛ. Obaanyɛ oná nɔmimaa akɛ tso titri lɛ baaná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when soil stays soaked with excess water for too long due to poor drainage or heavy rains. Waterlogged soil prevents the roots from breathing, allowing fungal diseases to attack and decompose the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ nu ni fa fe nine ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu. Ha ni tsɛŋemɔ helai atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbala amɛmli.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, extreme dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save water and energy instead of trying to nourish growing peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upward and feeling dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni minuɔ he akɛ amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viral diseases, or by heavy heat combined with irregular watering. Keeping your farm free of weeds and controlling sap-sucking insects helps keep leaves flat and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa fataa he lɛ mli Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi akafee nɔ ko, ni okwɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the living shade and moist environment needed for young cocoa seedlings to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa koni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or insect pests like mirids. Keeping soil moist with shade and applying organic fertilizer helps the tree hold onto its flowers so they can form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni efeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize plant mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores green leaf growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaa eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize takes nitrogen out of the soil, while groundnuts and beans put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Rotating these crops restores soil fertility naturally without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because there is poor drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves up on poles allows them to catch maximum sunlight. When the leaves get direct light, the plant produces more energy, resulting in larger yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee tso ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la tɛ̃ɛ Tsei lɛ baajie hewalɛ babaoo kpo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit, making them top-heavy. Supporting the trunk with a strong forked wooden pole prevents the tree from snapping or uprooting in high winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tso lɛ akumɔ loo eshishijee yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why does covering the ground with dry grass keep my soil moist for longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mulching wo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil, blocking direct sunlight from evaporating water away. This technique, called mulching, keeps the ground cool and retains moisture for crop roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni etsiɔ naa koni nu akafee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ ŋaa nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa tsei shishifãi.

english: Why do people spray water mixed with crushed neem leaves onto crops to stop pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ nu ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ efutu mli lɛ shwieɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛkɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ?

english: Neem leaves contain natural bitter compounds that repel and stop insects from feeding on plants. Spraying neem water protects crops from pests without using expensive synthetic chemicals.
ga: Nɔ ko ni yɔɔ neem baai lɛ amli ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkpaa amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye tso lɛ. Neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni tsofai ni akɛfee nibii ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Leaf curling on tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viruses between plants. Controlling these insects using soaps or mesh nets helps keep tomato leaves healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ samla loo ŋshɔŋlooi tsu nii ni akɛye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tomato baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my young mango fruits turning black and dropping off the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose or attacks from fruit flies. Wet weather helps the fungus spread, causing dark spots that expand until the fruit rots and falls off early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose loo aduawai amli tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ feɔ diŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa aahu kɛyashiɔ aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my crop is suffering from a disease or just needs more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo nu babaoo he miihia lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Water-stressed plants usually wilt in the hot sun but perk back up in the cooler evening. Diseased plants will show specific signs like spots, white powder, dark blotches, or rotting leaves regardless of the time of day.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu haa amɛhe feɔ shoo lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ baajie okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi akpo, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ, ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ, loo baai ni egbo, ekɔɔɔ gbi lɛ mli be he.

english: How long does a crop disease usually take to show visible signs after it infects my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai jieɔ okadii ni anaa lɛ akpo beni amɛbote miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Some diseases show signs within a few days, while others can stay hidden inside the plant for two to three weeks before yellow leaves, dark spots, or rotting fruits appear on the outside.
ga: Helai komɛi jieɔ okadii akpo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni helai krokomɛi Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ehe awo tso lɛ mli otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ dani baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmɔtɔ diŋ, loo aduawai ni egboi aba kponɔgbɛ.

english: If I see signs of disease on just one plant in my farm, should I destroy it immediately?
ga: Kɛji mina hela he okadii yɛ tso kome pɛ mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani Esa akɛ makpãtã ehiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, carefully removing and destroying a single infected plant—a practice called roguing—prevents the disease from spreading through wind, rain splashes, or insects to the rest of your healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie tsei komekomei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akpata amɛhiɛ. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ shishiumɔ. Ebaatsi hela naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo kooloi amli kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Does rain make crop diseases spread faster across my farm?
ga: Ani nugbɔ haa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Yes, rain splashes disease spores from infected soil and leaves onto healthy plants. The damp air after rain also creates the ideal environment for fungi and bacteria to grow quickly.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ shwieɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ baai ni hela emɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ hu feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and turn yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the plant's juices and spread viruses. It can also happen when the soil is too dry or the weather is extremely hot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ tsei amli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa.

english: Many flowers fail to form fruit because heavy rains wash away pollen, insect pests destroy the blossoms, or fungal diseases infect the flowers before fruits can set.
ga: Fɔfɔi babaoo nyɛɛɛ awo yibii ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ etsumɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔii. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient. The plant automatically pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛya ŋwɛi baai ni miida lolo lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant the same crop on the same land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating with different crops starves these pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start spoiling just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ beni mikɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Cassava roots deteriorate quickly after harvest because injuries from digging allow air and rot organisms to enter. Processing or selling them within two to three days prevents this spoilage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. Yɛ pilamɔi ni jɛɔ ŋtayaa mli baa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ baanyɛ abote mli. Kɛ́ atsu he nii loo ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: Can pests attack my rice seeds under the ground before they even sprout?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua miŋmaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Yes, insects like mole crickets, ants, and soil grubs often eat seeds underground before they have a chance to germinate and grow above the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ kriket, ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yeɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my rice seeds failing to sprout even though I planted good quality seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ?

english: Hidden soil pests or birds might be eating the seeds beneath the ground; applying an early-stage protective treatment right after planting keeps these hidden pests away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi loo okpoi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ hebuu tsu nii mra yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Does spraying chemical medicine on the soil right after planting help my crop?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, spraying early creates a safe environment in the soil that kills insects before they can damage your unsprouted seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, mra be mli shwiemɔ Ehaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui ni ekwɛko lɛ.

english: How do I protect my newly planted field from insects hiding in the dirt?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ ni midu ehee lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: You can use specific pre-emergence or soil-applied pest chemicals right around planting time to clear out underground bugs before seeds start sprouting.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi dani dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛgbe shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi dani dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is it safe to spray chemical medicine on my rice field when I have only one week left until harvest?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashɛrɛ tsofai ashwie ŋmãa ŋmɔji anɔ? Beni eshwɛ otsi kome pɛ ni abaakpa nii lɛ?

english: Yes, but only if you use specific quick-breakdown chemicals designed for late-stage crops that kill the pests without leaving harmful chemical residues on your food.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ko ni fiteɔ nii oya ni afee aha tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii pɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do bugs attack my rice field when the grains are already fully grown and almost ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Maturing crops produce sweet, nutrient-rich grains that attract hungry pests like stink bugs and grain-eating insects right before harvest time.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmaa ni ŋɔɔ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmeii ni shãa mɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmaa dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: What should I do if insects suddenly swarm my rice field a few days before I harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji trukaa lɛ, ŋmeii ba mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli gbii fioo komɛi dani akpamɔ?

english: Inform your extension officer immediately so they can give you a fast-acting, short-duration chemical spray safe for crops close to harvest.
ga: Ha mɔ ni kwɛɔ ohiɛyaa nɔ lɛ ale amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni amɛnyɛ amɛfɔ tsofai ni tsuɔ nii kuku ni tsuɔ nii oya lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ ahe.

english: How long do I have to wait to harvest my crop after spraying pest medicine on it?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Every chemical has a safety waiting period called a Pre-Harvest Interval; some safe late-stage sprays allow harvest within a few days, while stronger ones require weeks.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɛɔ lɛ dani akpaa nii. Abaanyɛ akpa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ sɛɛ mli ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ ekomɛi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii babaoo lɛ biɔ otsii babaoo.

english: Why does the extension officer need to know the exact stage of my crop before recommending a pest spray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ ale be pɔtɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ dani amɛtsɔɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ?

english: Young seeds and mature grains handle chemicals differently; giving the wrong chemical at the wrong growth stage can burn young plants or make mature food unsafe to eat.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii kɛ ŋmaa ni eda lɛ tsuɔ tsofai ahe nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni ejaaa mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii loo eha tsei ni eda lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Can I use the same pest medicine for newly planted seeds that I use for mature crops ready for harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ dumɔwui ni adu ehee ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ni eda ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: No, early-stage sprays are meant for long-lasting soil protection, while late-stage sprays must break down quickly so the harvested grain is safe for human consumption.
ga: Dabi, shishijee tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ afite oya koni eha dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai niyenii.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen nutrients or are getting waterlogged. When maize lacks proper food in the soil, it cannot produce green chlorophyll, causing the lower leaves to yellow and die off first.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiye nitrogen loo nu eyi lɛ. Beni ŋmãa bɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Enyɛŋ ekɛ klorofil eŋɔli aba. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my tall maize plants fall over so easily whenever a heavy rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over, or lodge, when their roots are shallow or when stalks are thin from planting seeds too close together. Giving plants proper space and earthing up soil around the base strengthens the roots against wind.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ bafee bibioo kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ sũ ni bɔle eshishi lɛ, ewajeɔ eshishifãi lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: How can I tell when my corn is completely ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Corn is ready when the outer green husks turn brown and dry, the silks at the top turn dark, and pressing a seed kernel releases a firm or milky starch rather than clear water.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ. Siliki ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ. Ni kɛ́ anyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse yɛ nu ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: Officer, how far apart should I place my maize seeds when planting so they grow well?
ga: Official Kɛ́ adu lɛ, te esa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ato amɛhe kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting seeds about two feet apart between rows and one foot apart between plants ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbor.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ aaafee ninetalɔi enyɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ateŋ kɛ ninetalɔi 1 yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu.

english: Is it good for me to plant cassava together with maize on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, mixing them works well because maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the space later, giving you two harvests from one piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko yɛ sɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm land has lost its strength and needs manure or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Land loses its strength when the soil becomes hard and pale, rainwater washes away quickly without soaking in, and crops grow slowly with thin stems even when there is good rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛ́ ebatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni eboteee mli. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa blɛoo ni amɛyɛ tsei bibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can heavy rain actually harm my crops, or is more water always good for them?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ? Aloo ani nu babaoo hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be?

english: Too much water fills up all the air holes in the soil, effectively drowning the roots. Without air, roots rot and cannot feed the plant, causing leaves to turn yellow and wilt.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ayi obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my tender young seedlings wilt and drop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ miigboi ni amɛmiiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short roots that cannot reach deep groundwater. Under intense sun, leaves lose moisture faster than roots can drink, so the plant wilts to save water until the sun cools down.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛkɛ lɛ tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ koni amɛkɛ nu ato kɛyashi hulu lɛ baajɔ.

english: Officer, what causes small caterpillars to suddenly appear and eat holes in the middle of my maize leaves?
ga: Ofisa, mɛni ha nɛkɛ trukaa nɛɛ ba trukaa ni ŋmeii bibii ba ni amɛye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: Moths lay hidden eggs on the plant leaves, which hatch into hungry caterpillars like fall armyworms. They hide inside the center leaf whorl during the day to feed on fresh foliage away from the heat.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi fɔɔ amɛwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Enɛɛmɛi fɔɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ cutworms yɛ fɛ̃i be mli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Why do crops grown from seeds I saved from last year's harvest yield much less than new bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni ahe ehee lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from high-yielding crops lose their natural vigor and disease resistance in the next generation, whereas fresh certified seeds are specially bred to give strong growth every time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni afɔɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo dalɛ ni mli wa be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Why does my rice field need so much water to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rice thrives in flooded conditions because standing water suppresses weeds and keeps the root zone consistently moist, which helps the plant absorb essential soil nutrients effectively.
ga: Omɔ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni nu afua yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ejaakɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crops if the rain stops earlier than expected this season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: When water recedes too early, crops experience drought stress, which causes leaves to curl and drop, preventing flowers from developing into full grains or tubers.
ga: Kɛ nu lɛ ba shi oya tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baaná hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ dumɔwui loo bulbs ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does the soil in my farm dry out so quickly a few days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil low in organic matter, such as compost or decayed leaves, cannot hold moisture well, causing water to drain away or evaporate rapidly instead of staying available for crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egbo lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ loo etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-rice tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor water flow, preventing the plant from producing the chlorophyll it needs to grow strong and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ afee klorofil ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why does my crop seem to grow so slowly during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In early stages, plants spend most of their energy growing deep underground roots to anchor themselves and search for water before they start growing tall leaves above ground.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛdaraa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ koni amɛkɛma amɛhe shi ni amɛtao nu. Dani ebaaje baai lɛ akwɛmɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ

english: Why do pests and diseases attack my crops more heavily during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and warm weather create ideal conditions for fungal spores to spread rapidly and for insect eggs to hatch faster on tender crop leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Ni kooloi bibii afɔɔ oya yɛ tsei ahe baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing rice or if I should plant maize instead?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa loo esa akɛ madu ŋmãa moŋ?

english: Low-lying swampy areas or riverbeds that hold water are best for rice, whereas well-drained, higher land is ideal for maize because maize roots rot in standing water.
ga: He ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ shishi loo faai ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ ji hei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ. Yɛ be mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why is flooding a rice field helpful for controlling farm weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akudɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Most common farm weeds cannot breathe underwater and die when submerged, whereas rice plants are uniquely built to survive with their roots submerged in water.
ga: Okwaafoi amli jwɛi ni afɔɔ naa waa lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ nu shishi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu shishi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, abɔ ŋmãa tsei pɔtɛɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ebote nu mli.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in weak, thin plants with small yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Why are my crop yields getting smaller every year even though I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil, so resting the land or rotating crops is necessary to restore soil fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ he miihia koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden nutrient shortages in the ground.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava turning yellow and curling up into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on the sap of the plant leaves.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Whiteflies bibii ni yeɔ tsei baai amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do I know the right space to leave between my maize seeds when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing gives each maize plant enough room to take up soil nutrients, sunlight, and water without competing with its neighbors, leading to larger stalks and bigger cobs.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ akaŋ akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the soil is moist, so the roots can absorb the nutrients before the hot afternoon sun dries out the soil.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii dani shwane mli hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: What happens to my soil if I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases tailored to that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni etsɔ tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that bugs like weevils do not destroy it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato? Koni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii akafite lɛ.

english: Dry your maize completely until the grains are very hard, then store them in sealed, airtight containers or hermetic bags that cut off oxygen so insects cannot survive inside.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa loo vacuum bag mli, ni no ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ mli koni kooloi akahi mli.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture for me to start sowing seeds after the early rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball; if it holds together without leaking excess water and crumbles easily when gently tapped, the soil is ready for sowing.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔɔɔ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji akɛ ata he fioo lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why do my tomatoes rot quickly on the vine during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess humidity and wet soil during heavy rains create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like late blight and blossom-end rot to attack wet tomato fruits.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight kɛ blossom end rot ni baatutua tomato aduawai ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants natively adapted to the local soil, allowing them to steal soil nutrients, water, and light much faster than farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ la mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to build strong, green leaves. It can also happen when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi ni nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants have thin leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to protect them from harsh heat and keep the soil moist while their roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very thin and weak when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops have to fight one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy stretching upward to reach the light instead of growing thick stems and healthy fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsu nii ni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛtee la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ duɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ yiblii nɛ ngɛ he wami.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests that feed on maize to multiply in your field. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps rebuild soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmãa yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nibii amli.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry grass during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha he ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around the base of your plants, known as mulching, acts like an umbrella for the soil. It blocks the hot sun from evaporating moisture, keeps the roots cool, and reduces the need for frequent watering.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni afɔɔ amɛ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the leaves and center stems of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ tsei lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is commonly caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They crawl inside the funnel or center leaves of young maize plants to chew on the soft growth, which weakens the plant if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi loo amɛteŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa bibii ni eda lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Excess water in heavy soil fills up all the air spaces around the roots, effectively drowning them. This wet environment encourages fungal rot to attack and destroy the tubers before harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsii mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ nɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ dani akpa amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers can drop off if the plants suffer from extreme heat, lack of water, or if there are no insects like bees visiting the farm to pollinate the flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbo kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, nu bɛ, loo kɛji kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii eyaaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of leafy branches but very few pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo shi pepper yibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into growing leafy green branches instead of flowers and fruits. Plants need balanced food containing phosphorus to produce plenty of flowers and pods.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja ni fɔsfɔs yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my farm right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash the fertilizer away from the crop's root zone into nearby streams before the plants can drink it up. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist so the roots can absorb it properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted poultry manure helps the leaves regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloi ashishifã ni egbo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, keeps the ground cool and traps moisture so you do not need to water as often. It also blocks weeds from getting light and slowly breaks down into natural food for your plants.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. Ehaa jwɛi hu shɛɛɛ la he, ni ekwɛ̃ɔ fiofio. Efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa otsei lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or a sudden lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying a fertilizer high in phosphorus will help the plant hold onto its flowers so they can form peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni faaa trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔii lɛ ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my cassava produce very tall, leafy tops but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or grows in heavy shade, it uses all its energy to build leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo edaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛya shi koni ekɛdu shikpɔŋ shishi tsei.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wild weeds around my young crop plants even if I do not touch the crop itself?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie koo mli jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔle mitsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ? Kɛji mitaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe po?

english: Weeds act like silent thieves on your farm; they aggressively drink the water, steal soil nutrients, and block sunlight that your crop needs to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni efee dioo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu kɛ hiɛdɔɔ. Ju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni otsĩ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade from surrounding trees or temporary plantain plants to protect them and keep the air humid while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nuɔ la he ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ adɛŋ. loo plantains ni akɛwoɔ be kukuoo mli koni akɛbu kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he ni eha edɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber below, while keeping the leaves off the wet soil protects the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha tsei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have natural microbes in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. This extra food stays in the soil and feeds neighboring plants like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ niyenii ni akɛfataa he nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the exact same garden spot where I harvested peppers last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ abɔɔ ni mifo mi-peppers lɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Tomatoes and peppers are close relatives that suffer from the same soil-borne diseases and pests. Moving crops to different spots each season starves out pests left behind in the soil.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji wekumɛi ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yeɔ amɛ awui. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa hei srɔtoi Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hɔmɔ gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom end rot, happen when the plant cannot pull up enough calcium, usually because watering is irregular. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant move calcium smoothly into the fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhaa calcium lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce a lot of leaves but very few flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and thick green leaves instead of producing the flowers needed to make pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a woɔ fɔfɔi nɛ a kɛ peeɔ pods.

english: How far apart should I plant my bean seeds so they produce the best harvest?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-beans lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni maná yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces plants to fight for sunlight and soil food. Giving beans about 15 to 20 centimeters of space ensures every plant gets enough nutrients to produce healthy pods.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Peas ni akɛto he ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 15 kɛyashi 20 lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa.

english: Why do flowers drop off my bean plants before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or small pests attacking the blossoms cause stress to the plant, making it shed its flowers to conserve its remaining water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my bean leaves turn yellow instead of staying green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Bean leaves usually turn yellow when the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil, when the soil lacks key nutrients, or when root diseases prevent the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ bote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Be mli ni niyenii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni shishifã hela haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ eye niyenii

english: Why do crop leaves roll up tight during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the heat, which slows down water loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsei haa he ni hulutsoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do legume plants like beans make the soil better for future crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans have special root nodules that absorb nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into rich soil food. When the crop season ends, that natural nitrogen remains in the dirt to nourish the next crop.
ga: Beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni shwieɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni ehaa efeɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. Kɛ́ dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eya nɔ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant beans in the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot repeatedly allows pests and soil diseases that target that specific plant to multiply in large numbers while draining the exact same soil nutrients year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ. Enɛ baaha sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crop seeds too deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: A seed has only a limited amount of stored energy. If buried too deep, it exhausts all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil before reaching the light, causing it to die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli dani eshɛ la lɛ he. ha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if a dry spell happens right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji hɔmɔ ba beni adu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds require steady moisture to soften their outer shells and trigger growth. If the soil dries out completely after planting, the germinating seed dries up and dies before emerging from the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni eha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni eha amɛdara. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my crops when left in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?
