english: Weeds compete directly with your crops by stealing soil water, fertilizer, and light, leaving your actual crop plants weak, malnourished, and vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ sũ mli nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa, ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why does maize grow very well in some parts of Ghana but struggle on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana hei komɛi shi ekɛ naagbai kpeɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops react differently depending on your district's specific rain patterns, heat, and soil type. Some maize varieties require heavy, consistent rain like in the Ashanti region, while others are specially bred to survive shorter rainy seasons like in Northern Ghana.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ, dɔlɛ, kɛ sũ henɔ. Abɛi henɔi komɛi biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni enɛɔ daa, tamɔ yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu biɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa ni enɛ daa. Atsɔse amɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔ bei kukuji tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight. Taller shade crops like plantains or forest trees act as natural umbrellas, protecting delicate cocoa leaves from burning until the plants are old enough to handle the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry weather to save water and keep its roots alive underground. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha eshishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why are my corn plants staying very short with reddish-purple leaves along the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves and stunted growth usually mean the soil lacks phosphorus. This nutrient helps crops build strong root systems and grow tall, so low levels cause the plant to stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ eshɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ akpa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of yellow flowers but very few actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers without forming fruit if the weather gets too hot, if the soil lacks moisture, or if there are no insects around to move pollen within the flowers.
ga: Tomato baafɔ̃ ni ewooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni baanyɛ ajie pollen awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ bɛ

english: Why do fall armyworms suddenly appear and eat up my corn leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ je kpo ni amɛye mi-corn baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Moths lay hundreds of eggs on the undersides of leaves, and the young caterpillars hide deep inside the center of the corn plant where you cannot easily see them until they grow larger and eat fast.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi fɔɔ amɛwuji ohai abɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. Ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ. Onyɛŋ ona amɛ mlɛo kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛye nii oya.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds before they produce flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ dani amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Once weeds flower, they release hundreds of seeds into your soil. Clearing them early prevents those seeds from spreading and competing with your crops for water and plant food next season.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi lɛ fɔ lɛ Ebaajie dumɔwui ohai abɔ awo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi nakai dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii aka akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ tsei niyenii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root helpers that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, leaving behind natural food that helps the next maize crop grow strong.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ nyɛmɔi krɛdɛɛi ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni edara waa.

english: How do I know if it is the right time to plant my seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu tsei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground gets two or three good, heavy rains. A single early rain can deceive you, leaving the deep soil dry so that newly sprouted seeds wither if the rain stops for a week.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni naa wa waa, ni naa wa waa enyɔ loo etɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ alaka bo. Ha shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ agbi. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ baagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome.

english: Why do tiny insects hatch inside my stored maize grains even when I put them in a sealed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii No hewɔ lɛ efɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ tsu ko ni aŋã mli moŋ.

english: Weevil insects often lay invisible eggs inside the grain kernels while the corn is still in the field. If the grain is not dried thoroughly before storage, heat causes those eggs to hatch inside your barn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmaa lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baaha nakai ŋmeii lɛ afɔ yɛ otsu lɛ mli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly because the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for leaf growth. Adding well-decomposed manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps the leaves turn green and manufacture food for bigger cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores nutrients to the soil for the next planting season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know which cassava stem to cut and plant so it yields big tubers?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole ŋmei tso ni esa akɛ ofolɔ ni odu koni onine ashɛ ŋmeii wuji anɔ lɛ?

english: Choose strong stems from healthy, mature cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old. Cut the middle portion of the stem into pieces about 20 to 25 centimeters long with visible nodes, as these sprout faster and establish stronger roots.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli bibii ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 25 ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ ji akɛ, enɛɛmɛi baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaafee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Which kind of plantain sucker is best for me to dig up and plant in my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow, blade-like leaves and a large underground bulb—are best. They grow faster, resist diseases better, and yield heavier bunches than water suckers that have wide leaves early on.
ga: Sword shoots, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Amɛ daa oya. Helai ahewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui ni tsii fe nu mli tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: These are fall armyworms, which hide inside the growing center of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves. Controlling them early prevents them from destroying the growing point, which would otherwise stop the plant from making cobs.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil moist continuously helps the roots draw up calcium to keep the fruit healthy.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ calcium koni aduawai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep falling off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by heavy sunlight, lack of soil moisture, or poor nutrients. Providing adequate shade trees and mulching helps the plant retain flowers and convert them into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii ni esaaa ni enine shɛɔ nɔ Shade ni sa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to produce food, which travels down to swell the underground tuber into a large yam.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni egbɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli eshwa koni etsɔ ŋmeii agboi.

english: Planting peppers too close forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin with very few branches, producing fewer peppers overall.
ga: Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛkwɔ ni amɛhe tse ni amɛniji fioo pɛ yɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji chili feemɔ ni baa shi.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool and prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the hot sun, helping your young plants survive dry spells.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ye obua odumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I see small shoots growing at the bottom of my plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: These small shoots at the base are natural offshoots or suckers. If you feed the plant early with fertilizer, these shoots can grow strong and give you extra yields instead of competing with the main plant.
ga: Tso bibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli tso loo suckers. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ha tsei lɛ mra, Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ tso titri lɛ baabɔ akaŋ lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What should I do to fix weak shoots coming up around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: When small shoots appear around the base, it means the plant needs extra food to support new growth. Applying fertilizer early gives the roots the nutrients needed to strengthen those base shoots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii kroko he miihia tso lɛ koni eye ebua dalɛ hee. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Fertilizer should be applied early in the crop's growth cycle. Feeding the plant early helps establish strong roots and base growth so that you can reach harvest time within a few months.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ dalɛ be mli mra. Niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei mra Ebaaye ebua ni etswa shishifãi ni wa kɛ basal dalɛ ni eha bo kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: Will putting fertilizer early on my farm speed up when I can harvest?
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli mra Ani ebaanyɛ efee oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa nii?

english: Yes, giving your crops nutrients early in their growth helps them develop properly without delay, allowing you to begin harvesting within two to three months.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ha tsei kɛjɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe kwraa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojeɔ nikpamɔ shishi yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: How many months will I wait before I start harvesting my crops?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mabɔi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpamɔ?

english: With proper care and early fertilization, many short-cycle crops or secondary shoots begin yielding food for harvest within one to three months.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra lɛ, tsei babaoo ni shwereɔ kuku loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ baabɔi niyenii ni akɛbaakpa yɛ nyɔji kome kɛyashi etɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my fast-growing crops are ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Around two to three months after planting or shoot emergence, mature crops reach full size and show ready fruit or tubers, indicating it is time to start harvesting.
ga: Aaafee nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni adu loo ekwɛ̃. Tsei ni eda lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ he ni amɛjieɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii ni asaa he lɛ kpo. Etsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni abaaje nikpamɔ shishi.

english: Can the small plants growing at the base of my main crop give me food to harvest?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitso titri lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mi niyenii ni mikɛkpa?

english: Yes, if you nourish the main plant early with fertilizer, those base shoots will mature and produce crop yields within two to three months.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso titri lɛ mli mra. Nɛkɛ tsei bibii nɛɛ baadara ni amɛbaawo yibii yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops require fertilizer so early in their lifecycle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ eshihilɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Early fertilization ensures the plant has enough energy to develop its base structure and small shoots, fixing early growth weaknesses so you get a full harvest in one to three months.
ga: mra be mli fɔmɔ Ekwɛɔ koni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee eshishijee gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ eshishifãi bibii lɛ. Koni okɛsaa bɔjɔmɔi ni yɔɔ dalɛ oya mli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná okpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nyɔji kome kɛyashi etɛ mli.

english: Is it difficult work to manage short-season crops that mature in a few months?
ga: Ani ewa akɛ aaakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ nɔ?

english: Managing fast-maturing crops requires concentrated work early on—mainly applying fertilizer quickly and caring for base shoots—but the reward comes fast since you harvest within one to three months.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya lɛ akwɛmɔ biɔ nitsumɔ ni mli wa mra. Nɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ, amɛwoɔ amɛ fɔ oya ni amɛkwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ. Shi nyɔmɔwoo lɛ baa oya beni okpaa nii yɛ nyɔji kome kɛyashi etɛ mli lɛ.

english: What basic routine work do I need to perform to get a good harvest in three months?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee daa koni maná yibii kpakpai yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli?

english: The main tasks are monitoring new growth at the base of the plant, applying fertilizer early, and keeping the field clean so the crops can mature steadily for harvest in two to three months.
ga: E nitsumɔ titri ji ni ekwɛ nibii heei ni yaa hiɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli mra ni aha he lɛ he atse bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ be fɛɛ be kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within two to three years if they are well cared for, unlike older varieties that take up to five years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii enumɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily in strong sunlight. Planting shade plants like plantains alongside them keeps the soil moist and protects them from heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: It is normal for cocoa trees to shed many flowers. The tree naturally drops flowers it cannot support with its available water and nutrient levels to focus energy on a manageable amount of pods.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei baafɔ̃ babaoo. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni nyɛɛɛ atsu nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ ahe nii koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ ama fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop many of their leaves when the Harmattan starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tso lɛ baai babaoo fite beni Harmattan je shishi lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the tree's natural way of saving water. By shedding leaves during dry weather, the cocoa tree loses less moisture through evaporation and stays alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli Cacao tso lɛ mli nu fioo pɛ fiteɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ. ni ehiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning branches and clearing weeds helps air flow and reduces humidity, preventing the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo baa shi. Tsi gbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ naa

english: Why are the young shoots on my cocoa trees turning black and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: This damage is often caused by tiny insects called capsids or mirids that suck sap from young stems and leaves. Applying approved control measures during the right months protects young growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo myrids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ gbekɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ nyɔji ni sa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu gbekɛ lɛ dalɛ he.

english: Pruning off extra branches and unwanted shoots (chupons) actually helps the tree. It directs plant food to the flowering parts and allows sunlight to reach the tree, encouraging more pods to grow.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo (chupons) ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ niyenii ni akɛbaa fã ni fɔfɔii yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. ni oha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe Kanyaa ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛdara babaoo

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa seedlings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting trees too closely causes them to fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin trees with fewer pods and making it easier for diseases to spread between leaves.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la he. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛnáa ŋmeii fioo. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa baai lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do government-supplied cocoa seedlings perform better than seeds I take from my old farm pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii momoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Government extension offices distribute specially bred hybrid seeds that grow faster, tolerate diseases better, and yield significantly more pods than seeds saved from older trees.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ nitsumɔhe nine ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni ji tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ. Enyɛɔ helai anaa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni edara amli lɛ.

english: Why is my cocoa tree growing lots of heavy green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes the tree to invest energy into foliage instead of flowers. Using balanced fertilizer formulated specifically for flowering and pod development helps fix this balance.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ baai amli moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni afee pɔtɛɛ aha fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ahi shi.

english: If I plant a new variety of cassava on my farm, how long will it take before I can harvest it?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei henɔ hee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani akpa?

english: Most improved cassava varieties in Ghana mature within 9 to 12 months, whereas traditional varieties often take up to 15 to 18 months before the tubers are ready for harvesting.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, blema henɔi lɛ heɔ nyɔji 15 kɛyashi 18 dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Yam is mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up, indicating that the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eyitso lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when left under full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantain to protect them and keep the soil cool during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Extreme heat and dry soil stress tomato plants, causing the flowers to dry up and fall off before pollination can take place.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell from looking at my maize leaves if the crop needs more nutrients?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛtsɔ ŋmãa baai ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ akɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia tso lɛ?

english: If the lower leaves of your maize turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip toward the center, it usually means the plant is starving for nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do improved high-yielding seed varieties require more fertilizer than my local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni atsake lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe mimaŋ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: High-yielding varieties grow faster and produce much larger harvests, which means they consume soil nutrients at a much higher rate than traditional varieties.
ga: Nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii babaoo fe blema ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ.

english: Will planting cowpeas alongside my maize harm my maize crop?
ga: Ani cowpea ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye mi ŋmãa tso lɛ awui?

english: No, cowpeas actually help maize because their roots take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer while suppressing weeds.
ga: Dabi, cowpea yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, which damage the leaves and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwa tso lɛ mli.

english: When is the right time to plant my maize in southern Ghana for the major season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ yɛ prime season mli?

english: In southern Ghana, major season maize is best planted right after the rains become steady, usually between late March and mid-April.
ga: southern ghana Aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ March naagbee kɛ April teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do some of my bean seeds fail to sprout even after I water the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ nu ewo amɛnɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in the soil, if the ground is so flooded that the seeds rot, or if the seeds were stored improperly and lost their viability.
ga: Dumɔwui ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aahu kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ fite loo kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ etooo jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi dɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an important food for crop growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the maize the energy it needs to stay green and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmei hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava stems should be planted about one meter apart from each other. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and underground space to grow large, heavy roots.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe aaafee mita kome. Nɛkɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji ni tsii baakwɛ̃.

english: Why does rainwater collect and sit on top of my farm for days after a heavy storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ buaa ehe naa ni ekɛ ehe woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Water pooling on top of the ground means your soil is packed tightly or contains heavy clay, which stops water from sinking in. Adding organic compost or digging simple drainage ditches helps excess water flow away so crop roots do not rot.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni tsiɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekabote mli. Organic compost ni akɛbaafata he loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ mli nubu ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaakumɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteee.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stems before growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛmiitsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the plants receive irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and planting temporary shade crops can protect the blossoms from intense heat.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni adu tsei ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up tight during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves fold or turn away from direct sunlight during the hottest hours to reduce water loss. This is the plant's natural defense mechanism to keep itself cool and survive dry conditions.
ga: Akɛ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo koni eha ehe ajɔɔ ni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: How can I tell if my yam tubers are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines begin to turn yellow and dry up completely. This sign shows that the plant has stopped growing above ground and stored all its energy into the underground tuber.
ga: No mli lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa lɛ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young cocoa seedlings every few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mi cocoa tso bibioo lɛ daa No hewɔ lɛ otsii enyɔ komɛi he hia.

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, soil moisture, and sunlight from young cocoa trees. Regularly clearing weeds gives the young cocoa plants full access to these resources so they can grow faster and stronger.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa sũ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe awa.

english: What causes small round holes in my cabbage leaves, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo baa kaaba mli ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are caused by caterpillars or insects eating the plant. You can control them by handpicking caterpillars off the leaves early in the morning or by spraying safe biological pest treatments.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii loo koolooi ni yeɔ tso lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni oootsi kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ leebi maŋkpa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong rainstorms before the fruits are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbee shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli dani aduawai lɛ shwere kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy stem during strong winds. Mounding extra soil tightly around the base and propping up heavy trees with wooden poles prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi tso ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Okɛ sũ kroko ni fata he lɛ ato shishigbɛ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tsei ni akɛ tsei ebɔ he lɛ afi tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Is it better to plant pepper seeds directly into the main field or start them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu pepper dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Pepper seeds are tiny and delicate, so starting them in a protected nursery bed gives them the best chance to germinate safely. Once the seedlings grow strong after a few weeks, they can easily be transplanted into the main field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni abuɔ he lɛ haa pepper dumɔwui lɛ náa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa waa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli. Abaanyɛ ajie kɛya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: How do I know if my inherited family land is suitable for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miweku shikpɔŋ ni miná akɛ gboshinii lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cocoa thrives best in deep, fertile, and well-drained dark soil rich in organic matter. Land that previously supported dense forest trees or wild vegetation usually has the right moisture retention and soil depth for healthy cocoa root growth.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ekwɛɔ tsei anɔ yɛ kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli loo koo mli tsei amli lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ lɛ sa. Bɔni afee ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ

english: How far apart should I plant my young cocoa seedlings on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa seedlings should generally be planted about 3 meters by 3 meters apart (roughly 10 feet by 10 feet). This spacing ensures that mature trees have enough sunlight, air circulation, and root space to grow well without fighting for nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3 (aaafee ninetalɔi 10 x ninetalɔi 10). Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tsei ni eda lɛ náa hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ akaŋ.

english: What food crops can I plant together with my young cocoa without harming it?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii tsei manyɛ mikɛ mibi cocoa lɛ akwɛ ni miyeee lɛ awui?

english: Planting plantains, cocoyams, or cassava alongside young cocoa seedlings is beneficial because these food crops provide essential shade for the young cocoa while giving you food and income before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Plantain, cocoa loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa dumɔwui bibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ nɛkɛ niyenii tsei nɛɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo bibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani ajeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: My family land has very old cocoa trees on it; can I still get good yield from them?
ga: Kookoo tsei ni etsɛ waa yɛ miweku lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ani manyɛ maná sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai kɛjɛ amɛdɛŋ lolo?

english: Very old cocoa trees naturally produce fewer pods over time and become vulnerable to diseases. While proper pruning and fertilizer can boost yields slightly, it is often best to gradually replace old trees with new hybrid seedlings for higher long-term harvests.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni egbɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ, ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ fioo moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooŋɔ blɛoo. Okɛ tsei momoi lɛ atsake tsei heei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to prune or trim branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mikoo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, weak, or diseased branches, allowing sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree. This simple practice keeps the tree healthy, reduces pest habitats, and directs the plant's energy into producing more cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni egbɔjɔ, loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shi ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds on my newly planted cocoa farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mafo jwɛi yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni midu ehee lɛ mli?

english: During the first two years, young cocoa seedlings cannot easily compete with aggressive weeds. Clearing weeds every 2 to 3 months ensures that weeds do not steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from your young crop.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Cocoa dumɔwui kɛ jwɛi ni mli wa waa lɛ yeee akaŋ mlɛo. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ, ehaa jwɛi lɛ ejuuu nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Traditional cocoa varieties take about 4 to 5 years to bear fruit, but modern high-yielding hybrid varieties start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years if provided with proper shade, moisture, and soil nutrients.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi amli kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani ewoɔ yibii, shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baaje shishi amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, kɛji akɛ amɛná hulutsoo, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa.

english: Yellowing leaves on young cocoa are usually a sign of too much direct sunlight, lack of adequate shade, drought stress, or nutrient deficiencies in the soil. Adding temporary shade plants like plantains can protect them from harsh sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ. Shade ni sa ni bɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa shade be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is at the start of the rainy season when the soil is soft and moist. Moist soil helps the roots absorb the nutrients quickly so the plant can grow strong and form healthy flower buds.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya.

english: Why do many tiny flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo gbee shi kɛjɛ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: It is normal for a cocoa tree to shed many flowers due to factors like dry weather, nutrient lack, or poor insect pollination. Maintaining healthy soil moisture and protecting natural pollinating insects helps more flowers turn into full pods.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nibii tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ahewɔ. niyenii ni esaaa loo kooloi bibii ni ehiii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahebuu yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow after germination?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your young crops are suffering from a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Giving them fertilizer early provides the essential food they need to produce green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Eji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ dalɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to give fertilizer to my crops right around planting time instead of waiting until later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔ nii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni miduɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings need quick access to soil nutrients right at the start to grow a deep root system. If you wait too long, their early growth gets stunted, which permanently lowers your harvest.
ga: Ehe miihia ni dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya kɛjɛ shishijee koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji omɛ be kakadaŋŋ Amɛ mra be mli dalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ baaha nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: What happens to my crops if I put too much chemical fertilizer near their stem at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata tso lɛ he yɛ be kome mli?

english: Applying too much fertilizer directly next to young crops can scorch or burn their tender roots because the high salt concentration pulls water out of the plant, causing it to wilt or die.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi bibii lɛ aba loo eshã amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei ni fa babaoo lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha egbi loo egbo.

english: How do my crops react differently when I feed them chemical fertilizer compared to animal manure?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ha amɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Chemical fertilizer gives your crops a quick burst of nutrients for fast leaf and stem growth, while animal manure releases food slowly over time while improving the soil's ability to hold water.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya koni amɛba kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adara oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei jieɔ niyenii blɛoo. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before any small fruits can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai bibii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience heat stress or when the soil lacks vital nutrients like phosphorus and potassium needed to hold and develop the fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni he hiaa koni amɛhiɛ aduawai ni amɛwo lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing huge green leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of storing energy in the roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even if the ground was watered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu po

english: On very hot days, young leaves lose water into the hot air faster than their small roots can drink it from the soil, causing temporary wilting until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ, baai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe shishifãi bibii. koni enyɛ enu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster and taller than my main crop right after I fertilize the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb nutrients faster than crop seedlings, so if you do not clear them early, they will steal the fertilizer meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ ojieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli dani be ni ato lɛ ashɛ. Jwɛi hu baaju ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and yellow after a heavy rainfall even though the land was recently fed with nutrients?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ená niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Heavy downpours can wash away soluble nutrients from the topsoil deeper into the ground where small root systems cannot reach them yet, leaving your crops hungry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ mli. ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii.

english: When crops are crowded, they compete against each other for sunlight and soil food, stretching upward to reach light instead of using their energy to build thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔmɔ la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct heat. Large trees provide natural shade and keep the soil moist, giving young cocoa the protection it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa abuɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The maize plant moves its remaining nutrients up to the growing ears, causing the bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa toi ni miida lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very leafy and tall but produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai kakadaji ni kɛlɛ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen or excessive shade causes cassava to spend all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo haa yucca lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early stops the virus from damaging your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Mra be mli ni oooye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ Ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Planting too close makes crops fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce much smaller fruits and lower total yields.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii bibii kwraa kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni baa shi.

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so the soil stays wet longer, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ ni eha jwɛi akaye oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. Leaving vines on the hot ground increases their risk of fungal disease and reduces tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ hu baa shi.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry heat spell that can scorch young sprouts. Waiting for the rains to become steady ensures seeds get continuous moisture to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni abaamɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak side branches so the plant doesn't waste energy on useless stems. This directs water and nutrients straight into growing larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baatsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa tree roots grow deep into the ground, and how does that help the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Deep and large roots help the cocoa tree anchor firmly in the soil and reach deep underground water and nutrients during dry seasons, keeping the tree strong and healthy.
ga: Shishifãi wuji ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ ni enáa shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ

english: How do I make sure the soil supports strong root growth for my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi-kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: You can ensure strong root growth by planting in soft, deep, well-draining soil, clearing hard rocks, and adding organic matter or fertilizer to nourish the young roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona nɔmimaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ dumɔ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ tɛi ni wa ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná hewalɛ

english: Can planting crops too close together affect how their roots grow?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, planting trees too close causes their roots to fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil, which stunts root development and reduces your overall harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni aaadu kɛbɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi.

english: How can pests spread from a neighbor's farm to my cocoa trees?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya mi cacao tsei lɛ amli?

english: Pests like capsids and mealybugs can easily crawl, fly, or be carried by wind and insects from nearby infected farms to your healthy trees if proper pest control is not maintained.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids kɛ mealybugs baanyɛ atsɔ, afo, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii aŋɔ amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ anaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa

english: Leaf yellowing and curling are often caused by sap-sucking pests like capsids or insects that feed on the plant's vital nutrients, weakening the whole tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: What should I do if I notice pests damaging my cocoa trees for the first time?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina akɛ ŋmeii miifite mi-cacao tsei lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa?

english: Inspect your trees immediately to identify the specific pest, prune away badly damaged branches or pods, and apply approved sprays before the problem spreads across your whole farm.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji loo ŋmeii ni efite waa lɛ. Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What makes cocoa trees look healthy and produce plenty of pods?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Healthy cocoa trees need a good balance of shade, regular weeding, well-nourished soil, and protection from pests and diseases to grow strong leaves and produce abundant pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hia hulutsoo ni ja. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai atsimɔ Koni baai lɛ awa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo

english: How do I know if a farm is too big for me to manage by myself?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔ ko da tsɔ ni mi diɛŋtsɛ manyɛ makwɛ nɔ?

english: If you struggle to finish weeding, pruning, and pest control on time across all your land, the farm is likely too big for one person and needs additional farm hands or division into smaller plots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ona naagba yɛ jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ oshikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ he. Ekolɛ ŋmɔ nɛɛ da tsɔ kɛha mɔ kome ni ehe baahia ni aná ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi krokomɛi loo aja mli awo shikpɔji bibii amli.

english: Why is it important to cut away extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo niji krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unproductive branches, allowing fresh air and sunlight to flow through the tree, which prevents diseases and helps the plant send energy into growing pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I bring back an old cocoa farm that has been neglected for a long time?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔji momo ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ?

english: Restoring an old farm requires clearing overgrown weeds, pruning diseased branches, controlling pests with appropriate sprays, and replanting dead spots with new, high-yielding cocoa seedlings.
ga: Ni aaasaa ŋmɔ momo ko ekoŋŋ lɛ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ. Niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ Pest Control kɛ Proper Sprays kɛ hei ni egboi lɛ adumɔ kɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for growth, or that excessive water is sitting around the roots and preventing them from breathing.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ abɛi bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri kɛha dalɛ. Aloo nu babaoo feɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaaa amɛmu.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look green and healthy above ground but produce empty shells with no nuts inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e pee ngmɔkɔ nɛ nɔ́ ko be mi nɛ nɔ́ ko be mi.

english: Groundnuts need calcium in the topsoil to fill out their pods; if the soil lacks calcium or is too hard for the pegs to penetrate, the plant grows green leaves but fails to form seeds.
ga: Calcium he miihia ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo ewa tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ, Tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli shi enyɛɛɛ ewo dumɔwui.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become watery and spoil quickly when I harvest them during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During heavy rains, cassava roots absorb excess water from the ground, which lowers their starch content and speeds up rotting once they are removed from the soil.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves inward to protect themselves from losing water through evaporation under intense sun, and they usually relax again when the evening cools down.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu akafite yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni bei pii lɛ, ekɛ ehe jɔɔ ehe ekoŋŋ kɛ́ edɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my pepper plants drop off as soon as the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ kɛkɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes soil-dwelling fungi onto the lower leaves, creating damp conditions that cause leaf spot diseases, which forces the plant to drop its leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni kɛ leaf spot hela baa. ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they are stressed by long dry spells, excessive shade, or insect pests like mirids that feed on the delicate stems of new blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Shade babaoo loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen ni yeɔ fɔfɔi heei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do pests attack my farm more when I plant only one crop on the entire field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When you grow single crops across a whole farm, pests that prefer that crop can feed and multiply easily without natural barriers or different plants to slow them down.
ga: Kɛji odu tso henɔ kome yɛ ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii ni biɔ tsei ni tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye niyenii ni amɛfɔ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ ni adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii loo tsei krokomɛi ni baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce a shoot after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi plantain tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers pause growth while their roots recover from being cut and moved; if planted in hard soil without enough moisture or organic matter, root recovery takes even longer.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ he waaa kɛji afo amɛ ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ ahe tsakemɔ baanyɛ ahe be babaoo po.

english: How do I know if my land is fertile enough for planting without paying for laboratory soil tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu nii yɛ mli ni miwooo shikpɔŋ lɛ he kaa he nyɔmɔ yɛ laboratorio mli?

english: Fertile soil usually has a dark color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well after rain, and shows active earthworms or soft decaying plant leaves near the surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni ejieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ahe baai ni egboi ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ akpo.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants with strong, wide root systems that react instantly to water, allowing them to suck up nutrients faster than newly introduced farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni kɛ nu bote mli lɛ tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛba lɛ.

english: Can I harvest my pepper crops while they are still green, or do I have to wait until they turn red?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa pepper tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔji lolo lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi amɛbaafee tɔrɔmɔɔ?

english: You can harvest pepper while it is green or wait until it turns red. Green peppers are fresh and great for immediate cooking, while red peppers are fully ripe, sweeter, and much better suited for drying and long-term storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmeii be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lolo loo omɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Chili eŋɔli lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ ehee ni ehi kɛha nihoomɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi chili tsuru lɛ, eshɛre kwraa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my green peppers change color to red on the plant as time goes on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-chili eŋɔli lɛ feɔ tsuru yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Color change is a natural sign of ripening. As the pepper fruit matures from green to red, its natural sugars develop, its seeds fully mature, and it becomes ideal for processing or seed saving.
ga: Su tsakemɔ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ egbɔ. Kɛji akɛ pepper aduawai lɛ shwere kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee etsuru mli lɛ E-adebɔɔ mli sugars lɛ baaje kpo. Edumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa. ni ehi kɛha dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔ loo ni akɛtoɔ

english: What is the best way to dry my harvested peppers so they do not rot?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ koni amɛkafite?

english: Spread your harvested peppers evenly on clean mats or raised drying racks in full sunlight. Proper airflow and strong sunlight quickly remove moisture, preventing mold and rot.
ga: Jaa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Okɛto tsɔne ni he tse loo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ nɔ ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa

english: How can I keep my fresh peppers from spoiling quickly if I cannot sell them right away?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni chili heei lɛ akafite oya kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ be naa?

english: Keep fresh peppers in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated space away from direct heat. If you cannot sell them within a few days, drying them in the sun is the best way to prevent total loss.
ga: Kɛ chili ŋmɔŋ lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ onyɛɛɛ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ, Amɛgbimɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nibii ni baafite kwraa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do dried peppers break and crumble easily when I roll or crush them in my hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ chili ni egbi lɛ fãa ni efoɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛ minine shwie nɔ loo mikɛshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying removes almost all the water from the pepper flesh and skin, making it brittle. This low moisture content is what allows the pepper to be easily crushed or ground without sticking together.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ loo kɛ ehewolo lɛ mli lɛ. Ha chili lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa shi nɛɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsɔ loo aaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛɛɛ he.

english: Why do some farmers grind their dried peppers into powder instead of selling them fresh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ chili ni egbi lɛ nɔ amɛfeɔ powda yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahɔ̃ɔ lɛ ehee lɛ?

english: Grinding dried pepper into powder dramatically extends its shelf life and allows you to package it for sale during off-seasons when fresh pepper is scarce and market prices are high.
ga: Kɛ́ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ afee lɛ powda lɛ, ebaaha ehi shi be babaoo. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ okɛwoɔ kotoku mli koni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, be mli ni ewa akɛ aaana ŋmɔtɔ hee ni jara wa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: How does drying pepper help me if I want to prepare black pepper sauce like shito?
ga: Te chili ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji miisumɔ ni mafee Shito-style black pepper ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Dried pepper has very little water content, which stops spoilage and allows the pepper to absorb frying oil and local spices properly, giving shito its dark color, long storage life, and rich taste.
ga: Nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ chili ni egbi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ kpaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ fɔ ni akɛshãa nii kɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa Shito feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ su mli. Shihilɛ kakadaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa

english: What is the difference between making pepper flakes and grinding pepper into fine powder?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni afeɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Pepper flakes are coarsely crushed pieces of dried pepper skin and seeds, while powder is finely ground. Both allow you to package and sell your crop in different forms to suit what local buyers want.
ga: Pepper flakes ji pepper ŋmɔji kɛ dumɔwui ni egbi ni agbɛlɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ be mli ni powda lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ kotoku mli ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ̀i srɔtoi anɔ koni ekɛ nɔ ni maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Does drying hot pepper reduce its hotness when used for cooking?
ga: Ani okpo hiŋmɛi nɔ ŋmeii ni agbiɔ lɛ baaha la lɛ aba shi kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii homɔ mli?

english: No, drying does not reduce heat. Removing the water actually concentrates the natural spice, meaning dried pepper can taste just as hot as fresh pepper while lasting much longer.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ehaaa hulutsoo lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ ojie nu lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, chili ni egbi lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔ babaoo tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. kɛ pepper hee shi ehiɔ shi be babaoo hu

english: Is it better for me as a farmer to sell my peppers fresh or to process them first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mi akɛ okwaafonyo lɛ mahɔ̃ɔ chili hee loo matsu he nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Selling fresh green pepper brings fast cash right after harvest, but processing pepper by drying or grinding protects you from low market prices and gives you a product you can store until prices rise.
ga: Bell peppers heei ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha aná shika oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi pepper ni oootsu he nii kɛtsɔ egbimɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ buɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ jara ni baa shi lɛ he. Ni ehaa okɛ nibii lɛ toɔ ohe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ejara lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and dry out quickly under direct, hot sunlight. Keeping or planting shade trees protects them from harsh heat and retains soil moisture until the crops grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni naa wa waa baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to produce larger, healthier yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I bury them deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Burying seeds too deeply uses up all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil before they reach the surface and sunlight, causing them to rot underground.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afuɔ amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, leaving space for the slower-growing cassava to expand and mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa ni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young corn usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding organic compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and feed the plant to produce good cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ organic compost loo nitrogen fertilizer fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha tso lɛ niyenii koni ekɛ cob kpakpa aba.

english: Why is it bad to wait until weeds grow tall before I clear them from my crop fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mamɛ ni jwɛi lɛ aya hiɛ dani majie amɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Tall weeds have already stolen most of the fertilizer, water, and nutrients from the soil, leaving your crops weak and stunted even after you finally weed.
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ eju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be mli ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ efo mli po sɛɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which hide inside the young leaves to eat the tender growth; checking your farm early and applying recommended treatments into the leaf funnel controls them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai bibii amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni edara lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii yɛ baai amli koni akɛkudɔ amɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when exposed to extreme heat or water stress to save energy, or when excess nitrogen makes the plant grow stems and leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ wo dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ mli koni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Aloo beni nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I remove small side branches from my tomato plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Shi tomato tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Removing small side branches, known as suckers, directs the plant's food and energy into developing bigger, healthier tomato fruits rather than unnecessary extra stems.
ga: Niji bibii ni yɔɔ afã, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ ajiemɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo je tso kpahi nɛ a he hia we ɔ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Spreading dry grass, or mulching, shades the soil from direct heat, preventing soil water from evaporating quickly and keeping the root zone moist for much longer.
ga: Mulch ni egbi loo mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger trees or plantains because direct sunlight scorches their leaves, making them turn yellow and dry up before the roots can establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up toward the sunlight so they can make food efficiently, which directs energy downward to help the subterranean yam tuber grow larger.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli koni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ baa shi.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen; it takes nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Ekɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer tricks the cowpea plant into spending all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ lakaa cowpea tsei lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when there is heavy rain for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil; when soil remains waterlogged for too long, the roots suffocate and fungal diseases develop that rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaaná tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during intense heat to reduce their surface area and prevent excess water loss through evaporation, expanding back to normal when it cools down.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni fa fe nine ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. ni ebaagbɛ eshwa ekoŋŋ kɛya bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ edɔ.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in standing water while maize dies in the same conditions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa gboɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni tamɔ nɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels that transport oxygen from the leaves down to the roots under water, whereas maize roots suffocate when flooded.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli lɛ yaa. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu shwie amɛnɔ.

english: When temperatures get too high or water is scarce, tomato plants experience heat stress and shed their flowers to conserve moisture and survival energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa Tomato tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hulutsoo kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ wala nɔ lɛ he.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain stalk for soil nutrients and water, so removing them allows the main stem to produce a much bigger bunch.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii ni da kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I cut off all the green lower leaves of my oil palm tree while harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ fɛɛ kɛ́ mikpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Green leaves function like solar panels that produce energy for the tree; removing healthy leaves starves the oil palm and reduces future fruit yield.
ga: Baai eŋɔlii tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye mu tso lɛ, ni ebaaha yibii ni ebaawo wɔsɛɛ lɛ aba shi.

english: How do I know when my maize is dry enough to harvest from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When maize is mature and ready, the outer leaves turn brown and dry, and the kernels become hard. You can test by pressing a kernel with your fingernail; if it leaves a deep mark or feels soft, the maize still contains too much water and needs more drying time before harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ onineshi ŋmei lɛ ni ooonyɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji eshi okadii ni mli kwɔ loo enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ nu babaoo lolo ni ehe miihia be babaoo ni ekɛgbi dani akpa.

english: Why does my harvested corn get warm and start rotting when I leave it in a heap?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔɔ ni ebɔi fitemɔ beni mishiɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn is still living tissue that holds trapped water. When piled high, air cannot flow through, so heat and wetness build up inside the pile, creating the perfect warm environment for mold and bacteria to multiply and spoil the crop.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ ji fãji ni hiɛ ka lolo ni hiɛɔ nu. Kɛ́ ŋtayaa lɛ nɔ kwɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ koni amɛshwere ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What makes maize go bad inside a storage silo after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa fiteɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ mli beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If maize is stored inside a silo while it still contains internal moisture, that trapped water evaporates and creates humidity inside the dark, sealed space. This damp air causes mold to grow and encourages storage pests like weevils to multiply.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to ŋmãa mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo lɛ, Nu ni amɔmɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa he ni yɔɔ duŋ ni afo mli lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii baa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe, tamɔ ŋmeii, hewalɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why is it risky to store wet corn right after shelling it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Shelled corn packs tightly together, leaving very little space for air movement. If the kernels are still damp, the trapped moisture heats up rapidly, causing black or white mold to spread throughout the entire bag in just a few days.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa ni ajie lɛ lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa gbɛ fioo ko pɛ eshwɛɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aya. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii diji loo eyɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa kotoku lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my dried maize kernels turn black or powdery during storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ ekomɛi batsɔ ediŋŋ loo ebatsɔ powder beni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: The powdery texture and dark spots are caused by mold growth and insects like weevils eating the inside of the kernel. This happens when the grain was put into storage with dampness still inside or kept in a room with humid air.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ powder ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa ji ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ adalɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo. loo okɛto tsu ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli

english: What happens to my corn if I leave it standing on the farm too long during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: If corn remains on the stalk during heavy rains, water gets trapped inside the protective husks. The excess water can cause the kernels to start sprouting fresh green shoots right on the cob or rot on the plant before you can collect it.
