ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa hi tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Nu baatsi ŋmãa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo amɛgboi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: How does sun drying help protect my harvested grain from spoiling?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo be buɔ mikpamɔ lɛ he koni ekafite?

english: Sunlight draws out the hidden moisture inside each grain. Removing this water starves bacteria and mold, preventing them from growing, which allows you to keep the harvested grain safe in storage for many months.
ga: Hulu la jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli lɛ kpo. Nu nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ odumɔwui ni okpa lɛ toɔ shweshweeshwe ni okɛtoɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why does my stored corn develop a sour smell after just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ ŋmɔɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A sour smell is a sign that bacteria and fungi are actively breaking down the wet starch inside the grain. This fermenting process happens when damp corn is kept in an enclosed space without proper airflow or sufficient pre-drying.
ga: Nɔ ni mli edɔ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii miifite ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛ nɛɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ lɛ to he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli loo egbiɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers use mechanical dryers instead of drying corn on the open ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛgbiɔ amɛŋmei lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛaagbi amɛŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Mechanical dryers blow warm air directly through large volumes of grain to dry them quickly and evenly. Spreading corn on the ground relies on sunny weather, takes longer, and exposes the crop to dirt, rain, insects, and animals.
ga: Tsɔnei ni akɛgbiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmaa babaoo mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛgbi oya ni amɛfee ekome. Abɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be. Eheɔ be babaoo ni ehaa tsei lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nugbɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ kooloi ahe

english: Can I put newly harvested cobs directly into a closed sack for storage?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni akpa ehee lɛ awo kotokui ni agbe naa lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛto?

english: No, fresh cobs carry moisture that needs to evaporate first. Sealing wet cobs inside a sack traps dampness, causing the corn to sweat, sprout, and develop dangerous molds that ruin the harvest.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔtɔ ni esa akɛ efo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ wo kotoku mli lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa abele shwieɔ latsaa, ekwɛ̃ɔ, ni enáa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that scorch easily in strong sunlight. They need shade trees or plantain plants grown beside them to act as natural sunshades until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when we get too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave water standing in the soil for days, the roots drown from a lack of air, allowing rot-causing fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves up toward sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground helps the plant make more energy for growing large tubers while protecting the leaves from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni baa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ hu ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my plantain stem snap or fall over when the fruit bunch grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akuu lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are made of soft leaf sheaths rather than hard wood, making them weak under heavy weight. As the fruit bunch grows heavier, strong winds or the fruit's weight can easily tip the plant over unless it is supported with a wooden prop.
ga: Akɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ feɔ plantain tsei lɛ, shi jeee tso ni wa. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ tsɔne ni tsii fiɔ esɛɛ Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ mli wa Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo aduawai lɛ tsiimɔ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ atsɔ ŋwɛi oya. ja akɛ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from under the leaves, or by viruses spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ ashishijee naa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when the plant experiences drought stress. Without stable moisture and moderate temperatures, the flowers fail to form fruit and drop off.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the plants decay, they leave this nitrogen behind as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei fite Amɛshiɔ nitrogen yɛ amɛsɛɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mitso titri lɛ miifee mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with crops for the same water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. When weeds surround your crop, they consume the nutrients first, leaving your crop starved and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ beni jwɛi ebɔle onibii ahe lɛ. Amɛbaaye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves and leaving powdery sawdust inside the central leaf shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmãa ni afee lɛ powder yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by stem borers or armyworms feeding inside the growing shoot. They chew through the young curled leaves and leave behind frass (sawdust-like waste), which weakens the plant stem if not controlled.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji stem borers loo cutworms ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi. (sũi ni tamɔ ŋmei) ni baaha tso lɛ shishi afee gbɔjɔmɔ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if the oil palm seedlings I am buying will actually give me good fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mu ni miheɔ lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You should buy certified seedlings directly from accredited agricultural research centers or official government nurseries like CSIR-OPRI. Seedlings bought from roadside sellers often look healthy at first but may turn out to be wild varieties that produce thin flesh, thick shells, and very little oil after years of waiting.
ga: Esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ hei ni awo he odase loo nɔyeli dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei tamɔ CSIR-OPRI. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe yɛ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli. Shi ebaanyɛ ebatsɔ koo mli tsofa ko ni woɔ loo ni mli tseee, ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɔ fioo ko pɛ yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛmɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it better to buy government-researched crop seeds instead of saving seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ epɛi mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahere dumɔwui kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Researched seeds are specifically bred in laboratories to resist local diseases and yield maximum crop output. When you save and plant seeds from hybrid crops you harvested, the new plants often lose those superior qualities, resulting in weaker crops and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akwɛ mli lɛ amli yɛ laboratori lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛte shi ewo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ aba. Beni okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid tsei ni okpaa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni oduɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei heei laajeɔ nakai sui ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: What is the difference between the hard-shell palm fruit and the soft-shell palm fruit?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei ni hewolo wa kɛ ŋmei ni hewolo yɔɔ blɛoo teŋ?

english: The hard-shell variety (called Dura) has a thick shell with very little palm oil flesh inside. The soft-shell variety (called Tenera) is a high-yielding hybrid bred by scientists to have a very thin shell and a thick outer layer rich in oil, making it much more profitable for farmers.
ga: Henɔi ni amɛhe wa (ni atsɛɔ amɛ dura) lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli wa, ni ŋmei fɔ fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ emli. Softshell henɔ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ Tenera) lɛ ji tso ni jeŋ nilelɔi kwɛɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Eyɛ ŋmei ni mli tse waa kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni mli tse ni fɔ eyi mli obɔ. Ehaa okwaafoi náa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo

english: Why do some farmers invest heavily in oil palm but end up losing all their money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ amɛshika babaoo woɔ ŋmei fɔ mli shi amɛfiteɔ amɛshika fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Farmers often lose money when they plant unverified seed varieties that produce low oil yields, or when they do not give the trees proper fertilizer, water, and weed control during their early growing years. Without good management and right seed selection, palm trees will not produce enough fruit to cover costs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi laajeɔ shika kɛ́ amɛdu dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ mu fioo. Aloo kɛ́ amɛwooo tsei lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, nu, kɛ jwɛi kudɔɔ tsei lɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ahala dumɔwui ni ja lɛ, Palm tsei lɛ wooo yibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsu shika he nii.

english: Why do oil palm farms in other countries produce so much more oil than ours in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ jieɔ mu babaoo fe wɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: High-producing countries use improved high-yielding hybrid seeds, follow strict fertilizer application schedules, maintain exact spacing between trees, and prune regularly. When we combine high-quality hybrid seedlings with modern care practices, our soil and climate can produce equal yields.
ga: Maji ni feɔ nibii babaoo lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni afee lɛ srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nyiɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa sɛɛ. Ha tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ko ahi shi. ni ŋmɔɔ daa Kɛ wɔkɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ji hybrid kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kwɛmɔ fata he lɛ Wɔshikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo ni tamɔ amɛhe.

english: Why does my young oil palm seedling take so long to start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees spend their first three to four years focusing energy underground to grow a strong root system and a sturdy trunk. The plant must build a strong physical structure first so it can support the weight of heavy fruit bunches in the future.
ga: Mu tsei kɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa kɛ tso ni wa. Esa akɛ tso lɛ ama gbɔmɔtsoŋ tsɔne ni mli wa klɛŋklɛŋ dani enyɛ ekwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ amli tsiimɔ nɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my oil palm tree turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks important soil nutrients like potassium or nitrogen, or that it is stressed from drought. The tree deliberately sheds its older lower leaves to conserve food and water for the young, growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen. aloo hɔmɔ kɛbaa Tsei tsɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛto niyenii kɛ nu he amɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do oil palm trees produce fewer fruit bunches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees need large amounts of water to form heavy fruit. When water is scarce during dry weather, the tree enters a protective survival phase, delaying the growth of new flower buds and producing fewer or smaller fruit bunches until rains return.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia oil palm tsei koni amɛwo yibii ni tsii. Beni nu faaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ baabote wala yiwalaheremɔ mli. Ehaa fɔfɔi heei ni baa lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. ni amɛwoɔ aduawai akui fioo loo bibii kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What happens if I plant my palm trees too close to each other on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When palm trees are planted too close together, their broad leaves overlap and shade each other, blocking necessary sunlight. Their roots also fight for nutrients and water, causing the trees to grow tall and slender while bearing very few, small fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo be lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Amɛshishifãi lɛ hu wuɔ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ aduawai bibii bibii.

english: What is the best time of year for me to plant new palm seedlings in my field?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant palm seedlings is at the beginning of the major rainy season. This gives the young roots plenty of water and time to settle deep into the soil before the harsh dry season begins, giving the plant a much higher chance of survival.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa nu kɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛyahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize plants need to grow strong and green. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa akwɛ̃ waa ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni nitrogen fa yɛ mli lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: What benefit does adding animal manure bring to my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Animal manure feeds your soil with essential nutrients, helps the soil retain water longer during dry spells, and improves soil structure so plant roots can spread easily.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain leaves act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which direction to insert cassava stems into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the leaf buds along the cassava stem cutting. Always plant the stem with these small buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the leaves can sprout properly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ni afo lɛ mli fɛɛ. Dumɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be koni baai lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch sunlight for energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil to prevent diseases and helps the underground yam tubers grow much larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛha hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni hela akabote mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early prevents weeds from choking your young crops and stunting their growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi jwɛi ni tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anaa lɛ anaa ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Providing steady moisture directly at the root zone helps the flowers stay attached and set healthy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be ha yɛ shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves look droopy and wilted during the hot afternoon sun even if the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, pepper leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. This temporary wilting is a protective reaction, and the plants usually recover by evening as temperatures cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ shwiemɔ ni baa be kukuoo nɛɛ ji nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with powdery dust inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli edɔ kɛ sũ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding on the tender inner leaves. Catching them early and applying suitable control methods helps protect your corn yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Ni gbɛi ni sa ni oootsɔ nɔ okwɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-abele ni ooofee lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I visit and check on my field every day instead of leaving them alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miyasara miŋmɔji lɛ ni mikwɛ mli daa gbi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: Regular field visits help you spot early signs of weeds, pest attacks, or dry soil before they damage your crops, allowing you to take quick action to keep plants healthy.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ saramɔi ni afeɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona jwɛi lɛ ahe okadii mra. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite onibii Ehaa ofeɔ nɔ ko oya koni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my delicate young tomato seedlings die when I transplant them into the main field under bright sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have fragile roots that get heat-shocked under direct midday sun. Transplanting them late in the afternoon or providing temporary shade helps them settle into the soil without drying out.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa amɛdɔɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shwane mli loo aha amɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly and matures later. Planting them together gives you two different food harvests from one plot without the crops competing for the same space at the same time.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Yɛ ŋmei gbɛfaŋ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo ni ehiɛɔ blɛoo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni tsei kɛ amɛhe akaŋ yɛ he kome yɛ be kome mli

english: Why do my corn plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough strength to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my crops wilt during dry periods even after I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli beni mikɛ nu shwie nɔ leebi po lɛ?

english: Strong heat quickly evaporates water from uncovered soil. Covering the ground around plant roots with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the soil moist and protects the roots from heat stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ahako nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Hard or heavily compacted soil prevents water from draining properly. Loosening the soil with a hoe and adding compost allows water to soak in naturally so roots do not drown.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ abote mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieee shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the key soil food plants need to stay green and grow strong leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of proper soil nutrients needed to support fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni sa ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more heavily during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During dry spells, crops become weak from water shortage, making it easier for pests to attack them to feed on the plant juices.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ nu ni faaa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatutua ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛye nu lɛ.

english: Why does my neighbor get a bigger cassava harvest than me even though we planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ woɔ ŋmei babaoo fe mi eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Different plant varieties yield differently; high-yield or improved crop varieties are bred to produce bigger roots and resist diseases better than traditional seeds.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi woɔ yibii srɔtoi. Afɔ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo loo ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi wuji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa plants turning yellow and dying when the sun is too bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil quickly; planting plantain trees alongside them protects them until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaha abu he kɛyashi tso lɛ he baawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the leaves of my young maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that attacks the growing tips of maize, but applying approved control measures early stops them from destroying your crop before harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tutuaa ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yitsei lɛ. Shi kɛ akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ momo lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very small roots even though they grow tall with lots of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi bibii waa lɛ? Ni edaa ni eyɛ baai babaoo?

english: If cassava plants are planted too close together or have too much nitrogen in the soil, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in large tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛbaa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso nguahi a mi ngɛ zugba sisi.

english: If your previous crops had pale or yellowish leaves, thin stems, or small yields, your soil is low on essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus and needs organic manure or fertilizer added.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ, tsei bibii, loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Leaving too many young shoots forces them to compete for the same nutrients and water, which leaves you with small, weak bunches instead of one or two large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii bibii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni no baaha ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ahi ohe. Yɛ plantain agboi ni tsii ni abua naa lɛ 1 loo 2 najiaŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper farm in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering early in the morning lets plants absorb water before the sun gets too hot, whereas hot afternoon watering causes fast evaporation and can stress or burn the roots.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atsɔ la oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ aná haomɔ loo eshã.

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, which multiply fast in warm, dry weather and suck sap from the leaves, weakening the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baa curl ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ amli. ni ekɛ nu ni jɛɔ baai ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, working as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant there next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Staking spreads out yam leaves so they can catch direct sunlight, allowing the plant to make more food and transfer that energy into producing big, healthy tubers.
ga: Staking lɛ gbɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tsei feɔ niyenii ni ekɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ yaa koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi ni he wa.

english: Does my swamp rice always need to stay flooded with deep water to grow well?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mi-swamp rice lɛ ahi nu ni mli kwɔ mli be fɛɛ be koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: While rice loves water to block weeds, keeping the field continuously flooded can suffocate the roots; letting the field drain slightly at specific stages helps roots breathe and grow deeper.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ nu ni tsiɔ jwɛi anaa moŋ, Shi kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ oha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ ho fioo yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it means the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa amɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my crop yield when I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant food in the soil. Planting them alongside maize feeds the soil naturally so your maize grows bigger without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, o-abele lɛ baanyɛ adara ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Curling leaves with yellowish-green patches are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems during planting prevents this sickness from taking over your farm.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the very center whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, destructive pests that hide deep inside the young maize leaves during the daytime to escape heat and feed on the tender growth. Detecting them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts protects the plant's main growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛjo latsaa lɛ naa foi ni amɛye ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tso lɛ hei titri ni edaa yɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the farm is overgrown with shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: While young cocoa trees love shade, mature cocoa trees need direct sunlight and clear airflow to produce flowers and pods. Excessive shade creates damp air that promotes black pod disease and reduces the tree's ability to make cocoa pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii po sumɔɔ hulutsoo. Shi kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Shade babaoo haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa, ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee cocoa pods lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant instead of growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or sudden dry soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting windbreaks or light shade can keep the plant cool enough to hold its flowers until they form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu kɔɔyɔɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi yibii lɛ baawo.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots at the bottom end before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the ground, usually due to irregular watering. Consistent watering helps the roots continuously take up calcium to build firm, healthy tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli daa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa calcium ni yaa nɔ koni ekɛfee tomato ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves look wilted and lifeless during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi ni wala bɛ amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, water evaporates from leaves faster than roots can drink it from the soil, so the plant droops its leaves to shield itself from heat. Once the sun goes down and air cools, the plant naturally recovers its standing shape.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ Nu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shiɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ esɛɛ koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by converting sunlight into food through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves high into the air so they catch maximum sunlight and stays dry, which prevents leaves from rotting on the damp soil surface.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbi. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard, woody, and tasteless if I leave them in the ground past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa, amɛfeɔ tsei ni amɛhe bɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for a specific period, but if left unharvested too long, the plant converts that stored food into tough woody fibers to survive future dry weather. Harvesting cassava at maturity ensures the tubers remain soft and rich in starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch toɔ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi ni akpaaa lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ amɛfeɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi mli wɔsɛɛ be mli lɛ, ŋmãa ni akpaa kɛji ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋtayaai lɛ feɔ blɛoo lolo ni ŋmãa babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do international buyers pay premium prices for certain crop varieties while our local native ones sell for much less?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi ahe nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ waa yɛ be mli ni wɔ maŋ lɛ mli tsei lɛ ahe jara ni baa shi kwraa lɛ?

english: Foreign markets often prefer specific crop varieties that meet strict international processing standards, flavor profiles, or uniform sizes. Native varieties are great for local meals and local climate resistance, but export buyers pay extra premiums for specific varieties that fit their factory machinery and international consumer tastes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei sumɔɔ tsei srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni kɛ majimaji ateŋ nitsumɔ he mlai lɛ kpãa gbee. Flavor Profile loo dalɛ ni tsakeee Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi lɛ hi kɛha maŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Shi esa akɛ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ awo nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha nibii srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha nitsumɔhe tsɔnei kɛ nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ.

english: With farm inputs getting so expensive nowadays, will my crops still grow well if I use animal manure instead of buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ jara wa waa amrɔ nɛɛ. Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lolo kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahemɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, animal manure is a great way to feed your crops when chemical fertilizers are expensive. Manure slowly releases nutrients into the soil while improving the soil's ability to hold water, though you need to let it decompose (rot) fully before applying it so it doesn't burn plant roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa onibii lɛ niyenii be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ jara wa. Fiofio lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛya sũ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ nu ni ehiɛɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe baahia ni oha egbo (egbo) kwraa dani okɛfata he moŋ. Enɛ haŋ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why are soldier ants and armyworms attacking my maize plants, and how does their presence affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ asraafoi akutsei kɛ asraafoi akuu mli ŋmeii miitutua mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ amɛhe ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he?

english: Pests like armyworms feed on the young, soft leaves inside the center of maize plants, preventing the crop from making food through sunlight. Soldier ants are often attracted by small sap-sucking insects called aphids. Both pests weaken the plant, leading to poor cob development and reduced yields if not controlled early.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei akaho kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ gbalaa asraafoi ŋmeii. ni atsɛɔ lɛ aphids Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ekɛ cob lɛ shweremɔ ni ehiii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow and curling leaves are usually a sign of insect damage (like whiteflies spreading cassava mosaic virus) or a lack of nutrients in the soil. When leaves curl and turn yellow, the plant cannot absorb sunlight properly, which stops the roots under the ground from growing big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii efite (tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ cassava mosaic virus lɛ eshwaa) loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves that dry out quickly under strong, direct sunlight. Shade plants like plantains act like temporary umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist around the seedlings until their roots grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔi. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo be muu lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, too much or too little water, or lack of nutrients like calcium. When the weather is too hot, the pollen inside the flower dies before it can fertilize the flower to form a tomato fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu babaoo loo fioo loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ dani enyɛɔ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli ni etsɔɔ tomato yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants yellow and rot at the base during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess water around the roots smothers the plant by cutting off oxygen, allowing soil fungi to infect the root system. This root rot prevents the plant from drinking water and taking up food, causing the leaves to turn yellow and the plant to collapse.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ hela. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ nɛɛ haaa tso lɛ anu nu ni eye niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of putting energy into growing big cobs, the maize plants stretch upward to steal sun from their neighbors, resulting in weak stems and small yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli yɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ najiaŋ Abɛi shwieɔ shi koni eju hulu la kɛjɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ adɛŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested maize to plant next season, or is it better to buy fresh seeds from the shop?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli?

english: If you are growing hybrid seeds bought from a shop, saving seeds from your harvest will result in weaker plants and smaller yields next season. However, traditional open-pollinated varieties can be saved and replanted, provided you pick the healthiest cobs for seed selection.
ga: Kɛji oodu dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, abaanyɛ ahere blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni agbele naa lɛ ayiwala ni adu ekoŋŋ. Esa akɛ ohala ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ kɛha dumɔwui halamɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in the dry soil waiting for water. Because weeds are wild plants adapted to survival, their roots shoot out fast to steal water and fertilizer before your crop roots have a chance to spread.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi waa ni amɛwɔɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni miimɛ nu Ejaakɛ jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya koni amɛju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean your maize plants are stressed, which can be caused by a lack of water, missing nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or early signs of pest attacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso mli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ enɛ aba. Niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua

english: How can I tell if a dark spot on my plant's leaf is just sunburn or a real crop disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji hulutsoo kɛkɛ loo tso hela diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Sunburn leaves dry, pale patches only on upper leaves exposed to direct heat, whereas fungal or bacterial diseases create growing spots with dark rings or yellowish borders that spread across the whole plant.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Su ni mli tse yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ pɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni fungal loo bacteria helai haa tso lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: What should I do when I first notice mild spots starting on my cassava leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mina akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo miibɔi baa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe?

english: Mild spots are early warnings of disease; removing affected leaves immediately and keeping the farm clear of weeds stops the illness from spreading to the roots.
ga: He ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ji hela he kɔkɔbɔɔ mra. Jiemɔ baai ni ena hela lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni oha jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa hela shwereɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil still has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛ Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: In intense sunlight, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up, so the leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves from overheating.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ he.

english: Cassava drops leaves in the dry season as a natural survival mechanism to save moisture, and it will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing huge green leaves but failing to produce any flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants spend all their energy growing thick leaves instead of making flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo baai ni mli tse. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ

english: Is it safe to wait until a leaf disease spreads across my whole farm before treating it?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi baa hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ dani matsa?

english: No, waiting allows the disease to multiply and destroy your harvest; treating or removing sick plants at the very first mild symptom saves money and protects your healthy crops.
ga: Dabi, mɛmɔ baaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ekpata oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ otsa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ loo ojie amɛ kɛjɛ shishijee fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ shika akafite, ni ebaabu onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How does removing sick plants from my field help the surrounding healthy crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ?

english: Sick plants act as breeding grounds for germs that spread through wind, rain droplets, and insects, so removing them breaks the path of infection to healthy crops.
ga: Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ helai ni kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ fɔɔ yɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛji ajie amɛ lɛ, etsĩɔ hela lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I try new improved seed varieties instead of using saved seeds from my old harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka dumɔwui heei ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ makwɛ? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ mi kpamɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii.

english: New improved seeds are specially bred to withstand common local diseases, handle hot weather better, and give higher yields than older seeds.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kpeɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui momo

english: How can I train my children to spot early signs of crop illness when we work on the farm together?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔse mibii lɛ koni amɛna mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela miiba ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ́ wɔfee ekome kɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Take your children on regular walks through the fields, teach them to inspect under leaves for spots or small bugs, and explain the difference between a healthy green leaf and a sick one.
ga: Okɛ obii lɛ aya nyiɛmɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ amɛ ni amɛkwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli. ni otsɔɔ srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ baai ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ateŋ.

english: How do I know if a specific crop seed is good for selling to commercial buyers rather than just feeding my family?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui komɛi hi ni ahɔ̃ɔ ahaa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makwɛ miweku lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Certain seed varieties are specifically bred to produce high yields and produce uniform traits that factory processors and large buyers look for, making them ideal cash crops for quick income.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ sui ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ ni nitsumɔhei ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ kɛ mɛi wuji ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ shika ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shika ni anáa oya.

english: Why do commercial buyers prefer buying specific named seed varieties over our traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ gbɛi lɛ fe wɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ?

english: Commercial buyers favor specific varieties because they dry better, store longer, and have consistent quality that works best in processing machinery.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ sumɔɔ srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ejaakɛ amɛgbiɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ su ni yaa nɔ daa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ amli.

english: If money is tight, which type of crops should I plant to get income as quickly as possible?
ga: Kɛji shika faaa lɛ, mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ odu koni onine ashɛ shika nɔ oya?

english: Short-duration market crops or high-demand commercial seed varieties allow you to harvest quickly and sell in bulk to big buyers, providing fast cash during hard times.
ga: Jarayeli mli nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli loo jarayeli dumɔwui ni ataoɔ waa lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa oya ni ohɔ̃ɔ babaoo ohaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ babaoo. Kɛtsɔ shika ni akɛhaa oya yɛ jaramɔ bei amli lɛ nɔ

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested market crops to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: While you can save traditional seeds, many specialized market varieties lose their strength and yield potential after one season, so buying fresh certified seeds gives you better market harvests.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ okɛ blema dumɔwui ato moŋ. Shi jarayeli hei sɔrɔtoi babaoo ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be kome sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ hemɔ baaye abua bo ni oná ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How do I tell the exact right time to harvest my crop so it doesn't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops show clear physical signs like leaves drying out, stalks turning brown, or grains hardening; harvesting at this peak moment prevents field rot and loss of market value.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ baai ni miigbi kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni tsɔɔ asasu. loo dumɔwui ni wa Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni fa fe fɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni akafite jɛmɛ ni jarayeli jara lɛ akafite.

english: Why do some crops need to be harvested multiple times in a season while others are harvested all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akpa tsei komɛi shii abɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ akpa tsei komɛi fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Crops mature differently; fruit and vegetable crops often ripen in stages requiring multiple harvests, while grain and seed crops usually mature evenly for a single big harvest.
ga: Tsei daa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, aduawai kɛ aduawai shwereɔ yɛ be mli ni biɔ ni akpa shii abɔ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ agbo kome.

english: Why is it important to dry my harvested crop thoroughly before selling it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Drying removes excess water from the seeds, which prevents mold from growing, stops premature rotting, and ensures the produce can survive long travel in big trucks.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. ni tsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Ekpaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ oya lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛtsɔ lɔlei wuji anɔ.

english: What will happen to my produce if I pack and load it for buyers while it is still damp?
ga: Mɛni baa minibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛwo kotoku mli ni mikɛtee mɛi ni heɔ lɛ aŋɔɔ be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Damp crops generate heat when packed together, leading to rapid mold growth and spoilage during transport, which causes buyers to reject the load or pay a lower price.
ga: Tsei ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ dɔlɛ kɛji akɛ akɛfee ekome. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Enɛ haa mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ shika ni ekɛwoɔ edɛŋ lɛ loo ewoɔ jara ni baa shi.

english: Why do large produce buyers bring big articulator trucks directly to the farm community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nibii babaoo lɛ kɛ tsɔnei wuji ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ baa ŋmɔ mli akutsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Large trucks allow factory buyers to collect massive quantities of harvested crops directly from multiple farmers at once, saving on transport costs and moving produce quickly to drying or processing centers.
ga: Lɔlei wuji haa mɛi ni heɔ tsei lɛ buaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akpa lɛ anaa kɛjɛɔ okwaafoi babaoo adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ shikome. Enɛ haa tsɔne he nyɔmɔwoo baa shi, ni ekɛ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ yaa hei ni agbiɔ loo atsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ oya.

english: Why do industrial processors prefer buying raw crops straight from farmers instead of buying at the local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔhei ni feɔ nibii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ okwaafoi adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni amɛbaahe yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ?

english: Buying directly from farms gives processors access to fresher produce in larger quantities at wholesale prices, ensuring their processing factories have enough raw materials to operate.
ga: Nibii ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa mɛi ni feɔ nibii nɛɛ náa nibii heei babaoo yɛ jara ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛ nitsumɔhei lɛ náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leaf growth, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields every year even when I clear and weed the land the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mijieɔ jwɛi yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every season drains specific nutrients without giving the soil time to recover, which reduces soil fertility over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall leaves but produce small roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen from excess fertilizer or fresh manure, the cassava plant sends all its energy into leaf growth instead of storing energy in its roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin if I plant four or five seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ fee ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds in one hole forces the young plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die so easily when planted in an open field without big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei gboiɔ oya kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni tsei wuji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because harsh direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out their shallow roots before they can establish deep roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ agbi dani amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the dry afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: High afternoon heat causes plant leaves to lose water faster than roots can draw it up from the soil, making the leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei ahe baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my cowpea crops fail to produce pods when it rains heavily during the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ wooo ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away pollen from open flowers and can cause blossoms to rot before they turn into crop pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni agbele lɛ anɔ pollen. ni ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔi lɛ agboi dani amɛbatsɔ tsei amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants look like they have holes eaten through them with powdery waste inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu ni aye kɛ sũ ni efite yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing center of the plant and leaves visible feeding damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni yeɔ tso lɛ he ni edaa lɛ. ni eshiɔ niyenii he fitemɔ ni anaa.

english: Poorly drained soil holds excess water, which cuts off oxygen to the roots and allows soil fungi to invade and rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine. ni ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my okra plants get sticky leaves covered in small white flying insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ baai ni wa lɛ? Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ni foɔ ehà nɔ.

english: Whiteflies gather on the undersides of leaves to suck plant sap, releasing a sugary liquid that coats the leaves and attracts dark mold.
ga: Whiteflies buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Amɛjieɔ nu ni mli edɔ ni haa baa lɛ nɔ ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops suddenly wilt and die even after they start growing very well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops often collapse suddenly when their root system is damaged by soil pests, root rot, or severe drought. If the roots fail, the plant can no longer draw water and nutrients up to sustain the leaves and stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi trukaa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi, shishifãi ni egbo, loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa fite shishifãi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ agbala nu kɛ niyenii ni haa amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ hewalɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to focus on soil health rather than just looking at the leaves of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ maa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai ni mikwɛɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: The root system in the soil acts as the heart of the plant. If the roots are healthy and well-fed, they can support all other parts of the crop, including the leaves, stems, and fruits.
ga: Shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ tsui. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli wa ni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ Shishifãi baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi hu, ni baai, shishifãi, kɛ aduawai fata he.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: When soil nutrients are low, the plant moves food from older leaves at the bottom to protect the new leaves at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow first.
ga: Kɛji niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ebu baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do flowers drop off my pepper plants before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients as a defense mechanism to keep the main plant alive.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Koni efee gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ tsei titrii lɛ ahe ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to prune side branches from my cassava or tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei loo tomato tso mli lɛ?

english: Removing excess or weak branches prevents them from taking away nutrients from the main stem, allowing the plant to direct its energy into developing bigger roots and fruits.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni aaafo lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha shishifãi kɛ aduawai wuji ni baa lɛ.

english: My crops start growing fast in the first two weeks but then stop growing tall entirely, why is that?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ lɛ amli shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛkpa shweremɔ kwraa. Mɛni hewɔ enɛ ji nakai lɛ?

english: Young plants initially rely on food stored inside the seed. Once that food is exhausted, if the surrounding soil lacks sufficient nutrients, the plant's growth stalls.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, tsei bibii kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ nɔ. Beni niyenii lɛ eho Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ adalɛ baakpa.

english: Why does standing water on my farm cause my crops to rot and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni ekã shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite ni amɛgboi lɛ?

english: Too much standing water suffocates plant roots by cutting off air. Without air, the roots decay and can no longer transport water or food to the rest of the plant.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ nu loo niyenii aya hei krokomɛi. ni ji tsei dɔŋŋ

english: Should I pour fertilizer directly on the stem of my crop or around the soil near it?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifã lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo ebɔle he? Ani eji shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be placed in the soil around the root zone, not directly touching the stem, because direct contact can burn the stem while roots need space to absorb nutrients safely.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli ni akataa tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ ashã. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my plants dying from pests even when I do not see insects eating the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miigboi kɛmiijɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ moŋ?

english: Many destructive pests attack underground roots or bore inside the stem, damaging the crop's internal support system without leaving visible signs on the leaves.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ nii babaoo tutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ loo amɛboteɔ tso lɛ mli. Efiteɔ tso lɛ mligbɛ yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni eshiuuu nɔ ko ni anaa yɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: If I am getting into farming for the first time, why is it better to grow more than one type of crop on my land?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ mihe miiwo okwaayeli mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe ekome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing multiple crops protects you if one crop fails due to pests or bad weather. Different crops also use soil nutrients differently, which keeps your land fertile for longer.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni ooodu lɛ baabu ohe kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii hewɔ. Tsei srɔtoi hu kɛ niyenii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which crops will grow best during the major rainy season compared to the minor rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ wulu kɛ nugbɔ bibioo mli?

english: Crops like maize and cassava require a lot of water over a longer period, so they thrive during the major rainy season. Fast-growing crops like cowpeas or vegetables can do well during the shorter minor rains.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa biɔ nu babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli. Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tsina loo aduawai tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, or that too much water is sitting around the roots, preventing the plant from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni sa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face extreme heat, lack water, or receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of developing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ewo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to grow when I plant them close to large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains need full sunlight and abundant soil moisture. Large trees block sunlight and their mature roots compete for water and food, slowing down the plantain's growth.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu ni fa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni eda lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni shishifãi ni eda lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing pods during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds strip moisture from the air and soil. Cocoa trees respond by shedding leaves and dropping flowers to save water, which temporarily pauses pod production.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cacao tsei haa hetoo kɛtsɔ amɛbaai kɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwieɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha pod feemɔ akpa.

english: Why can I harvest tomatoes multiple times from one planting, but maize can only be harvested once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ maná tomato ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ dumɔ kome pɛ mli lɛ? Shi abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa shikome pɛ.

english: Tomatoes are continuous-bearing plants that produce new flowers and fruits as long as the plant stays healthy, while maize is a single-cycle crop that dies after its grain ear matures.
ga: Tomato ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai heei kɛji tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, eji tso ko ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ shikome ni gboɔ beni ŋmãa lɛ toi lɛ edara sɛɛ.

english: Why do cassava roots stay fresh in the soil for months, but yams start to rot if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo lɛ? Shi sweet potatoes jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Cassava roots remain alive and draw water from the living stem while underground, whereas yams reach a dormant state after maturing where excess ground moisture causes them to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, sweet potatoes boteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do some cassava plants produce very small tubers even when planted on the same field as healthy ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli po kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Tuber size depends on whether the soil was properly loosened before planting and how early weeds were cleared, as heavy weeds steal food from the roots during key growth stages.
ga: Bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara ha lɛ damɔ kɛji akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ nɔ. Ni te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ yɛ shishijee mli? Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi ni tsii lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas help improve my soil before I plant my next crop?
ga: Te tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ dani adu tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas work with natural soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally feeding the soil so the next crop grows stronger.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara waa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct sunshine. Leaving big trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantains creates natural umbrellas that provide the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa lɛ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore foliage and improves yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water pools in flat soil and suffocates them. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛdamɔ nubui amli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off the plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when crop plants experience sudden heat stress or irregular watering. Giving your pepper plants steady moisture and mulching around their roots keeps soil temperatures balanced so flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo pepper tsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shishifãi lɛ ahe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas in the same farm rows as my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, while their spreading foliage shades the ground to stop weeds and keep soil moist.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he. Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni baai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and dirt inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli kɛ muji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the plant's core. Spraying early in the morning when the pest is feeding reaches them before they ruin the growing stem.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ amɛ niyenii lɛ dani amɛfite tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Covering the ground (mulching) acts like a blanket that stops heat from drying out soil water during warm spells, while slowly rotting to feed beneficial nutrients back into the land.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli koni ekɛtsi dɔlɛ ni haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Efiteɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by converting sunlight through leaves. Staking lifts leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight, which directly feeds the energy needed to swell tubers below.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Awoɔ staking lifts lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛwo yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant tomatoes on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing tomatoes repeatedly on one spot drains specific nutrients and allows specialized soil bugs and sicknesses to build up. Switching to legumes or grains breaks disease cycles and lets the land recover.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi kɛ shikpɔŋ helai ni yɔɔ srɔto aba. Kɛ́ atsake kɛtee ŋmãa loo ŋmaa nɔ lɛ, hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ fiteɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow tall and thin without producing food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ shwiili ni amɛfeɔ shwiili ni amɛwooo niyenii lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and light from your crop plants. Clearing weeds during the crop's first few weeks ensures all soil food goes into your plants instead of unwanted wild greenery.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii fɛɛ aba otsei lɛ amli. Yɛ koo mli tsei ni esaaa lɛ najiaŋ.
