english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and full. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure to the soil will help keep the leaves healthy and feed the growing corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ewaje baai lɛ ni eha niyenii aha ŋmãa toi ni miida lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over, leaving the ground tired. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally and helps break crop disease cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, etɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni efoɔ tsei ahe helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ amli

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the centers of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide deep inside the funnel of young maize plants to eat the tender growing leaves. Applying approved treatments or local remedies directly into the center funnel early in the morning or late afternoon kills them before they ruin the whole plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai ni miida ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai loo maŋ lɛ mli tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo shwane lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛbaakpãtã tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies that suck the juice out of young leaves and spread plant diseases. Spraying the underside of the leaves with soapy water or neem oil helps destroy these insects so healthy new leaves can sprout.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpãtãa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahiɛ koni baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I clear all the large trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby creates a natural roof that shields cocoa seedlings from sun heat and keeps soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni shwereɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft, black, and smelly underground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rainwater collects around them and cannot drain away. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or long ridges gives water a pathway to run off, keeping the roots in dry, well-aerated soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nu buaa amɛhe naa lɛ. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛya Shishi ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi kakadaji anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ naa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejɛɔ mli. Ha shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without producing any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to save energy. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass helps keep the roots cool and preserves moisture so the plant can hold onto its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Okɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashwie shi koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite. Mulching around Jwɛi ni egbi shishitoo yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in dry soil before the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Seeds require continuous moisture to wake up and push roots into the ground. If they sit in hot, dry dirt, they either dry out completely or get eaten by ants before the first rainfall arrives.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu daa koni amɛte shi ni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ Ebaagbi kwraa loo ŋmeii baaye lɛ dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow slow and thin when I leave weeds growing around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal light, water, and soil fertilizer away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the planting season ensures all the soil nutrients go straight into feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily in heavy wind before the fruit is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa mi plantains lɛ oya dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain stem weakens the root base and forces the main plant to share its strength. Cutting away extra suckers leaves one strong main stem anchored firmly in the soil.
ga: Ni aaaŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ Plantain kome he lɛ baaha shishifã lɛ agbɔjɔ ni enyɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ aha. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri kome ni mli wa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shiŋŋ.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa tree to turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, damp, and overly shaded conditions. Damp environments allow fungal spores to multiply quickly and attack the pod skin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ oya ni amɛtutuaa pod hewolo lɛ.

english: How does a disease spread from one sick cocoa tree to the rest of my healthy farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni hela gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ cacao tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fã kroko lɛ nɔ?

english: Crop diseases spread through wind carrying fungal spores, rain splashing infected soil onto leaves, insects moving between plants, or farm tools that carried infected sap from a sick tree to a healthy one.
ga: Tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hiɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ nɔ Kooloi bibii ni nyiɛɔ tsei ateŋ loo okwaayeli nibii ni hiɛɔ nu ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How do I know if a chemical or medicine sold at the market will actually cure my sick cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai loo tsofai ni akɛheɔ yɛ tsofafeemɔ he lɛ baanyɛ atsa cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Approved crop medicines target specific issues like fungi or insects. You must first identify whether the problem is a pest, fungus, or virus, because using a chemical made for insects will not cure a fungal disease.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ kwɛɔ naagbai pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo kooloi bibii. Esa akɛ okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ akɛ naagba lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela, tsɛŋemɔ hela, loo hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ. Tsofai ni afee aha kooloi bibii lɛ tsaŋ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that cannot pull up water fast enough to survive intense sun. They require shade trees or plantains to shield them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdamɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before the flowers can turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani fɔfɔi lɛ etsɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Trees shed flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of nutrients, or heavy pest attacks, or naturally through a process called cherelle wilt where the tree discards extra fruit it cannot support.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui babaoo lɛ hao amɛ. loo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherel wilt lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baashi yibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ.

english: Why does trimming or pruning extra branches off my cocoa tree help it bear more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tso niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ loo afolɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unwanted branches that steal food and water from the tree, opens up the leaves to sunlight, and allows air to flow through, which lowers dampness and reduces disease risks.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni ataooo ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Gbelemɔ baai lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: How can I tell the difference between damage caused by insects and damage caused by a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ nibii ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni tsei ahelai fiteɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Insect damage usually leaves visible physical signs like chewed leaves, holes in pods, or tiny bugs present on stems, whereas diseases usually cause color changes like leaf yellowing, wilting, swollen stems, or fuzzy fungal spots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni anaa, tamɔ baai ni atsɔ mli, bu yɛ ŋmeii amli, loo kooloi bibii ni jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei lɛ ahe, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela haa tsei lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, baai ni egbɔjɔ, tsei lɛ amli ni efuu, loo ŋmeii ni bɛ faŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during severe drought to protect themselves and conserve water, but early leaf fall can also indicate root damage or a nutrient deficiency in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he. Shi baa ni fiteɔ mra lɛ hu baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ efite loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is tired and needs fertilizer to help crops grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Tired soil shows signs like slow plant growth, thin stems, pale or yellowish leaves, and low yield despite good rainfall, indicating essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium are depleted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baatsɔɔ okadii tamɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ blɛoo, tsei bibii, kɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium lɛ faaa.

english: Who can I report a strange or new disease to if treatments are not working on my farm?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ mabɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ loo hela hee ko he amaniɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii hu?

english: You can report unusual crop diseases to local government agricultural extension officers or national research bodies like the Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana (CRIG), who test treatments and guide farmers on safe solutions.
ga: Obaanyɛ obɔ tsei ahe helai ni jeee nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ he amaniɛ otsɔɔ maŋ nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi loo maŋ niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei tamɔ Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana (CRIG), ni kaa tsofafeemɔi amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛwoɔ okwaafoi ŋaa yɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a key soil nutrient needed for green leaves and fast growth. Applying compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plants regain their deep green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating big holes in the middle leaves of my young corn shoots overnight?
ga: Mɛni ye bu agbo lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji mi tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɔɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms. These caterpillars hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of the corn plant during the hot afternoon and come out at night to eat tender leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni amɛje kpo amɛbaye baai bibii gbɛkɛ

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight for water, sunlight, and soil food. This competition results in thin, weak stalks with very small ears of corn instead of healthy plants with large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa baa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e ngɛ ngma ngua.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under hot direct sun. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa wala hiɔ shi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Exposure to sunlight allows the leaves to make food that travels down to feed and expand the yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eyatao niyenii. ni okɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around roots helps protect the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready for harvest since they grow underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the stem base starts cracking as expanding tubers push upward, typically 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii ni dara lɛ daraa kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants look like they are wilting in the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense heat, pepper leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can pull water from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, usually recovering once the evening cool arrives.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i eba.

english: How do wild weeds actually harm my crops if they are just harmless plants growing in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye midumɔ nii lɛ awui? Ni kɛji akɛ amɛji tsei ni yeee mɔ awui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli kɛkɛ hu?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your harvest. They can also hide destructive insects and fungal diseases that spread to your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa kɛha okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa onibii titrii lɛ hu ato.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is tired and needs rest or fertilizer before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔ nii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni mafo mli loo awo mli ŋmɔshi nii dani madu?

english: Tired soil often becomes very hard, pale, and dry, and crops planted in it grow very slowly with yellowish leaves and small yields compared to previous years. Allowing the land to rest under fallow or adding organic manure restores its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ wa waa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbi, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa. Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ ni ehi shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashishi loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient found in animal manure or fertilizers like Urea. Without nitrogen, the crop cannot produce enough green chlorophyll to feed itself and grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea mli, kɛji nitrogen bɛ Ŋmãa lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil eŋɔli ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ ehe ni ekwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant the exact same crop on the same farm plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific soil nutrients that crop favors and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on it to build up in large numbers in your field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ ajɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers and tiny green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli Dani ebaada agbo?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop excess flowers and small pods when they lack sufficient water, nutrients, or shade. The tree intentionally sheds them to conserve energy so the remaining pods can survive and mature.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Nɔ ni fe nine lɛ baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ ejieɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or by extreme heat stress where the plant rolls its leaves to protect itself from losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers but no tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo shi tomato ko bɛ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too hot or dry winds blow, the pollen inside tomato blossoms dries up and dies. If the flowers are not fertilized, the plant drops them off without forming fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tswa Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ tso lɛ baagbee shi ni ewooo yibii.

english: How are the improved seeds from government programs like Feed Ghana different from seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni atsake kɛjɛ nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ Feed Ghana mli lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Government-certified seeds are specially bred by plant scientists to mature faster, resist local pests and dry spells, and yield more food compared to saved seeds, which lose their strength over generations.
ga: Tsei ahe nilelɔi ekwɛ dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ amli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ. ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato he. ni ebaafite ehewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo mli lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot under the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil without proper drainage, oxygen is trapped out, allowing destructive fungal rot to attack the roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Oxygen lɛ baatsi mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do plantain crops require much more water to survive than cassava crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa plantain tsei koni amɛhi shi fe cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Plantains have massive leaves and shallow root systems that lose moisture rapidly into the hot air, whereas cassava has deep roots and narrow leaves designed to store water during dry periods.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai bibii, ni afee koni ehiɛ nu mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunshine to manufacture energy for building tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground so leaves catch maximum sunlight while staying safe from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni eha tsei ahe tsei lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, soil space, and water. Instead of building thick stalks, they stretch upward abnormally fast to reach light before their neighbors block them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko, kɛ nu. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ koni amɛyashɛ kane lɛ he dani amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Why should I cut off branches from my cocoa tree if they are not carrying any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo niji lɛ kɛji kookoo tso lɛ wooo yibii kwraa?

english: Branches that do not produce fruit still drink water and consume plant food from the soil. Removing them allows the tree to send all its energy and nutrients directly to the branches that actually produce cocoa pods.
ga: Tso niji ni wooo yibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie kookoo yibii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa niji ni feɔ kookoo yibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If a branch is already bearing fruit, why would I still need to trim parts of it back?
ga: Kɛji nine lɛ ewo yibii momo Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji lɛ ekomɛi aku sɛɛ lolo?

english: Trimming healthy, fruiting branches controls the shape of the plant and prevents it from wasting energy on extra growth. This forces the tree to put its strength into making the remaining fruits grow larger and healthier.
ga: Niji ni woɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ, ni ehaaa efite hewalɛ ni fa ni ekɛbaadara lɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni eha yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ dara ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Will cutting away leaves and branches from my trees not weaken or kill them?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mifolɔ mitso lɛ baai kɛ eniji lɛ, no haŋ ekwɛ̃ loo egbo?

english: No, proper trimming does not kill the plant. When done correctly, it actually stimulates the tree to grow fresh, stronger shoots that will bear more flowers and fruit in the next season.
ga: Dabi, tso ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ egbeŋ tso lɛ. Kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ tsei heei ni mli wa ni baawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I leave dry, dead, or yellowing branches on them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mishi tsei niji ni egbi, ni egboi, loo ni efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ?

english: Dead and yellowing branches attract pests and fungal diseases. Leaving them on the plant allows these problems to spread to the healthy parts of the crop and reduce your harvest.
ga: Niji ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha naagbai nɛɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli, ni ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my older mango trees stop producing fruits inside the middle of the canopy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ ekpa yibiiwoo yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Thick outer branches block sunlight and fresh air from getting into the center of the tree. Clearing out crowded inner branches allows sunlight to reach the middle, encouraging flowers and fruits to grow inside as well.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Kɛ́ akumɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, hulu la lɛ shɛɔ teŋgbɛ. Wo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ mli hu.

english: How does removing small extra shoots at the base of my plantain tree help me get bigger bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná tsei niji wuji?

english: Too many shoots around one plantain stand compete for food and space. By cutting away the extra shoots and leaving only the strongest main trunk, all nutrients go into forming a heavy, full bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi ni adu yɛ he lɛ Plantains babaoo ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ baatswa niyenii kɛ he ko he akaŋ. Afoɔ tsei ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ ni tso lɛ yitso titri ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ baafee plantains ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of green leaves but produce very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi niyenii fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: When a plant has too many leafy branches, it puts all its energy into growing big leaves instead of making flowers and fruits. Cutting back extra leaf stems forces the plant to focus on fruiting.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo tsɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: How does trimming diseased branches help protect the rest of my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he?

english: Diseases like black pod travel easily from one branch to another, especially when branches touch. Cutting off and removing infected branches stops the sickness from jumping to clean trees nearby.
ga: Helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛjɛɔ tso nine kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ mlɛo. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ tsei niji lɛ ta amɛhe. Niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ajieɔ lɛ Baaha helatsɛmɛi akatu ni amɛkatsumɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to trim the branches on my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: It is best to trim right after major harvest periods or just before the rainy season starts. This gives the tree enough rest time to heal its cut areas and sprout fresh growth before the next flowering period.
ga: Esa akɛ akpɛ tsei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ sɛɛ loo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛtsa he ni afo lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ dani fɔfɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Do I need to keep trimming my tree crops every year, or is doing it once enough?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ mitso lɛ daa afi loo eko ni afoɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Trimming is an ongoing practice that must be done regularly throughout the tree's lifespan. Continuous maintenance keeps the tree clean, manageable, and productive year after year.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ ji nifeemɔ ko ni yaa nɔ ni esa akɛ afee daa yɛ tso lɛ wala be fɛɛ mli. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tseɔ, anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why is it important for me to farm throughout the whole year instead of stopping after six months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsu okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makpa yɛ nyɔji enumɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Farming year-round allows you to make the best use of your land, maintain continuous income, and produce steady food supplies, rather than relying on a single short rain season that leaves land empty for months.
ga: Afi muu lɛ fɛɛ okwaayeli haa onyɛɔ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ shika ni anáa daa lɛ nɔ ni oha niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ aba Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ nɔ Ekome ni ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee efolo nyɔji babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: What preparation do I need if I want my crop field to last and produce for a full year?
ga: Mɛɛ hesaamɔi esa akɛ mafee kɛji miisumɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi ni ewo yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: To sustain crops over a full year, you need to enrich the soil with compost or manure, plan a irrigation or hand-watering system for dry periods, and choose crop varieties that can handle extended seasons.
ga: Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Too nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo nu ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ohala tsei srɔtoi ni baanyɛ aye abua be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I keep my young seedlings alive in the nursery when the rains are not falling well?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akwɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Seedlings in a nursery need a shaded cover made of palm fronds or thatch to block harsh sunlight, along with regular morning and evening manual watering to prevent them from drying out before transplanting.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aná hulutsoo ni akɛ ŋmei baai loo jwɛi fee koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛfata he lɛ, akɛ nine shwieɔ nu nɔ leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ daa koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi dani adu amɛ.

english: How can I tell when my nursery plants are ready to be moved into the main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-nursery tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are ready to be transplanted when they have developed a strong root system and a few full leaves, preferably moved during a week when the soil in the main field is moist from rain.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli wa ni baai babaoo bɛ jɛmɛ. Esa akɛ ajie amɛ yɛ otsi lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops when the rain suddenly stops during their growing stage?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: When rain stops unexpectedly, crops suffer from moisture stress, causing leaves to droop or turn yellow, stunted growth, and a lower yield if the plant cannot get enough water to form fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ he haomɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. growth stalls Ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni amɛfee aduawai loo dumɔwui.

english: What simple step can I take to keep moisture in the soil when rain is scarce?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves (mulching) keeps the sun from drying out the ground and traps water in the soil much longer.
ga: Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ (mulching) lɛ baaye abua ni hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni nu lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What crops can I plant if I know my area gets very little rain?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu kɛji mile akɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Drought-hardy crops like cassava, cowpeas, millet, and sorghum are great options because their root systems are built to find and store water even under dry ground conditions.
ga: Tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ji tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ama amɛshishifãi lɛ koni amɛna nu ni amɛhiɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi po nɔ.

english: How do I recognize that my young plants are getting stressed by too much heat and no water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ miihao yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Signs of stress include leaves rolling inward, wilting in the afternoon sun, leaves drying at the tips, and very slow growth compared to normal wet weather.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mɔ ko miifee nɔ ko lɛ he ji: baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli Egboɔ yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli baai lɛ egbiɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni edaa blɛoo waa kɛ akɛto shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ ahe.

english: Why does harvesting tiger nuts (atedwe) take so much physical energy compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tiger nuts (atedwe) ni akpaa lɛ biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ babaoo kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Tiger nuts grow underground attached to fine root networks in heavy soil, requiring intense digging, threshing, and beating (hitting) to separate the small nuts from the dirt and roots.
ga: Tiger nuts lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi kpakpai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli. Enɛ biɔ ni atsa shi waa, atsɔ mli, ni atswa (atswa) koni akɛgbala ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How can I organize my farm work so I do not get completely exhausted during long farming seasons?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato nitsumɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Bɔni afee ni nijiaŋ aje wui yɛ okwaayeli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: To avoid extreme fatigue, do heavy field labor in the cooler early morning hours, rotate heavy tasks across different days, and use simple tools or shared community labor to lighten the burden.
ga: Bɔni afee ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he Feemɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ ni tsii yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ waa lɛ amli. Tsɔmɔmɔ nitsumɔi ni tsii daa gbi. ni amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii loo amɛja nitsumɔ yɛ akutso lɛ mli koni jatsu lɛ afee mlɛo

english: Why does my cocoa crop sometimes dry up or die unexpectedly across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miiho trukaa loo amɛmiigboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees in regions like Western North Ghana can be hit by severe viral outbreaks such as Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease. When infected, the trees lose strength, stop producing good pods, and eventually die.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni yɔɔ hei tamɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná helai ni naa wa tamɔ cocoa top swelling disease lɛ. Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ mɔ lɛ Tso lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. Kpaa pods kpakpai feemɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbo

english: If a severe disease hits my cocoa farm, why do officers advise me to cut down all the trees instead of just spraying them?
ga: Kɛji hela ko ni naa wa ba mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafo tsei lɛ fɛɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsofa baashwie nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Certain viral crop diseases have no chemical cure once inside the tree. Cutting down and removing all infected trees stops the disease from spreading to healthy farms nearby and prepares the field for planting new, healthy seedlings.
ga: Tso mli helai komɛi ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli lɛ bɛ tsofa ko ni akɛbaatsa amɛ kɛji amɛbote tso lɛ mli pɛ. Tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaafolɔ ni ajie lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. ni osaa he lɛ kɛha dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ adumɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are suffering from a disease rather than just a lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela miipiŋ mi-cacao tsei lɛ, shi jeee nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Drought causes uniform leaf wilting during dry seasons, whereas major diseases cause swollen stems, red leaf veins, deformed pods, or sudden dieback in patches even when there is enough rainfall.
ga: Hɔmɔ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni hela ni naa wa kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efuu, baa lɛ mli fãji tsuji, ŋmeii ni efite loo gbele ni baa trukaa, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po

english: How long does it usually take for oil palm trees to start bearing fruit after planting them?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Oil palm trees generally take about 3 to 4 years after planting to mature and begin producing harvestable palm fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu mu tsei lɛ, amɛheɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani amɛdaraa ni amɛjeɔ tsofa yibii ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ shishi.

english: What basic maintenance do my palm trees need while waiting for them to reach maturity?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee saamɔ biɔ ni esa akɛ akwɛ mihe yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young palm trees need regular weeding around their bases, protection from grazing animals, adequate water, and proper soil nutrients so they grow strong trunks and bear fruit early.
ga: Palm tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ he daa, ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe, ni aha amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa. Koni tso lɛ tso lɛ mli awa ni ewo yibii oya

english: Why is cocoa farming considered a good crop for supporting my family's income?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ akɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni akɛnáa weku shika lɛ?

english: Cocoa provides a reliable seasonal income for many years once established, benefits from an organized purchasing market in Ghana, and yields products that remain in high market demand.
ga: Cocoa ha shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ be mli lɛ ba afii babaoo beni ato shishi lɛ. Na jarayeli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ he sɛɛ. ni amɛfee nibii ni jara nɔ bii taoɔ waa

english: While both grow well in Ghana, mature oil palms cast heavy shade and compete strongly for soil nutrients, so it is best to plant them in separate fields rather than mixing them directly with cocoa.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana moŋ, shi mu tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛfutu kookoo tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: How does planting permanent tree crops like palm or cocoa affect traditional land arrangements with a chief or landowner?
ga: Te tsei ni hiɔ shi daa tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ saa kusum shikpɔŋ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛ maŋtsɛmɛi loo shikpɔŋtsɛmɛi feɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting long-term tree crops often involves customary land agreements like 'Abunu' or 'Abusa,' where the mature farm or its yields are shared between the farmer and the landowner once the trees mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ kɔɔ kusum shikpɔŋ he kpaŋmɔi tamɔ ‘Abunu’ loo ‘Abusa’ he ni ŋmɔ loo nibii ni adu lɛ jaa okwaafonyo lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ teŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why is it important for all farmers in our village to clear disease-affected crops together at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaafonyo fɛɛ okwaafonyo ni yɔɔ wɔ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Pests and crop diseases spread easily across farm borders. If one farmer leaves infected trees standing, insects can carry the infection back to neighboring farms that were recently cleaned.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji husui lɛ amli oya. Kɛji okwaafonyo ko shi tso ko ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ Kooloi baanyɛ amɛkɛ hela lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛya ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni atsuu he nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ amli.

english: How does the government get involved or help us when our crops face major widespread destruction?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔyeli lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ mli loo eyeɔ ebuaa wɔ kɛ́ wɔŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hiɛkpatamɔ lɛ kpe yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: The government relies on agricultural exports like cocoa for national revenue, so it often steps in during widespread crop disasters to offer free seedlings, field support, and rehabilitation assistance to help farmers restart.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ okwaayeli nibii tamɔ kookoo ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛná maŋ shika. Bei pii lɛ, nɔyelii tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe osharai ni gbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he lɛ amli koni amɛkɛ dumɔwui aha yaka. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ yelikɛbuamɔ kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛyeɔ abuaa okwaafoi ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛ kpakpa nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa cacao tso bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni efeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts before planting maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei dani madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts put natural fertilizer (nitrogen) into the soil through their roots. Planting maize after groundnuts allows the maize to feed on this leftover nutrients, helping it grow taller and yield more without needing as much store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii (nitrogen) fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why is leaving cleared grass to rot on my field better than burning it off before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaaha jwɛi ni egbi lɛ agbo yɛ ŋmɔ mli fe nɔ ni ashã dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning grass destroys soil nutrients and kills helpful earthworms. Letting cleared weeds decay naturally creates organic compost, which holds moisture in the ground during dry spells and feeds your crops over time.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni he tse lɛ fite yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli, ni ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot and turn yellow when standing water remains in my field after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air from the soil to breathe just like humans do. When standing water covers the soil for too long, roots suffocate, drown, and begin to decay, preventing the plant from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ nu mli, ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off during the dry season, and does it mean the crop is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to save water and prevent drying out. The plant is still alive underground, focusing its energy on building tubers, and it will sprout fresh leaves as soon as rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni nu akafite ni amɛkagbi. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo. Nɔ ni agbalaa jwɛŋmɔ kɛyaa nɔ ji yitso lɛ maa. Ni ebaatswa baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why do I need to use wooden stakes to support my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni mikɛfiɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ he hiaa mi lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves higher off the hot ground toward sunlight. Staking allows sunlight to reach every leaf and improves airflow, which keeps the plant healthy and produces bigger subterranean tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ baa fɛɛ baa he ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear in huge numbers on my young maize shoots after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo je kpo trukaa yɛ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay thousands of eggs that hatch right when soft, tender maize shoots emerge after early rains. Checking the center leaves of young maize plants weekly helps you catch and treat these caterpillars before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii akpei abɔ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ kɛji ŋmeii bibii je kpo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ pɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ daa otsi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ ŋmãa nɛɛ ni otsa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why should I clear wild weeds from around the edges of my vegetable farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie koo mli jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Weeds around farm borders act as breeding grounds and hiding places for insect pests and plant diseases. Keeping borders clean prevents these pests from migrating directly onto your main food crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji husui lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai fɔɔ yɛ kɛ he ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ. Kɛ́ oha husui lɛ ahe tse lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafã kɛya oniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Concentrated fertilizer placed directly on plant stems chemically burns the tender bark and roots. Placing fertilizer in a ring a few inches away allows the outer roots to safely draw in the nutrients with soil water.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa tsofai shãa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ni amɛkɛ sũ mli nu lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seed corn instead of planting leftover seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe kernel ŋmãa ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ piɛ ngɛ ye nyagbe ngmɔ ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to yield heavily and resist common diseases. Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, resulting in uneven plant sizes and lower overall harvests.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba ni ekɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ atsu nii. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛi kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that quickly lose moisture when exposed to direct sun. Planting plantains alongside them provides natural shade and preserves soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la.

english: How can I tell if the cocoa seed varieties I am planting are approved for high yield in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ akpɛlɛ kookoo henɔ ni miduɔ lɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii babaoo yɛ Ghana?

english: Approved varieties are certified by official cocoa research nurseries and seed production units. They are specially bred to produce pods faster, yield more beans per tree, and resist common local diseases compared to uncertified seeds.
ga: Kookoo niiamlipɛimɔ hei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ kui haa henɔi ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ he odaseyeli. Atsɔse amɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛfee pods oya. Ha ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso fɛɛ tso mli. kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ ahe.

english: Which type of plantain sucker is best for me to dig up and plant on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a strong bulb at the bottom—are best. They establish strong roots faster and grow into healthier plantain trees than suckers with wide, broad leaves.
ga: Sword shoots, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛ bulb ni mli wa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa oya ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ.

english: How many years should I wait before my newly planted cocoa trees start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ aje shishi ewo ŋmeii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties typically begin flowering and bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional cocoa types take 5 years or more to yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo ni etsɛ waa lɛ heɔ afii 5 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small portion become pods. Shedding happens naturally if the tree lacks water, missing essential soil nutrients, or if there are not enough small insects called midge flies to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ Kɛkɛ ni ebatsɔ pod Shedding baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ gliders lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Will pruning branches off my grown cocoa trees reduce the total amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ajie niji kɛjɛ kookoo tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ fɛɛ aba shi?

english: No, proper pruning actually increases your yield. Removing extra or weak branches lets light reach the trunk where flowers form, improves air circulation to stop diseases, and ensures the tree sends food to healthy pods.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onibii ni owoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni helai akpa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii yaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my plantain plants turning yellow before the bunch is fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani panicles lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or is experiencing water stress. Adding manure or balanced fertilizer helps keep leaves green so the tree can support heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. loo nu mli haomɔ he naagbai ni akɛkpeɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye abua plantain tsei ni tsii lɛ.

english: How does leaving tall weeds around my young cocoa plants affect how fast they grow?
ga: Te jwɛi kakadaji ni mishiɔ yɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ saa bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Tall weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from young cocoa roots. They also block airflow and hide harmful insects, which slows down cocoa growth and makes seedlings weak.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu naa, ni ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ dalɛ baa shi ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet weather and excess shade. Clearing heavy shade, pruning branches, and picking infected pods promptly helps keep the farm dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shade ni fa fe nine mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jiemɔ hulutsoo ni tsii lɛ kɛjɛ mli. tsei ni afoɔ Ni ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oooŋɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ekpa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the stems of my cocoa tree swelling up and showing swollen spots on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fũuɔ ni hei ni fũuɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems are a major sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Because there is no chemical cure for the virus, infected trees must be cut out to protect the remaining healthy cocoa trees on your farm.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu lɛ ji okadi titri ni tsɔɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ ji akɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni baanyɛ atsa hela lɛ. Esa akɛ afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛbu kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer upper leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow lots of green leaves but very few pods when I add chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi pods fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fata he?

english: Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen in the soil. If you add too much rich fertilizer, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall green stems and leaves instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ tsei kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ ni ji eŋɔli. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why do weed seeds keep growing even after I dig up and clear my land completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi dumɔwui yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni mifo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mijie jɛmɛ po lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant deep in the soil for years. When you turn over the soil during clearing, you expose those hidden seeds to sunlight and oxygen, which triggers them to wake up and germinate.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. Ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Beni otsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be mli ni ojieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Nakai dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa amɛteɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly and stop growing big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa aduawai wuji lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the leaf sap and spread viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: What causes my yam leaves to develop dark brown spots and die before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads quickly during heavy rain. Planting clean seed yams and clearing infected leaves helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Sweet potatoes ni he tse ni aduɔ ni ajieɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rainy season lasts too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When rain floods the ground for a long time, the roots drown from lack of air, allowing rot-causing organisms in the wet soil to destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any tomatoes during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the pollen inside tomato flowers dries out and fails to fertilize the plant. Without successful pollination, the plant drops its flowers to conserve water and energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ tso lɛ awo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Groundnuts flower above the ground, but once the flower is pollinated, the stem grows downward into the soil so the nuts can safely grow and mature underground away from heat and animals.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ shwie shi lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni hulutsoo kɛ kooloi bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg fruits get dark, sunken soft spots at the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplants ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebote shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. When soil dries out completely between waterings, the plant cannot transport calcium to the fruit properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛ calcium aya aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is this cocoa disease people call 'kokoo sasabrɛ' that causes the tree stems to swell?
ga: Mɛni ji kooo hela ni gbɔmɛi tsɛɔ lɛ ‘kokoo sasabrɛ’ ni haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Kokoo sasabrɛ' is the local name for Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. It causes swollen stems and roots, leaf discoloration, and smaller pods, eventually killing the cocoa tree if left unmanaged.
ga: Koku Sasabra’ ji maŋ lɛ mli gbɛi ni akɛtsɛɔ kookoo bud hela lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ fuuɔ, baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaanyɛ eha kookoo tso lɛ agbo kɛji atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why are the branches on my cocoa trees swelling up and taking a strange shape like a disease called 'wafuo'?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efuu ni amɛhe yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ? Tamɔ hela ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘wafuo’ lɛ?

english: Swollen branches, often referred to locally as 'wafuo', are a key symptom of swollen shoot disease. It is caused by a plant virus transmitted by small sap-sucking insects called mealybugs.
ga: Niji ni efuu, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli akɛ ‘wafuo’ lɛ ji okadi titri ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso niji ni efuu lɛ hela. Tso mli hela ko ni koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why do the young leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow with red veins instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Discolored leaves with red patterns or yellow veins are often the earliest warning sign of a viral infection like swollen shoot disease, showing that the plant's nutrient transport system is damaged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni etsake su ni yɔɔ tsuru loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji mra be mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko eba, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ efite.

english: My cocoa farm is getting older and producing fewer pods every year; do cocoa trees stop bearing fruit as they age?
ga: Mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ miigbɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ baa daa afi. Ani cacao tsei lɛ kpaa yibiiwoo beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, as cocoa trees age past 25 to 30 years, their natural yield drops significantly. Old trees become less efficient at absorbing nutrients and become more vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, akɛni cacao tsei hiɔ shi fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 hewɔ lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi waa. Tsei ni edara lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: Why is my cocoa farm yielding less cocoa now than it did ten years ago even though the leaves still look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ kookoo fioo fe afii 10 ni eho nɛ lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lolo moŋ?

english: Over many years of harvesting, nutrients in the soil get depleted, and older trees suffer internal wear and low-level infections that reduce pod production even if the leaves look healthy.
ga: Yɛ kpamɔɔ afii lɛ amli fɛɛ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Ni tsei ni edara lɛ naa mligbɛ fitemɔ kɛ helai ni baa shi ni haa pod lɛ feemɔ baa shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa po.

english: Why do extension officers advise cutting down cocoa trees infected with swollen shoot disease instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛshishifãi efuu lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsofa ko kɛkɛ?

english: Swollen shoot is caused by a virus living inside the tree's vascular system. Chemical sprays only kill insects on the outside, so cutting down infected trees is the only way to prevent the virus from spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Virus ni hiɔ tso lɛ lá gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni efuu baa. Tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ pɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How does a disease like 'kokoo sasabrɛ' move from my neighbor's cocoa farm into my own farm?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni hela ko tamɔ ‘Koku Sasabra’ fã kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The virus is carried by tiny insects called mealybugs, which are moved between farms by ants, wind, or farmers carrying infected plant material on their tools and clothes.
ga: Koolooi bibii gbɛɔ helai amli. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Akɛ ŋmeii, kɔɔyɔɔ loo okwaafoi ni hiɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ amɛdɛŋdadei kɛ atadei anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ.

english: If I cut down cocoa trees infected with swollen shoot disease, can I plant new cocoa seedlings in the same spots right away?
ga: Kɛ́ afo kookoo tso ko ni eshishifãi efu lɛ, ani abaanyɛ adu kookoo tso hee yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to wait a few months and plant shade crops like plantains first. This starves out remaining mealybugs so they cannot attack your new, vulnerable cocoa seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baagbe mealybugs fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkatutua kookoo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ.

english: Does having too much shade on my cocoa farm cause crop diseases to stay around longer?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ha yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei ahe helai ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Excess shade creates cold, dark, and damp conditions that favor fungal diseases like black pod disease, though moderate shade is still necessary to protect cocoa trees from harsh sunlight.
ga: Shade babaoo haa shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli ejɔ ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ baa, eyɛ mli akɛ shade ni fa fioo he miihia lolo koni akɛbu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he moŋ.

english: Can planting barrier crops around my cocoa farm protect my trees from getting diseases from nearby farms?
ga: Gbɛtsii nii ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mitsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ amli lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting a buffer line of thick non-host plants like citrus or plantain around your farm helps block mealybugs and wind from carrying viruses into your healthy cocoa crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni mli tse ni jeee gbɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Buffer ŋmɔ baaye abua ni mealybugs kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ akakɛ helai aba o-cocoa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from excessive sun heat and keeping the soil moist so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my pineapples get scorched and turn pale on one side before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ efã kome dani eshɛɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Pineapple fruit gets sunburned when exposed to intense, direct heat from the sun for long hours. Covering the ripening fruits with dry straw or leaf litter protects them from heat damage.
ga: Hulu shãa pineapple yibii kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ wo amɛmli ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ahe sũ ha aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu aduawai lɛ ahe koni la akafite amɛ.

english: Pale yellow leaves are a signal that your maize crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow. Feeding the soil with compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does leaving cut weeds on top of the farm soil help my crops during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with cut weeds creates a protective blanket called mulch. This blanket blocks direct sunlight from hitting the ground, keeping the soil cool and preserving moisture for your crop's roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni afo lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does heavy rainwater wash away the rich soil on the sloping areas of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater collects speed as it flows down a slope, carrying away the loose topsoil that holds plant nutrients. Planting crops in rows across the slope rather than up and down helps slow water down and keep the soil in place.
ga: Nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa oya beni ehoɔ kɛyaa gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni toɔ tsei amli niyenii lɛ mli lɛ ni etswaa lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ moŋ fe ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ baa shi ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled and patchy leaves usually indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. This sickness stops the plant from producing enough food, resulting in small or thin cassava roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ yucca mosaic hela. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛhe waaa.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly humid conditions. Trimming extra branches to let air and sunlight through the canopy helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around one stem, they all steal water and plant food from each other. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce a much heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains akui ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant multiple maize seeds together in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome yɛ bu kome mli.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the young plants to fight for the exact same spot of water and food. Giving each seed its own space allows roots to spread out so the plants grow tall and produce full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ awuu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ he kome. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ada ni ewo ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my young oil palm trees drop their early flowers without forming fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso bibioo lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Young oil palm trees often shed early flowers if they lack sufficient water or nutrients, or if the tree is not yet mature enough to support heavy fruit. Proper feeding and patient care will allow full fruit bunches to form as the tree matures.
ga: Mu tsei bibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi oya kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo kɛji tso lɛ edako bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii ni tsii Niyenii ni sa kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa baaye abua ni ewo yibii ni eyi obɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How do I know if it is safe to start planting my crops when the rains come late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi tsei kɛji nugbɔ nɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the soil stays moist for a few days after a rain, rather than planting immediately after the very first light shower, so seeds do not dry up and die in the dry soil.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ, moŋ fe ni ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛkagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my seeds if I plant them in dry soil and the rain takes two weeks to come?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ otsii enyɔ kroko?

english: Seeds left in dry soil can spoil, get eaten by insects or birds, or fail to germinate properly, which leads to weak crops and empty spots in your field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbo. Kpluka loo okpo ko emɔ bo loo ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa oŋmɔji amli.

english: Is it too late to plant my food crops in November, or can they still survive?
ga: Ani eshɛ sɛɛ tsɔ akɛ madu mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ November mli loo amɛbaahi shi lolo?

english: Late November is usually too dry for standard crops, but quick-maturing crop varieties or fields with access to river water can still yield a successful harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, November naagbee lɛ mli egbi tsɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Shi tsei loo ŋmɔji ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni nu yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ omanye lolo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize curl up and turn yellow when the sunny days last too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from high heat and reduce water loss, but yellowing shows the crop is under extreme drought stress and needs moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli, ni ehe miihia ni ená ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Will my crops still produce good yield if the rain stops completely right after they flower?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Flowering is the most crucial stage for crops; if rains stop completely during this time, flowers may drop off and seeds or fruits will not fill properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbee shi ni dumɔwui loo aduawai eyimɔ obɔbɔ kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my young plants are suffering from strong heat or lack of soil water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo ni fe nine loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ?

english: If plants droop only in the hot afternoon but recover by morning, it is heat stress; if they stay wilted and dry early in the morning, the soil lacks water.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli pɛ shi ehiɛɔ shi leebi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛji amɛgboi lolo ni amɛgbi leebi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How does covering the ground around my crops with dry leaves help them during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni mikɛ baai gboi haa tsei lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks hot sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why do crops planted at the bottom of a valley stay green longer than crops on top of a hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ shishi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe tsei ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Valley soils collect water that flows down from hillsides and hold moisture deep underground much longer into the dry period than high slope fields.
ga: Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔji lɛ amli lɛ mli, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmɔji ni ŋshɔkei lɛ yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ.

english: Should I switch to short-season crop seeds when the rainy season starts late in the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsake kɛya dumɔwui ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ afi lɛ naagbee?

english: Yes, short-season seeds mature faster, allowing you to harvest your food before the rain stops completely and the heat sets in.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni yeɔ be kuku lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii dani nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ ni latsaa lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout out of the ground even after a good rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if planted too deep in the soil, if the soil is packed too hard, or if the seeds were old and lost their power to germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Aloo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ dɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is too worn out to grow a good maize crop this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ efite tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ madu ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: If your soil is hard, pale, and previous crops grew thin with yellow leaves, the land has lost its nutrients. Adding compost, animal manure, or letting the land rest helps rebuild soil health before you plant.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔŋ komɛi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ efo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani adu nii.

english: What will happen to my land if I keep growing cassava on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil until the land fails completely. Rotating cassava with crops like legumes or groundnuts puts nutrients back into the soil naturally.
