ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite kwraa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsake ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does using a planting machine help my farm compared to planting seeds by hand with a hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akɛ niji duɔ kɛ ŋmei lɛ he?

english: A planting machine places seeds at an equal depth and distance very quickly across the whole field. This ensures almost all seeds sprout together evenly while saving you time and heavy physical labor.
ga: Mɔ ni duɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ kome mli oya. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ be kɛ niji nitsumɔ baa shi.

english: Why is it better to plow my field with a tractor before the main rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ trakta baatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Plowing before heavy rains breaks up hard ground so early rainfall can soak deep into the soil. It also makes it easier for young plant roots to spread quickly once seeds are planted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ anyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo hu kɛha tsei bibii ashishifãi akɛ amɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that shocks young seedlings, or cold soil that stops roots from taking up nutrients. Waiting until the rains are regular protects young crops from dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ahe feɔ shoo. loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ Mɛmɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe koni amɛkagboi.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees wilting and drying up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains near them protects the seedlings from severe sun heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli dɔlɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava tubers come out thin and woody instead of big and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛfee blɛoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain small and woody when planted in soil that is too hard and packed, or when left in the ground past their ideal harvest time. Loose, soft soil allows tubers to swell easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho kpamɔɔ be ni sa lɛ he Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ bulbs lɛ baafu.

english: Why are holes appearing in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars eating the middle part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ye nii yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: That is an attack by Fall Armyworms, which target the growing center of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying proper pesticides or neem treatments saves the crop from total destruction.
ga: Nakai ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ kwraa.

english: Under intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it up. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass mulching keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni egbi shwie tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How do I tell the exact right time to harvest my maize so it does not spoil on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmɔ lɛ akafite?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husk turns dry and brown, and the grain feels hard when pressed with a fingernail. Harvesting too late exposes crops to farm pests and mold from late rains.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ akɛ nine ŋmei miimɔ amɛ. Nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ mli baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a larger harvest from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting seeds too close causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This results in weak, thin stalks and tiny corn cobs, whereas proper spacing yields bigger, healthier crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nii lɛ adara ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil season after season. Rotating different crops, like swapping maize with beans or groundnuts, gives the soil time to rebuild its nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to heap the soil into high mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ sũ ni nɔ kwɔ ato dani odu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep under the ground and need loose, soft soil to expand easily. Mounds also prevent heavy rainwater from drowning the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Gɔji hu tsiɔ nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekabote shishifãi lɛ amli ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground when it rains continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: When rain saturates heavy soil without proper drainage, water blocks air from reaching the roots. Without air, the roots suffocate and rot-causing germs in the soil easily destroy the cassava.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu tsɔɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni helai ni haa sũ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baafite ŋmei lɛ oya.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my dry-season vegetables with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo mi-be mli aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, protects the dirt from hot sunshine. It traps water in the ground so you irrigate less often and keeps the soil cool for healthy root growth.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ muji he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa okɛ nu awo mli shii abɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ koni shishifãi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or insect attacks. The plant drops flowers to save energy to survive rather than using energy to grow fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves, or transmitting a plant disease. Treating the insects early helps the leaves grow flat and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo amɛji mɛi ni kɛ tsei ahe helai baa Kooloi bibii ahe tsamɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yields even after I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight intended for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do improved seeds from the agricultural office give better harvests than the seeds I save from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, tolerate drought, and produce uniform crops, whereas seeds saved year after year gradually lose their strength and yielding power.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baafite fiofio Hewalɛ kɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I easily test if my crop seeds are still good quality before I plant them in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ lolo yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can place a sample of seeds in a bowl of clean water; healthy, solid seeds will sink to the bottom while light, insect-damaged, or empty seeds will float to the top.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwu lɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ awo nu ni mli tse mli. Dumɔwui ni mli wa ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni kooloi efite, loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why do some of my crop seeds fail to come up out of the soil after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep, eaten by ants or soil bugs, planted in dry soil, or if the seeds were already old and decayed before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Aŋmeii loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ. adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni amɛmiifite dani adu

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, making the whole plant weak and reducing the size of the harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young crop plants turn yellow instead of deep green early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is missing essential food like nitrogen from the soil, or that too much standing water around the roots is suffocating the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle ehe. Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my crop flowers fall off the plant before turning into fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Crop flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, severe dry spells, or when pests feed on the delicate blossoms before pollination happens.
ga: Tso lɛ fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛhe fɔfɔi.

english: Why does my farmland yield much less food now than it did ten years ago when I started farming it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii faaa kwraa fe bɔ ni eji afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ beni mibɔi okwaayeli lɛ?

english: Planting crops on the same piece of land year after year drains the natural food from the soil, so you need to restore it using manure, compost, or resting the land.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ atsu nii ni okɛsaa lɛ.

english: Why should I plant different types of crops on the same farm plot from one season to the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛjɛ be kome mli kɛyashi be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Rotating crops breaks the cycle of pests and soil diseases that target specific plants, and different crops help put back nutrients that previous crops used up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ kɛtsu nii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly during short dry spells while my neighbor's crops stay fresh and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni akutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo lɛ.

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass or leaves traps water in the soil and keeps root systems cool during hot dry weather.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ koni nu lɛ amɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ

english: Why is it helpful for both men and women in our community to be involved in selecting seeds for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ hii kɛ yei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ baahala dumɔwui ni amɛbaadu lɛ?

english: Involving everyone combines different farming experiences; traditional seed selection by women ensures careful sorting for healthy, clean seeds, which leads to better harvests for the whole household.
ga: Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ okwaayeli mli niiashikpamɔi srɔtoi feɔ ekome. Kusum dumɔwui ni yei halaa lɛ haa akwɛɔ koni ahala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni he tse. Enɛ haa shia muu lɛ fɛɛ náa nikpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong direct sunlight. Without shade from larger trees or companion crops like plantains, the hot sun scorches their tender leaves and dries out their roots before they can establish deep roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo bɛ kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni egbiɔ shishifãi lɛ dani amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers if I do not provide tall sticks for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ misaaaa tso nine kakadaŋŋ ahãaa amɛ koni amɛkwɔ nɔ hu?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch maximum sunlight. When they climb tall stakes, their leaves spread out to capture light efficiently, which gives the plant energy to feed and expand the growing tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Beni amɛkwɔ sũ kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwaa koni amɛmɔmɔ la jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip along the middle line while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This yellowing pattern is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. When there is not enough nitrogen in the soil, the maize plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the newer leaves at the top to survive.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Abele lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli koni ehi shi.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm help my maize crop grow better in the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the leaves and roots decay, they leave behind natural nitrogen that feeds the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni ekɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. The damaged tissue distorts as the leaf attempts to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Fãji ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ be mli ni baa lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the afternoon even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Ani nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: This is typically caused by bacterial wilt, a soil pathogen that enters through the plant roots. The bacteria multiply inside the stem and block the tiny tubes that carry water upward, causing the plant to collapse from internal dehydration.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli kɛboteɔ mli Bacteria babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛtsiɔ tsɔnei bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. ni kɛ nu baa ŋwɛi Ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nu ni bɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide deep inside the leaf funnel of my young maize plants and chew holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is the characteristic behavior of the Fall Armyworm. The central whorl of the maize plant provides moist shelter and soft, nutrient-rich young leaves for the pest to feed on safely away from birds and hot sun.
ga: Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni Fall Armyworm subaŋ lɛ feɔ enii ehaa. Abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ he ko ni mli edɔ kɛ baai bibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ koni eye shweshweeshwe. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ okpoi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rains make water stand on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shiɔ nu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the field for days without draining, it starves the roots of air, causing them to drown and decay underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ. Ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes during very hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures damage the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When heat stress is too severe, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni etsĩɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛ́ latsaa he haomɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains right when the fruit bunch becomes big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems rather than deep taproots. When a heavy fruit bunch develops, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for rainwater to soften the topsoil and strong winds to pull the shallow roots right out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná nɔ ni fe fɛɛ. Ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mlɛo oya. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Enyɛɔ ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eba

english: Why does weed killer medicine sometimes make my pepper plants wilt alongside the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ kɛfataa jwɛi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Chemical weed killers can drift in the wind or linger in the soil. Pepper plants are sensitive, so if the spray touches their leaves or gets absorbed by their shallow roots, it disrupts their ability to take up water, causing them to wilt.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ afo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ loo amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Pepper tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ kpe loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔ mli lɛ, etsĩɔ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaaŋɔ nu lɛ naa. ni eha amɛgbi

english: Will spraying pest medicine too close to harvest time make my cassava unsafe to eat?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ kpamɔ lɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha mi-cassava lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ?

english: Yes, crops hold onto chemical residues for a specific number of days after spraying. If you harvest too early, the chemical has not broken down yet, which leaves harmful toxins in the food.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei lɛ baahiɛ tsofa ni eshwɛ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ashwie amɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji okpa mra tsɔ Tsofai lɛ efiteee lolo. ni shĩɔ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ niyenii lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ewo mli po lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve so the roots can drink it. If the soil is too dry, or if you applied the wrong type of nutrient, the plant cannot absorb food and its leaves will turn yellow from stress.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo okɛ niyenii ni ejaaa tsu nii Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii. Ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ haomɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young flowers during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fioo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When the weather is extremely hot and dry, cocoa trees get stressed and drop their flowers to save water and protect themselves. Keeping shade trees and mulching around the base keeps the soil cool so flowers stay on the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil before sprouting when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: When soil gets soaked with too much water, it cuts off air to the seeds. Without air to breathe, the seeds weaken and fungal rot in the wet soil attacks them before they can sprout.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni abaanyɛ amu Dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How do I know if the insects on my tomato plants are damaging the crop or helping it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo amɛmiiye amɛmiibua lɛ?

english: Insects that bite leaves, bore into stems, or make fruit rot are pests. However, insects like bees visit flowers to help fruits form, and spiders eat harmful bugs, so you should only spray when you see clear crop damage.
ga: Abuɔ kooloi bibii ni ŋmɔɔ baai, amɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli, loo amɛhaa aduawai fiteɔ lɛ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Shi kɛlɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yasaraa fɔfɔi koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai lɛ. Ni ŋmeii yeɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ oshara. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ pɛ kɛji obaanyɛ ona tsei ni efite lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with small tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ bulbs bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and stretch upward instead of putting energy into growing big roots underneath the ground. Proper spacing allows sunlight to fuel tuber growth.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkwɛ shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa tuber lɛ daa.

english: How does animal manure improve my crop growth compared to store-bought chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ ahe?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the crop quickly for a short time, but manure builds up the soil structure itself. It helps the soil trap moisture longer and slowly feeds the crop throughout the entire growing season.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii oya yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shishitoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ fiofio. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year if I plant maize on the exact same farm plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that plant needs and lets pests that feed on it build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like legumes puts nitrogen back into the land.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni amɛha kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I cut off some side branches from my tomato plant, won't that reduce my harvest?
ga: Kɛ mifo mi-tomato tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ, Ani no haŋ minitsumɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Cutting off extra side branches actually forces the plant to send its water and food straight to the growing fruits, resulting in larger, healthier tomatoes rather than lots of weak leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii aya tso lɛ yibii ni miida lɛ he. Enɛ haa tomatoi ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai bibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are crabs constantly digging burrows and destroying my lowland crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋlooi shwieɔ bu ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mi ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Crabs live in wet, muddy soils like swampy rice fields or riverbanks. They dig holes to stay moist and cool, but in doing so, they chew through young crop roots and fell tender shoots.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ, ni mli ewo muji tamɔ omɔ ŋmɔji loo faa naa. Amɛfoɔ bui koni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe ajɔɔ. Shi kɛ́ amɛfee nakai lɛ Amɛyeɔ tsei bibii ashishifãi ni amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii bibii amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How can I keep wild animals like grasscutters from eating my crops at night?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛkɛ?

english: Wild animals come out at night searching for easy food. Clearing the tall bushes around the edges of your farm removes their hiding spots, and setting up boundary fences or strong-smelling organic repellents keeps them away.
ga: Koolooi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo koni amɛbatao niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔle oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie hei ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ gbogbo loo tsofa ko ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ to he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkabote mli.

english: Can local plant mixtures or herbal treatments really protect my crops from pests?
ga: Ani maŋ lɛ mli tsei loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, extracts from local plants like neem leaves or hot pepper contain natural chemicals that taste bitter or are toxic to insects, repelling them without harming your crops or the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli tamɔ neem baai loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni mli edɔ loo ni gbeɔ kooloi. Enɛ shwieɔ amɛ ni eyeee onibii loo oshikpɔŋ lɛ awui.

english: Why do tiny insects hide on the underside of my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Insects hide under leaves to protect themselves from hot sunlight and heavy rain while feeding on the plant's juicy sap, which weakens the plant and stops it from growing properly.
ga: Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves mean your crops are missing essential nutrients, usually nitrogen, in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ otso lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon heat but perk up by the next morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛfeɔ ehee enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ?

english: Under strong afternoon sun, plants lose water faster through their leaves than their roots can pull from the dry soil. At night, when temperatures cool down, the roots catch up and replenish the moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ gbɛkɛ, be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ baafata he.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my pepper plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when there are no bees around to pollinate them. Keeping the soil moist helps fruits set.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baanyɛ afee pollination Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are crops on one side of my farm growing taller than crops on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ miiya hiɛ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality is rarely uniform across a farm. Areas with deeper, richer topsoil or better water retention will grow bigger plants than spots with hard, nutrient-poor soil or heavy shade.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ jeee nɔ kome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Hei ni sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli kwɔ loo nu ni hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baadara fe hei ni sũ ni wa, ni niyenii bɛ mli loo ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli waa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast even right after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can sleep deep in the soil for years. When you disturb the land during clearing, you bring those buried seeds up into the sunlight and moisture, causing them to sprout immediately.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ afii babaoo. Kɛji ogbala shikpɔŋ lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni ojieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Obaahã nakai dumɔwui ni afu lɛ ahi hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: How do I stop insects and weevils from eating my harvested grain during storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ yɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Storage pests need moisture and warmth to thrive. Make sure your grains are fully dried in the sun until hard before storing them in sealed, airtight sacks kept off the cold floor in a dry room.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ latsaa koni amɛshwere. Kwɛmɔ akɛ oŋmaa lɛ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛwo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum efo mli ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli egbi mli lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and dry out quickly. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains provides a canopy that protects young cocoa from sun damage and preserves moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni ashiɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo aduɔ plantains lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in the sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground on stakes allows them to capture more sunlight and air, which results in larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young sucker shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one plantain tree, they all compete for the same water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ, single plantain tso Dumɔwui fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize are a clear signal that the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to build strong, green leaves, so when it runs out, the plant takes it from old leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ etee lɛ Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field before I plant maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the dirt. When you plant maize afterward, it uses that natural fertilizer left behind to grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ baatsu nii koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni baai egbi loo jwɛi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating water from the earth. It keeps the roots cool, conserves water, and prevents weeds from growing easily.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ akajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ, ehaaa nu ahi shi, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots get soft and rot when left in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the ground stays flooded for too long, water blocks air from reaching the cassava roots. Starved of oxygen, the tubers weaken, allowing soil fungi and bacteria to attack and cause rotting.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ Yitso lɛ bagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi tutuaa ni amɛkɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck juices from the underside of leaves and transmit plant viruses. The damage prevents the leaf from opening normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baa tsei amli Nɔ ni efite lɛ haaa baa lɛ agbele bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot get fertilized. Unfertilized flowers cannot form fruit, so the plant drops them to save energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔmɔ nyɛŋ aba mli. Fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal water, light, and fertilizer faster than your crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I make sure my young crops survive the heavy sun after planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mitsei bibii lɛ baahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ mli beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crops have delicate root systems that dry out quickly. Providing temporary shade, applying mulch around the base to retain soil moisture, and planting at the start of the rainy season help them establish strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. be kukuoo mli shade Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Ni kɛ́ adu mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Which fast-growing crops can young people plant to get a quick harvest and early income?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya oblahii kɛ oblayei baanyɛ adu koni amɛná ŋmaa oya ni amɛná shika oya?

english: Vegetables like okro, pepper, tomato, and short-duration maize mature within three to four months, making them ideal for quick cycles of harvest and income compared to tree crops like cocoa or oil palm.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ okra, ŋmɔtɔ, tomato, kɛ ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha nikpamɔ oya kɛ shika ni anáa kɛ akɛto tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo mu ŋmei he.

english: Crops planted too closely will compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak plants that produce very small yields or no fruit at all.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ kwɔlɔ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ loo amɛwoɔ yibii kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the crop is lacking essential nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the afternoon even when the soil still has some water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo moŋ?

english: Extreme heat causes leaves to lose water faster than the roots can absorb it from the ground. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from drying out, but usually recovers when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my crops producing plenty of green leaves but no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi loo aduawai bɛ mli lɛ?

english: This often happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which encourages the crop to focus all its energy on leaf growth instead of flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: How do I know if my land's soil is healthy enough for cassava to yield well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmei kpakpa?

english: Healthy soil for root crops like cassava is loose, well-draining, and rich in organic matter. If the soil is too hard or compacted, the cassava roots cannot expand easily to grow large tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ adara ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my crop roots rot under the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Root rot occurs when soil stays waterlogged for too long, cutting off oxygen to the roots and creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases to attack and decompose the root tissue.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baatutua shishifãi lɛ amli fãji lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Can crop seeds brought from foreign countries grow successfully in our local soil?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu dumɔwui ni akɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ yɛ wɔmaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Foreign seeds can grow, but they must first be tested to see if they can tolerate local temperatures, rainfall patterns, and common pests. Some foreign varieties require different care or fertilizers to yield well in local conditions.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Shi esa akɛ aka lɛ akwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ana kɛji ebaanyɛ edamɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli latsaa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ anaa. Maŋsɛɛ tsoi srɔtoi lɛ ekomɛi biɔ kwɛmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops yield less food now compared to when I first cleared this farm years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ faaa fe beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming on the same land without restoring soil nutrients depletes the earth. Over time, the crops run out of natural plant food, leading to weaker growth and lower yields.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ atsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaa shi lɛ, ebaaha shibɔlemɔ ŋulami lɛ afite. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii. Enɛ haa dalɛ baa shi ni nibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the farm has too many large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei wuji ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ?

english: While young cocoa needs shade, mature cocoa trees need adequate sunlight to convert food into flowers and pods. Too much shade reduces sunlight, creates damp conditions that encourage fungal diseases, and limits yield.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo bibioo he miihia hulutsoo. Kakao tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛtsake niyenii amɛfee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ha lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ aba shi. Ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ baa. kɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ he husu

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny insects like midges to transfer pollen between flowers. If there are few pollinators, or if the tree suffers from drought or poor soil nutrients, it naturally drops unpollinated or unsustainable flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii hia kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛkɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa loo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ loo sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa lɛ miipiŋ tso lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli loo ni ehiii shi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do some of my tiny young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ Eyɛ bibioo kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: This is often a natural process called 'cherelle wilt.' The cocoa tree thins out extra pods it cannot afford to feed due to limited water or soil nutrients, ensuring the remaining pods can grow to full size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ni ale lɛ akɛ 'cherelle wilt'. Cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye yɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do cocoa trees take three to five years before they start bearing their first fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani cacao tsei jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees must first build a strong root system and a sturdy canopy of branches to store enough energy before they can support the heavy demand of producing flowers and pods.
ga: Esa akɛ cacao tsei lɛ ama shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niji ni mli wa koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ato dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua nibii ni he hiaa waa ni ji fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ni afeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, humid conditions. Rain drops splash the fungal spores from the soil or infected pods onto healthy pods, causing them to rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli Nugbɔ shwieɔ ŋmei mli ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do insect pests like capsids attack only the young leaves and shoots of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ capsid tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ tutuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ baai bibii kɛ amɛshishifãi pɛ lɛ?

english: Young shoots and new leaves are soft and rich in plant sap, making them easy for capsids to pierce and feed on, whereas older branches have tough bark that insects cannot easily penetrate.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii bibii kɛ baai heei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni tsei amli nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kapsid lɛ baabote mli ni eye. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei niji ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni wa ni kooloi nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo.

english: Why does mistletoe growing on my cocoa branches weaken the whole tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni ji mistletoe ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mikoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: Mistletoe is a parasitic plant that drills its roots directly into the cocoa branch to steal water and food made by the tree, starving the branch and reducing pod production.
ga: Mistletoe ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni shwieɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa kookoo niji amli koni eju nu kɛ niyenii ni akɛfee tso lɛ. Hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei niji ni ehaa pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: During dry weather, cocoa trees shed their older leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation, helping the tree conserve moisture in its trunk and roots to survive the drought.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai ni egbɔ lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli.

english: Why does pruning extra branches help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi krokomɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that waste the tree's energy. It also opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and airflow, which reduces diseases and directs food straight to pod growth.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ hoɔ lɛ. Egbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ hu koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni etsɔɔ niyenii lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops start wilting and stop growing when the rain stops coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Crops rely on water to carry nutrients from the soil up into their roots, stems, and leaves. Without enough water, the plant cannot feed itself, cool down, or produce new leaves and fruits, causing it to dry up and stop growing.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya amɛshishifãi, amɛshishifãi, kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ eye ehe niyenii. ŋmɔlɔ loo ebɔɔ baai kɛ aduawai heei Enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ kɛ dalɛ kpaɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too little water during the dry months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu fioo pɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ náaa yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves usually curl up, droop during the hottest part of the day, or turn yellow and brown at the tips. The soil around the plant will also look light in color, dry, and cracked.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei bɛ nu lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ gbee shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli loo etsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ hu baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbi ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Can I safely use water dug out from a well underground to grow my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi bui amli lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, water from a dug well is natural groundwater filtered by layers of soil and rocks beneath your farm. It contains no harm for your crops and is a reliable source of water when there is no rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu bu mli nu ji adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni shikpɔŋ kɛ tɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ shwieɔ mli. Eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui, ni ehaa nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: How does water remain deep under my land even when the surface soil looks completely dry?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni nu yɔɔ lolo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi kwraa moŋ.

english: When rain falls, some of the water sinks deep underground through soil and rocks and gets stored in natural underground pools called groundwater, which stays there even when the sun dries out the surface soil.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu lɛ ekomɛi yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi tɔ̃ɔ kɛtsɔɔ sũ kɛ tɛi lɛ amli. Ni akɛtoɔ adebɔɔ mli nubu ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni atsɛɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli. Ebaahi jɛmɛ kɛji hulu lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩ po.

english: How will buying a motorized water pump help me on my crop farm?
ga: Te nu pɔmp ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ hemɔ baaye abua mi yɛ mi tsei aŋmɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A motorized water pump pulls water quickly from a well, river, or storage tank and pushes it through hoses to your crops, saving you from carrying heavy buckets of water by hand all day.
ga: Nu pɔmpii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ, faa, loo nu ŋtayaa mli oya. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsimɔ kɛtsɔ paipi lɛ mli kɛya onibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haaa okɛ onine awo baagi ni tsii gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What is the benefit of using sprinklers to water my crops instead of pouring water directly on the roots with a bucket?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ baagi baashwie nu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ he?

english: Sprinklers spray water into the air like natural rain, covering a large area evenly. This keeps the leaves cool and moistens the soil gently without washing away topsoil or exposing the plant's roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ. Ehaa he ko ni da pɛpɛɛpɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ blɛoo. ni ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ efɔɔɔ loo ejieee tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akpo.

english: Why is it useful to keep a large water storage tank on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaaha nu tsɛnsi agbo ko ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A water tank allows you to store water pumped from wells or collected from rainfall ahead of time, ensuring you always have water ready to use on your crops if your pump breaks down or a dry spell lasts long.
ga: Nu ŋtayaa haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nu bu mli loo ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ toɔ dani. Enɛ haa onáa nu ni okɛbaatsu nii be fɛɛ be kɛji pɔmp ko fite loo hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ba.

english: Is it possible for me to grow fresh vegetables during the hot dry season when there is no rain at all?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ aduawai heei yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, crops can actually grow very well in the dry season because there is plenty of sunlight. As long as you feed them water continuously using wells, pumps, or sprinklers, they will thrive without rain.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ejaakɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ. Shii abɔ ni okɛ nubu, pɔmp, loo tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ baaha amɛ nu be fɛɛ be lɛ. Amɛbaashwere jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do I still need to spray chemical medicines on my crops if I am already watering them well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lolo lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu ha tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Water gives your crops energy to grow, but it does not stop insect pests or diseases from eating the leaves and fruits. Chemical sprays act like medicine to protect the crop from pests that regular watering cannot control.
ga: Nu haa tsei hewalɛ koni amɛdara. Shi etsĩii kooloi bibii loo helai anaa koni amɛkaye baai kɛ aduawai lɛ. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ nyɛŋ akudɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I mix crop chemicals directly into my water tank or watering pump to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ afutu nu tsɛnsi loo pɔmp lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Some liquid fertilizers can be added to irrigation water, but pesticides and fungicides usually need to be mixed separately and sprayed directly onto the leaves to be effective and safe for the crop.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ ekomɛi awo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii afutu mli srɔtoi ni akɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can watering my crops too much actually kill them?
ga: Ani tsei ni akɛ nu woɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ agbe amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, crops need oxygen around their roots just as much as water. When roots stay submerged in water, they suffocate and fungal diseases move in, causing the roots to rot and turn into dark, dead sludge.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɔleɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bote nu mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Amɛmuɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela baa amɛmli, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ sũ ni mli edɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot into black mush when water settles on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ kɛ́ nu gbee miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a crop that dislikes waterlogging. When standing water sits around cassava tubers, fungal organisms breed rapidly, breaking down the root tissues until they rot completely into dark, smelly liquid.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni sumɔɔɔ nu ni hoɔ. Kɛji nu ŋmɛ Cassava shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya. Ekpãtãa shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ ni egboɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etsɔɔ nu ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli.

english: Is it bad if heavy rainfall sits on my field without draining away?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ mishia lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli?

english: Yes, stagnant water prevents plants from taking up nutrients and creates a breeding ground for rot-causing fungi. Good field drainage is essential to keep plant roots dry and healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia koni tsei shishifãi lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a water-loving fungus that spreads rapidly when excess moisture sits on the pods. The fungus attacks the tissue, turning healthy green pods into black, ruined shells.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine ba ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Fungus tutuaa fãji Etsakeɔ pods eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ewoɔ husks diji ni efite mli.

english: Is it safe for me to pour soapy water from my laundry onto my crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ nu ni akɛ saamɔ yɔɔ mli kɛjɛ mitadei amli lɛ mashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: No, household soap contains chemicals and salts that ruin plant tissue and harm the soil. Washing soap can strip away the natural protective coating on leaves and destroy sensitive crop roots.
ga: Dabi, tsofai kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ tsei ahe fãji ni eyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ shia samlai amli. Samla ni akɛfɔɔ he lɛ baanyɛ ajie adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why did my vegetable leaves turn dark and dry up after I used soapy water to kill insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Strong detergent soaps burn delicate plant leaves by stripping away their protective wax layer. This causes the leaf cells to collapse and die, leaving behind dark, scorched foliage.
ga: Samla ni mli wa shãa tsei ahe baai kɛtsɔ wax ni buɔ he lɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baa mli wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ. Shi baai ni edɔ ni edɔ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Will pouring soapy waste water near my farm spoil the soil for future crops?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ shi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, detergent residues leave behind sodium and chemicals that disrupt the natural microbes in the soil, making it hard for future crop roots to absorb water and oxygen.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛjieɔ muji lɛ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ shĩɔ sodium kɛ tsofai ni fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: What causes my harvested yams to turn into a black mushy mess in storage?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Yams store best in dry, cool conditions. Excess moisture or high humidity encourages rot fungi to enter through tiny cuts, quickly turning the firm yam flesh into black, watery sludge.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine loo fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo woɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni ebote mli kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni afo lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni nu yɔɔ mli oya.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings rot and fall over right at soil level after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is known as damping-off, caused by soil fungi that thrive in cold, wet conditions. Too much water softens the base of the stem until it rots completely black and collapses.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ dampening, ni sũ mli ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa. Nu babaoo baaha tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni ebaagbee shi.

english: How can I tell if a crop I am planting dislikes very wet soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ni miduɔ lɛ sumɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa?

english: Crops that dislike heavy water usually show early warning signs when flooded, such as leaf yellowing, stem softening, and rapid black decay at the soil line, rather than growing faster.
ga: Tsei ni sumɔɔɔ shwiili lɛ jieɔ nu afua he kɔkɔbɔɔ mra kpo, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni egbɔjɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni baa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ oya

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient crops need to stay healthy. It can also happen when the ground is waterlogged or too dry, which stops the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ bei pii amli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha hewalɛnamɔ kpakpa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo egbi tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my farm make the soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have helpful organisms on their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it uses this natural plant food to grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why are small caterpillars suddenly eating the leaves inside my corn plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli lɛ trukaa nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that hatch in large numbers and feed hidden inside the funnel of young corn plants. They eat very fast, so catching them early with natural traps or appropriate sprays is necessary to protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fɔɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni eyeɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Amɛyeɔ nii oya waa. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔmɔ amɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔnei loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni abu onibii ahe.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Heat stresses the flower, preventing it from forming fruit, so the plant drops it to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ haoɔ fɔfɔi tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop's growth even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal sunlight, root space, and soil food meant for your crops. Even with enough water, your crops will starve because weeds take up the nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po baaye hɔmɔ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that create living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni feɔ ambrela. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava stems very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close, their roots compete heavily for soil nutrients and moisture underground. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin, resulting in small, thin tubers instead of big yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 8 to 12 months after planting. Look for signs like the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and small cracks appearing in the soil around the base of the stem as the tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Taomɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi. ni ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli Tso lɛ shishi be mli ni bulb lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra or weak branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes old or shaded branches that waste the tree's energy and block sunlight. Good airflow through the branches reduces fungal diseases like black pod and helps the tree put its energy into growing large pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egbɔ loo ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni etsĩɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji amli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ gbɛ koni efee tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Heavy rainfall washes fertilizer away from the roots before the plant can drink it in. This wastes your money and can wash the fertilizer into nearby streams instead of feeding your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ nuɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaaha okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli moŋ fe ni oooha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen or when the ground is too dry for roots to take up nutrients. Nitrogen acts like main food for green leaf growth; without enough of it, the plant steals nutrients from older leaves to feed young growth, turning the bottom leaves yellow first.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa. Kɛji akɛ eshɛɛɛ Tsei juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni oootsɔ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cowpea crop grow plenty of lush green leaves but produces very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excess leaves and fewer pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when they receive heavy shade. The plant uses its energy to make green leaves instead of shifting its strength into flowering and setting seed pods.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ baai babaoo kɛ ŋmeii fioo kɛji nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ amɛhe ejɔ amɛ waa. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ feɔ baai eŋɔli. Mohu ɔ, e tsakeɔ e he wami ɔ kɛ yaa fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwu ɔmɛ a he.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off during periods of extreme heat or when water supply changes suddenly from dry to very wet. High temperatures stress the plant, causing it to drop its blossoms to survive rather than spending energy growing fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo beni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why do my cassava tubers begin to rot in the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil for days, water fills all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and allowing soil fungus to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and open instead of forming tight, hard balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ nɔ́ ko nɛ wa nɛ e mi mi wa.

english: Cabbage heads fail to firm up when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. Cabbages require continuous moisture and cooler weather to force the inner leaves to pack tightly together into a hard head.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee shiŋŋ kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Cabbage he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ aba be fɛɛ be koni enyɛ emli baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee yitso ni wa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids, or a virus carried by them. As these insects feed on the sap underneath tender young leaves, they damage the tissue, causing the leaves to distort and curl upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, mites loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ Enɛ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ. Amɛfiteɔ fãji. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe.

english: Why are the vines of my yam plants turning black and dying off early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Blackening yam vines are usually caused by a fungal disease called yam anthracnose, which spreads quickly in hot, wet weather. The fungus attacks the leaves and stems, burning them black and preventing the tubers underground from growing to full size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei tsei ni etsɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Fɛ̃i lɛ tutuaa baai kɛ tsei lɛ. shãa ediŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa kɛyashɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that easily scorch under direct sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist so the young cocoa seedlings can establish strong roots before facing harsh sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo dumɔwui baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni wa dani hulu la ni naa wa aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why are the lower fronds of my young oil palm trees turning brown and hanging down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifo shi lɛ?

english: Brown, drooping lower fronds on oil palms are a sign of severe water stress or a lack of potassium in the soil. When the plant cannot get enough water or potassium, it sacrifices its oldest outer leaves to keep the growing center spear alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ mu tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa loo potassium ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana nu loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Ekɛ kponɔgbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ baashã afɔle koni ekɛkwɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that spread sideways near the soil surface rather than going deep. When the plant produces a heavy bunch of fruit, the top becomes heavy, making it easy for wind to pull the shallow roots right out of soft, wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeeya shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ wo yibii ni tsii lɛ, yiteŋgbɛi lɛ feɔ tsii, ni no haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni edɔ oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and dry up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants get sunburned easily when exposed to direct sunlight and extreme heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects delicate leaves until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Hulu shãa cacao tsei bibii oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when they start producing large bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ebɔi yibii babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that struggle to support the heavy weight of a maturing fruit bunch, especially during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a prop stick made from bamboo or a sturdy tree branch prevents the tree from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni eda lɛ akui ni tsii lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso nine ni mli wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip downward even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which maize plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the base of the plant will help restore its green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why am I seeing tiny holes in my young maize leaves with dark powder inside the central whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ, ŋmãa ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides and feeds inside the growing point of the maize plant.
