Applying recommended organic sprays like neem seed extract or proper pest treatments early in the morning or late evening targets the worms before they destroy the crop yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ hei ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ daa lɛ amli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baatutua tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ.

english: Cowpeas and leguminous crops have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots decay after harvest, they release this nitrogen, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop planted in that field.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ legumes yɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni adu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What happens under the soil if I plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close together, their roots fight for limited soil nutrients, water, and space. This competition results in plants producing many small, thin tubers instead of a few large, heavy cassava roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ he ko ni faaa lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ ha tsei lɛ nyɛ amɛwo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo. Mohu ɔ, e ji kaa tso agbo komɛ nɛ a he wami bɔɔ ko pɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce the food required to enlarge the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil toward the sun, which maximizes sunlight exposure and protects the leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem before any tomatoes start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress caused by sudden heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining consistent watering schedules and shading young plants during extreme heat helps blossoms turn into tomato fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli baa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei bibii daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ tomato aduawai.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that feed on the undersides of the leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying neem oil or soapy water under the leaves helps control these pests and prevents further leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baai ashishigbɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi baa lɛ sɛɛkuu kroko naa.

english: Why do my garden eggs and vegetable plants look wilted in the afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During intense heat, vegetable leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can suck up from the ground, causing temporary wilting to conserve moisture. As long as the soil remains moist, the leaves will bounce back when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei ahe baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: How long do I usually have to wait after planting tree crops before I can harvest my first major yield?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ beni midu tso lɛ sɛɛ dani manyɛ makpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji lɛ?

english: Most long-term tree crops like cocoa, cashew, or citrus take about three and a half to four years to fully mature and give a main harvest, though you may start seeing early fruits a few months before the four-year mark.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli babaoo tamɔ kookoo, cashew nuts Aloo eheɔ aaafee afii etɛ kɛ fã kɛyashi ejwɛ dani ŋmei ko shɛɔ shweremɔ he ni ekɛ eŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ obaaje nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ shishi kɛjɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi kɛyashi afii ejwɛ mli moŋ.

english: Is it normal if my young crop trees do not produce any fruit during their first three years?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja kɛji midumɔwui lɛ wooo yibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, that is completely normal. During the first three years, tree crops focus their energy on building strong roots, thick trunks, and healthy leaves before they are strong enough to support fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kwraa. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni wa, ŋmeii ni mli wa, kɛ baai ni wa amamɔ nɔ dani amɛhe waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua aduawai.

english: Can proper farm care help my tree crops start bearing fruit a bit earlier than four years?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ ni sa baaye abua mitsei lɛ ni amɛje yibiiwoo shishi mra fioo fe afii ejwɛ?

english: Yes, giving your crops good fertilizer, proper weeding, and adequate water can speed up their growth, allowing you to see early progress and small yields slightly before four years.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi akɛ oookɛ fɔmɔ nii awo mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ adara oya. Enɛ haa onaa hiɛyaa mra ni owoɔ yibii fioo dani afii ejwɛ baashɛ.

english: What early signs should I look out for on my farm to know my trees are progressing well before they yield?
ga: Mɛɛ mra be mli okadii esa akɛ matao yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana kɛji mitsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ dani amɛwo yibii?

english: You should look for a steady increase in height, lush green leaves, and a thick, sturdy trunk base, which shows the tree is storing enough strength to bear fruit later.
ga: Esa akɛ otao ŋwɛi ŋta ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be. baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishitoo ni mli tse ni mli wa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ toɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ewo yibii sɛɛ mli.

english: Why is the trunk at the base of some of my crop trees becoming very thick while others stay slender?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ ekomɛi ashishi lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kã he amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: A thick base means the plant is absorbing good nutrients and building a strong foundation. Thinner trees may be struggling with poor soil, weeds, or lack of sunlight.
ga: Shishitoo ni mli tse lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shishitoo ni wa baa. Tsei ni mli tseee lɛ baanyɛ abɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, jwɛi, loo hulu la ni bɛ lɛ he mɔdɛŋ.

english: Does a tree crop with a big, wide base mean it will produce a good harvest?
ga: Ani tso ni shishi agbo ni mli lɛɛ ni aaadu lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ebaawo ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Generally, yes. A wide, strong trunk base indicates a healthy root system and a sturdy tree structure that can support a heavy load of pods or fruits without breaking.
ga: Yɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, hɛɛ. Tso lɛ shishitoo ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ tso lɛ shishitoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii loo aduawai ni tsii ni efoŋ.

english: What should I do if my crop trees are almost four years old but still look too small to bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mitso lɛ miihe ashɛ afii ejwɛ shi etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ bibioo tsɔ lolo ni enyɛŋ ewo yibii?

english: You should inspect the trees for pests or diseases, clear surrounding weeds that steal nutrients, and consider applying fertilizer to help them complete their growth into maturity.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ tso lɛ mli kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai komɛi yɛ mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ Ni osusu he akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do I notice that one tree on my farm carries a lot of fruit while the tree right next to it has very few?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɔseɔ akɛ tso kome ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni tso ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo lɛ? Yibii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Even on the same farm, individual trees can differ due to small changes in soil richness, sunlight access, water levels, or natural plant genetics, causing some trees to produce more than others.
ga: yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli po Tso fɛɛ tso baanyɛ afee srɔto yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsakeɔ fioo lɛ hewɔ. hulu la ni anáa, nu mli ŋwɛi ŋta, loo adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe nibii ni haa mɔ he feɔ shoo Enɛ haa tsei komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo fe ekrokomɛi.

english: What causes some trees on the same plot to mature faster than others planted on the exact same day?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ daa oya fe ekrokomɛi ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Differences in underground water pockets, slight variations in shade, or stronger natural genetics can give certain trees an extra boost, making them reach maturity faster than their neighbors.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu nibii amli lɛ tsakeɔ hulutsoo fioo Aloo, adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nii ni mli wa baanyɛ aha tsei komɛi aná hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya fe amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my tree crop is finally ready to transition from growing to full production?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ efee klalo yɛ naagbee akɛ amɛbaatsake kɛjɛ dumɔ mli kɛya nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: You will notice a thick, established base at the soil level, healthy spreading branches, and the steady appearance of flowers and early fruit across the tree.
ga: Obaana shishitoo ko ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niji lɛ gbɛ eshwa waa. kɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni jeɔ kpo mra be fɛɛ be yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure early in the season will turn the leaves green and help the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo mli loo okɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ baa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua ni tso lɛ adara waa.

english: How does planting groundnuts in the same farm with my maize help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally enriches the farm so that companion crops like maize can grow better without needing as much artificial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni fata he tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee lɛ babaoo awo mli.

english: What causes my pepper plant leaves to curl up into small balls?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bɔɔlu bibii?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying the leaves early with neem leaf extract mixed with mild soap water can repel these pests and allow healthy leaves to unfurl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Neem baai lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Okɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ afutu mli. Ebaanyɛ eshwie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do small insects bore holes into my harvested maize while it is stored in the room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ mli be mli ni eyɔɔ nitoohe lɛ?

english: These insects are maize weevils that lay eggs in dry grain. Storing maize in clean, airtight hermetic bags (like PICS bags) suffocates the insects and prevents them from breeding and destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui ni egbi amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa wo vacuum kotoku ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni otsĩ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee babaoo ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping the soil constantly moist with mulch and watering regularly during hot weeks helps the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɔ́ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why are my cassava tubers coming out thin and woody even though the stems look very bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or given too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and thick green leaves instead of sending energy underground to thicken the tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo aha lɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni eŋɔli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ yaa zugba a sisi konɛ e ha nɛ tsɔwi ɔmɛ nɛ a pee tsɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides quick-growing, large leaves that act as natural umbrellas to shade the cocoa trees until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaa baa agboi ni daa oya ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta, ni ehaa kookoo tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulutsoo tso lɛ naa.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow at the base of a plantain stem, they steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Pruning away smaller shoots and keeping only one or two healthy successors leaves enough food for the main tree to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. ŋmeii bibii ni afoɔ Tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden sticks to support my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atsu nii koni mikɛmɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch more sunlight to feed the tubers underground, while keeping leaves away from damp soil reduces fungal rot and leafy diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhaa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛ baai ahe helai aba shi.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I save and replant seeds from last year's hybrid maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo beni mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high performance only in their first planting generation. Replanting seeds harvested from hybrid crops results in weak, uneven plants that yield far less grain than the original seed.
ga: Atsɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni miida ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni woɔ dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize farm curl up tightly like straws during the dry afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl during intense heat as a natural defense to trap moisture and slow down water loss through their surface so the crop can survive hot sun.
ga: Abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni nu ni hoɔ fiofio kɛtsɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ adamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: How does using government irrigation channels help my crops grow better than waiting for the rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔyeli lɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mɛmɔ?

english: Irrigation gives your crops a steady supply of water throughout the year, preventing drought stress and allowing crops to continuously absorb nutrients for higher yields regardless of rain patterns.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa onibii lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Buɔ he kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he haomɔ he ni ehaa tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛha yibiiwoo babaoo ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot and die when heavy rain leaves standing water on my land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe. Standing water suffocates roots and creates conditions for waterborne diseases that rot the roots and kill the plant.
ga: Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi baa kɛha helai ni jɛɔ nu mli baa ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni egbeɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my young cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the soft shade and cool moisture cocoa saplings need to establish roots.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei lɛ afee shishifãi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my cassava turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops lower leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve internal water and send remaining energy down to the underground roots.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without forming fruits when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit formation. The plant sheds unpollinated flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ aduawai anaa Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha wala.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb instead of trailing on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ moŋ fe ni eeenyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb naturally to expose more leaves to sunlight for making food. Staking keeps leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases quickly attack crop leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha baai lɛ aya hulu la babaoo nɔ kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Fungal hela lɛ baatutua tso lɛ baai lɛ oya.

english: Why does plowing my farm land with heavy machines help crop roots grow better than just clearing the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɔnei ni tsii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmeii ni ajieɔ lɛ?

english: Tractor plowing breaks up hard soil layers, creating loose soil that crop roots can easily penetrate to reach deeper nutrients and stored groundwater.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ abote mli oya koni amɛyashɛ niyenii ni mli kwɔ lɛ he ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ ato.

english: Why do my cowpea crops seem to grow strong without me adding commercial nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ daraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni mikɛ jarayeli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally work with friendly soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and convert it into plant food, enriching the soil naturally.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee tsei aniyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli sɛɛnamɔ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do some cocoa trees produce pods all year round while others only bear fruit during the main harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei komɛi woɔ yibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ mli pɛ.

english: Continuous cocoa pod production depends on reliable year-round soil moisture and tree genetics. Trees planted near reliable water sources can flower and fruit outside the standard season.
ga: Cocoa pod feemɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ damɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ sũ mli fɛ̃i ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ tso mli wala yibii nɔ. Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afɔlɔ ni amɛwo yibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient plants need to make food and grow strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer can help restore the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot in heavy rain because waterlogged soil starves the roots of air and allows harmful fungi to thrive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ aná shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal infection called black pod disease, which spreads rapidly in dark, wet conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and wind pass through the farm helps keep the pods dry and free from the fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ kookoo diji baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbiɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up towards the light and keeps them off the hot, damp soil where diseases can easily infect them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ kɛ la lɛ kpeɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni helai baanyɛ ajɛ mli agbɛ ashwã lɛ naa. Ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela lɛ eshwa mlɛo

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers until they turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I cut down the extra young shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing most of them leaves more food for the main tree to produce a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsofai krokomɛi, loo tseitsei, kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo shĩɔ niyenii ahaa tso titri lɛ koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize make the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have special roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When they grow next to maize, they share this natural fertilizer, helping the maize grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ amɛdara yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaajara adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nɛɛ koni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves and spreading viruses. Spraying the plants with neem oil extract helps kill these pests and stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ehaaa baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around No hewɔ lɛ, akɛ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do my stored maize grains end up full of small holes and white powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ powda yɛŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: The holes and powder are caused by tiny insects called weevils that bore into the grains to eat and lay eggs. Drying your maize properly until it is completely hard and storing it in airtight bags or containers prevents weevils from surviving inside.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils ni boteɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli koni amɛye ni amɛwoɔ wɔji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu kɛ powda lɛ baa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa ni akɛto kotoku loo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi yɛ mli.

english: How often do I really need to go to my farm to check on my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miyakwɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You should visit your farm at least once a week. Crops can change quickly, and regular visits help you notice early signs of insect attacks, diseases, or lack of water before your whole field gets destroyed.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsake oya. Ni saramɔi ni afeɔ daa lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi tutua bo, hela loo nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli. dani akpata okpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: What simple things should I look out for when inspecting my crops every week?
ga: Esa akɛ makwɛ mihe jogbaŋŋ yɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ahe. Mɛni ofeɔ kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli daa otsi?

english: Pay close attention to leaf color, look under leaves for hidden insects, check if stems are firm, and feel if the soil is dry. Changes in leaf color or shape are usually the first warning sign a plant gives you.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ su jogbaŋŋ. Taomɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi. Kwɛmɔ kɛji tsɔne lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ loo ehiɛɛɛ shi. Ni ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi loo enuuu he? Bei pii lɛ, baa lɛ su loo bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ tsakemɔ ji klɛŋklɛŋ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tso ko kɛhaa bo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pawpaw trees turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pawpaw tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that your pawpaw plant is stressed. This is usually caused by too much water around the roots, lack of plant food (fertilizer) in the soil, or sap-sucking insects attacking the leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ o-pawpaw tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, nu babaoo ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tso niyenii (ŋmeii) ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni tutuaa baa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up or drop off during the dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When the weather is hot and dry, crops naturally curl or drop leaves to reduce water loss. It is the plant's way of surviving the heat until it gets more moisture.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baabɔle loo ebaagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enine shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo nɔ.

english: What does it mean when the lower leaves of my crops dry up while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: As plants grow, older bottom leaves naturally die off so the plant can send energy to new top leaves. However, if this happens too fast, it usually means your soil needs more nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara lɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ gboiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Shi, kɛji enɛ ba oya tsɔ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why are white powdery spots appearing on the leaves of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔi yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: White powder on leaves is usually a sign of a fungal disease or tiny insects like mealybugs. It blocks sunlight from reaching the leaves, which weakens the plant if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, powda yɛŋ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo kooloi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs, ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ he okadi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: How can I tell if my young pawpaw tree is healthy and ready to give a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-pawpaw tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni efee klalo akɛ ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: A healthy pawpaw tree has wide, dark green leaves, a thick stem, and grows steadily without leaves turning yellow early. Good leaves feed the tree so it can produce big, sweet fruits.
ga: Pawpaw tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ, amɛshishifãi lɛ mli tse, ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛdaraa ni baai lɛ efeee ŋmɔŋ mra. Baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni ewo yibii wuji ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Why are my pawpaw trees flowering but not producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Some pawpaw trees are strictly male and only produce pollen, so they will never bear fruit. Also, if a female or hermaphrodite tree suffers from water stress or extreme heat, it can drop its flowers without setting fruit.
ga: Pawpaw tsei komɛi ji tsei ni hii pɛ yɔɔ mli, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ewoŋ yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛji akɛ tsei ni ji yei loo hermaphrodite lɛ na nu mli haomɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ, Fɔfɔi hu baanyɛ agbo ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Does pawpaw need a lot of water to give good fruits?
ga: Ani nu babaoo he miihia Paw Paw koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pawpaw needs regular water to grow broad leaves and heavy fruits, but its roots easily rot in standing water. The land must drain water well so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Nu he miihia pawpaws daa koni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ amɛyibii ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi eshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli. Esa akɛ nu atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Can I grow other crops like pepper or beans on the same land with my young pawpaws?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ miniji bibii lɛ akwɛ tsei krokomɛi tamɔ pepper loo beans yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop short-season crops like pepper, garden eggs, or beans between young pawpaw plants. This makes good use of your land while the pawpaw trees are still small and not casting too much shade.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli nibii tamɔ ŋmeii, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ pawpaw tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni pawpaw tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni ekɛ hulutsoo babaoo haaa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is no rain for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow during dry spells because plants need water to absorb nitrogen from the soil. Without water, the plant cannot take up nutrients, causing the leaves to lose their green color and stop food production.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei hia nu koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛkpaa niyenii feemɔ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does covering my soil with dry leaves and grass help my crops during the hot season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Covering the soil with organic material, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and prevents weeds from taking light and water from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do my crop roots burn when I apply chemical fertilizer while the soil is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shãa kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are concentrated salts that need moisture to dissolve properly. When applied to dry soil, the fertilizer draws remaining moisture directly out of the plant's roots, causing them to dry out and burn.
ga: Fertilizers ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni biɔ nu ni mli edɔ koni etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ gbalaa nu ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch under direct intense sunlight. Shade trees act as natural umbrellas, protecting cocoa trees from high heat and retaining moisture in the air and soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, forcing the plant to grow tall and weak to reach light instead of using energy to build big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ la ni amɛaana lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee ŋmeii wuji

english: How do I know the best time to harvest my cassava so the tubers do not turn hard and woody?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafee nɔ ni wa ni efee tsei?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping; leaving them in the ground too long makes the roots fibrous, dry, and tough to cook.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmeii, amɛgbi ni ewa akɛ amɛaaho.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat up the leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which crawl into the hidden center (whorl) of young maize plants to feed on new leaves where sprays and predators cannot easily reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ (rings) ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ koni amɛye baai heei yɛ he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe mlɛo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high moisture, cool air, and heavy rain, especially when tree branches are too dense to let sunshine and fresh air dry off the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli, titri lɛ be mli ni tso lɛ niji lɛ mli eyi tsɔ ni eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbi.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one high-yielding generation; planting saved seeds from a hybrid harvest results in lower yields, uneven growth, and weaker resistance to pests and diseases.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ hybrid ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi. shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I protect my crop farm from bushfires during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ koo mli la he yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: You can clear a wide strip of land around the boundary of your farm, removing all dry grass and bushes. This cleared strip, called a fire belt, stops fire from traveling into your farm and burning your investment.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie he ko ni da waa. Oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ band ni mli tse nɛɛ akɛ la bɛlt. Kpa la ni boteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eshãa oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after a fire burns my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ yɛ la ni tso yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds deep under the soil survive the heat. The ash left behind by the fire acts like quick fertilizer, so when the first rains drop, the seeds sprout very fast.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Sũ ni la ni tsoɔ yɛ nsara mli lɛ shiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya waa.

english: Why are the flowers on my mango trees falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mango tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Mango flowers drop when the tree suffers from sudden water shortages or pest attacks. Steady moisture and protecting the blooms during flowering helps them set strong fruit.
ga: Mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu faaa trukaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai batutua tso lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ hebuu yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ haa aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why does my mango tree spend years growing only leaves before giving fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mango tsei kwɛ̃ɔ baai dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Young fruit trees focus their energy on building strong roots, trunks, and branches first. Once the tree is fully established and strong enough to carry heavy weight, it naturally starts fruiting.
ga: Tsei bibii ni woɔ yibii lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi, ŋmeii, kɛ tsei niji ni wa ni amɛmaa lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Beni tso lɛ eda kwraa ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ muji babaoo awo mli lɛ. Ebaabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crop trees drop their leaves when the long dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Trees shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water. Leaves lose moisture fast in hot sun, so dropping them helps the tree save water in its stem and stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi baai lɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ nu yɛ eshishifã lɛ mli, ni ebaahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my tree produce plenty of fruit this year, but gives very little fruit next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ afi nɛɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ, aduawai fioo ko pɛ baaba?

english: Producing a heavy harvest takes a lot of energy from a tree. After a massive harvest, the tree gets exhausted and spends the following year recovering its energy instead of making new fruit.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni abaakpa lɛ biɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. Yɛ kpamɔ wulu lɛ sɛɛ Tso lɛ he ejɔ ni ekɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii heei.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight for sunlight. They stretch upward as fast as possible to catch light, which makes their stems thin, weak, and easy to fall over.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛgbala amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, egbɔjɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my crop seedlings droop and die right after I move them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when their roots are disturbed or exposed to harsh sun during moving. Transplanting late in the afternoon and watering them immediately keeps them healthy.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa shoofeemɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛji akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbala amɛnaa loo hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛduɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ otsi amɛ shwane mli ni okɛ nu ha amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear dry grass away from the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni egbo kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer and water meant for your crops. Removing dry grass around your plants gives them full access to soil nutrients and removes dry material that could easily start a fire.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni yɔɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni ojie nibii ni egbi ni baanyɛ atswa la oya lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing during extremely hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the topsoil, making it hard for roots to drink water and nutrients. The plant turns yellow and slows down growth to protect itself until cooler rainy weather arrives.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaanu nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Tsei lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaafee amɛdalɛ blɛoo koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings need to be planted at a slant instead of flat in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle helps the roots spread deeper into the soil for water, while keeping the growing tubers close enough to the surface for easy harvesting.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji 45-degree lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛbua nu naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha bulbs ni adu lɛ abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he bɔ ni sa koni ekpamɔ afee mlɛo.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed young leaves, showing it needs compost or fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tsitsii lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia bo.

english: Tomato leaves roll up during extreme heat as a natural defense to trap moisture inside and stop water from evaporating quickly into the hot air.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtsi nu naa koni ekaho oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight for energy. Staking also prevents fungal diseases caused by wet soil touching the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛha hewalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ ni mli efɔ ni kɛ baai kpeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines root into the soil wherever they touch the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ekɔɔɔ he eko be ni eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Sweet potato vines naturally form new roots at their joints when they touch moist soil, which helps the plant absorb more nutrients and form extra underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ shishifãi heei yɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce suckers around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miiwo ŋmeii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers are the plant's way of reproducing. Since the main stem dies after bearing one bunch of fruit, these suckers take over as the next generation to produce food.
ga: Plantain ŋmeii ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ tsei ashwaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ tso titri lɛ gboɔ beni aduawai akuu kome eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ nɛkɛ suckers nɛɛ ji yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ niyenii feemɔ mli.

english: Why do some of the tiny young pods on my cocoa tree turn shriveled and black early on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ mra.

english: This is called cherelle wilt. The cocoa tree naturally thins out excess pods it cannot feed with its current water and nutrient levels, saving energy for the pods that remain.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli amrɔ nɛɛ naa. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi kɛha pods ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do sticky threads called silks come out of my maize cobs before corn kernels grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kpãa ni mli wa ni atsɛɔ lɛ siliki lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli dani ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Each silk thread connects to a future kernel inside the cob. Wind carries pollen from the top flowers onto these silks to fertilize them so solid corn grains can form.
ga: Akɛ siliki kpãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tsa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli pollen lɛ kɛyaa siliki nɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo amɛmli kɛyashi amɛfeɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency or waterlogging in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants use to build green leaves, so adding nitrogen-based fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa loo nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close to each other, their roots fight underground for water, nutrients, and physical space. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the tubers room to expand and grow fat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu, niyenii, kɛ he ko ni amɛyɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa bulbs tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni ehaa fɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What causes my tomato fruits to get dark, rotten spots at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ shishi dani eshɛɔ po?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it is forming, often triggered by irregular watering. Ensuring your tomato plants get steady, even moisture helps the roots pull up calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni efeɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ni o-tomato tsei lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Fɛ̃i po yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I save and replant the seeds harvested from my hybrid maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ mi-hybrid corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred first-generation crosses designed to give high yields. If you replant the seeds saved from that harvest, the second-generation crops will grow unevenly and produce much smaller cobs.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ji klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ ni ji hybrid ni afee koni ewo yibii babaoo. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ du ekoŋŋ lɛ, Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ tsei lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food that gets stored in the underground tuber. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight and keeps them off damp soil where fungal diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aba. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ naa he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during very hot and dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: High heat combined with dry soil causes heat stress in pepper plants, forcing them to drop their blossoms to conserve water and survive. Mulching the soil around the plant and watering regularly during hot dry spells keeps the flowers intact to form peppers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fataa he lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Anyɛɔ enɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei ahe kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning cocoa trees regularly to allow sunlight and airflow into the canopy, along with removing infected pods, stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ daa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ hu. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs chemical fertilizer or if animal manure is enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure and holds water well over long periods, but releases nutrients slowly. Chemical fertilizers provide an immediate boost during rapid growth; using a combination of manure to build the soil and targeted chemical fertilizer gives crops the best results.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ. Shi ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiofio. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee shikpɔŋ kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my topsoil when I plant on a hill, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu nii yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ lɛ naa?

english: Rainwater flows quickly down slopes, taking light, nutrient-rich topsoil with it. Planting your crops in rows across the slope (contour farming) or planting cover crops acts like natural barriers that slow down the water and trap soil on your farm.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa ŋshɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛtsɔ la ni enine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni niyenii mli nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa Contour okwaayeli, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do weevils attack my harvested cowpeas even after I seal them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miitutua mi-cowpea ŋmaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weevil eggs are often laid on the pods while the crop is still in the field, so insects hatch inside the sealed bags. Drying the cowpeas thoroughly until they are hard, and using airtight storage bags (like PICS bags), suffocates any pests before they can multiply.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii awoɔ ŋmeii anɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, kooloi bibii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli. Gbimɔ cowpea lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa. ni okɛ vacuum storage bags (tamɔ PICS kotokui) atsu nii ni okɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ dani amɛfɔ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are getting sick before they completely die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela mɔ mi-abele lɛ dani egbo kwraa?

english: Look for early signs like small discolored spots on leaves, leaves curling inward during cool morning hours, or stunted growth. Checking your crops regularly helps you catch these subtle changes early before whole plants die.
ga: Taomɔ mra be mli okadii, tamɔ ŋmeii bibii ni su etsake yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli. loo shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Kɛ́ okwɛ onibii amli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni oyɔse tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɛɛ mra. Dani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbo

english: Leaf curling and mosaic patterns are caused by cassava mosaic virus, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Affected plants cannot make enough food, which leads to small and weak roots.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ mosaic he mfonirii baa. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Tsei ni ena hela lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when there is a sudden lack of water in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: How can I check if my crops are getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: You can push a dry stick or your finger two inches into the soil near the roots; if it comes out dry, your crops need water. Plants also show thirst by wilting or dropping their lower leaves during the day.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tso ni egbi loo niji enyɔ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ mli. Kɛji egbi lɛ, nu he miihia onibii lɛ. Tsei hu jieɔ kumai he okadi kpo kɛtsɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehi kɛha midumɔ nii lɛ?

english: Morning is best because soil absorbs the water before the hot afternoon sun evaporates it. Evening watering leaves leaves wet overnight, which encourages fungal diseases to grow.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani etsɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ mli fũuɔ nyɔɔŋ kome, ni no woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin instead of developing strong, thick stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows tall and weak when plants are squeezed too close together or shaded by tall trees, competing for sunlight. Proper plant spacing gives each stalk enough light to grow thick and strong.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atswa tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo tsei kakadaji ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ ha amɛhe tsɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During peak heat, pepper leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil, causing temporary drooping. If the plants bounce back by morning, they are healthy; if they stay wilted, they need shade or more root protection.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ be kukuoo mli shigbeemɔ baa. Kɛji tso lɛ ku esɛɛ efo leebi lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe wa. Kɛji amɛgboi lolo lɛ Amɛmiitao hulutsoo loo hebuu babaoo kɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crops turning yellow while the leaves at the top remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Lower leaves turn yellow first when the soil lacks nitrogen nutrient. The plant automatically moves its stored nitrogen from older bottom leaves up to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ sũ lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii. Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: What causes a white powder to spread across the leaves of my garden crops?
ga: Mɛni haa powda yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: That white powder is powdery mildew, a fungal sickness that spreads in warm, humid weather with poor airflow. Spacing plants out and watering the soil instead of the leaves helps prevent it from spreading.
ga: Nakai powda yɛŋ lɛ ji powda ni mli edɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ tee nɔ, ni afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu yɛ baai lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa egbɛ eshwa.

english: How do I know if my crop is wilting from drought or from pests attacking the roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ?

english: Drought stress affects whole fields or rows evenly and plants recover after watering. Root pest damage causes scattered, individual plants to wilt and die even while the soil around them remains damp.
ga: Hɔmɔ he haomɔ saa ŋmɔji loo ŋmɔji fɛɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ awo lɛ nu sɛɛ. Nibii ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi gbɛɔ eshwaa, amɛgboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ po.

english: How do I know when my corn is fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Your corn is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn brown and dry, the silks at the top become dark brown, and the kernels feel firm and hard when you press them.
ga: Oŋmãa lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ. Siliki ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa kɛ́ onyɛ amɛnɔ.

english: What will happen to my corn crop if I cannot find enough labor to harvest it on time?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji minyɛɛɛ mana nitsulɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛkpa yɛ be naa?

english: Leaving mature corn in the field for too long exposes it to pests like insects and birds, causes mold if it rains, and makes the stalks dry out and fall over, leading to severe yield loss.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii tamɔ kooloi kɛ okpoi yeɔ ŋmãa, ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa baa. ni eha tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ ni fiteɔ waa.

english: Is it better for me to plant a very large field of maize all at once or divide it into smaller sections over time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa ŋmɔ agbo waa shikome loo majara ŋmãa lɛ mli awo ŋmãa bibii amli yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Planting in smaller sections at different times spreads out your harvest work, making it easier to gather the crops without needing a huge labor force all at once, while also reducing the risk of weather damage.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ he bibioo ko yɛ bei srɔtoi amli Ebaaye ebua ni egbɛ okpamɔ lɛ eshwa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaabua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa ni ehe ehiaaa ni atsu nitsumɔ babaoo shikome. yɛ be mli ni ebaa oshara ni kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ nii ahe lɛ shi.

english: Rolling leaves is the corn plant's natural way of saving water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the amount of surface exposed to the sun and slows down moisture loss.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni ŋmãa tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves, or that the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do some of my corn stalks fall over before the cob is ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Stalks fall over because of weak roots from shallow planting, strong winds, or pests like stem borers that eat the inside of the plant stem and make it weak.
ga: Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ mli, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ stem borers ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does my corn grow very tall and healthy on one part of my land but stays short on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome nɔ shi ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality changes across a farm. Areas with deeper soil, better water retention, or more organic manure produce taller corn, while hard or nutrient-poor patches produce stunted crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ yɔɔ Nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ahiɔ shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni yɔɔ lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ adara babaoo. yɛ be mli ni hei ni wa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can pictures of my farm taken from high above help me grow better crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mfonirii ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋwɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pictures taken from above show the exact boundaries of your land, highlight areas where crops are struggling or thirsty before you can spot them on the ground, and help predict your harvest size.
ga: Mfonirii ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ husui pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii miitswa loo kumai miiye amɛ yɛ lɛ dani obaanyɛ ona amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eye ebua ni otsɔɔ bɔ ni okpamɔ lɛ da ha.

english: How can I prepare my land properly so my maize seeds sprout evenly across the whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Clear heavy weeds, loosen the soil by plowing so young roots can grow easily, and plant seeds at a uniform depth right after the first reliable rains.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsu lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo. ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ tamɔ amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: How does growing a good crop of maize on my farm help my community and Ghana as a whole?
ga: Abele kpakpa ni aduɔ Te Mi-Famɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi akutso lɛ kɛ Ghana fɛɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Producing high yields of maize increases local food supply, lowers market prices for staples like Kenkey and Banku, boosts your income, and reduces the country's need to buy grain from abroad.
ga: Abele ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Niyenii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ Kenkey kɛ Banku lɛ jara ni aba shi, ni eha oshika ni onáa lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni eha maŋ lɛ he ŋmaa kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ aba shi

english: Yellowing leaves, especially starting from the bottom of the plant, usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to build strong leaves and stay green, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost will help them recover.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, titri lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows its roots to spread and gather enough food to produce larger fruits and ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ebuaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni ewo yibii kɛ toi wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers just fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting mainly due to extreme heat, lack of consistent watering, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding heavy dry spells helps the flowers stay attached long enough to form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii, titri lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ajie ŋmɔtɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that drink up the water and eat up the soil fertilizer intended for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients and sunlight they need to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa tsei lɛ naa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe wa.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with dirt inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli ni muji yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves. Catching them early and applying approved organic or chemical control protects the growing tip of the maize.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yitsei lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or from a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafee nɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Underground cassava rot usually occurs when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, creating conditions for fungi to attack the roots. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ atutua shishifãi lɛ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorching and dropping during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle full sunlight and dry Harmattan winds. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees around young cocoa protects them from direct sun exposure and keeps the air moist around them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la kɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baabu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds when the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain has fallen consistently two or three times and the soil is damp deep down before sowing. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a hot week follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa dani odu nii. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji otsii babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning extra branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight and airflow into the farm, which stops the fungus from growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ akpa.

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green leaf growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over so easily when strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa waa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are shallow or when planted too close together. Heaping soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) during weeding gives the roots extra support to stay upright.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ) yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ babaoo koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light while protecting them from pests and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu ahe.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a viral disease, or by water stress from high heat. Keeping the soil evenly moist and controlling pests early prevents the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo nu mli haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants in the hot afternoon or early morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu shwane loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the cool ground allows the soil to absorb moisture deeply to the roots before the afternoon sun evaporates the water.
ga: Nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ hei ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ dani shwane hulu lɛ shwieɔ lɛ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously strips the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating with crops like groundnuts gives the soil a break and resets its health.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmã he hiaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for other crops?
