ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have microscopic bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil, leaving free nutrients behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ helai bibii ni anaaa yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko ni ashiɔ ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting like tiny ribbons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites, thrips, or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites, thrips, loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: What are those tiny worms eating the centers of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, destructive caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by moths and feed on the soft, growing leaves inside the maize whorl.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ.

english: Why do I see tiny white creatures swarming around the roots when I pull up my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bɔɔ nii bibii yɛŋ lɛ? Swarming ni miibɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe beni migbala ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: These are root mealybugs, soil-dwelling pests that attach themselves to cassava tubers and roots to suck sap, causing the plant to weaken and leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji shishifãi amli ŋmeii. Amɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmei tsei kɛ shishifãi ahe koni amɛnu nu lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is caused by bacterial wilt, a disease caused by tiny organisms in the soil that block the passages water uses to travel up the stem.
ga: Bacteria ni shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ jɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amli. ni ji hela ko ni nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ kɛbaa Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ gbɛ ni nu tsɔɔ nɔ eyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ naa lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn completely black and dry up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet weather and spreads when rain splashes soil or fungal spores onto cocoa pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ, ni ehaa sũ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ shwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ.

english: Why are yellow spots appearing on the leaves of my garden eggs, causing them to fall off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ kpo yɛ eggplant tsei ahe yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow spots on garden egg leaves are usually fungal leaf spots, which spread in humid conditions when water sits on leaves for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii. Egbɛɔ eshwaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli kɛ́ nu hi baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of lower leaves means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy leaves but very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava puts too much energy into leaves and neglects tubers when soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer but lacks potassium, which is needed for tuber development.
ga: Cassava kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ ebaai lɛ amli ni ekuɔ ehiɛ eshwieɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli ni potassium ni he hiaa koni eshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when there is sudden water stress, as the plant tries to save energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: When seeds are planted too close, seedlings fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, forcing them to stretch tall and thin instead of growing thick and strong.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛshwere ni amɛfee mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Where in Ghana is the best place for me to start planting mangoes if I want a good harvest?
ga: Higbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana ni manyɛ mabɔi mango dumɔ kɛji miitao yibiiwoo kpakpa?

english: Mangoes grow very well in regions with distinct wet and dry seasons, such as parts of the Greater Accra region (like Shai Osudoku), Eastern, Volta, and the middle-to-northern transition zones like Sunyani and Kintampo.
ga: Mango kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be sɔrɔtoi yɔɔ, tamɔ Greater Accra kpokpaa lɛ fãi komɛi (tamɔ Shai Osudoku), Bokagbɛ, Volta, kɛ Teŋgbɛ kɛya Kooyigbɛ Tsakemɔ He tamɔ Sunyani kɛ Kintampo.

english: Does my land need to receive heavy rain all year long for mango trees to grow well?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni nugbɔ anɛ waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ dani mi-mango tso lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, mango trees actually need a dry spell to trigger flowering. While young trees need regular water, continuous heavy rainfall throughout the year can spoil the flowers and encourage plant diseases.
ga: Dabi, mango tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná be ni mli egbi koni amɛha fɔfɔi aba. Tsei bibii po he miihia nu daa. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii lɛ agbo ni ewo tsei ahe helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Is it possible for me to start a successful mango farm near a big city in Ghana?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mabɔi mango ŋmɔ ko ni yeɔ omanye yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ maŋtiase ko ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Yes, planting near major cities like Accra or Kumasi is very practical because it puts your farm closer to large markets and buyers, reducing transportation costs after harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ maji wuji tamɔ Accra loo Kumasi lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔ lɛ abɛŋkɛ jara lɛ kɛ jarayelɔi wuji ahe. Enɛ haa shika ni akɛyaa he kroko yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my plot of land is suitable for growing mango trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha mango ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Mangoes prefer deep, well-drained soil where water does not sit for long after heavy rain. You can check by digging a small hole and pouring water into it; if the water drains within a few hours, the soil is suitable.
ga: Mango sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu lɛ ehiŋ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko ni oootse lɛ nɔ. no sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ nu mli Kɛji nu lɛ ho yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni sa.

english: How much space should I leave between each mango tree when planting them on my farm?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ maŋmɛ mango tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: You should space your mango trees about 8 to 10 meters apart so their broad branches and deep roots have enough room to get sunlight and nutrients without competing.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi omango tsei lɛ ateŋ aaafee mitai 8 kɛyashi 10 bɔni afee ni amɛniji ni mli kwɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe akatswa akaŋ.

english: If I plant mango seedlings today, how many years will it take before I can harvest my first fruits?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu mango ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani akpa klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ?

english: Grafted mango seedlings usually start producing fruit in 3 to 4 years, whereas trees grown directly from raw seeds can take up to 7 to 10 years to bear fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I buy grafted mango seedlings instead of just planting the seed from a good mango I ate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mango kpakpai ni miyeɔ lɛ amli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Grafted seedlings produce fruit much faster, stay at a manageable height for easy harvesting, and guarantee that the fruit will be sweet and high quality just like the mother plant.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa. Eyɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ koni akpamɔ mlɛo. Ni aná nɔmimaa akɛ aduawai lɛ baafee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni nɔ kwɔ tamɔ tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ.

english: How often do I need to water my young mango seedlings during the dry Harmattan season in Ghana?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mawo mi mango dumɔwui lɛ nu yɛ harmattan be ni nu egbi yɛ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Young mango seedlings need watering about two to three times a week during their first dry season until their roots go deep enough into the ground to find water on their own.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awo mango dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu aaafee shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛna nu.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my mango tree instead of turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Flower drop is usually caused by heavy rain during flowering, insect pests, or fungal diseases. Keeping the area under the tree clear and allowing good air movement through pruning helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ aha he ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli tse ni aha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ho kɛtsɔ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Will weeds and tall grass around my young mango plants prevent them from growing well?
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle he fɛɛ. Ani abaatsi mi mango tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from young seedlings. Clearing a wide ring around the base of each young tree helps it grow faster and stay healthy.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa tsei bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli kwɔ ni bɔle tso bibioo lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eda oya ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to nurse my pepper seeds in a shaded bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shia mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya saatso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are tender and vulnerable to heavy rain and hot sun. Nursing them under shade allows them to develop strong roots and stem strength gradually before facing the tough conditions of the main farm.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa dani amɛkɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ akpee.

english: Why do my maize seeds need to be planted at a specific depth in the soil instead of just throwing them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ko lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeedu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need to be buried at a controlled depth so they stay moist, stay safe from birds, and establish deep anchor roots that keep the growing stalk standing firm.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni akudɔ koni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni okpoi akafee amɛ shweshweeshwe, ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni haa tso lɛ ni miida lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Is it better to give my crops all their fertilizer at once or split it into smaller portions over time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ awo mli shikome loo majara ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli bibii bibii? Yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Feeding crops small amounts of fertilizer at different stages of growth matches how they eat. It ensures the roots absorb the nutrients gradually as the plant grows, rather than burning young roots or washing away unused fertilizer.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko haa tsei yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ be mli lɛ kɛ gbɛi ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛyeɔ nii lɛ kpãa gbee. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ fiofio Ejieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa Yɛ shishifãi bibii ni ashãa loo ni akɛbaafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ ahe lɛ najiaŋ lɛ,

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for soil nutrients like nitrogen. While water keeps the plant hydrated, crops also need nutrient food from healthy soil to maintain green leaves and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, eyɛ mli akɛ nu baaye abua ni tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu he miihia niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli koni amɛha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: If I see another farmer getting high yields from a new crop variety, how can I safely try it on my own land?
ga: Kɛji mina okwaafoi krokomɛi ni miiná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka dumɔwui yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ nɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: You can start by planting a small trial portion or single bed on your farm to watch how the crop behaves in your specific soil and climate before committing your entire farm to it.
ga: Obaanyɛ oje shishi kɛtsɔ kaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii loo saatso kome ni oookwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni ona bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli dani ofee oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I buy fresh hybrid maize seeds each season instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ daa afi moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high strength and yields in their first generation, but saved seeds from that harvest lose their energy and produce weaker, inconsistent plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ ni amɛwo klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ. Shi dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Yam plants tell you they are mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up, showing that the plant has stopped growing above ground and stored all its food in the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ edara kɛji akɛ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shweremɔ ni ekɛ eniyenii fɛɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive heat stresses tomato plants and prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy until conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ pollination ni sa. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why can cassava stay green through the dry season while my corn wilts and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmei lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava develops a deep root system and stores moisture in its thick tubers, allowing it to tap into deep soil water that shallow-rooted crops like corn cannot reach.
ga: Cassava feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ nu toɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ amli. Ha ni ekɛ ehe awo nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni tsei ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain sucker take many months of growth before it starts showing a fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛdaraa dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains must grow slowly to build a thick pseudostem and large leaves first, accumulating enough energy reserves before they have the strength to push out and support a heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Esa akɛ plantains lɛ ada blɛoo. Koni afee tsei ni akɛ niji fee ni mli tse kɛ baai wuji klɛŋklɛŋ. Koni abua hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa naa dani ajie nɔnyɛɛ lɛ kpo ni eye ebua aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ.

english: Why are the young leaves on my new cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves are tender and lose moisture fast. They need temporary shade crops like plantains planted beside them to shield them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ ji bibii ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. koni amɛtsu nii akɛ gãimlibii kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so they get full sunlight and good airflow, which helps build bigger tubers and prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa bulbs lɛ feɔ bulbs wuji ni etsiɔ folier helai anaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your maize crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs a lot of food to grow big ears, so applying poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the leaves back their rich green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Niyenii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekwɛ toi wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the field where I harvested maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts actually put nitrogen back into the soil naturally. Rotating crops keeps your soil rich without needing to spend as much money on chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ofite shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips that feed on plant juices. Spraying the leaves early with neem oil or appropriate remedies stops these insects before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa kroko ni sa baashwie baai lɛ anɔ mra. Etsiɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do small weeds actually stop my crops from growing well if there is enough land?
ga: Te jwɛi bibii baafee tɛŋŋ amɛtsi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji miyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Weeds eat from the same plate as your crops. Their roots steal water and nutrients underground, while their leaves block sunlight above ground. They can also hide destructive pests that move onto your crops.
ga: Jwɛi yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ niyenii ni oduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii ni fãa kɛyaa onibii anɔ lɛ hu ato.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This makes the stems thin and weak, resulting in very small maize cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii waa baa loo ŋmãa ko bɛ kwraa.

english: Tomato flowers usually fall off when the weather gets too hot, the soil dries out completely, or there are no insects to pollinate them. Regular watering around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi, loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he daa lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when we get heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the soil loses air and wet-loving fungi grow quickly. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ daa oya. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How long should I wait after the first rain of the year before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait until after two or three good, consistent rainfalls when the soil is deeply moist. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi kpakpai enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ko ba ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are there holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hidden inside the growing leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine yɛ bu ni akɛtee baa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They feed on young leaves, which stops the plant from making food and growing well if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni baanyɛ atsĩ tso lɛ naa koni ekafee niyenii ni eda jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce small leaves and small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential nutrients, water, and sunlight from your crops, effectively starving them and reducing their final harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni ehaa naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or trees to shield them from high heat and keep the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with weak stems when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants compete heavily for sunlight and stretch upward rapidly instead of building sturdy stems and strong roots.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛshwereɔ oya moŋ fe ni amɛaawo shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food. Staking raises the leaves off the ground so they catch light easily, sending nutrients down to grow larger tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la oya. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa shi koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stem section to plant for a good yield?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei bibii ni sa kɛha dumɔ koni aná yibii kpakpai?

english: Use mature stems taken from the middle portion of a healthy plant with strong nodes. Avoid soft top stems because they dry out easily, and avoid very old bottom stems that take longer to sprout.
ga: Kɛ tso ni eda ni ajie kɛjɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nodes ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛgbiɔ oya. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ shishigbɛ tsei ni egbɔ waa, ni heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plant turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to form healthy green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why is it dangerous to place fertilizer directly touching the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer acts like strong salt and can burn sensitive stems and fine roots, damaging or killing the plant instead of feeding it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei ni mli ewo muji ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni fiteɔ loo efiteɔ tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell, which can cause seeds to sprout and then wither away before their roots can find deep soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi dani shishifãi lɛ ana nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat and dry soil stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers as a survival mechanism to preserve water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛshwie fɔfɔii amɛshwie shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their soft leaves from harsh sunlight while their root systems are still small. Planting quick-growing trees like plantains alongside young cocoa provides early shade and retains soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba mra ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my plantain shoots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi plantains lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly during hot weather. It keeps the soil cool, prevents weed growth, and turns into natural fertilizer as it rots.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbo

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be saŋŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is running out of nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehe wa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get a bigger yield from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani mana nibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and very small cobs. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow strong and produce full ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eda ni ehiɛ baai babaoo.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot periods helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into pepper pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi ni feɔ pepper pods lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my yams are fully mature and ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When yam vines and leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up naturally at the end of the season, it means the plant has stopped growing leaves and stored all its energy into the tuber below ground, signaling that the yam is ready to be dug up.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ atsa sweet potato lɛ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal the soil nutrients and fertilizer meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your main crops get full access to food and light.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa tsei titrii lɛ náa niyenii kɛ la babaoo.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn watery and rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when the soil stays overly wet for too long or gets infected by soil fungi. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots do not rot in waterlogged soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fitemɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteee yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomato plants is often caused by a plant virus carried by tiny insects like whiteflies. Removing heavily infected plants early and controlling insect pests stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli helai ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants get sunburned easily when exposed to full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to protect their soft leaves until they are mature enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Hulu shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can expose themselves to maximum sunlight to produce energy. When vines spread on the hot ground, they receive less light, catch diseases more easily, and produce smaller tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ gbɛ eshwa hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ Amɛnáaa la fioo. Okɛ hela aba oya ni oha yitso lɛ afee bibioo

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them restores natural nutrients into the earth that hungry crops like maize used up during the previous season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tips usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient plants require to build strong, healthy green leaves and stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai kɛ tsei eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree to stay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ji nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: If too many shoots (suckers) grow around one main plantain stem, they steal water and nutrients from each other. Removing most of them and keeping only two or three healthy ones ensures you get large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) miida yɛ ehe lɛ Tso titri kome fa tsɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ojie emli babaoo ni okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha oná plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do some of the tiny young pods on my cocoa tree turn black and dry up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: This is often caused by a natural condition called cherelle wilt, where the tree sheds extra pods it cannot support. However, it can also be worsened by damp conditions, bad weather, or fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Biɛ ji he ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shihilɛ lɛ aya hiɛ waa. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry season, and are they dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fite yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ ni ani eegbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells to save water and protect itself from drying out. The plant is not dead; its root tubers stay safe underground and will sprout fresh green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eshishifãi lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why is it very important for my maize crop to get enough water when the flowers at the top start to open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ mi-abele lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛji fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: When flowers (tassels and silks) appear on maize, the plant is entering its grain-forming stage. A lack of water during this critical window causes cobs to grow poorly with missing or empty seeds.
ga: Kɛji fɔfɔii (tassels kɛ silk) je kpo yɛ ŋmãa nɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibote dumɔwui afeemɔ mli. Nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ ni dumɔwui ni bɛ loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit mainly due to extreme heat stress, lack of water, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow thick leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Nɔ titri ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni yibii bɛ mli lɛ baa ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ewo baai ni mli tse yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why should I cut off old or extra branches from my mango trees after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi mango tso lɛ niji ni egbɔ loo ni fa fe nine lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Cutting off old or overgrown branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the inside of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to produce fresh, healthy shoots that will bear fruit in the next season.
ga: Niji ni egbɔ loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ewo tsei heei ni mli wa ni baawo yibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know which branches on my mango tree need to be cut and which ones to keep?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niji ni yɔɔ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ ni esa akɛ afo lɛ? Ni mɛɛ niji esa akɛ akɛto?

english: You should remove dead, diseased, or weak branches, as well as older branches from last season that block sunlight from reaching the inner canopy. Always keep healthy, strong young branches that will produce future flowers and fruits.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ agbɛnɛ tsei niji momo ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli ni miitsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji oblahii kɛ oblayei ni baawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai wɔsɛɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be.

english: Will cutting back the branches of my fruit trees reduce the amount of harvest I get?
ga: Ani mitso ni woɔ yibii lɛ niji ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmaa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: While heavy cutting might slightly reduce fruit quantity immediately after, proper pruning improves the overall quality, size, and health of your fruit over time by focusing the tree's energy on its strongest branches.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii baanyɛ aha aduawai lɛ ayibɔ aba shi fioo yɛ no sɛɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ ahi, amɛdalɛ, kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Ekɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ eniji ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe nii.

english: What is the best time of year for me to trim or cut back my mango tree branches?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afo loo afo mango?

english: The best time to trim branches is right after you finish harvesting the main crop. This gives the tree enough time to grow new, healthy shoots before the next flowering season begins.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni okɛbaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji beni ogbe ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ akpamɔ naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛduɔ tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ dani fɔfɔii afeemɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why is my mango tree producing plenty of leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive leaf growth often happens when the tree receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or when dense outer branches block sunlight from triggering flower buds inside the canopy. Trimming shade branches helps stimulate flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baa lɛ shwereɔ fe nine kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. aloo beni kponɔgbɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni kanyaa fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ahe hewalɛ.

english: What causes the flowers on my mango tree to drop off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mango tso nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani enɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: Flower drop is typically caused by insect pests, fungal diseases like powdery mildew during humid periods, strong winds, or inconsistent water supply when the tree is flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ powdery mildew yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo nu ni baa shi yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miifɔlɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: How do new shoots on my tree affect fruit production for the upcoming season?
ga: Te ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaná aduawai ni baa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: New shoots that mature after the last harvest become the primary points where fresh flowers and fruit will grow in the upcoming season, making their health vital for a good yield.
ga: Tsofɔi heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ bafeɔ hei titri ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai heei baajɛ mli aba kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Ha hewalɛnamɔ afee nɔ ni he hiaa kɛha nibii kpakpai afeemɔ.

english: Why do some branches on my mango tree suddenly dry up while the rest of the tree remains green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji komɛi ni yɔɔ mango tso nɔ lɛ gbiɔ trukaa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi lɛ yɛ frɔ̃frɔ̃ lolo lɛ?

english: Single dry branches are usually caused by stem borer insects or fungal infections. Cutting off these affected branches well below the dead section prevents the problem from spreading to the healthy parts of the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei niji komekomei ni egbi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afo nɛkɛ tsei niji ni ena hela nɛɛ yɛ hei ni egboi lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni naagba lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tso lɛ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: What should I do with the branches I cut off from my fruit trees after clearing them?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee niji ni mifolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ beni mijie amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should gather all cut branches and fallen leaves and remove them from under the trees. Burning or composting them far away prevents pests and diseases from surviving in the dead wood and infecting your farm.
ga: Esa akɛ obua tsei niji ni afolɔ kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ fɛɛ anaa ni ojie kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Shãa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai anaa. Hiɛ shi yɛ koo ni egbo lɛ mli ni okɛ hela awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does letting sunlight reach inside my fruit tree canopy help my crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulu la ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni eboteɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Sunlight dries out trapped moisture inside the tree canopy, which prevents fungal rot and powers photosynthesis across all branches, leading to bigger, healthier fruits throughout the tree.
ga: Hulu la lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa fotosintɛtik hewalɛ yɛ tso nine lɛ fɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa tso lɛ he fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong direct sunlight because their leaves are tender. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to block the intense heat while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make enough food for big underground tubers. Leaving vines on the damp ground leads to leaf rot and small harvests.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni eha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbo ni ebaaha yibii fioo pɛ aba.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tight little balls and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee bɔɔlu bibii lɛ? Ni akpa tso lɛ dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying neem oil extract or appropriate pest treatment early frees the leaves to open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Neem mu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbele

english: Why do my young maize leaves have lines of tiny holes in them as they unfold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Lines be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo?

english: These holes are caused by young caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, eating the leaves while they are still rolled up inside the center funnel of the plant before they expand.
ga: Nɛkɛ bu nɛɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai be mli ni amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe lolo yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli dani amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ feɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy green leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai eŋɔlii akui shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of feeding and swelling the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔlii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Mohu ɔ, e yeɔ ní nɛ e haa nɛ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ puɛɔ.

english: Why do farmers say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny beneficial bacteria in their roots that catch nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers turn yellow and fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛjieee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when water supply drops suddenly, causing heat stress that prevents the flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ shwie shi trukaa. Enɛ kɛ hulutsoo haomɔ ni tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee aduawai baa.

english: How do groundnuts end up forming under the ground when the flowers bloom up in the air?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ amɛfɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli?

english: Once the groundnut flower opens and gets pollinated above ground, it sends out a peg-like stem that grows downward, pushes itself into the soil, and then swells to form the nut underground.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ gbele amɛhe ni amɛfee pollination yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsuɔ ŋmei ko ni tamɔ peg ni daa kɛyaa shishi. tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛkɛ ni efuɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ ebafeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei.

english: Having too many shoots causes them to fight with the main plant for soil nutrients and water, which results in small, thin plantain bunches. Keeping only one or two healthy shoots ensures big fruit.
ga: Nibii ni shwieɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni jɛɔ tso ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ he mɔdɛŋ. Enɛ haa plantains bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why is my flooded rice turning yellow even though the field has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ nu afua mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nu babaoo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Water keeps rice hydrated, but yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil or that stagnant water is suffocating the roots from getting air.
ga: Nu haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How deep should I dig a water storage pit or fish pond on my farm to make sure it lasts?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔ mli nutoohe loo loo nubu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni ehi shi daa?

english: You should aim to dig around 1.5 meters deep. While digging 1 meter deep might seem enough at first, soil will naturally erode into the pit over time, so digging to 1.5 meters keeps it useful for longer.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ohiɛ afɔ shi akɛ obaafo mli aaafee mitai 1.5, eyɛ mli akɛ mita 1 baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni sa yɛ shishijee mli moŋ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛboteɔ bu lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ atsa mitai 1.5 lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If I dig a 1-meter hole for my farm pond, is that deep enough?
ga: Kɛ mifo nubu ni kɛlɛ ji mita kome lɛ, ani nakai mlibotemɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa?

english: A 1-meter hole is okay to start with, but it will quickly become too shallow as sun and rain erode the edges into the pit. Digging closer to 1.5 meters gives you extra depth to protect against this natural loss.
ga: Abaanyɛ aje mita 1 bu shishi. Shi oya nɔŋŋ ni etsɔɔ mli tsɔ beni hulu kɛ nugbɔ shwieɔ bu lɛ naa lɛ. Kɛ́ otsa shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mitai 1.5 lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋshɔ lɛ mlibotemɔ babaoo koni akafite adebɔɔ mli nibii.

english: What common mistake should I avoid when digging a fish pond on my land?
ga: Mɛɛ tɔmɔi ni afɔɔ feemɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ he beni mifoɔ loo ŋshɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Many people treat a fish pond like an ordinary hole in the ground without considering depth and weather. You must dig it properly to about 1.5 meters deep so rain and sun do not erode the sides and ruin it.
ga: Mɛi babaoo buɔ loo ŋshɔi lɛ tamɔ bu folo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni bɔ ni mli kwɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ ha lɛ kɔɔɔ he eko. Esa akɛ otsa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ aaafee mitai 1.5 koni nugbɔ kɛ hulu akafite sɛɛgbɛ lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why should I dig a farm pit deeper than what I actually need right now?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔ mli bu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni ehe hiaa mi diɛŋtsɛ amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Exposed dirt around a dug pit will crumble and settle at the bottom over time due to weather. Digging deeper at the beginning—around 1.5 meters—ensures the pit remains at a functional depth even after soil erosion happens.
ga: Muji ni ebɔle Bu ni atsa lɛ he lɛ baakumɔ ni ebaagbee shi yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Kɛ́ akumɔ mli kɛyashɛ he ni ejɛɔ shishijee lɛ (aaafee mitai 1.5) lɛ, ehaa bu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ he ko ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efo moŋ

english: Why shouldn't I just dig a quick, shallow hole on my land when I need water storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ bu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ? oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Mɛɛ be ehe baahia ni mato nu?

english: A basic shallow hole breaks down very fast under heat and rain. Proper farm pits need sufficient depth, around 1.5 meters, so that as the sides wear down, the hole still holds water effectively.
ga: Buji ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baafite oya waa yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shishi. Esa akɛ ŋmɔ mli bu ni sa lɛ mli akwɔ bɔ ni sa, aaafee mitai 1.5, bɔni afee ni kɛ́ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ gbee shi lɛ, bu lɛ ahiɛ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lolo.

english: Why do the pits and holes I dig on my farm keep getting shallower over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu kɛ bu ni mifo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifee mlɛo kɛmiifee mlɛo lɛ? Beni be hoɔ lɛ

english: The strong sun bakes and cracks the exposed dirt on the sides of the pit, while rain washes that loose soil down into the bottom. This constant weather exposure slowly fills up the hole from within.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã ni ebaagbala muji ni yɔɔ bu lɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ lɛ wo sũ ni mli tse kɛba shi kɛtee bu lɛ shishi. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo fiofio lɛ Okɛ bu lɛ awo mli kɛjɛ mli

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the edges of a newly dug hole on my land?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa bu ni atsa ehee yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains beat against the loose, exposed dirt on the walls of the hole, washing topsoil straight into the bottom. Over time, this erosion reduces the usable depth of your pit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswaa muji ni etse ehe yɛ bu lɛ gbogboi lɛ anɔ. Efoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋshɔkei nɛɛ baaha obu lɛ mlibotemɔ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ aba shi.

english: Can intense heat from the sun damage the depth of a hole I dug on my farm?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite bu ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mlibotemɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, harsh heat dries out the exposed soil along the rim and walls of the hole, making it crumble easily. Wind and incoming rain then carry this loose dirt down to the bottom, making the pit shallower.
ga: Hɛɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa sũ ni yɔɔ kpo lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ yɛ bu lɛ naa kɛ gbogboi lɛ ahe. ha efee mlɛo akɛ oookumɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ shwieɔ muji ni etse ehe nɛɛ kɛyaa shishi. ha bu lɛ mli afee mlɛo

english: How can I protect my dug farm pits from getting ruined by weather elements?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ mli bu ni mifo lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he?

english: The best protection is digging deeper than your minimum requirement—around 1.5 meters. This compensates for the soil that will inevitably erode into the pit from sun and rain exposure.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni buɔ mɔ he ji ni otsa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe nɔ ni he hiaa bo fe fɛɛ, aaafee mitai 1.5, koni okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni hulu kɛ nugbɔ baatsɔ mli kɛya bu lɛ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: What happens to exposed soil inside a newly dug trench or pit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo yɛ ŋmeii loo buji ni atsa ehee lɛ amli lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During the dry season, intense sun bakes the exposed walls of the pit, breaking down the soil structure. When weather changes, this loose soil slides to the bottom, reducing the hole's overall depth.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã bu lɛ gbogboi lɛ. Ekpãtãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ ahiɛ Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe nɛɛ baatsɔ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, bu lɛ mlibotemɔ fɛɛ ba shi.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to build healthy green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the soil and starve the roots of air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ he miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ekɛ baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves have yellow patches and curl up into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbɔle amɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a common virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings for planting is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall and weak with tiny cobs when I plant them under large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu yɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulutsoo lɛ shishi?

english: Maize needs direct sunlight for most of the day to make food. When shaded by trees, the plant stretches upward searching for light instead of using its energy to build strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Abele he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli babaoo koni ehoo. Beni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso nguahi.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young corn leaves and small brown dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli edɔ kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Yɛ teŋgbɛ tutswaa lɛ mli

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm damage. The caterpillars hide inside the growing center of the plant during the day, chewing through the leaves before they unfurl.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ efite nii. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ hei ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oooye dani ogbele amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough moisture to plant my maize after the early rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Avoid planting after just one light rain. Dig down a few inches into the soil; if you can squeeze a handful of earth into a soft ball that holds together without dripping water, the soil is ready for planting.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔ he yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. shikome pɛ Tsɔɔmɔ inchi fioo komɛi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko afee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ he kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why should I apply my fertilizer in two different stages instead of putting it all in the soil at planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi enyɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: Applying fertilizer in stages feeds the crop when it needs it most. Putting all fertilizer down at planting risks losing half of it because heavy rains can wash it away before the young roots grow deep enough to absorb it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ fata dumɔ ko he lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fã afite ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo lɛ dani shishifãi bibii lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the corn seeds I saved from my last harvest produce smaller cobs than the packaged seed I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii fe ŋmãa ni akɛwo kotoku mli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Most purchased seeds are hybrids bred for high yield in their first year. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their hybrid strength, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields in the next season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aheɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ hybrid hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: What is the purpose of the bushy flowers at the top of my maize plant and the hair growing out of the cob?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ yiteŋ kɛ yitsɔi ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The flowers at the top (tassels) produce pollen, and the silky hairs catch the pollen as it drops. Each individual silk thread must catch pollen to produce a single grain of corn on that cob.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi (tassels) lɛ jieɔ pollen. Ni yitsɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mɔ̃ɔ pollen kɛji egbee shi. Esa akɛ siliki kpãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko amɔmɔ pollen koni ekɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield so drastically even during seasons with plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop for plant food, space, and sunlight. Even with plenty of rain, your crops will starve if aggressive weeds take up the nutrients in the soil first.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha tsei niyenii, he ko kɛ hulu la, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po. Hɔmɔ baaye onibii po kɛji jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha niyenii kpakpai klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How can I protect my harvested dried corn from small insects in storage without using liquid chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni ji nu tsuuu nii?

english: You can store thoroughly dried maize in airtight storage containers or hermetic bags (like PICS bags). Closing the bags tightly cuts off oxygen, which naturally suffocates any insects without needing chemical sprays.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ awo ŋmãa ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo vacuum kotoku mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku). Kɛ́ ogbala kotoku lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baaje mli. ni baaha kooloi srɔtoi agbɔjɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni akɛ tsofai wooo mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and get sunburnt easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains around them creates a living shade canopy that protects the young seedlings until they grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ wala mli ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ baa.

english: What will happen if I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots fight for nutrients and their branches block sunlight from reaching each other. This high humidity also creates a warm, damp environment where black pod disease spreads rapidly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni tsei niji lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo nɛɛ hu haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo baa. Black pod hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oya.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms that hide in the center leaves of the maize stem to feed. Catching them early with appropriate treatments or wood ash prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai amli koni amɛye nii. Kɛ́ mɔmɔ amɛ mra kɛtsɔ tsofafeemɔ ni sa loo tso sũ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ.

english: It is best to wait until the soil has received two or three heavy, steady rains that soak deep into the earth. Planting too early after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if rain pauses for a week.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome.

english: Yam vines produce leaves that act like solar panels to feed the tuber growing under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves lifted off the damp earth where they get more sun and stay away from ground pests and fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ he ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow and white?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ eyɛŋ lɛ?

english: This is cassava mosaic disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-free stems from healthy farms for your new planting is the best way to keep your cassava crop healthy.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛji woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Helai ni bɛ mli ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ dumɔwui heei amli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha o-cassava tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, erratic watering, or a lack of specific soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant keep its flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper crops grow big bushy green leaves but fail to produce peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni eyɛ ŋmɔji shi ewooo pepper lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-based fertilizer makes plants focus all their energy on growing tall, green leaves instead of making flowers and fruits. Balancing your plant food encourages the crop to start fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni kɛlɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii. Tso niyenii ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baawo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛje yibiiwoo shishi.

english: The small suckers steal food and water away from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to focus its energy on producing large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers bibii juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantain tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa dani kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can struggle to hold up heavy bunches during strong winds. Propping the main trunk with a strong bamboo stick shaped like a fork supports the weight and prevents the tree from breaking.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni baanyɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni emɔ ŋmeii wuji Yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso ni wa ni tamɔ fɔk fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛfiɔ tso lɛ tsiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ akumɔ.

english: How can I tell if store-bought certified seeds will produce better crops than seeds I saved from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred and treated to produce high yields, resist common pests, and grow uniformly. Seeds saved from past harvests often lose these strong traits over time, leading to weaker crops and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ daa Bei pii lɛ Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Why do plantain suckers taken from an old farm sometimes fail to produce big bunches of plantain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, plantain ŋmeii ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo plantain babaoo lɛ?

english: Old plantain suckers often carry hidden diseases, stem weevils, or microscopic root worms from the old soil. Using cleaned or certified suckers ensures the plant starts free of diseases, allowing it to grow strong and bear heavy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei momo lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, ŋmeii loo shishifãi bibii waa ni jɛ shikpɔŋ momo mli. Sucker ni he tse loo ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai bɛ tso lɛ mli. Ha etsɔ hewalɛ ni ewo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects their delicate leaves from burning until they are mature enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plants before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they face heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. When temperatures get too hot or the soil dries out, the plant sheds blossoms to conserve energy and water.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to generate food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, improves air circulation, and helps the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji, ni amɛhe wa ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow many green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excessive leaves and few pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Legumes naturally make their own nitrogen, so giving them extra nitrogen fertilizer forces leaf growth instead of pod formation.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Legumes lɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha baai akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when the soil holds too much water and cannot drain properly. Waterlogged soil starves the roots of oxygen and creates conditions for soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni enyɛɛɛ etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards and stop growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Upward curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ mli helai lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai lɛ afitemɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves compete with each other for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough resources to grow thick stems and high yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and trap soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is a essential nutrient for leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain waterlogs the soil, stopping the roots from taking in food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with many big leaves, but the tubers underground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and green leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to swell the underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye níhi kɛ baa si konɛ e ha nɛ ngmlɛfia ɔmɛ nɛ a hwɔɔ.

english: How do I know if my vegetables are getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-vegetables lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo eshɛɛɛ he?

english: When plants don't get enough water, their leaves wilt, curl inward, and feel dry. When they get too much water, the leaves turn yellow, the stems get soft, and roots rot underground because they cannot breathe.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagboi. curl inward and feel water dry Kɛ́ onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and why do I see tiny caterpillars hiding inside the top whorl?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ baa, ni mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo ŋwɛi kooyigbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides in the central funnel of maize plants during the day and feeds on young leaves. Spraying late in the evening or early morning when they come out to feed helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie amɛnɔ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa beni amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering. If the plant feels stressed by dry soil followed by heavy watering, it drops its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛji tso lɛ miinu he akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miihao lɛ, no lɛ, okɛ nu ni mli wa awo mli. Fɔfɔi baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi shi.

english: Is it bad to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be Ani afi lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ?

english: Yes, planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives plant-specific pests a permanent home. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
