ga: Hɛɛ, tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa shia ni baahi shi daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I just throw fertilizer on my crops at any time, or does the timing matter?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be fɛɛ be? Aloo be he miihia?

english: Timing matters greatly. Crops need fertilizer at specific key stages, like when roots first establish and right before flowering. Applying fertilizer during dry spells or late in the season wastes money and can scorch plant roots.
ga: Be ji nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ. Tsei he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli, tamɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ heɔ shika, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Do weeds really reduce my crop yield, or can I just let them grow alongside my plants?
ga: Ani jwɛi lɛ miiba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ shi diɛŋtsɛ aloo manyɛ maha amɛkwɛ̃ kɛfata mitsei lɛ ahe kɛkɛ?

english: Weeds actively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. If left unchecked, weeds grow faster than your crops, hiding them from the sun and leaving them too weak to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni ekɛteeɔ hulu la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last harvest grow weaker plants than the certified seeds I buy from the agricultural store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specifically bred in laboratories for high yield and disease resistance. The seeds saved from those plants lose that special strength in the next generation, producing smaller and less consistent crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade, keeping the young cocoa moist and protected while giving you food and income early on.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika mra.

english: Will planting plantains next to my cocoa trees make them fight for soil nutrients?
ga: plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If you space them properly, they work well together. Plantains have shallower roots while cocoa roots go deeper into the soil, but adding compost or fertilizer ensures both plants get enough food to thrive.
ga: Kɛji okɛ ohe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ lɛ to bɔ ni sa Amɛbaafee ekome kɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni cocoa shishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaadara.

english: When is the right time to remove plantain trees from my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie dumɔwui kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should start thinning out or removing plantains after 3 to 4 years when the cocoa trees grow large leaves and create their own shade canopy.
ga: Esa akɛ oje dumɔwui lɛ ashishi loo ojie yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ, beni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai wuji ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee hulutsoo lɛ.

english: How do plantain trees help keep my farm soil moist during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui yeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain stems store a lot of water and their large leaves shade the ground, which slows down water evaporation from the soil and protects surrounding crops.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ kɛ nu babaoo toɔ ni amɛbaai wuji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo, ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ahe.

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the fingers become full and rounded rather than angular, the dry flower ends fall off easily, and the skin color shifts from dark green to light green.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni eniji lɛ eyi obɔ ni efee kokroo yɛ koŋ najiaŋ. Fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. ni hewolo lɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛtee eŋɔli ni mli tse.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow and drying up prematurely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks water or nutrients like nitrogen and potassium, or it could be infected by common fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. Aloo ekolɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ sigatoga diŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: How many suckers should I allow to grow around one plantain plant?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii enyiɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu kome he?

english: It is best to leave only 3 plants per stool: the main producing mother plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot. Removing extra suckers prevents competition for nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsei 3 pɛ yɛ shwiili kome mli, ni tso nyɛ ni feɔ nibii titri lɛ fata he. 1 ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛ 1 ni dalɛ ji bibioo. Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ akaŋshii ni kɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he lɛ naa.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa tree take to start producing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit in 2 to 3 years, whereas traditional cocoa varieties take around 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why are my small green cocoa pods turning black and dying on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ.

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and overly shaded farms. Pruning thick leaves to let in sunlight and spraying copper fungicides helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ amli koni hulu lɛ ashɛ he, ni akɛ akɔɔble tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ enaa.

english: What short-term crops can I plant to earn quick money while waiting for my main tree crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo manyɛ madu koni maná shika oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni yeɔ daa lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Food crops like plantain, cassava, maize, and vegetables can be planted alongside young tree crops to give you early food and income during the first few seasons.
ga: Abaanyɛ adu niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains, cassava, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai yɛ tsei bibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ahe koni eha bo niyenii kɛ shika mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the right time to put fertilizer on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni mikɛbaawo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is moist, usually at the start of the rainy season. Applying it during dry periods can burn the roots, while applying it during heavy downpours can wash the nutrients away before the cocoa tree absorbs them.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nɔ ni bei pii lɛ eji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani cacao tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Can I still put fertilizer on the ground when my crop is almost ready for harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii lolo beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: It is generally better to apply fertilizer earlier in the growth cycle, during flowering and pod development. Applying fertilizer right at harvest does not help the current yield and can lead to wasted nutrients.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli mra yɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli. yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ be mli Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ eyeee ebuaaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa amrɔ nɛɛ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite.

english: Why does adding animal manure or compost to the soil make my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Animal manure and compost act as natural food for the soil. They improve soil structure, help the ground hold water longer during dry days, and slowly release essential nutrients that crops need to stay strong.
ga: Koolooi ashishi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ jogbaŋŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei lɛ taoɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: What should I do to the soil right after I finish harvesting my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji akpa kookoo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: After harvesting, the soil loses nutrients used to grow the cocoa pods. Adding organic matter or a post-harvest soil treatment helps replenish the earth and prepares the trees for the next flowering cycle.
ga: kpamɔ sɛɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he loo atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ ni esaa tso lɛ he kɛha fɔfɔii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How many years does a new cocoa tree take before it starts giving pods for harvest?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko woɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take about three to five years to produce pods, while newer hybrid varieties can start bearing fruit in about two to three years if cared for properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. be mli ni hybrid henɔi heei Ebaabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ afii 2-3 mli kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the tree is missing key nutrients in the soil, like nitrogen, or that it is getting too much direct sunlight without enough shade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo enine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Flowers drop when the tree is stressed by drought, lack of nutrients, or heavy pest attacks. Trees also naturally drop excess flowers if they cannot support that many pods at once.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui waa lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ ehe kɛji enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɔ shikome.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the sun gets strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and tender leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees or companion crops like plantains to shelter them until they grow older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ tsei bibii, koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: When is the best time during the year for me to plant new crops in my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni esa akɛ madu tsei heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant is at the beginning of the major rainy season. This gives young roots enough moisture to establish deeply before the dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ shishijee. Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛma shi shiŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How close to harvest time can I spray pest treatments on my farm?
ga: Te manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ashwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ he eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Chemical treatments must be stopped a few weeks before harvest, known as the pre-harvest interval. This ensures the chemicals break down safely so the harvested crop is non-toxic for consumers.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ otsii fioo komɛi dani akpa. Ale lɛ hu akɛ be ni tsɔ ŋmaakpamɔ hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsofai lɛ fiteɔ shweshweeshwe. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ jeee nɔ ni gbeɔ mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ.

english: Flowers fall off when they are not pollinated by tiny midges or when the tree is stressed by heat or lack of food. Without successful pollination, the flower cannot develop into a fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli loo kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be mli loo niyenii bɛ ehe. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ atsɔ aduawai.

english: What is cocoa pollination, and why is it so important for my yield?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo mli ŋmɔtɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi yɛ nitsumɔ mli lɛ?

english: Pollination is the process where pollen moves from one flower to another so the tree can produce seeds and pods. Proper pollination directly leads to more and larger cocoa pods on your trees.
ga: Pollination ji gbɛ ni pollen tsɔɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo dumɔwui kɛ pods. Pollination ni sa baaha cocoa ŋmɔtɔi wuji kɛ wuji aba otsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my tiny cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi dani eda lɛ?

english: This is often caused by black pod disease or cherelle wilt, where excess humidity and fungal spores attack young pods, causing them to rot before reaching maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji black pod hela loo Cherel’s wilt. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii lɛ yɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: What basic steps should I take on my farm before the flowering season starts?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Before flowering, you should clear heavy weeds, prune excess branches to let air in, and remove old diseased pods so the tree can send all its energy to fresh blossoms.
ga: Dani fɔfɔi lɛ baawo lɛ, esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni tsii lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. ni ojie ŋmeii ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ awo fɔfɔi heei lɛ amli.

english: Why do agricultural officers need to visit my farm in person instead of just telling me what to do at the office?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ abasara miŋmɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛɛ amɛ nɔ ni esa akɛ amɛfee yɛ ɔfis lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Officers visit in person to inspect your farm's unique shade levels, soil moisture, and pest presence, allowing them to spot specific issues that cannot be diagnosed from a distance.
ga: Amralofoi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ basara koni amɛyakwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ yɔɔ ha. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsɔɔ naagbai pɔtɛɛ ni anyɛɛɛ ana kɛjɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away some branches from my cocoa tree when it looks healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi amli be mli ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni amɛji eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Pruning allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the main trunk where flowers grow, reducing fungal diseases and helping the tree focus its energy on making fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso titri lɛ he ni fɔfɔii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from the base of my crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water and soil nutrients away from your trees and provide hiding places for pests that attack young flowers and pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ naa he ni amɛhiɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides shelter and keeps the soil moist while the young trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer before my crop flowers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani ewo fɔfɔi?

english: If your plant leaves look pale yellow instead of deep green, or if the tree grows very slowly, the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen or potassium needed for healthy flowering.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ loo kɛji tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔi kpakpai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing flowers during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, trees save water by dropping leaves and shutting down flower production to survive the dry heat until the rains return.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei buɔ nu he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛkpaa lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and moisture for cocoa seedlings to survive their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases and allows maximum light exposure for bigger tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ naa la babaoo.

english: That is how groundnuts form their pods. After the flower is fertilized above ground, the plant grows a stem called a peg that burrows into the soil where the groundnut nuts develop.
ga: Nakai ji bɔ ni ŋmeii feɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Beni awo fɔfɔi lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ mli.

english: Flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant moves the limited nitrogen it has to its newer leaves, causing the older leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛyaa baai heei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai momo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer on dry soil when there is no rain coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve so plant roots can safely drink it in. Fertilizer put on dry soil stays concentrated around roots, which can scorch the plant and waste the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu ni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ ashã ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite.

english: Planting too close causes the maize plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin stalks with very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso kakadaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa. Ayɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ŋmeii bɛ kwraa.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is typically caused by a virus carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Once infected, the plant's growth stalls and fruit production drops significantly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii hiɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji hela lɛ emɔ lɛ pɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why are my small green cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up on the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ tsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy, humid weather, or by natural thinning where the tree drops excess pods it cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. aloo kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ nɔ, ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye niyenii lɛ ashwieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if heavy rains flood the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Soil soaked with standing water suffocates the roots, allowing water-loving fungi to attack and rot them rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Shikpɔŋ ni nu ni ekã shi ewo mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: How long after planting a mango tree should I expect it to start producing fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ ebaabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ mango ni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grafted mango trees usually start bearing their first few fruits about three years after planting, whereas trees grown directly from seed take longer, often between five to seven years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu amɛ. Yɛ be mli ni mango tsei ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo teŋ.

english: My mango tree is full of flowers right now; how long will it take for these flowers to turn into mature fruits I can pick?
ga: Mi mango tso lɛ eyi kɛ fɔfɔi bianɛ. Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani fɔfɔi nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ ni manyɛ makpa?

english: After flowering, it typically takes about three to five months for mango blossoms to develop into fully mature fruits ready for harvest, depending on the variety and weather conditions.
ga: Kɛji akɛ mango fɔfɔi lɛ wo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 3-5 dani mango fɔfɔi lɛ baatsɔ aduawai ni eda ni esa akɛ akpa. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ.

english: Why is my young mango tree producing only two or three fruits this year instead of a full harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso lɛ ewo yibii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ afi nɛɛ, shi jeee ni ewo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Young trees focus most of their energy on growing deep roots and strong branches first. The initial harvest is naturally small, but yield will increase significantly as the tree matures.
ga: Kɛha tsei bibii lɛ, okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ niji ni mli wa ni miida lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ ji nɔ bibioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi yibiiwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ waa beni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Will my fruit trees produce the same amount of fruit every year, or does the yield increase over time?
ga: Ani mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo daa afi loo yibiiwoo lɛ baaya hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Fruit trees yield much larger quantities as they grow older and bigger because a larger canopy supports more blossoms and supplies more energy to sustain a heavy harvest.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋwɛi ŋta ni da lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi babaoo ni ehaa hewalɛ babaoo koni ekɛkwɛ nibii ni tsii ni afeɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why did my fruit tree give a huge harvest last year but is hardly producing anything this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso yibii lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ? Shi eshɛɛɛ nɔ ko kwraa ni ekɛbaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: Some fruit trees experience alternate bearing, where a very heavy crop exhausts the tree's nutrient reserves, requiring it to rest and store up energy the following year before fruiting heavily again.
ga: Yibii tsei komɛi yɛ sui ni tsakeɔ amɛhe. Tso lɛ tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa ejɔɔ ehe ni ebuaa hewalɛ naa yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli dani ewoɔ yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some small mangoes fall off the tree before they grow big enough to eat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni ayeɔ lɛ?

english: Trees naturally drop excess young fruits if they do not have enough water, nutrients, or strength to support all of them, ensuring the remaining fruits grow healthy and strong.
ga: Tsei lɛ baajie aduawai bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛye amɛbua aduawai muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ baaha yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni efee nɔ ni wa ni eye emuu.

english: How does cutting back older branches help my fruit trees yield more in the future?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji momo ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo wɔsɛɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or weak wood and opens the inner tree to sunlight and airflow, encouraging new growth that can support larger quantities of fruit in upcoming seasons.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ. ni ogbele tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ dalɛ hee ni baanyɛ aye abua aduawai babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: If I water my young fruit trees during the dry season, will it help them bear fruit sooner?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tsei bibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ani ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii oya?

english: Yes, keeping young trees watered during dry spells prevents stunted growth and helps build a strong root system faster, allowing the tree to reach fruiting maturity on schedule.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛhaa tsei bibii yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ baaye abua ni amɛtsi amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shishifãi ni mli wa oya Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyashɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ be naa.

english: What happens to my harvest if I plant my fruit trees too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tsei ni woɔ yibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting trees too closely causes them to fight for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water, which slows their growth and leads to fewer fruits on each tree.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni haa tso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo ni ehaa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko woɔ yibii fioo.

english: Will adding fertilizer make my fruit tree start producing fruits faster, or does it just make the tree tall?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaje yibiiwoo shishi oya loo ebaaha amɛfee shwiili kɛkɛ?

english: Fertilizer provides essential nutrients that build a strong trunk and leaf canopy early on, and once the tree is mature, specific nutrients encourage abundant flower and fruit formation.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei ahe tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ feɔ ŋmɔji mra. Ni kɛ́ tso lɛ eda kwraa Niyenii pɔtɛɛi baawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava and maize crops die so quickly when a bushfire passes near my farm, even if the flames do not touch them directly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ koo mli la ho yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ la lɛ kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ po.

english: Extreme heat from nearby fires scorches the leaves and dries out moisture inside plant stems instantly. Even without direct flame contact, intense heat bakes the upper soil and damages delicate roots near the surface.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ la ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ baashã baai lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Kɛji akɛ la kɛ la kpaaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ po lɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ.

english: How does clearing a wide strip of bare soil around my farm protect my crops from dry season fires?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ la he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: A fire belt creates a boundary where fire runs out of fuel. Because fire needs dry grass and crop waste to spread, a clean strip of bare dirt stops the flames from crossing into your cultivated field.
ga: La bɛlɛi feɔ husu ko he ni la lɛ mli tsofa lɛ baaho yɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la biɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ tsiɔ la naa koni ekafo mli kɛbote oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops grow so poorly in soil that was burnt by heavy bushfires during the last dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni koo mli la shã waa yɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fire burns away vital organic matter and kills beneficial organisms in the soil that naturally feed crop roots. This leaves the soil nutrient-poor and hard, making it difficult for new crops to thrive.
ga: La shãa nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ewaa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei heei akɛ amɛakwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crops curl up tightly during the hottest afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to trap moisture. By reducing leaf surface area exposed to direct sunlight, the crop loses less water through evaporation until the heat subsides.
ga: Baai lɛ akumɔ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ emɔɔ nu mli nu. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei laajeɔ nu fioo kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and drop leaves when planted in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunshine. They need natural shade from tall plants like plantains to protect their delicate leaves from sun scorching and to keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni jɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my pepper plants lose their flowers without producing fruit during extremely hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fite ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heat stress becomes too severe, crops drop their flowers to save water and energy for basic survival rather than spending resources on developing new fruits.
ga: Kɛji dɔlɛ he haomɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee aduawai henɔi heei

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during midday even when the ground is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiko kwraa lolo?

english: In hot sunshine, leaves evaporate water faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. This temporary water deficit causes wilting, but the plant usually recovers overnight when temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni bɛ be kukuoo nɛɛ haa ŋmeii baa. Shi bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he waa nyɔɔŋ kome mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains flood my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil pushes out oxygen that crop roots need to breathe. Without air in the root zone, root tissues suffocate and rotting organisms thrive in the saturated soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni esa akɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ kɛyaa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ Shifã lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back faster than my planted maize after the first rains of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ oya fe ŋmãa ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild species adapted to survive harsh local conditions and store energy in deep seeds or roots, allowing them to absorb rainwater and sprout faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli kooloi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato dumɔwui loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ amli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow taller and darker green around spots where rotting plant leaves were left in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei ni baai ni egboi eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Decaying leaves break down into natural compost that enriches the soil with essential nutrients like nitrogen, which feeds crop roots and promotes healthy green leaf growth.
ga: Baai ni fiteɔ lɛ gbálaa amɛhe amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ daraa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, harsh sunlight because it dries out their leaves and burns the stems. Keeping some tall shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects the young trees from sunburn and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa amɛshishifãi lɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When a plantain tree produces too many suckers (young shoots), they all compete for the same food and water in the soil. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to put its full energy into growing big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ wo ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of saving water during dry spells. By letting its leaves fall, the plant reduces water loss and protects the underground tubers so they stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ ji ŋmei adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni egbee shi lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight high off the ground to make food for the underground tuber. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and prevents them from rotting on damp ground, leading to larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli ni ehaaa amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ baatsɔ agbo.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce small cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize plants are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to grow thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars inside the center stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which hides in the central growing point of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves. Spotting them early and applying recommended control measures protects the stem so the plant can mature.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela ko, ni kɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni daraa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Ni gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe koni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from getting fertilized to form fruits. Providing light shade and maintaining consistent watering helps protect the blossom development during hot periods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛ amɛwo fɔmɔ nii ni amɛwo yibii. Shade ni mli tse kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that feed on the sap and transmit viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the foliage healthy so the plant can produce good peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, this extra nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that shields the ground from direct sun heat. It slows down water evaporation from the soil, suppresses weeds, and breaks down over time to enrich the earth.
ga: Mulching ni egbi (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them provides shade and keeps the air humid, protecting the young leaves until the trees are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu baai bibii ahe kɛyashi tso lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are there holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ yɛ bu ko ni akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that eat through young maize leaves. Catching them early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts into the central leaves helps protect your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni ji bio-insecticide loo neem extract ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ lɛ baashwie baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water sits around them in flat, poorly drained soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping moisture steady in the soil helps flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto tall stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to get maximum sunlight for growing big tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Maize needs fertilizer at two main stages: first within two weeks after germination to build strong roots, and a second time at knee-high stage when the plant is growing rapidly and building cobs.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ lɛ ji yɛ otsii enyɔ mli beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ koni efee shishifãi ni wa. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ daa oya ni efeɔ ŋmei lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stems and tiny harvests. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to thrive.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when I add manure to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early in the crop's growth ensures your plants get the benefit of the manure.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ tsei adalɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe sɛɛ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. Seeds that germinate right after the first rain can dry up and die in the hot soil before the main rainy season fully established itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early with sticky traps or safe sprays stops the virus from stunting the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Early Whitefly Kudɔmɔ kɛ tsɔne ni shwieɔ mɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe Etsiɔ helai ni baa tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm in Ghana is good enough for cocoa trees to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni cacao tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, soft soil that drains water easily and is rich in decayed leaves and organic matter so their deep taproots can spread and absorb nutrients without rotting in standing water.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ oya, ni baai ni egboi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, taproot ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni efiteee yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: If I expand my farm to a new area or town in Ghana, will my cocoa grow the same way as my old farm?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ tee he ko loo maŋ hee ko yɛ Ghana. Ani mi-cocoa lɛ baakwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔ momo lɛ daa lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Cocoa performance changes depending on local rainfall, soil depth, and forest cover, so a new location may need different shade tree density or soil nutrients to yield well.
ga: Cocoa hewalɛ tsakeɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ naa. shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ kooi lɛ amli No hewɔ lɛ, he hee ko baanyɛ abi ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ayibɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto aba koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high temperatures. Shade trees protect them from intense heat and conserve soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trunk drop off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers drop easily when the tree experiences stress from dry weather, lack of nutrients, or a lack of tiny insects called midges that pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ lɛ mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce plenty of pods during some months and very few in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli, ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa tree flowering and pod growth follow rainy weather patterns, leading to one major harvest season and a smaller minor harvest season in Ghana each year.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi náa cacao tsei lɛ afɔfɔi kɛ amɛdalɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa kpamɔ be titri kome kɛ kpamɔ bei bibii ni ji enyɔ baa Ghana daa afi.

english: Why do I need to cut off excess branches from my growing cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ cacao tso ni miida lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unwanted branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach the inner trunk, which encourages more flowers to bloom and stops fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni ataooo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi babaoo afɔlɔ ni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How many years can my cocoa tree keep bearing fruit before it gets too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ mi cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A healthy cocoa tree starts bearing fruit around 3 to 5 years after planting and can remain productive for 25 to 30 years if properly pruned, weeded, and protected from pests.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ amɛmli, ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Black Pod Disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during cold, damp rainy seasons when too much shade and water trap moisture around the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ nu ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my cocoa crop even after the trees are tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye mi-cacao tsei lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer and moisture from the top layer of soil that cocoa surface roots rely on, while dense weeds hold unwanted dampness that attracts pests to the tree trunks.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni kookoo shishifãi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni ataooo ni gbalaa kooloi kɛbaa tso lɛ shishi.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to be plucked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color completely, turning bright yellow or orange depending on the variety, and makes a hollow sound when gently tapped.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni egbɔ lɛ baatsake amɛhe su kwraa. Amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. ni efeɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛji akɛ ata he fioo

english: Why are my crops drying up even though it rained heavily just a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ egbi lɛ? Ni nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ?

english: When rainfall patterns change and become unpredictable, sudden heavy downpours often wash away topsoil without soaking deep into the earth. If your soil lacks organic matter like compost to hold moisture, the strong sun quickly dries out the ground, leaving crops thirsty shortly after it rains.
ga: Beni nugbɔshiimɔi tsakeɔ ni ebafeɔ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa trukaa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ, kumai yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs when the rains start late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Maize needs steady water during its flowering and grain-filling stages. If delayed rains push these critical stages into hotter, drier weeks, the plant gets stressed and channels its energy into basic survival rather than growing big, full cobs.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa daa yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ni awoɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ lɛ, nɛkɛ bei ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ baaya otsii ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ amli. Tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shishijee wala mli. Mohu ɔ, e daa nɛ e peeɔ ngma nɛ e hyi.

english: Why does buying chemical fertilizers cost so much more these days, and do my crops really need them all the time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara wa waa yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ? Ni ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be?

english: Fertilizer prices rise due to high fuel and transport costs worldwide. While crops need nutrients to yield well, relying only on chemical fertilizers gets expensive. You can lower costs by mixing smaller amounts of fertilizer with manure or compost, which improves soil health and helps crops withstand harsh weather.
ga: Fertilizer jara miiya hiɛ yɛ fuɛl kɛ tsɔne ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo ni fa babaoo yɛ je lɛŋ he fɛɛ he lɛ hewɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai he miihia tsei koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai moŋ, Shi tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ ni akɛaafɔ lɛ he jara wa. Obaanyɛ okɛ shika ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni okɛfutuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdamɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai anaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my vegetables turning yellow and curling up during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce its surface area and prevent water loss when temperatures get too high. Yellowing happens when excessive heat slows down the plant's ability to absorb nutrients from the dry soil.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsiɔ nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ naa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Yellowing baa kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Which high-value crops can I grow in Ghana that sell for good money to big hotels and supermarkets?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ shika kpakpa ahaa gbɔiatoohei wuji kɛ jarayeli hei wuji?

english: Specialty crops like sweet peppers, broccoli, cucumbers, and seedless watermelons command higher prices from high-end buyers. However, these crops require extra investment in reliable watering systems and careful pest control to meet strict market standards.
ga: Tsei krɛdɛɛi tamɔ ŋmeii, brokoli, kukumba, kɛ watermelon ni dumɔwui bɛ mli Enɛ haa amɛjara wa waa kɛhaa mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni jara wa waa lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ biɔ ni akɛ shika kroko awo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ mli, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ashɛ jarayeli he mlai ni mli wa lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds now that the traditional rainy seasons are no longer predictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu nii yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ji ekome lɛ? Enyɛŋ etsɔɔ nɔ ni baaba dɔŋŋ.

english: Instead of planting strictly by calendar dates, wait until the soil gets a deep soak from at least two good rains. Using early-maturing or drought-tolerant seed varieties can also protect your investment if the rains stop earlier than expected.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ kalanda gbi lɛ naa lɛ. Mɛɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ mli waa. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ he kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni okpaa gbɛ.

english: Why are expensive pesticides failing to stop insects from eating my crops this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jara wa lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsĩ kooloi ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Unpredictable weather and warmer temperatures cause insect populations to multiply faster. Additionally, spraying right before an unexpected rain washes the chemical away, wasting money. Rotating different pest control methods instead of relying on one expensive spray works better.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ shihilɛ ni bɛ shiŋŋ kɛ latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ miiha kooloi ayibɔ miifa oya. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ aya. Eji shika fitemɔ. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi lɛ atsakemɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa pɛ baatsu nii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ hi fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why are my crop yields dropping every year even though I farm the land the exact same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Farming the same land repeatedly without giving the soil rest or adding organic matter depletes essential plant nutrients. Irregular rains also wash away the fertile topsoil, leaving behind hard ground that makes it difficult for crop roots to spread and feed.
ga: Okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Kɛji akɛ ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ, tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baafite. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ hu hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ shiɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa yɛ sɛɛ, ni haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛna niyenii.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants keep falling off before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when daytime temperatures are extremely high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between dry and wet. The plant drops its blossoms to save energy because extreme heat damages the pollen needed to form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ejaakɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi ni he hiaa koni akɛfee tomato lɛ.

english: Why is it so risky for me to spend money planting high-cost crops when the weather is uncertain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mawo oshara kpele ni ji shika ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ ahe lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High-cost crops require expensive seeds, fertilizers, and extra care. If unpredictable rains cause a drought or flood mid-season, you lose all the money invested upfront, which can be hard to recover without financial insurance or guaranteed buyers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni jara wa waa lɛ biɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ loo nu afua ba yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ. Obaafite shika fɛɛ ni okɛwo mli kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa akɛ aaaná ekoŋŋ kɛji shika he inshuɔrans loo mɔ ko ni yɔɔ nɔmimaa akɛ ebaahe lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow better inside the forest shade than on open land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ koo lɛ mli fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally thrive under forest shade because the tree canopy protects their sensitive leaves from harsh sun scorch, keeps the soil moist, and provides natural nutrients from fallen leaf litter.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ shishi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ejaakɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ buɔ baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ amli

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa is recommended because plantains grow quickly to provide vital shade for young cocoa seedlings while giving you food and income before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ kookoo dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, plantains lɛ daa oya koni ekɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa aha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani ajeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the thick trunk of the tree instead of on small stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe tsei akutsei bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods grow heavy as they mature. Growing flowers directly on the solid trunk and thick main branches allows the tree to support the weight of full cocoa pods without breaking branches.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsii kɛji amɛdara kwraa. Kɛ́ adu fɔfɔii yɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ niji wuji ni mli tse lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekwɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli tsiimɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni efoŋ niji lɛ.

english: Why do my crops shed their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants drop their leaves during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss, helping the main stem and roots survive until the rainy season returns.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Weeds are naturally wild, hardy plants with aggressive root systems designed to absorb soil nutrients and water immediately, outcompeting cultivated crops for early growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ atsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ehi fe tsei ni akwɛɔ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why does land cleared in the forest produce healthier crops than my farm near the village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajie yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe miŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Forest soils have accumulated decayed leaves and organic matter over many years without disturbance, creating naturally rich soil full of nutrients compared to land near villages that has been farmed continuously.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ ebua baai kɛ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa yɛ afii babaoo mli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ akrowai ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ he.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees produce fewer pods than they did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni edara lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their internal transport systems slow down, making it harder for roots to pull nutrients to the upper branches, leading to lower pod yields.
ga: Beni cacao tsei hiɔ shi fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, tso lɛ mli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbala niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛya tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pod yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: How do I know the exact time when my cocoa pods are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready to harvest when the skin changes color completely, typically turning from green or deep red to a yellow or orange color, showing the beans inside are mature.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni amɛhiɛ su etsake kwraa lɛ. Etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do cocoa beans need to be covered with banana leaves for a few days right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ banana baai aha kookoo yibii ahe gbii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Covering freshly harvested cocoa beans with plantain or banana leaves creates heat that ferments the beans. Fermentation kills the bean embryo, removes the sweet pulp, and creates the chocolate flavor.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantains loo banana baai ha kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa ehee lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa koni ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Fɛ̃i gbeɔ ŋmãa fɔmɔ kotokui. Jiemɔ loo ni ŋɔɔ lɛ. ni afee tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, and overly wet conditions when rain droplets stay on the cocoa pods for too long.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hei ni edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ hi kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ,

english: Leaves turn yellow when the maize plant lacks essential plant food, especially nitrogen, or when the roots are drowning in too much standing water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the plant build fresh green leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa. titri lɛ nitrogen loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ ebote nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn and tomato plants curl up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kɛ tomato tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. When the sun is very hot, plants roll their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the heat, which stops them from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ akafite kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience severe heat stress, dry soil, or a sudden lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil moist around the root area helps the plant feel stable enough to turn flowers into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni etsɔɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with wide leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing plants properly gives each plant enough room to grow big leaves, strong stems, and larger fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaakwɛ baai wuji. tso ni mli wa kɛ aduawai loo bulbs wuji

english: Why do I need to provide long sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi niji kakadaji koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can catch full sunlight to make plant food. That food travels down to swell the yam tubers underground. Leaving vines on the hot ground can also burn them and lower your harvest.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛkɛfee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Niyenii lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ oshi wein tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã wein tsei lɛ ni eha onibii lɛ aba shi.

english: Heavy rain in soil that doesn't drain well chokes the roots by cutting off air. Without air, soil fungi attack the soft tubers and make them rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away from roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Fungi lɛ tutuaa bulbs bibii ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans make my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can draw invisible plant food (nitrogen) from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant harvest is done, that stored food remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii, ni baanyɛ agbala tsei aniyenii ni anaaa (nitrogen) kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji agbe ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ naa Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛye ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Covering soil with dried leaves or grass (called mulching) acts like a blanket. It shades the dirt from the hot sun so water doesn't dry out quickly, stops weeds from taking over, and turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ muji ni jɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ naa. koni nu lɛ akagbi oya Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni ebafeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ kɛ́ egbo.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if they are not touching each other?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛtaaa amɛhe po?

english: Weed roots spread quickly underground and steal water and nutrients away from your crop's roots. Weeds also grow tall and block sunlight, causing your crops to starve and produce smaller yields.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Jwɛi hu daa ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshinii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and intense heat. Planting shade crops like plantains protects them from scorching, keeps the soil cool, and helps the trees retain moisture to survive until maturity.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shãa naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize crop look weak and pale green even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize requires nitrogen to develop healthy, dark green leaves. Pale leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which can be fixed by applying balanced fertilizer like NPK or urea at the right stage of growth.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ená baai ni mli wa, ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛbaafata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. Look for yellowing lower leaves that begin to drop and cracks forming in the earth around the base of the stem.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni miibɔi gbee kɛ ŋmeii ni miifee yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking fields early and applying recommended pest treatments inside the leaf funnels before the damage spreads protects your final harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni adu lɛ anɔ mra. Ni kɛ okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ ayeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli dani nɔ ni efite lɛ gbɛ eshwa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onaagbee ŋmaa lɛ he.

english: Bare soil loses water quickly to sun exposure and wind. Covering the soil around plants with dried leaves, grass, or crop stalks acts like a blanket, trapping moisture in the earth longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo tsei ahe tsei lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crop seeds very close together?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stems and low yields. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce fully.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni enyɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Excess water and soil splashing onto stems create a moist environment for fungal diseases like blight to spread. Staking tomato branches to lift them off the wet soil helps keep plants clean and dry.
ga: Nu kɛ sũ ni fa fe nine ni shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Tomato ni ajieɔ lɛ koni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tseɔ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my pepper plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, uneven watering, or a shortage of essential plant food like phosphorus. Keeping water supply steady and improving soil nutrients helps flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Nu jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in a field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize uses up heavy amounts of nitrogen from the ground, but leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it back into the soil, restoring fertility naturally for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my main crops during the early weeks of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi ni mikɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardy and quick to absorb available moisture and plant nutrients. Removing weeds within the first 3 to 6 weeks gives young crops a strong head start to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei amli niyenii oya. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 6 lɛ mli lɛ, ebaawo dumɔwui lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to cut off some of the healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mifolɔ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting off selected branches, called pruning, allows sunlight and air to flow freely through the tree. This prevents dark, damp conditions where diseases like black pod thrive, and helps the tree direct its energy into growing larger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni ahala lɛ ni afolɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa. Biɛ ji he ni helai tamɔ black pods lɛ daa yɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa farm if I leave the trees to grow naturally without ever pruning them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji miha tsei lɛ dara yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni mifooo amɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Unpruned trees grow too bushy, blocking sunlight and trapping moisture. This creates a perfect environment for pests and fungal diseases to spread, which reduces the number of healthy pods you can harvest.
ga: Tsei ni afolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ baakwɛ̃ tsɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Why is it important for me to clean my cutting tools before moving from one cocoa tree to another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsumɔ mitsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ amli dani majie amɛ kɛjɛ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Dirty pruning tools can carry disease spores from a sick tree directly into the open cut of a healthy tree, quickly spreading infections across your entire farm.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni he tseee lɛ baanyɛ ajie helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Can using heavy motorized machines or motorized pruners do any harm to my crop yields?
ga: Ani tsɔnei wuji ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii loo tsɔnei ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?
