english: Yes, if motorized tools are not handled correctly, they can strip off too much bark or crush healthy wood. These jagged wounds take longer to heal and make the tree vulnerable to insect attacks and rot.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ akɛ tsɔnei ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ agbo loo efo tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ pilamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ heɔ be babaoo dani etsaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni kooloi baanyɛ atutua lɛ ni efite.

english: How do I know if a motorized weeding or pruning machine is causing damage to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-lawn tsɔne loo tsɔne ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If you notice torn or shredded plant tissues instead of clean cuts, or if bark is peeling off the main trunk after using the machine, the equipment needs adjustment or gentler handling.
ga: Kɛji ona tso lɛ mli fã ko ni egbɛ eshwa loo egbɛ eshwa Yɛ tso lɛ fã ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ loo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ fã kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he beni okɛ tsɔne lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ Ehe miihia ni atsake nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ loo akɛtsu nii blɛoo.

english: Why should I join a local cocoa farmers' cooperative in my town?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe awo maŋ lɛ mli kookoo okwaafoi akuu ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Joining a cooperative allows you to buy farm supplies like fertilizers at lower prices, share the cost of modern farm equipment, receive direct training from extension officers, and sell your harvest at reliable prices.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo kuu ko mli lɛ, obaanyɛ ohe okwaayeli he nibii, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ. Jaa ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo. Na tsɔsemɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔi lɛ adɛŋ. ni ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ jara ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Can a younger farmer like me join a local farming group if mostly older elders belong to it?
ga: Ani okwaafonyo oblanyo fioo ko tamɔ mi baanyɛ afata maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli kuu ko he? Kɛji onukpai lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo yɛ kuu nɛɛ mli

english: Yes, farming groups welcome energetic younger members to help with physically demanding work like pruning and spraying, while you benefit from the elders' years of practical experience and knowledge.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli kui hereɔ oblahii kɛ oblayei ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ lɛ atuu koni amɛye amɛbua yɛ nitsumɔi ni biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ babaoo tamɔ tsei ahe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ amli. Beni onáa wɔ onukpai lɛ afii babaoo anilee kɛ nilee ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ he sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the small cocoa pods on my tree turning black and dying before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pods often die early due to fungal diseases like black pod or damage from insects like mirids (capsids). Too much shade, lack of airflow, or bad weather can make this problem worse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii gboiɔ oya yɛ ŋmeii helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji, loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii, tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ ahewɔ. Shade babaoo tsɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ Loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii baanyɛ aha naagba nɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is shedding leaves normally or if it is suffering from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo tso lɛ miiho baai lɛ bɔ ni sa loo hela emɔ lɛ?

english: Normal leaf shedding happens gradually during dry seasons across the whole tree. If leaves suddenly turn yellow, develop dark spots, or if branch tips start dying back quickly, your tree is likely suffering from a disease or severe pest damage.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi daa lɛ baa fiofio. Ebaa yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa. Hei ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ jeɔ kpo loo kɛji tso lɛ nine lɛ naagbee lɛ bɔi gbele oya Etamɔ nɔ ni Otso lɛ hu baaná hela ni naa wa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods even when the trees look very big and tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda waa ni ekɛlɛ moŋ?

english: Overly tall trees put most of their food and energy into growing wood and leaves instead of flowers and pods. Keeping trees at a manageable height through pruning encourages them to fruit heavily.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ tsei kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ Tso lɛ ni oooha ehi he ko ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are some of my cassava plants growing straight up while others branch out and spread wide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu shwereɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ?

english: Stem branching depends on the cassava variety. Straight-growing varieties are easier to weed around and intercrop with other plants, while branching varieties spread out early to cover the soil and prevent weeds from growing.
ga: Niji ni shwereɔ lɛ damɔ ŋmei henɔ lɛ nɔ. Henɔi ni adu tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbe jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. ni ewaaa akɛ akɛ tsei krokomɛi baakwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni niji srɔtoi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin instead of strong and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiifee mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow thin and weak when planted too close together or in shaded areas. They stretch upward competing for sunlight, so keeping proper spacing between seeds helps them build strong, thick stalks.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛfee tsei ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow slanted and weak instead of straight up from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ etsɔ ŋwɛi ni egbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaajɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Slanted, weak suckers with broad leaves are called 'water suckers' which grow from shallow buds and produce poor yields. Strong 'sword suckers' grow straight up with narrow leaves from deep roots and should be chosen for planting.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ akɛ ‘nu tsei’, ni jɛɔ tsei ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. ‘Klante tsei’ ni he wa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ baai bibii ni jɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli ni esa akɛ ahala kɛha dumɔ.

english: Peppers drop flowers when the soil is too dry, temperatures get too hot, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to produce lush green leaves instead of holding onto its blossoms.
ga: Peppers baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: How can I tell if my tomato leaves are curling because of hot weather or a disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ o-tomato lɛ baai lɛ miihoso yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hewɔ loo hela ko yɛ amɛhe?

english: Leaves that curl neatly upward during the hottest part of the day usually mean water stress. However, if the leaves look rough, twisted, and yellow-mottled, it is a sign of a viral disease carried by insects like whiteflies.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi fɛfɛo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ nu he haomɔ, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛtsake ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ eji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies kɛbaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants looking rough and crinkled instead of smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Rough, crinkled, or twisted leaves on cowpea are a signal of viral infection spread by sap-sucking insects like aphids. Healthy plants naturally maintain smooth, dark green leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbɔjɔ, loo ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tsina ŋmei nɔ lɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eŋɔli diŋŋ nɔ.

english: What makes my rice plants fall over flat on the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa?

english: Rice plants fall over, or lodge, when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or are planted too close together, making their stems soft and weak under the weight of the ripening grain heads during rain or heavy winds.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashishi yɛ nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees produce smooth pods while others have very rough, bumpy pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Pod shape and surface texture depend on the cocoa variety and insect damage. Smooth pods are common in certain hybrid varieties, while rough or deformed pods can be a natural trait of older varieties or caused by mirid bug attacks.
ga: Pod su kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ damɔ kookoo henɔi lɛ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Smooth pods ji nɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ hybrid henɔi komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni efite lɛ baanyɛ afee adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmeii sɔrɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ amli loo nɔ ni jɛ naakpɛɛ kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ mli baa lɛ,.

english: How can I make sure my yam crop produces straight tubers that are easy to harvest and market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni ja ni akpaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ mlɛo?

english: Tuber shape is controlled by both variety choice and soil preparation. Planting varieties like 'Pona' in deep, loose, heap-built soil allows tubers to grow straight down without hitting hard ground that causes them to twist or branch.
ga: Yitso su ji nɔ ni akudɔɔ srɔtoi ni ahalaa kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi tamɔ ‘Pona’ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa bulb lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shi ni etswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ehaa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe loo amɛkuɔ niji.

english: Why do my garden eggs look shiny and smooth on some bushes but small and wrinkled on others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkpɛɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ tsei bibii komɛi anɔ shi amɛji bibii ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ekrokomɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Wrinkled or distorted garden egg fruits happen when tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites feed on young fruit buds, or when the crop lacks consistent water during fruit formation.
ga: Yibii amli ŋmeii ni egbɔjɔ loo efite yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips loo mites, ye aduawai bibii lɛ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ.

english: Can I just buy any ripe coconut from the market and plant its seed on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ jara nɔ ni madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is better to trace where the seed comes from. You should inspect the parent (mother) tree first to make sure it produces plenty of large fruits before using its nuts for planting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ he ni dumɔwui lɛ jɛ. Esa akɛ okwɛ tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ (tso ni ji nyɛ) lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ eewo yibii wuji babaoo. Dani abaadu ŋmeii

english: How does the history of a parent tree affect the crop I will harvest on my farm?
ga: Te nyɛ tso lɛ he yinɔsane saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni makpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops inherit traits from their parent tree. If you plant a seed from a mother tree that produces large fruits consistently every year, your new tree is far more likely to do the same.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ sui kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui kɛjɛ tso nyɛ ni woɔ yibii wuji be fɛɛ be daa afi lɛ mli lɛ, eeenyɛ efee akɛ Otso hee lɛ hu baafee nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I ensure that the coconuts I harvest in the future will be big enough for market buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmeii ni mikpaa wɔsɛɛ lɛ baafee babaoo bɔ ni sa kɛha mɛi ni baahe nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit size is inherited. To harvest large coconuts, select your planting seeds exclusively from mother trees that naturally produce big, heavy fruits.
ga: Yibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ gboshinii mli lɛ dalɛ Kɛji oosumɔ ni okpa ŋmeii wuji Halamɔ dumɔwui ni adu kɛjɛ nyɛ tsei ni jɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli amɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: How many years do I need to wait after planting a coconut tree before I can start harvesting?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi amɛkpamɔ?

english: A good coconut tree usually starts bearing fruit after about six years, after which it will yield continuous harvests for many years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tso kpakpa jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii enumɔ sɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaya nɔ ewo yibii afii babaoo.

english: Will my coconut tree continue to give me fruits every single year once it starts bearing?
ga: Ani mi ŋmei tso lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii eha mi afi fɛɛ afi kɛji ebɔi yibii womɔ pɛ?

english: Yes, if you select seeds from a mother tree that bears fruit every year and give your crop proper care, it will keep producing harvests season after season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ohala dumɔwui kɛjɛ nyɛ tso ko ni woɔ yibii daa afi mli ni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Ebaaya nɔ ekpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ naa.

english: Is there a way for me to know if a crop will yield well before I spend time planting it?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ko baawo yibii kpakpai dani maŋɔ be kɛdu?

english: Yes, by checking the background of the parent tree. If the mother tree bears a lot of fruit regularly, its seedlings are very likely to give you a heavy yield too.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ tso ni jɛ mli ba lɛ sɛɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo daa lɛ Dumɔwui hu sumɔɔ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some coconut trees produce fruits continuously while others stop after one season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii shi ekrokomɛi kpaɔ yɛ be kome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yield consistency comes from genetic background. Seedlings selected from mother trees known to bear fruit every year will produce reliable harvests annually.
ga: Yibiiwoo lɛ mli ekomefeemɔ lɛ jɛɔ fɔmɔ su mli. Dumɔwui ni ahala kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tsei ni ale akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii daa afi lɛ amli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: I saw farming tips on social media like YouTube, but can I rely on them for my local farm?
ga: Minaa okwaayeli he ŋaawoi yɛ social media tamɔ YouTube nɔ, shi ani manyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ amɛnɔ kɛha mimaŋ ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: While online videos give general ideas, nothing beats practical experience like going into the field to check the actual performance history of local mother trees before planting.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ vidioi ni yɔɔ Intanɛt lɛ nɔ lɛ haa susumɔ ko ni kɔɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ he moŋ. Shi nɔ ko bɛ ni hi fe niiashikpamɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii tamɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aya koni ayakwɛ maŋ lɛ mli tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ he yinɔsane diɛŋtsɛ dani adu lɛ.

english: Is it better to get planting seeds from high-producing trees in my own village?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ okrowa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, using seeds from high-performing mother trees in your village is great because those trees have already proven they can thrive and bear fruit in your local environment.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ fɔlɔi tsei ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ okrowa lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii ejaakɛ nakai tsei lɛ ejie amɛhe kpo akɛ amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: What specific things should I look out for when selecting a mother tree for seeds?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ mihe jogbaŋŋ yɛ he titri kɛ́ mihala nyɛ tsei kɛha dumɔwui?

english: Look for a parent tree that is healthy, bears a large quantity of big fruits, and produces consistently every year without long breaks.
ga: Taomɔ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ha aduawai babaoo ni owo yibii ni yaa nɔ daa afi ni okɛ hejɔɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ akafee

english: Why do the crop chemicals I buy from the market these days seem weaker and take longer to kill weeds in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛduɔ nii ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ be babaoo gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many newly introduced agrochemical products on the market have very low potency or active ingredient concentration, which makes them less effective than genuine, high-potency products.
ga: Agrochemical nibii heei ni ajie lɛ kpo yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ nibii ni tsuɔ nii loo nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni fa fioo kwraa. Enɛ haaa etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni ji anɔkwale ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ.

english: How can using weak or low-potency chemicals affect my final crop harvest?
ga: Te tsofai ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni bɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naagbee ŋmaa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Low-potency chemicals fail to control pests and diseases completely, allowing pests to continue damaging your crops and severely reducing your yield.
ga: Tsofai ni he waaa lɛ nyɛŋ akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kwraa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ yaa nɔ efiteɔ oŋmɔshinii lɛ ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why are some crop protection chemicals cheaper than others even when the bottles look very similar?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ jara waaa fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tɔi lɛ tamɔ amɛhe waa moŋ.

english: Cheaper products often contain diluted or low-potency ingredients, meaning you have to buy and apply much more of the chemical to get the same result as a strong, high-potency chemical.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni jara waaa lɛ amli nibii ni mli ewo nu loo nibii ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ohe tsofai babaoo ni okɛtsu nii koni onine ashɛ nɔ ni tsofai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: How does buying high-potency agrochemicals help me save money as a farmer?
ga: Te agrochemicals ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahemɔ baanyɛ aha maná shika akɛ okwaafonyo lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: High-potency chemicals work effectively in smaller amounts and require fewer spray applications, which reduces overall spending on farm inputs over the season.
ga: Tsofai ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mlijaa bibioo mli, ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fioo pɛ afɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa shika fɛɛ ni afiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe lɛ baa shi yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it risky to try every new farm chemical that gets introduced in my community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ maka ŋmɔ mli tsofa hee fɛɛ tsofa ni akɛba miakutso lɛ mli lɛ aka lɛ?

english: Many new products introduced to the market are of low quality and unverified potency, which can fail to protect your crops during critical growth stages.
ga: Nibii heei babaoo ni miiba jara nɔ lɛ ehiii kwraa, ni anaaa nɔmimaa akɛ amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ nyɛŋ abu onibii ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: What key things should I look for when buying crop chemicals to make sure I am not buying fake ones?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ matao beni miheɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ miheee tsofai ni ji amalei?

english: You should closely inspect the bottle for official company branding, registered logos, and clear product labels that confirm high quality and authenticity.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ tɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ona nitsumɔhe lɛ gbɛi ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ. logo ni aŋmala awo wolo nɔ kɛ nibii ahe okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni maa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ anɔkwale nɔ mi.

english: How can I identify a genuine chemical sales agent when they visit my farm community?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse tsofai ahe jarayeli najiaŋdamɔlɔi diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ amɛbasara miŋmɔ akutso lɛ?

english: Genuine sales representatives usually wear official branded attire, such as company T-shirts displaying the verified logo and product details of the inputs they sell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nihɔɔmɔ najiaŋdamɔlɔi diɛŋtsɛ woɔ atadei ni maŋ lɛ gbɛi tsɔɔ nɔ, tamɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ atadei ni jieɔ nibii ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ ahe okadi ni akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo.

english: Why is it important to pay attention to brand logos when purchasing inputs for my maize and cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama brand logos lɛ anɔ kɛ́ oohe nibii ni akɛwoɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ mi kookoo mli lɛ?

english: Branded logos show that the manufacturer guarantees the high potency and safety of the chemical, helping you avoid low-potency imitations.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsofa nɛɛ he lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mɔ ni fee tsofa lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ tsofa lɛ he wa waa ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe. Enɛ haa otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ nibii ni akaseɔ ni hewalɛ faaa lɛ ahe.

english: What should I do if a chemical seller offers me a farm product in a plain bottle without clear branding?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tsofa-kɛ-ŋma jarayelɔ ko kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni yɔɔ tsɛnsii folo mli ni gbɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ bɛ nɔ lɛ ha?

english: You should avoid buying unbranded or poorly labeled chemicals, as they are likely low-potency or fake products that can harm your crops or fail to control pests.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa tsofai ni aŋmalako nɔ ko loo nɔ ni aŋmalako nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahemɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekolɛ amɛji nibii ni he waaa loo amale nibii ni baanyɛ aye onibii awui loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ.

english: How do I know if the chemical I applied on my crops is working properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miitsu nii?

english: A high-potency, genuine chemical shows fast and visible results on pests or weeds according to the instructions provided by the official manufacturer's label.
ga: Tsofai ni he wa waa, ni ji anɔkwale lɛ jieɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa oya ni anaa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo jwɛi ahe taakɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni akɛha yɛ mɔ ni fee lɛ wolo lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land as my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, shading the young cocoa trees and keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanting angle helps the roots spread out wider near the surface, which produces larger and more numerous tubers while making them easier to harvest later.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ baaha yitsei lɛ afee wuji ni amɛyi fa babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch sunlight for energy. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛha hewalɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly during the dry season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Bare soil loses water fast due to hot sun and wind. Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, traps moisture in the ground and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ hewɔ. Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get consistent water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ tamɔ tomato.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow well. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost around the plant restores its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ Tsei ahe lɛ baaha tsei lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer is concentrated food and can burn the stem and roots if touched directly. Placing it a few inches away in a small circle or hole allows the roots to safely absorb the nutrients without damage.
ga: Fertilizer ji niyenii ni mli edɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei kɛ shishifãi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Okɛ amɛ awo he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo yɛ kooyigbɛ loo bu bibioo ko mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in that spot. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni akwɛɔ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the young leaves inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms feeding inside the leaves. Inspecting your farm early and using neem leaf mixtures or recommended sprays helps protect the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ fallworms ni yeɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ neem baa ni akɛfutu loo spray ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu nibii ni adu lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies carrying plant diseases. Clearing weeds around the farm and applying soapy water or neem extract helps keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ tsei ahelai baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ Okwaafoi kɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly at the bottom of the slope on my farm after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash topsoil and nutrients down the slope, causing water to pool at the bottom. This overly soaked soil starves the plant roots of oxygen, leading to root rot and poor crop growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shishigbɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does rainwater wash away my fertilizer whenever I plant crops straight up and down a hillside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ shwieɔ mi-fertilizer lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni madu tsei tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa gɔŋ ko nɔ kɛbaa shi lɛ?

english: Planting straight down a slope creates natural channels for water to rush down quickly, taking seeds, topsoil, and fertilizer with it. Planting across the slope in curved lines slows down the water and keeps nutrients in the soil.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni nu lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ etsɔɔ shi oya. Kɛ dumɔwui, shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the crops mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The maize plant automatically moves its remaining nitrogen up to support new leaves, leaving the older, bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ekɛ baa heei awo mli. Ha baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress or lack of water during flowering. High temperatures disrupt pollination, causing the plant to shed unpollinated flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa yɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ loo nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ hewɔ. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Ha tsei afɔ fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting them too close starves each plant, resulting in smaller and thinner tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Kɛ́ adu nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tso fɛɛ tso. Enɛ haa yitsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Yam tubers become deformed when the soil underneath is hard, compacted, or stony. Soft, deeply tilled soil allows yam roots to expand downwards smoothly without hitting hard barriers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtswaaa gbɛtsii nii ni wa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or plants like plantain to protect their tender leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni ebu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts before maize make my maize grow better without added fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei dani miwo ŋmei lɛ, ehaa mi ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ ŋmei wooo mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest groundnuts, this trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are wild rodents like grasscutters easily destroying my cassava farm even after I clear around the borders?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi miifite mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ mifo husu lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Clearing around the field creates open space that makes it easy for animals to see and walk straight into your farm. Planting thick living hedges or using mesh barriers helps block rodents from entering.
ga: He ni ebɔle he lɛ mli ni ajieɔ ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ hei ni agbele ni haa kooloi naa ni amɛnyiɛɔ kɛyaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Tsoi bibii ni mli tse ni aduɔ Aloo okɛ ŋshɔŋloo atsu nii ni okɛtsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkabote mli.

english: Lifting tomato plants off the ground prevents leaves and fruits from touching damp soil, which causes fungal diseases and rot. It also exposes the plant to better airflow and sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ owó tomato tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ he. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei hu ni amɛnáa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la.

english: Why do some large seed suppliers store harvested corn in cold rooms with air conditioners?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi wuji komɛi ni kɛ dumɔwui haa lɛ kɛ amɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ toɔ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cold air slows down the natural aging of the corn and puts insect pests to sleep. Keeping corn in a cool environment keeps the seeds fresh, prevents mold, and ensures they will sprout well when planted.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ haa ŋmãa lɛ daalɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ wɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ to he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ afee ehee. Tsiɔ ŋmeii anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu

english: Why does my harvested maize heat up and sweat when I stack the bags together inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔ ni ekɛ latsaa miiwo mli beni mikɛ kotokui lɛ toɔ he kome yɛ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested maize is still living and breathing, which produces natural heat and moisture. Stacking bags tightly in a warm room traps this heat, causing sweating, mold growth, and rotting.
ga: Abele ni akpa lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni eemu. ni haa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa Kɛ́ okɛ kotoku lɛ wo tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ nɛɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji latsaa Fungus lɛ daa ni efiteɔ

english: Can keeping my harvested corn in a cool space help it stay good for a longer time?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, lowering the storage temperature slows down the grain's natural decay process. Cool storage keeps the corn dry, protects it from pests, and maintains its quality for many months.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ajie hulutsoo ni akɛtoɔ lɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ aya hiɛ fioo. Kɛ́ akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni egbiɔ. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo

english: How does hot weather inside my store room damage my harvested maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ mi nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ?

english: Excessive heat causes maize to lose its nutrients, color, and weight faster. Heat also encourages mold growth and creates the perfect environment for destructive insects to multiply rapidly.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmãa mli hewalɛ, ehiɛ su, kɛ egbɔjɔmɔ baa shi oya. Dɔlɛ hu haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ koni amɛshwere oya.

english: How does keeping my harvested grain in a cool area prevent weevils from eating it?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye amɛ?

english: Weevils and grain beetles need warm temperatures to feed and breed. Cold temperatures slow down their movement, stop them from laying eggs, and prevent them from multiplying inside your stored grain.
ga: Weevils kɛ seed moths biɔ he ko ni mli edɔ koni amɛye nii ni amɛfɔ. Fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ haa nyiɛmɔ baa shi. Tsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo ŋmeii. ni etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkashwere yɛ dumɔwui ni okɛtoɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to dry my maize completely in the sun before putting it into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mi-ŋmã lɛ agbi kwraa dani mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sun drying removes excess water from inside the grain. Storing maize with too much moisture causes mold and fungi to grow quickly, which will rot the entire harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mli ewo muji lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Enɛ baaha nibii ni adu lɛ fɛɛ agbo.

english: Why does fresh green corn spoil so much faster than fully dried maize grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ ni afee ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya fe ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fresh corn cobs contain a lot of water and natural sugars that bacteria and fungi love to feed on. Dry corn grains have very little moisture, making it difficult for rot to start.
ga: Nu kɛ adebɔɔ mli sugars babaoo ni bacteria kɛ fungi sumɔɔ ni amɛye lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ mli. Fɛ̃i fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli. Ehaa ewaa akɛ aaabɔi fitemɔ

english: Why does mold grow on my stored corn even if I keep the store room doors closed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shwereɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ shinaa lɛ ŋmɛɔ moŋ?

english: If the air inside the room is warm and trapped, humidity builds up from the corn itself. Mold thrives in warm, still air, so the storage area needs cool temperatures or fresh air flow to stay dry.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ tsu lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Fɛ̃i baabua ehe naa kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mli. Mold shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ekã shi lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, hei ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ he miihia ni hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abɔle he koni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I keep them in a hot shed for several months before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli edɔ mli nyɔji babaoo dani midu lɛ?

english: High heat damages the tiny living embryo inside the seed over time. Storing seeds in hot conditions destroys their vitality, turning them into dead grains that cannot germinate in the soil.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baafite fɔmɔ kotokui bibii ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛshihilɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ bafeɔ dumɔwui ni egboi ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it recommended to keep my seed corn in a cool, shaded area before planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Shade keeps the temperature low and steady around the seeds. Protecting seeds from heat preserves their stored energy so they can sprout quickly and grow into strong crops once planted.
ga: Shade yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni ehiɔ shi daa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Dumɔwu lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ ni ato lɛ hiɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ oya ni etsɔ tso ni he wa kɛji adu lɛ pɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or food crops like plantains to block the sun, the young leaves burn, lose moisture quickly, and turn yellow.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei tamɔ hulutsoo tsei bɛ lɛ, baai bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛbaafite ŋmɔtɔ oya. ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, humid weather. Excess rainwater and dark shade keep the pods wet, allowing the fungus to grow and rot the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni edɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ baaha pods lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ada ni egbo.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra branches from my adult cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata cacao tso ni eda lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning extra or unnecessary branches allows sunlight and fresh air to flow through the tree canopy. This reduces humidity that causes disease and directs the tree's energy into growing more cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of holes with sawdust-like material inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They eat the tender leaf whorls of the maize plant and leave behind waste that looks like coarse sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii ni amɛshiɔ ŋmãa bibii ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up with yellow patches and producing tiny roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ shishifãi bibii.

english: Your crop likely has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or spread through infected planting sticks. It stops the leaves from making food, which prevents roots from growing big.
ga: Ekolɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ cassava mosaic hela he. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ loo egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turn black and sunken before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, usually caused by irregular watering. When the soil dries out completely between waterings, the plant cannot absorb enough calcium to build healthy fruit tissue.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee aduawai amli fãji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs fertilizer or if it is already healthy enough for crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo eyɛ hewalɛ momo bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crop leaves look pale green or yellow instead of dark green, grow very slowly, or give poor yields despite good rain, your soil is low in nutrients and needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal the nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the soil food they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce much smaller fruits when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kwraa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete against each other for limited sunlight, root space, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing lets them grow freely and bear larger fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shishifãi ahe he, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves or grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni baai loo jwɛi ni egbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, keeps the root area cool, and prevents dry soil from baking under the hot sun.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high to capture as much sunlight as possible for tuber growth. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp soil, which prevents rot and leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni bulb lɛ adara. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying a balanced nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the green color and healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil, enriching it naturally for crops planted next, like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does covering my soil with dry grass help my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, reduces evaporation from the sun, and keeps plant roots cool while stopping weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: What is causing small worms to eat holes in the leaves at the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ni oooye bu ni yɔɔ baa lɛ mli ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, destructive pests that hide in the central whorl of young maize. Checking your field early and applying recommended neem extracts or bio-pesticides directly into the center of the plants protects them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli lɛ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking leaf juices, or by viruses they spread. Controlling these insects early with insecticidal soap or neem oil keeps leaves growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ Samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy, poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, protecting the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. koni akɛbu shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when plants experience water stress or lack key nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and proper fertilizer application ensure flowers set into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ amɛmli lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I alternate planting maize with other crops instead of planting maize on the same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi atsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be mli lɛ?

english: Growing maize on the same land continuously drains specific nutrients and allows pests to build up in the soil. Alternating crops breaks pest life cycles and gives the soil time to rebuild essential nutrients.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ wala shihilɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and turn brown when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees or shade trees planted nearby act as living umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and protecting the young plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Amɛ fɛɛ amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller pods when I plant my cocoa trees too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii kɛ́ midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots compete under the soil for water and nutrients, while their branches block sunlight from each other. Spacing them correctly allows every tree to get enough sun, air, and food to grow big pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei aniji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support as full pods. However, losing too many flowers is usually caused by heat stress, lack of rain, or a shortage of tiny beneficial insects like midges that pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ, loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ midges ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baa.

english: Why are some of the small green cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ ekomɛi batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is often cherelle wilt, where the tree naturally sheds extra young pods it cannot feed due to low water or soil nutrients. It can also be caused by black pod disease, which spreads during very wet weather when humidity is high.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ, ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii ejaakɛ nu loo niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Black pod hela hu baanyɛ aha eba, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce lots of green leaves during heavy rains instead of making pods right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo ŋmeii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains arrive, the tree uses the abundant water to build fresh foliage and store up energy. Once leaf growth stops, the tree uses that accumulated strength to blossom and feed new pods.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Tsei kɛ nu babaoo lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai heei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ kpa shweremɔ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ebua naa lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei baa.

english: If I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree, won't that lower the amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Kɛji mifolɔ niji babaoo kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ Ani kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ baaa shi?

english: Pruning actually increases your yield. Removing unnecessary branches ensures the tree directs all its water and nutrients into developing heavy pods instead of wasting energy on excess leaves, while also letting in sunlight to prevent disease.
ga: Kpojiemɔ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha hulu la lɛ akpɛ koni helai akabote mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa shoots and pods look like they have burned dark patches during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii kɛ mi-pods lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those dark, burned patches are caused by sap-sucking insects called mirids or Akate. They bite into the green bark and pods to drink the juices, leaving behind toxic saliva that kills the surrounding plant tissue.
ga: shãa he okadii ni mli ewo duŋ Nibii nɛɛ ji kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo akates lɛ. Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛnu nu lɛ. Amɛshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my mature cocoa trees turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that the plant is struggling to absorb nutrients from the ground. This happens when the soil lacks essential minerals like nitrogen, or when roots are damaged by dry soil or waterlogging.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does leaving fallen cocoa leaves on the ground around the tree trunk help my farm during dry months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi kookoo baai ni egbee shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei akutsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves act as a protective natural blanket over the soil, trapping moisture beneath and keeping root zones cool during dry weather. As the leaves decompose, they return rich nutrients back to the soil.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishi ni oha shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Beni baai lɛ fiteɔ Niyenii ni jara wa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do cocoa beans need to be fermented under leaves for days before sun-drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ kookoo yibii lɛ atsɔ baai lɛ ashishi gbii babaoo dani hulu lɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa seeds inside a pod are bitter and lack chocolate flavor. Fermenting them under plantain leaves allows natural heat and chemical reactions to develop the rich flavor and brown color that buyers look for.
ga: Cocoa yibii heei ni yɔɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ ni ebɛ tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ kɛ tsofai ni tsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during prolonged dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to conserve water. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up under high heat and intense sunlight to reduce water loss through evaporation. It is a protective reaction, but if leaves stay curled even in the morning, it may signal water stress or a virus carried by whiteflies.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulu la shishi koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Eji hebuu hetoo. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi lɛ Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ nu mli haomɔ loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ woɔ.

english: Why are my young maize plants staying short and turning reddish-purple on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni baai lɛ feɔ red-purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking phosphorus in the soil, or the ground is too cold and wet for the roots to absorb nutrients properly. Adding well-rotted manure or a phosphorus-rich fertilizer helps them grow green and tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to yield fruit when I plant them in sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains require large amounts of water and organic matter to grow fast. Sandy soil drains water and nutrients away too quickly, so applying mulch around the base and mixing manure into the soil helps hold moisture and feed the crop.
ga: Nu kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo he miihia plantains koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishigbɛ lɛ he ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that can capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a free, natural fertilizer that helps the neighboring maize crop grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the parasitic Striga weed only seem to appear around my sorghum and maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi ni ji parasaiti lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Mi sorghum kɛ ŋmãa pɛ ni miyɔɔ.

english: Striga weed seeds lying in the dirt are awakened by specific chemical signals released by the roots of crops like sorghum and maize. Once awake, the weed attaches itself to the crop's roots to steal food and water.
ga: Striga jwɛi dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ teɔ shi kɛtsɔ tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni tsei tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi jieɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ mite shi lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tsei shishifãi ahe koni amɛju niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil. Consistent watering and light shade during peak heat can keep the blossoms on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Kɛji nu lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ, abaanyɛ akwɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of green leaves but no seed pods when I plant them late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Many local cowpea varieties depend on day length and daylight hours to trigger flowering. If planted at the wrong time of year, the crop will focus all its energy on leaf growth instead of forming pods.
ga: Cowpea henɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ damɔ gbi lɛ sɛɛtsɛmɔ kɛ gbi lɛ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔii ahe hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe pod lɛ feemɔ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark conditions with little air movement. Pruning shade trees and trimming extra branches lets sunlight and breeze into the farm, which dries the pods and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli efɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ kɛ tsei niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are the roots of my yams forming rough, swollen knobs instead of smooth tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfuu moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen knobs on yam tubers are caused by microscopic worms in the soil called root-knot nematodes. Rotating your field with non-host crops and applying compost to the soil can help reduce these pests naturally.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ root-knot nematodes lɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni efuu yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni jeee gbɔi lɛ tsake tsei ni adu lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ maa ehe shi lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts on the same field with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize plants and improves soil fertility.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ fɛo.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch sunlight for making food. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground to prevent leaf decay and disease.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii. Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni baa lɛ akafite kɛ helai.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat or dry soil stress, which prevents proper pollination from taking place.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ loo nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ haaa pollination ni sa aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting and developing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on the plant's sap and stunt its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛhaa amɛdaraa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, humid weather. Excess moisture on pods allows fungal spores to take hold.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine yɛ pods lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha fungal spores lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop needs nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia mi-ŋma lɛ?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen, the lower leaves start turning yellow at the leaf tip, forming a 'V' shape down the center while the edges stay green.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔŋ yɛ baa lɛ naa. Baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ji 'V' yɛ be mli ni baa lɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ eŋɔli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves when the weather gets very dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to reduce water loss through transpiration when soil moisture is very low.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛba nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ.

english: Why do hybrid maize seeds I buy yield more than seeds I save from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni miheɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two strong parent varieties for high yield, but their saved seeds lose those parent traits in the next generation, producing weaker plants.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ dumɔwui enyɔ ni he wa lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baaje amɛfɔlɔi asui lɛ amli yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do tiny holes appear in my stored cowpea beans a few weeks after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: These holes are caused by cowpea weevils. The insects lay invisible eggs on the pods in the field, which hatch inside stored bags and eat their way out of the dried beans.
ga: Cowpea ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kplukai woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ. Amɛfɔɔ yɛ kotoku ni akɛto lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni egbi.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow strong and green. The plant moves the little nitrogen it has from older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil, enriching the field with free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa Koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha jɛmɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing tall stems with lots of leaves, but producing tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ kɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: Cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of root tubers when there is too much shade or when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer relative to phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni miida lɛ mli yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ najiaŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. aloo kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the air gets too hot during the day or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells, which prevents the flowers from successfully pollinating.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ gbi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni yeɔ omanye.

english: Why do my cabbage plants grow wide outer leaves but refuse to form tight heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai ni mli kwɔ shi efeŋ yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form solid heads if temperatures are too high, if watering is irregular, or if they are planted too close together in nutrient-poor soil.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni wa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ ejaaa loo adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the branch during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tsei aniji ahe lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in high humidity and deep shade. Excessive water on the pods allows the mold spores to grow and ruin the crop.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids sucking the plant sap, or by viruses transmitted by whiteflies.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees split into strips when high winds blow through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split along their natural leaf veins during strong winds to reduce wind resistance, preventing the whole plant from getting snapped or uprooted.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ahe yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ aba shi. Tsi tso lɛ naa koni akakumɔ loo akajie kɛjɛ shishi.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds from my yam farm while the yam shoots are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young yam shoots grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, soil nutrients, and moisture, leading to poor tuber development later.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ abɔ akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ mli Enɛ haa sɛɛ mli lɛ, tuber lɛ daaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly before putting it into storage sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kwraa dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Moist maize grain creates a perfect environment for dangerous mold and weevils to grow, which quickly rots the stored grain and makes it unsafe to eat or sell.
ga: Abele mli ŋmeii ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui ni ato lɛ agbo oya. ni ehaa ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees have swollen shoot disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-koko tso lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: You will notice swollen stems or branches, red or yellow patterns along the leaf veins, and small, abnormally shaped cocoa pods. If you see these signs together, the tree is infected with the swollen shoot virus.
ga: Obaana tsei akutsei loo tsei niji ni efuu. Ayɛ mfoniri tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ahe. kɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni amɛhe bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli. Kɛji ona okadii nɛɛ ekome lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ emɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the tree is under stress from sap-sucking pests, fungal infections, or viral diseases like swollen shoot, which block the plant from taking up food and water properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Fungal helai loo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ haaa tso lɛ aye niyenii kɛ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is cutting down my cocoa trees the only cure for swollen shoot disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni afoɔ lɛ pɛ ji tsabaa kɛha ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ?

english: Swollen shoot is caused by a virus living inside the tree's sap system. Because there are no chemical sprays that can kill a virus inside a living plant, cutting down infected trees is the only way to stop the sickness from spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Virus ni hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni efuu baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni baanyɛ agbe helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ bɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Can plant diseases spread across my farm the same way sickness spreads among people?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ gbɛ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa gbɔmɛi ateŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, plant viruses spread quickly from tree to tree through insects like mealybugs, contaminated tools, or close root contact, very much like how viruses spread between humans in close contact.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs, nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ. loo shishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa Taakɛ bɔ ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa adesai ateŋ kɛ́ amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ.

english: If I cut down my sick cocoa trees, how soon can I plant new ones on the same farm?
ga: Kɛji mifo cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu tsei heei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli oya?

english: You should remove all infected stumps and roots, wait a few months to ensure the insects carrying the virus are completely gone, and then replant using disease-resistant cocoa varieties.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Mɛɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ kooloi ni hiɛ hela lɛ etee. Kɛkɛ lɛ, akɛ kookoo henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ kɛduɔ amɛ.

english: Will the soil remain infected after my cocoa trees die from swollen shoot disease?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baakã he ahi hela mli beni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ gboi kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, the swollen shoot virus only lives inside the living plant tissues, not in the soil itself. Once all parts of the infected tree are completely removed, the soil is safe for fresh planting.
ga: Dabi, bud swollen virus lɛ hiɔ tso mli fãji ni hiɛ ka lɛ pɛ amli, shi jeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ajie tso lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe kɛha dumɔ hee.

english: Will my new cocoa seedlings automatically catch swollen shoot disease if I plant them where old trees were cut down?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei heei baaná bud swelling hela amɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ni afo tsei momoi lɛ?

english: New seedlings will only catch the disease if infected tree stumps or virus-carrying insects remain nearby. Clearing the area fully and planting hybrid, disease-tolerant seedlings protects the new farm.
ga: Dumɔwui heei baanyɛ aná hela kɛji akɛ tso ko ni hela emɔ loo kooloo ko ni hiɛ hela lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛ pɛ. He lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ kwraa ni aduɔ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔ hee lɛ he.

english: Why does swollen shoot disease keep coming back even after I treat my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso hela ni efuu lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa ekoŋŋ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mihere kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yiwala moŋ.

english: The disease returns because tiny insects called mealybugs carry the virus from neighboring infected farms or wild trees back onto your healthy trees, especially if surrounding farms are not treated at the same time.
ga: Hela nɛɛ eku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ yɛ kooloi bibii ahewɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mealybugs lɛ hiɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ loo koo mli tsei amli kɛyaa otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu ŋmɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe nii yɛ be kome mli.

english: How do insects spread diseases from one cocoa tree to another?
ga: Te kooloi bibii feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛgbɛɔ helai kɛjɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ?

english: Insects like mealybugs feed on the sap of a sick tree, picking up the virus, and then move to a healthy tree to feed, passing the virus directly into the healthy tree's sap.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mealybugs yeɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ, amɛheɔ hela lɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛyaye nii. Amɛkɛ hela lɛ yaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I protect my healthy cocoa farm from catching diseases from my neighbor's farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ amli lɛ ahe?

english: You can plant a barrier row of non-cocoa plants or shade trees along your boundary to stop insects from traveling over, and regularly inspect border trees to catch any early signs of sickness.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni jeee kookoo tsei akɛ gbɛtsii nii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ohusu lɛ he koni kooloi akabɔle ohe. Ni okwɛ husu naa tsei lɛ daa kɛha hela he okadii mra.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no plantains or canopy trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui loo tsei bibii bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive tender leaves that burn easily under direct tropical sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains creates a protective living canopy that cools the air and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
