ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni nuɔ he waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the center outward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow strong stalks. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains fill flat, hard ground with standing water, the roots drown and rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away naturally.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa kɛ nu ni damɔ shi. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme afternoon heat or irregular watering because the plant gets stressed and tries to save water. Keeping the soil consistently damp with mulch helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Ejaakɛ tomato tsei lɛ miihao ni amɛmiitao ni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce the energy required to grow big underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing soil-borne diseases and improving tuber size.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ anaa ni oha tuber lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Multiple suckers compete directly with the main plantain stem for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to small bunches. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one strong replacement shoot and ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni amɛfeɔ kui bibii. Kpojiemɔ kroko ni fata he lɛ baaha tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. ni ehaa tso titri lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on young shoots and transmitting viruses. Spraying neem water or an appropriate insect control early stops these pests from stunting the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ. Neem nu loo kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akahã tsei lɛ afee shoo.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer onto bone-dry soil during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni fãji yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so that crop roots can safely absorb it. Applying chemical fertilizer directly to dry soil can scorch crop roots and waste money because the nutrients stay locked in dry ground.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efite shika ejaakɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my harvested hybrid maize yield much smaller cobs when planted the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ mi-hybrid corn lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa kɛ́ adu yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two distinct parent plants for high performance in the first generation only. The seeds saved from that harvest split their genetic traits, resulting in uneven growth and smaller yields if replanted.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ nii ahe su kome. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo fioo baa kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy green vines but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce their own nitrogen in the soil, so if you give them too much extra nitrogen fertilizer, they focus entirely on growing lush green leaves instead of flowers. They need phosphorus-rich nutrients to make flowers and full pods.
ga: Cowpea haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli lɛ, Cowpeas lɛ hu kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ baama baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ phosphorus he miihia amɛ koni amɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build green leaves. Adding compost, manure, or urea fertilizer around the base of the plant will help it regain its rich green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo urea baafata he Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ kɛba eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni eda waa.

english: How does adding dried animal manure help my farm soil stay moist during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be kukuoo mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ?

english: Manure acts like a sponge underground. It binds dry soil particles together and holds onto rainwater longer, giving your crop roots steady moisture even when the rains pause for a couple of weeks.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sponji. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Ha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi po.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and strong heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from burning and to keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I remove extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Cutting away the excess suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main tree gets enough energy to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rainy season gets too wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the ground and water sits around the roots, they drown and decompose. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hoɔ ni nu feɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Amɛbaagboi yɛ nu mli ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam leaves need as much direct sunlight as possible to produce the food that swells the underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the wet ground using stakes also prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from destroying the leaves.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ tsei anɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafite tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miishwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, inconsistent watering, or tiny insects like thrips attacking the flower stems. Keeping soil moisture steady and monitoring for tiny pests stops flowers from falling.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni ŋmɔɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hiŋmɛi ni akɛkwɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do insect pests keep coming back even after I spray my vegetable crop with chemical spray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ moŋ.

english: Using the exact same chemical repeatedly allows remaining bugs to build up resistance to it. Rotating different pest sprays and clearing weeds around your plot prevents pests from becoming immune to your treatments.
ga: Tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ Enɛ baaha kooloi ni eshwɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hela lɛ. Spray ni okɛtsakeɔ koni egbe kooloi srɔtoi Ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baatsi kooloi ni yɔɔ otsofa lɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I avoid putting chemical fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away loose fertilizer from the root zone before the plant can drink it in. Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp, but rain is light, so nutrients sink in without washing away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli dani tso lɛ nuɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi nugbɔ fioo ko nɛ. Akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ mɔ mli ni afɔɔɔ he.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's harvest give smaller crops than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred for uniform growth, pest resistance, and high yields in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits in the next generation, producing mixed plant sizes and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara daa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ baafite nakai sui lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ futuɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees turning yellow and failing to bear fruit when there is heavy galamsey near my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni galamsi ni tsii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Illegal mining dumps chemicals like mercury and heavy mud into the ground. This destroys the soil's natural nutrients and blocks the tree's roots from drinking clean water, causing the leaves to yellow and the plant to stop producing fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsofai tamɔ mercury kɛ muji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu ni mli tse. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ kpaɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the streams near my farm turning muddy, and how does using that water affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo muji lɛ? Ni te nakai nu ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Muddy water from land clearing and mining carries fine silt that coats crop roots, choking off oxygen and preventing the plants from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shika tsuru ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ yɛ sũ kpakpa ni haa tsei ashishifãi ahe, emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni ehaaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before they can grow into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ cacao ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as intense heat, lack of water, or low soil nutrients. The tree sheds flowers to save energy so it can stay alive.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔii lɛ kɛji amɛ hao, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Their leaves burn and dry out easily unless they have shade trees overhead to protect them from the midday heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya, ja tsei ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ aná hulutsoo ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shwane mli latsaa lɛ he.

english: How does adding fertilizer or manure change the way my cocoa tree grows and yields?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa kɛ amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer supplies essential food elements like nitrogen and potassium that soil loses over time. Adding it helps the tree produce stronger stems, greener leaves, and more flowers that develop into healthy pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. shikpɔŋ ni baafite yɛ be ni sa mli Kɛ akɛfata he lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ewo tsei ni wa. baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree before they are ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight in and air flow through, stopping the moisture that the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ adara lɛ ni ekpa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the stems and branches of my cocoa trees swelling up and losing their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛniji efuu ni amɛbaai lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: Swollen branches are a clear sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. It blocks the flow of food within the tree, causing branches to swell and foliage to fall off, eventually killing the plant if not managed.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cocoa bud virus lɛ yɛ. Etsiɔ niyenii ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ fuɔ ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: As a young person starting out in farming, how many years does a new cocoa seedling take before it starts producing pods?
ga: Ákɛ oblanyo loo oblayoo ni je okwaayeli shishi lɛ Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui heei jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties begin flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years if planted in rich soil with adequate shade and care, unlike older varieties that took up to 5 years.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni akɛfee tsofai lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔii ni amɛbaawo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni hulutsoo kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii 5 lɛ.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my young cocoa trees, or will they fight for food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe? Aloo amɛbaashi akaŋ yɛ niyenii he?

english: Planting food crops like plantain alongside young cocoa is actually beneficial because the plantains provide vital shade and early farm income. However, cassava should be spaced carefully so its large roots do not overcrowd the cocoa roots.
ga: Niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa tsei bibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ, ejaakɛ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ekɛ shika baa mra yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ akwɛ gbɛ ni kã ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni dara fe nine lɛ akayi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli fe nine.

english: Why do my crops grow very slowly and stay stunted even when I weed the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo waa ni amɛhiɛ kã shi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeding removes competition for space, but plants also need rich organic matter in the soil to grow tall. Stunted growth usually means the soil lacks key nutrients, requiring compost or targeted fertilizer to rebuild soil health.
ga: Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛha he ko. Shi tsei hu he miihia ni amɛná nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ sũ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃. Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii koni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I start by planting on a small plot of land first instead of clearing my entire farm right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko aje shishi klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni majie ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Starting small allows you to focus your attention, soil nutrients, and water on a manageable space. When crops are cared for properly on a small area, they produce a much higher yield than a large farm that gets neglected.
ga: Kɛ́ oje shishi bibioo lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli kɛyaa hei ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii Kɛji akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he bibioo ko Nibii ni anáa lɛ fa babaoo fe ŋmɔji wuji ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ.

english: Wait until the rain has fallen consistently for two or three days and the soil feels wet deep down. Planting into dry soil after just one short drizzle can burn the seeds or stop them from germinating.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii enyɔ loo etɛ. ni enu he akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa Edu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã loo etsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops grow stronger when I plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa waa kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, so the beans naturally feed the maize plants while growing next to them.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ yeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant is stressed from lack of water and nutrients. Cassava naturally drops its outer leaves during dry periods to save water and energy so its underground tubers can survive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli. Cassava shwieɔ esɛɛ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What causes my tomato plants to drop their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ tomato.

english: Why do the young leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are hiding on the undersides of the leaves and sucking out the juices. Spraying early prevents the plant from getting stunted.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii, kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiinu nu lɛ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mra be mli Ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to pile loose soil into mounds around my yam and cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabu muji ni etse ehe lɛ naa yɛ mihe lɛ? Atomɔ kɛ ŋmei tsei?

english: Loose, mounded soil gives underground tubers room to swell and expand easily. It also stops heavy rainwater from standing around the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baafu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaaa amɛgboi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees, but my older cocoa trees need full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ? Shi ani hulutsoo be fɛɛ he miihia mi-kokoo tso ni eda lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong sun. As the trees grow older, they need direct sunlight to produce plenty of cocoa pods, though they still need a light tree canopy for protection.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ tso lɛ miida Amɛmiitao hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee kookoo ŋmeii babaoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo kɛha hebuu moŋ.

english: Why do weeds damage my young crops much faster during the first few weeks after planting than later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi fiteɔ midumɔwui lɛ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu sɛɛ lɛ amli fe sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have small roots and few leaves, so weeds easily steal all the sunlight, water, and nutrients. Once the crops grow tall and bushy, their leaves block sunlight and keep weeds from growing.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai fioo. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ jwɛi lɛ baaju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni amɛtsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if my plantain bunch is ripe enough to harvest green before it rots on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain tso lɛ ekwɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii dani egbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the sharp, flat edges on the fingers become rounded and plump, and the dry flower ends at the tips break off easily when touched.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ niji ahe ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ ata he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to get a bigger harvest from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops end up competing against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong roots and yield more produce.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my soil give me fewer crops each year when I plant maize on the same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop every season drains the same nutrients from the soil over and over. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil and keeps it healthy for future harvests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be ni Seasons lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni eha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying during the hot sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates a protective canopy that shelters young cocoa until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ ŋtayaa tso bibioo lɛ he lɛ baa kɛyashi ŋtayaa lɛ daa waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants lack essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is either waterlogged or too dry. Applying the right fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my farm so it doesn't get washed away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekaho?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist, but not during heavy downpours. Applying fertilizer slightly under the soil surface near the root zone prevents rainwater from washing it away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo afata shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ koni nugbɔ nu akafɔ lɛ.

english: What is making tiny holes in my corn leaves and leaving dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the plant. Checking your crops early and applying recommended treatments to the center of the plants helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than my food crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the food and moisture your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop without fruiting when the weather is too hot, when soil moisture is uneven, or when there are no insects around to pollinate them. Regular watering and mulching can help protect the plants.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeee ekome Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaawo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Mature cassava tubers are sensitive to wet soil conditions. If left in saturated ground too long after maturity, soil bacteria and fungi attack the roots, causing rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ nuɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni edara sɛɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. kɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last harvest yield less food than the store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ wo niyenii fioo fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought seeds are often hybrid varieties specially bred for high yields and disease resistance. Seeds saved from these harvests lose their original strengths in subsequent generations, leading to smaller crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ srɔtoi ni afee amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi nɛɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛshishijee hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baa.

english: What is the main difference between hybrid corn seeds and the regular seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa kɛ daa ŋmãa ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred by seed scientists to produce higher crop yields and resist diseases, but their high performance only lasts for one season. Seeds saved from your previous harvest cost nothing, but their yields will drop significantly each time you replant them.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe nilelɔi ji mɛi ni fɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ titri koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ. Shi nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ hiɔ shi be kome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ okpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ aheee nɔ ko. Shi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa be fɛɛ be ni obaadu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are imported seed varieties so expensive compared to our local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ jara wa waa kɛ akɛto wɔmaŋ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Imported seeds carry extra costs for international research, shipping, and currency exchange. While they are designed for high yields under ideal conditions, local Ghanaian seeds are often cheaper and specifically bred to tolerate local weather, soil, and common local pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ heɔ nyɔmɔwoo kroko kɛha majimaji niiamlipɛimɔ, majemɔ kɛ shika tsakemɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ afee amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ shihilɛi ni hi fe fɛɛ amli moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli ghana dumɔwui lɛ jara waaa ni akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, shikpɔji kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa.

english: Can locally produced corn seeds compete with imported hybrid seeds in terms of yield?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni afeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ abɔ akaŋ yɛ yibiiwoo he?

english: Yes, high-quality local hybrid varieties developed by Ghanaian agricultural institutions can produce high yields that rival imported seeds, especially because they are already adapted to local climate conditions and rainfall patterns.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni Ghana Agricultural Institute lɛ fee lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo babaoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ. Titri lɛ, ejaakɛ ekɛ ehe ewo maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi amli momo.

english: Why do the leaves on my corn plants start turning yellow when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or heavy waterlogging around the root zone. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK early on helps the leaves stay green and produce food for the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha niyenii aha tso lɛ.

english: What causes my corn stalks to fall over easily when there is heavy wind or rain?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Corn falls over when its roots are shallow or damaged by soil pests, or when the stems are weakened by stalk borers. Planting seeds at the correct depth and mounding soil around the base of the plants helps anchor them firmly.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite lɛ. Aloo be mli ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahewɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni ooodu yɛ he ni sa ni okɛ sũ ni ato shishi lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ ahi he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my harvested corn cobs have missing grains and empty spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii kɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains are usually caused by poor pollination during the flowering stage, which often happens when the crop suffers from extreme heat or water stress right when the silks are receiving pollen from the tassels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa ji pollination ni ehiii yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni siliki lɛ nine shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I estimate how much corn I will harvest from my farm before I actually harvest it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni makpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he akɔntaa dani akpa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can estimate your total yield by counting the average number of full cobs across a few small sample areas on your farm, multiplying that by your total plant count, and using the average grain weight for your seed variety.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ ayibɔ ni oookane lɛ nɔ. fioo ko yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli Okɛ tsei ayibɔ fɛɛ afata he. ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛha odumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my corn in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without overcrowding. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli tsɔ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my corn if I want to dry and store the grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Ni kɛji akɛ miisumɔ ni magbi ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato hu?

english: Corn is ready for dry storage harvest when the husks turn brown and dry, the stalk turns yellow, and the grains become hard enough that your fingernail cannot easily dent them.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa akɛ otsitsii lɛ nyɛŋ atswa amɛ mlɛo.

english: What allows commercial farmers to get so much more corn per acre than smallholder farmers?
ga: Mɛni haa jarayeli okwaafoi lɛ naa ŋmãa babaoo yɛ acre kome mli fe okwaafoi bibii lɛ?

english: Commercial farmers usually achieve higher yields per acre because they combine high-yielding certified hybrid seeds with precise plant spacing, timely fertilizer applications, and proper pest control measures throughout the growing season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ jarayeli mli lɛ náa yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli. Ejaakɛ amɛkɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just dig up any small shoot growing at the base of a mother plant to start a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɛ tso lɛ shishi koni ekɛje he hee ko shishi

english: Shoots taken directly from the base of an old plant can carry hidden pests, root rots, or weak genetic traits. It is better to use certified clean planting materials or healthy, disease-free suckers to ensure good yields.
ga: Tso momo ko shishi tɛ̃ɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, shishifãi ni egbo, loo sui ni bɛ hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. Esa akɛ akɛ dumɔ nii ni he tse ni awo he odaseyeli loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii koni aná yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do seedlings grown from the same parent plant sometimes turn out completely different in growth and harvest quality?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso kome mli lɛ dalɛ kɛ kpamɔ su lɛ yɛ srɔto kwraa lɛ?

english: When crops reproduce, natural genetic variations occur, meaning some offspring will inherit weaker traits, different fruit characteristics, or poorer resistance to weather compared to the original plant.
ga: Be ni tsei fɔɔ bii lɛ Adebɔɔ mli wala yibii sɔrɔtoi baaba. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ seshibii komɛi baaná sui ni bɛ hewalɛ. Sui ni yɔɔ aduawai srɔtoi amli loo ebɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe hewalɛ ni ehiii kɛ akɛto blema tsei ahe

english: How can I tell if a mother plant is safe and healthy enough to take fresh planting material from?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ dumɔ nibii heei baaba?

english: Select parent plants that are vigorous, yield heavily, show no signs of leaf discoloration or strange decay, and have strong roots free of unusual spots or pest damage.
ga: Halamɔ nyɛ tso ni he wa, ni woɔ yibii ni etsɔɔɔ baa lɛ su tsakemɔ loo fitemɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ he okadi ko kwraa. ni eyɛ shishifãi ni wa ni nɔ ko bɛ he loo nɔ ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efiteɔ.

english: What is the safest way to remove a young sprout from the stem of a parent crop without destroying it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mra be mli tso lɛ shishi ni afiteee lɛ?

english: Use a clean, sharp knife to detach the sprout with some intact roots, keep soil around the root bundle, and plant it immediately into moist, shaded soil so the roots do not dry out.
ga: Kɛ kakla ni naa wa, ni he tse agbala dumɔwui ni shishifãi bɛ mli lɛ amli. Ha shikpɔŋ abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akagbi.

english: Why does the harvest from my crops sometimes have a strange or unusually strong smell compared to what I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ loo ehe wa waa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto nɔ ni miduɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Changes in plant aroma or flavor are often caused by variations in soil nutrients, extreme weather stress, or bacterial activity, which alter the natural compounds the plant produces.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa tsei ahe loo amɛ ŋɔɔmɔ mli lɛ jɛɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɔrɔtoi. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa loo helatsɛmɛi anifeemɔi ni tsakeɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsei feɔ lɛ

english: Does a foul or heavy odor coming from the root area of my crop mean the plant is sick?
ga: Ani ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ tso lɛ?

english: Yes, a foul odor around the plant stem or roots usually signals bacterial soft rot or fungal decay caused by waterlogging, which damages plant tissues and requires removing the infected plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo ko yɛ he fɛɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ashishifãi loo amɛshishifãi lɛ jieɔ helatsɛmɛi loo ŋmeii ni nu ni hoɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ahe okadii akpo. Enɛ fiteɔ tsei ahe fãji ni ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some crops produce flowers that wither away instead of forming proper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ fɔfɔii ni gboɔ yɛ yibii ni sa najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop or wither when crops experience high heat stress, nutrient shortages, improper watering, or pest attacks, leaving the plant without enough energy to support fruit development.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgboɔ kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. niyenii ni esaaa ni ayeɔ nu ni esaaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ.

english: Is it safe to pour liquid fertilizers or chemical mixtures directly onto open flowers on my crop?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔse nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ awo fɔfɔi ni agbele yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, applying heavy chemical or liquid mixtures directly onto delicate blossoms can burn the flower parts and wash away pollen, preventing the plant from setting fruit.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai loo nu wo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã fɔfɔi lɛ fãi lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why is my young crop wilting even though I pour plenty of water around its base every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ miiho lɛ? Ani nu shwieɔ shishitoo lɛ he daa gbi?

english: Pouring too much water right at the base of a stem drowns the roots by removing air from the soil, causing root rot that stops the crop from absorbing water and nutrients properly.
ga: Nu babaoo ni oooshwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant new crops too close to the base of established, older trees?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu tsei heei ni bɛŋkɛ tso momo ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shishi tsɔ?

english: Young crops planted too close to mature trees suffer from heavy shade and intense competition for soil nutrients and water, which stunts their growth and makes them weak.
ga: Tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tsei ni eda lɛ tsɔ lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa ni kɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii he lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava cuttings is the best way to protect your farm.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn purple or yellow when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ purple loo yellow be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ?

english: Yellow or purple leaves on young maize indicate that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus. Applying organic manure or the right starter fertilizer early in the season helps the plants grow green and strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or sudden flooding. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know when my underground yam tubers are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines above ground turn yellow and start dying back naturally. This shows that the plant has finished transferring its nutrients down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to yield well only in their first planting. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation will grow unevenly and produce much smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji okɛto ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo.

english: Why does elephant grass keep growing back so quickly after I clear my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shwuɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Elephant grass has deep underground stems called rhizomes that store food. Unless you dig these roots out completely or smother them with cover crops like cowpeas, the grass will regrow every time it rains.
ga: Shɔ jwɛi yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni akɛtoɔ niyenii. Jwɛi lɛ daa ehee be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ. Ja ogbala shishifãi nɛɛ kwraa loo okɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko tamɔ tsina ŋmei ha amɛhe.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my tomato plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Crowding tomato plants traps moisture between leaves and blocks sunlight, which encourages fungal diseases like blight to spread. Proper spacing allows sunlight and fresh air to flow through, keeping the plants healthy.
ga: Tomato tsei ni mli wa lɛ mɔɔ nu yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. He ni jɛkɛ ni sa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli. ha tsei awa

english: Why does my farmland get hard like rock after a heavy rain followed by hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or compost to keep it loose. Adding organic manure improves soil structure so water can soak in easily without forming a hard surface crust.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha ehi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni nu lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ oya ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa efeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are grasscutters attacking and chewing the bases of my young cassava stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔ lɛ tutua mi-cassava bibioo lɛ shishi ni ekɛyeɔ lɛ?

english: Grasscutters target young cassava stems during dry periods because the stems are soft and contain water. Clearing brush around the perimeter of your field removes their hiding spots and deters them from coming near your crops.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmei bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Akɛni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne shwie oyale lɛ naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie hei ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ lɛ, ni ebaaha amɛkabɛŋkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants curling up and turning yellow during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves curl during hot weather, it means the plant is losing water faster than its roots can drink it from dry soil. Curling is the plant's natural defense to shield its surface from sunlight and prevent further water loss.
ga: Beni ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Curling ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he, ni ekɛtsiɔ nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow better when I leave dried leaves on top of the soil around the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving dried leaves around your plants creates a natural blanket called mulch. This layer keeps the soil cool under the hot sun and stops rainwater from evaporating quickly, leaving more moisture for your cassava roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egbi yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya Ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall with thick green leaves but producing no flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse shi fɔfɔii bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Your plants are getting too much nitrogen fertilizer or fresh animal manure. High nitrogen encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing big leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Otsei lɛ miiná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo tsɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛkwɛ baai wuji kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Is it better for my pepper crop if I pour a small amount of water every day or soak the ground deeply once a week?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-pepper tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu fioo ko shwie shi daa gbi loo mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo mli shɔŋŋ shikome yɛ otsi mli?

english: Soaking the ground deeply once a week is better because it encourages the roots to grow deep into the soil to find moisture. Deep roots make your pepper plants stronger and better able to survive dry periods.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo mli shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehaa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa o-pepper tso lɛ mli waa ni enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay very small when I plant the seed yams close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need space, light, and nutrients to expand underground. When you plant them too close, the roots fight each other for the limited water and food in the soil, leaving little energy to build big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia he ko, la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji odu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ahi shi koni akɛfee yitso agbo.

english: Why do my garden eggs develop white powdery spots on their leaves when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The powdery white spots are a leaf disease caused by excessive dampness and high humidity. When rainwater stays on leaves for too long without sunlight and air circulation to dry them, fungi easily grow and spread.
ga: Powdery white spot ji baa hela ko ni hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛbaa. Kɛ nugbɔ nu hi baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ bɛ mli ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ lɛ, Fungus lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my groundnuts grow well in a field where my maize failed to grow properly last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can feed itself by pulling nitrogen gas from the air and trapping it in the soil. Maize cannot do this and starves when planted in soil that has run out of nutrients.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he ni enyɛɔ eyeɔ ehe niyenii kɛtsɔ nitrogen gas ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Abɛi nyɛŋ afee enɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cowpea plants have small holes chewed into them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Okɛwo mli?

english: Insects like caterpillars or beetles are eating your leaves. Plants use leaves like solar panels to make food from sunlight, so when insects destroy the leaves, the plant cannot produce enough energy to grow big beans.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii miiye obaai lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛbaai tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei feɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ kooloi bibii kpata baai lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my crop seeds after the first rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are natural wild plants adapted to your local climate, so their seeds react much faster to rainwater than cultivated crop seeds. If you do not clear them early, they will drink all the soil water before your crops get a chance.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ hereɔ nugbɔ nɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji ojieee amɛ oya lɛ, Amɛbaanu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ fɛɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ.

english: How do I know when my plantain bunch is fully mature and ready to be cut down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantain tso lɛ eda kwraa ni esa akɛ afo lɛ?

english: Plantain is ready to harvest when the individual fingers lose their sharp, angled edges and become plump and rounded. The dark dried flower tips at the bottom of the fruit will also break off easily when touched.
ga: Plantains efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ nineshi nine fɛɛ nine ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo ni ebatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ shishi lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ ata he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to stay green and build healthy stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ ekwɛ eŋɔli lɛ nɔ ni etswa tsei ni wa.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to build big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they are stressed by intense heat, irregular watering, or lack of insect pollination, saving their energy for survival instead of fruiting.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni bɛ Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛhiɔ shi yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die if I clear away all the large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct harsh sunlight. Larger trees provide essential shade and retain air moisture, protecting young cocoa from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and thin even though the plant leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: If stem cuttings are planted too close together, the roots compete underground for space and food, leading to many small roots instead of large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni afo lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtaoɔ he ko kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi bibii babaoo yɛ yitsei wuji najiaŋ

english: Extra shoots steal water and plant food from the main mother plant. Removing excess suckers allows the main tree to focus all its energy on growing a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there is plenty of soil for every plant?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso fɛɛ tso?

english: Weeds act like food thieves in your farm. They aggressively drink up water, suck out fertilizer nutrients, and block sunlight from reaching your crops.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu kɛ hiɛdɔɔ. Gbalamɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ onibii ahe.

english: Heavy rainfall creates dampness that allows the Black Pod fungal disease to grow and spread quickly across wet cocoa pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni haa black pod fungal hela lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni efɔ lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides in the central funnel of maize plants where leaves are tender, eating the foliage before the crop can produce ears.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ afee toi.

english: Why does spreading dry leaves on the ground around my pepper plants help during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ pepper tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating quickly under hot sun and keeps plant roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baatsi nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why do some of my harvested cassava roots grow very big while others from the same farm remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ daa lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shishifãi krokomɛi ni jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ faaa lolo.

english: Cassava roots grow to different sizes depending on soil nutrients, moisture, and how much space each plant has underground. Sorting your harvest by size helps you sell the larger roots for higher prices to buyers who specifically ask for big ones.
ga: Cassava shishifãi baanyɛ adara kɛyashɛ dalɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulutsoo kɛ he ni tso fɛɛ tso yɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa. Kɛ́ ohala onibii lɛ amli yɛ amɛdalɛ naa lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ shishifãi wuji yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ohaa mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni miitao shishifãi wuji tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Why do market women pay me more money when I sort my peppers by size before selling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jara nɔ yei woɔ mi nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛ́ mihala ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ amɛdalɛ naa dani mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Sorting your crops into uniform sizes makes them more attractive and convenient for different buyers. Large peppers are usually bought by restaurants, while smaller ones go to household buyers, so grading allows you to charge premium rates for the big ones.
ga: Kɛ́ ato ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛdalɛ afee ekome lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ fɛo ni ehaa mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ. Bei pii lɛ, niyelihei heɔ chili ŋmɔtɔi wuji. yɛ be mli ni aheɔ chili bibii yɛ shia. No hewɔ lɛ, shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ obiɔ shika krɛdɛɛ ko kɛha ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: What causes my plantain bunches to remain light and small instead of developing heavy, big fingers?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná niji wuji ni tsii?

english: Plantain bunches stay small when the plant lacks water, soil nutrients like potassium, or when too many sucker shoots grow around the main stem and steal its food. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to produce big plantains.
ga: Plantains bafeɔ bibii kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, loo be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ he. main trunk and steal food Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is the best way for me to pack fresh tomatoes into baskets so they do not rot on the way to the market?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mawo mi-basket ni tomato hee yɔɔ mli lɛ mli? Koni tomatoi lɛ akafite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly when bruised. To protect them, line woven baskets with soft leaves, place firmer and larger tomatoes at the bottom, and avoid overfilling so the top basket does not crush the fruit underneath.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ. koni obu amɛhe Okɛ tsɛnsi ni akpɛ́ ni baai bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ atsu nii. Okɛ tomato ni mli wa, ni da fe tsutsu lɛ awo shishigbɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ ahe koni ŋwɛi tsɛnsi lɛ akakumɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains spoil quickly when I store them in woven bags at home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛwo mama kotokui amli yɛ shia lɛ?

english: Maize spoils in storage if it is packed while still containing moisture or if insects are inside. Drying the maize thoroughly in the sun until the kernels are hard before storing them in clean, airtight bags keeps moisture and pests away.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo mli be mli ni edɔ lolo loo kooloi yɔɔ mli. Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee shiŋŋ dani okɛwo kotokui ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii ahe.

english: Why do my pineapples get soft and bruised on one side when I stack them up for buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ efã kome beni mikɛtoɔ he mihaa mɔ ni heɔ lɛ lɛ?

english: Pineapples have heavy, sweet flesh that crushes easily under weight. Transporting and storing them upright in padded wooden crates or shallow baskets prevents pressure damage and keeps the fruit fresh for buyers.
ga: Pineapple yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii ni ŋɔɔ ni fãa oya yɛ etsiimɔ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tso adekai ni akɛ tsɔne ewo mli loo tsɛnsii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ mli lɛ tee ni akɛto shi shiŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɔnyɛɛ akafite nii, ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ afee ehee aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my garden eggs so they stay fresh longer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Harvest garden eggs when they are full-sized, firm, and shiny before their skin turns yellow. Picking them early in the cool morning hours keeps them from losing moisture and shriveling up quickly.
ga: Bua ŋmeii anaa yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli kɛji amɛshɛ amɛdalɛ he. Ehe wa ni ekpɛɔ dani ehewolo lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Kɛ́ ajie amɛ mra yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi oya lɛ naa.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes rot a few days after I dig them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ fite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes get tiny cuts during digging that let decay organisms enter. Leaving the harvested tubers in a warm, dry, shaded area for a few days allows the skin to heal and harden, protecting them from rot.
ga: Afolɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli bibii bibii. yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ koni bɔɔ nii ni miifite lɛ abote mli Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ, ni egbi, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha hewolo lɛ atsa ni ewa. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Why do the outer leaves of my cabbage plants turn yellow and dry up before the head grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabii tsei lɛ asɛɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛyitsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Cabbage leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or suffers from heat and insufficient water. Providing adequate water and compost helps the plant hold its leaves and grow a firm, large head.
ga: Kaabaji baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ miipiŋ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ etso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper fruits turn bitter and small during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ mli edɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants produce small, bitter fruits when exposed to strong heat and dry soil stress. The plant protects itself by withholding water from the fruit, so mulching around the roots and regular watering helps keep the peppers mild and full.
ga: Pepper tsei woɔ yibii bibii. Ehe ŋɔɔ waa kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ mli. Tsei buɔ amɛhe he kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛtsiɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛyibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha shishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ nu wo nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi bibii ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and heat. They need temporary shade trees like plantain or banana plants grown nearby to shield them and keep the soil cool until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii loo banana tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Enɛ ji koni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: What will happen to my yam crop if I do not provide sticks or poles for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ niji loo tsei haaa wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to spread their leaves and catch sunlight. Without stakes, the leaves remain shaded on the ground, which leads to lower plant energy, weak growth, and much smaller yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baakã he afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bibioo kwraa lɛ

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal nutrients, food, and water from the main plantain tree. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two allows the main tree to produce a much bigger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ, niyenii, kɛ nu kɛjɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantain ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves start turning yellow from the bottom leaves going upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Maize needs sufficient nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure early in its growth to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Abele biɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Koni ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same farm patch every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen to the soil and improves future harvests.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the soil when heavy rains last for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when left in waterlogged soil because water blocks air from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily and protects the tubers from rotting.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni ehaa yitso lɛ fiteɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or when tiny pests damage the blossoms. Giving plants consistent water at the root level and protecting them from pests helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ he ni obuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking plant sap and spreading plant viruses. Keeping the farm free of weeds and controlling sap-sucking insects helps prevent leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper mli. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akudɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to develop dark black spots and turn hard during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ewaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in wet, humid conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight flow through the farm, reducing humidity and protecting cocoa pods from the fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa hulutsoo baa shi ni ebuɔ kookoo ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing large green leaves but failing to form a tight, solid center head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitsei ni mli wa ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer, suffer from high heat, or experience dry spells. Balanced feeding and steady watering encourage the center leaves to wrap tightly together into a head.
ga: Kaabage lɛ ebɔŋ ehe kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Piŋmɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli loo hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli kpeɔ Niyenii ni ja kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ feɔ ekome jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ bulb.

english: Why am I being advised to cut down my cocoa trees when they are still producing a few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ awo mi ŋaa akɛ mafo kookoo tso lɛ be mli ni mifooo lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ yibii lolo lɛ yɔɔ?

english: Even if an infected cocoa tree still produces a few pods, viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot live inside the plant and spread to neighboring healthy trees through insects. Cutting down the infected tree stops the disease from spreading and destroying your entire farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cacao tso ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii komɛi lolo po lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ cacao ni efuu lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii amli amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni efiteɔ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Can I get into trouble with government officers if I refuse to cut down sick cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nɔyeli mli onukpai lɛ abote naagba mli kɛji mikpoo akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, because contagious crop diseases can easily spread across neighboring farms, agricultural authorities enforce rules to cut down infected cocoa trees to protect the overall cocoa industry and local farming communities.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei ahe helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya. No hewɔ lɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhei lɛ kɛ mlai ni kɔɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ afolɔ he lɛ tsuɔ nii. Koni abu kookoo nitsumɔhe lɛ fɛɛ kɛ akutsei ni tsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ ahe

english: How long should I wait to plant new crops after clearing out diseased cocoa trees?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu tsei heei beni mijie kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After removing diseased cocoa trees and their roots, you should let the ground rest for a few months to ensure pests like mealybugs die off. You should then plant shade crops like plantains before planting new, disease-resistant cocoa seedlings.
ga: Kɛji ojie kookoo tsei kɛ shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Esa akɛ Oha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe nyɔji fioo komɛi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mealybugs lɛ gboi. No sɛɛ lɛ esa akɛ odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains dani odu kookoo dumɔwui heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: Why are the stems of my young cocoa trees swelling up and the leaves turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efuu ni amɛbaai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems and yellowing leaf veins are signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. The virus blocks water and nutrients from moving through the tree, causing swollen growths and eventually killing the plant.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni efuu kɛ baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji kookoo tso mli hela ni efuu lɛ he okadii. Virus lɛ tsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fuuɔ ni naagbee lɛ efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, overly shady, and wet conditions. Pruning branches to allow sunlight and fresh air into the farm helps prevent the fungus from destroying the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ He ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ.

english: As cocoa trees pass 20 to 25 years of age, their root systems lose efficiency in taking up nutrients from the soil, making them weaker and naturally reducing the number of pods they can produce.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli baa lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving large trees or planting fast-growing crops provides the shade and soil moisture young plants need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni aaashi loo tsei ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ baaha aná hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: What are the tiny white insects under my cocoa leaves, and do they hurt my crops?
ga: tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo Mɛni yɔɔ mi koko baa lɛ shishi? Ni ani amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Those insects are mealybugs. They suck nutrients from the tree leaves and branches, and they carry deadly viruses like Swollen Shoot from sick trees to healthy ones.
ga: Nakai kooloi lɛ ji mealybugs. Amɛmuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛniji amli. Ni amɛhiɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu, kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: When cocoa trees are planted too closely, their branches block out sunlight and trap moisture, creating an ideal environment for fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread rapidly between trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eniji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ black pod hela lɛ, baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya yɛ tsei ateŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant plantains on the same land where I am starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni maje kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that protect young cocoa trees from sun scorch, while providing food and extra income for your household while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
