ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa oshiabii lɛ náa niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them creates living shade, which protects the young leaves and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aaadu yɛ masɛi lɛ Baaha wala aná hulutsoo Enɛ buɔ baai bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the stalk usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build strong green leaves and healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize takes nutrients out of the soil, but beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know that my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni akuuu mli?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare woody stem, and small cracks appear in the soil near the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ kã he eji tso ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Yam plants need their leaves high up in the sunlight to make energy, which then travels down to feed and grow the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato tsei lɛ baai lɛ ahi ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛkɛ ni efã gbɛ kɛba shi koni eyakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni edu.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water, causing stress that prevents fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni tsiɔ aduawai anaa lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the juice from under the leaves or spreading a virus to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ shishi loo amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many shoots causes them to compete for water and soil nutrients, while cutting them back to just 2 or 3 leaves the main plant strong enough to produce big bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔ tso titri lɛ baai 2 loo 3 pɛ ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: How does laying dry grass on the soil around my crops help them in hot weather?
ga: Akɛ jwɛi fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating into the air, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Is it best to apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: No, heavy rain will wash away fertilizer before roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp after a light rain.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: Why does my farm yield less food after planting crops on the same piece of land for four or five years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nine shɛɛɛ niyenii nɔ fioo beni midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii ejwɛ loo enumɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take nutrients out of the earth with them. If you do not put those nutrients back into the land using compost, manure, or fertilizers, the soil becomes tired and worn out over time.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaaŋɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛya. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni ebaafite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Fertilizer acts like food for your plants. Just as people need healthy food to grow strong and work, crops need essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus to grow deep roots, green leaves, and heavy grains or fruits.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa otsei lɛ. Taakɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa he hiaa gbɔmɛi koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsu nii lɛ. Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii. Koni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, baai eŋɔli, kɛ dumɔwui loo aduawai ni tsii.

english: How can I find out what food or nutrients my soil is missing before I spend money on fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niyenii ni haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii kpakpai dani mafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: You can ask an extension officer to help you take a sample of your soil for testing. A soil test shows exactly what nutrients your land has and what it needs, so you do not waste money buying the wrong fertilizer.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi extension nitsulɔ ko ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko ni ekɛka lɛ akwɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa tsɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni ofite shika kɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa.

english: Why do my crops still perform poorly after several years even though I apply chemical fertilizer every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii daa be moŋ.

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant directly, but it does not feed the living soil microbes and earthworms that keep the ground soft and healthy. Over many years, soil without organic matter loses its ability to hold water and nutrients.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Shi ehãaa sũ mli nibii bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ hewalɛ lɛ niyenii. Afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli dɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I bother putting animal manure or compost on my farm if I am already buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu kooloi ashishifã loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaafata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ he? Be ni miheɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ momo?

english: Chemical fertilizer gives plants a fast boost, but compost and manure feed the soil's natural biology and build up organic matter. This helps the ground stay moist like a sponge during dry periods and keeps the soil fertile for years to come.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa sũ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ niyenii ni amɛbuaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tamɔ sponji yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Is there life inside the soil that helps my crops grow, and how do I keep it alive?
ga: Ani wala yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ehi shi?

english: Yes, healthy soil is filled with tiny living organisms like earthworms, fungi, and helpful bacteria. They break down dead plants into natural plant food. You keep them alive by adding compost, avoiding burning bush on your land, and keeping the soil covered.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ eyi kɛ nibii bibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Amɛshwieɔ tsei ni egboi lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii. Obaanyɛ oha amɛhi wala mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ brɔshi ni ashãa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my crops wither quickly during short dry spells even when I have applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ fɔmɔ efɔ shi moŋ

english: Fertilizer needs water to be absorbed by plants. If your soil lacks organic matter, it cannot trap and hold rainwater, causing the fertilizer to sit uselessly while the crops dry up.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni tsei lɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ato nugbɔ nu. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he ehiaaa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to change the crop we plant on a field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔtsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni wɔduɔ yɛ wɔŋmɔji amli lɛ daa afi lɛ?

english: Different crops take different nutrients from the ground and attract different pests. Changing crops, such as planting beans or groundnuts after maize, gives the soil a break and naturally restores nitrogen back into the earth.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi kɛ niyenii srɔtoi ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛgbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow at the tips even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a cry for help showing that the plant is hungry, specifically for nitrogen. Even with enough rain, a plant will turn yellow if the soil does not have enough nutrients to support its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji bolɔmɔ ni akɛbiɔ yelikɛbuamɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ Tsei hu baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛdalɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop and land if I apply more fertilizer than the recommended amount?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ tsu nii?

english: Using too much fertilizer can burn the plant roots and damage the natural balance of the soil. It also wastes your money, as heavy rains will simply wash the extra fertilizer off your farm into nearby streams.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efite bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Eji oshika fitemɔ hu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ashi oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender stems and small root systems that cannot survive strong, direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that traps moisture and shields young plants until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tɛ̃ɛ Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Black pods are usually caused by a fungal disease that spreads fast during the rainy season. Excessive shade, high humidity, and poor air movement allow fungus to grow, so pruning extra leaves and weeding around the base helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji black pods lɛ baa. Shade babaoo, hulutsoo babaoo, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, abaafolɔ baai krokomɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ. Konii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops drop their blossoms before any fruit or pod actually forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai loo ŋmeii baa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers when they are under severe stress, usually from sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like potassium and boron that help plants hold onto their fruit buds.
ga: Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii kɛji amɛyɛ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni bɛ, tamɔ potassium kɛ boron, ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Tired soil often shows in pale or yellow leaves, slow plant growth, and smaller crops year after year. Applying well-rotted animal manure or the right mineral fertilizer restores lost nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus so crops grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ daa blɛoo. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi afi fɛɛ afi. Nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni elaaje tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too closely makes crops fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants with smaller yields and makes it easier for pests and plant diseases to spread across your farm.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai baagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops slow down their growth when the Harmattan wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛji Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind draws water rapidly out of soil and leaf surfaces. Crops slow their growth and shed older leaves as a defensive mechanism to conserve water and prevent themselves from drying out completely.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ anɔ oya. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi ni amɛshwieɔ baai momoi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he ni akɛtsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Pruning removes non-producing shoots and dead wood so the tree does not waste energy feeding leaves that produce no fruit. It allows sunlight into the lower trunk and improves airflow to reduce disease.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni wooo yibii kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ baai ni wooo yibii lɛ niyenii. Ehaa hulu la boteɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ shishigbɛ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni helai aba shi.

english: Is it safe to grow food crops like cassava or maize on the same farm as my tree crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping young trees with food crops like cassava or plantain gives you quick food and income while the trees mature. However, keep short-term crops far enough from the tree stems so they don't block sunlight or choke the main crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii ni niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baanyɛ aha oná niyenii kɛ shika oya be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ tsiŋ hulu la lɛ naa loo efiteee tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In strong afternoon heat, plants evaporate water through leaves faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. Covering the soil around plants with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and moist throughout the day.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli nu lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad practice to harvest unripe pods along with mature ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ abaakpa ŋmeii ni edako lɛ kɛfata ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Unripe pods contain flat beans with very low sugar content. When mixed with good beans during fermentation, they reduce the overall quality and flavor, leading to lower prices or rejection by buyers.
ga: Raw pods lɛ ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni sugar faaa kwraa yɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii kpakpai futu mli yɛ ŋmeii be mli lɛ Ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ aba shi. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, jara lɛ baa shi loo mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo.

english: Why does the price of soup vegetables and local spices go up so high in Ghana between December and March?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli kɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli lɛ jara yaa hiɛ waa yɛ Ghana yɛ December kɛ March teŋ lɛ?

english: December to March falls in the dry Harmattan season when rainfall drops significantly. Since fewer farmers can grow crops without rain, harvest amounts decrease across the country while holiday cooking demand stays high, driving up market prices.
ga: December kɛyashi March ji Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, okwaafoi fioo ko pɛ baanyɛ adu nibii ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ ba shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ gbijurɔyeli he lɛ fa babaoo lolo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jarayeli jara ni yaa hiɛ.

english: If I harvest my spice crops at the same time as every other farmer, how can I save them to sell later when market demand is higher?
ga: Kɛji mikpaa tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli kɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛto koni mahɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli be mli ni jara nɔ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: You can dry and process crops like chili peppers, ginger, and garlic into powders or dried spices. When completely dried and stored in airtight bags in a cool place, they can last for months until market supply drops and prices rise.
ga: Obaanyɛ ogbi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ chili, ginger, kɛ galiki afee powda loo tsofai ni egbi. Kɛji egbi kwraa lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi jara nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ baa shi ni amɛjara hu baaya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do consumers buy more fresh ingredients for soups at certain specific times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nihɔɔlɔi heɔ nibii heei ni akɛwoɔ shwiili mli yɛ afi lɛ mli bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli lɛ?

english: During festive periods like Christmas and the New Year, families cook larger meals and hold celebrations that require heavy use of traditional soups and stews, leading to a sudden surge in household market purchases.
ga: Yɛ gbijurɔyelii tamɔ Blonya kɛ Afi Hee lɛ amli lɛ Wekui baahoo niyenii wuji ni amɛbaafee gbijurɔyelii ni damɔ kusum mli shwiili kɛ shwiili nɔ waa lɛ. Enɛ eha shĩa nibii ni aheɔ lɛ etee hiɛ trukaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing fruits and drop their flowers during the hot months from December to March?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo ni efɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ December kɛyashi March nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry dry-season winds cause heat stress in pepper plants, making them drop flowers to save water. Watering early in the morning and using light shade netting helps the plants keep their flowers and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni baa yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Ha amɛshwie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi kɛ shade netting ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: How can I keep my vegetable crops alive and healthy when there is no rain during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-vegetables lɛ ahi shi ni amɛná hewalɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your plant stems with dry grass or leaves (mulching) to trap soil moisture, and use simple drip irrigation or hand-watering directly at the roots rather than spraying water into the air.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ koni ekɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ. ni okɛ simple drip irrigation Loo nu ni akɛ nine tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni oookɛ nu afɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: How do I know when my local spice crops like peppers and ginger are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mimaŋ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tsei tamɔ pepper kɛ ginger lɛ yɛ? Ani ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Pepper pods become fully ready when they turn deep red or their full mature color and feel firm to touch, while ginger is ready when the green leaves above ground turn yellow and start drying out.
ga: Pepper pods lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ etsɔ tsuru ni mli edɔ loo ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ kɛji eta he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ efee klalo beni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ.

english: What is the best way to dry my harvested spices under the sun without them getting moldy or dirty?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ tsofai ni akpa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛhe ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo amɛhe ewoɔ muji?

english: Spread your harvested crop in a thin, single layer on raised wooden racks or clean tarpaulins off the bare ground. Turn them daily so moisture escapes evenly, preventing mold growth and contamination.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. Tier kome yɛ tso shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ. loo tarp ni he tse ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ daa gbi koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ajɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ dalɛ kɛ mujiwoo naa.

english: Why do some pepper plants keep bearing fruit after the first harvest while others die off completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ chili tsei komɛi woɔ yibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi egboi kwraa lɛ?

english: Perennial pepper varieties naturally live longer and continue flowering if they get regular nutrients and water, whereas annual crop varieties finish their natural life cycle once their first major crop matures.
ga: Pepper henɔi ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛji amɛná niyenii kɛ nu daa. yɛ be mli ni tsei sɔrɔtoi ni yeɔ daa afi lɛ gbeɔ amɛshihilɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni klɛŋklɛŋ tso titri lɛ daa lɛ.

english: What local crops can I grow easily in Ghana that are always needed for daily household soup making?
ga: Mɛɛ maŋ tsei manyɛ makwɛ yɛ Ghana ni he hiaa yɛ mi daa gbi shia shwiili mli?

english: Crops like hot peppers, tomatoes, garden eggs, onions, and ginger grow very well in local soils and enjoy constant daily demand because they form the base of almost all traditional Ghanaian soups.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ, tomato, abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ daa gbi Enɛ ji akɛ, no ji nɔ ni miihe ashɛ Ghanabii akusum nifeemɔi fɛɛ ashishitoo nɔ.

english: What should I add to my soil before planting so my spice crops yield heavily before the high-demand market season starts?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani madu koni mi-spice plant lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo dani be ni ataoɔ nibii babaoo lɛ aje shishi?

english: Mixing well-rotted cow or poultry manure into the soil two weeks before planting enriches it with organic nutrients, helping plants build strong roots and produce more abundant fruit in time for the peak season.
ga: Tsina loo kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli otsii enyɔ dani aduɔ. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli kɛha be ni tsei lɛ fa babaoo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that scorch easily under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain or banana trees alongside your cocoa provides living shelter, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young trees from heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo banana tsei yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa mɔ náa he ko ni ehiɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: What is eating small holes into the leaves of my young maize plants, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Small holes inside the leaf funnels of maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Checking your field early and spraying recommended neem extract or botanical pesticides directly into the leaf center stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsĩ amɛnaa dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: How far apart should I plant cassava cuttings so that the roots grow big tubers?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu amɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni shishifãi wuji aba?

english: Cassava cuttings should ideally be planted about 1 meter apart from each other. Giving plants enough space ensures that their underground roots have sufficient soil and nutrients to swell into large tubers without crowding.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ náa shikpɔŋ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛshwere ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crop turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil food needed for healthy leafy growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the plant roots restores green leaf strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ waa Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛbaafata he lɛ he Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaha baai eŋɔli lɛ mli awa.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a condition called blossom end rot, which happens when plants don't get steady water to absorb calcium from the soil. Watering your tomatoes regularly and evenly prevents this rot.
ga: Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato shishi diŋ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkɛjie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa kɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds immediately after the very first short rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kuku ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that bakes the ground and kills newly germinated seeds. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to grow strong roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ ni shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbeɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ oomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and yield very little harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and steal essential sunlight, soil water, and fertilizer away from your plants. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting removes this competition so your crops get full nutrition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: How do I select healthy plantain suckers to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni mikɛje dumɔhe hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword suckers' that have narrow, sword-like leaves and strong, broad bases from healthy mother plants. Avoid suckers with damaged roots or dark spots on the cut stem to keep your new field free from pests and diseases.
ga: Halamɔ ‘klante tsei’ ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ klante kɛ shishitoo ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛjɛ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni shishifãi efite loo hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ tsei ni afo lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe. Koni he hee ni oyɔɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai bɛ mli

english: How can I prevent insects from destroying my stored maize grains inside bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp conditions. Drying your maize properly until the grains are hard and dry, cleaning out broken kernels, and storing them in airtight hermetic bags prevents insect infestation without relying entirely on chemical sprays.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi. Tsumɔ dumɔwui ni ekumɔ lɛ ahe Ni okɛwo vacuum bag mli koni kooloi akabote mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts between rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpeas loo peanuts yɛ ŋmãa ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil plant food through their roots. Intercropping them with maize enriches the soil naturally and improves overall crop harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the bud nodes pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems will struggle to sprout properly, leading to weak plants and very low tuber yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ohiɛ shi lɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ ekwɛ̃mɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo baa shi waa.

english: How should I position my yam setts in the soil mound when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ awo muji lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Yam setts should be placed with the cut side facing downward or sideways and the outer skin facing upward. This protects the soft inner pulp from rotting in damp soil while allowing the new shoot to grow easily toward the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ sweet potato kui lɛ awo fã ni afo lɛ shi loo kɛya sɛɛ. ni oha kponɔgbɛ lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi Enɛ buɔ mligbɛ fã ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii heei ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa ŋwɛi oya.

english: Which direction should pineapple suckers face when I plant them in my field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ pineapple sucker lɛ akwɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ mi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The base of the pineapple sucker goes firmly into the soil with the leafy top pointing straight up. Keeping them upright stops soil from falling into the center growing heart, which would otherwise rot or stunt the plant.
ga: Akɛ pineapple sucker lɛ shishitoo lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ. Ni baa lɛ yiteŋ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ oha ehi shi jaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi sũ naa koni ekagbee tsui ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔ loo egbɔjɔ.

english: How do I correctly position a plantain sucker when placing it in a planting pit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-plantain sucker lɛ ato he jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛwo dumɔ bu lɛ mli?

english: After trimming damaged roots, place the bulb base flat at the bottom of the pit with the main growing shoot pointing straight upward. Covering it in this position gives the young stem the support it needs to grow strong and resist wind.
ga: Beni afo shishifãi ni efite lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Okɛ bulb lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ awo bu lɛ shishigbɛ ni ŋmei titri lɛ ada kɛya ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ha yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛhe nɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ aná yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: How should I pack my harvested tomatoes into wooden crates so they do not spoil on the way to market?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ awo tso adekai amli koni amɛkafite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Place tomatoes gently into crates with the flat stem side facing down, stacking them lightly without pressing down. Avoid overfilling or rough handling, as squeezed fruit easily bruises, soft-rots, and ruins the whole crate during transport.
ga: Okɛ tomato lɛ awo mli fioo. kɛbote adeka lɛ mli ni tso lɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kwɛɔ shi. Okɛ amɛ ato he blɛoo. ni okɛmiimɔɔɔ shi Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine loo nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai ni ashɛre lɛ shwieɔ, egboɔ, ni efiteɔ adeka muu lɛ fɛɛ oya kɛ́ akɛmiiya.

english: What is the proper way to handle and arrange fresh garden eggs when putting them into harvest baskets?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii heei ahe nii ni atoɔ he gbɛjianɔ beni akɛwoɔ ŋmaakpamɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Place garden eggs gently into baskets without dropping them or shaking the container repeatedly. Constant turning and rough contact damages their delicate skin, causing dark spots and rapid rotting.
ga: Okɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ awo tsɛnsi lɛ mli blɛoo. ni ekɛ tsɛnsi lɛ shwieee shi loo ekpokpoee shii abɔ Kɛ́ otsake be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ohe wo mli waa lɛ, ebaafite hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Why shouldn't I move or turn my stored yams repeatedly once I stack them in the yam barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mitsiɔ loo mitsakeɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ shii abɔ lɛ? Beni atoɔ sweet potato ŋmɔ mli?

english: Repeatedly moving or turning stacked yams scrapes off their protective skin and breaks dormant growing tips. Leaving them still in a cool, well-ventilated barn helps them stay fresh and prevents post-harvest rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni oootsi loo otsake lɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha hewolo ni buɔ ehe lɛ agbo. ni ebaaha tsitsii ni edaa ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ akumɔ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Is it harmful if I toss harvested cocoa pods forcefully into large piles before breaking them?
ga: Ani oshara yɛ he akɛ mikɛ mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ shwie ŋtayaa agbo ko mli dani mifo mli?

english: Yes, throwing cocoa pods violently creates small cracks in the outer husk and bruises the inside. Fungal diseases can enter through these cracks, which lowers the quality and grade of the cocoa beans.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ yiwalɛ shwie kookoo ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ bibii aba. yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii baa mligbɛ Fungal helai baanyɛ abote mli kɛtsɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ amli. Enɛ baaha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ kɛ amɛhe ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings wilt and die right after I transplant them into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seedlings suffer severe transplant shock if their delicate roots are disturbed or handled roughly. When moving seedlings, keep the ball of nursery soil around the roots intact so the plant can absorb water right away.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu waa kɛji akɛ agbala amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ. Be ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ Ha sũ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ ekomɛi abɔle he. shishifãi lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: How carefully do I need to handle sprouted oil palm seeds before planting them in nursery bags?
ga: Te esa akɛ makwɛ oil palm dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ tɛŋŋ dani mikɛwo grow bag mli?

english: Sprouted oil palm seeds must be handled with great care so you do not snap the small, white shoot or root tip. Place the seed in the soil bag with the root tip pointing downward and the shoot pointing up without crushing them.
ga: Esa akɛ akwɛ mu tsei ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni okafo ŋmeii bibii komɛi amli. white loo root tip Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo sũ kotoku lɛ mli ni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ shi ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi ni okɛ amɛ akatswaaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need for healthy green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their strength and green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ kɛ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but yield small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or crops are planted too close together, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leafy stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds close together in a hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the young crops fight each other for sunlight, soil moisture, and food. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough space and food to develop strong stems and big yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhaa amɛhe niyenii Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo tsei ni wa ni woɔ yibii.

english: Covering the ground with organic mulch acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the sun from drying out soil moisture, keeps roots cool during hot days, and turns into plant food as it rots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni ebafeɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ́ egbo

english: Why do I need to trim or prune some branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing fresh air and sunlight to pass through the tree. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to direct its energy into growing large pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la kpɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Koni akɛtsi fungal helai tamɔ black pods naa ni awo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ amaje koni amɛfee pods wuji.

english: What is making small ragged holes in the middle leaf shoots of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: Ragged holes inside the center shoot are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the whorl. Catching them early and applying recommended natural sprays or pesticides protects the crop's main growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu hei titri ni onibii lɛ daa yɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm reduce the final weight of my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mikpamɔ lɛ naagbee muji lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the food they need to produce heavy fruits and grains.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo aduawai kɛ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and lets pest populations build up. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ yaa hiɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: The first rainfall often heats up dry soil without soaking it deeply. If a short dry spell follows, the newly germinated seeds will dry out and die before the main rains fully settle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli. Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ kuku nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming any fruits when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes pollen inside tomato flowers to dry up, preventing pollination. When a flower is not pollinated, the plant naturally sheds it to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi pollination naa Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination Tsei jieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: How do I know the exact right month or time of the year to start harvesting my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ loo afi lɛ mli be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their color changes from green or red to yellow or orange. In Ghana, this main harvest period usually runs from October to February, with a smaller mid-crop harvest around May to June.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, nikpamɔ be titri nɛɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ October kɛyashiɔ February. Nibii ni akpaa yɛ May kɛyashi June mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni faaa.

english: How often should I pluck ripe cocoa pods from my trees during the main harvest season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ mli?

english: You should harvest ripe pods every 2 to 3 weeks. Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes the seeds inside to germinate or rot, which ruins the beans.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ daa otsii 2 kɛyashi 3. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Enɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: My cocoa tree leaves grew thick and green after the rains, so why am I not seeing flowers yet?
ga: Yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, mi-kookoo baai lɛ shwere ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Mɛni hewɔ minako fɔfɔi ko lolo lɛ?

english: When heavy rains start, cocoa trees put most of their energy into growing fresh leaves first. Once those new leaves mature, the tree will shift its energy toward producing flowers.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa Cacao tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai heei klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ nakai baai heei lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Tsei lɛ baatsake hewalɛ amɛwo fɔfɔii amli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and spoil when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high humidity on the farm, which causes a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread quickly and destroy healthy pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Enɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa.

english: During the dry harmattan, cocoa trees shed their leaves to save water and protect themselves from drying out. Providing temporary shade or mulch helps them survive this dry period.
ga: Yɛ harmattan ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be nɛɛ mli.

english: Why do so many tiny flowers fall off my cocoa trunk without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo gbee shi kɛjɛ mi kookoo tso lɛ mli ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: It is natural for a cocoa tree to shed many flowers it cannot support. However, extreme flower drop can also be caused by lack of soil nutrients, hot dry weather, or lack of tiny insects called midges that pollinate the flowers.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo aahu akɛ anyɛɛɛ aye abua amɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔii ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ajɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ.

english: If my father's old way of farming worked for him, why should I change how I prune my cocoa trees today?
ga: Kɛji akɛ Da okwaayeli nifeemɔi momo lɛ tsu nii eha lɛ lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ mitsake bɔ ni mifoɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: Traditional methods built a good foundation, but modern pruning techniques open up the canopy so sunlight and air reach the branches, which prevents disease and increases pod yields higher than before.
ga: Kusum gbɛi lɛ feɔ shishitoo kpakpa. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ tsei lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ helai anaa ni eha pod yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Will cutting off unnecessary branches reduce the number of cocoa pods I get?
ga: Ani tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha kookoo ŋmeii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: No, removing dead or excess branches actually increases yields because it directs the tree's food and energy straight to forming healthy pods instead of wasting energy on useless leaves.
ga: Dabi, niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when there are too many tall shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo be babaoo ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: While young cocoa needs shade, mature cocoa trees need good sunlight to produce flowers and pods. Heavy shade traps moisture and blocks the light needed for a good harvest.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo bibioo he miihia hulutsoo. Kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ he miihia hulu la kpakpa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Shade ni tsii baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaatsi la ni he hiaa kɛha kpamɔ kpakpa lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to cover my cocoa seeds with plantain leaves for days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo ŋmeii ahe gbii babaoo dani mikɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermenting the beans under plantain leaves for 6 days kills the seed embryo, removes bitterness, and develops the rich chocolate color and flavor that buyers require.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo plantain baai lɛ ashishi gbii enumɔ lɛ, egbeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsokolate su kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is a natural way the plant reduces evaporation when the soil is dry.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa la ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi.

english: Which crops can survive well on my farm even when the dry season lasts longer than expected?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ po?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas have deep roots or tough leaf structures that allow them to endure long periods without rain much better than delicate vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni mli wa ni haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ fe aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops are drinking too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miinu nu babaoo loo amɛnuuu nu bɔ ni sa?

english: If plants do not get enough water, their leaves wilt, turn brown, and dry out. If they get too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow, look limp, and the roots can rot because the soil has no space for air.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ baagbi. Etsɔɔ blɔfo ni egbiɔ kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nu babaoo. Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse, amɛbaafee tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ, ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ.

english: Why is it important to plant my seeds right at the beginning of the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Planting early allows seeds to take advantage of the moist soil so their roots grow deep and strong before the heavy sun and warm weather dry out the top layer of dirt.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ ji koni eha eshishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe awa dani hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ aha muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do some crops grow tall and thin without producing fruit when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibioo ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ atɛo amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their own food. When planted in thick shade, they stretch upward searching for sunlight instead of spending energy to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ eda yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ekpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ena hulu la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite hewalɛ ni ekɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ latsaa he lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves during hot, dry weather usually mean the plant is saving water and nutrients for its main stem and growing tip by letting go of its older, less useful leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu nu kɛ niyenii kɛha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ etsitsii ni miida lɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni egbɔ ni he ehiaaa tsɔ lɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants need watering almost every day while my cassava grows fine without it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo mi tomato tso lɛ nɔ nu nɔ ni miihe ashɛ daa gbi shi mi-cassava lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ awooo mli nu lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have soft leaves and short roots that dry out quickly, whereas cassava develops deep root systems and thick stems that allow it to store water underground for long periods.
ga: Tomato yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Beni ŋmei lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants die when heavy rainwater stands around their roots for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ beni nugbɔ babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ anɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe. When standing water covers the roots for too long, it drowns them, causing root rot that stops the plant from taking up food and water.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my garden egg plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off without making fruit when the weather becomes too hot and dry, or when the plant does not get enough water to support the growth of the new fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai heei adalɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Akɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Covering the ground with organic material, called mulching, protects the soil from the direct heat of the sun, keeping the soil cool and trapping water so plants stay hydrated longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow strong. This often happens in poor soil or when heavy rains wash nutrients away, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ fiteɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does stubborn spear grass keep growing back on my farm even after I clear it completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mli wa ni ji spear jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ edaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mijie kɛjɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep underground stems called rhizomes that store energy and remain alive even when you cut the top leaves. To get rid of it, you need to dig out the underground roots completely or use recommended weed control before it spreads.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes. Amɛtoɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛji ofo baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ po. koni ojie kɛjɛ mli Esa akɛ okɛ shishifãi lɛ atsu nii kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo okɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ agbeɔ naa lɛ atsu nii dani egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without producing good yield when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of growing thick stems and big fruit, they waste all their energy stretching upward to catch sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa, nɛ e woɔ yiblii nguahi. Mohu ɔ, e puɛɔ e he wami ɔ tsuo nɛ e ngmɛɛɔ kɛ yaa hɛ mi konɛ e nyɛ nɛ e ná hulu la ɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep dropping off the branches without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or pests, or when insects fail to pollinate the flowers. Providing shade trees and keeping soil moist helps the flowers stay on and grow into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli fɔfɔii lɛ He ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help my soil produce better crops in the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that catch nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When the season ends, this leftover nitrogen fertilizes the soil naturally for whatever crop you plant next, such as maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ be lɛ ba naagbee Nitrogen ni eshwɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing the central leaves of my maize crop at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the funnel of young maize leaves during the day and feed during cooler hours. Catching them early and applying proper treatment into the funnel stops them from destroying the plant's growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛtsuɔ nii waa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni sa tsu nii yɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die during the dry afternoon, even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nɛkɛ shwane ni nu bɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: Watering in the hot morning causes fast evaporation and can heat up wet soil, which stresses the roots. Applying dry grass mulch around the base of the plant keeps the root area cool and holds moisture in the ground throughout the hot day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha hulu lɛ atsɔ oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli adɔ, ni no baaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ Tso lɛ shishi haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or uneven watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents the plant from drying out and helps it draw calcium up from the ground.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi, ni ebaaye ebua ni ejie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I don't harvest them before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains leave the soil waterlogged, which chokes the cassava roots by cutting off their air supply. Fungi and bacteria grow quickly in wet ground, causing the trapped roots to rot before you can dig them up.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ yɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Mold kɛ bacteria daa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni akɛkpɛtɛ he lɛ fiteɔ dani obaanyɛ okɛfo mli.

english: Why do I need to dry my harvested maize thoroughly before storing it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ dani mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize holds moisture that encourages destructive molds and weevils to spread quickly inside closed bags. Drying the grains until they are hard keeps them safe from damage and safe to consume or sell.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli, ni no woɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kotoku ni agbe naa lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi ewa lɛ, ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛha niyeli loo jarayeli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dying in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight because their root systems are still small and lose moisture quickly. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as natural umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from intense heat or dry soil. Placing dry grass or mulch around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and holds moisture in the soil so the flowers can turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ he. Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow strong green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I plant maize on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, mikpamɔ lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Maize pulls the exact same nutrients from the soil every season, leaving the ground exhausted. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil and restores its natural fertility.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when sitting water stays around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away quickly, protecting the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ye obua ni abu yitso lɛ he

english: Why do my crops wilt during the dry season even when I water them occasionally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛnɔ yɛ bei komɛi amli moŋ lɛ?

english: Light watering only dampens the top of the soil, causing roots to stay shallow where the hot sun dries them out quickly. Deep watering less often encourages roots to grow deeper into the ground where moisture stays longer.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ. Ha shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ hei ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ lɛ agbi oya. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni mli kwɔ woɔ shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and air. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough energy from the sun and soil to produce a heavy yield of fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ato tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the maize seeds I stored from last season fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ lɛ?

english: Stored seeds lose their ability to sprout if they are kept in warm or damp places where insects or mold can spoil them. Storing dried seeds in airtight containers with clean wood ash keeps them dry and safe until planting time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni kooloi loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aha amɛfite. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni tso sũ ni he tse yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi be mli ni aduɔ.

english: What is eating holes into the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the leaves. Inspecting your farm early in the morning allows you to catch and manage them before they destroy the growing point of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ omɔɔ amɛ ni otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Weeds are tough wild plants designed to grow fast and steal water and plant food from your soil. Clearing weeds early before they flower prevents them from dropping thousands of new seeds back into your farmland.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni afee koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Dani jwɛi lɛ baafɔ lɛ amɛtsiɔ dumɔwui heei akpei abɔ naa koni amɛkaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba oŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves dry out quickly. Providing shade using plantain trees or shade nets keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the young cocoa survive until it develops stronger roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui loo shade tsɔne ha shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. This happens when the soil is worn out or heavy rains wash the soil food away. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or NPK can make the leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ laaje. Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the middle leaves of my young maize plants looking torn with small dark dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɛ eshwa ni muji bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by a pest called Fall Armyworm, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant and eats the tender leaves. The dark dirt is its waste. Applying appropriate insecticides or neem seed extracts early in the morning stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Muji ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ji jwɛi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem dumɔwui amli nu wo mli leebi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpãtãmɔ lɛ akpa.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tightly like cigars during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ sigaret yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to protect the plant from losing too much water during hot hours. By curling inwards, less leaf surface is exposed to the harsh sun, preventing the crop from drying out.
ga: Leaf curl ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ mligbɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Hulu la fioo pɛ baashɛ baa lɛ nɔ. Tsi ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkagbi

english: Cassava roots rot underground when soil stays waterlogged for too long, especially during heavy rains. Excess water starves the roots of air, allowing rot fungi to grow. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. ni eha ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ akwɛ̃. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden sticks to tie up my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei kakadaji akpɛtɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need plenty of sunlight on all their leaves to produce large tubers underground. Staking holds the vines up toward the sun, keeps leaves off hot soil, and prevents diseases from spreading from the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kpɛtɛ wain tso lɛ he ni ekwɛ hulu la lɛ hiɛ. Etsiɔ baai anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. ni atsĩ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress or irregular watering. When the plant experiences high temperatures or dry soil, it sheds its flowers to conserve energy instead of attempting to feed growing fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ tsei lɛ shɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ena niyenii kɛha aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: When a plantain plant has too many side shoots (suckers), they all compete for the same food and water in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, which allows the main stem to grow large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ná ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from young leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps new leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Enɛ baaha baai heei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally enriches the ground with plant food, improves soil health, and helps choke out weeds.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei amli niyenii kpakpai lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa tree's first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts between my maize rows help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally adds fertilizer to the soil, helping your maize crop grow stronger without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your soil is low in nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed newer leaves, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or manure early on keeps the whole plant green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛye baai heei. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra. Ebaaha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Why do the small pods on my cocoa tree turn black and rot when the rains get heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain and excessive shade create high moisture, which causes black pod fungal disease. Pruning tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds around the base helps dry out the trees and prevent the rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo babaoo haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. ni ji black pod fungus hela lɛ Niji ni afolɔ koni hulu la abote mli ni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akagbi ni ekɛtsi fitemɔ naa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Plants lose water through their leaves very quickly during peak heat. Curling their leaves is a defense mechanism to reduce exposed surface area and save moisture until the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ kɛyashiɔ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers during the hot season, but no tomatoes grow from them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Shi ani tomato ko bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen dries out and becomes sterile, preventing the flowers from producing fruits. Providing light shade or choosing heat-tolerant tomato seeds prevents this flower drop.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be lɛ ha loo tomato dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa lɛ halamɔ lɛ, ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: How do I know if my cassava is growing good tubers under the ground when the tops look healthy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi? Be ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil to expand its tubers. If the soil is too hard or clay-heavy, the plant spends its energy growing leafy stems above ground instead of large roots below.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he miihia cassava koni ekɛdu ŋmeii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ Tsei yeɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch full sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build big tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, protecting them from fungal infections.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: If buried too deeply, the seed uses up all its stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil and may exhaust itself and die before its leaves reach the sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ egbɔjɔ ni egbo dani hulu la lɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I buy seed varieties produced locally in Ghana instead of imported seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni afee yɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ mli lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ?
