english: Locally produced seeds are bred to handle local soil conditions, native pests, and Ghana's specific rainfall and heat patterns, making them more likely to produce a strong harvest than seeds brought from elsewhere.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ajieɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛtsu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he nii. maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ Ghana nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ dɔlɛ pɔtɛɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ewoɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ hei krokomɛi kɛbaa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so when there isn't enough, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. No hewɔ lɛ kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my soil stay fertile?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When planted with maize, they naturally feed the soil so your maize can grow better without using as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha o-abele lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why do I need to plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slanting angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu cassava niji lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at a slant encourages the plant to produce tubers closer to the surface in an even pattern, making them grow larger and making it much easier for you to harvest them later.
ga: Kasava ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ cassava shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ aba yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ekome nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaakpa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why must I put tall wooden stakes next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Ani aduɔ sweet potato wain tsei?

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need plenty of sunlight to produce big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, which boosts food production for the tuber and prevents leaf rot diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii ni anáa ahaa ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Leaving too many small shoots (suckers) causes them to steal water and plant food from the main plant. Pruning extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones ensures the main plantain tree yields large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli ni ahiɛ tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha plantain titri lɛ niji agboi ni tsii akwɛ̃.

english: What causes the green cocoa pods on my trees to turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a tiny fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning heavy shade trees and clearing weeds allows air and sunlight to dry the cocoa pods and reduce fungal rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛ ŋmei bibioo ko mli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the blossom ends of my green tomato fruits turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually triggered by irregular soil moisture. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering helps the plant move calcium into the developing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ aya tomatoi ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I see ragged holes and small dark droppings inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ baai lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant to eat young leaves. Checking your farm early and applying recommended neem extracts or insecticides will protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishifãi lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cover the bare ground around my vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha he ni etse ehe lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or dead leaves is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from drying out quickly, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ

english: Why are the flowers on my hot pepper plants dropping off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi chili tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho ni ekɛ chili ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot dry air, insufficient soil moisture, or excess nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist and avoiding over-fertilization encourages flowers to set fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛyashɛ haomɔ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akawo yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my green maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen in the soil or are damaged by sitting in too much water. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back their strong green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo efite amɛ. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow small and weak when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to end up stunted and weak.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of pushing them straight into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at an angle allows roots to spread out evenly near the surface, giving the tubers room to grow larger and making them easier to harvest.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ náa he ko ni da ni ehaa amɛkpamɔ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Yams are climbing plants that need maximum sunlight to make food. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes exposes leaves to sunlight and keeps them away from pests and damp ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛhoo. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the days get extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. High heat prevents the flowers from pollinating successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkaye omanye yɛ fɔfɔii amli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why is it good to cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material traps water in the dirt so it doesn't dry out quickly in the sun, keeps the ground cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ekagbi oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to plant maize in the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets pests that eat that specific crop multiply in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why am I seeing tiny ragged holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee tso lɛ mli lɛ anɔ

english: Ragged holes in young maize are a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. These caterpillars hide inside the plant shoot during the day and eat the soft growth, which can destroy the farm if untreated.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni shwereɔ waa lɛ. ni baanyɛ akpata ŋmɔ ko hiɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: How do scented lures and physical traps help protect my farm from crop pests?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ abu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe?

english: Insect traps use specific scents or bright colors that fool pests into thinking food or a mate is nearby. Once the insects fly into the trap, they get stuck or captured, reducing pest numbers on your farm without harming your crops.
ga: Bug zappers kɛ tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi loo sui ni kpɛɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛlaka ŋmeii ni amɛsusu niyenii loo hefatalɔ ko bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Kɛji kooloi bibii fo kɛbote tsɔne lɛ mli Amɛbaatsi amɛhe loo abaamɔmɔ amɛ. Ye obua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ aba shi ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Why are caterpillars eating big holes in my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like the fall armyworm hatch from eggs laid on maize leaves and feed heavily on young growth to grow. They hide inside the plant's funnel during the day and chew the leaves, which can stunt the plant if not managed early.
ga: Kplukai sumɔɔ cutworms ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii waa beni tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei akui amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle intense heat and sun. They need shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la naa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce small peppers when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ pepper bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for the same soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Because each plant gets a smaller share of food, they grow smaller fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii fioo ko nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ yibii bibii.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, humid weather. Rain drops splash fungal spores from the soil onto lower cocoa pods, causing them to rot rapidly if the farm is too shaded or unweeded.
ga: Blɔfo diŋ hela jɛɔ ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni edɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa. Nugbɔ nɛɔ, ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo jwɛi bɛ mli tsɔ.

english: Cassava leaves often curl and turn yellow when tiny insects called whiteflies spread the cassava mosaic virus, or when the plant is stressed by severe dry weather. Keeping weeds under control reduces the insects that spread this sickness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ amɛshwã. aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ Jwɛi ni akudɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha kooloi ni gbɛɔ hela nɛɛ eshwaa lɛ aba shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is a lack of nutrients like potassium in the soil. High heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni niyenii tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nyɛ fɔfɔi anɔ koni amɛgbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing plenty of big green leaves but no fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-heavy fertilizer causes plants to focus all their energy on growing leafy branches instead of setting flowers and fruit. Balancing your fertilizer encourages the plant to start fruiting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ tsei niji ni baai miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why do plantain trees fall over so easily during strong winds before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees carry heavy fruit bunches but have shallow roots that stay near the top layer of soil. If root pests damage the root system or the soil becomes waterlogged, strong winds can easily pull the entire plant out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo. Shi eyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi amli kooloi fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tsei muu fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: How does rotating different crops in my field prevent soil diseases?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsĩ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every season allows specific crop pests and diseases to build up. Switching to a different crop family starves out those pests because they lose their preferred food source.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei komekomei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai komɛi aba. Kɛ́ atsake kɛtee tsei aweku kroko mli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii lɛ ejaakɛ amɛlaaje niyenii ni amɛsumɔɔ waa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow strong and green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their healthy green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my corn field so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni ekashi jwɛi?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer in two stages: a small amount at planting to help early roots grow, and a second boost (top-dressing) when the corn is about knee-high, which is when the plant eats the most nutrients to build cobs.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo awo mli yɛ dumɔ be mli koni eha shishifãi lɛ ada oya. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ nɔ (Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nɔ) beni ŋmei lɛ shɛɔ aaafee tsitsi nɔ lɛ. Be nɛɛ ji be ni tsei yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas on my land after I harvest my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Corn takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but beans and cowpeas actually put good food (nitrogen) back into the soil through their roots, keeping your soil fertile for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shi ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ niyenii kpakpa (nitrogen) lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's clever way of protecting itself from losing water when the sun is too hot. By rolling its leaves, it reduces the surface area exposed to the heat to conserve moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋaa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why is my corn growing very tall but only making small or half-empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni fã ko bɛ mli pɛ lɛ?

english: Tall plants with small cobs usually happen when plants are planted too close together or lack sufficient nutrients like phosphorus. When overcrowded, the plants compete for light and water instead of putting energy into filling out the cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei kakadaji ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ amɛmli, kɛ́ amɛyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii. Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la kɛ nu he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛ jwɛi ŋmɔtɔ afata he lɛ

english: How far apart should I plant my corn seeds in the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting seeds about one step (75 centimeters) between rows and a forearm length (30 centimeters) between plants gives each root enough space, air, sunlight, and soil nutrients to yield large, heavy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ aaafee ŋwɛi ŋta kome (sentimitai 75) kɛ nine kome (sentimitai 30) yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso shishifãi náa gbɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young corn leaves have ragged holes in them that look like caterpillar bites?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ egbɛ eshwa tamɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Small holes in young corn leaves are a sign of pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the plant. Catching them early with proper biological or chemical spray protects the central leaf funnel where new growth happens.
ga: Bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni miiye tso lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ mɔmɔmɔ amɛ mra kɛtsɔ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi ni shweremɔ heei miiba lɛ ahe.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my corn if I don't clear them?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ aha mi-ŋma lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji mijieee amɛ?

english: Weeds are like aggressive neighbors that drink the water and eat the fertilizer meant for your corn. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks gives your young crop the head start it needs to outgrow them.
ga: Jwɛi tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ o-ŋma lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa otsei bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi mra fe bɔ ni osumɔɔ.

english: Why are some of the corn seeds I planted failing to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep, if the ground is too dry, or if insects eat them underground. Planting seeds about two finger-joints deep in moist soil usually gives the best germination.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dumɔwui Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ aaafee inchi 2 yɛ inchi kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What type of soil works best for growing a good maize harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Maize grows best in loose, rich soil (loam) that drains water well after rain but still holds enough moisture for roots to drink without rotting.
ga: Abɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ sũ (loam) ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Shi ehiɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why do I need to clear big tree roots from my field before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei wuji ashishifãi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Tree roots left underground steal water and nutrients away from your young crops. Clearing them gives your crop roots room to spread freely and get the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Tso shishifãi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: How does plowing hard soil help my yam tubers grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Yam tubers grow directly underground, so hard dirt stops them from expanding. Loosening the soil allows the tubers to spread easily, resulting in larger and healthier yields.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni bulb lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Enɛ haa anáa nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off when there is too much sun and dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells to protect itself from losing too much water. It is a natural survival trick so the plant stays alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ hi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ nɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the afternoon heat even if the soil was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon air makes water leave plant leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. As long as the soil has moisture, the plants will usually rest and stand up straight again by evening.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu shĩɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ baajɔɔ ehe ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ.

english: The very first rain often heats up the dry soil without soaking it deeply. A dry spell usually follows, which can scorch and kill young seedlings before the main rain season begins.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli. Bei pii lɛ, hela ni egbi lɛ he okadii nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ni efite amɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to take immediate advantage of direct sunlight and fresh soil nutrients. Crops need extra care and protection until they grow big enough to shadow out the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ he sɛɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe miihia kwɛmɔ kɛ hebuu krɛdɛɛ ko kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the stalks fight each other for sunlight, stretching upward instead of putting their energy into growing strong stems and big ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Ekɛ ehe shwieɔ ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmãa toi wuji anɔ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, drink water and food meant for the main mother plant. Removing the weak ones ensures all nutrients go into producing a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi lɛ loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ feɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my maize crops grow better when I plant cowpeas in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that catch natural air food called nitrogen and put it into the dirt. This natural fertilizer feeds neighboring crops like maize and makes the soil richer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli niyenii ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ abele, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more when the weather is warm and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Dry heat weakens crops and leaves them vulnerable, while warm weather helps insects reproduce much faster, causing pest populations to burst during dry seasons.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii ni amɛfɔɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many pods during certain months of the year and almost nothing during others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli, ni ŋmeii ko kwraa wooo yɛ nyɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees react to natural weather cycles like rainfall and sunshine. During the main rainy season, the trees get enough water to form and grow pods, leading to a major harvest, while during dry periods, the tree slows down to conserve water.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsuɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulu la he nii. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii ni amɛdara. ni kɛ kpamɔ babaoo baa yɛ be mli ni yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu nu he.

english: Is crop production strictly controlled by nature, or can I plan my farm practices to manage dry and wet seasons better?
ga: Ani akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ mli? Aloo ani manyɛ mato miŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ahe gbɛjianɔ koni manyɛ matsu hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: While weather comes from nature, good farming practices can help. Planting shade trees, mulching soil to hold water, and pruning early help your crops withstand dry seasons and maximize yields during rainy periods.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ jɛ adebɔɔ mli moŋ Shi okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai baanyɛ aye abua. Tsei ni aduɔ koni eha hulutsoo Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni nu ahi shi. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ mra Ye obua otsei lɛ ni amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ naa ni amɛha nibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What kind of medicine can I apply to my crop when the cocoa pods start turning black and rotting on the tree?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofa manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ bɔi diŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that thrives in high humidity. You can protect your trees by spraying approved fungicides before the heavy rains start and removing infected pods so the sickness does not spread.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Obaanyɛ obu otsei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookɛshwie amɛnɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ nɔ. ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know the right month or season to spray chemical treatments on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ loo be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Chemical treatments should be timed with the crop cycle and weather. Insect sprays are best applied when pest numbers begin rising early in the season, while disease sprays should be used just before and during damp, wet months.
ga: Esa akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ atsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ shwereɔ kɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ je shishi eya hiɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ atsu nii dani nyɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ aba, kɛ yɛ nyɔji nɛɛ amli.

english: It is normal for cocoa trees to shed extra flowers if they do not have enough nutrients or water to feed all potential pods. However, heavy flower drop can also mean the tree lacks key nutrients or is experiencing heat stress.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titri loo ekɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ miikpe.

english: Why are trees in one section of my farm producing mature pods while trees in another section are still empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ fã kroko lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Variations in soil depth, sunlight exposure, and moisture across different areas of your land cause trees to flower and fruit at slightly different rates, even on the same farm.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ ni hulu la kɛ hulutsoo be srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei srɔtoi lɛ haa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo nɔ. Kɛji amɛyɛ ŋmɔ kome mli po.

english: Can I do anything to help my cocoa trees yield more pods during the smaller harvest season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni baaye abua cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be bibioo lɛ mli?

english: Yes, maintaining proper shade levels, pruning dead branches, and applying fertilizer early in the rainy season helps the tree stay strong enough to produce extra pods during the minor harvest period.
ga: Hɛɛ, shade ni sa lɛ mlihiɛmɔ. Niji ni egboi lɛ ni aaafolɔ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ kpamɔɔ be bibioo lɛ mli.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree keep producing good harvest before it gets too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: Cocoa trees usually produce their best yields between 10 and 25 years of age. After 30 years, production naturally drops, and old trees may need to be replaced with new seedlings or rehabilitated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25. Yɛ afii 30 sɛɛ lɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni akɛ dumɔwui heei loo tsei ni afee amɛ ehee lɛ ato tsei momoi lɛ anajiaŋ.

english: Do my young cocoa plants need full sunshine or shade from bigger trees to grow well?
ga: Ani mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ he miihia hulu la loo hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade from trees like plantains to protect their delicate leaves from burning. As the cocoa trees mature, you can reduce the shade so they receive enough light to form flowers and fruit.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda kwraa Obaanyɛ otsi hulutsoo be lɛ shi koni ona la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai aba.

english: How does crop sickness spread from one diseased cocoa tree to neighboring healthy trees?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Diseases spread through rain splashes, wind, insects, or dirty farming tools. Pruning infected branches and cleaning your tools after working on sick trees prevents the sickness from traveling across your farm.
ga: Helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, koolooi, loo okwaayeli nibii ni he tseee nɔ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oookpa ni otsumɔ onitsumɔ dadei lɛ amli beni okɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants look weak and thin when I grow them under big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe efee shoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Maize plants need full, direct sunlight to make food for themselves. When they are shaded by big trees, they cannot capture enough sunlight, causing them to stretch tall, remain weak, and produce small yields.
ga: Abɛi tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Kɛ tso agbo ko ewo amɛhe shade lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ mɛi ni shwereɔ waa, amɛyaa nɔ amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: How can I tell if my vegetable crops are getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛnáaa nu babaoo?

english: If crops do not get enough water, their leaves wilt, curl, and feel dry to the touch. If they get too much water, the soil stays waterlogged, roots rot from lack of air, and the leaves turn pale yellow.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛgbi kɛji akɛ ata he. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee nu. Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ. ni baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse.

english: Why do I need to put manure or fertilizer in the soil when my crops are already growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ momo lɛ?

english: Soil contains food that plants draw up through their roots to grow. Over time, crops use up these nutrients, so adding manure or fertilizer replenishes the soil food so your plants do not starve.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni tsei gbalaa kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi amli koni amɛdara lɛ ji nɔ ni feɔ shikpɔŋ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafite niyenii nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. koni hɔmɔ akaye tsei lɛ

english: Why do weeds make my cassava crops produce much smaller tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-cassava tsei lɛ miifee bulbs bibii waa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your cassava for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. When weeds surround your crop, the cassava plant loses energy fighting for survival instead of feeding its underground tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwuuɔ koni ehi shi lɛ baa shi.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together to get more crops, why do they perform poorly?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hu? Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the young plants to crowd each other and fight over limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong and fruit well.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ abua amɛhe naa ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii.

english: Planting tomatoes repeatedly in the same spot completely exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows tomato-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, leading to weaker crops each year.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaho kwraa. ni ehaa helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ tomato pɔtɛɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under hot, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and feature wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and protecting soil moisture during its critical early growth stage.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ fãi ni he hiaa lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my pepper roots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the ground quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are usually a sign that the plant is short on nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to send remaining energy to support new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua dalɛ ni yɔɔ baa heei anɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I pinch off the small extra shoots growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Extra side shoots consume nutrients and water to grow unnecessary leaves instead of fruit. Removing these shoots redirects the plant's energy toward producing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Lateral shoots lɛ biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu koni amɛkwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: When the lower leaves of maize turn yellow starting from the tip and moving down the center, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food crops need to build strong, green leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no plantains planted nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting plantains next to them provides fast-growing shade that protects the young cocoa trees and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. plantains plantains next to Ehaa hulutsoo ni daa oya ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without forming fruit when the weather becomes too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when the soil lacks key nutrients like phosphorus needed for fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei bɛ nu loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and weak when I put four or five seeds into the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ, beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to stay weak and produce smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Cassava plants signal that roots are ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and small cracks begin to appear in the soil right around the base of the stem.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Ebaabɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ sũ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen out of the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass keep them from wilting in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haaa amɛgboi yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from hitting the soil, keeping the root area cool and trapping moisture so the plant stays hydrated longer.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ akatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear weeds when they are still very small instead of waiting for them to grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛdara kwraa lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil food, water, and sunlight from your young crops; clearing them early prevents them from starving your plants during their most critical growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye otsei lɛ hɔmɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why did my maize seeds rot in the ground when I planted right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often warms up the hot soil without providing enough deep moisture. If rains pause right after, the seeds get cooked or dry out before they can properly sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ loo amɛbaagbi dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves in the center of my young maize plants coming out with ragged holes and dark dirt on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli etse ni muji ni tsuɔ diŋ ekpɛtɛ he lɛ?

english: Holes and dirt in the central leaves of young maize are typical signs of caterpillars like the fall armyworm, which hide inside the funnel of the plant and feed on the tender new leaves before they open.
ga: Buu kɛ muji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ahe. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants take about four months to mature before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ dani ekpaa lɛ?

english: Maize needs a specific amount of time to go through distinct growth stages: germination, leaf growth, flowering, and grain filling. Standard maize varieties in Ghana are bred to complete this life cycle in around 90 to 120 days to produce fully developed, dry grains.
ga: Abɛi heɔ be fioo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ: ekwɛ̃ɔ, ebaa dalɛ, fɔfɔi, kɛ dumɔwui ni eyiɔ obɔ. Akwɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana ni ji standard lɛ koni amɛgbe wala shihilɛ nɛɛ naa yɛ aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 mli koni amɛná ŋmãa ni egbi ni eda kwraa.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller when I plant my seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the plants compete with each other for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress prevents individual plants from growing strong roots or producing large fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi anaa koni amɛkawo shishifãi ni wa loo amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no big trees around to shade them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ ni baaha hulutsoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out and burn easily under the harsh direct sun. Nursery trees or plantains act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young plants until they are strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nursery tsei loo plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water when the sun is hot. It is a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to direct heat and preserve internal moisture.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni dɔlɛ baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi ni eha emli fɛ̃i ahi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a plant usually mean it is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. The plant naturally moves the limited nitrogen it has from older leaves to the newer leaves at the top to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is it wasteful for me to apply chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji fitemɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the topsoil before the roots have time to drink it in. This process, called leaching, leaves your plants without nutrients and wastes the money spent on fertilizer.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ leaching. Ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni amɛbaafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do worms target the soft inside leaves at the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miitutua baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm prefer the tender, hidden center (the whorl) of young maize because it provides rich nutrients and protects them from sunlight and natural predators.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm sumɔɔ ŋmãa bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa amɛyeɔ nii babaoo, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Flower drop happens when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, poor pollination, or irregular watering. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for basic survival.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ pollination ni ehiii. loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, prevents weeds from taking over, and keeps the soil cool during hot weather so roots can absorb nutrients easily.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Cutting away all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough nutrition to produce big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ fɛɛ amli, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to build strong green leaves. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer harvests when I plant maize on the same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil each season. Rotating your crop with beans or cowpeas feeds nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives when there is too much moisture and shade around the trees. Pruning extra tree branches lets air and sunlight in to dry out the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ tso lɛ he. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive chemical fertilizer can shock the plant, causing it to shed flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee gbeyei. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into leaf growth instead of roots. Balanced nutrients and good sunlight signal the plant to store energy underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa kɛ hulu la ni hi haa tsei lɛ feɔ okadi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water rapidly. During dry spells, the plant naturally sheds older leaves to preserve moisture in its main trunk until the rains return.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu sɛɛ foɔ oya. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai momoi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl and droop in the afternoon heat even if I watered them earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ mra moŋ?

english: In intense midday sun, leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it up. The leaves curl to reduce sunlight exposure, but usually bounce back once temperature drops in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni hulu la lɛ aba shi. Shi efɔɔ sɛɛkuu kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant beans in the same rows with their maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni amɛduɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plant so both crops thrive together on the same land.
ga: Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Bɔni afee ni tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ afee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he kome.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to sprout after I planted them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds require warm soil and steady moisture to wake up and germinate. Planting them too deep or in dry, hard soil delays sprouting or causes the seed to decay.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ loo ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my young yam vines early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ he hiaa mi.

english: Young yam vines grow slowly at first and cannot easily compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil food during their first few weeks.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. Ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni shwereɔ oya lɛ ashi akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay dark green and grow healthy stems and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely, as the plant tries to save water and energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to chew holes deep inside the heart of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmei bibioo lɛ ŋmɔ bu ko ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides inside the central leaves of young maize plants and eats the growing shoots before the cob forms.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli ni eyeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions where water sits on the cocoa pods for too long.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, shade ni nu hiɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when too much rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy water collects in heavy soil without draining away, suffocating the roots and allowing soil fungi to destroy them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ muji bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaaa. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kpataɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaf surfaces and shallow roots that burn quickly in full sun; they require shade crops like plantains to protect them during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I remove the small shoots growing around the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Removing extra suckers prevents them from stealing food and water from the main tree, ensuring the main plant yields a bigger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: Staking gets the vine leaves off the hot ground into the air and light, helping the leaves capture maximum sunshine to feed and grow a large tuber underground.
ga: Staking haa wain tso lɛ baai lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ hei ni edɔ lɛ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni amɛye niyenii ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know if my farmland has lost its strength and needs fertilizer or a rest period?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ hewalɛ miiho ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ be?

english: Soil is worn out if crops grow short and thin, leaves stay pale or yellow even with good rain, and harvest sizes drop year after year.
ga: Soil deteriorates if plants grow short and thin. Baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Ni ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell; planting too early causes seeds to sprout and then wither from a lack of steady moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ daa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to spend money on watering my crops when rain falls naturally in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afite shika kɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ Ghana yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ?

english: Crops require a steady, predictable supply of moisture to grow strong. Relying only on irregular rainfall can stress your plants, stunt their growth, or lead to total crop failure during sudden dry spells.
ga: Tsei taoɔ nu ni yaa nɔ daa, ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ nɔ ni baaba koni amɛdara hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha otsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. etsĩɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ naa loo efiteɔ yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli.

english: How does proper watering actually help my crop produce more yield at harvest time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni sa ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Water acts as a transport system inside the plant, carrying food and nutrients from the soil up into the leaves and fruits. Without enough water, plants cannot feed properly, resulting in small and light produce.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo yɛ tsei amli. Kɛtsɔ niyenii kɛ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ faaa ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Do my crops need the same amount of water when they are young as when they start flowering?
ga: Ani nu ni he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ beni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, crop water needs change as they grow. Young seedlings need light watering to establish roots, but crops require the highest amount of water when flowering and forming fruits or seeds.
ga: Dabi, ehe miihia ni atsake tso lɛ mli nu lɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Nu fioo pɛ he hiaa tsei bibii koni amɛná shishifãi. Shi nu babaoo he hiaa tsei fe fɛɛ beni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How can I keep the soil around my crops moist for longer without spending extra money on water?
ga: Matsu shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ he nii. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛfite shika kɛhe nu babaoo?

english: You can use mulching, which means spreading dry leaves or grass over the soil around your plants. This shades the ground from the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mulching atsu nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, esa akɛ afɔse baai loo jwɛi ni egbi lɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: How do my crop plants show me that they are suffering from a lack of water?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔɔ mi bɔ ni nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ miipiŋ amɛha.

english: When crops lack water, their leaves wilting or curling during the daytime is usually the first sign. If the dry conditions continue, the leaves will turn yellow and flowers or young fruits will drop off.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi loo ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ okadi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tee nɔ egbi lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii lɛ baagbee shi.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leaves every plant hungry and weak instead of strong and healthy.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e ngɛ he wami.

english: Why should I treat buying farm inputs like fertilizer and water as a business investment?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ŋmɔ mli nibii, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu hemɔ he akɛ jarayeli nitsumɔ mli shika?

english: Just like feeding livestock makes them bigger, putting money into proper nutrients and water for your crops increases the size and quantity of your produce, which earns you more income when sold.
ga: Taakɛ kooloi ni ayeɔ niyenii lɛ haa efeɔ agbo lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ shika wo niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni sa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebɔi babaoo. Enɛ baaha oná shika babaoo kɛ́ oohɔ̃ɔ nii.

english: How does investing money in soil care early in the season affect my total crop yield?
ga: Te shika ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Good soil care gives young crops a strong foundation, allowing them to absorb nutrients quickly, resist diseases better, and produce a larger harvest at the end of the season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa haa tsei bibii lɛ shishitoo ni wa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛbaatsu nii ni ewoɔ babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee.

english: What causes my crop plants to produce fewer bags of produce than expected at harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baagi fioo fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Low yield is usually caused by poor soil nutrients, irregular watering, pest attacks, or harvesting too early. Correcting these issues helps plants reach their full yield capacity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli niyenii ni bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo nikpamɔ oya tsɔ Naagbai nɛɛ ahe tsabaa yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛshɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee lɛ he.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my crops so the produce stays heavy and good for the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Koni afee babaoo ni ehi aha jara lɛ?

english: Most crops show clear signals like leaves changing color, stems drying up, or fruits reaching a specific size and firm texture. Harvesting at full maturity ensures maximum weight and quality.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ baai ni tsakeɔ amɛhe su, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni egbiɔ, loo aduawai ni dalɛ kɛ amɛhe yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Nikpamɔ yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ haa anáa shwiili ni tsii fe fɛɛ kɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young nursery plants dying when I keep them covered in a dark area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ to duŋ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants and seedlings need light to grow. Keeping nursery plants in dark places or pits deprives them of sunlight, which causes them to weaken, rot, and die instead of producing healthy leaves.
ga: La ni tsoɔ waa he miihia tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei bibii wo he ko ni duŋ yɔɔ loo yɛ bu ko mli lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Should I put weak or slow-growing seedlings out in the sun to help them recover?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni miida blɛoo lɛ awo hulutsoo be mli koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe awa amɛ?

english: Yes, moving weak or underperforming seedlings into adequate sunlight gives them the light energy they need to produce food, strengthen their stems, and bounce back to healthy growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa mli lɛ baaha amɛná la hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Wajemɔ tso lɛ ni ekwɛ ekoŋŋ ni efee hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: What happens if I plant my seedlings too deep in a pit instead of on flat bed soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ wo bu ko ni mli kwɔ tsɔ mli moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ?

english: Planting too deep cuts off essential sunlight and air circulation from the young plant, causing roots to suffocate and the crop to die before it can establish itself.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaafo hulu la ni he hiaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ dani enyɛɔ emaa shi.

english: Why is it recommended to leave a wide space like 10 feet between my crops when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ ashi he ko ni miihe ashɛ ninetalɔi 10 yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each plant has enough room to catch sunlight and draw water and nutrients from the soil without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni ekɛjie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I squeeze more crops together on my small piece of land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo shwie mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for food and light. Overcrowded farms usually result in thin, weak plants and a lower total yield.
ga: Dabi, ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wuɔ yɛ niyenii kɛ la he. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: What should I do if my farm is not big enough to give every plant the recommended distance?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ daaa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahã tsei fɛɛ ahi he ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛhi shi lɛ mli?

english: It is better to plant fewer well-spaced crops than to crowd many plants together, as properly spaced crops produce larger, healthier harvests even on smaller land.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ hi fe tsei babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome, ejaakɛ tsei ni ato he jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ he ko bibioo po.

english: Is it true that allowing many stems to grow on one crop will give me more yield?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ kɛ́ miŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha maná yibii babaoo?

english: No, having too many stems actually reduces your yield. The crop spreads its food and water too thin among all the stems, resulting in small and poor-quality fruit.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ oyɛ tsei babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ gbɛɔ niyenii kɛ nu mli fioo tsɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã fɛɛ shishifã nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ daraaa ni ehiii kwraa.

english: What is thinning, and why is it important for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji shwiemɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Thinning is the practice of cutting away extra or weak stems from a plant so that the remaining strong stems get all the plant's food energy to grow bigger produce.
ga: Thinning ji nifeemɔ ni ji tso lɛ shishifãi ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ aná tso lɛ mli niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How does removing extra shoots from my plants help them produce better fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: When you remove excess shoots, the plant stops wasting food on useless stems and focuses all its resources on developing larger, healthier fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛji ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ Tsei lɛ baakpa niyenii ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ. ni amɛkɛ nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ ama aduawai loo ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Will leaving extra stems on my plants make my farm work harder to manage?
ga: Ani tsei akutsei ni mashi yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔ lɛ atsu nii waa koni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, leaving too many stems creates thick, bushy plants that clutter the field, shade out lower leaves, make weeding difficult, and waste soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi tsei tsei babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni mli tse ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo aba shia lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fã lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli. kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my green maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen or that too much water in the soil is suffocating the roots, preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ loo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haaa anyɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich animal manure, cassava puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to swell the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Is it better to plant my maize right after the first short rain, or should I wait longer?
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be loo esa akɛ mamɛ be babaoo?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. Planting after an early isolated rain can cause seeds to sprout, only for the young seedlings to dry up and die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛ mra sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Tsei bibii pɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear away all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct heat and sun. Tall shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the air moist and cool while the young cocoa plants grow.
ga: Cocoa yibii bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ ni edɔɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have natural microbes in their roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil, acting like a free natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni damɔ shi ekome kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are small black ants suddenly swarming all over my okra plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ trukaa lɛ, ŋmeii bibii diji miibɔle mi gumbo lɛ he lɛ?

english: Ants are attracted to a sweet juice secreted by tiny insects like aphids or mealybugs hiding under the leaves. The ants actually protect these destructive insects from predators.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, wuo ni kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mealybugs ni akɛtee baai lɛ ashishi lɛ feɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, ŋmeii buɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why does Striga weed seem to appear and spread mostly where my crops are growing weakly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ jeɔ kpo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo yɛ hei ni mi tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ?

english: Striga, also known as witchweed, targets weak crops in poor soil because it attaches to their roots to steal food. It thrives in worn-out soil where crops lack strength to defend themselves.
ga: Striga, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Witchweed lɛ, tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ anɔ. Ejaakɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ ahe koni eju niyenii. Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji ni efite ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaabu amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather becomes extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden drought followed by heavy watering, which stresses the plant during pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ trukaa ni nu babaoo nyiɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ pollination baa lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my yams are fully mature and ready to dig up from under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli?
