english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and dry up, showing that the plant has stopped growing and stored its energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ miito bulb lɛ mli.

english: How do I choose a healthy banana sucker to plant on my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala banana tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for sword suckers that have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. These grow much faster, establish stronger roots, and produce bigger bunches than maiden suckers with wide, flat leaves.
ga: Taomɔ klante tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya kwraa. Bɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni ofee kui ni dara fe tsei bibii ni baai lɛ yɔɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my banana suckers when planting them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo banana tsei lɛ amli kɛ́ midu?

english: Space your banana suckers about 3 meters apart in every direction. This prevents their large leaves from blocking sunlight from each other and ensures their roots do not fight for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Okɛ banana tsei lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 yɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ ji koni baai wuji lɛ akatsi hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkaye niyenii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: How deep should I dig the hole before placing my banana sucker inside?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ dani mikɛ banana sucker lɛ awo mli?

english: Dig a hole about 45 centimeters wide and 45 centimeters deep. Placing the sucker at this depth keeps it firmly anchored against strong winds while giving the young roots loosened soil to grow through.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni elɛɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 45 ni elɛɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 45. Kɛ́ okɛ vacuum lɛ wo nɛkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni emɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ mli shiŋŋ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ hu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my crops as soon as floodwaters drain off my field?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nu afua lɛ ho kɛjɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli pɛ?

english: Yes, once standing water recedes and the land is no longer waterlogged, the remaining damp soil provides ideal moisture and trapped nutrients for young suckers and seeds to establish quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni nu ni damɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni nu ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ haa fɛ̃i ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui adalɛ oya.

english: Can I use treated pipe-borne water to water my crop nursery?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu atsɔ paipii ni atsa nɔ lɛ anɔ aha miŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhe lɛ nu?

english: Yes, pipe-borne water is clean and safe for crops. If possible, let it sit in an open container for a few hours before watering so any chlorine used in treatment can evaporate.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛ paipii tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli tse ni ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ ebaahi lɛ, ha ehi tsɛnsi ko ni agbele naa mli ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi dani okɛ nu awo mli. Bɔni afee ni chlorine ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ helatsamɔ mli lɛ atsɔ la.

english: Why is it bad for me to delay planting after I finish clearing my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mafo dumɔ mli beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Delaying gives weeds the chance to grow back first and steal nutrients. Planting immediately allows your crops to establish their canopy before weeds can compete with them.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ be to he lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta dani jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛ yeɔ akaŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough moisture for planting without flooding the crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ ni nu shwieee miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Pick up a handful of topsoil and squeeze it into a ball. If it holds its shape without dripping water or crumbling into dry dust, the soil has the right moisture for planting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni okɛmimɔ mli ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi loo efolɔɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ sũ ni egbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young banana plant turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-banana tso bibioo lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is holding too much water around the roots or the plant lacks nitrogen. Ensuring good land drainage and adding compost around the base will help it recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. loo tsei bɛ nitrogen Kwɛmɔ ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛbɔle he. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua bo ni oná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How many months will it take for my newly planted banana sucker to produce fruit?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ ni mi sucker banana ni midu ehee lɛ woɔ yibii?

english: Banana suckers usually take between 9 to 12 months to flower, and another 3 to 4 months for the fruit bunch to fully mature for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, banana ŋmeii lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, kɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How can I protect my new banana suckers from insects hiding in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu banana tsei heei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Clean the bottom of the sucker with a sharp cutlass to peel away dead roots and dark spots where pests hide before placing it in the soil, or dip the base in hot water briefly to kill insect eggs.
ga: Kɛ tsɔne ni mli wa atsumɔ suction cup lɛ shishi. Koni ajie shishifãi ni egboi kɛ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ dani akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo okɛ shishitoo lɛ awo nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli be kukuoo ko. koni akɛgbe kooloi bibii lɛ afɔfɔi

english: Why are my crops wilting even when I water them with water from the nearby river near the mining site?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ ni bɛŋkɛ he ni atsaa shika tsuru lɛ yɛ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Illegal mining (galamsey) pollutes river water with heavy metals and chemicals like mercury and mud, which poison the plant roots and stop them from taking in clean water and nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mla eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ (galamsey) lɛ kɛ dade ni tsii kɛ tsofai tamɔ mercury kɛ muji woɔ faa mli nu lɛ mli muji, ni no haa tsei shishifãi lɛ yeɔ awui ni ehaaa amɛná nu ni mli tse kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why is it so hard to grow crops on land that was previously used for galamsey?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa waa akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ galamsey tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Illegal mining strips away the rich topsoil where nutrients live and leaves behind compacted, chemical-laden subsoil that roots cannot easily penetrate or get food from.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni ajieɔ yɛ mla naa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii mli nibii yɔɔ mli lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni tsofai eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni eshiɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli loo amɛná niyenii mlɛo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for too long, allowing soil fungus to attack the waterlogged roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when it gets extremely hot or when they lack sufficient water, as a way to save energy and protect the main plant.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite ni abu tomato tsei ahe.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees or plantains around my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains yɛ he lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under harsh direct sunlight, so larger plants provide vital shade and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow, weak roots and top-heavy fruit stalks, making them easily unrooted unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai tsei ni tsii. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ shishi, ja akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo tsei kakadaji anɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight and stay off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and produces bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni okɛ ohe akabɔ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ foliar helai anaa ni ehaa bulbs wuji baa.

english: Why did my crops dry up and die after I placed fertilizer right against their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is strong and extracts moisture out of the plant roots if placed too close, causing root burn; it should always be placed a few inches away in moist soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa ni ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ akɛ amɛ ato he ko ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi be fɛɛ be.

english: Is sandy soil good for planting coconut trees on my farm?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Coconut trees can grow and do reasonably well in sandy soil because their roots adapt easily to it. However, because sandy soil holds fewer nutrients than rich black soil, the trees may not grow as strong or produce as heavily without extra fertilizer.
ga: Kokoo tsei baanyɛ adara ni amɛshwere yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Shi, akɛni shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli fe shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ hewɔ lɛ, Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei kroko fataaa he lɛ, ekolɛ tso lɛ edaŋ waa loo ewoŋ yibii babaoo tamɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crops planted in sandy soil seem weaker than those grown in darker, richer soils?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ ni nii yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large particles that allow water and plant nutrients to drain away quickly. Because the plants receive less steady food and water, their overall growth and strength are lower compared to crops in better soils.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii bibii wuji ni haa nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii lɛ hoɔ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náaa niyenii kɛ nu daa. No hewɔ lɛ, dalɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Will my coconut trees produce fewer fruits if I plant them in sandy soil instead of rich soil?
ga: Ani mi ŋmei tso lɛ baawo yibii fioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni baa nii?

english: Yes, crops in sandy soil often yield less because the soil lacks the high nutrient levels found in rich dark soil. You can boost yields in sandy soil by regularly adding manure or compost.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo fioo ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni edɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ oya hiɛ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni okɛbaafata he daa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if a piece of land on my farm is suitable for growing coconuts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmeii akwɛmɔ?

english: Coconuts are hardy crops that can grow in places where many other crops struggle, including sandy coastal areas and low-lying swampy lands with plenty of sunlight.
ga: Kokoo ji tsei ni wa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ, ni ŋshɔnaa hei ni ŋã yɔɔ kɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni hulu babaoo yɔɔ lɛ fata he.

english: Why does fertilizer seem to wash away so quickly when I apply it to sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ oya kɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has wide gaps between its grains, so when heavy rain falls, it washes the fertilizer deep underground past the plant roots before the crop has time to absorb it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ babaoo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ tsei ashishifãi anɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔɔ.

english: What simple step can I take to help my crops grow stronger if my farm land is mostly sandy?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo mafee koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ji ŋã babaoo?

english: Mixing organic matter like cow manure, poultry droppings, or decayed leaves into sandy soil helps it hold onto water and nutrients longer, giving your crops a better food supply.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ tsina ŋmei, kooloi ŋmei, loo baai ni egboi futu ŋã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Ha otsei lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do plants dry out so fast in sandy soil even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Sandy soil cannot store water well because moisture drains right through it. Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps trap moisture in the soil.
ga: Shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Can I plant coconut trees in swampy or waterlogged areas of my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ hei ni ŋmeii loo nu afua yɔɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, coconut trees can tolerate very wet and swampy conditions quite well compared to many other crops, making waterlogged areas a good option for planting them.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsei baanyɛ adamɔ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe. Enɛ haa hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ feɔ hei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Which crops can survive in parts of my farm that stay wet and swampy most of the year?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ afi lɛ mli babaoo lɛ amli?

english: Crops like rice, sugarcane, cocoyam (taro), and coconut trees handle wet soils well because their root systems are adapted to survive high water levels that would rot other plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kookoo (taro) kɛ ŋmãa tsei tsuɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ nu ni fa babaoo ni kulɛ tsei krokomɛi baafite lɛ mli.

english: How do coconut tree roots manage to survive in wet, swampy ground without rotting?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tso shishifãi hiɔ shi yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ni amɛgbooo?

english: Coconut trees have tough, fibrous root systems that spread out broadly rather than going deep, allowing them to anchor securely and extract nutrients even in waterlogged soils.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa he ko ni da moŋ fe ni eeebote mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei tso lɛ ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ehe jogbaŋŋ ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ po mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves keep turning yellow even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni mikɛ nu haa daa gbi?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Just like people grow weak without food, crops turn pale when the soil lacks nutrients, which you can fix by adding organic manure or the right fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Taakɛ bɔ ni gbɔmɛi gbɔjɔɔ kɛ niyenii bɛ amɛhe lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to put fertilizer on my farm if my land used to grow crops well in the past?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they pull nutrients out of the ground and take them away. Over time, the soil becomes empty and tired, so you must feed the soil again with fertilizer or compost to get good harvests.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛyaa. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ efolo ni etɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni ená yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and thin without producing big corncobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach the sun instead of using that energy to make big, full corncobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛshɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ jamɛ a he wami ɔ kɛ pee ngmɔ tso ngua ko.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small and thin even when the leaves on top look green and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard, the cassava plant spends all its energy making leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below. Cassava needs loose soil and balanced nutrients so the roots can expand.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ wa tsɔ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ niyenii ni ja he miihia cassava koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Why do the fruit bunches on my plantain trees stay small compared to other farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ faaa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain trees grow small shoots called suckers around their base. If you leave too many suckers growing around one mother tree, they steal her food and water, causing all the plantain bunches to remain small.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ suckers ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛji oshi suckers babaoo obɔle, nyɛ kome tso Ebaaju eniyenii kɛ enu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ aniji fɛɛ ji bibii lolo.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. During intense heat, the tomato plant curls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping it hold onto its water so it doesn't dry out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baafo amɛbaai lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa amɛgbi.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to strong direct sunlight and hot winds. Leaving large shade trees or planting plantains beside young cocoa creates a canopy that protects the young crops until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How can too much rainfall cause my crops to wilt and die?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ aha midumɔ nii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi?

english: When soil stays completely flooded with water, it pushes out all the air roots need to breathe. Without air, the roots rot and stop working, causing the plant to wilt and die from lack of water and food even in a wet field.
ga: Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛmu lɛ kɛjeɔ kpo. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaakpa nitsumɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni bɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ po amli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, poor soil moisture, or severe nutrient shortage. The plant drops its flowers to save its own life when conditions are too tough to support fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa waa Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛhere amɛhe kɛji shihilɛi lɛ bafee nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive tough conditions and aggressively steal water, light, and nutrients from the soil. Because food crops are weaker, weeds will quickly starve them if you do not clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ hewɔ lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye jwɛi oya kɛji ojieee amɛ oya.

english: This usually means your soil is low on nitrogen. The maize plant moves nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa ni miida lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does spreading dried animal manure on my vegetable bed help my crops survive short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure adds organic matter to the soil, which acts like a sponge. It holds water in the root zone much longer than plain soil and slowly releases natural nutrients as plants grow.
ga: Manure kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ daa lɛ, ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fiofio. Be ni tsei lɛ daraa

english: Why do small caterpillars keep chewing holes right inside the center leaf fold of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the center fold (the whorl) where leaves are tender to feed on young growth, which can destroy the plant's growing point if not treated early.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms, amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei (crease), ni ji he ni baai bibii yeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why does the purple-flowered Striga weed keep appearing and killing crops in my field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo ni egbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔji amli daa afi lɛ?

english: Striga, or witchweed, attaches its roots directly to crops like maize or sorghum to steal water and food. Its seeds stay alive in low-fertility soil for many years, so improving soil nutrients helps weaken it.
ga: Striga loo Witchweed lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he tɛ̃ɛ. koni eju nu kɛ niyenii Edumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔji ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ afii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni aaaha ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects like midges to pollinate them, along with steady water and soil nutrients. Extreme dry weather, lack of shade, or insect pests can prevent flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii koni amɛfee pollination, kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atsĩ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop during hot afternoons even when I watered the farm in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛfeee nakai moŋ? Namɔ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi?

english: In intense afternoon sun, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can pull it up. Drooping is the plant's natural response to shrink leaf exposure to the sun and conserve water.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Defoliation ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hetoo kɛha baai ni shwieɔ shi ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ kɛ nu ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or when soil moisture fluctuates too much, causing the bottom cells of the developing fruit to die.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ shishi lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and watery if I leave them in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rains start, mature cassava plants use up the starch stored in their tubers to grow new branches and leaves, turning the thick starch into water and fiber.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Cassava tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ starch ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo niji kɛ baai heei. Tsɔmɔmɔ starch ni mli edɔ lɛ owo nu kɛ fiber mli.

english: Why do my cowpeas make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the roots decompose, that natural nitrogen fertilizes the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to heap up soil around the base of my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua muji naa kɛbɔle he lɛ? Sweet potato tsei lɛ ashishitoo be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: Yam tubers expand underground and need soft, shaded soil to grow big. Heaping protects the developing tubers from direct sunlight, which can burn them or turn them green and bitter.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ amli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ he hiaa koni amɛdara. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã loo eha ŋmeii lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa seedlings in the nursery are healthy enough to move to the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy seedlings have dark green leaves, sturdy stems, and no spots or mold on their foliage. They should be around 3 to 6 months old with strong root systems before you transplant them into the field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli diŋŋ, tsei ni wa, ni baa he tsɔi loo ŋmei bɛ amɛhe. Esa akɛ amɛye aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi waa dani okɛ amɛ awo saatso lɛ nɔ.

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet and humid conditions. You can prevent it by clearing tall weeds, pruning extra leaves to let sunlight in, and removing infected pods early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai krokomɛi koni hulu la babaoo abote mli. ni ojie pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra branches and dead shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei ni egboi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cutting extra or damaged branches lets air and sunlight flow through the tree canopy. This stops moisture build-up that causes fungal diseases and helps the tree focus its energy on growing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni efite lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ kpaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are some of my young cocoa fruits turning shriveled and dark before they reach full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo yibii bibii lɛ ekomɛi miigbo ni amɛmiifee duŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop small pods—a process called cherelle wilt—when they are stressed by drought, lack nutrients, or produce more fruit than the tree can naturally feed.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii, ni ji nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt, kɛ́ hɔmɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo amɛwo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ hao amɛ.

english: How can I tell if insects are damaging my cocoa pods while they are growing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kooloi bibii miifite mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Insects like mirids cause small, dark, sunken spots on the pod skin and young shoots. Over time, these spots dry out, crack, and can cause the pods to deform or die.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mirids kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Su ni mli edɔ ni ebote mli yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ, pods kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ hei nɛɛ baagbi, amɛbaagbala ni ebaanyɛ eha pod lɛ afite loo egbo.

english: Look at the pod color. Ripe pods change color completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvest them as soon as they reach full color so they do not overripe or rot.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɔɔ ha. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji loo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Kpaa kɛji amɛhe ewo kɔla fɛɛ pɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ fe nine loo amɛkafite.

english: Should I remove bad or infected pods from the tree even if I cannot sell them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni ehiii loo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ moŋ?

english: Yes, always pluck off and destroy diseased or rotten pods. Leaving bad pods on the tree allows fungal spores to spread to nearby healthy pods and remain in your farm for the next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo amɛfite lɛ be fɛɛ be ni akpata amɛhiɛ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii gbohii yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli ni amɛhi oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning light green or yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are waterlogged from poor drainage. Adding organic compost or appropriate fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the large shade trees grow too big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ be mli ni cacao tsei wuji lɛ daraa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need balanced sunlight to produce the energy required for flowering and pod development. Too much shade keeps the farm dark and damp, which lowers yields and encourages disease growth.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni sa koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ. Shade babaoo baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee duŋ ni edɔ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni ehaa helai yaa hiɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny insects called midges for pollination. If the soil lacks moist leaf mulch where midges live, or if harsh sprays clear them out, flowers will drop without turning into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi hiɔ nɔ, Aloo kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa ha amɛlaaje. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight burns their sensitive leaves and dries out soil moisture before their root systems are strong enough to handle full heat.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ latsaa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I cut down extra shoots growing around my main plantain stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow causes them to compete for soil nutrients and water, which results in smaller plantain bunches. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures maximum fruit yield.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants developing tiny holes with small caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmei bibioo ko yɔɔ mli?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the fall armyworm, which hide inside the plant leaves and eat them, reducing the crop's ability to make food and produce full ears of corn.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms. ni kɛ ehe teeɔ tsei ahe baai amli ni eyeɔ amɛ Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tsei yɔɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes the cassava plant to direct its energy into growing upper leaves and stems rather than storing food reserves in the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ yaa baai ni miida kɛ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the leaves into the air so they can absorb full sunlight for growth and keeps them off damp soil, which prevents leaf rotting during heavy rain.
ga: Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛdara. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkwɛɛɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat causes heat stress in the plant, making the pollen inside tomato flowers sterile so the blossoms drop off before fruit setting can occur.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Ehaa pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ woɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and turning crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, preventing the plant from growing healthy leaves and producing good pepper yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ baa curling lɛ eshwaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ baai ni mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa aba.

english: When soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves its limited nutrients from older bottom leaves up to feed the growing top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni fa fioo kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: The early season's first rain is often followed by a short dry spell, which can dry out the upper soil and kill seeds that have just started to sprout.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi ni ekpata dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make the land better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops have natural roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural food supply for the next crop.
ga: Legumes yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: What is the difference between the seeds I save from my harvest and certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ateŋ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor over time, resulting in lower yields and higher disease risk, whereas certified seeds are specially bred by research institutions to grow uniformly, resist pests, and produce larger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi, ni helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ji nɔ ni niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei fɔɔ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara daa lɛ. Enyɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo

english: What is a foundation seed, and why can't I buy it directly to plant on my regular farm?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwu shishitoo? Ni mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahe lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Foundation seeds are pure, high-quality seeds produced by agricultural researchers. They are intended for licensed seed growers to multiply into larger quantities (certified seeds), rather than for direct grain production on regular farms.
ga: Primer dumɔwui ji dumɔwui krɔŋŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi feɔ. Afee aha dumɔwui akwɛlɔi ni yɔɔ gbɛŋmɛɛ wolo lɛ koni amɛdu babaoo. (dumɔwui ni awo he odase) yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaawo dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ daa lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ

english: Where do new crop varieties in Ghana come from before they hit the market?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jɛɔ dani amɛyaa jara nɔ?

english: Government agricultural research institutions develop new crop varieties first. Once tested and proven, these initial seeds are multiplied and passed to certified private seed producers to sell to farmers.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei lɛ baafee ŋmɔshi nibii heei klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji aka akwɛ ni ana akɛ eji anɔkwale lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, afeɔ shishijee dumɔwui nɛɛ babaoo ni akɛhaa aŋkroaŋkroi ni feɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛha okwaafoi.

english: Where can I get reliable, approved seeds for my farm so I don't buy fake ones from the market?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni akpɛlɛ nɔ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni mahe dumɔwui amalei kɛjɛ jara nɔ.

english: You can buy certified seeds from registered agro-dealers, local agricultural extension offices, or recognized seed producer associations that display official seed inspector certification tags.
ga: Obaanyɛ ohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Kuu ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ loo dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔi akuu ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ ni jieɔ dumɔwui akwɛlɔ he odaseyeli wolo ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ kpo.

english: Why do new crop varieties yield much more harvest than the traditional ones my father planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe shishijee ŋmeii ni mitsɛ du lɛ?

english: New crop varieties are developed by scientists to better absorb soil nutrients, withstand common local pests, and thrive in Ghana's changing climate, allowing them to produce more food on the same amount of land.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi efee tsei srɔtoi heei. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. ni amɛshwere yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei nɛɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ he ko ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize grow tall but produce very small cobs when I re-use seeds from last year's improved harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ kpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Improved or hybrid crops lose their special high-yielding qualities after the first generation. Planting seeds saved from a hybrid harvest leads to weaker plants and poor yields in the second season.
ga: Tsei ni atsake amɛ loo tsei ni afee amɛ ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ waa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni ji hybrid mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu aba shi yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature faster than others planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daraa oya fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred with different genetic lifespans. Early-maturing varieties are specifically designed to grow and produce quickly before short rainy seasons end.
ga: Afɔ tsei srɔtoi ni wala be sɔrɔtoi yɛ amɛmli lɛ. Afee tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Why do my crops get attacked by diseases even when I clear and weed my land properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi jogbaŋŋ ni mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Clearing land removes weeds, but many crop diseases are carried inside poor-quality or uncertified seeds. Using disease-free certified seeds prevents infections from starting inside the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ jɛmɛ. Shi afuu tsei ahe helai babaoo yɛ dumɔwui ni ehiii loo ni bɛ he odaseyeli mli. Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni atsɔɔ akɛ hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaje shishi yɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: How do agricultural scientists create crop seeds that survive long dry spells in Ghana?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi fee dumɔwui ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Researchers select naturally resilient parent plants that use less water, cross-breed them over several seasons, and test them in dry regions until they produce a stable seed variety that withstands drought.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi hala tsei ni ji nyɛmɛi ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi, ni kɛ nu fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii. Krɔsbreed yɛ bei babaoo mli ni aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ hei ni nu bɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi hɔmɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for farmers in my community to plant the same improved seed variety?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ baadu dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the same improved variety ensures your crops mature at the same time, prevents cross-pollination from inferior varieties, and makes it easier to combine your harvest to sell to large buyers for higher prices.
ga: Kɛ́ odu tso ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ be kome mli. Tsi crossbreeding ni jɛɔ kooloi ni baa shi lɛ amli lɛ naa. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ akɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baafata he koni akɛhɔ̃ɔ aha mɛi ni heɔ nibii babaoo lɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how can it help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A greenhouse is a covered structure that protects crops from harsh rainfall, intense heat, and pests. It creates a stable environment so your plants can grow healthy regardless of bad weather outside.
ga: Greenhouse ji nɔ ko ni aha nɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɛ kooloi awuiyelɔi ahe. Ehaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ baa bɔni afee ni otsei lɛ anyɛ adara waa ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ ji.

english: Is it possible for me to plant vegetables during the dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Yes, by growing crops inside a protected greenhouse or covered shed, you control the water supply yourself and can plant and harvest successfully at any time of the year, rain or shine.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ loo ŋmɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Bo diɛŋtsɛ obaanyɛ okudɔ nu jɛɛhe lɛ. ni abaanyɛ adu ni akpa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ loo hulu tsoɔ.

english: How does growing crops under a cover save me money on fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ ko nɔ lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mikɛ shika akato ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: In an open field, heavy rain washes away expensive fertilizers before plants can absorb them. Inside a greenhouse, water is controlled, so your fertilizers stay in the soil and feed the crops directly.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ dani tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ. Yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli Abaakudɔ nu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, o-fertilizer lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crops suffer or die whenever the rain falls at the wrong time of year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amanehulu loo amɛgboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni esaaa mli lɛ?

english: Traditional crops rely heavily on predictable rainfall patterns. When rains fail or come too heavily, plant roots either dry up or rot, which is why controlling moisture through covered farming protects your yield.
ga: Kusum nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ loo enɛ waa tsɔ lɛ Tse lɛ shishifãi baagbi loo amɛbaafite. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni hulutsoo be ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ onibii ahe lɛ.

english: What is the benefit of keeping young seedlings under a covered shed instead of open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei bibii ni akɛtoɔ tsũ ko ni aha nɔ ko shishi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ he?

english: A covered shed acts like a protective shield, preventing heavy rain droplets from damaging fragile young leaves and blocking harsh direct sunlight that can burn young seedlings.
ga: Greenhouses ni aha nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafite baai bibii ni waaa. ni etsĩ hulu la ni naa wa ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops get diseases more frequently during heavy rain periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ yeɔ helai shii abɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes soil onto plant leaves and keeps them wet for long periods, which allows fungi and diseases to spread rapidly. Keeping crops under cover keeps foliage dry and reduces disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo hulutsoo shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Why are my farming costs rising even though I am getting the same amount of crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okwaayeli he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ eyɛ mli akɛ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ moŋ?

english: Inputs like seeds, water, and chemicals are becoming more expensive. Using modern methods like greenhouse farming helps you produce higher yields in smaller spaces so you get better value for the money you spend.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ dumɔwui, nu kɛ tsofai miifee nɔ ni jara wa waa. Kɛ okɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi tamɔ greenhouse okwaayeli tsu nii lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo baa yɛ he bibioo ko. No hewɔ lɛ, onine shɛɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo nɔ kɛhaa oshika lɛ.

english: Why do vegetable prices go up so high in major market cities during certain months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe jara ni yɔɔ maŋtiasei wuji amli jarayeli hei To lɛ yaa hiɛ waa yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli lɛ?

english: Market prices rise in dry months because standard open-field farms cannot produce crops without rain. Farmers who harvest during these off-seasons using covered planting can sell at much higher profit margins.
ga: Jarayeli jara yaa hiɛ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ nyɛŋ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Okwaafoi ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa babaoo kwraa.

english: Why should I try new farming methods if my family has always farmed open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka okwaayeli gbɛ hee ko makwɛ? Akɛni miweku lɛ etsuɔ ​​okwaayeli yɛ ŋmɔji amli be fɛɛ be hewɔ lɛ?

english: Weather conditions and input costs have changed over time, making traditional methods riskier. Adopting newer techniques, even step-by-step, helps protect your farm from losses and improves your income.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ shihilɛ kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Feemɔ blema gbɛi lɛ Oshara babaoo yɛ. Gbɛi heei ni akɛtsuɔ nii Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baabu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ fitemɔ he ni eha oshika ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I start learning modern farming techniques if I do not have experience with them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabɔi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaai akasemɔ kɛji mibɛ niiashikpamɔ ko tsutsu?

english: Modern farming is a gradual learning process where you pick up practical skills over time. Extension officers and demonstration farms can show you simple ways to adopt new methods like greenhouse growing.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli ji nikasemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni yaa nɔ fiofio ni onine shɛɔ ŋaa ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nitsulɔi ni yaa hiɛ kɛ ŋmɔji ni akɛtsɔɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ bo gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Yɛ gbɛi heei tamɔ greenhouses ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow big and green. The plant is moving whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ agbo ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ miijie nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why should I not apply chemical fertilizer to my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Crops can only drink in plant food dissolved in soil moisture. Applying fertilizer to dry dirt means the crops cannot absorb it, and the concentrated fertilizer can actually burn and damage the roots.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ anu tsei niyenii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ mli nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade trees or temporary cover crops like plantains to act as natural umbrellas, protecting their leaves and keeping soil moisture stable until their roots get established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa amɛhe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ baai ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Staking lifts the vine off the damp ground, increasing sunlight exposure and preventing leaves from rotting due to soil-borne fungi.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains last for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain floods the soil without proper drainage, water displaces the air, causing the tubers to suffocate and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high temperatures or irregular watering. To protect itself from dying, the plant sheds flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Small shoots (suckers) steal water and food from the main plant. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii (tso lɛ) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ akɛ tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes split open on the plant after a sudden rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When a dry period is followed by sudden heavy water, the inside of the tomato grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, forcing the skin to crack open.
ga: Beni gbee ni tsii trukaa lɛ nyiɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ gbeleɔ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas have natural bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which helps feed neighboring crops like maize naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do wild weeds come back so much faster than my planted crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in the dirt for years waiting for light. Clearing the land exposes those seeds to sunlight and warmth, causing them to germinate rapidly before your planted seeds catch up.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo ni amɛmiimɛ la Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa hulu la kɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya dani dumɔwui ni adu lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ he.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which helps it make food and grow strong, or that too much standing water around the roots is suffocating the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni efee niyenii ni eda waa. loo nu ni yɔɔ lolo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices, which causes the leaf to deform as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ mites loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Which way should I point the tiny buds when I plant cassava stems in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei tso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei bibii lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: The small bumps or buds on the cassava stem must point upwards toward the sky so the shoots can easily grow straight up into the sunlight.
ga: ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii Esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifã lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do I need to give my yam vines long wooden sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Sweet potato wain tsei ni miikwɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ hu?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food that travels down to build large tubers underground; climbing sticks lift the leaves off the wet soil into the sun and air.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Ivy woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Too many shoots steal water and plant food away from the main stem, so removing extra suckers ensures the main plant grows big, healthy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi babaoo juɔ nu kɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed, so the tree drops extra flowers to save its energy for only the pods it can successfully grow.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato fɔfɔi ni eye omanye lɛ pɛ anɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help my soil grow better maize next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that grab natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the dirt, acting like a natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps rainwater in the dirt so it doesn't dry out fast, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekagbi oya. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Is it better for me to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rain or after the rain stops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa loo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer after heavy rain stops while the soil is still moist, because a sudden heavy downpour will wash away your fertilizer before the plant roots can soak it in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baajie o-fertilizer lɛ dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do new seed varieties from research institutes like SARI give a bigger harvest than my traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei Kɛjɛ niiamlitaomɔ he ko tamɔ SARI lɛ, ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe mishishijee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Improved crop varieties are specially bred by scientists to resist local pests, fight off common diseases, and use soil nutrients more effectively, which allows them to produce more food than older, unselected seeds.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi ekwɛ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Awuu helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni etsɛ ni ahalaaa lɛ.

english: If I buy an improved seed variety this season, can I save some of the harvested grain to plant next year?
ga: Kɛji mihe dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Ani manyɛ makɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi ato koni madu afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is better to buy fresh seed each season. Improved seeds lose their special yield power and resistance after the first harvest, meaning saved seeds will grow into weaker plants with smaller yields.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ laajeɔ yibiiwoo hewalɛ kroko kɛ shitee-kɛ-woo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baatsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni wooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are extension officers recommending short-duration crop varieties to us nowadays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ jieɔ tsei srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ ahe ŋaa amɛhaa wɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: Short-duration varieties mature quickly in fewer days. They help you get a good harvest even when the rainy season is short or unpredictable due to changing weather patterns.
ga: Be kukuoo mli henɔi lɛ daa oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa anáa yibii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa loo anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ lɛ po.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like tubes during hot sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the crop's natural way of saving water. By hiding part of the leaf surface from the hot sun, the plant reduces water loss until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ nɔ fã ko ni ekɛteeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Tsei baaha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when rain water stands on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe. When water covers the ground for too long, the roots starve for air and cannot absorb nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crop plants fight each other for light, water, and food. They spend all their energy growing tall to search for sunlight instead of growing thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛdara ni amɛtao hulu la moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ tsei ni mli ewo wu kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers drop off the plant before forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiifee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop off when tiny insect pests like thrips attack the buds, or when the plant suffers from extreme heat. Treating the farm for flower-eating pests at the right time helps pods form properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua fɔfɔi lɛ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ana kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the purple-flowered witchweed, or Striga, cause my crops to dry up even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ witch grass loo striga ni yɔɔ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches its roots directly to your crop's roots. It steals the water and plant food straight out of your crop, causing the plant to starve and dry up.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa tsei ashishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do insects destroy my stored maize grains in the barn even when the ears felt dry during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni miifite ŋmãa ni ato yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ toi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli po.

english: Grains can look dry on the outside while still holding internal moisture, or they may already contain tiny pest eggs from the field. Drying grains properly on clean tarpaulins before storage prevents insects from multiplying.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmaa lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni egbi yɛ kponɔgbɛ, shi ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Aloo ekolɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii komɛi yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejɛ ŋmɔ mli momo Dumɔwui ni agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ dani akɛto lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi bibii akafee babaoo.

english: How do I know if a crop variety being talked about by other farmers will perform well on my own soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ ko ni okwaafonyo kroko wieɔ he lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Varieties proven by local research institutes are tested across different soil zones in Ghana. You can ask your extension officer if the variety matches your specific area's soil and rainfall levels.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni maŋ lɛ mli niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ hei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ anɔ. Obaanyɛ obi o-extension officer lɛ kɛji akɛ srɔtoi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for growing green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the ground too soaked for roots to breathe.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nitrogen. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei shwereɔ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up tightly like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves usually curl up when tiny unseen insects like thrips or mites are sucking the juice from under the leaves, or because the plant is trying to protect itself from extreme sun and heat.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kooloi bibii ahiɛ. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai ashishi Aloo akɛni tsei miitao ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he hewɔ lɛ?

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of lush green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich compost, they put all their energy into growing big leaves instead of making flowers and pods. High heat during flowering can also cause flowers to drop.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ fɔfɔi afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers before they turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo dani amɛbatsɔ cacao ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed. The tree drops extra flowers to save energy for a small number of pods, but excessive flower drop can also mean the ground is too dry or there are not enough beneficial insects around to pollinate them.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi ashwie shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ato fɔfɔi lɛ ahe. Shi fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ babaoo lɛ hu baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why does my main plantain tree stop producing big bunches when many small shoots grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain titri lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii wuji feemɔ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: The small shoots—called suckers—are like extra mouths feeding from the same soil and root system. They steal food, water, and sunlight from the main mother plant, which reduces the size of the plantain bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Etamɔ daaŋ krɛdɛɛ ko ni yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shishifãi kome mli. Amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ titri lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni plantains akuu lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make energy. Climbing up stakes keeps the leaves exposed to light and off the wet ground, which prevents leaf rots and helps the underground tubers grow much bigger.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ la mli ni amɛjeɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekafite, ni ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara babaoo.

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the fruit, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil gets very dry and then very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baagbi waa, ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to dig up if the tubers are hidden deep in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ etee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ?

english: Cassava lets you know it is ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack open as the tubers expand beneath.
ga: Yucca haa oleɔ akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni eshiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants fall flat on the ground right when the grains start filling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛbɔi dumɔwui ayimɔ lɛ?

english: This is called lodging. It happens when stems become too tall and weak from too much chemical fertilizer or when plants are crowded too close together, making them easily blown over by rain and wind once the heavy grain heads form.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ wɔɔhe. Ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ tsɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ hewɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Enɛ haa nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ oya kɛ́ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii ba.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow better in the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket that shades the earth. It stops the hot sun from drying out water in the soil, keeps root zones cool, and prevents weeds from stealing crop food.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaju ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore healthy green leaves and bigger cob sizes.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even though the leafy tops are growing very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ? Yɛ baa lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ, ebɔi agbojee diɛŋtsɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of expanding its swollen roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ shishifãi ni efuu yɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it harmful if I apply fertilizer right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater washes away the topsoil fertilizer before plant roots can drink it up, wasting your money and leaving the crops unfed.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Eji shika fitemɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there are no trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse plants like plantains to retain moisture and survive their first years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I plant seeds very close to each other to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛ he akafite lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too tightly together, their roots fight over water and nutrients while their leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in thin, weak plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the middle of hot dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural self-defense habit where the plant reduces its surface area to stop water from evaporating too quickly in hot weather.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli su ko ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Tsei lɛ baa amɛhe shi koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I snap off the small side branches growing at the joints of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Removing those extra side branches, called suckers, forces the plant to send its food energy directly into making larger fruits rather than extra leaves.
ga: Nakai niji krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ lɛ shoo lɛ ni ajieɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ eniyenii hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ koni ekɛfee aduawai wuji. yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases to build up in that field year after year.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do aggressive weeds grow so much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with strong root systems that absorb available water, fertilizer, and sunlight much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa ni ŋmɛɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains rot quickly when I store them in bags straight after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui amli beni mikpa ŋmaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain still contains internal moisture that creates mold and attracts pests when sealed in bags; sun-drying the grain thoroughly before storage prevents spoilage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ mli ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ dani akɛtoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛfiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a living canopy that protects the young trees from heat and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together is a effective practice. Maize grows rapidly and can be harvested in about three months, leaving space and nutrients for the slower-growing cassava to expand later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nifeemɔ ko ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ niyenii haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa sɛɛ mli.
