english: Why do the foreign hybrid maize seeds give a bigger harvest than the seeds I saved from my previous crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred in laboratories to withstand local pests and weather while maximizing yield. Saved seeds lose their strength and consistency over generations, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tips usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the key nutrient responsible for healthy green leaf growth, and crops show deficiency symptoms when soil nutrients are depleted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ daa. Ni tsei lɛ baajie nɔ ni he ehiaaa amɛ lɛ he okadii akpo kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ etee.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when we experience too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ wɔna nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain causes waterlogging in heavy soils, which prevents air from reaching the roots. Without air, root tissues decay rapidly and become vulnerable to soil fungi that cause rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ amli fãji lɛ fiteɔ oya ni sũ mli ŋmeii ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves of my cowpea plants to curl up and get covered in a sticky substance?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cowpea baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni nɔ ko ni shwieɔ shi miiha amɛhe?

english: This damage is caused by tiny insects called aphids that suck sap from the plant. As they feed, they excrete a sweet, sticky liquid called honeydew, which can attract mold and weaken the crop.
ga: Kooloi bibii kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ amɛ aphids, ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ Amɛjieɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi. Atsɛɔ nakai nu lɛ akɛ nu ni ŋɔɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmeii ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small yields when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants compete against each other for limited resources like sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to weak stems and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nibii fioo tamɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkpaa nii fioo.

english: Why do my mango trees drop most of their flowers before any fruit begins to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani eyibii lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers due to stress such as sudden dry spells, insect damage, or fungal diseases. Strong winds or lack of pollinating insects can also prevent flowers from turning into fruit.
ga: Mango tsei gbeeɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni baa trukaa, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii loo tsɛŋemɔ hela hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi lɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I nurse my pepper seeds in a seedbed before transferring them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ mi-nursery lɛ mli dani mikɛya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are small and delicate; nursing them allows you to protect the young seedlings from harsh weather and pests until they develop strong roots for the main field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Tsɔsemɔ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa kɛha ŋmɔ titri lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my yams under the ground are mature enough to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Yam tubers reach full maturity when the leaves and vines on top of the ground naturally turn yellow and dry up, signaling that the plant has stopped growing and stored its food.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ kɛ niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save yam tubers or seeds from my last harvest to plant for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato ŋmeii loo dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved year after year accumulate diseases and lose their strength, leading to smaller harvests. Buying clean planting material from official channels ensures you get healthy, high-yielding crops that resist pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ buaa helai anaa ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo. Nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni he tse ni ooohe kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni amralo lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: Where can I get clean, disease-free planting material for my farm in Ghana?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana nibii ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: You should buy certified seeds and planting materials through official channels, such as accredited seed dealers, agricultural extension offices, or recognized research institutions like the CSIR-Crops Research Institute.
ga: Esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ kɛ dumɔ nibii kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni amralo lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ajalɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ anɔ. Okwaayeli He Nitsumɔhe loo niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ tamɔ CSIR Nibii Amli Nibii Amlipɛimɔ Nitsumɔhe.

english: Why are certified seeds from official dealers more expensive than seeds sold in the local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aŋmala he odaseyeli kɛjɛ mɛi ni jaa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ jara wa fe dumɔwui ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Certified seeds undergo strict inspection, disease screening, and quality testing by agricultural experts to guarantee high germination and strong yields, whereas market seeds may carry hidden pests or poor growth traits.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ, akwɛɔ mli kɛji helai bɛ mli, ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi kaa bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ekolɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo amɛdalɛ sui ni ehiii.

english: What is the difference between foundation seed and the regular seed I plant to produce food for the market?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ shishijee dumɔwui kɛ daa dumɔwui ni miduɔ koni maná niyenii kɛha jara lɛ teŋ?

english: Foundation seed is a high-purity, elite seed produced directly by plant breeders to grow certified seed. Commercial seed is what regular farmers buy to grow crops intended for eating or selling at the market.
ga: Shishijee dumɔwui ji dumɔwui ni he tse waa ni tsei akwɛlɔi feɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkɛdu dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ. Jarayeli dumɔwui ji nɔ ni okwaafoi fɔɔ hemɔ koni amɛkɛdu tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: How do vine cuttings grow into full crops without using traditional seeds?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni wain tso ni afo lɛ atsɔ tso ni yeɔ emuu ni akɛ blema dumɔwui tsuuu nii?

english: Crops like sweet potatoes and certain yams have special buds on their stems. When healthy vine cuttings are placed in moist soil, these buds sprout roots and leaves, forming an entirely new plant identical to the parent.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ yams komɛi yɛ fɔfɔii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ akɛ wain tso niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baakwɛ shishifãi kɛ baai. Etsɔɔ tso hee tamɔ tsutsu tso lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to cut vines from my crop to use as planting material?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mafolɔ wain tsei kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔ nii?

english: Vines should be cut when the parent plant is young, strong, and showing no signs of disease—usually a few months after planting—so the cuttings have enough energy to root quickly in the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ afo wain tso lɛ be mli ni nyɛ tso lɛ ji gbekɛ, ehe wa ni hela he okadi ko bɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tsei niji lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo shishifãi oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How can diseases transfer to my new field if I use stem cuttings from my old crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momo mli lɛ tsu nii?

english: Microscopic pests, viruses, and fungi live inside the plant sap of infected stems. If you cut and plant an infected vine, you directly transfer that disease into your new field and soil.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, kɛ ŋmeii hiɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Kɛji ofo wain tso ni hela emɔ lɛ ni odu Obaajie nakai hela lɛ kɛya oŋmɔji kɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can I use leaves to start a new crop, or do I always need stems or tubers?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ baai lɛ aje ŋmɔshi nibii hee shishi? Aloo ani tso loo tuber he miihia mi be fɛɛ be?

english: Leaves alone usually cannot sprout roots and develop into full plants. Most root and tuber crops require stem cuttings (vines) or tubers that contain specialized growth nodes or 'eyes' to start new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ pɛ nyɛɛɛ ashishifãi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tso ni yeɔ emuu. Tuber kɛ shishifãi babaoo biɔ ni afo tso lɛ yitso (wain tso) loo tuber ni yɔɔ dalɛ he ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi loo ‘buds’ koni ekɛje dalɛ hee shishi.

english: What does it mean if I become an out-grower for a commercial seed producer?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ miji mɔ ko ni duɔ nii yɛ he kroko kɛha jarayeli dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔ ko?

english: As an out-grower, you contract with a seed company or institution to grow specialized crops like foundation seeds on your land following their strict guidelines, and they buy the harvest back from you.
ga: Ákɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛlɔ ni yɔɔ kpokpaa lɛ sɛɛ Okɛ dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhe loo nitsumɔhe ko feɔ kpaŋmɔ koni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi, tamɔ shishijee dumɔwui, yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli wa lɛ anaa. Ni amɛbaahe nibii ni amɛdu lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ odɛŋ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted even though the green vines on top look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni efite eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow underground and need loose, well-prepared soil or high mounds to expand smoothly. Hard soil or underground pests like nematodes will deform the tubers even if the upper vines look green.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ebiɔ sũ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli moŋ,.

english: Why do my rubber trees shed all their leaves at a specific time of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔba tso lɛ baa fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Rubber trees drop their leaves naturally during the dry season to conserve water. During this time, the tree uses its stored energy to grow new leaves rather than producing rubber sap.
ga: Rɔba tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ baajie nu lɛ, ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai heei.

english: Is there a specific month when I should stop tapping my rubber trees to let them rest?
ga: Ani nyɔji komɛi yɛ ni esa akɛ makpa mi-gum tso lɛ tswaa koni maha lɛ hejɔɔmɔ?

english: Yes, farmers usually stop tapping around March when the trees shed their leaves. This gives the trees a necessary rest period until April, when new green leaves have fully grown back.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kpaɔ tsei lɛ tswaa yɛ March be mli beni tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hejɔɔmɔ ko ni he hiaa waa kɛyashi April. Enɛ ji be mli ni baai eŋɔli heei lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How do I know when my rubber trees are ready to be tapped again after their rest period?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-rɔba tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaatswa ekoŋŋ beni mihe ejɔ mi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: You can safely start tapping again when the tree has refoliated with mature, dark green leaves, which normally occurs around April.
ga: Obaanyɛ oje tso lɛ he tsɔne lɛ shishi ekoŋŋ shweshweeshwe kɛji tso lɛ kɛ baai ni egbɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ efee ekome. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April afi lɛ mli.

english: Why does the rubber sap from my trees sometimes become very thin and watery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni eyɛ nu lɛ?

english: Sap turns thin and watery when the tree is under stress, exhausted from continuous tapping, or tapped during its leaf-shedding period when it lacks the nutrients to make rich latex.
ga: Nu lɛ mli nu lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni efeɔ nu kɛji tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli. Egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli Loo ŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli beni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa efeɔ latɛs ni mli edɔ.

english: Will I get less sap if I tap my rubber trees while they are dropping their leaves?
ga: Ani maná nu fioo kɛji mita tso ko he beni egbeeɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yes, tapping during leaf shedding yields very low amounts of sap, and the little sap you get will usually be low-quality and watery because the tree is focusing its energy on leaf regrowth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ otswa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, ebaaha nu fioo ko pɛ aba. kɛ mliki fioo Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ehiii kwraa ni eyɛ nu ejaakɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I make a mistake and tap my rubber trees during their resting month?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mitɔmɔ ni mifo tso bibioo ko yɛ hejɔɔmɔ nyɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Tapping during the rest period causes severe stress to the tree, results in watery sap, damages the bark, and reduces the tree's ability to produce good sap in the upcoming season.
ga: Kɛ́ atswa tso lɛ yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tso lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nu baahi jɛmɛ. efiteɔ tso lɛ he tsɔi ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee latɛs kpakpa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Can tapping my rubber trees continuously without giving them a break ruin my farm in the long run?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt tsei ni mikɛtswaa ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ baafite miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, tapping without a break permanently damages the tree's bark and exhausts its nutrients, which shortens the tree's lifespan and drastically lowers your future harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ afolɔ ni akumɔɔɔ lɛ, ebaafite tso lɛ yibii lɛ kwraa. ni efiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Enɛ baaha tso lɛ wala afee kuku. ni ebaa nitsumɔ ni obaafee wɔsɛɛ lɛ shi waa.

english: Why is it important to balance taking sap from the tree with protecting its leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni anáa kɛ baai lɛ ahe ni abuɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves act as the food factory for the tree. If you over-tap the tree when it needs its energy to build leaves, you destroy the factory that creates the rubber sap in the first place.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe. Kɛji ota tso lɛ he tsɔ beni ehe hiaa hewalɛ ni ekɛfee baai lɛ, Obaakpãtã nitsumɔhe ni fee latex lɛ hiɛ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ.

english: How do the green leaves on a tree help in producing thick rubber sap?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ latɛs feemɔ mli?

english: Green leaves use sunlight to make food for the tree. This food is converted into latex; without healthy foliage, the tree cannot produce thick, high-quality sap.
ga: Baai eŋɔli kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Atsakeɔ niyenii nɛɛ afeeɔ latɛs. Kɛji baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie nu ni mli edɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many months in a year can I continuously tap my rubber trees before they need a rest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ yɛ afi mli ni manyɛ matswa rɔbɔt tso ko be fɛɛ be dani ehe baahia ni ejɔɔ ehe?

english: You can tap continuously for about eleven months—from April through to February of the following year—before taking a one-month break during leaf shedding in March.
ga: Obaanyɛ otswa nɔ daa aaafee nyɔji 11, kɛjɛ April kɛyashi February yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. dani ekɛ nyɔŋ kome hejɔɔmɔ yɛ March fɛ̃i be lɛ mli.

english: Why does my farm yield smaller harvests now than it did five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops remove food (nutrients) from the soil every time they grow. If you keep planting on the same piece of land without adding manure, fertilizer, or letting the land rest, the soil gets tired and hungry, so crops cannot grow as big as before.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii (nutrients) kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni aduɔ amɛ. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ fataaa he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa tamɔ tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I clear my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil for a long time. Once you clear the land and the rain falls, weeds sprout quickly because they are wild plants adapted to survival, and they rush to steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your crops can grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ojie he ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ejaakɛ amɛji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi. Ni amɛkɛ oyaiyeli yajuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why is my maize growing very tall and thin with small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When you plant maize seeds too close together, the young plants have to stretch up very high to fight each other for sunlight. Instead of building thick stems and large cobs, they waste all their energy trying to reach the light.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Esa akɛ tsei bibii lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ waa koni amɛnyɛ amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi agbohi. Mohu ɔ, a puɛ a he wami tsuo kɛ bɔ mɔde kaa a maa su la a he.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize help or hurt my main crop?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awui?

english: It actually helps! Beans and cowpeas gather nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This acts like a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize and helps it grow stronger.
ga: Eyeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ! Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa o-ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni edaraa waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I cut down all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Shade trees act like big umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa ni enáa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch direct sunlight and avoid catching diseases from wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ he

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or when there are no small insects like bees to carry pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ni baanyɛ aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli.

english: Why are small worms eating the inner leaves inside the middle of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms. The parent moths lay eggs in the hidden central funnel of the plant, where the newly hatched worms can safely eat the tender green leaves out of sight.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms ji enɛɛmɛi. Nyɛmiyoo lɛ woɔ ewui yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli. Kplukai ni efɔ ehee lɛ baanyɛ aye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ shweshweeshwe ni mɔ ko mɔ ko enaaa amɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots soft and rotten underground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When rain falls heavily on land that does not drain well, water settles around the cassava roots for too long. The roots cannot breathe underwater, which causes them to rot and die in the soggy ground.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hei ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ Nu baakpɛtɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ nu shishi. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to plant my seeds as soon as the very first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry period. If you plant too early, your seeds will sprout, but without follow-up rains, the delicate seedlings will dry up and die in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees and plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ? Ni adu lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong heat and bright sunlight. They need partial shade from plantains or shade trees during their first few years to protect their leaves from burning and to keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Koni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning pale yellow starting from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient responsible for leaf greenness and growth. When nutrients run low, the plant steals food from older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ baai lɛ shweremɔ. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ eho lɛ Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava yields every season when I grow cassava in the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmei fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously in one plot drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt without giving the soil time to recover. It also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting beans in the same field with my maize make the maize grow greener and stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ewaa lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the dirt. This acts like natural fertilizer that helps neighboring heavy-feeding crops like maize grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains flood my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water covers the field for too long, it drowns the roots by cutting off air, allowing rot-causing bacteria in the soil to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ha he ko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Akɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my green pepper plants suddenly wilt and collapse during the daytime even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili tso ni ji eŋɔli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by soil bacteria that block the tiny water pipes inside the plant stems. Even though there is water in the ground, the blocked stems cannot carry that water up to the leaves, causing the leaves to dry up in the heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii bibii anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. tso ko shishi Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ Shi tso lɛ shishifã ni etsi lɛ nyɛŋ atere nakai nu lɛ kɛya baai lɛ anɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ kɛji akɛ amɛwo la mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers but then the blossoms drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant sheds flowers to conserve its energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide inside the rolled center leaves of my young corn plants instead of feeding on the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaye kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm prefer the soft inner funnel of the corn plant because it provides tender young leaves to eat and shields them from scorching heat, heavy rain, and natural predators.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa tsei amli gbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa baai bibii lɛ naa nɔ ko ni amɛyeɔ, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout out of the ground when I bury them deep in the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni mifuɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A seed has only a small store of food energy inside it. If planted too deep, the shoot runs out of energy trying to push through the thick soil before it reaches the surface to catch the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko toɔ amɛmli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Hewalɛ ni ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut long wooden poles to support my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei kakadaji koni mikɛfi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward light. Holding the stems high on stakes lifts the leaves into full sunlight, allowing the plant to make maximum energy to feed and swell the underground yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ wo tso ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo kɛha niyenii ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each maize plant enough space and food to produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Dropping leaves during hot, dry weather is a natural survival trick cassava uses to conserve water. The plant is not dead; it is saving its energy and protecting the roots underground until rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni yucca kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when temperatures get extremely hot or when watering is irregular. Heat prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to drop its blossoms instead of setting fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yaa hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Wrinkled and curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of new leaves. Using approved organic or chemical pest control protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai heei ni eda lɛ ahe.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually reduce my harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ haa mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds steal vital food, fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass and leaves around the stems of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai shwieɔ amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ? Kpɔ̃ɔ tso?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, prevents weed growth, and enriches the soil as it decays.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for big tubers. Lifting vines off the wet ground also protects leaves from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii wuji lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why does lowland rice need to stay flooded with water during its growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni nu awo ŋmãa folo mli yɛ edalɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice is adapted to grow in standing water, which keeps its roots continuously moist and naturally suffocates most weeds that would otherwise crowd the crop.
ga: Atsake ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ koni akɛdu yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli. Enɛ haa eshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa jwɛi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi, ni baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crop yields keep getting smaller every year even when I put in the same amount of hard work on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tamɔ tsutsu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously on the same piece of land drains essential nutrients from the soil over time. Without adding compost, manure, or rotating crops, the exhausted soil cannot support healthy crop growth, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ tsuuu nii. Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara. Enɛ haa anáa kpamɔ bibioo.

english: Why does resting my land without planting anything for a season help crops grow better later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ ni aduuu nɔ ko yɛ be ko mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Resting the land, or fallowing, allows natural wild plants to grow, die, and decompose. This process returns organic matter and vital nutrients back into the soil, restoring its strength for future crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ, loo fallow lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli koo mli tsei daa, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛfiteɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my maize plants dry up and die even when we get short showers of rain during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi eyɛ mli akɛ wɔnine shɛ nugbɔ fioo nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Light or irregular rain evaporates quickly from hot bare soil before crop roots can absorb it. Covering the soil around plants with dried grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps moisture longer for the roots to use.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo loo ni baaa shi daa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni shishifãi lɛ kɛtsu nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Which crops can I plant if the heat in my region is increasing and the rains no longer come at the usual times?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ be ni afeɔ daa lɛ mli?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like sorghum, millet, cowpeas, or early-maturing cassava varieties handle heat better and require less water, making them safer choices when rainy seasons become unpredictable.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, tsina loo ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa babaoo ni amɛbiɔ nu fioo. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe be mli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow, curling up, and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Curled kɛ bibioo?

english: Yellow, curled leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings provided by agricultural officers prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ni hiɛɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ du ŋmei niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: What is eating strange holes in the middle of my young corn leaves and stopping them from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ni miitsi enaa koni ekakwɛ̃?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking your field early and applying recommended biological controls or neem oil sprays early in the morning can protect the young plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ he loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu tsei bibii ahe.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the land where I harvested my maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing and enriching the soil with nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize need for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa kooloi ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop plants grow tall and thin with small fruits when I sow many seeds close together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and nutrition to grow strong and produce large fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster and stronger than my food crops right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miniyenii tsei lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that naturally absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domestic crops. Clearing weeds early within the first few weeks stops them from stealing the food and water your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ enɛ baatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and get damaged by insects so quickly after I put them in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ amɛ oya beni mikɛwo kotokui amli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil when stored while still damp or in standard woven bags where insects and moisture can easily enter. Thoroughly drying grains in the sun and using sealed, airtight (hermetic) storage bags keeps insects out and stops mold from growing.
ga: Ŋmãa fiteɔ kɛ akɛto be mli ni edɔ lolo loo awo mama kotokui ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ mli he ni kooloi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ abote mli mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la mli ni akɛ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli ni atsĩ naa (vacuum) tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my crops growing much slower nowadays compared to how crops grew on this same land during my grandfather's time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa ŋmɛnɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ minaa beaŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Over years of continuous farming without rest, the soil loses its natural nutrients. Modern farming uses soil testing and targeted organic or chemical fertilizers to restore those missing nutrients so crops can grow strong and fast again.
ga: Afii babaoo ni akɛyaa nɔ atsuɔ okwaayeli he nii ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛku sɛɛ akɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ada waa ni amɛdara oya ekoŋŋ.

english: How does adding fertilizer actually make my maize plants grow taller and produce larger cobs?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa mi-abɛi tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji?

english: Fertilizers feed plants essential elements like nitrogen and phosphorus, which act like rich food for crops, helping them build strong stems, healthy leaves, and bigger cobs.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tso niyenii ni jara wa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi, baai ni wa, kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the leafy bush on top grows very big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ dara ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of underground tubers. Modern nutrient management helps balance the plant so it focuses on growing big roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai anɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ekome, no hewɔ lɛ amaa shishifãi wuji ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ mi.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and wilt so quickly when the rain stops for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya ni egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops get stressed when soil loses surface moisture quickly in hot weather. Modern techniques like mulching—covering the bare soil around plants with dry grass—keep the root area moist and cool during dry spells.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ fo oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tamɔ mulching—ni ji sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli. Tsei ni jwɛi ni egbi yɔɔ mli lɛ—haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe jɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do insects attack and ruin my vegetables more during the hot dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry heat stresses crops, making them weaker and less able to defend themselves, while warm weather makes pests reproduce much faster. Spacing crops properly and early watering help plants stay strong against pests.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efã ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ oya kwraa. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhe waa kɛshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die from the bottom leaves going up, even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This is usually caused by crop diseases in the soil that enter the plant's roots and block water from traveling up the stem. Rotating tomatoes with crops like corn stops these soil diseases from building up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni boteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekaho kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ nɔ kɛ enɛ baa. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small knots after the plant starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe bibii bibii lɛ? Beni tso lɛ ebɔi fɔmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that damage young leaves and transmit viruses. Extension officers recommend early spraying or using insect-resistant seed varieties.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni fiteɔ baai bibii ni ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baa Extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afɔ dumɔwui ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ anɔ loo akɛtsu nii mra.

english: Why do crops planted in neat, measured rows give me a better yield than scattering seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni akɛ niji shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Planting in straight, spaced rows gives every single plant equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors, while making weeding and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ awuu yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ŋmɔmɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How does using a tractor to plow deep into the soil help my crop roots grow better than digging by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ni akɛ nine shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Tractors break up hard, compacted soil deep below the surface, allowing crop roots to penetrate deeper into the ground to find hidden water and stay anchored during heavy winds.
ga: Traktɔi lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do improved seed varieties from the agriculture office give more harvest than the seeds I save from my last crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ wo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred by scientists specifically to withstand local diseases, handle hot weather, and turn soil nutrients into food much more efficiently than old saved seeds.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi fɔɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he nitsumɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakemɔ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui momo ni ato

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, or when heavy rain has washed nutrients away. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants drying up and turning brown at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under hot direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains planted nearby to act as living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist around them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ehaa ehe jɔɔ ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving your plants steady water and keeping the soil cool with mulch helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant juices, or by a virus carried by those insects. Clearing weeds around the farm and spraying organic pest controls can help protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe tee baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaayeli kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu tsei ahe.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants will fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This makes the stalks thin and weak, resulting in very small maize cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo kwraa.

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy, which travels down to make big, healthy yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Covering the ground with dry plant material, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps water from evaporating under the hot sun, keeps the soil cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ la yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy, poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps extra rainwater drain away quickly so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Weeds steal the plant food, water, and sunlight that your crops need to grow. Removing weeds early gives your crops all the resources they need to mature quickly and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaaha onibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my soil become weak and produce smaller harvests after planting the same crop on it every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ewooo yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season consumes the exact same nutrients from the soil until nothing is left. Rotating your crops—like planting beans or groundnuts after maize—puts good nutrients back into the dirt and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ heɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko eshwɛɛɛ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha niyenii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: How do I know which crops buyers will actually want to buy before I spend money planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛhe dani mafite shika kɛdu amɛ?

english: Market demand changes based on seasons and harvest times. Checking with local market queens, agricultural extension officers, or farm cooperatives before planting helps you pick crops that will be scarce and valuable at harvest time.
ga: Jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be naa. Kɛji okɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ nuŋtsɔ lɛ miikwɛ Agricultural Extension Officer Loo ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔhe ko ni feɔ ekome dani aduɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafee nɔ ni anaaa ni jara wa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are specially tested to produce stronger plants that resist diseases and handle dry weather better. Seeds saved from past harvests lose their vigor over time, leading to smaller yields and higher crop failure.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ akwɛɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛná tsei ni he wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hu fiteɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and dying even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or pests like fall armyworms are attacking the base of the plant. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or applying safe pesticides early can save the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etutuaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Enyɛɔ ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: How can I protect my cassava and vegetable crops from being destroyed by pests before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cassava kɛ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite amɛ dani akpa?

english: Protecting crops requires catching pests early. You can clear surrounding weeds where insects breed, rotate your crops each season to break pest life cycles, and spray approved organic or chemical treatments when you see early signs of damage.
ga: Nibii ni abuɔ he lɛ biɔ ni amɔmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai mra. Obaanyɛ ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. He ni kooloi baanyɛ afɔ́ yɛ Tsakemɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa be mli koni okɛfo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli. Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai tsuɔ he nii ni aŋmala he odaseyeli awo mli lɛ awo mli kɛ́ ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ nɔ ko efite mra.

english: What can I do to keep my harvested maize from getting eaten by insects while in storage?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe be mli ni miyɔɔ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp grains. You must dry your maize thoroughly in the sun until it is hard before storing it in sealed, airtight storage bags (like PICS bags) or treating it with recommended grain preservation powder.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛwo ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) loo okɛ powda ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year when I plant on the same field without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth every time they grow. If you keep planting without adding organic manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes depleted, causing crop yield to drop year after year.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛji odu ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ aba shi afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer right when I plant the seed or wait until the crop sprouts?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu loo mamɛ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Seeds carry their own initial energy to sprout, so applying heavy fertilizer at planting can burn young roots. It is best to apply fertilizer a few weeks after sprouting when the plant has active roots ready to feed.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishijee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii wo mli beni aduɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni tso lɛ eshishifãi efee klalo akɛ ebaaye niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do crops like maize grow better when I plant beans alongside them on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. This natural food feeds neighboring crops like maize, helping them grow stronger without extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my seeds when the rains are unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Avoid planting after the very first rain, as a dry spell usually follows. Wait until the soil receives two to three steady rains to ensure enough deep soil moisture, or use drought-tolerant seed varieties.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ shii 2-3 ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa. Aloo okɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni baanyɛ adamɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ atsu nii.

english: How can I keep soil moist for my plants when the hot sun is drying up my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha mitsei lɛ beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass, straw, or leaves (a practice called mulching) blocks direct heat from the sun, trapping soil moisture longer and keeping root zones cool.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai (nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching) aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi hulutsoo ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry weather to save water and protect the tubers growing underground. Once the rains start again, the stem will sprout fresh leaves and keep growing.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Koni akɛ nu akafite ni abu bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my tomato leaves start curling upward even when I don't see any insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Ni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi?

english: Tomato leaves often curl as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss during intense heat and hot dry winds, but it can also be a sign of a virus spread by tiny, hard-to-see insects like whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. Shi ebaanyɛ efee hela ko ni koolooi bibii ni anaa waa tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi hu.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpaa ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer that restores soil nutrients for heavy-feeding crops like maize in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How does planting my crops in rows across a slope stop my topsoil from washing away when it rains hard?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ koni ekaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Planting across a slope creates natural barriers that slow down running rainwater, giving the water time to soak into the soil instead of carrying your fertile soil into nearby rivers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ fioo. Enɛ haa be ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ kɛya faa ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Pepper flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil gets too dry or waterlogged, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen fertilizer fa babaoo Ha tsei lɛ aná baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my maize ears have many empty spaces with missing kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ amli ŋmeii babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when hot, dry winds dry out the corn silks before pollination can finish, or when the soil lacks enough nitrogen while the cob is forming.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baa naagbee. aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow thin and crooked instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɔleɔ shi moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yam tubers grow thin or twisted when planted in hard, stony, or shallow soil that prevents the tuber from expanding easily, or when the planting mounds are not made high and soft enough.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɔ, ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. aloo be mli ni gɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ebɛ blɛoo bɔ ni sa

english: Why does my plantain tree produce small bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ tso lɛ he hu?

english: Leaving too many suckers attached to one mother tree forces them to compete for the same food, water, and sunlight, which weakens the main tree and leads to smaller bunches.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔlɔ kome he lɛ. Enɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ niji bibii baa.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable farm early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane mli?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the soil absorbs moisture before the heat of the day, and so the leaves can dry quickly in the sun to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli adɔ nakai gbi lɛ. kɛ koni aha baai lɛ agbi oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce fewer fruit bunches after a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ miiwo aduawai fioo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni eho lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees need a constant supply of water to develop female flowers that turn into fruit. During severe dry weather, the tree produces mostly male flowers or sheds young fruit to save itself.
ga: Nu he miihia oil palm tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfɔfɔi yei lɛ afee aduawai. Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ mli Tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii loo aduawai bibii babaoo koni ekɛkwɛ ehe.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow green and strong, or that the ground is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally fertilizes the ground for your corn and improves soil health.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the crops are actively growing—usually two to three weeks after sprouting—and when the soil is moist so the roots can absorb the nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tso lɛ miida lɛ—bei pii lɛ, otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ—kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks next to my yam plants when they start sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam is a vine plant that naturally climbs; lifting its leaves up on sticks helps them catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food, resulting in bigger and healthier tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli amɛyaa ŋwɛi. Amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Groundnuts flower above ground, but after pollination, the plant naturally extends stems called 'pegs' into the soil so the actual groundnuts can develop safely underground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhaa ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients during the critical flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ hao yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the rainy season to fully settle in the North East Region before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ agbe naa yɛ Bokagbɛ dani odu dumɔwui?

english: Sowing seeds after just one early rain is risky because if a dry spell follows, the newly germinated seeds will dry up and die before the main rains return.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛji hɔmɔ ko nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: How can I tell which part of the cassava stem is best to cut and plant in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafolɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Choose mature, healthy stems from the middle section of the cassava plant, and plant them with the small bud nodes facing upward toward the sky so they sprout properly.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni mli wa, ni eda kɛjɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli. ni adu kɛ ŋmeii bibii Tsɔɔmɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the fresh center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer feeding on the soft, inner leaves of young corn; identifying them early allows you to treat them before they destroy the crop's main growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli. Amɛyoomɔ mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ otsa amɛ dani amɛfite hei titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do farmers cover the ground around their crops with dry grass during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa he ni amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the earth cool, traps moisture so you water less often, and prevents weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo oŋmɔji lɛ amli fioo ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow from the tip downwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and build big cobs, so when the soil runs out of it, the plant pulls nutrients from its lower leaves to feed newer growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ etee Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do people tell me to plant beans or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. Planting them alongside maize naturally adds food to the soil, helping your maize grow stronger without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abele masɛi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why are there small holes and brown dirt inside the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm that crawl into the central leaves of young maize plants to eat the soft parts, leaving behind tiny holes and dark waste.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ su diŋŋ ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much water for too long. Poorly drained or soggy soil starves the roots of air and invites fungal diseases that cause the tubers to spoil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo ni efɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aye shishifãi lɛ ahe hɔmɔ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa tuber rot baa lɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Shade trees protect them from harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist while the cocoa seedlings build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa baa.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in hot weather to hide from the harsh sun and stop water from evaporating out of their leaves. Once the afternoon heat cools down, the leaves usually flatten back out.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni amɛtsi nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ naa. Kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ ba shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass on the soil around my vegetables help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the earth quickly, keeps roots cool, and slows down weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking the vines off the ground lets the leaves make energy efficiently, which produces bigger tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ feɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce small and weak leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee baai bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil food, groundwater, and sunlight from your main crop. When crops have to fight weeds for survival, they end up hungry and produce small yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli lɛ. Be mli ni esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi awuu koni amɛhi shi Hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo pɛ.

english: How do I know if my harvested maize is dry enough to store safely without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe ni efiteee?

english: You can test maize by biting a grain or using a sealed glass jar with dry salt; if the salt stays dry and does not stick to the glass, your maize is dry enough to store without developing mold or attracting pests.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmãa lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni oooŋmɔ loo glase tsinsii ni akɛ ŋoo ni egbi ewo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ egbi lolo ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa glase lɛ he lɛ, Abɛi lɛ baagbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto ni ŋmei loo ŋmeii ni baa lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Is it better to dry my harvested crops directly on the ground or on a raised platform?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ magbi mikpamɔ nii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ kpoku ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ?

english: Drying crops on a raised platform or clean tarpaulin keeps them away from ground moisture, dirt, and farm animals, allowing airflow underneath so the crops dry faster and stay clean.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni agbiɔ yɛ kpoku ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo tarp ni he tse nɔ lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, muji kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ahe. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shishi. Koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi oya ni amɛhe atse.

english: Why do some varieties of maize take three months to harvest while others take four months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi heɔ nyɔji etɛ dani akpaa ŋmãa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii komɛi heɔ nyɔji ejwɛ dani amɛkpaa nii lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred for different seasons; early-maturing varieties grow quickly so you can harvest before a short rainy season ends, while late-maturing varieties take longer but usually produce bigger yields if there is steady rain.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛha bei srɔtoi. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ daa oya. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa amɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ aba naagbee, yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo. Shi amɛfɔɔ yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ daa.

english: How many days after planting my grain seeds should I expect to see sprouts coming out of the soil?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu dumɔwui lɛ esa akɛ mana dumɔwui ni miije kpo kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?
