english: Most grain seeds like maize or sorghum sprout within four to seven days after planting, provided the soil has enough moisture and warmth.
ga: Nibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa, kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii ejwɛ kɛyashi kpawo mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How does strong wind help or hurt my maize farm during the growing season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ mi ŋmãa awui yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: A gentle wind helps by carrying pollen between flowers to produce full cobs of grain, but very strong wind can knock down tall crops, so planting in rows that face away from major wind paths helps protect them.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ pollen lɛ yaa fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ koni ekɛ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ aba. Shi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa baanyɛ aha tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ agbee shi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli ni amɛkwɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ titri lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava plants easily fall over when strong winds blow through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants grow top-heavy with heavy stems and leaves, which makes them easy for wind to push over if their roots are shallow. Mounding soil around the base gives them stronger support.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ daa kɛ amɛhe tsei kɛ baai ni tsii. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baatsɔ mli kɛji eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Muji ni abua naa ni bɔleɔ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ haa yelikɛbuamɔ ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to sort out damaged or small cocoa beans from the good ones before taking them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbala kookoo ŋmeii ni efite loo bibii lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni hi lɛ amli dani mikɛwo jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Sorting removes flat, insect-damaged, or moldy beans so they do not spoil the taste and quality of the good beans, helping you get a higher market grade and better payment.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kplukai fitemɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni akafite ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa kɛ ekpakpafeemɔ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa jara nɔ grade ni nɔ kwɔ ni onáa nyɔmɔwoo kpakpai.

english: Why shouldn't I keep newly harvested wet crops inside closed plastic bags overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ ni akpa ehee lɛ toɔ plastic kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops trap moisture and heat inside closed bags, creating a hot, damp environment that causes mold to grow and rots the harvest within a few days.
ga: Tsei ni akpa ehee lɛ mɔɔ nu kɛ dɔlɛ yɛ kotokui ni aŋã mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni edɔ waa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii shwereɔ ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Crops curl their leaves during high afternoon heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve water so it does not dry out.
ga: Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from lack of water, extreme heat, or poor soil nutrients, as the plant tries to save energy rather than grow fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni faaa lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei miitao ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ aduawai.

english: Where do the new improved crop seeds I see on the market come from—were they created by scientists or are they natural seeds God created?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni tsei ahe dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni minaa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ jɛɔ—ani jeŋ nilelɔi ji mɛi ni bɔ loo amɛji adebɔɔ mli dumɔwui ni Nyɔŋmɔ bɔ?

english: New improved seeds come from natural seeds that agricultural scientists have carefully selected and cross-bred over many years. Scientists combine the best natural traits from different parent plants—such as strong stems or sweet fruit—to produce a stronger seed variety.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ jɛ adebɔɔ mli dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi ehala jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfo mli yɛ afii babaoo mli lɛ amli. Jeŋ nilelɔi kɛ adebɔɔ mli sui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni jɛ fɔlɔi tsei srɔtoi amli, tamɔ tsei ashishifãi ni wa loo aduawai ni ŋɔɔ lɛ fata he. koni ekɛfee dumɔwui ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Can crop seeds that were developed in foreign countries perform well on my farm here in Ghana?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni afee yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Foreign seeds can grow well if local conditions match where they came from, but many need to be adapted first. Local researchers test and adjust imported varieties so they can survive Ghana's specific soil, temperatures, and native pests.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ he ni amɛjɛ lɛ kpãa gbee. Shi ehe miihia ni atsake dumɔwui babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ. Kuu lɛ mli niiamlitaolɔi ka ŋmeii srɔtoi ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ lɛ amɛkwɛ ni amɛtsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ Ghana maŋ shikpɔji, hulutsoo be kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some types of crops grow very tall while other varieties of the same crop stay short on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different varieties have different built-in genetic traits. Short varieties are often bred intentionally so they do not fall over in strong winds, while taller varieties may be bred to produce more biomass or reach higher sunlight.
ga: Kooloi srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ sui srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, ajɛɔ yiŋtoo mli afɔɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ kukuji lɛ koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ afɔ henɔi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ koni amɛná biomass babaoo loo amɛná hulu la babaoo.

english: Why do plants grown from cassava stem cuttings look identical, while plants grown from seeds show so many differences?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ ŋmei mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ kome lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ yɛ srɔto kwraa lɛ?

english: Stem cuttings are direct clones of the mother plant, so they carry the exact same traits. Seeds are formed when pollen from one plant fertilizes another, mixing two parents' traits and creating variation among the offspring.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni afo lɛ ji tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he mfoniri tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyɛ sui kome pɛpɛɛpɛ. Dumɔwui baa kɛji tso kome mli muji lɛ kɛ tso kroko fee ekome. Kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi enyɔ asui ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ nɔ. kɛ tsakemɔ ni wɔbaafee wɔbii kɛ wɔnabii lɛ

english: Why do some crop varieties give me a heavy yield with many fruits, while my local crops yield very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo shi mimaŋ tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are bred to focus their energy mainly on producing fruit or grains rather than big leaves and stems. When given proper nutrients, these varieties naturally yield far more than traditional types.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ama aduawai loo ŋmaa feemɔ nɔ titri. Yɛ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ Kɛji akɛ onine shɛ niyenii ni sa nɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ woɔ yibii ni fa babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe blema ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Is it possible to find a maize variety that naturally gives birth to two or three large ears on a single stem?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ana ŋmãa henɔi ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ woɔ toi wuji enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ ŋmãa kome nɔ?

english: Yes, plant breeders have developed specific prolific maize varieties that naturally produce multiple healthy ears per plant, provided the soil has enough nutrients and water to support all the growing cobs.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ efee ŋmãa henɔi ni woɔ yibii titri ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ amɛwoɔ toi babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso kome mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii fɛɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: If I plant seeds saved from my best harvest, will all the new plants grow exactly the same way as the mother plant?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ Ani tsei heei fɛɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ nɔ?

english: Not always. If the mother plant was pollinated by different nearby plants, the saved seeds will contain mixed traits, meaning some offspring may grow shorter, yield less, or look different from the original plant.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be kɛji akɛ tso kroko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ woɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baaná sui ni efutu. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ seshibii komɛi baanyɛ adara ni amɛfee kuku. ewoɔ yibii fioo loo esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ shishijee tso lɛ he

english: Why do extension officers tell me to buy new hybrid seeds every planting season instead of planting seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mahe hybrid dumɔwui heei daa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ? Mohu ɔ, nyɛɛ du wuhi kɛ je nyagbe ní kpami be ɔ mi.

english: Hybrid seeds lose their special vigor and high-yielding qualities after the first generation. Saving and replanting hybrid seeds results in uneven plant growth, weaker crops, and much lower yields in the second season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ amɛdumɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ. ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature fast in just three months while my traditional seeds take much longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi daa oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mishishijee dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo lɛ?

english: Early-maturing varieties are specifically bred to complete their life cycle quickly. This helps farmers harvest successfully before dry seasons set in or squeeze two planting seasons into one year.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ omanye dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa loo amɛfoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ bei enyɔ mli kɛfeɔ afi kome.

english: Why are some crop varieties able to withstand pests and diseases while other varieties die easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi nyɛɛɛ helai kɛ kooloi bibii amɔ amɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi krokomɛi gboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Certain crop varieties have built-in natural defenses—like tougher skin, specific plant juices, or stronger immune systems—that stop local insects and diseases from easily attacking or damaging them.
ga: Dumɔwui komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ amɛhe, tamɔ hewolo ni mli wa. Nu ni tsei komɛi loo gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ ni he wa Enɛ haaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akatutua amɛ loo amɛfite amɛ mlɛo.

english: How long does a new cocoa tree take to start producing pods after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually take about 2 to 3 years to produce their first pods, while older traditional varieties take 4 to 5 years. Proper weeding, watering, and shade management help young cocoa trees mature faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 dani amɛfeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli, nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain or yam on the same land where I am establishing new cocoa?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo sweet potato. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ ni manyɛ madu kookoo hee yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting food crops like plantain or cocoyam with young cocoa is very beneficial. The food crops provide essential shade to protect young cocoa leaves from scorching sun while giving you food and income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo cocoa ni akɛ cocoa bibii duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Niyenii tsei haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa trees very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting trees too closely makes them compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The trees will grow tall and thin with few pods, and diseases will spread quickly between them due to poor airflow.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛmli ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: If I plant my whole farm with crops at once, will the land always yield well every year?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai daa afi?

english: Harvesting crops continuously removes nutrients from the ground. Without adding organic manure, compost, or fertilizers to feed the soil, the land will gradually produce lower yields over time.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi fiofio Yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and choking your young plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni amɛkamɔ odumɔwui lɛ.

english: Do old cocoa trees keep giving high yields forever, or do they stop producing?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kɛya naanɔ loo amɛbaakpa yibiiwoo?

english: Cocoa trees produce their best yields between 10 and 25 years of age. After 30 years, their production naturally declines, and they become more vulnerable to pests and diseases, meaning they may need to be cut back or replanted.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25. Yɛ afii 30 sɛɛ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara waa kɛha helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ ehe baahia ni afo lɛ loo adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my tree turning black and rotting before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, wet conditions. Pruning excessive tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods off the tree stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni afoɔ fe nine koni hulu lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ nɔ, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: My cocoa tree produces hundreds of small flowers, but most drop off without turning into pods. Why is this?
ga: Mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii ohai abɔ, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii. Mɛni he je nɛ e ba jã a?

english: It is natural for cocoa trees to shed many flowers because only a small percentage get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. However, extreme heat, lack of water, or insect damage can cause higher flower loss.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei baafɔ̃ babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Shi kɛlɛ, latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa drops leaves during hot, dry weather to conserve water and prevent the tree from drying out. Providing temporary shade trees and covering the soil around the stem with dry grass (mulching) helps keep the soil moist.
ga: Okɛ kookoo ni afee lɛ blɛoo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ egbi nɔ koni nu akafite ni tsei lɛ akagbi. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ha, ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some parts of my farm produce healthy, green crops while plants in other spots stay small and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ hei krokomɛi lɛ Amɛji bibii ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ.

english: Soil quality varies across the same piece of land. Areas with yellow, stunted crops may have poor drainage, compacted soil, or lack specific soil nutrients, which can be improved by adding animal manure or compost.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Hei ni tsei ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi bɛ mli. Abaanyɛ aha enɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have big leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, helping the young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I am planting cassava stems in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ atsɔɔ ŋmei tsei adumɔ mli?

english: The small buds on the cassava stem where leaves sprout should always point upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down makes it difficult for shoots to emerge and reduces your tuber yield.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ yucca tsei lɛ anɔ ni baai lɛ jɛɔ mli lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashishi lɛ, ehaa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃, ni ehaa tuber yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can trap sunlight to make food. Leaving vines to trail on hot ground increases disease risk and results in much smaller yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ ashi wain tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa helai baa, ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii bibii babaoo baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes in rotation helps keep the foliage green and supports full cob development.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen loo ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. Very high temperatures or sudden dry spells prevent proper pollination, causing the flowers to fall off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa pollination esaaa. ha fɔfɔii agbo

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding under the leaves. Spraying with neem oil solution or an appropriate insecticide protects the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni sa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi kooloi heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cabbage heads turn soft and rot when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, kaaba yitsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain creates stagnant moisture that allows rot-causing bacteria to enter the plant. Planting on raised mounds or ridges improves drainage and prevents water from pooling around the heads.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa, ni no haa helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ boteɔ tsei amli. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaaa nu lɛ abɔle yitso lɛ he.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer during the dry season or after the rains begin?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist right after rains begin. Crop roots need water to dissolve and absorb fertilizer nutrients, so applying it in dry soil is ineffective.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Nu he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛshwie shi ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in small root nodules. When the crop is harvested, the roots break down and leave natural nitrogen fertilizer in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Shishifãi lɛ fãa ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when grass and weeds are growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds actively compete with your crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early leaves all the available water and nutrients for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba koni onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside them creates a canopy that shields the delicate cocoa leaves and helps retain moisture in the soil until the trees mature.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo cassava lɛ ekome lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe lɛ baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes during hot afternoons is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss. Giving the plants a thorough watering at the root level early in the morning helps them stay hydrated and reduces leaf stress.
ga: Tomato baai ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛbuɔ nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishifã lɛ he leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ ahe haomɔ baa shi.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up while still hanging on the branch?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight flow through the farm, which keeps the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark powder inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei baai amli lɛ ni eshiɔ powda ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is typically caused by fall armyworms or stem borers. Applying recommended organic sprays or neem leaf extracts into the central leaves early in the morning can effectively kill the caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo stem borers ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli loo neem tso lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to get more crops from my small land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ mihe bibioo lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak plants with small yields. Proper spacing gives each crop room to grow strong and yield more harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsũ fɛɛ tsũ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds around my pepper plants while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Pepper tso lɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water and soil nutrients that your young pepper plants need to establish strong roots. Early weeding removes this competition, allowing your crop to grow faster and healthier.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa o-baby pepper tsei lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to erect wooden stakes for my yam vines as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei ato mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that require sunlight to produce large tubers underground. Lifting the vines onto stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight and keeps them away from damp ground where diseases can spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, hulu la babaoo shɛɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ anɔ, ni ehaaa efee he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã

english: How do I know if my soil is fertile enough before I plant my cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmei?

english: If your soil looks very pale or sandy, or if past crops grew slowly with weak stems, the soil is likely low in nutrients. Mixing in composted animal manure or organic matter before planting improves soil structure and nutrient levels for your cassava.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋã waa loo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo ni eyɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo mli dani odu lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli nibii kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ o-cassava lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: It is best to plant after two or three continuous, deep rains have thoroughly soaked the soil. Planting too early after just one light shower can cause seeds to dry out and fail to sprout.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni eha amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important to cut off dead or overcrowded branches from my older cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ aniji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing or diseased branches so the tree can direct its energy into growing healthy cocoa pods. It also allows sunlight to penetrate the canopy, keeping the farm dry and less prone to fungal diseases.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ hewalɛ lɛ ama kookoo ŋmɔji ni mli wa. Ehaa hulu la hu tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ nyɛɛɛ aba enɔ.

english: If I have a small plot of land near the city, what crops are best to plant for a fast harvest?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ maŋ lɛ, mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ madu koni makpa nii oya fe fɛɛ?

english: Short-season vegetables like hot peppers, tomatoes, and leafy greens (such as gboma or contour greens) are ideal for small land sizes because they mature quickly within 2 to 3 months and give high yields in tight spaces.
ga: Aduawai ni yeɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ ŋmeii, tomato, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai (tamɔ burdock loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai) lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei bibii ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hei ni ŋmeii yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yes, maize grows fast and is harvested within 3 to 4 months, while cassava grows more slowly and takes up to a year to mature, allowing both crops to share space and sunlight without crowding each other out.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa daa blɛoo ni ekɛ afi dani edaa. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ jaa he ko kɛ hulu la ni amɛtsiii amɛhe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to stay green and build strong stalks for a good harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná tsei ni wa koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the middle of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaves of maize plants and needs early treatment to prevent damage to the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji cutworm caterpillars, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ mra Koni akafite he ni edaa yɛ lɛ

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I crowd my seeds very close together?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: No, crowded plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and smaller fruit compared to plants given proper spacing.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Which crops are best to plant if I live in the city and can only check my farm occasionally?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ kɛji mihi maŋtiase mli ni manyɛ mayakwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ bei komɛi pɛ?

english: Hardy root crops like cassava or tree crops like cashew are ideal because once established, they tolerate dry spells and resist pests better than delicate leafy vegetables that require daily care.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli wa tamɔ ŋmei loo tso mli nibii tamɔ cashew nuts Ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ Amɛnyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ fe aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ daa gbi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot at the stem when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess rainwater sitting around the stems causes waterlogging, which suffocates plant roots and causes fungal disease; growing peppers on raised earth beds allows surplus water to drain away.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer at the exact same time I place seeds in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ be kome too mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: It is better to wait until the seeds germinate and form roots—usually 1 to 2 weeks after planting—so the young plant can actually absorb the nutrients rather than letting heavy rains wash the fertilizer away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtswa shishifãi (bei pii lɛ, otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ) koni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ,.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without making fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when plants suffer from stress due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus, which are necessary for blossoms to set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Officer, when is the main rainy season in southern Ghana, and when does it hit its highest point?
ga: Official Mɛɛ be ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ? Ni mɛɛ be ebaashɛ he ni eyɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: In southern Ghana, the major rainy season begins building up in April, continues through May, and reaches its peak in June, bringing the heaviest rainfall of the season.
ga: ghana kooyigbɛ Nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ April mli. Etee nɔ aahu kɛyashi May ni eshɛ eshishijee he yɛ June mli. ni kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fe fɛɛ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ baa

english: Why shouldn't I plant all my crops immediately when the very first rains fall in April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ yɛ April mli lɛ?

english: April rains are just the start of the season building up. Planting too early can cause seeds to dry out if a dry spell occurs before continuous rains set in during May and June.
ga: April nugbɔshiimɔ ji be lɛ shishijee kɛkɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ba dani nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ May kɛ June mli.

english: Is it better to plant my crops in May or wait until June when the rains are at their peak?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu nii yɛ May mli loo aaamɛ kɛyashi June be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Planting in May allows young crops to establish strong roots during moderate rains so they can fully absorb and tolerate the heavier peak rains in June.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ May mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni wa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ eŋɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ June mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni edamɔ shi.

english: Why is the beginning of June usually so wet with frequent rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, June shishijee lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: The first 10 days of June represent the peak of the rainy season in southern Ghana, where weather patterns bring the most continuous and concentrated rainfall.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ gbii 10 yɛ June mli lɛ damɔ shi kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana wuoyigbɛ. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɛɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni naa wa fe fɛɛ baa.

english: What does it mean for my crops when June rains come on and off instead of pouring continuously?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ June mli yɛ faa ni hoɔ daa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: On-and-off rain gives crops essential moisture while allowing sunlight and air to reach the soil between showers, which prevents roots from rotting in stagnant water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ojuɔ ohe lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Can heavy peak rains during June damage my young seedlings?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ June mli lɛ baanyɛ afite mi dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yes, intense June downpours can wash away topsoil or submerge young plants, so building raised mounds or drainage paths is important to protect them.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ June mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ loo ekɛ tsei bibii awo nu shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ama gɔji ni awó nɔ loo nu homɔ gbɛi koni akɛbu amɛhe.

english: What should I do if the early rains in April and May start later than expected?
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ April kɛ May shishijee gbɛ lɛ je shishi sɛɛ fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: If early rains are delayed, delay your planting or apply mulch to conserve soil moisture so seeds do not germinate only to wither before the heavy June rains arrive.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ mra lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafite. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbo dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ June mli lɛ aba.

english: How should I prepare my land before the peak rains in June arrive?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa yɛ June mli?

english: You should clear drainage channels and build ridges on your field so heavy June rainwater flows off smoothly without washing away your valuable topsoil.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni ofee ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ koni June nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ oshikpɔŋ ni jara wa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akafɔ.

english: How does the gradual increase in rain from April to June affect my soil?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fiofio kɛjɛɔ April kɛyashi June. Te enáa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The lighter early rains in April and May gradually soften and soak dry soil, preparing it to absorb maximum water deep down when heavy June rains arrive.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ April kɛ May shishijee be lɛ mli lɛ baa shi fiofio. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa edɔɔ. Koni esaa ehe koni ekɛ nu awo mli bɔ ni eeenyɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ June mli lɛ.

english: Which crops grow best during the major rainy period from April through June?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ April kɛyashi June?

english: Crops like maize, cassava, and leafy vegetables grow very well because they benefit from the steady build-up of water starting in April through the peak moisture in June.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa ejaakɛ amɛnáa nu ni yaa nɔ abua naa kɛjɛɔ April mli kɛyashiɔ hulutsoo be ni fe fɛɛ yɛ June mli lɛ he sɛɛ.

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a natural defense mechanism to reduce surface exposure to the sun and conserve moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide broad leaves that create living shade and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni wala yɔɔ mli baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed leaves during dry weather to stop water from evaporating through the foliage, allowing the plant to survive on underground root reserves until rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛho. Enɛ haa tsei hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Does it mean my yam crop is dying if the leafy vines turn brown and dry up late in the year?
ga: Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ miigbo kɛji wain tso lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi yɛ afi lɛ naagbee?

english: No, late-season vine drying is a natural signal that the yam plant has finished feeding the underground tuber, indicating that the tuber is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Dabi, wein tsei lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ egbe eshishifãi lɛ niyenii naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when plants experience extreme heat stress or sudden dry spells, causing the plant to drop blossoms to protect its main stem.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa trukaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu eshishifã titri lɛ he.

english: How does planting cowpeas help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas work with natural soil bacteria to take nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ejie nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwo sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does my plantain stem produce so many small shoots around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally sprout shoots called suckers to propagate. Removing excess suckers allows the main plant to focus its energy on producing larger fruit bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ akɛ ŋmeii kɛha shweremɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai akui wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my rice stalks fall over flat on the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice stalks fall over (lodging) when they become top-heavy from heavy grain heads or when weak stems are caused by excess nitrogen fertilizer and strong winds.
ga: Omɔ tsei shwieɔ shi (jɔɔ amɛhe) kɛji tsei bibii ni mli tse je kpo kɛjɛ dumɔwui tsei ni tsii amli. Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ.

english: Why do groundnut flowers bloom above the ground but the nuts develop hidden under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ teemɔŋ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, special growing pegs push downward into the soil so the nuts can safely grow underground protected from sun and animals.
ga: Beni ashɛɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ashɛɔ Special planting pegs awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ kooloi ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or that the soil is waterlogged, which suffocates the roots. Adding well-composted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn dark green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn leaves have small holes with sticky, sawdust-like powder in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center (funnel) of the maize plant during the day and eats young leaves. Checking your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or wood ash inside the funnel helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei (cones) lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛtsu nii loo tso mli sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know which way is upside down when planting cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole bɔ ni aduɔ ŋmei niji ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small bumps (nodes) on the cassava stem where the old leaves grew. The small buds above those bumps should point upwards toward the sky; planting them upside down makes it difficult for the roots and leaves to sprout properly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii (nodes) ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ he ni baai ni egbɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa ewaa akɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on high poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food and grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground to prevent fungal diseases and ensures the plant catches enough sunlight to produce large yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi fungal hela naa. ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning black and rotting at the bottom before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Rotting at the bottom of green tomatoes is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil dries out repeatedly, preventing the plant from taking up calcium. Keeping the soil moisture steady with regular watering and mulching prevents this.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato eŋɔli shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi shii abɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsei akaŋɔ calcium Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking sap from the underside of the leaf, or from a plant virus carried by these insects. Spraying the plants with soap-water solution or neem oil helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ agbɛfalɔi lɛ amli Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing large leaves but failing to form a tight, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when the weather is too hot, when plants don't get enough direct sunlight, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer is applied late in growth. Planting during cooler periods and using balanced fertilizers encourages firm heads.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ atsɔ yitso nɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo be mli ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo woɔ amɛmli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ. Dumɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni bulb lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do flowers on my okra plants drop off without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi gumbo lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Okra flowers often fall off if there are not enough bees around to pollinate them, or if the soil experiences sudden changes from very dry to very wet. Avoiding chemical sprays during morning flowering allows bees to work and help form pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Roselle fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee amɛ ŋmeii lɛ bɛ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ okpa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ leebi fɔfɔi be mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their flowers without producing any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees drop flowers when exposed to excessive heat and full sunshine without enough moisture. Planting plantain trees alongside young cocoa provides living shade and humidity, helping the cocoa trees hold onto their flowers and form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ waa bɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe ni efeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: It is normal for older, bottom leaves on plantain trees to dry out as the plant matures. However, if many leaves dry up rapidly from the edges inward, the plant may need more water or could be affected by leaf spot disease, which requires clearing dead leaves to keep the field clean.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ baagbi be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gĩ oya kɛjɛ mligbɛ ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ, Ekolɛ nu babaoo he baahia tso lɛ loo baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ aná enɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni ajie baai ni egboi lɛ koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually show that the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for growth. This often happens when heavy rains wash plant food away or when the soil lacks organic nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ tsei aniyenii tee loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sheds its blossoms to conserve energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Leaf curling is a natural mechanism to reduce moisture loss. In intense heat, the plant rolls its leaves inward to shrink the surface area exposed to sunlight and trap moisture inside.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade with their broad leaves, keeping the soil moist and protecting the cocoa plants until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo baa kɛjɛɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: When planted too close, cassava roots compete fiercely for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures the roots have enough room and resources to swell into large tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu Cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛhaa nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deeply, if the soil lacks sufficient moisture, or if soil insects and birds destroy the seed before it germinates.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ bɔ ni sa loo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my tomato plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, and stops weeds from growing and taking nutrients away from your tomatoes.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ

english: Why does my farm soil become hard like concrete after it rains and then dries?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit beni nugbɔ enɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or manure. Mixing organic material into the soil keeps it loose and soft, allowing crop roots to breathe and water to sink in.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli futu sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha egbɔjɔ ni eha efee blɛoo. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni nu boteɔ mli.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil, resulting in lower yields over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the land with free fertilizer for the next crop planted there.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: I just cleared and cleaned all the natural bush off my land, so why is my soil drying out so quickly now?
ga: Etsɛko tsɔ ni mijie adebɔɔ mli tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mijie amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miiho oya amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Completely clearing all ground cover exposes the topsoil directly to harsh sunlight and strong winds. Leaving some tree cover or applying mulch helps retain soil moisture after clearing.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ kwraa lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Tsei ni ashiɔ ni akɛ nɔ ko shwieɔ nɔ loo akɛ nɔ ko woɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi beni ajie tsei lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can strong seasonal winds completely destroy my farm crops?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tswaa yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baanyɛ afite midumɔ nii lɛ kwraa?

english: While heavy winds can bend young plants, well-rooted crops usually withstand wind without total destruction, especially if you plant windbreak trees around your field.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa po baanyɛ aha tsei bibii akumɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa ni amɛfiteee kwraa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ odu tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my crops close to the banks of the Volta River?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ Volta Faa lɛ naa?

english: Farming near major rivers like the Volta is very beneficial because the soil is rich in nutrients and moisture, though you should choose crops that can tolerate moist soil.
ga: Okwaayeli ni bɛŋkɛɔ faai wuji tamɔ Volta lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ eyi mli obɔ. Shi esa akɛ ohala tsei ni baanyɛ akpɛlɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Should I be afraid that heavy rain and rising water levels will destroy my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashe gbeyei akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nu ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Rising water from heavy rains is generally not something to fear immediately, as it deposits rich nutrients onto the land and supplies needed moisture, provided the water drains off within a few days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa mli baa lɛ jeee nɔ ko ni esa akɛ ashe gbeyei amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ ekɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni he hiaa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nu lɛ baaho yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why do crops planted near big water bodies seem to produce better yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni aduɔ yɛ nui wuji ahe lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Big water bodies like rivers continuously supply moisture to the surrounding soil and deposit fertile silt, which naturally feeds the crops throughout the growing season.
ga: Nui wuji tamɔ faai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ebua ŋmeii ni fa babaoo ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ anaa

english: How do I stop my farm soil from washing away when heavy rain falls near the river?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekaho kɛji nugbɔ miinɛ waa yɛ faa ko masɛi?

english: Leaving a strip of natural vegetation or trees along the water's edge holds the soil in place with deep roots, preventing erosion when water levels rise.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsei loo tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ nu lɛ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ ŋshɔkei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa kɛji nu lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: How does strong wind affect my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Strong winds can strip leaves of moisture and push over weak plants, but healthy plants with strong stem development usually flex with the wind and recover quickly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli ni ekɛtsi tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anɔ. Shi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkoto yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhe wa oya.

english: If I clean my farm properly, will that protect my crops from harsh weather?
ga: Kɛji mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Ani ebaabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe?

english: Proper clearing removes competing weeds, allowing your crops to grow stronger roots that better withstand heavy rains, wind, and dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ. Ehaa onibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo bei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do if heavy rains cause water to overflow into my crop field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ho yɛ miŋmɔji amli?

english: Do not panic, as short-term water rises can nourish the soil; simply ensure you have small drainage channels to let excess water flow back toward the river gradually.
ga: Kaaha ohe miiwo bo gbeyei, ejaakɛ nu ni yaa hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Kwɛmɔ pɛ akɛ oyɛ gbɛ bibioo ko ni nu tsɔɔ mli koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ aku sɛɛ aya faa lɛ mli fiofio.

english: Why do my crops look stressed after a heavy downpour even though they received plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiifee basaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛná nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Too much standing water temporarily cuts off oxygen to the roots, but as the water recedes, the roots breathe again and use the fresh soil moisture to thrive.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi kɛ́ nu lɛ ba shi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baamu ekoŋŋ ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hee lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃.

english: Covering the ground, which is called mulching, keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating into the air quickly under the sun. It acts like a protective blanket that holds moisture in the ground longer for your crops to drink.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ koni efee nɔ ni onuɔ kɛhaa onibii.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when rainwater sits on my farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need both air and water to stay alive. When heavy water sits on the field without draining, it fills up all the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots because they cannot get oxygen.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu fɛɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu babaoo hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: Why do my plants grow better when I loosen hard soil with a hoe before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmei shwie shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ dani mikɛdu lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil creates spaces for fresh air and water to enter the ground. It makes it easier for soft plant roots to spread, breathe, and pull nutrients into the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa gbɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ nu boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛgbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers encourage us to put shade roofs over nursery beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ jwɛi aha gbekɛbii askul saatsoi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are like newborn babies that burn easily under full sunlight and break under heavy rains. A simple shade roof protects them from severe heat and falling rain until they grow strong enough to be moved to the open field.
ga: Tsei bibii tamɔ abifabii ni afɔɔ amɛ ehee, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa amɛ oya, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ amɛ. Hulu ŋwɛitsu ni yɔɔ mlɛo Ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛya ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli.

english: Why do some vegetable farmers cover their tomatoes with clear plastic structures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni feɔ aduawai lɛ kɛ plastic ni mli tse haa amɛ tomato lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plastic coverings shield delicate crops from heavy rains that wash away soil and spread diseases, while trapping warmth and moisture inside to help the plants grow faster and produce clean fruit.
ga: Plastic ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, emɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii ni he tse.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up tightly to protect themselves from losing water. By rolling inward, the plant exposes less leaf surface to the hot sun, helping it conserve internal moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ koni nu akaje mli. Kɛtsɔ mligbɛ ni eeetsɔ mli lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ baajie ebaa lɛ hiɛ kpo koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ ehe fioo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay alive during the dry season when other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli beni tsei krokomɛi gboi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots grow deep into the ground to reach deep water sources. The plant can also shed its leaves to save water and wait patiently for the rains to return.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyashɛ nu jɛɛhei ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. Tsei baanyɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ hu koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛkɛ tsuishitoo amɛ ni nugbɔ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves drop off when the soil gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ lɛ?

english: When the soil loses all its water, the pepper plant drops its leaves to save energy and stay alive. Without leaves, the plant uses much less water, allowing its stem and roots to survive until it receives water again.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fɛɛ fite Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ baai bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ nu fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnáa nu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full sunlight without getting scorched. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the air humid around the cocoa seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛshãaa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ mli fũuɔ.

english: Why should I plant my vegetables on raised earth mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu aduawai yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Raised mounds keep the soil loose so roots can breathe easily, and they allow excess water to drain off the sides so roots do not get soaked and rot after heavy rains.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu mlɛo. ni oha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli kɛya sɛɛgbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieee nu ni amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why do some crop varieties take over five months to mature while others can be harvested in just three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi heɔ nɔ ni fe nyɔji enumɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ akpa ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred for different purposes. Fast-maturing crops are designed for quick yields, while long-duration varieties take more time because they spend energy developing strong root systems, thicker stems, and higher resilience against pests and droughts.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛha yiŋtoi srɔtoi. Afee tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo, ejaakɛ amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa, amɛshishifãi ni mli wa, ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Why should I choose to plant a long-duration crop variety instead of one that matures quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni daa oya lɛ?

english: Long-duration varieties take longer to harvest, but they often produce larger yields, have a stronger tolerance against dry weather, and can offer better market prices depending on the farming season.
ga: Henɔi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani akpaa. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ waa. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ jarayeli jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ aha yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ naa.

english: Why do my newly planted crops seem to grow very slowly during their first few months in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni midu ehee lɛ daraa blɛoo waa yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the initial months, many plants focus their energy underground to build a deep, strong root system first. Once those roots are well established, the plant will start growing faster above the ground.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ Tsei babaoo kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ ema shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baabɔi dalɛ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will watering my crops every day make them grow faster and mature sooner?
ga: Ani nu ni oooha ŋmɔshi nibii daa gbi lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛdara oya?

english: No, every crop variety has a natural growth timeline set by its biology. While adequate water keeps plants healthy, overwatering can rot the roots and actually delay growth instead of speeding it up.
ga: Dabi, tsei srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ be ni wala yibii ahe nilee tsɔɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ moŋ, shi nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afite ni amɛdara blɛoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛya oya.

english: How does proper spacing between seeds during planting affect how fast my crops will mature?
ga: Te dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ saa bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ oya aha lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with its neighbors, allowing the crop to develop steadily at its natural speed.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ akaŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli oyaiyeli naa.

english: Why are some plants in my field growing quickly while others planted on the exact same day are taking much longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo lɛ?

english: Differences in soil quality across your farm, small changes in shade, or uneven seed depth can cause plants put in the ground on the exact same day to develop at different rates.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ tsakemɔ fioo yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo dumɔwui lɛ amlibotemɔ lɛ jeee ekome Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ.

english: If my crops are taking a long time to develop, should I add extra fertilizer to speed them up?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa Ani Esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ?

english: Adding too much fertilizer will not force a long-term crop to mature faster and can actually burn the roots. Fertilizer should only be applied in recommended amounts at specific growth stages.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ nyɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ awo mli yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli pɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly around my long-term crops help them develop better?
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi-be kakadaŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential moisture and soil nutrients that your crops need to build strong stems and leaves. Clearing them gives your main crop the resources it needs for continuous, healthy development.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni otsei lɛ kwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni wa. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aná nibii ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my slow-growing crop is developing normally or if it is failing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ loo amɛmiiya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: As long as the leaves remain bright green, the stem feels firm, and you see new leaves appearing bit by bit over time, the plant is healthy and following its natural growth pace.
ga: Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baahi shi akɛ eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ. Ni onaa akɛ baai heei jeɔ kpo fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli. Tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do some slow-growing crop varieties handle harsh weather better than fast-growing ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi ni daa blɛoo lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya lɛ?

english: Slow-growing varieties take the time to build tough stems and deep roots that reach far underground, which allows them to pull up hidden water and stay strong during dry periods.
ga: Henɔi ni daa blɛoo lɛ he miihia be koni amɛná tsei kɛ shishifãi ni wa ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: If I trim the top branches of my cocoa trees, will it harm them or help them produce more pods?
ga: Kɛji mifo kookoo tso nine ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Ani ebaaye kookoo tso lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua kookoo tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Trimming the top branches does not harm the tree; it opens up the canopy to let in sunlight and fresh air. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to put energy into growing heavy, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeee tso lɛ awui. Gbelemɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii ni mli wa.

english: Why do people cut off the top growing tip of tomato and pepper plants when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ ashishifãi beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ?

english: Removing the top tip stops the plant from growing too tall and thin. It forces the plant to spread out sideways with extra branches, which leads to a stronger bush that produces far more fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋwɛi naagbee lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ tsɔ ni efee mlɛo. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ kɛ niji babaoo. Enɛ haa anáa jwɛi ni mli wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it necessary to reduce excess leaves on bushy crop plants if the plant looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo baai ni fa fe nine yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi amli lɛ amli kɛji tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: When a plant has too many leaves, it consumes all its food just to keep those leaves alive. Cutting back extra leaves ensures the plant directs its food toward making big roots, tubers, or fruits instead.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ baai babaoo tsɔ Ebaaye niyenii lɛ fɛɛ koni nakai baai lɛ ahi shi kɛkɛ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baatsu nii ni ekɛwo shishifãi, bulbs, loo aduawai wuji moŋ.

english: Why do vegetable farmers cover their young seedbeds with fine netting or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni duɔ aduawai lɛ kɛ ŋshɔŋlooi loo tsei ahe tsei haa amɛdumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are extremely soft and weak. Covering them acts as a protective shield against scorching hot sun, heavy rains that wash seeds away, and destructive insects that eat young leaves.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ darako kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Amɛhe nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hoɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why do extension officers recommend putting net shade over young cocoa nurseries during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afee shade yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Baby cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight and harsh dry winds. Shade nets keep the air humid and the soil moist so the young plants can grow strong roots without dying from heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa shishi. Shade nets yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shishifãi ni wa ni hulutsoo lɛ akagboi amɛ.

english: Will covering my crops with fine mesh nets prevent pests without using chemical sprays?
ga: Ani ŋshɔŋlooi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, physical nets create a complete barrier that stops insects, moths, and birds from reaching your crops to lay eggs or eat the leaves, keeping the plants safe naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni yeɔ emuu koni kooloi akabote mli. ŋmeii kɛ okpoi shɛɔ onibii ahe koni amɛwo ŋmeii loo amɛye baai. Ha tsei lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why should I clear the tall wild grass around the outer borders of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie koo mli jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle miŋmɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Tall grass and weeds around your border act as breeding grounds and hiding places for external pests like insects and rodents. Clearing them creates a clean buffer zone that keeps pests away from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle he fɛɛ. Ohusu lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ tamɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ kɛ he ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ. Amɛ ni oootsi lɛ haa buffer zone ni he tse ni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe.

english: How does putting up a simple fence or net around my farm protect my crops from diseases?
ga: Fɛnsi loo ŋshɔŋloo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atoɔ Te ŋmɔ mli ŋshɔŋlooi baanyɛ aye abua ni abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fences and netting physically block farm animals like goats and wild grasscutters from walking through your field, preventing them from eating plants and carrying crop diseases from neighbor farms onto your land.
ga: Gbogboi kɛ ŋshɔŋlooi baatsi ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ tooi kɛ jwɛi shwielɔi anaa yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ koni amɛkatsɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni amɛkaye tsei ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli helai aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do farmers cover the ground around young plantain suckers with dry leaves and straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around plants creates a protective blanket that traps moisture in the soil, keeps the root area cool during hot days, and stops weeds from stealing plant food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa Tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni ehaaa jwɛi akaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli

english: Why should I cover exposed crop roots with topsoil after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aha tso shishifãi ni eje kpo lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Exposed roots quickly dry out in the sun and leave the plant vulnerable to pests and diseases. Covering them protects the roots so they can continue absorbing water and nutrients safely.
ga: Shishifãi ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli. ni ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ha amɛhe lɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛya nɔ amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai shweshweeshwe.
