english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under the hot sun. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains around them acts like an umbrella, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until they grow strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he lɛ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi ebaada waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop still grow good tubers even when there is no rain and the soil is poor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kpakpai lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu ehiii kwraa lɛ?

english: Cassava is a very tough crop with deep roots that dig far into the ground to find hidden water and nutrients. It naturally copes with drought and low-quality soil much better than crops like maize or tomatoes.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni wa waa ni eshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ, ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni etao nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Amɛtsuɔ hɔmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii he nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo tomato.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's way of protecting itself from hot weather. By curling its leaves, the maize plant reduces how much surface is exposed to direct sunlight, which helps it hold onto its water so it does not dry out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tso lɛ baa shi yɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli koni ekagbi.

english: Why do I need to put up tall wooden stakes for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to make food for their underground tubers. Lifting the vines off the damp soil prevents disease and lets the leaves catch maximum sunlight to grow bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable seedlings with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates a protective layer over the soil. This layer blocks direct sun, keeping the soil cool and stopping moisture from evaporating too quickly so your plants stay hydrated.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ baatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ. koni tsei lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain trees split open and turn yellow during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ mli gbalaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The strong, dry Harmattan wind sucks water out of large leaves very fast. The leaves split to let the wind pass through without blowing the whole tree over, but the yellowing shows the plant is thirsty and stressed by the heat.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni egbi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai wuji lɛ amli oya. Baai lɛ fãa koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni etswaaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ. Shi ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ ni ehao kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli.

english: Extreme heat spoils the pollen inside tomato blossoms before the flowers can be fertilized. When the plant senses it is too hot to support fruit, it drops the flowers to save its strength until cooler days return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa gbeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ dani fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ awo fɔmɔ nii. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ edɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo yibii Ebaajie fɔfɔi hu koni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil richer for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and turn it into plant food in the soil. When the crop dies, that food stays in the dirt and acts like natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi lɛ Nakai niyenii lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaatsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow and stay small even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients right out from under your crops. Even if you water the land, the aggressive weeds drink it first, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi. Kɛji okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po Shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ baanu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why does my maize plant keep trying to push out new leaves even after caterpillars chew up the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ baai heei kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei lɛ etsɔ teŋgbɛ moŋ.

english: Maize grows from a deeply protected growing heart inside the central stem. As long as pests only eat the outer leaves without destroying that inner growing point, the plant has the strength to recover and grow new leaves.
ga: Abɛi daa kɛjɛɔ tsui ni miida ni abuɔ he waa yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ yeɔ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ pɛ ni efiteee mligbɛ shweremɔ hei lɛ, Tso lɛ hu yɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaatsake ehe ni ekɛ baa heei akwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen acts like food for green leaf growth, and when there is not enough in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the newer leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native plants that are naturally tougher and adapted to the soil, allowing them to quickly absorb water and nutrients faster than newly planted crop seeds can.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji maŋ tsei ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young corn leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the tender leaves inside the central funnel of the plant. Spraying approved treatments early in the morning when the worms are active helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsaa hela lɛ tsu nii leebi be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the leaf juices, or by a plant virus spread by those insects that disrupts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi bibii ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and small root systems that cannot handle heavy heat. They need shade crops like plantains to shelter them from direct sun and preserve soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly, causing stress that makes the plant reject flowers to preserve energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tsei kpooɔ fɔfɔi bɔni afee ni amɛbu hewalɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nɔ ni fata he ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Removing extra shoots, called suckers, prevents them from stealing water and nutrients from the main plant, allowing the main stem to produce larger bunches of plantain.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ehaa tso lɛ tso titri lɛ woɔ plantains akui wuji.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground around my crop vines and stake my yam plants with wood?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie he ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Ani oduɔ wain tsei ni okɛ tsei shwieɔ sweet potato tsei anɔ?

english: Yams are climbing plants that need to spread their leaves high on stakes to catch maximum sunlight for tuber growth, while keeping leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã tsei anɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni bulbs lɛ adara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the soil if I leave them after heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water in waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to the cassava roots and promotes fungal rot, causing mature tubers to spoil quickly if not harvested before the heavy rains.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni eda lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow well in flooded water while my highland rice rots in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-flat rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi gɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties have special root tissues that can breathe in standing water, whereas highland rice varieties have standard roots that drown and rot if kept continuously underwater.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ amu nu ni yɔɔ kpoo mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni sa ni baagbo ni amɛbaafite kɛji akɛ akɛto nu shishi be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting tender cocoa leaves from burning until the crop is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives crops their green color and growth energy, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves stay healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ amɛhe su eŋɔli kɛ fuel kɛha amɛdalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my field make the maize I plant next grow so well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the crop season ends, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth, serving as natural food for your next crop of maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni dumɔwui be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni aŋã lɛ baakã he ahi je lɛŋ. Okɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-cornmeal ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without giving me any fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up their pollen. When it gets too hot, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and water rather than trying to feed developing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground if heavy rain floods my land for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ha he ni miyɔɔ lɛ gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it suffocates the roots and creates the right conditions for rotting fungi to grow underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and give me small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing plants properly ensures every plant gets enough food to grow thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my pepper plant grow plenty of dark leaves but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages pepper plants to grow big stems and leaves instead of flowers. Balancing the soil food helps the plant switch its energy from growing foliage to producing peppers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha chili tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji kɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize crops so much faster during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn lɛ mra kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Warm and dry weather helps armyworms hatch and grow rapidly. Without rain to wash the young caterpillars away or drown them, they multiply quickly and feed on the tender heart of the maize plant.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya. Nugbɔ bɛ ni baafɔ ŋmeii lɛ loo ekɛ amɛ baawo nu mli. Amɛshwereɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei amli loo bibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up with yellow patterns on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow patterns are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the leaf from making food properly, leading to poor root yields.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ he mfoniri. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi ni ehiii.

english: Why do seeds I save from last year's maize harvest produce weaker crops than new seeds bought from certified dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid crop seeds lose their vigor and high yields after the first generation. Saving and replanting them results in uneven growth and smaller cobs, whereas certified seeds are fresh hybrids produced for maximum yield.
ga: Hybrid tso dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni abuɔ he ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui heei ni afee koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged, which drowns the roots and prevents them from absorbing food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaaaa amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat stress or lack of moisture, causing the plant to abort fruit production to preserve its own life.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kpaɔ yibii bɔni afee ni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala he.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big foliage and leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall leaves instead of directing nutrients down into the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji. Mohu ɔ, a haa niye níhi kɛ yaa sisi ɔ mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do weeds keep invading my farm so quickly even after I completely clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miibote miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mifo jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds can rest underground for years; when you clear or turn the soil, it brings those hidden seeds up to the sunlight and rain, causing them to sprout all at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo. Beni otsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ loo otsakeɔ lɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni no haa amɛfeɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why does my land give me smaller crop harvests every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific crop pests to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do insects attack my green crops more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: In the dry season, wild bushes dry up, so hungry pests travel from everywhere to your green, irrigated farm because it is the only fresh food and water available.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, koo lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ gbiɔ. Hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛjɛɔ he fɛɛ he kɛyaa ŋmɔ ni okɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ niyenii kpakpa kɛ nu pɛ yɔɔ biɛ.

english: What causes the roots of my yam tubers to rot underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po?

english: Tiny invisible worms called nematodes and soil beetles puncture the yam tubers underground, creating wounds that allow rot-causing fungus and bacteria in the moist soil to enter.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni anaaa amɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni haa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly dry up and die just when they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ kɛji ebɔi yibii womɔ pɛ?

english: This sudden wilt is caused by fungal diseases in the soil that block the plant's internal water tubes right when fruit production demands the most water from the roots.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ anaa beni tso lɛ yibiiwoo biɔ shishifã nu babaoo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight; they need canopy trees to provide gentle shade and preserve soil moisture so their delicate leaves do not burn.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akashã.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, wasting energy stretching upward instead of growing thick stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu amɛha hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Efiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: It is best to wait until the soil stays consistently moist after several steady rains rather than planting immediately after the very first rain, which can dry up quickly and ruin the seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbi oya ni efite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or the roots are soaked in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn dark green and grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops and improves overall soil health.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I spread dried leaves and crop remains on top of the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, traps moisture in the ground, keeps root temperature cool during hot days, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted too close to other crops, it puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of developing thick root tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, sisi yitso nɛ mi wa ngɛ sisi.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree lacks water, faces extreme heat, or is not pollinated by beneficial insects like midges. Keeping shade trees helps maintain the humidity needed for pod formation.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ midges lɛ ekɛ amɛhe wooo mli lɛ, tso lɛ ni oooha ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i ni he hiaa kɛha pod feemɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra side shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Removing small side stems allows the plant to direct its food and water straight to developing large, healthy tomato fruits rather than wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Ajieɔ sɛɛ tso bibioo lɛ Ehaa tsei lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo tomato yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to take up soil nutrients and water much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early stops them from stealing food and light from your young plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are there small holes and ragged edges on the leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ amɛhe ni etse lɛ?

english: Holes in corn leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm eating the leaves. Checking the farm early and applying recommended treatments into the center of the plant stops the pest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Can I keep planting seeds saved from my previous harvest, or do I need to buy new seeds every season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui kɛtsɔ shika ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei daa afi?

english: You can reuse seeds from traditional crops, but hybrid seeds bought from shops produce much lower yields if replanted. Using certified seeds ensures strong plants, disease resistance, and bigger harvests.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ blema tsei amli lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ. Shi dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ baawo yibii ni baa shi kwraa kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa, helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe, ni amɛkpaa nii babaoo.

english: How do I correctly uproot plantain suckers from an old farm so they grow well in my new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie dumɔwui kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Select healthy maiden suckers with narrow, sword-like leaves. Dig around the base carefully without damaging the main underground root, slice it clean off the mother plant, trim the old leaves and root tips, and plant immediately.
ga: Halamɔ yei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai bibii tamɔ klante. Tsɔɔmɔ shishitoo lɛ he jogbaŋŋ ni ofiteee shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi titrii lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai momoi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi. ni adu amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Why is it helpful for me to start growing seedlings in my backyard before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yɛ mishia lɛ sɛɛ dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A backyard nursery allows you to easily water, shade, and protect young seedlings from pests during their delicate first weeks. Once they develop strong stems and roots, they can survive harsher field conditions.
ga: Tsoi akwɛmɔhe ni yɔɔ shia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu woɔ tsei bibii amli, ohaa amɛ hulutsoo, ni obuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ni mli wa lɛ amli mlɛo. Kɛ amɛná tsei kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wa waa amli hu.

english: If I leave my farm land untouched for a few years, why does the soil become good for crops again when I return?
ga: Kɛji mishi miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa nɔ afii fioo komɛi Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ beni miku misɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving land to fallow allows wild vegetation to grow and drop leaves that rot into rich organic manure. Their deep roots break up hard soil and bring hidden nutrients up to the surface, naturally restoring soil fertility.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa koo mli tsei kwɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ

english: What easy food crops can I grow around my compound that require minimal investment to feed my family?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii tsei manyɛ makwɛ yɛ mihe? He ko ni biɔ ni akɛ shika fioo pɛ awo mli koni akɛkwɛ weku ko.

english: Fast-growing crops like pepper, garden eggs, okra, and leafy greens like kontomire grow well in backyards. They thrive on household compost and water, giving you quick food without needing costly inputs.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmeii, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, okra, kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ contours lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shia lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ shia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu nɔ. Ehaa oyeɔ niyenii oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why do crops like cassava and plantain keep growing new shoots after harvest, but maize dies after one season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ cassava kɛ plantain lɛ náa ŋmeii heei lolo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmãa baagbo yɛ be kome sɛɛ?

english: Maize is an annual plant designed to produce seeds once and die. Plantain and cassava are perennials that store food in their stems and underground roots, allowing them to sprout continuous new growth year after year.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ daa afi ni afee koni ewo dumɔwui shikome ni no sɛɛ lɛ egbo. Plantains kɛ cassava ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni toɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei kɛ shishifãi amli. Enɛ haa amɛyaa nɔ amɛfeɔ amɛhe ehee afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do the fruits and leaves at the very top of my crop canopy grow faster than the ones down below?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ daa oya fe nɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaves at the top receive direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to make its own food through photosynthesis. This extra energy causes the top branches and fruits to grow bigger and faster than shaded lower leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ naa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. ni haa tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji kɛ ŋwɛi aduawai lɛ daraa oya ni amɛdaraa fe shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ shade lɛ.

english: How do I know when tree fruits up high are ready to be harvested and taken to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni gɔŋ nɔ aduawai lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa ni akɛba jara nɔ?

english: Look for visible changes in color—such as dark green turning light green, yellow, or orange—and a slight softening of the skin. Harvesting at full maturity ensures better taste and a higher sale price at market.
ga: Kadimɔ tsakemɔ ko ni anaa yɛ su mli, tamɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni tsɔɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse, ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmɔŋ, ni hewolo lɛ feɔ blɛoo fioo. Nikpamɔ beni eda lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni hi kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ baa.

english: What happens if I leave mature cassava tubers in the ground for too long before uprooting them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei shishifãi momo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani ajie amɛ?

english: Leaving cassava in the ground too long after it matures causes the roots to become hard, woody, and lose starch content. In rainy periods, waterlogged soil can also cause the underground tubers to rot completely.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ, amɛfee tsei, ni amɛmli ŋmei lɛ hu baaje mli. Yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: After harvesting my yam tubers, how should I store them so they do not spoil before I can sell them?
ga: Beni akpa sweet potato tubers lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛto koni ekafite dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Store yams in a well-ventilated, shaded yam barn off the ground by tying them to vertical wooden poles. Keeping them away from direct sunlight, rain, and damp ground prevents heat damage and fungal rot.
ga: Okɛ sweet potato ato sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oookɛfi tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni hulu la, nugbɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ bɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ akafite lɛ ni ŋmeii akafite lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛfeee nakai moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves during peak heat to trap moisture inside and stop the sun from sucking out water. It is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from drying out until the temperature cools down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekamu nu lɛ. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ he.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them every single day or give them a heavy soak once a week?
ga: Ani ebaahi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli daa gbi loo mikɛ nu ni wa ha amɛ shikome yɛ otsi mli?

english: Most crops prefer regular, moderate watering every day or two so the soil stays evenly moist. Heavy weekly watering often wastes water because it runs off dry soil or drowns the roots, leaving the plant thirsty later in the week.
ga: Tsei babaoo sumɔɔ ni aha amɛ nu yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ daa gbi loo gbii enyɔ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo daa otsi lɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, egbiɔ, loo ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kumai yeɔ tsei lɛ yɛ otsi lɛ naagbee.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or plant leaves on top of the soil around my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo madu baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry material acts like an umbrella that keeps the ground cool and blocks the strong sun from evaporating water. This keeps moisture in the soil longer so your crops do not dry out quickly.
ga: Mulching ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni shwieɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbiɛɛ oya tamɔ bɔ ni eji lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry for plant food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛha tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When crops lack proper food, their leaves usually turn light green or yellow instead of dark green, and their stems stay short and weak. Feeding the soil with fertilizer or manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to grow strong leaves and fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ Bei pii lɛ ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baafee kuku ni egbɔjɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ baai kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: When water and plant food are low, cassava plants drop their oldest bottom leaves on purpose. This allows the plant to save its remaining food and water for the fresh young leaves at the top to stay alive.
ga: Kɛ nu kɛ tsei aniyenii faaa lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛyiŋtoo amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ mli koni eha baai bibii heei ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they are stressed by uneven watering or extreme heat. If the plant feels it does not have enough daily water and food to raise fruit, it drops the flowers to protect its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ daa gbi ni ekɛwo yibii lɛ, Ebaajie fɔfɔii koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala he.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that create a living shade shield, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist while its roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni feɔ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops growing under big trees look tall and thin but yield very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛhe tse shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need sunlight to turn plant food into energy. When planted under heavy shade, they stretch upward searching for sunlight, using up all their energy to grow tall stems instead of producing food.
ga: Dumɔwui hia hulu la koni amɛtsake tsei aniyenii amɛfee hewalɛ. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ Ebaakpã mli koni eyatao hulu la. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei kakadaji moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee niyenii.

english: What will happen if I plant several maize seeds in the exact same hole instead of separating them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ bu kome mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni magbala mli?

english: When seeds are crowded in one hole, their roots fight each other for the small amount of water and food in that spot. This makes all the plants grow thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abu dumɔwui lɛ anaa awo bu kome mli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baawu amɛha nu kɛ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ nakai he lɛ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to dry out and turn yellow so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbi oya ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that drink up soil water and eat plant nutrients much faster than your crops can. If left unattended, weeds starve your crops of essential food and moisture every day.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii oya kwraa fe otsei lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ haaa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ daa gbi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and burn up when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, such as plantains or leafy trees, to create a cooler microclimate and retain soil moisture until the cocoa plants are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Plantain plants have shallow, fibrous roots rather than deep taproots. As heavy fruit bunches grow at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for rain-soaked soil and strong winds to uproot it unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ fiber moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Beni aduawai akuu agbo ko kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatse shishifãi lɛ. ja akɛ tso nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant copes by pulling nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the newer growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ kwɛɔ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but produce tiny tuber roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, cassava puts its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of expanding its underground tubers. Balanced soil nutrients are required for good root formation.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Cassava haa hewalɛ kɛha baai kɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni sa lɛ he miihia koni shishifãi kpakpai afee.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have beneficial bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into a nutrient form that stays in the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Emɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ ewoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips, which feed on sap and often transmit viruses that stunt the plant's development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites loo thrips, ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni bei pii lɛ amɛhaa helai ni haa tsei lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Tomatoes shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollination. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why does my soil dry out so quickly after it rains when I clear all grass from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni ajie jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bare, unmulched soil is directly exposed to sun and wind, which causes ground moisture to evaporate rapidly. Leaving crop residues or mulch acts like a cover to trap water in the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni awoko nɔ ko lɛ baashɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni akɛhaa nɔ koni nu akahi sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I get smaller yam tubers if I delay weeding during the first three months of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ sweet potato tubers bibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ ni mikɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During early growth stages, yam vines establish the root system that determines final tuber size. Weeds compete heavily for water, light, and nutrients during this critical window, reducing overall yield.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni tsɔɔ naagbee tuber lɛ dalɛ. Jwɛi lɛ kɛ nu, la kɛ niyenii he akaŋ waa yɛ haomɔ be nɛɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ nɔbaa.

english: Why do citrus trees grown from seed take many years to bear fruit compared to grafted ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ citrus tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni akɛwo amɛmli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Seed-grown fruit trees must go through a natural juvenile phase that can last several years before maturing. Grafted trees use branches taken from mature, fruit-bearing trees, allowing them to skip this long juvenile phase and bear fruit much earlier.
ga: Yibii tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ be mli ni baanyɛ ahi shi afii babaoo dani amɛdara. Tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni eda ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa amɛfoɔ oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya kwraa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat stress and retain soil moisture until their canopy grows big enough to protect itself.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo. Bɔni afee ni akatsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni ŋshɔ lɛ mli ŋshɔ lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ abu ehe.

english: Why are my young maize plants suddenly getting full of holes and covered in green waste?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni jwɛi ŋmɔji ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This is a typical sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the central leaves (the whorl) and eat the plant from the inside out, leaving behind damage that looks like ragged holes and frass that resembles damp sawdust.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ (whorl) ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Eshiɔ nibii ni efite ni tamɔ bu ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow along the center while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the middle of lower leaves usually means your soil is low on nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay leafy and green, so when the soil lacks it, the plant drains nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the growth of new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I know if my cassava tubers are ready for harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will know it is getting ready when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and fall off naturally, and the bottom of the main stem thickens and cracks near the soil line.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaale akɛ eesaa ehe beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small suckers growing around my main plantain shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi plantain tsei titri lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow at once, they fight with the main mother plant for nutrients and water in the soil. Pruning away extra suckers and keeping only one or two ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce a large, heavy cluster of fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ shikome lɛ Amɛkɛ tso titri ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ahiɛ eko loo enyɔ pɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks next to my yam vines to let them climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato wain tso ko masɛi koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need as much direct sunlight as possible to produce the food needed to fill out big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaves from rotting and allowing the plant to catch enough light.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ amli. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ afite ni ehaa tso lɛ naa la ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and twisting like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. As these insects feed on leaf sap, the damaged leaf tissue deforms and curls up, which stops the plant from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ ji akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Baa lɛ mli fãji ni efite lɛ efite ni ebɔle ehe. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ adara bɔ ni sa.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground, especially nitrogen. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that fix nitrogen from the air back into the soil, enriching your farm naturally for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ha oŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruit during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and the air is very dry, tomato pollen gets damaged and dries out before it can fertilize the flower. Without successful pollination, the plant drops the blossom to conserve energy and water.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Afiteɔ tomato mli fɔfɔi lɛ ni egbiɔ dani enyɛɔ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very thin and tall with tiny cobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted closely together, the roots compete aggressively for soil food and water. The plants stretch upward to fight for sunlight before their leaves get blocked, leaving them too weak to form full, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ dani amɛbaa lɛ atsĩ amɛnaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so fast before I even reach the market to sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ po koni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly if harvested when fully red or packed tightly in deep wooden crates, which causes bruising and traps heat. Harvesting them when partially ripe and using shallow, ventilated containers keeps them fresh longer during transport.
ga: Tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ beni eyɛ tɔrɔmɔɔ kwraa loo akɛwo tso adekai ni mli kwɔ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni emɔɔ dɔlɛ. Kpãa kɛji eshɛ fã ko ni okɛ tsɛnsii ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbɛfaa mli.

english: How can I keep my harvested maize safe from weevils without spending too much money on chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mifiteee shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ahe?

english: Drying maize thoroughly in the sun until the grains are hard reduces moisture that insects need to survive. Storing the dry grains in airtight sacks or hermetic bags smothers weevils without requiring expensive chemical treatments.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kooloi lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ wo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie ŋmeii lɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii.

english: How do I know if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer to produce a good yield?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Tired soil usually causes crop leaves to turn yellowish, grow slowly, or produce small fruits. Observing these signs or getting a basic soil test tells you that essential nutrients are missing and need to be replaced with compost or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse lɛ haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, loo amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii. Kɛ́ okwɛ okadii nɛɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shishijee kaa lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ato najiaŋ.

english: Why do experts recommend planting beans or groundnuts in the same field where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and put it naturally back into the soil. Planting them alongside or after maize feeds the soil and reduces the amount of commercial fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ odu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aya hiɛ, ni ebaaha jarayeli ŋmãa ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ aba shi.

english: What causes the leaves of my young maize to have small holes and look like something chewed them overnight?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ miifee bu bibii? Etamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko ŋmɔ lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by armyworms or caterpillars that hide in the plant foliage and feed at night. Catching them early with proper biological or recommended spray treatments protects the heart of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni teɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaabu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsui lɛ he.

english: Why do the cassava roots in my farm turn soft and black inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot is caused by fungal diseases that thrive in heavy, waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ cassava shishifãi fitemɔ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant my crop seeds in straight, measured rows instead of scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni asusu he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ oshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ

english: Planting in straight, measured rows ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, water, and soil space without competing with neighbors. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni asusuɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves roll up and droop during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Leaves roll up in the hot afternoon to reduce their surface area and save water from evaporating too quickly in the heat. It is a natural defense mechanism, and crops usually recover by evening if the soil has enough moisture.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo. Ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: What is the benefit of buying certified improved seeds compared to saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni asaa he ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ hemɔ he kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ he?

english: Certified improved seeds are specially selected and tested to produce higher yields, withstand local dry spells, and resist diseases. Saved seeds often lose these strong qualities over time, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Eŋmɛɔ etsui shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli. ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai srɔtoi Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Weeds are wild, native plants naturally adapted to survive on very few resources and aggressive growth. They steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops unless cleared early before they establish deep roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛtsɔ nibii fioo komɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa nɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. ja ajie lɛ mra dani ewo shishifãi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field with direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate intense, direct heat because their young leaves lose water faster than their roots can absorb it. They require temporary shade crops, like plantains, to shield them until their roots grow deep and strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli baawo wu ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do so many of the small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support to ensure survival. Many flowers drop because they were not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or because the tree does not have enough water and nutrients to feed every potential pod.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua koni amɛhi shi. Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ hewɔ.

english: Excess rain and cool moisture create the perfect environment for a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread. The fungus travels through water droplets splashing from the soil or infected pods onto healthy ones.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa. Fung lɛ tsɔɔ nu mli nu ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa gbɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my other food crops grow poorly when I plant them too close to cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni midu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei lɛ tsɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava is a very aggressive feeder with widespread roots that rapidly drain water and nutrients from the topsoil, leaving nearby crops starved of food.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni fiteɔ nii waa. kɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni hoɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: How does cutting off branches from my cocoa tree actually help it grow more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes useless branches that waste the tree's energy and block sunlight. Opening up the tree allows air to circulate, reduces disease, and directs energy straight into flowering and making pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni he ehiaaa ni fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Tsei ni agbeleɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli, ehaa helai baa shi ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔi kɛ pod feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize and cocoa plants turning yellow even though it is raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is so waterlogged that the plant's roots are suffocating and cannot draw up food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aahu akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛbua niyenii naa.

english: How many years can a single cocoa tree keep producing good harvests before it gets too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso kome baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A well-cared-for cocoa tree can produce high yields for about 25 to 30 years. After this age, pod production naturally slows down, and the farm will need side-grafting or replanting to stay profitable.
ga: Cacao tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo aaafee afii 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ afii nɛɛ sɛɛ. Pod feemɔ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni ehe baahia ni ŋmɔji lɛ akwɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ loo amɛdu amɛ ekoŋŋ koni amɛya nɔ amɛná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my crops at the start of the rains instead of during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into a form that roots can drink up. Applying fertilizer in dry soil wastes your money because the plants cannot absorb dry powder, and hot ground can burn the roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛfee nɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ baaha ofite shika ejaakɛ tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ powda ni egbi lɛ. Ni hei ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why is a strange green bush growing directly out of my cocoa tree branches causing the main branch to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi eŋɔli ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ, ni no haa niji titrii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ?

english: That bush is mistletoe, a parasitic plant whose roots grow inside your cocoa branch to steal water and food directly from your tree, eventually killing the branch if you do not cut it off.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ ji mistletoe tso. Enɛ ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo niji amli koni eju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, tso nine lɛ baagbo kɛji ofooo lɛ.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my crop stems with dry leaves keep them green during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitso lɛ shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the dirt with dry leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks the hot sun, keeping the soil cool and trapping underground moisture so the plant roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big shade trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate like human babies and cannot survive intense, direct sunlight. Leaving taller shade trees or planting plantains provides essential shade and keeps the soil cool while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifabii, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that spreads quickly in damp, overly shaded farms. Pruning crowded branches and weeding regularly allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, preventing the fungus from multiplying.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi akashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafee babaoo

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of tall green leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil pushes cassava to spend all its energy growing foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the roots. Planting cassava in balanced soil without excess chemical fertilizer helps the tubers grow big.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ja nɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni edaraa.

english: Yes, because yam leaves need maximum sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out, leading to much larger yam harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, abaanyɛ akpa ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize is starving for nitrogen in the soil. Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients, so applying manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season keeps the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ebaawo yibii kpakpai.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and builds up pest populations. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally restores soil fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know if my farmland is getting tired and needs a rest or organic manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔi lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe loo amɛmiitao ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, produce pale leaves, or yield less harvest every year despite good rains, your soil lacks nutrients. Adding animal manure, compost, or letting the land rest helps rebuild soil life.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo, amɛbaai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛwooo yibii babaoo daa afi yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifãi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ni aha sũ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etswa sũ lɛ wala ema shi ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I stop my plantain trees from falling over when strong rain and winds come?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkagbee shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit. Planting suckers deeper into the ground, supporting heavy bunches with sturdy wooden Y-sticks, and planting windbreak trees around your farm edges prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii. Okɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y lɛ atsu nii ni okɛfi tsei niji ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. kɛ tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa ni ooodu yɛ Edge oŋmɔ lɛ he koni tsei akagbee shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of calcium in the ground. Regular watering and placing dry grass mulch around the root base keeps the soil cool and moist so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ he daa. Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni aduawai aba.

english: Can planting hot pepper alongside my vegetable crops help protect them from insect pests?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe?

english: Yes, hot peppers contain strong natural chemicals and odors that repel many destructive insects. Intercropping pepper with other vegetables creates a natural barrier that reduces overall pest attacks on your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ ashwie kooloi bibii srɔtoi babaoo ni fiteɔ nii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Peppers kɛ aduawai krokomɛi adumɔ Ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai fɛɛ ni baa oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow strong. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-composted poultry manure will feed the plants and turn them green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni etsɔ hewalɛ. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni aha tsei lɛ niyenii ni eha amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the ground every season and allows soil pests to multiply. Rotating maize with beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas adds nitrogen back into the soil naturally and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa babaoo. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them and cannot drain away. Planting your cassava stems on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow off easily, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough moisture to plant my seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil from your farm into a ball in your hand; if it holds together without dripping water, the soil is wet enough to plant. If the ball crumbles into dry dust, seeds planted inside will dry up and fail to germinate.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ko ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ofee bɔɔlu yɛ onine mli. Kɛji amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni nu shwieee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu nii. Kɛji bɔɔlu lɛ gbá ni etsɔ sũ ni egbi Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ mli lɛ baagbi ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the weather is too dry or when chemical sprays kill the tiny midges needed to pollinate them. Providing light shade with plantains and avoiding harsh chemical sprays during flowering helps midges do their job so pods can form.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ gbe kooloi bibii ni he hiaa kɛha pollination lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ aná hulutsoo fioo ni akɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dwarf lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii koni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee.

english: Keep only two or three suckers per mat—the main parent, one medium follower, and one small shoot. Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for water and soil nutrients, resulting in small, thin plantain bunches.
ga: Ha ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi mat kome nɔ, ni fɔlɔ titri lɛ fata he, sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ. kɛ ŋmei bibioo kome Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes inside the central funnel of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which love to hide and feed on the tender young leaves inside the maize funnel. Checking your farm early and spraying neem leaf extracts or recommended treatments directly into the funnel kills them before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei ŋmeii amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ ni oooshwie ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbe amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning black and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efo lɛ?

english: This black rot at the base of tomatoes is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant usually brought on by irregular watering. Water your tomato plants consistently and add compost or agricultural lime to help the plant absorb calcium.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Ha o-tomato tsei lɛ nu daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo lime awo mli koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy, which is sent underground to grow large tubers. Staking holds the leaves up toward the sun, while keeping vines off the damp ground prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ bulb agboi. Staking haa baai lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ kpeɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie wain tso lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi foliar helai anaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon heat makes water evaporate from pepper leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground, causing temporary wilting. If the plants recover by evening, it is normal heat stress; spreading dry grass mulch around the base will keep the soil cool.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eha egbɔjɔ be kukuoo ko. Kɛji tso lɛ he wa lɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji hulutsoo be ni sa. Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: If my cocoa trees are still producing some pod fruit, why do extension officers advise cutting them down when they get sick?
ga: Kɛji mi-cocoa tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lolo lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ helatsɛmɛi ahe ŋaa akɛ ajie amɛyi lɛ?
