english: Certain viral diseases like Swollen Shoot cannot be cured by spraying chemical medicine. Keeping an infected tree allows insects like mealybugs to carry the virus to healthy nearby trees, which will eventually ruin your entire farm.
ga: Helai komɛi ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ fãji ni efuu lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ tsamɔ haa kooloi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs, kɛ hela lɛ yaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds and bushes around my crop field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? He ni aduɔ nii yɛ dani aduɔ nii?

english: Clearing weeds removes competition for soil nutrients and water, while also destroying hidden places where insect pests and plant diseases breed before attacking your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni akɛtaoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai fɔɔ yɛ lɛ dani amɛtutuaa oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell whether my crop is suffering from poor rainfall or an actual plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo amɛyɛ tso hela diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Drought usually makes all crops across a field wilt evenly, whereas a disease often starts on individual plants showing specific symptoms like swollen stems, unusual leaf spots, or rotting pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela jeɔ shishi yɛ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi ni jieɔ okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi akpo, tamɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efuu, baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni efite lɛ amli.

english: Can a plant disease from my neighbor's farm spread to my crops even if we have a clear boundary between us?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ahe helai ni jɛɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ husui ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ wɔteŋ moŋ?

english: Yes, plant diseases can spread across boundaries through wind, insects traveling between farms, rainwater runoff, or shared tools like cutlasses that carry infected plant sap.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã husui amli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Kplukai ni nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ loo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii, tamɔ dade ni tso mli nu ni hela emɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and turn yellow when there are no big trees left on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ko eshwɛɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade protection because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out soil moisture before their root systems are fully developed.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ hiɛ kwraa.

english: If I see sick leaves on my plant, can I save the tree by just cutting off those bad leaves?
ga: Kɛji mina baai ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ tso ko nɔ Ani manyɛ mahere tso lɛ yiwala kɛtsɔ nakai baai fɔji lɛ ni mafolɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Trimming leaves works for basic fungal spots on the outside, but if the illness is inside the plant's sap system, cutting off leaves will not stop the disease from killing the rest of the plant.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ baai ni afo lɛ atsu nii yɛ fungal spots ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ anɔ. Shi kɛji hela lɛ yɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ etsĩii hela lɛ naa koni ekafite tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: If I cut down a diseased crop tree today, can I plant a new seedling in the exact same spot immediately?
ga: Kɛji ofo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ mli ŋmɛnɛ Ani manyɛ madu tso hee yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait, because disease pathogens and insect pests can live on inside the old decaying roots in the soil and attack your new seedling right after planting.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, helatsɛmɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ ahi shishifãi ni egbɔ ni miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. ni amɛtutuaa dumɔwui heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu amɛ

english: Why does a sick crop tree sometimes produce many flowers or pods right before it dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii babaoo dani amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: When a plant realizes it is dying from stress or disease, its natural survival response is to put all its remaining energy into producing fruit and seeds so its offspring can survive.
ga: Beni tso ko le akɛ eegbo kɛjɛ haomɔ loo hela mli Adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo hetoo ji ni ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii kɛ dumɔwui koni seshibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I avoid burning the bush when clearing land for my new crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni ashãa beni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and beneficial living organisms in the topsoil that feed your plants, leaving the soil dry and poor over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni haa otsei lɛ niyenii lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni efite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do experts ask farmers to keep a clean, well-managed field as an example for others in the village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi biɔ okwaafoi koni amɛha amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atse ni amɛkwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kɛha mɛi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A clean, well-maintained farm acts as a practical demonstration showing neighboring farmers that proper disease control and weeding directly result in healthier crops and higher harvest yields.
ga: Okwaafoi ni he tse ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii ni tsɔɔ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɔ ni helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ ni sa haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo baa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is my mango tree giving me so many fresh green leaves but no flowers or fruits this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: When a tree gets inputs like water or nitrogen fertilizer at the wrong stage, it puts all its energy into foliage growth. It needs specific signals and correct timing to switch its energy from growing leaves to producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ nu loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ he ni esaaa lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Ehe miihia okadii pɔtɛɛi kɛ be ni sa koni ekɛtsake hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli kɛyaa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ amli.

english: What signs should I look for on my crop to know it is mature enough to start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ matao yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ koni male akɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Look for a pause in the growth of soft new leaves, hardened mature stems, and full canopy development. These show the plant has built up enough stored food energy to support flowering and fruit production.
ga: Taomɔ he ko ni baa ehe yɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ adalɛ mli. Tso lɛ yibii ni edara ni wa ni ehiɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yeɔ emuu Enɛɛmɛi tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ebɔ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Is it true that I can force my crops to produce flowers earlier than their natural season?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ manyɛ manyɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi mra fe adebɔɔ mli be lɛ?

english: Yes, techniques like flower-inducing sprays or controlled water stress can trigger blooming, but the crop must already be mature enough; forcing an unprepared plant will result in failure or weak leaf growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋaai tamɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔii amli loo nu mli haomɔ ni akudɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo fɔfɔii ahe hewalɛ. Shi esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ momo. Tsei ni asaaa amɛhe lɛ ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ loo baai lɛ adalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my citrus trees produce plenty of flowers some years, but only new leaf flushes in other years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ afii komɛi amli shi ewoɔ baai heei pɛ yɛ afii krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Trees alternate their energy based on weather and soil nutrients. If conditions favor rapid vegetation during flower bud initiation, the plant shifts back into vegetative growth and grows leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tsei tsakeɔ amɛhewalɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Kɛji shihilɛi hi kɛha tso lɛ ni etsɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni yaa hiɛ oya yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa tsofafeemɔ mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to apply fertilizer to my fruit trees for heavy yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Apply fruiting fertilizer just as the tree prepares to bloom—when buds begin to form—rather than during active leafing periods. Timing it right feeds the bloom rather than pushing out unnecessary leaves.
ga: Okɛ tsofa awo tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli be mli ni tso lɛ saa ehe koni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. (Beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ) yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ be ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsi tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ kɛya.

english: What happens if I put chemical fertilizer on my farm at the wrong time of the year?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni esaaa mli?

english: Applying strong fertilizers too early or late can misdirect the plant's growth, causing it to shoot out leaves when it should be forming fruit, or even causing delicate young flower buds to fall off.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ wo mli mra tsɔ loo sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite tsei lɛ adalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ ewo yibii lɛ. Aloo eha fɔfɔi bibii lɛ po agbɔjɔ.

english: Is there a difference between the fertilizer I use for leaves and the one I use for fruiting?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ baai anɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa yibii sɔrɔtoi baa lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, nitrogen-rich fertilizers build green leaves and stems, while potassium and phosphorus fertilizers encourage flowering and fruit growth. Using leaf fertilizer right before fruiting causes the tree to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ baai kɛ tsei eŋɔli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, potassium kɛ phosphorus ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai daa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ mli dani ewo yibii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ baawo yibii najiaŋ.

english: Should I trim off fresh green shoots from my fruit trees if I want more harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛji miitao nikpamɔ babaoo?

english: Pruning excess soft green shoots at the right time stops the plant from wasting energy on foliage, redirecting essential nutrients into flower development and fruit growth.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ be naa lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Etsɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ kɛ aduawai adalɛ nɔ.

english: Can heavy rainfall cause my fruit trees to stop producing fruit and only grow leaves?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha mi tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ akpa yibiiwoo ni ehiɛ baai pɛ?

english: Yes, abundant water encourages nitrogen uptake, which signals the tree to keep growing leaves; mild dry conditions are often required to stress the tree into flowering.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu babaoo haa nitrogen lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ebaabu ebaai lɛ ahe ni eya nɔ eda. Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi fioo lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ yɛ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: What will happen if I use flower-inducing spray on my avocado trees too early in the season?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ tsu nii yɛ mi-avocado tso lɛ nɔ mra tsɔ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Forcing a tree before it has built up enough energy will backfire, causing the plant to respond with a burst of new leaves instead of developing healthy fruit buds.
ga: Kɛ́ anyɛ tso ko nɔ dani ená hewalɛ ni fa lɛ, ebaaku esɛɛ aba. Ha tso lɛ aha hetoo kɛtsɔ baai heei ni ebaakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ yiblii nɛ mi wa.

english: How many months does it usually take for tomato plants to mature and start bearing harvestable fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani tomato tso ko kwɛ̃ɔ ni ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Most common tomato varieties mature in about 3 months (or 12 weeks) from the time you transplant them into the main field, after which you can begin harvesting.
ga: Tomato henɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ babaoo lɛ shwereɔ yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3 (loo otsii 12) mli kɛjɛ be mli ni okɛwoɔ saatso wulu lɛ mli lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ obaanyɛ oje ŋmaakpamɔ shishi.

english: Why do extension officers usually talk about crop age in weeks rather than months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ wieɔ tsei ashihilɛ he yɛ otsii amli moŋ fe nyɔji amli lɛ?

english: Counting crop age in weeks gives you exact control over farm activities like applying fertilizer, spraying against pests, and harvesting, because calendar months have different numbers of days.
ga: Kɛ́ okane tsei awala yɛ otsii amli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi tamɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ kpamɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, kalanda nyɔji lɛ yɛ gbii ayibɔi srɔtoi.

english: Why do some vegetable crops mature in three months while other crops take up to six months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni aduawai komɛi heɔ nyɔji enumɔ lɛ?

english: Different crops have distinct genetic growth cycles; fast-growing plants like tomatoes produce fruits quickly within 3 months, whereas longer-term crops take 6 months or more to develop deep roots and heavy yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tomato lɛ baawo yibii oya yɛ nyɔji 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baahe nyɔji 6 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani shishifãi ni mli kwɔ aba ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know the right stage to pick my tomatoes off the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie tomato kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: If you are taking them to a far market, pick tomatoes when they just start turning light pink or orange; if you are selling locally the same day, you can let them turn fully red on the vine.
ga: Kɛji okɛ amɛ miiya jarayeli he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ Kpɔ̃ɔ tomato beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ pinki loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ. Kɛji ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli yɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ Obaanyɛ oha wain tso lɛ afee tɔrɔmɔɔ kwraa.

english: Once my tomato farm reaches harvest time after 12 weeks, do I harvest all the fruits in one day?
ga: Kɛ́ mi-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ bashɛ kpamɔ be lɛ he yɛ otsii 12 sɛɛ lɛ, ani makpa aduawai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome mli?

english: No, tomato plants produce fruits continuously over several weeks. You will harvest ripe fruits in batches every few days over a period of one to two months.
ga: Dabi, tomato tsei yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii otsii babaoo. Obaakpa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akui fɛɛ akui. gbii fioo komɛi yɛ nyɔji kome kɛyashi nyɔji enyɔ mli

english: What happens if I leave ripe tomatoes on the vine for too long without harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mikpaaa lɛ?

english: Leaving ripe tomatoes on the plant causes them to crack, rot, and attract pests like fruit flies, while also signaling the plant to stop producing new flowers and young fruits.
ga: Tomato ni ekwɛ̃ ni ashiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ejaraa, egboɔ ni egbalaa kooloi tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii, yɛ be mli ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hu akɛ ekpa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai heei feemɔ.

english: What time of the day is best for me to harvest my crops from the field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ makpa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Harvest early in the morning before the sun gets hot. Cool temperatures keep the harvested fruits firm and stop them from losing water rapidly.
ga: Kpaa nii lɛ leebi dani hulu lɛ ashɛ. He ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ haa aduawai ni akpa lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya.

english: After picking my fresh tomatoes, how many days can they safely stay on the farm before going to the market?
ga: Beni amɛkpa tomato hee sɛɛ lɛ Gbii enyiɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe dani amɛya jara nɔ?

english: Freshly picked tomatoes should not remain on the farm for more than 1 to 2 days, as heat and direct sunlight cause them to soften and spoil very quickly.
ga: tomatoi ni ajie ehee Kaahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli fe gbi kome kɛyashi gbii enyɔ, ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha tomatoi lɛ afee mlɛo ni efite oya waa.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and watery so quickly when kept in crates on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo adekai amli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested tomatoes are still living tissue that breathes and generates internal heat. When stacked together in warm conditions without cooling, they break down quickly and become soft.
ga: Tomato ni akpa lɛ ji fãji ni hiɛ ka lolo ni muɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ baa emli. Kɛ́ ato amɛhe yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ lɛ, amɛfiteɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo.

english: Should I harvest my tomatoes when they are green or red if I am traveling a long distance to sell them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makpa tomato be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛji ehe bahia ni mafã gbɛ kakadaŋŋ koni mayahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Pick them at the 'pink' or 'breaker' stage when they are firm. They will safely complete their ripening to a full red color during transport without getting squashed or damaged along the way.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ amɛ yɛ ‘pink’ loo ‘breaker’ stage lɛ mli beni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ lɛ. Amɛbaakwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ. ni aguuu loo afiteee yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and scorching in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates a natural canopy that provides the essential shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and go moldy so quickly inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ oya yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage when it is put away with too much internal moisture. High humidity creates the perfect environment for mold and insects, so maize must be dried thoroughly in the sun until hard before storing.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ nitoohe mli kɛji akɛ akɛto ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛto.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge green leaves above ground but producing tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi bulbs bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has excessive nitrogen, the plant focuses all its energy on leaf growth instead of root development. Roots need balanced soil nutrients like potassium to expand into thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Shishifãi lɛ ahe miihia ni amɛná sũ mli niyenii, tamɔ potassium, koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: What makes the cocoa pods on my farm turn black and rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, humid conditions. When weeds and dense branches block sunlight and airflow, moisture stays on the pods and causes them to rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni edɔ. Kɛ jwɛi kɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa lɛ, Fɛ̃i baakã ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni ebaaha amɛgboi.

english: Why do my corn stalks grow thin and tall with tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for limited sunlight, groundwater, and plant food. Giving each plant proper space ensures it receives enough nourishment to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves and sucking out sap. This damages the leaves and stops the plant from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent watering. If the plant feels it lacks the water or nutrients needed to nourish fruit, it sheds flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ ebɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛha aduawai lɛ aná hewalɛ. baafite fɔfɔi koni ehi shi

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by several hot, dry days. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the fragile young seedlings will wither and die before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ Tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale yellow even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the vital plant food (nutrients) out of the soil before your crops can reach it. Without those nutrients, crop leaves lose their green color and stop growing.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa (nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ) kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ bɛ lɛ Tse lɛ baai lɛ baaje amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest plantains so they do not rot on the way to the market?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ okpa plantains koni amɛkafite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Plantains should be harvested while they are fully plump but still completely green and hard. If you wait for them to turn yellow on the tree, they will become soft and spoil quickly during transit.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa plantains yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ kã shi amɛji ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa lolo lɛ. Kɛji omɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ.

english: How can I stop stray animals and pests from destroying my food crops when I am not at the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni elaaje kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ? Be ni mibɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: You can protect your crops by planting dense, thorny boundary hedges like lemon grass or cactus, building simple local fencing, or clearing the surrounding bush to remove hiding places for rodents and stray livestock.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ni mli tse ni ŋmeii yɔɔ mli, tamɔ sagebrush loo cactus ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ gbogbo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ jɛmɛ loo jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Koni ajie hei ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni elaaje lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow and curling leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Uprooting and burying the sick plants early keeps the disease from spreading across your entire field.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛfumɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Those black spots are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and humid weather. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets sunlight and fresh air reach the cocoa, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ kookoo lɛ he. Ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant coconut trees in the middle of my land instead of near the boundaries?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha mi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ husu lɛ?

english: Planting coconut trees toward the center of your land protects them from boundary disputes with neighbors and keeps them safe from fire or animals coming from outside roads, while providing a stable shelter area for your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ husu he béi ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ baaná lɛ he. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii tsei lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ la loo kooloi ni jɛɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ náa he ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni ehiɔ.

english: What causes my coconut trees to drop their young green fruits before they mature?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmei tso lɛ shwieɔ eyibii bibii lɛ dani amɛdaraa?

english: Young coconuts drop when the tree suffers from a sudden lack of water during dry spells or lacks nutrients in the soil. Giving the base of the tree organic mulch helps hold moisture and stops fruit drop.
ga: Kokoobii bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Can I plant vegetables like peppers directly under my big coconut trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ chili yɛ ŋmei tso agbo ko shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, but you must plant them a few meters away from the tree trunk. Coconut roots gather tightly near the base, so planting slightly further out ensures your peppers get enough light, water, and plant food.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe miihia ni odu yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai fioo ko pɛ. Akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ amɛ kɛya sɛɛ fioo koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ o-peppers lɛ ná la, nu kɛ tsei niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops grow very well on one side of my farmland but keep dying on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome shi amɛmiigboi yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil can change across the same farm. One side might hold too much water and rot plant roots, while the other side has rich, well-draining soil. Adding compost to the poor side helps improve its soil quality.
ga: Shikpɔŋ baanyɛ atsake yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Ekolɛ fã kome baaná nu babaoo tsɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ baagboi. yɛ be mli ni fã kroko lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata fã ni ehiii lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and weak even after I clear all the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Stunted maize usually means the soil is low in essential nutrients like nitrogen. Applying well-rotted animal manure or the right fertilizer early in the plant's life gives it the boost it needs to grow tall and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni ji dwarf corn lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa wo tso lɛ mli yɛ egbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: How often should I walk around my farm to check on how my plants are behaving?
ga: Ani esa akɛ manyiɛ kɛbɔle he? Shii enyiɛ ŋmɔ lɛ kwɛɔ bɔ ni etsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa lɛ mli?

english: You should walk through your farm at least twice a week. Regular visits help you spot early signs of pest attacks, leaf diseases, or dry soil before major damage happens to your crops.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Saramɔ ni ooofee daa lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsei ahe hela, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miiba mra dani nɔ ko ni mli wa aba oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit during storms. Planting them deep in loose, rich soil and using wooden props to support the main stem prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ ahum be mli. Dumɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni okɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei titrii lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why should I not plant maize on the same piece of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops need fertilizer or if they are just thirsty when the leaves look light green?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo kumai miiye lɛ kɛkɛ be mli ni baai lɛ efee ŋmɔŋ?

english: Light green or yellow leaves across the lower part of the plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients. If crops are thirsty, the leaves will curl up or droop during hot afternoon hours even if they are still green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kumai miiye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Eyɛ eŋɔli lolo, moŋ.

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight underground for space, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and form thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni efeɔ bulbs ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Can I plant cowpea between my rows of cassava, or will they steal nutrients from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: You can safely plant cowpea with cassava because cowpea grows fast, covers the soil to prevent weeds, and actually feeds nitrogen into the soil, which helps the cassava grow better.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei adu cowpea shweshweeshwe. Ejaakɛ tsina ŋmei daa oya Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akaje mli. ni ekɛ nitrogen boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the central green leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai eŋɔli lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that hides inside the central funnel of young maize to feed on tender leaves. Spotting them early allows you to apply recommended organic or chemical controls before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji fallworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms keep falling off without forming fruits during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ? Ni nɔ ko jɛɛɛ mli baaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Heavy rainfall and very high air moisture can wash away pollen or damage delicate tomato flowers before they are pollinated. Without successful pollination, the plant drops the blossoms instead of growing fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe loo efite tomato fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi yɛ aduawai ni ebaakwɛ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why should I wait for the second major rainfall before sowing my seeds at the start of the planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni ji shii enyɔ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The very first rain often moistens only the top layer of dirt, which can trick seeds into sprouting before drying out completely in the following days. Waiting for steady rains ensures deep soil moisture so seedlings survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ dani amɛgbi kwraa yɛ gbii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the hot harmattan winds start blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ je shishi etswa lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds pull moisture out of plant leaves faster than roots can suck water from the dry ground. Cocoa trees drop leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water during dry spells.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back on my land so quickly right after I clear the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie hidden under the soil for a long time. Clearing the surface lets sunlight and air reach these seeds, which triggers them to sprout rapidly all at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ dumɔwui nɛɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya shikome.

english: Why is it important for me to dry my harvested maize thoroughly before putting it in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ agbi kwraa dani mikɛwo baagi mli lɛ?

english: Storing damp maize creates an ideal environment for dangerous molds like aflatoxin to grow and attracts grain weevils that destroy your crop inside the bag.
ga: Abele ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ adalɛ ni egbalaa dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ onibii ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my mango tree dropping off before any small fruits start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? Ani ebaaje shishi efee?

english: Mango flowers often fall off due to attacks by tiny pests like thrips, fungal diseases like anthracnose, or sudden dry spells. Pruning the branches to let light through and applying safe pest treatments during early flowering helps the flowers stay on to form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose, loo hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli koni la atsɔ mli, ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my mangoes so they do not spoil before I get them to the buyer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mango? Koni mango lɛ akafite dani akɛyaha mɔ ni heɔ lɛ?

english: A mango is ready to harvest when its 'shoulders' at the top swell up round and flat, and the skin tone changes from dark green to a slightly lighter greenish-yellow. Plucking them at this stage ensures they ripen smoothly on the way to the market without rotting early.
ga: Mango lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji ‘tsitsii’ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ efuu, efee kokroo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni hewolo lɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛtee eŋɔli ni mli tse fioo. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ ni efiteee oya.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain or cassava next to them provides crucial living shade and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantain loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa kɛha wala, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, a nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen away, so adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen lɛ shwiemɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long in flat or heavy clay ground. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: What causes tiny holes in my corn leaves and chewed-up centers in the growing shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ fãi ni atsɔ mli lɛ amli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center whorl of the maize plant. Applying recommended pest controls or putting clean wood ash or dry sand into the plant center early in the morning can destroy the caterpillars.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni boteɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii loo akɛ tso sũ ni he tse loo ŋã ni egbi fata tso lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite kooloi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up tightly and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a plant virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by heat stress and uneven watering. Controlling whiteflies with organic sprays and mulching the soil base helps protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ akudɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei ahe.

english: Why does my pepper crop produce plenty of blossoms, but all the flowers fall off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, poor soil moisture, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Watering regularly during the cooler early morning hours helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo hulutsoo be mli. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ leebi maŋkpa ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ ahi efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build big tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the bunches on my plantain trees getting smaller with every new shoot that grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui niji ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ bibii be fɛɛ be ni ŋmeii heei baakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: When too many suckers shoot up around a single plantain plant, they compete for nutrients and water. Cutting away extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong shoots per plant allows the parent plant to put all its energy into making larger bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dumɔwu kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Afoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ tso fɛɛ tso mli. Enɛ baaha tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee kuu agbo.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how can it help my crops grow better than on an open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: A greenhouse is a structure covered with clear plastic or net that protects crops from extreme sunshine, heavy rain, and destructive pests, creating a safe space for plants to grow faster and healthier.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsu ko ni akɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋlooi ni mli tse ehà nɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Bɔɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsei ni amɛdara oya ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Is farming inside a greenhouse less stressful on my body than traditional open field farming?
ga: Ani okwaayeli ni afeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ aná haomɔ babaoo fe kusum naa ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli ni agbele naa lɛ?

english: Yes, working in a greenhouse requires less physical labor because systems like watering and feeding are controlled easily, reducing heavy tasks like manual weeding and carrying water across big fields.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ nu ni akɛhaa kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ ji nɔ ni akudɔɔ lɛ mlɛo, ni no haa nitsumɔi ni tsii tamɔ jwɛi ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ baa shi. kɛ nu ni akɛyaa ŋmɔji wuji amli

english: Why do plants grow differently inside a plastic house compared to outside in the open air?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa yɛ plastic tsũi amli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ akɛto kponɔgbɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Inside a greenhouse, heat, water, and pest protection are controlled, so plants do not waste energy fighting harsh weather or insects and can focus all their strength on growing and fruiting.
ga: Yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ, akwɛɔ dɔlɛ, nu kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahebuu nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei efiteee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa loo kooloi bibii. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ama dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: What is irrigation, and why shouldn't I just rely on natural rainfall for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nu shwiemɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Irrigation is the controlled application of water to plants at needed intervals. Relying only on rain leaves crops vulnerable to dry spells, while irrigation keeps soil moisture steady for continuous growth.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ji nu ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ be ni sa mli ni akudɔɔ. Ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ nyɛɔ efiteɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ be fɛɛ be koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why is watering crops inside a covered structure easier than watering them out on the open farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaaa akɛ aaaha tsei nu yɛ tsũ ko ni akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ fe ŋmɔ ni agbele mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covered structures often use pipe networks like drip lines that deliver water directly to the plant roots automatically, saving you from carrying heavy buckets or hoses across large distances.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsũi ni akɛwoɔ tsũi anɔ lɛ kɛ paipii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ, tamɔ paipii ni hoɔ nu, ni tsɔɔ nu lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ehereɔ bo kɛjɛɔ baagi loo hoses ni tsii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli. Yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ

english: Why do my crops dry out so quickly during the hot afternoon sun in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Direct afternoon sun causes water to evaporate rapidly from both the hot soil surface and the plant leaves, causing crops to lose water faster than their roots can pull it up.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ.

english: Does using drip pipes to water my crops save more water than using a watering can?
ga: Ani drip hose ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛha mitsei lɛ nu lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ?

english: Yes, drip pipes release small, steady drops directly onto the soil at the roots, which stops water from wasting through evaporation or running off into areas without crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, paipii ni hoɔ nu lɛ jieɔ nu bibii. Akɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ afite kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ loo efoɔ kɛyaa hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do my crops actually absorb food and nutrients from the soil to grow big?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Crops feed by taking up water through their roots; the essential plant nutrients dissolve in this soil water and travel up the stem to feed the leaves and fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa niyenii kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛnuɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni efãa gbɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ koni eyaha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: Can I feed my crops their fertilizers at the same time that I water them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii yɛ be mli ni mikɛ nu shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, this practice is called fertigation. By dissolving liquid fertilizer straight into the irrigation water, plants receive food and water at the exact same time right at their root zone.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ nii. Kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii kɛ nu nɔ yɛ be kome mli yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How often do vegetable crops need to be fed nutrients to produce good yield?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni aha aduawai niyenii koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Vegetable crops need regular feeding matched to their growth stages—usually lighter nutrients during early root growth and stronger nutrient mixes when they start producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Aduawai tsei biɔ niyenii ni kɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ kpãa gbee daa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛnáa niyenii ni mli wa fioo yɛ shishijee be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ. ni ebaaná niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo beni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Planting shade trees or temporary crops like plantains creates a cool canopy that protects young cocoa leaves and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green leaves. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves green up and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara oya.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy soil because the roots drown without air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛbote ŋwɛi babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over soil nutrients and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Giving plants proper spacing allows each plant to grow bigger and produce more.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni baai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and drink up the fertilizer and water before your crop roots can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures all applied nutrients go directly into feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛnuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa otso lɛ niyenii lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut away small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food away from the main stem. Pruning excess suckers allows the main tree to concentrate its energy on growing a large, heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai akui wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight so their leaves can create food for the tubers under the ground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the wet soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. yɛ hulu la mli bɔni afee ni ebaa lɛ afee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ akashɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from the leaves. Spraying organic controls like neem water protects the leaves so normal growth can resume.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tamɔ neem nu lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛdalɛ ni sa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea field mostly when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ babaoo beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers and young pods produce sweet scents and nutrients that naturally attract insect pests like pod borers. Checking the farm at flower bud stage helps you catch and manage pests early before they destroy the yield.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii tamɔ pod borers lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni omɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra ni otsa amɛ. dani amɛbaakpãtã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ

english: Can I grow the exact same type of corn in my district as farmers in other regions of Ghana?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmãa henɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ tamɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ. ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Not always. Different districts in Ghana have varying soil types, temperatures, and rainfall patterns. For example, forest districts like Bekwai have different growing conditions compared to coastal areas, so specific corn varieties perform better in certain regions than others.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Kpokpai srɔtoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi, hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kooi amli hei tamɔ Beckwai yɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli kɛ akɛto ŋshɔnaa hei ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa henɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpai komɛi anɔ fe ekrokomɛi.

english: Is corn the right crop for every farmer in Ghana to plant?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni okwaafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ baadu?

english: While corn is widely grown across Ghana, it is not suitable for every single location or soil type. Factors like local rainfall timing, soil fertility, and drainage determine whether maize or another crop like cassava or legumes will yield better in your area.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa babaoo yɛ Ghana fɛɛ moŋ, shi esaaa he fɛɛ he loo shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ. Nibii tamɔ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ akutso lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji ŋmãa loo ŋmãa kroko tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baawo yibii babaoo yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crop yields differ so much between different districts in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ srɔtoi babaoo yɛ kpokpai ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Districts differ in their microclimates, seasonal rainfall duration, soil nutrient levels, and pest pressures. A crop variety that produces a bountiful harvest in one district may give poor yields in another if the local conditions do not match its needs.
ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ amɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi bibii amli. Nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli Tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ aha yibii kpakpai aba yɛ he kroko kɛji akɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ haaa nɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ aba mli.

english: Why aren't my crops growing well even though my field received plenty of rain this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔji amli afi nɛɛ?

english: Crops need rain at specific stages of their growth. If heavy rain falls at the wrong time—such as during flowering or drying—or if the water sits on the soil without draining, the plant cannot absorb nutrients properly and can suffer despite the abundance of water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ nugbɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ be ni esaaa mli, tamɔ yɛ fɔfɔi loo be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ. Aloo kɛji nu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna amanehulu kɛ nu babaoo po.

english: Why does standing rainwater on my farm harm my crops instead of helping them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ lɛ?

english: When rainwater collects on top of the soil and does not drain, it drowns the roots by cutting off their oxygen supply. Without oxygen, crop roots rot and cannot absorb water or nutrients, causing the plant to turn yellow and fail.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo lɛ Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: How does heavy rainfall during the wrong season affect my crop yield?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni jeee be ni sa mli lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Unseasonal or poorly timed rains can wash away pollen during flowering, increase the risk of fungal diseases, prevent proper grain drying, and cause mature seeds to rot or sprout prematurely on the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni sa mli loo ni baa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie fɔfɔi amli ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ fɔfɔii amli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii lɛ. Fungal helai ahe oshara ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Tsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa dumɔwui ni eda lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops lose their blossoms when unexpected heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni mikpaaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall during the flowering stage physically knocks delicate flowers off the plant and washes away pollen. It also prevents bees and other beneficial insects from pollinating the blossoms, resulting in fewer fruits or grains.
ga: Heavy rain during flowering will cause the delicate flowers to fall off the plants and wash away the pollen. Ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hu ahe. Do not pollinate flowers This results in less fruit or grains.

english: Why does rain during harvest time ruin my mature corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ fiteɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbɔ lɛ?

english: Mature corn needs dry weather to lose its moisture. When rain falls during harvest, water gets trapped inside the corn husks, leading to mold growth, grain discoloration, and rotting before you can harvest it.
ga: Abɛi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akaje mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli Nu baakpã ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ekɛ fungal dalɛ baa. ŋmãa ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe su Ni egboɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa.

english: What happens to my corn if unexpected rains fall right when it is ready to dry?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ trukaa be mli ni efee klalo akɛ ebaagbi lɛ?

english: If corn gets wet while drying on the field, the high moisture encourages fungal growth and causes seeds to germinate right on the cob. This drastically lowers the market value and makes the grain unsafe for eating or storing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli fũu beni egbiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo woɔ ŋmãa lɛ shweremɔ he hewalɛ ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ha jara ni akɛheɔ lɛ ba shi waa, ni eha ŋmaa lɛ efee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ loo akɛtoɔ.

english: How can I tell if my local district gets enough useful rain during the right months for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miyɔɔ lɛ naa nugbɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nyɔji ni sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli?

english: You can check with your local agricultural extension officer or observe traditional rainfall patterns in your district. Maize needs steady rain during its early growth and flowering stages, followed by a dry period for maturing and harvesting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyabi okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ loo okwɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ yɛ blema beaŋ. Abele he miihia nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa yɛ shishijee dalɛ kɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji be ni nu egbi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ kɛ nikpamɔ.

english: This usually means your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow tall. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or manure early in the season prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus. Controlling these small bugs early with soap sprays or targeted treatments stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Kɛtsɔ samla ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akpa hela gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are black spots spreading across the leaves of my groundnut plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ egbɛ eshwã mi-peanut tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on groundnut leaves are caused by a fungal leaf spot disease that thrives in warm, wet weather. Rotating your crops each season and planting resistant seed varieties keeps the fungus away.
ga: Fungal leaf spot disease ni yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni edɔɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ helai diji ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa nɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa afi ni odu dumɔwui ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee bo.

english: Peppers often shed their flowers when the soil gets too dry or when the weather becomes extremely hot. Ensuring regular watering during hot spells helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Peppers fɔɔ fɔmɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do the tips of my maize cobs stay empty without any kernels growing on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ efee efolo ni dumɔwui ko bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Empty cob tips happen when the plant lacks water or food during the pollination stage when silks appear. Planting at the start of reliable rains helps the cob fill out completely.
ga: Cob tips ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii yɛ pollination be mli beni siliki jeɔ kpo lɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ eyiɔ obɔ.

english: Cabbages stay loose if they do not receive full sunlight, enough water, or proper nutrients while growing. Giving them direct sun and steady watering helps the inner leaves pack tightly together.
ga: Kaabaji baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji enine shɛɛɛ hulu ni fa nɔ. Na nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo ná niyenii ni sa yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ baaye abua ni emli baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and thin even though the leaves look giant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed hard, the plant puts its energy into giant leaves instead of expanding its underground roots. Loose soil and balanced nutrients encourage tuber growth.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo edɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ woɔ baai wuji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ niyenii ni ja haa tuber lɛ daa.

english: Why is my yam tuber growing twisted and split instead of smooth and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yams twist and split when they hit hard stones, packed soil, or gravel while expanding underground. Creating soft, deep mounds free of stones gives the yam space to grow straight.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ tsɔɔ ni amɛmli gbalaa kɛji amɛtswa tɛ ni wa, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, loo ŋmeii beni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tɛi bɛ mli lɛ ni ooofee lɛ baaha o-sweet potatoes lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves turn brown and roll up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees lose water quickly under direct sun and hot Harmattan winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains above them blocks the harsh light and keeps moisture in the air.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi la ni tsoɔ lɛ naa ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over before the fruit bunches are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai akutsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and become top-heavy as fruit bunches grow, making them easy for wind to knock down. Supporting the stem with strong forked wooden poles prevents them from snapping.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni aduawai akuu lɛ daa lɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akɛ ebaatswa lɛ kɛba shi Kɛ akɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa efo.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow instead of staying healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plant is stressed. This is commonly caused by a lack of soil nutrients like nitrogen, too much or too little water, or insects and diseases attacking the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ miihao. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. loo kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni tutuaa tsei

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning yellow from disease rather than just growing old?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hela hewɔ moŋ fe dalɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Leaves turning yellow from old age usually happen slowly on the lowest, oldest leaves. Disease yellowing appears quickly, often creates spots or patchy patterns, and can spread from one plant to nearby healthy plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛgbɔlɛ mli lɛ baa blɛoo. Yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ nɔ ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yellow leaf hela jeɔ kpo oya. Bei pii lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are plants in my farm turning yellow in small groups rather than all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ ŋmɔŋ shikome lɛ

english: Diseases often spread in patches because fungi or insects move slowly from one neighboring plant to another. Isolating or treating infected plant clusters early prevents the problem from taking over the entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hei srɔtoi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii nyiɛɔ blɛoo. kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛtee ekroko mli Atsi tsei akui ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe loo atsa amɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni naagbai akaye ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Should I uproot a crop tree that has withered roots before it infects the rest of my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei ni shishifãi egbo lɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Yes, completely digging up and carefully removing plants with root rot prevents fungi and soil-borne diseases from moving through the dirt to healthy neighboring trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni shishifãi egboi lɛ ni akumɔ kwraa ni ajie amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akatsɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: What causes the roots of my tree crops to wither and rot underground?
ga: Mɛni miiha mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Root rot and withering are caused by soil-borne fungi that thrive in overly wet conditions, or by pests like termites and nematodes damaging the roots so they can no longer absorb water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ kɛ shishifãi fitemɔ kɛ shwiemɔ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ termites kɛ nematodes ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu dɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can small insects or worms in the soil cause an entire tree to wither from the base?
ga: Ani ŋmei loo ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ agbi kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ?

english: Yes, tiny soil pests like nematodes and termites chew through plant roots underground. Once the root system is destroyed, the whole tree dries up and withers from the bottom.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes kɛ termites yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei shishifãi. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo kɛjɛ shishi.

english: Which fertilizer should I apply when my crop leaves begin to lose their green color?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii kɛ́ tso baai lɛ bɔi amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ sɛɛ fomɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate a need for nitrogen. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure supplies nitrogen to help plants regain their green leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná nitrogen ni baaye abua ni ená ebaa lɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does leaving heavy, stagnant water on my land make crop roots decay?
ga: Ani nu ni tsii ni ekã shi shiŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ?

english: Yes, stagnant water suffocates plant roots by cutting off oxygen. Choked roots begin to rot and die, leading to yellowing leaves and plant collapse.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Enɛ haa baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do crop trees suddenly wither and collapse even when they looked healthy a short time ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni duɔ nii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛkuɔ shi lɛ? Ni tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ?

english: Sudden wilting occurs when diseases block the internal pipelines that transport water from roots to leaves. Once the stem or root base is fully blocked, the tree loses water quickly and collapses.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa kɛji hela tsi mligbɛ tsɔnei ni kɛ nu jɛɔ shishifãi amli kɛyaa baai lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ loo shishitoo lɛ tsi ehe kwraa Tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛkuɔ shi.

english: How can I prepare my farm to stop crop roots from rotting during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa miŋmɔ lɛ koni tsei shishifãi akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Creating good drainage channels or planting crops on raised mounds prevents water from collecting around the roots, protecting them from fungal rot during heavy rainy seasons.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he gbɛjegbɛi kpakpai ni afee loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baatsi nu naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants prefer shaded environments because direct, intense sunlight overheats the plant and dries out leaf moisture faster than the roots can drink it from the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii sumɔɔ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ mli adɔ fe nine. Ni enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a primary soil nutrient required for leaf greenness and plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hia kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei adalɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ?

english: Planting cassava too close together forces the roots to compete for water and soil food, resulting in long thin roots instead of large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ abɔi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoots growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ Mi plantain tsei lɛ.

english: Those extra shoots suck away water and plant food from the main mother plant, reducing the size of the main plantain bunch.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa plantain tso titri lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: How does mixing dried leaves and cow dung into my dirt help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi kɛ tsina ŋmei ni mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Decomposing plant material and animal manure turn into organic matter, which holds moisture in the soil longer and feeds the crops naturally.
ga: Tsei ahe nibii kɛ kooloi ashishifã fiteɔ kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do I find small holes in my young corn leaves and tiny caterpillars inside the center stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ

english: Those holes are caused by fall armyworms, a caterpillar pest that burrows into young corn plants to feed on the tender growing leaves.
ga: Cutworms ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli koni amɛye baai ni miida ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stems instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon heat or dry soil, which prevents pollination.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna haomɔ ni jɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli. ni tsiɔ pollination naa lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I delay clearing the tall weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ be shwie jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ ajiemɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tall weeds steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water from your crops while also providing a hiding place for insect pests.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni jɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai hu kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli.

english: Why must I build high mounds of soil before planting my yam seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand downwards easily; high soil mounds provide space and airflow for the tubers to grow big.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa gbɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni bulb lɛ adara.

english: Why can't I just scatter my pepper seeds directly onto the big field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ magbɛ pepper dumɔwui ashwã ŋmɔ agbo ko nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds produce small, delicate sprouts that need shelter from heavy rain and direct heat in a managed nursery bed until they are strong enough to survive transplanting.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni he hiaa ni amɛná he ko kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the heavy fruit bunch starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: When plantains start fruiting, the top becomes heavy. If pests like stem borers or eelworms (nematodes) have eaten the roots or trunk, the plant becomes weak and easily falls over in strong winds.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baafee tsii kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ stem borers loo eel worms yɛ jɛmɛ. (Nematodes) yeɔ shishifãi loo ŋmeii. Tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ.

english: I noticed small holes and dark spots inside my plantain stems, what is causing this trouble?
ga: Miyɔse bu bibioo ko. kɛ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ plantain tsei lɛ amli Mɛni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa?

english: This trouble is usually caused by the plantain weevil (stem borer). The small worms tunnel inside the stem to feed, which weakens the plant and stops nutrients from reaching the leaves and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji plantain ŋmeii lɛ kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa. (Trunk borer) Kplukai bibii tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli kɛtaoɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii shɛɛɛ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and drying up from the bottom leaves upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This yellowing is often a sign of Panama disease or a lack of nutrients like potassium. It causes the lower leaves to die early, leaving the plant too weak to produce a good bunch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji Panama hela loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni faaa lɛ he okadi. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ gboiɔ oya, ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ efee ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Why do so many small plantain shoots grow around my main plant, and should I leave them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains bibii lɛ Mɛi babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ. mi tso titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mashi fɛɛ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: The small shoots (suckers) compete with the main plant for food, water, and light. You should remove most of them and leave only one or two strong ones so the main plant can grow a big fruit bunch.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ (tso lɛ) kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ la. Esa akɛ ojie amɛteŋ babaoo ni oshi tso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ada ni etsɔ aduawai akuu agbo.

english: How do I know the right time to cut down my plantain bunch before it spoils?
