ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ plantains kuu ko mli dani amɛgboi?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the fruit becomes plump, the sharp corners on the fingers become round, and the dried flower tips at the ends break off easily.
ga: A bunch of plantains is ready to harvest when the fruits are plump. Koji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ niji lɛ anɔ lɛ bafeɔ kokroo. kɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi ni egbi ni fiteɔ oya

english: Will growing plantains next to my maize or cassava take away all the nutrients from the soil?
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Ani mi ŋmãa loo mi ŋmãa lɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Plantains feed heavily on water and soil nutrients like potassium. If planted too close to other crops without fertilizer or compost, they will compete and slow down the growth of the other crops.
ga: Plantains yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ potassium. Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ Ebaatswa akaŋ ni eha tsei krokomɛi adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Can plantain trees cause trouble for lower crops by blocking too much sunlight?
ga: Ani dumɔwui baanyɛ amɛkɛ naagbai aba ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛtsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, as plantains grow bigger, their large leaves block sunlight. Crops that need direct sun, like maize or peppers, will struggle to produce well if planted under dense plantain shade.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ plantains lɛ dara Baai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Tsei ni hulu la he hiaa amɛ tɛ̃ɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaawo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ adu yɛ plantains tsei ni mli wa lɛ ashishi.

english: Does growing plantains on the same piece of land for many years reduce soil fertility?
ga: Ani plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afii babaoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aba shi?

english: Yes, because plantains suck up a lot of nutrients continuously. Over time, the soil becomes tired unless you add manure, compost, or fertilizers to replace what the plants took out.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ plantains lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo be fɛɛ be. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he koni akɛto nɔ ni tso lɛ ejie lɛ najiaŋ.

english: What trouble does the dry harmattan season bring to my plantain crops?
ga: Mɛɛ naagbai harmattan be ni egbi lɛ kɛbaa mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ?

english: The dry harmattan weather dries out the soil and causes plantain leaves to split and dry up. Without enough water during this time, the plant will delay fruiting or produce very small bunches.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa plantain baai lɛ fãa ni amɛgbiɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baatsɛ yibiiwoo loo ebaawo ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do strong rainstorms destroy plantain farms more easily than cassava or yam farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ahum ni naa wa waa lɛ baanyɛ akpata plantain ŋmɔji ahiɛ fe ŋmɔji ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ŋmɔji woɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and tall, heavy stems with massive leaves that catch the wind like a sail. This makes them much more likely to be uprooted or snapped by strong winds during heavy rains.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei kakadaji ni tsii. Eyɛ lɛlɛ agbo ko ni mɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tamɔ lɛlɛ. Enɛ haa kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi amli loo ekumɔ amɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice crop need standing water, while my maize dies if water stays on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa nu ni yɔɔ kpoo lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-abele lɛ baagbo kɛji nu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their roots that allow them to breathe even in flooded soil, whereas maize roots suffocate and rot when trapped in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛmuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ po nɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the rice plant is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for making green chlorophyll and growing leaves; adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea quickly fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha klorofil eŋɔli kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii oya.

english: Why do the new improved rice seeds yield so much more grain than the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ni atsake lɛ wo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikpa kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved rice seeds are specially bred to spend their energy producing heavy grain heads rather than growing very tall stems, while saved seeds lose these high-yielding traits over generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii ni akɛfee dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tsei ni kɛlɛ waa lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni haa yibii babaoo nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli.

english: Can I put fresh dropping waste from my chicken coop straight onto my growing crop fields?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi jwɛi heei ni jɛ kooloi atsu lɛ mli lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fresh chicken manure contains strong ammonia that can burn crop roots; it must be allowed to dry and decompose for a few weeks to become safe and rich plant food.
ga: Ammonia ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi lɛ fa babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ mli. Esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbi ni efite otsii fioo komɛi koni ebatsɔ tso niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni fa babaoo.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the soil better for next season's cereal crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny root nodules filled with beneficial bacteria that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer factory.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi bibii. Eyi kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔhe.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like tubes during the hottest afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural defense mechanism to shield its surface from the hot sun, preventing precious moisture from evaporating away.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ebuɔ ehiɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my tall maize plants fall flat to the ground whenever a strong rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ be fɛɛ be ni ahum ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over (lodges) when its roots are shallow or the stem base is weak; gathering soil around the base of the stalks (eathing up) gives the plants stronger support against wind.
ga: Abele baashwie baai (hejɔɔmɔ) kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni abua naa kɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi (eyeɔ) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering, as the plant sheds parts it cannot afford to feed to save energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pepper tso lɛ laajeɔ fã ni enyɛɛɛ ena niyenii ni ekɛto hewalɛ he koni ehi shi lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects that slows down root growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ni ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraaa oya.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow so much faster than the crops I planted carefully?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants built to survive under harsh conditions, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni ama koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist so the cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and dark, unpruned farms. Trimming extra tree branches lets sunlight and air in, which keeps the pods dry and stops the rot.
ga: Enɛ ji blackpod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ kɛ duŋ ni afolɔɔɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow like a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will bring back the dark green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaku esɛɛ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What are these tiny caterpillars eating the central leaves inside my young maize stems?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni yeɔ teŋgbɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn stems lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on young corn shoots. Applying recommended insecticides or natural neem leaf extracts into the central leaf funnel early in the morning kills the pests before they destroy your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Does it matter which way I point cassava stick cuttings when pushing them into the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔɔ yucca tso nine beni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, the small buds on the cassava stem must point upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the plant wastes energy trying to bend its shoots upward, leading to weak plants and low tuber yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ abɔle ehe lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do we make high soil mounds to plant yam tubers instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni wɔkɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to expand into big tubers. Mounding the soil gives roots room to grow deep easily, improves water drainage so the tubers don't rot, and makes harvesting much simpler.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ haa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ oya. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite. Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ mli edɔ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently damp helps the roots continuously pump calcium up to the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛpomp calcium kɛya aduawai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by extreme dry heat, poor watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and light shade during hot spells will help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. nu ni ehiii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on the plot where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil nutrients, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. Rotating with legumes naturally restores fertility to your field for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to cover dry soil with dry grass or leaves around my crop stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ? mi tso lɛ shishi

english: This practice is called mulching. Covering the ground traps soil moisture during hot days, prevents weeds from sprouting, keeps the plant roots cool, and gradually decomposes into natural compost.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How long can a coconut tree live and keep producing food on my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei tsei baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo niyenii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A healthy coconut tree can stand and yield fruit for 70 to 80 years. Once planted, it serves as a long-term resource that stays on your land for many decades.
ga: Kokoo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ adamɔ shi ni ewo yibii afii 70 kɛyashi 80 kɛji adu lɛ pɛ. Ebaatsu nii akɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli nibii ni baahi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant coconut trees if I am already getting older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ makwɛ ŋmei tsei beni Namɔ miida lɛ?

english: Planting long-term tree crops like coconut creates a lasting legacy. Even if you plant later in life, the trees will continue to produce food and income for your children and grandchildren for generations.
ga: Growing perennial plants like coconuts creates a lasting legacy. Kɛji odu tsei yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ oshihilɛ mli po Tsei baaya nɔ amɛha niyenii kɛ shika aha obii kɛ obii kɛjɛ yinɔ kome mli kɛya yinɔ kroko mli.

english: What should I do if my coconut trees show small signs of disease or pests?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ jieɔ hela loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe okadi fioo ko kpo?

english: If the disease or pest problem is minor, do not give up on the farm. Continue with proper farm care and maintenance to help the trees recover and keep producing.
ga: Kɛji helai bibii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe naagbai pɛ yɔɔ lɛ, kaashi ŋmɔ lɛ. Feemɔ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ kɛ ekwɛmɔ ni sa koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii.

english: Should I abandon or destroy my coconut trees as soon as they develop a minor health issue?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔ̃ loo makpãtã ŋmei tso ko hiɛ kɛji ená helai bibii komɛi pɛ?

english: No, minor issues are common over the multi-decade life of a tree. As long as the damage is limited, regular care and monitoring will allow the crop to overcome the problem.
ga: Dabi, naagbai bibii ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni tso ko hiɔ shi lɛ fɛɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni nɔ ni efite lɛ faaa lɛ Nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ekwɛmɔ daa baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye naagba lɛ nɔ kunim.

english: How are tree crops like coconut different from seasonal crops like maize or vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be mli tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ahe?

english: Seasonal crops only produce once and must be replanted every few months, whereas perennial tree crops like coconut stay in the soil and yield food continuously for 70 to 80 years.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ be mli lɛ woɔ yibii shikome pɛ ni ehe miihia ni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ daa nyɔji fioo. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii be fɛɛ be afii 70 kɛyashi 80 lɛ.

english: How does planting coconut trees secure food supply for my household?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ana niyenii aha mishiabii lɛ?

english: Because coconut palms remain productive for almost a century, they act as a stable, long-lasting source of food and nutrition that remains on the farm year after year.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei tsei etee nɔ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii aaafee afii oha nɛ. No hewɔ lɛ eji niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can my children and extended family inherit and harvest from the coconut trees I plant today?
ga: Ani mibii kɛ miweku ni mli elɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná gboshinii ni amɛkpa ŋmei tso ni midu ŋmɛnɛ lɛ mli nii?

english: Yes, because coconut trees live for up to 80 years, your children and grandchildren will grow up to meet and harvest from the exact same trees you plant today.
ga: Hɛɛ, akɛni ŋmei tsei baanyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi afii 80 hewɔ lɛ, obii kɛ obii lɛ baada ni amɛkɛ tsei ni oduɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ akpe ni amɛkpa nii.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers encourage us to plant permanent tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Extension officers encourage permanent crops because they establish long-term value on your land, protecting soil health and securing your family's economic future for decades.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi fiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Ejaakɛ amɛfeɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he ni oha oweku lɛ shika gbɛfaŋ wɔsɛɛ be ahi shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni baa lɛ.

english: Is it normal for a coconut tree to remain in the same spot for a lifetime?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ ŋmei tso baahi he kome yɛ ewala be fɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, coconut trees are deep-rooted perennials designed to stand firmly in the same location, growing steady and producing fruit for over 70 years.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei ji tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni afee amɛ koni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ he kome. Etee hiɛ be fɛɛ be ni ewo yibii nɔ ni fe afii 70 nɛ.

english: How do I know if my long-term tree crop farm is progressing well despite temporary challenges?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi tsei aŋmɔ ni mikɛtsu nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ miiya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli naagbai fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: If the trees are established and continuing to grow or bear fruit, temporary setbacks like minor pests or weather changes should not stop you from maintaining the farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ato tso ko shishi ni etee nɔ eda loo ewo yibii lɛ, esaaa akɛ be kukuoo mli naagbai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Leaving tall trees or planting plantains provides shade and keeps the air humid, protecting the young cocoa until it is mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore the plant's green color and health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they feed the soil, reducing the need for expensive chemical fertilizers while giving you an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni okɛbaakpa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn hard and woody if I do not harvest them after one year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tsei kɛji mikpaaa amɛ yɛ afi sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for the plant, but as the plant gets older, it uses up that stored starch to maintain its stems and leaves. This leaves behind tough, woody fibers in the tuber, making it hard to cook and eat.
ga: Cassava shishifãi tsuɔ nii kɛtoɔ starch kɛhaa tso lɛ. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ da Ebaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛbu eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso mli tsɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli, ni no haa ewaa akɛ abaahoo ni aye.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants have small ragged holes with saw-dust like dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the central funnel of the maize plant to eat tender inner leaves. Spraying organic extracts like neem water or approved insecticides into the funnel early in the morning kills the pest before it destroys the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye amɛmli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ neem nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsɔne lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ.

english: Yam plants grow as vines that need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to manufacture food for the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves dry and off the wet soil, which prevents leaf diseases and ensures bigger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa tamɔ wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu lɛ aje kpo bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛje shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai anaa ni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is inconsistent, as roots need steady moisture in the soil to draw up calcium to the growing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛgbala calcium kɛba tomato ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme stress, such as severe dry heat or irregular watering. Providing shade during the hottest parts of the afternoon and keeping the soil evenly moist prevents the plant from shedding its blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ latsaa ni mli egbi. loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do I get tiny ears of corn when I plant three or four seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa toi bibii anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds close together forces the crops to compete for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. Giving each seed its own space allows roots to spread out and gather enough resources to build large, healthy ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛbuaa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ toi wuji ni he wa lɛ anaa.

english: Why is my maize crop weak and stunted even though there are no visible weeds growing on the surface of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa jwɛi ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Your field might be infested with Striga, a parasitic weed that attaches itself directly to the roots of maize underground. It steals nutrients and water before it even grows above ground, which stunts the crop unless crop rotation or resistant seeds are used.
ga: Ekolɛ Striga, ni ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmã shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ebɔle oŋmɔji lɛ ahe. Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu dani edaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpa. ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nii lɛ tsu nii.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need to be planted under plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ dumɔwui ashishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct tropical sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living shade, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall but produce very small yields when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into growing big fruits or grains, the plants spend all their energy stretching upward to reach the light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni Tsei kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its newest upper leaves to stay alive, leaving the older lower leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Ha shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my field before maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which have a unique ability to pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the legumes are harvested, that leftover nitrogen feeds the next crop like maize naturally.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Akɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays wet for too long during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe just as much as they need water. Excess water fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing fungal diseases to multiply.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni tsei hu taoɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often a 'false start' followed by a dry spell. Sowing too early means seeds might germinate, but without deeper soil moisture from steady rains, the young seedlings will dry up and die before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale shishijee’ ni nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars eat inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye nii yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the softest, newest leaves inside the growing tip (whorl) of the corn plant. They hide inside where it is safe from sun and predators while chewing through the plant's growth center.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tswaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi (rings) ni miida lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ hei ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe beni amɛyeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ dalɛ hei lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, sudden dry spells, or overwatering. Without balanced moisture and gentle temperatures, the plant aborts the flowers to protect itself from losing too much energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ he. aloo nu babaoo yɛ Kɛji hulutsoo be ni ja kɛ hulutsoo be ni esaaa bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid crop produce weaker plants than the original seed packet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe shishijee dumɔwui akuu lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from two distinct parent plants to produce strong, high-yielding first-generation crops. When you harvest and plant seeds from those crops, their offspring split back into unpredictable genetic traits, usually resulting in lower yields and unequal growth.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ tso ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛji okpa ni odu dumɔwui kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ Amɛshwiei lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛfɔmɔ sui ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than the seeds I planted in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted over thousands of years to thrive in poor soil and harsh conditions. They are naturally faster at taking up water and light than cultivated crop seeds, which need extra care to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii akpei abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ la oya fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ. ni biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa trees from the heat while giving you extra food and income while you wait for cocoa to mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni o-cocoa lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans on the same land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the soil, but leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves in the center of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient crops need to grow green. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or composted manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa ni akwɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise covering the soil around my veggies with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, protects the soil from direct heat, traps moisture so you don't need to water as often, and suppresses weed growth.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting, curling, and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This twisting is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agriculture extension officers prevents this problem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baa ji yucca mosaic hela, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Kɛ́ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ duɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads easily in dark, wet conditions. Pruning extra cocoa branches lets in sunlight and air to dry out the farm, and removing infected pods keeps the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli. kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What are those small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my maize, and how do I protect my field?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔji lɛ ahe?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, which attack the growing tips of young maize plants. Checking your farm regularly in the early morning and applying safe, recommended treatments inside the plant funnels stops them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa leebi ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii shweshweeshwe yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛnaa dani amɛbaafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get too hot or don't get enough water during hot afternoons. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering helps the flowers stay on the plant and develop into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo enáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward in direct sunlight to make energy. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground using wooden stakes prevents leaf rot and allows the yam tubers underground to grow larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite, ni ebaaye ebua sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has become too weak to grow good tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ madu tomato kpakpa?

english: If your tomato plants stay small, look pale, or produce tiny, poor-quality fruits despite receiving water, your soil is exhausted of essential plant nutrients and needs organic manure or fertilizer to regain strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ daraaa, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii ni ehiii yɛ be mli ni onine eshɛ nu nɔ po sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ewaje lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sun and heat. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby protects them from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil moist until they are old enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the leaves up off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha amɛ hulu la babaoo ni eha amɛhe tse kɛjɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tips usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant grow green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants get too stressed by high heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa ha tso lɛ hao fe nine. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and looking crumpled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these small pests early stops leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Mra be mli ni akudɔɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ Ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts like natural food for your maize, improving soil fertility naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes fertilizer away before plant roots can soak it up. This wastes your money and leaves your crops without the nutrients they need.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa bo lɛ akaje onibii amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when heavy water stays on my farm after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Standing water smothers the roots and promotes fungal diseases that cause the tubers to rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa tuber fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Too many shoots (suckers) fight with the main plantain tree for nutrients, light, and water. Removing extra shoots leaves energy for the main stem to produce big, healthy bunches.
ga: Suckers (tso) babaoo yɛ ni kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ miitswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii, la, kɛ nu. Tso lɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo koni ekwɛ niji wuji ni he wa.

english: Why should I cover the surface of my vegetable beds with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa mi-vegetables tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during sunny days, and stops weeds from taking over your bed.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu lɛ mli la ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaha otsu lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my crops need fertilizer even if my farm soil looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ?

english: Over time, plants draw out essential nutrients from the soil to grow and produce pods or fruits. Fertilizer restores these missing nutrients so your crops have enough energy to yield more produce season after season.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmeii loo aduawai. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni elaaje nɛɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: What is the best way to apply fertilizer so my crops actually get the benefit?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ awoɔ ŋmɔshi nii koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná he sɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and placed around the root zone of the plant rather than touching the main stem directly, which allows the roots to absorb the nutrients without burning the crop.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni akɛwo he fɛɛ he. tso lɛ shishifã he lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooota tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni shãaa tso lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off living leaves and branches from my cocoa trees when they are growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛniji ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli be mli ni amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess or shaded branches so sunlight and air can flow through the tree. This prevents black pod disease and ensures the tree spends its food making big pods rather than keeping extra leaves alive.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine loo ni yɔɔ shade lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ tsiɔ black pod hela naa ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji moŋ fe baai ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: How does leaving too many thick branches on my tree affect my final harvest?
ga: Te niji ni mli tse tsɔ ni mishiɔ yɛ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ saa minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When a tree has too many branches, it wastes its water and plant food trying to nourish all those leaves. Removing unneeded stems directs all the nutrients into producing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ niji babaoo Ebaafite nu ni edu niyenii ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha nakai baai lɛ fɛɛ aná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I choose the right seeds to ensure I get a strong crop yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni sa koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa?

english: Using approved, high-yielding seed varieties from certified agricultural officers ensures your crops grow uniformly, resist common local diseases, and yield more pods at harvest time.
ga: Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni jɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli

english: Is it safe to plant crop seeds that come from a completely different region or country?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni jɛ kpokpaa loo maŋ kroko kwraa mli lɛ?

english: Seeds brought from outside may not perform well because they are not adapted to your local rainfall, soil, or pests. It is safer to use tested seeds recommended for your specific district.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ kɛbaa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhe esaaa kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni aka amɛ akwɛ ni ajie yi akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do crop buyers offer lower prices if my beans are not dried properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa kɛji akɛ midumɔwui lɛ egbiko jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans with too much moisture develop mold during transport and lose their flavor quality. Buyers pay premium prices for clean, well-dried beans because they store longer and produce better chocolate or processed goods.
ga: Nuts ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ, ni ebaaha amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ aba shi. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha ŋmeii ni he tse ni egbi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni afee tsokolate loo nibii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What basic things can I do on my farm to make my crop yield increase every year?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nibii manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ daa afi?

english: Combining regular fertilizer application, timely pruning, clearing weeds, and protecting your crops from pests keeps the plants healthy and boosts overall farm production over time.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ aaafata he Afoɔ jwɛi yɛ be naa ni abuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ehaa nibii fɛɛ ni anáa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does doing basic processing of my harvest before selling help my farm income?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shishijee nibii ni mikpaa lɛ ahe nitsumɔ dani mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔ mli shika ni mináa lɛ?

english: Processing crops—such as fermenting and properly drying beans—increases their market value, prevents spoilage, and opens opportunities to sell directly to buyers who pay higher prices for ready-to-use produce.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli kɛ ŋmeii ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha jarayeli jara aya hiɛ Etsi fitemɔ naa ni eha hegbɛi ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni asaa he ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why does cocoa quality matter so much if international buyers are going to process it anyway?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bɔ ni kookoo lɛ hi ha lɛ he hiaa waa kɛji akɛ majimaji ateŋ jarayelɔi baatsu he nii lɛ?

english: International factories require high-standard raw beans free from defects, mold, or chemical contamination to make quality food products. Meeting these standards ensures your produce stays in high demand globally.
ga: Nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ biɔ ŋmeii ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni kɛ shishitoo mlai ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kpãa gbee, ni tɔmɔi, ŋmeii loo tsofai ni fiteɔ nii bɛ mli, bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Shishitoo mlai nɛɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ haa onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi akɛ nɔ ni ataoɔ waa yɛ je lɛŋ he fɛɛ he.

english: Why are my groundnut plants producing empty shells with no seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods usually happen when the soil lacks calcium or when the ground gets too dry while the nuts are forming underground. Adding agricultural lime to your soil gives the plants the calcium they need to fill out the shells with healthy nuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ okwaayeli mli lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa calcium ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ awo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my land is better for growing groundnuts or growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmei loo ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Groundnuts prefer loose, sandy soil because the pods need to push easily into the dirt to grow. Maize needs heavier, richer soil with plenty of organic matter and water to support its tall stalks and big cobs.
ga: Peanuts sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ejaakɛ ehe miihia ni ashɛre ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii, ni yɔɔ nii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa. Eyɛ nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nu ni fiɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ asɛɛ.

english: If my groundnuts are not yielding well on my farm, why is planting maize on that same land a good idea?
ga: Kɛji mi ŋmeii lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa?

english: Groundnuts naturally trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil when they die. Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen, so planting maize after groundnuts allows the maize to use that stored plant food to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ amɛgboi. Akɛ nitrogen babaoo haa ŋmãa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ŋmãa lɛ ni ekɛ tso niyenii ni ato lɛ atsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why does my maize turn yellow and stay small even when I water it regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Unlike groundnuts, maize cannot make its own soil food, so it needs compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer to stay green and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ ŋmei lɛ, ŋmei nyɛŋ afee niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do groundnut pods form underground when the yellow flowers bloom up in the air?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ beni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, their stems bend down toward the soil. These stems, called pegs, push themselves into the dirt where the nuts safely grow and mature underground.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ akɛ pins. Tsɔ ohe kɛya shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ lɛ mli ni okwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe?

english: When maize is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper space ensures every stalk gets enough food to develop large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Nu Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Which crop survives better without rainfall for a few weeks, groundnuts or maize?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii fioo komɛi? ŋmei loo ŋmei

english: Groundnuts handle short dry spells much better than maize because their roots reach deeper into the soil and their leafy bushes conserve water. Maize wilts quickly and will fail to produce cobs if it lacks water during its flowering stage.
ga: Peanuts tsuɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai kukuji ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni etso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Abɛi shwieɔ oya ni efeŋ ŋmei kɛji nu fite emli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants rolling up tight like pencils during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pensil yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up tight during hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing water in the sun. It is a natural defense mechanism showing that the crop is thirsty and experiencing heat stress.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni hulu lɛ akaje mli lɛ akaje mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye dumɔwui kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ.

english: How can I check if my groundnuts are fully ready to harvest before the pods start rotting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ ekpa kwraa dani ŋmeii lɛ aje shishi amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Pull up one or two test bushes and open the pods. If the insides of the shells have dark brown or purple veins and the nuts fill the casing tightly, your groundnuts are mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Gbalamɔ kaa tso kome loo enyɔ ni ogbele pods lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ eyi obɔ ni ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmeii lɛ eshɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and white powder inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ powda yɛŋ ni yɔɔ baa teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Small holes and powdery dirt in the central funnel of maize leaves are signs of armyworm caterpillars. These pests eat the growing heart of the maize plant, slowing its growth unless caught early.
ga: Buu bibii kɛ muji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji ŋmeii ahe okadii. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ. Enɛ baaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ja amɔ lɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily in strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and moisture, helping the young cocoa trees survive until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Can I leave big trees standing on my farm when I plant new cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu kookoo hee?

english: Yes, leaving a few tall trees provides beneficial shade for cocoa, but having too many trees blocks sunlight completely, which prevents the cocoa trees from flowering and bearing pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Tsei fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛhaa kookoo lɛ. Shi tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ hulu la lɛ naa kwraa. Enɛ haaa cacao tsei lɛ afee fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Why is it important for me to clear the weeds under my plantain and cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao dumɔwui kɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients from young crops. Clearing the ground around the stems helps your cocoa and plantains grow faster and stay healthy.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. He ni ebɔle he lɛ mli saamɔ Tsoi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo kɛ plantains ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I cut off the extra small shoots growing at the base of my cocoa trunk?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo ŋwɛi bibii lɛ? Ani ajie nakai ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, these small shoots (often called suckers) waste the tree's energy. Removing them allows the main trunk to stay strong and produce healthy cocoa pods.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ (ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii) lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaawaje tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ni ebaaha kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why are my cocoa trees growing very large without producing any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miida waa ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trees can put all their energy into growing leaves and height if they get too much shade or are not pruned properly, leaving no energy for producing pods.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ awo baai ni miida kɛ dalɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ enine shɛ hulutsoo be babaoo nɔ loo afolɔko lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, No hewɔ lɛ, hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How long does a new cocoa tree take before it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Improved cocoa varieties usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years if properly cared for, while older varieties may take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni eda lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the young plant is getting too much direct sunlight, lacks nutrients in the soil, or has water logging around its roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso bibioo lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nu ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know how many cocoa trees to plant on my land so they aren't crowded?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kookoo tsei enyiɛ ni esa akɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekafee nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi?

english: Cocoa trees should generally be spaced about 3 meters apart. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, air flow, and soil nutrients to yield well.
ga: Esa akɛ bei pii lɛ, cocoa tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ená yibii kpakpai

english: How does getting a cocoa license or selling through a licensed buyer help me as a farmer?
ga: Te kookoo he gbɛŋmɛɛ wolo ni minine shɛɔ nɔ loo ni mihɔ̃ɔ kɛtsɔɔ mɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi akɛ okwaafonyo lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Selling to licensed buying companies ensures your cocoa beans are weighed accurately and that you receive the standard, guaranteed government price for your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ ohɔ̃ɔ oha nitsumɔhe ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni heɔ nii lɛ, ehaa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ asusuɔ o-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. Ni onine shɛɔ jara ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishijee?

english: Good cocoa land has deep, fertile soil that drains water well without flooding, and gets a balance of good rain and sunlight throughout the year.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii. Nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ, nu afua bɛ mli, ni nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be kpakpa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Organic fertilizers come from natural plant or animal materials that feed the soil over time and improve its structure, while chemical fertilizers feed the crop directly but can degrade soil health over long periods.
ga: Organic fertilizers jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei loo kooloi anibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ be kɛ bei amli ni ehaa egbɛjianɔtoo lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii tɛ̃ɛ. Shi ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ afite yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why does my soil become weak and less productive after planting on it for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ewooo yibii babaoo yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops remove natural nutrients from the soil every season as they grow. Adding organic fertilizers restores those missing nutrients and builds up healthy soil organisms so crops can thrive again.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe daa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Organic fertilizer ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni etswa shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni hi jogbaŋŋ ema shi koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will applying organic fertilizer burn my crop roots if I put too much by mistake?
ga: Ani organic fertilizer baashã mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he yɛ oshara mli?

english: Organic fertilizers release their nutrients slowly into the soil, which makes them much safer for crop roots than chemical fertilizers that can burn young plants when applied heavily.
ga: Organic fertilizers lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiofio kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsei shishifãi fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii kɛ akɛwo mli babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow instead of growing dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the crop is starving for nitrogen. Applying an organic fertilizer feeds the crop the right balance of plant foods to restore a healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni sa ni baaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How does using organic fertilizer help my crops survive when the rains stop early?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic matter helps the soil hold onto rainwater like a sponge, keeping moisture near the plant roots for a longer time during dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli tamɔ sponji. Enɛ haa nu ni bɛŋkɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How soon will I see my crops responding after I apply organic fertilizer to the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii oya beni mikɛ organic fertilizer ewo miŋmɔji lɛ amli sɛɛ?

english: Because organic fertilizers nourish the soil naturally, you will typically see crops growing greener leaves and thicker stems within one to two weeks.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ bei pii lɛ obaana akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli.

english: Can proper organic soil feeding help my crops resist pests and diseases better?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni sa ni akɛyeɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai jogbaŋŋ?

english: Strongly fed crops develop thicker stem walls and stronger roots, making it harder for insects to damage them and helping them fight off diseases naturally.
ga: Tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii kpakpa lɛ feɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli tse kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa kooloi bibii akɛ amɛaafite nii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai. yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Heat stress causes plants to lose water faster than their roots can drink it. Rich organic soil encourages deep root growth so plants can absorb water faster during hot afternoons.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli lɛ haa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ nu oya yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow large top leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen without balanced minerals, they spend all their energy growing top leaves instead of storing food in roots or tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ ni mineral balance ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ woɔ tso sisifãhi aloo tso ɔmɛ a mi.

english: Flowers drop off when plants face nutrient shortages or heat stress. Organic inputs provide a steady nutrient flow that helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruits form.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpe. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the middle during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛteŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize that start from the tip and move down the middle of the leaf usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important soil food that helps crops stay green and grow strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa hewalɛ.

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows plant diseases and pests to build up in the ground, causing smaller harvests over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cassava roots store a lot of moisture, so when water stays on the farm for too long, air cannot reach the roots underground, causing them to drown and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi baanyɛ ato ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds after the first rain falls in the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until you get two or three heavy rains so the soil is wet deep down, because a single rain can trick seeds into sprouting, only for them to dry up and die if the sun returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ kuku kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃. kɛkɛ koni eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong heat from the sun and need shade trees or plantains nearby to protect them and keep the air cool while they are growing.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. ni ebiɔ ni tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ aná hulutsoo koni amɛbu kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he ni amɛha ejɔ be mli ni amɛduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves high into the air to catch sunlight; climbing up wooden stakes helps the plant make more food to grow bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Tsoi ni akɛkwɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Beans and cowpeas have a special ability to pull food from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the maize plants growing next to them without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛgbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ fataaa he.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal the water, sunlight, and food from the soil that your crops need to grow well and yield a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper flowers fall off without making fruit when the air gets too hot, when the plant gets too little or too much water, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náa nu fioo loo babaoo tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny flying insects that spread diseases to the plant, or by severe heat and dry conditions that stress the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni foɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ hela eshwaa tsei anɔ loo kɛjɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ mli.

english: Aside from applying chemical fertilizer, is there anything else I can add to my soil to help my maize grow better?
ga: Kɛfata tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ Mɛni kroko abaanyɛ akɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni eye ebua ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, adding compost or well-rotted animal manure improves soil structure, helps the ground retain water during dry spells, and continuously releases natural nutrients to feed your maize crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kpo be fɛɛ be koni ekɛha o-corn tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged and choking the roots. Checking soil drainage and applying manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer can help restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ miitsi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen in the soil, it puts all its energy into growing tall stalks and leafy leaves instead of expanding its roots. Using balanced nutrients prevents leafy overgrowth and encourages tuber development.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baa lɛ aya hiɛ fe nine, ni ehaa tuber lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants keep falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps protect the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves curl up tightly during the middle of the day when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in intense sunlight is a natural survival trick crops use to reduce water loss from evaporation. If the leaves relax again in the late afternoon, your plant is simply managing heat stress naturally.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ekoŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ otsei lɛ miiye dɔlɛ he haomɔ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my young crops as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle mitso lɛ he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and cannot compete with aggressive weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all available food and water to build strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why should I space my maize seeds out during planting instead of dropping several seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he beni miduɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, du wuhi fuu kɛ pee kake ngɛ bu kake mi.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces them to fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around young yam plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun, retains moisture, reduces soil erosion, and prevents weeds from growing around the crop.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ aba shi ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Apart from spraying liquid chemicals, how can I stop insects from destroying my cabbage leaves?
ga: Kɛfata tsofai ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ kooloi ni fiteɔ kaabii baai lɛ anaa?

english: You can protect cabbages naturally by rotating your crops each season, planting strong-smelling herbs nearby to confuse insects, or applying natural neem leaf extract to deter pests.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu o-cabbage lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ tsofai ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo. koni akɛfutu kooloi bibii Aloo akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ atsu nii ni akɛtsi kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa.

english: How can I tell if my crop is suffering from a disease rather than just lacking water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ moŋ fe ni nu efo mli kɛkɛ?

english: A thirsty crop wilts during the day but revives at night after watering. A diseased crop often shows dark spots, mold, sticky fluids, or rotten stems that do not improve even when the plant gets water.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ gboɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Shi ebaahi shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ beni awo lɛ nu sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ nu ni kpɛɔ. loo stem rot ni ehiii kɛji tso lɛ ná nu po.

english: Do all the crops I plant on my farm need to be pollinated before they can produce fruit?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awo mli dani amɛwo yibii?

english: No, not all crops require active pollination to give you a harvest. Some crops can still yield fruits naturally on their own, although proper care and pollination can make them produce much better.
ga: Dabi, jeee tsei fɛɛ he miihia ni okɛ pollin awo mli dani onyɛ okpa. Tsei komɛi hu baanyɛ awo adebɔɔ mli yibii kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Eyɛ mli akɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ pollination baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ waa moŋ.

english: Is it possible for my crop to still give me a harvest if bees or insects do not visit the flowers?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii lolo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii krokomɛi eyaaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli?
