english: Yes, certain crops can still yield fruits even without insect visitors or manual pollination, though ensuring good pollination usually leads to a much bigger and healthier harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei komɛi baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii lolo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ebasaraa amɛ loo amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeee ŋmɔshi nibii po. Shi bei pii lɛ, pollination kpakpa ni akwɛɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: What actually happens to my crops when pollination takes place?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ pollination ba?

english: Pollination helps the crop's flowers turn into fruits and seeds. When pollination is done well, your plants produce larger, healthier, and more abundant fruits.
ga: Pollination yeɔ ebuaa tso fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ dumɔwui. Kɛji pollination lɛ gbe naa Otso lɛ baawo yibii wuji. Na hewalɛ kpakpa kɛ fɔmɔ babaoo

english: If my crops are already producing some fruits naturally, why should I bother helping them with pollination?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii momo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maye mabua amɛ ni amɛfee pollination?

english: While some crops yield naturally, active pollination helps your farm thrive by increasing the overall quantity, size, and quality of the fruits you harvest.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi woɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ, shi Pollination yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔ lɛ ni eyaa hiɛ kɛtsɔ aduawai ni okpaa lɛ ayibɔ, amɛdalɛ, kɛ amɛhe fɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is proper farm preparation so important before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa miŋmɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Preparing your land well gives your seeds and young plants a strong foundation by improving soil condition, removing weeds, and allowing roots to easily access nutrients and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui lɛ shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ ni yaa hiɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli, kɛ shishifãi ni haa amɛnáa niyenii kɛ nu mlɛo lɛ nɔ.

english: If I prepare my land very well, will my crops automatically give me maximum yields without any other extra care?
ga: Kɛ misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji mikwɛɛɛ nɔ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ?

english: Good land preparation gives your crops a great start, but combining it with other key practices like proper weeding, crop care, and pollination helps the plants truly thrive and reach their highest yield.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ kpakpa haa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛ akɛ nifeemɔi titrii krokomɛi tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Which task is more important for my harvest: preparing the land or pollinating the crops?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔ he hiaa fe mikpamɔ lɛ: shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Both work together for a successful harvest. Preparing the land ensures your crop grows strong and healthy, while pollination ensures those healthy flowers actually develop into plenty of fruits.
ga: Mɛi enyɔ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa nikpamɔ ni yeɔ omanye. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooosaa lɛ haa onibii lɛ daa waa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, pollination yeɔ ebuaa nakai fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai babaoo.

english: What key practices can I combine to make sure my crops thrive and give me the best possible harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ nifeemɔi titrii manyɛ mikɛfata he koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ada ni amɛwo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: To get the best yield, you should start with good land preparation, maintain clean fields, and ensure your crops receive adequate pollination when they begin to flower.
ga: bɔni afee ni oná nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ Esa akɛ oje shishi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni ooosaa nɔ. Ha ŋmɔji lɛ amli atse Ni okwɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa beni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my crop plants look green and healthy, but still produce very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa lɛ? Shi ani ekɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ haa lolo?

english: Healthy plants show that your land preparation and soil are good, but a low fruit yield often means the flowers were not properly pollinated to turn into fruits.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ hi. Shi bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni baa shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo aduawai.

english: How can I tell if my flowering crops need help with pollination on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi fɔfɔi tsei lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ pollination he yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If your crops produce plenty of flowers but many of them fall off without forming fruits, or if you notice very few insects around your field, helping with pollination can boost your fruit yield.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii. Aloo, kɛji ona kooloi bibii fioo ko pɛ ni bɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, pollination yelikɛbuamɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha oyibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, a main food crops need to stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni niyenii titri ni aduɔ lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnut plants pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the groundnuts are harvested and roots decompose, they leave behind rich natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmeii ni shishifãi lɛ egboi Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle and die when planted in an open, sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out and burn easily in harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains nearby to block excess sun and keep the air cool and humid around them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ fe nine tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛtsi hulu la ni fa fe nine lɛ naa. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl downward during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl and droop to reduce the surface area exposed to direct heat, preventing water from evaporating too quickly from the plant until the evening cools down.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ kɛyashi ebaajɔ.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to sprout after I buried them very deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too deep, they burn through all their stored food energy trying to push up through the heavy dirt before reaching the surface sunlight, causing them to die underground.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shãa niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ. Amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi dumɔwui lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ dani amɛgbee hulu la lɛ mli. ni haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why are my pepper plants staying short and stunted even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air in the soil just as much as water. Overwatering or heavy soil starves the roots of oxygen, preventing them from taking up nutrients and growing properly.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ agbɛnɛ hu nu. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Ehaaa amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant yam on the exact same piece of land two years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii enyɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting yam in the same spot continuously lets soil pests and rot diseases build up, leading to smaller, damaged roots in the second year. Changing crops starves those pests.
ga: Kɛ́ oya nɔ odu sweet potato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii abua amɛhe naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nakai kooloi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and pale even when there are no insect pests on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds grow close, your crops starve because the weeds consume the resources first.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings sharply from very dry to very wet. Keeping soil evenly moist with grass mulch prevents flower loss.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I cut away the extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie Plantain shishitoo lɛ

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients from the main plantain stem. Removing all but one or two strong stems allows the plant to put its energy into making a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep down into the soil beyond the reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers underneath stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below. Balanced soil nutrients help push energy down into the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ tsiɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil has lost its food and needs manure before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo muji ni ehe miihia ni awo mli dani adu nii?

english: If your soil hardens like brick after rain, turns pale grey, washes away easily, or your crops grow very slowly with light-green leaves, the soil lacks organic matter and needs compost or animal manure to regain its strength.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ brikii yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse Eshɛɔ oya Aloo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo waa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni enyɛ ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together on the same farm with my cassava, or will they fight each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cassava lɛ? Aloo amɛbaawuu yɛ amɛteŋ?

english: Yes, you can plant them together. Cowpeas cover the ground to stop weeds and pull natural fertilizer from the air into the soil, which feeds the cassava as it grows.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome kɛkwɛ. Akɛ sũ woɔ tsina ŋmeii amli koni egbe jwɛi lɛ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛba sũ lɛ mli, ni no baaha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: What is causing the young leaves in the center of my maize plants to look torn up with small brown dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni haa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ feɔ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the soft center leaves to feed, so you need to inspect your farm early and apply recommended control measures before they destroy the main growing stem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai bibii ateŋ koni amɛye nii. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ lɛ atsu nii dani akpata tso titri ni miida lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko baa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when hidden soil pests like root nematodes or stem borers chew through the roots and underground base, weakening the plant's grip in the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ, ŋmɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishigbɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa bɔ ni tsei kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my pepper flowers dropping off the plants without turning into peppers when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to pepper plants, making them shed their flowers to save water and protect themselves. Covering the soil with dried leaves (mulching) and watering regularly helps keep the flowers on the stems.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni ji pepper lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (mulching) kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes get black, rotten spots at the bottom end while they are ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ diŋ beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: That black spot is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, which is usually caused by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely between rain or watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni ashwieɔ lɛ teŋ.

english: Yams rot fast if they were bruised during harvest, left under direct sunlight right after digging, or stored in a dark barn without proper air flow to keep them cool and dry.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Shi ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni ogbe sũ lɛ sɛɛ. Aloo okɛto ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli koni eha edɔ ni egbi.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cover the soil around our tomato plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ jwɛi ni egbi atsu nii akɛ mulch ni bɔleɔ tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool and moist, stops water from drying up too fast in the sun, and prevents soil diseases from splashing onto the leaves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi (mulching) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Ni tsi helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkashwie baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does swamp rice do well in standing water while my corn rots if water stays on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ swamp rice tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Rice plants are naturally designed to transport oxygen down to their roots even when submerged in water, whereas corn roots need air pockets in dry soil to breathe and will suffocate in standing water.
ga: Afee ŋmãa tsei yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi kɛya amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ awo amɛ nu mli po. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ koni amɛmu ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to lift watermelons off the bare dirt using straw while they are growing?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ jwɛi awo watermelon nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛmiida lɛ?

english: Yes, resting watermelons on straw or grass keeps them away from damp, bare soil, which prevents ground insects and fungal diseases from rotting the bottom of the fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ akɛ watermelon lɛ fɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni watermelon lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ akafite yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are telling me the soil is too dry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miikɛɛ mi akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, their leaves will start to curl inward, droop, or turn yellowish during the hottest part of the day to conserve moisture.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛya mli, ebaagbee shi, loo ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why does my cocoyam grow much bigger leaves when planted near riverbanks than on the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ baabii wuji kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ faa ko naa fe gɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoyam naturally loves moisture and broadens its leaves to grow strong when its roots have easy, continuous access to damp soil like that near streams.
ga: Cocoyam sumɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni mli edɔ ni ebaakwɛ̃ɔ baai ni wa waa kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ ná shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ mlɛo ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛyaa, tamɔ yɛ faai ahe.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings droop and die when I move them out into the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛtee shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young pepper seedlings are soft and delicate. They need temporary shade made from palm fronds for the first few days so they do not dry out before their roots settle in the soil.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛ ŋmei tsei ahe baai fee yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni ekagbi dani shishifãi lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Will leaving dried crop leaves on my farm after harvest help my soil for the next planting season?
ga: Ani tsei ahe baai ni egbi ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving dead leaves and stalks breaks down over time into natural manure, returning good nutrients to the earth and keeping the soil soft and rich for your next crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi ni ashiɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii kpakpai akuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant cassava on raised mounds of dirt instead of flat, hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds create loose, airy soil that lets cassava tubers expand easily and allows heavy rainwater to drain away so the roots do not rot underground.
ga: Gɔji feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa cassava shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa mlɛo. ni oha nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ atsɔ kɛya Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How does planting cover crops like cowpea protect my bare farmland?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu midumɔi ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ ahe?

english: Cover crops spread like a green carpet over the bare earth, blocking the harsh sun from drying out the soil, preventing heavy rains from washing away topsoil, and adding natural food to the dirt.
ga: Tsei ni ha shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ gbɛ eshwa tamɔ kapɛti eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he

english: How can I harvest my garden eggs safely so the main plant stays healthy and keeps bearing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ŋmeii yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe? Koni tsei titrii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii daa

english: Using a sharp blade or gentle snap at the stem instead of pulling forcefully keeps the main branches from tearing, protecting the plant from injury and allowing it to yield more fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsɔne ni mli wa atsu nii loo gbá tso lɛ blɛoo moŋ fe ni ooogbala lɛ waa. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso nine titri lɛ akagbala. Buu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ pilamɔ he ni oha ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle direct heat. They require shade trees like plantains to shelter them from intense sunlight and hold moisture in the soil until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa shade, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha amɛhe shade kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni amɛha sũ lɛ mli nu ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Leaves curl up in high heat to protect themselves from losing too much water through evaporation. Once the sun goes down and the air cools, the plant usually bounces back to normal.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu ni fa fe nine akafite kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited light, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow thick stalks and produce larger cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu amɛshi amɛhe koni amɛná la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu fioo Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my crops grow so poorly when weeds are left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your main crops, leaving your plants weak and starving.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii hiɛjoolɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crops perform poorly if I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating different crops refreshes the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Excess water trapped in clay or poorly drained soil smothers cassava roots, preventing them from breathing and inviting fungal diseases that cause rotting.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haaa amɛmu ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ baa.

english: Fertilizers are like concentrated salt; if applied to dry soil, they pull water out of the plant roots and burn them. Moisture helps dissolve the fertilizer safely into the plant's food.
ga: Fertilizer tamɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, amɛbaajie nu kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli ni amɛshã. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ tsei aniyenii amli shweshweeshwe.

english: Flowers drop off when plants experience stress from heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do caterpillars always hide and chew inside the middle leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe be fɛɛ be ni amɛyeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms target the soft, tender inner leaves (the whorl) where moisture gathers and they can stay hidden from heat and predators while feeding.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ kwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ (rings) he ni ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why does removing some of the extra leaves on my tomato plants help them produce better fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mijie baai ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Pruning lower leaves improves airflow to stop diseases and redirects the plant's energy away from growing useless foliage and into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛkpa helai, ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa ni miida lɛ amli kɛyaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops look weak and wilted around 11 o'clock in the morning when the sun gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ aaafee 11 a.m. be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: During the hot mid-morning heat, plants reduce water loss by closing small pores in their leaves, which can cause them to temporarily droop until the sun sets or cooler temperatures return.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ leebi lɛ Tsei haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛŋaa lɛ nɔ, ni baanyɛ aha baai lɛ agbi be kukuoo ko kɛyashi hulu lɛ baanyɔ shi loo hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow when I cut down all the shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mifoɔ hulutsoo tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from larger trees like plantains or timber trees because direct midday heat burns their tender leaves and dries out the surrounding soil.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hɔnɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei wuji, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ cowpea kɛ ŋmãa afata he lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants pull natural food (nitrogen) from the air into the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plants and helps them grow bigger without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ gbalaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii Ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa awo mli.

english: What causes my young maize leaves to look like they have holes eaten through them overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-baby corn baai lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu yɛ mli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: Holes in young leaves are usually caused by insects like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on tender plant leaves during the cooler evening and early morning hours.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai yɛ gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bulɛ baa tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves look light green or yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Light green or yellow leaves mean your soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, showing that the soil is exhausted and needs compost, manure, or fertilizer to feed the crop.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo onibii amli.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch of hot sun, which will dry out the soil and kill young sprouts before the main rainy season actually starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ ni efiteɔ tsei bibii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: How do weeds growing near my cassava plants stop my roots from growing big?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe lɛ aha mishishifãi lɛ akakwɛ̃?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your cassava, leaving less food for the plant to swell its underground tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmei mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa niyenii fioo koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my pepper plants drying up and dying even though the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Too much water around the roots creates fungal diseases that rot the roots, preventing the plant from drinking water and causing it to wilt as if it were dry.
ga: nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ baa. Ehaa tso lɛ nuɔ nu ni ehaa egbiɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow together, they fight for the same soil food, leaving the main plantain tree with small, light fruit bunches instead of a large yield.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛyeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ tso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni afee babaoo lɛ

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly if I leave them sitting on wet ground in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Freshly dug yams have thin skin and small cuts that let soil bacteria and fungi enter when left on wet ground, causing them to spoil faster in the heat.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni atsa ehee lɛ Kpãa bibioo ko baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni eyɛ ŋmei bibioo ko ni haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ oya kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo la mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunshine. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and soil moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava stems need to be planted at an angle instead of flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle helps the roots grow deeper and spread evenly into the soil, anchoring the plant firmly against wind and encouraging bigger tuber growth.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ 45 degree angle mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Ehiɛɔ tso lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulb lɛ ni edaa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni ená bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food using sunlight captured by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves high into the light, allowing the plant to generate maximum energy and store it underground in large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ hulu la ni ebaai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lɛ feɔ eniyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ bulb agboi amli.

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but the fertilised flowers push into the soil because the actual nut pods need the dark, moist earth to grow safely away from heat and surface pests.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi fɔfɔi ni awo amɛ fɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahewɔ. Ehe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ koni ekwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ ŋwɛi dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani eyibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer heat stress or lack water. Giving plants consistent moisture and light shade during high temperature periods helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ fɛ̃i kɛ la ha tso lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ hiɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it best to plant my maize right at the start of the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The season's first rain releases a quick burst of stored nitrogen trapped in dry soil. Early-planted maize catches this natural nutrient boost, growing faster and stronger than late-planted crops.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ oya. Abele ni adu mra lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excessive rain washes essential nutrients like nitrogen deeper into the dirt beyond root level, while waterlogged soil starves roots of oxygen, preventing the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cool, rainy weather causes fungal spores to spread quickly across cocoa trees. Pruning branches lets sunlight and air pass through, drying out moisture that encourages black pod rot.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ cacao tsei lɛ amli fɛɛ. Pruning allows sunlight and air to pass through. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do tiny green insects keep gathering on the undersides of my cowpea leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Insects hide under leaves to stay protected from direct hot sun and heavy rain while drinking the plant's sap, which slowly steals energy the crop needs to make healthy pods.
ga: Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he beni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ, ni fiofio lɛ, no juɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni wa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots on the bottom while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: This rot happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium, usually caused by uneven watering where soil dries out completely and is then soaked with heavy water.
ga: This rot occurs when the plant is unable to absorb enough calcium. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. The soil is completely dry and then soaked with a large amount of water.

english: Why should I spend money to build a greenhouse when I can just grow my crops directly on my open land for free?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shika he hiaa mi koni mikɛma ŋmɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Be mli ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ yaka.

english: A greenhouse structure protects your crops from extreme sun, heavy rainfall, and destructive pests. This protection allows you to grow high-quality vegetables like tomatoes and peppers all year round, leading to higher yields and better market prices.
ga: Greenhouse gbɛjianɔtoi buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Nɛkɛ hebuu nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa yibii babaoo baa, ni jarayeli jara hu hiɔ shi.

english: Why does constructing a covered crop structure require so much money upfront?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli kwɔ maa biɔ ni akɛ shika babaoo awo mli kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ?

english: The initial cost goes into durable materials designed to last for years, such as UV-protected plastic covers, sturdy wooden or metal framing, insect-proof nets, and drip irrigation systems.
ga: Shishijee shika ni akɛwoɔ mli ji nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni afee koni ehi shi afii babaoo, tamɔ plastic ni akɛhaa nɔ ni buɔ UV he lɛ. Tso loo dade frem kooloi kɛ nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo

english: Is it better for me to attempt building a greenhouse alone or join a group of local farmers to do it together?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikome too loo mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akuu ko baama ŋmɔ ko?

english: Partnering with other farmers allows you to pool financial resources to cover construction costs, share the physical labor, and combine produce to sell in larger quantities to major buyers.
ga: Kɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi afee ekome lɛ Ehaa okɛ shika feɔ ekome kɛwoɔ tsumaa he nyɔmɔ. amɛjaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ ekome koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ babaoo amɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ babaoo.

english: What key factors should I look for when choosing the right spot on my farmland to place a crop structure?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ matao beni mihalaa he ni sa yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛto miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: You need flat land with good soil drainage that gets full sunlight throughout the day, stays safe from strong destructive winds, and is located very close to a clean, reliable water source.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia bo. ni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli Shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ mli. ni eyɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni mli tse ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to build my crop structure close to a regular water supply?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ni sa lɛ?

english: Crops inside a greenhouse are completely sheltered from natural rainfall, meaning they rely entirely on manual watering or drip lines. Without a reliable water source nearby, the crops will quickly dry out and die.
ga: Abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe kwraa kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehe afɔ̃ nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ loo nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Does the direction my greenhouse faces make a difference in how my crops will grow?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni mi-greenhouse lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Yes, orienting the structure east-to-west ensures that sunlight is evenly distributed across your crops throughout the day while allowing natural air movement to cool the interior.
ga: Hɛɛ, bɔ ni tsũ lɛ tsɔɔ bokagbɛ kɛyaa anaigbɛ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa onibii fɛɛ amli yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsu lɛ mli lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to consult an expert before constructing a greenhouse on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mayabi mɔ ko ni le nii jogbaŋŋ dani matswa ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Agricultural specialists help you avoid costly mistakes by selecting durable materials suitable for local weather, positioning the structure correctly, and installing effective ventilation and irrigation.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi baanyɛ aye abua bo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tɔmɔi ni jara wa he kɛtsɔ nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni sa kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni ooohala lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tsɔne lɛ ato he jogbaŋŋ. ni akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ awo mli.

english: What land preparations do I need to complete before erecting the frame of my greenhouse?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ ehe hiaa ni masaa dani matswa ŋmɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: You must thoroughly clear all weeds, level the ground, remove sharp stones, and treat the soil to eliminate hidden pests and disease spores before putting up the shelter.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Jiemɔ tɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni otsa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ojie tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ dani oma shĩa.

english: Can I plant directly into the normal ground soil inside my new greenhouse structure?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-greenhouse hee lɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: You can use ground soil, but it should first be enriched with compost and treated to remove soil-borne diseases. Many farmers also use clean soil substitutes like treated coconut coir to prevent root diseases.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ sũ atsu nii. Shi esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he klɛŋklɛŋ ni atsa lɛ koni ejie helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ. Okwaafoi babaoo hu kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ ni he tse najiaŋ tamɔ ŋmei ni atsa lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtsi shishifãi ahe helai anaa.

english: Which crops should I plant inside a crop structure to make back my construction investment quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu yɛ mi tsei ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli koni maná shika ni mikɛwo tsumaa mli lɛ oya?

english: High-value vegetables with steady market demand—such as sweet peppers, cucumbers, and tomatoes—are ideal because greenhouse conditions allow them to produce continuous, high-quality harvests.
ga: Aduawai ni jara wa waa ni jara nɔ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, tamɔ bell peppers, cucumbers kɛ tomato lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ greenhouse mli lɛ haa amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yaa nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate root systems and cannot withstand direct heat and sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them protects them from harsh sun and keeps moisture in the soil until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantain loo cassava, yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves along the middle vein usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer, like Urea or well-rotted manure, around the plant helps fix this problem and brings back healthy leaf growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni etsɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ. Tso lɛ baaye abua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ ni eha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but yield very tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, or if plants are spaced too closely together, the cassava puts all its energy into leaf growth instead of storing nutrients down in the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. aloo kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaai lɛ akwɛmɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baato eyitso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves or transmitting a plant virus. Controlling these insects early with appropriate sprays prevents leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbeɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and yellowish powder in the whorl?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni powda ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the central leaf funnel (whorl). Applying recommended insecticides early inside the whorl prevents them from destroying the growing point of the maize plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii (rings) lɛ. Akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii mra ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii. Ring lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anaa koni ekafite hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: This condition is called Blossom End Rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot absorb enough calcium, often due to dry soil or irregular watering while the fruits are forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni baa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be beni aduawai miifee lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why drop flowers off my cowpea plants without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi fɔfɔi ni jɛ mi-cowpea tso lɛ mli lɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa efeee lɛ?

english: Flower dropping in cowpeas is usually caused by tiny pests called flower thrips eating the delicate flower parts. Spraying the crop just as flower buds begin to appear protects them so pods can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ tsina ŋmei nɔ lɛ baa. Atsɛɔ amɛ flower thrips, ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie tso lɛ nɔ beni fɔfɔii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ afee.

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow at once forces them to compete with the main plant for food and water. Pruning down extra suckers leaves enough nutrients for the main plant to yield a large bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ suckers (tsoji) babaoo gbɛ ni amɛdara shikome lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Does staking my yam vines really help the tubers underground grow bigger?
ga: Ani mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Yes, staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground so they can receive direct sunlight to produce food. This food travels down into the ground to feed the tubers and make them bigger.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking baawó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Niyenii nɛɛ fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eyaha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni eha amɛdara.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of soil nutrients, while leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, naturally restoring fertility for the next season.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo aba ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods now that they are over 30 years old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni eye fe afii 30 lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 25 to 30 years, their natural production slows down significantly, and they become more vulnerable to diseases. Even if the tree looks alive, its internal systems become less efficient at pulling nutrients from the soil to form new pods.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa. Ni helai ahe oshara babaoo yɛ, kɛji tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ wala po. Shi amɛmli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ miifee nɔ ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jiemɔ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii heei.

english: Should I completely clear my old cocoa farm to start over, or just plant new seedlings between the old trees?
ga: Esa akɛ majie kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mije shishi ekoŋŋ. Aloo dumɔ dumɔwui heei kɛkɛ yɛ tsei momo lɛ ateŋ.

english: Cutting down old, unproductive trees and fully replanting is often better than planting among old trees. Old trees compete for sunlight and soil nutrients, and they can easily pass on latent diseases or pests to young seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi akɛ aaafolɔ tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ ashwie shi ni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ fe ni aaadu amɛ yɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ateŋ. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ oya.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree produce a good harvest before it gets too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A cocoa tree typically reaches its peak production between 10 and 25 years of age. After 30 years, pod yields usually drop sharply, making the farm less profitable to maintain without rehabilitation or replanting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ feɔ amɛyibii babaoo yɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25. Yɛ afii 30 sɛɛ lɛ, podi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi oya. Enɛ haa sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ faaa kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni asaaa loo aduuu ekoŋŋ.

english: If my cocoa tree looks big and strong, does that mean it is safe from diseases like swollen shoot?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda ni ehe wa Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ahe?

english: A large trunk or thick green leaves do not mean a tree is immune to disease. Some viruses and fungal infections can live inside a visually strong tree for a long time before visible damage or yield drop occurs.
ga: Tso lɛ yitso agbo loo baai eŋɔli ni mli tse lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ helai nyɛŋ amɔ tso lɛ. Virus kɛ fungal helai komɛi baanyɛ ahi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ dani amɛfite nibii ni anaa loo amɛha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why does my cocoa tree grow thick leaves and branches but fail to produce many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ baai kɛ niji ni mli tse shi ebɛ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops get too much shade, over-fertilization of nitrogen, or are too old, they put their energy into growing leaves instead of flowers and fruit. Pruning and proper sunlight exposure encourage the tree to focus energy on pod growth.
ga: Beni tsei náa hulutsoo babaoo Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo ni egbɔ tsɔ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Tso lɛ he ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa pod lɛ dalɛ nɔ.

english: Are the new hybrid cocoa seedlings better than using seeds harvested from my own strong trees?
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he Ani ehi fe dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii?

english: Yes, standard modern hybrid seedlings are specially bred to resist common local diseases, grow faster, and yield more pods much earlier than seeds saved from traditional older trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya kwraa fe dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi shishijee kɛjɛ tsei ni edara amli lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear clear pathways inside my cocoa farm before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Clearing farm pathways improves air circulation to lower humidity that causes black pod disease, makes it easier to spot infected pods early, and allows workers to move safely without damaging healthy crop stems.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni agbeleɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛba ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaana pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. ni ehaa nitsulɔi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyaa he fɛɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛfiteee tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I follow modern agricultural methods instead of the traditional ways my family used?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi anɔ moŋ fe blema gbɛi ni miweku lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Modern methods are designed to adapt to changing rainfall patterns, new plant diseases, and soil depletion that did not affect older generations in the same way, helping to ensure higher crop yields per acre.
ga: Afee ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi lɛ koni ekɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni tsakeɔ lɛ akpã gbee. tsei ahe helai heei kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ enaaa yinɔi ni eho lɛ anɔ hewalɛ yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ. Ehaa anáa yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli.

english: Will letting wild bushes and weeds grow near my crop stems reduce my yields?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mahã koo mli tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ mitso lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds and wild brush steal water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients directly from your crops' root systems. They also trap unwanted moisture around stems, creating a ideal environment for fungal diseases to thrive.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ataooo lɛ hu shwieɔ tso lɛ he, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can agricultural extension officers help me if my farm is too old to produce well?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aba?

english: Extension officers can assess your soil and tree health, guide you on government cocoa rehabilitation schemes, provide certified disease-resistant seedlings, and show you proper spacing and pruning techniques.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ kɛ tsei lɛ yɔɔ ha. Wo bo ŋaa yɛ nɔyeli lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛbaajie kookoo lɛ he. Dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ helai ahe odaseyeli ni akɛhaa ni atsɔɔ gbɛ ni sa kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables have a powdery chemical film on them, and is it safe to send them straight to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ yɛ tsofa ni tamɔ powder nɔ lɛ? Ni ani abaanyɛ akɛya jara lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Pesticides protect crops from bugs while growing, but leaving residues on harvested food is unsafe. You must observe the 'pre-harvest interval'—waiting the required number of days between spraying and harvesting—so chemicals break down naturally, and always wash produce before consumption.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe be mli ni aduɔ amɛ. Shi nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ niyenii ni akpa lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe. Esa akɛ okwɛ ‘Pre-harvest period’, ni omɛ gbii pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ nikpamɔ teŋ Koni tsofai lɛ afite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni ofɔ nibii ahe be fɛɛ be dani aye.

english: Why do my tomato leaves look whitish and dull after I spray them for pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baa lɛ feɔ futafuta ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays leave a thin coating on leaves as they dry. While this residue shields the plant from insects and diseases, heavy buildup can block sunlight, so you should mix chemicals strictly according to instructions to avoid coating the leaves too thickly.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo shwieɔ nɔ. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ egbi Eyɛ mli akɛ nɛkɛ nɔ ni eshwɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi kɛ helai ahe moŋ, Shi nɔ ni tsii ni ebua naa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ hulu lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ tsofai lɛ afutu mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ anaa koni ekaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ.

english: Why do some of my oil palm bunches yield a lot of rich oil while others yield mostly hard seeds with very little oil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm aduawai akuu lɛ woɔ fɔ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii komɛi woɔ dumɔwui ni wa babaoo kɛ fɔ fioo ko pɛ?

english: Oil palm yield depends heavily on the variety you plant. Selected hybrid varieties like Tenera are bred to produce thick oil-rich pulp with tiny seeds, whereas unselected local varieties produce thick, hard shells with very little extractable oil.
ga: Mu tso ni anáa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ anɔ waa. Akwɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ahala, tamɔ Tenera, koni amɛná ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ dumɔwui bibii. yɛ be mli ni maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ahalaaa lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa kɛ mu fioo ko pɛ ni anyɛɔ ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnuts produce less oil when I crush them if I harvest them during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ amli fɔ lɛ faaa kɛji mikɛmiikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvesting groundnuts in high moisture prevents the seeds from drying properly. High water content inside the nut dilutes and spoils the natural oils, encouraging mold growth which reduces overall oil extraction quality.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli fɔji lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni efiteɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ yaa hiɛ Enɛ baaha mu ni ajieɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn dark blue or black inside just two days after I dig them out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ batsɔ bluu loo ediŋŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots react quickly with oxygen in the air because they no longer receive water from the stem. This natural breakdown, called post-harvest physiological deterioration, means raw cassava roots must be processed into gari or flour within 48 hours.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ kɛ oxygen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ekome oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛnáaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsɔne lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ afee ŋmei shishifãi ni afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli.

english: Why can't I sell my cocoa beans raw straight from the pod without fermenting and drying them first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni mikɛwooo mli ni mikɛgbiko klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Raw cocoa beans are bitter and covered in sweet pulp. Fermentation heats up the beans to kill the seed, break down bitterness, and develop the rich chocolate flavor and oils that buying companies require.
ga: Cocoa yibii ni ahoko lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ ehà nɔ. Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ koni egbe dumɔwui lɛ, ni efolɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli, ni eha tsokolate kɛ fɔ ni ŋɔɔ waa ni nitsumɔhe ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and looking shiny under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkpɛɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to reduce moisture loss when exposed to intense heat. However, if the leaves look shiny or sticky, it is usually a sign of tiny sap-sucking pests like mites or whiteflies attacking the undersides.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba fɛ̃i ni laajeɔ lɛ shi kɛji akɛwo dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkpɛɔ loo amɛhe wa lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ tutuaa shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open right when they start turning red on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ tswaa trukaa beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split open due to sudden changes in water supply. If a dry spell is followed by heavy watering or rain, the fruit inside grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst open.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa yɛ nu jɛɛhe lɛ tsakemɔ trukaa hewɔ Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ko ba ni nu ni akɛhaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ fãa.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning purple and yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ purple kɛ yellow yɛ green ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate a shortage of nitrogen, which the crop needs to build healthy stems, while purple leaves show a lack of phosphorus needed for root and grain growth. Adding well-timed fertilizer or organic manure restores the green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, baai ni ji purple lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs ni he hiaa kɛha shishifãi kɛ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines produce giant green leaves above ground but only thin, stringy roots beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni wa pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages the crop to spend all its energy growing leafy green vines. To get thick, starch-filled tubers, sweet potatoes need balanced soils richer in potassium rather than high nitrogen.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛdu wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli. Koni aná starch yitso ni mli eyi obɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ moŋ fe nitrogen.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves in dry weather to conserve water and keep its roots alive underground. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from forming fruit. Mulching the soil around the plants with dry grass and watering near the roots helps keep them cool and encourages fruit to set.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni ehaaa etsu nii jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ he, ni akɛ nu awo mli yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into curls and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with insecticidal soap or recommended sprays helps keep leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds across the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize in rows ensures every plant receives equal space, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier compared to broad-scattered planting.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight, which provides energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni ji hewalɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a windstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems topped with fruit, making them top-heavy. Supporting the main stem with sturdy wooden or bamboo forks prevents them from blowing down before harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni tsii ni aduawai yɔɔ nɔ. Ehaa efeɔ tso ni tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei ni mli wa fi tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbee shi dani akpa.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the soft leaves. Checking fields early and using approved natural or chemical sprays can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. ni kɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa hei ni tamɔ nɛkɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, humid environments. Pruning heavy shade tree branches to allow sunlight and fresh air into your farm helps keep the pods dry and prevents rot.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli efɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This leaves natural fertilizer behind for whatever crop you plant in that field next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings get scorched leaves when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ baai ni shãa yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa trees from intense heat and drying winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water, which washes nutrients away. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. ni baajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil gets too dry, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Regular watering and keeping the soil covered with mulch helps preserve the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly like tiny cups during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing too much water in the heat. However, if they stay curled even in the cool morning, it usually means tiny pests like mites or aphids are sucking the juice from the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ebu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Shi, kɛji amɛfo amɛhe yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be po mli lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai amli

english: Why are my sweet potato vines growing big green leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When sweet potatoes get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing foliage above ground instead of tubers below. Using a fertilizer higher in potassium encourages the plant to build bigger tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potatoes nine shɛ nitrogen fertilizer babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛbaakɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi tsei. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: What happens to my cassava roots if I plant the cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting cassava too close forces the plants to compete with each other for light, water, and soil food. This causes them to grow thin stems and small, poor quality roots instead of big tubers.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni ehiii kwraa yɛ bulb agbo najiaŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans pull natural nitrogen food from the air into the ground. This feeds the soil and acts like a natural fertilizer that helps your neighboring maize grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans gbalaa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa osɛɛ ŋmãa lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cabbage plants full of small round holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ eyi kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by caterpillars or beetles feeding on them. Spraying the leaves early in the morning with neem leaf extract or recommended organic remedies helps deter these insects.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ afɔ neem baai lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn dark black and dry up on the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Blackening cocoa pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in very damp and shady fields. Pruning excess branches lets sunshine into the farm and reduces the moisture that feeds the disease.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpods ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo tsei ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni haa helai baa lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I tell underground that my groundnuts are ripe and ready to pull out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ agbala?

english: You can check by digging up a few pods and cracking them open. If the inside of the shell has dark brown veins and the seeds fill out the casing completely, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ pods fioo komɛi ni oootsi ni ogbele amɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when planted on sloped ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Rain easily washes topsoil and plant food down hills, leaving the ground dry and poor in nutrients. Adding animal manure around the base of the plantain helps trap water and food in the soil.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaadu niyenii yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Koolooi amli ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ Plantain shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu kɛ niyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my farm soil get so dry and hard after just a few days without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi ni ewa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Hard soil lacks organic matter like compost or dry leaves that hold water like a sponge. Adding animal manure or spreading mulch around your crops helps keep the soil soft and moist for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi ni hiɛɔ nu tamɔ sponji. Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the maize is lacking water and nitrogen. When the soil is dry, the plant cannot suck up nutrients properly, so watering them or applying fertilizer right before a light rain restores their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu kɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ fioo ko nɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very helpful. Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize while giving you two crops from the same land.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmãa enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome.

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight to produce big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground so they catch maximum light and stay safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ koni la babaoo ashɛ amɛhe kɛ shweshweeshwe shihilɛ kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato leaves curl during intense sunshine to protect themselves from losing too much water. As long as they open back up in the evening and the plant gets regular water, it is a normal way the plant protects itself.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Shii abɔ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛtsu nii gbɛkɛ ni amɛha tsei lɛ nu bɔ ni sa. Eji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by hot weather, uneven watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Giving the plant steady water and organic fertilizer will help the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ ha tso lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. You can prevent it by harvesting ripe pods immediately, pruning excess branches to let sunlight in, and removing infected pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni oookpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli. ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep root systems that soak up water and nutrients much faster than young crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food away from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully grown and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?
