english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are some of the seeds I planted failing to come out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, if the soil is too dry, or if the seeds were old and damaged by insects. Planting good seeds at a shallow depth in moist soil ensures strong germination.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. aloo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni kooloi bibii efite Dumɔwui kpakpai ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ waa.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the cleared trees and bush when preparing my land for planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa tsei kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni ajie lɛ beni misaa he ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys beneficial earthworms and organic matter in the topsoil. Leaving cleared vegetation to decay naturally builds a rich soil foundation, keeps the ground moist, and provides natural nutrients for your maize.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni he tse lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ shishitoo baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii haa o-corn lɛ.

english: Why is it important to completely clear wild weeds and roots before putting my yam seeds into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛ koo mli shishifãi fɛɛ dani adu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Wild forest weeds grow much faster than crop seeds and will steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing them completely gives your yam sprouts a strong head start without competition.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii ko bɛ mli.

english: What is the benefit of starting my pepper seeds in a sheltered nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ pepper dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ amli dani ajieɔ amɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: A nursery provides a safe, indoor-like environment that protects fragile young seeds from harsh direct sunlight, heavy rains, and pests until the seedlings are strong enough to survive outdoors.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni tamɔ shĩa mli ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ kpo nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that dry out quickly under full sun. They need shade crops like plantain trees nearby to act as living umbrellas until their roots grow deep enough to handle heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ dɔlɛ.

english: Why do I need to dig deep mounds or ridges before planting sweet potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni mli kwɔ dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Loosening the soil creates soft ground that makes it easy for crop roots to expand. Deep mounds allow sweet potato tubers to grow large without fighting packed, hard earth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã. Gɔji ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ akpee.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for my next cassava crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-cassava dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This enriches the soil naturally, laying a fertile foundation for heavy-feeding crops like cassava.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ekɛ shishitoo kpakpa haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa kooloi niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my plantain suckers when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni da yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from competing over water and soil nutrients, and leaves paths open so you can walk through easily to inspect and care for your farm.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkatswa akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. ni ehaa onyɛɔ otsɔɔ mli mlɛo koni oyakwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okwɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young vegetable plants with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, keeps the blazing sun from drying out the earth. It traps moisture around the roots and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of green leaves but very little fruit if I don't trim them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛji mifolɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: When a tomato plant has too many side branches, it sends all its energy into growing leaves instead of developing flowers and fruit. Trimming helps focus energy on producing food.
ga: Kɛji tomato tso ko yɛ niji babaoo Etsuɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai baa lɛ, Trimming yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ maa niyenii feemɔ nɔ.

english: How do tall trees planted along the boundary of my farm help protect my plantain crops?
ga: Te tsei kakadaji ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ naa lɛ buɔ midumɔwui lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Tall boundary trees act as windbreaks. They break the force of strong seasonal winds that would otherwise snap fragile plantain stems or blow off their leaves.
ga: Tsei kakadaji tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsimɔ. Amɛfiteɔ be mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ akumɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ loo efo amɛbaai lɛ ahewalɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dying when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries up the topsoil before their roots can grow deep enough to find water.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛna nu.

english: Maize rolls its leaves to protect itself from the heat and slow down water loss through evaporation when the air is dry and warm.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ fiofio kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the green leaves on top look very bushy and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Kɛji baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tamɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po lɛ,

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔlii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why does rice grow better in low valley land than on high sloping land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli fe hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Valley lands naturally retain rainwater and stay muddy for long periods, which rice plants need to grow, whereas water drains away too quickly on high sloping land.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hiɛɔ nugbɔ nu yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛfeɔ muji be kakadaŋŋ. ni ji ŋmãa tso ni esa akɛ eda yɛ be mli ni nu hoɔ oya tsɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: When plantains are crowded, their roots and broad leaves fight with each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, leaving less energy to feed the growing fruit bunch.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ amɛbaai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, sũ mli niyenii, kɛ nu, ni no haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshiɔ ni amɛkɛbaahã aduawai akui ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, causing the plant to drop its blossoms because it cannot successfully form seeds and fruit under extreme temperature.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui kɛ aduawai jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa shishi.

english: Why do farmers plant cowpeas under maize plants after the maize has already grown tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa tsei ashishi beni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas spread along the ground to cover the soil, keeping it moist and cool, while their roots add natural nutrients to the soil that help the maize thrive.
ga: Cowpeas gbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do fall armyworms eat the leaves inside the center of my maize plant instead of the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide inside the tender central leaf roll of maize to protect themselves from hot sunlight, rain, and birds while feeding on the youngest, softest leaves.
ga: Asraafoi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ blɛoo yɛ ŋmãa baa ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ. Bɔni afee ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ, kɛ okpoi ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow from the tip inward in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiya mligbɛ, ni amɛmiifee V su lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips indicates that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives crops their strong green color and helps them grow.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa tsei lɛ su eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my yam tubers start to sprout leaves inside the barn even when I have not planted them in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miduuu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams have an internal biological clock that signals the tuber to wake up and grow new shoots when the rainy season approaches, even without soil or water.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko ni yɔɔ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ teɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba. Kɛ́ sũ loo nu bɛ jɛmɛ po

english: Why is it important to leave a measured space like 30 feet between my trees when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi aaafee ninetalɔi 30 yɛ tsei ateŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Giving trees enough space ensures that their roots do not fight for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves get plenty of sunlight to grow big and yield well.
ga: Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ etswaŋ akaŋ. Ni baai lɛ náa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to prune or trim the branches of my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Trimming extra or weak branches helps air and sunlight flow through the tree, prevents diseases from spreading, and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger fruits.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Tsi helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ewo yibii wuji

english: How do I know if a piece of land is suitable for my crops before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani mibɔi dumɔwui?

english: Good farming land has deep, dark soil that holds moisture well without staying flooded, is free of hard rock layers near the surface, and supports healthy wild plant growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii yɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ. Tɛ ni wa ko bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koo mli tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ

english: Why does my harvest drop if I plant the exact same crop on the same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients that the crop relies on and allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without fruiting when they are under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make food for producing fruit. In deep shade, plants stretch upward searching for light instead of developing fruit.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni niyenii awo yibii. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsei baagbala amɛhe koni amɛtao la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are damaged from waterlogged soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ yɛ niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they run out of stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil before they can reach sunlight and air.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ dani enyɛ eshɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he lɛ nɔ.

english: How does too much standing water hurt my crop roots?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ yeɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ awui?

english: Excess water drowns plant roots by blocking oxygen in the soil, causing the roots to rot so they can no longer absorb nutrients.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miigbɔjɔ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your crops need to stay strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fataa he ni bɛŋkɛɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's outer skin and roots; it is best to place it in a circle a few inches away where the root tips feed.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛwo kooyigbɛ ni kɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baabote mli lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plants grow green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting legumes like cowpeas help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but only produce tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of tubers. Loosening the soil and balancing nutrients encourages big root growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ wa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ bulbs najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ haa shishifãi wuji lɛ daa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too hot, when soil moisture is uneven, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Regular watering and keeping the soil cool helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeee ekome loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ bɛ Nu ni awoɔ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make food through their leaves. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes helps the plant produce more energy, which gets sent down to grow large tubers.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ wo baai anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa. ni abaamaje kɛba shi koni amɛkwɛ bulb agboi

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp and shady conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods keeps the rest of the farm safe.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Tsoi krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my plantain leaves bend and snap halfway down during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbalaɔ enyɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains lose a lot of water through their big leaves. In dry weather, the plant intentionally lets its outer leaves bend or drop to reduce water loss and protect the main stem.
ga: Plantains fiteɔ nu babaoo kɛtsɔɔ baai wuji anɔ. yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛhaa amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young crops as early as possible?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ oya bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and plant food directly from your crop roots. Clearing them early ensures your young crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why does my maize crop fall over easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over if its roots are shallow or damaged by pests. Mounding up soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) gives the plants strong support against wind.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛji eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi (grounding) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave dry fallen leaves on my farm soil instead of clearing and burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafolɔ amɛ ni mashã amɛ?

english: Leaving dry leaves on the ground creates a protective cover that keeps the soil cool, traps moisture, and slowly breaks down into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi baai ni egbi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How long does crop material lying on the ground usually last before it completely turns into soil?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi dani etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ kwraa?

english: Depending on rain and heat, soft leaves usually break down in a few weeks, while thick stalks can last several months before turning completely into rich black soil.
ga: Edamɔ nugbɔ kɛ dɔlɛ nɔ Bei pii lɛ, baai bibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni mli tse lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo dani amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nii.

english: Why do leaves leave a dark layer on the ground after lying there for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ shiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛkã jɛmɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: That dark layer is nutrient-rich organic matter left behind as soil organisms decompose the plant material, which makes your soil more fertile for future crops.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋ lɛ ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ fiteɔ tsei amli nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What happens to plant material lying on the ground when heavy rain hits it?
ga: Mɛni baa tsei ahe nibii ni ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ yɛ nɔ?

english: Rainwater speeds up how fast plant material breaks down, but if too much water settles on the ground without drying out, it can cause the plant matter to rot and smell.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa tsei fiteɔ oya. Shi kɛji nu babaoo gbee shikpɔŋ ni egbiko lɛ, Ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbo ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: What signs should I look for to know if my crops are getting too much standing water around their roots?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ matao koni mana kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe?

english: When crops sit in too much water, their leaves often turn yellow, the bottom of the stems become soft or discolored, and growth slows down.
ga: Kɛ tsei yɔɔ nu babaoo mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ shishi baafee bɔdɔɔ loo ehiɛ baatsake. ni dalɛ baafee mlɛo

english: How does covering my soil with dry plant leaves protect my crops during hot, sunny days?
ga: Te tsei ahe baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A layer of dry leaves blocks harsh sunlight from hitting the bare earth directly, preventing soil water from evaporating quickly and keeping root zones cool.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. kɛ shishifã lɛ he ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i

english: How can I tell if dead leaves on my field are rotting healthily or spreading plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji baai ni egboi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite jogbaŋŋ loo amɛmiigbɛ tsei ahe helai amɛshwã?

english: Healthy decomposition turns material dark and crumbly with a fresh earth smell, while disease-spreading rot often smells sour, looks slimy, or shows mold spots.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nibii ni tsuɔ, ni egbɔjɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hee yɔɔ mli baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Etamɔ mucus loo eyɛ fungus.

english: How do I know when it is time to add a fresh layer of dry plant material to my crop beds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ akɛ tsei ni egbi lɛ fã hee afata he? kɛtee midumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: You should add fresh plant material when the previous layer has thinned out, fully broken down into dark soil, and no longer covers the bare dirt.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tso mli nibii heei afata he kɛji akɛ tsutsu fã lɛ egbɔjɔ. Efo kwraa kɛbatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ. ni muji ehàaa nɔ dɔŋŋ

english: Does leaving old harvested crop stems on my land help or hurt my next planting season?
ga: Ani tsei ni akpa lɛ ashishifãi ni mishiɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ midalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ awui?

english: Healthy stems help nourish the soil as they decay, but stems from crops that had diseases should be removed so they do not pass infections to your next crop.
ga: Tsoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ. Shi eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ashishifãi koni amɛkagbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if dry crop stalks on the ground are still useful or if I should clean them off?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni egbi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ lolo loo esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: As long as the stalks cover the soil surface without harboring pests or smelling rotten, they are still helping to retain soil moisture and reduce weeds.
ga: Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii bɛ mli lɛ. Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa lolo ni sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni amɛhaa jwɛi lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct, intense sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil before their shallow roots can draw up enough water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in wet, humid weather when splashing rainwater spreads fungal spores onto the pods.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ enɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ shwieɔ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are flower buds falling off my cocoa trees instead of turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaatsɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or too much shade can stress the cocoa tree, causing it to drop its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo hulutsoo babaoo baanyɛ aha cacao tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, forcing the plant to pull food from its older leaves to nourish the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow big bushy leaves but give me very small roots at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that stops the leaves from making proper food for the roots.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii ni sa kɛha shishifãi lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ muji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl deep inside the central funnel of the plant to eat the soft, growing leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantains next to their new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ kookoo tsei yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow broad leaves quickly, acting as living umbrellas that shelter delicate young cocoa plants from harsh heat while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops turn pale and stop growing when water stays on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ be mli ni nu ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air from the soil to breathe; standing water suffocates the roots, preventing them from taking in food and causing them to rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye ni amɛkafite.

english: When daytime heat is too high or the soil gets too dry, pepper plants drop their flowers to save water and protect themselves from drying out.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their tender leaves burn and lose moisture quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a cool environment until the cocoa trees are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ baaha shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ aba kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know which part of the cassava stem is best to cut and plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni esa akɛ mafo ni madu koni maná ŋmaa ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: The best planting material comes from the mature middle portion of a healthy cassava stem with strong buds. The soft top section dries out easily, and the woody bottom stem sprouts slowly.
ga: Nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ teŋgbɛ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them grow along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eda lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture food to grow larger underground tubers. It also keeps leaves off wet soil, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Ehaa baai hu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aba shi

english: What will happen to my corn seeds if I plant them before the rainy season properly begins?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba?

english: If you plant seeds in dry soil during brief early rains, they may sprout and quickly dry up when the rain stops. It is best to wait until the rains are steady so the roots get constant moisture to establish.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔ kuku ko mli lɛ, Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi koni eha shishifãi lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil or that excess water is suffocating the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ miigba shishifãi lɛ anaa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high, when the soil is too dry, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during dry weather helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when plants are actively growing, usually two to three weeks after sprouting, and again during flowering. Applying it to moist soil helps the roots absorb the nutrients safely without burning.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni tsei lɛ miida waa, bei pii lɛ otsii 2-3 sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. ni okɛfata he ekoŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai ni amɛshãaa lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in air and sunlight, along with applying recommended treatments, protects the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Tso niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu pods lɛ ahe.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by viruses spread by these insects. Spraying neem oil or recommended organic treatments stops the damage.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ baaha nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ akpa.

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant whorl. Inspecting farms early and applying recommended pest controls directly into the whorl stops them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Ni aaakwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo loop lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha nakai ŋmɔji lɛ akpa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade from companion crops like plantain or shade trees, intense sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil, preventing the seedlings from establishing strong roots.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ahe lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkafee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Pruning removes old, diseased, or overcrowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach the middle of the tree. This reduces fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to direct its energy into forming healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egbɔ, ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for leaf growth. Applying balanced fertilizer or organic compost helps keep the leaves green so the plant can produce large ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot in the ground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without proper drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away, keeping the roots safe from rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: What is making holes in the leaf funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking plants early and using recommended controls like neem extract or approved pesticides keeps the foliage healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ amli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the resources they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la. Ehe hia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in hot weather and prevents weed seeds from growing, keeping the roots cool and moist.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why will my crops produce less yield if I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food. Giving each plant proper spacing allows its roots and branches to spread out fully.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ahe akaŋshii mli. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kwraa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to extreme heat stress, dry soil conditions, or poor pollination. Regular watering during hot spells and keeping soil moist helps flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do heavy yams stay good for longer after harvesting than light ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ fe ŋmeii ni tsiimɔ waaa lɛ?

english: Heavier tubers contain more solid starch and less excess water, which gives them dense food reserves that naturally resist decay and prolong shelf life.
ga: Tubers ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ starch ni wa babaoo kɛ nu ni fa fe nine fioo. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo. Amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ fitemɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa amɛshihilɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava has enough solid food in it before I harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niyenii ni wa ni fa bɔ ni sa dani akpa?

english: Cassava roots that feel dense and heavy for their size have accumulated high dry matter rather than just water, indicating maturity and long-lasting quality.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa yɛ amɛdalɛ hewɔ. Ebua nibii ni egbi babaoo naa yɛ nu kɛkɛ najiaŋ. Etsɔɔ anɔkwayeli kɛ su ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my harvested crops spoil very quickly while others last for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hiɔ shi otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops with high water content rot rapidly, whereas mature crops rich in solid dry food matter resist rotting and maintain their freshness over extended storage.
ga: Tsei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baagboi oya. Taakɛ tsei ni eda ni akɛ niyenii ni egbi ni wa yeɔ nii lɛ teɔ shi ewoɔ fitemɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ ehee lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do buyers at the market pay more for produce that feels heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha nibii ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Market buyers know that heavier produce is packed with actual food starch and nutrients rather than excess water, giving them better value and longer storage time.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ le akɛ, yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, niyenii ni tsii fe nine lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo fe nu ni fa fe nine. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji sɛɛnamɔ ni hi kɛ nitoo be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomatoes always get crushed when I transport them in traditional woven baskets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be kɛ́ mikɛwo blema tsɛnsii ni akpɛ́ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pouring heavy, soft produce into open baskets creates uneven pressure, causing lower layers to get crushed under the weight of those above.
ga: Aduawai kɛ aduawai ni tsii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi ni agbele mli lɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ ni ejaaa baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ fã lɛ shwieɔ ŋwɛi tsɔne lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I prevent my crop produce from getting crushed during transport to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni akafite yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Using rigid containers or lined crates instead of overloading deep baskets prevents pressure from squishing your produce and preserves its appearance.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsɛnsi ni mli wa loo adeka ni akɛ tsɔne ebɔ he lɛ tsu nii yɛ tsɛnsi ni mli kwɔ fe nine najiaŋ lɛ, ebaatsi nɔnyɛɛ naa koni ekamimɔ onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ amli, ni ebaaha ehiɛ afee fɛo.

english: Why does bruised or crushed produce spoil faster than undamaged crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni atswa loo atswa amɛ lɛ fiteɔ oya fe tsei ni efiteee lɛ?

english: Crushing breaks the protective outer skin of the crop, releasing liquids and opening pathways for fungi and bacteria to enter and cause rapid rotting.
ga: Nibii ni atswaa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kponɔgbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ. Enɛ haa nu jeɔ kpo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa fitemɔ baa oya.

english: How does proper packaging help me get better prices at the local market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Proper packaging prevents physical damage and crushing, ensuring your crops look neat, clean, and appealing, which attracts premium buyers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsiɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ kɛ fitemɔ naa. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo, amɛhe tseɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo, ni no gbalaa mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni jara wa waa lɛ.

english: How should I handle my plantains after harvesting so they don't get bruised before sale?
ga: Kɛ́ akpa plantains lɛ agbe naa lɛ, te esa akɛ akwɛ tɛŋŋ koni akafite amɛ dani ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Stack plantain bunches gently in padded trucks or crates using dried leaves as cushioning rather than tossing them loosely into baskets.
ga: Okɛ plantains lɛ ato lɔle loo adeka ni akɛ nibii ewo mli lɛ mli blɛoo ni okɛ baai ni egboi atsu nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ lɛ ashwie tsɛnsi lɛ mli mlɛo lɛ.

english: What is the best way to clean and present my root crops so they look nice to market women?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsumɔ mishishifãi lɛ ahe ni mikɛ amɛ aha koni amɛfee fɛo amɛha yei ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Gently wipe away dry dirt without scrubbing the outer skin, and arrange intact, undamaged tubers neatly by weight and size.
ga: Tsumɔ muji ni egbi lɛ blɛoo ni okɛ ŋmɔlɔ akashwie kponɔgbɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni oto yitsei ni yɔɔ lolo ni efiteee lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ bɔ ni amɛtsiimɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ji lɛ naa.

english: Why does corn grow very tall and healthy on a farm in a neighboring district, but stays short and weak on my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ ni ehiɛ wa yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ maji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ? Shi mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ kuku ni ebɛ hewalɛ lolo?

english: Soil type, water holding capacity, and rainfall can change from one district to another. Your neighbor's land might have richer soil with more natural nutrients, while your land may need organic manure or fertilizer to help the corn grow well.
ga: Shikpɔŋ henɔ, nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ baanyɛ atsake kɛjɛ kpokpaa kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ. Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ fe tsutsu lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo. Yɛ be mli ni ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he baahia humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients away or make the soil too soggy for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why do my tall corn plants fall over easily whenever a strong wind or rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Corn plants fall over (a problem called lodging) when their roots are weak, planted too shallowly, or planted too close together. Adding soil around the base of the stalks (mounding) as they grow helps anchor them firmly in the ground.
ga: Abɛi tso lɛ gbee shi (naagba ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ lodging) beni shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ Adu yɛ shishigbɛ tsɔ loo adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Sũ ni akɛfataa he kɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi (gɔŋ) beni edaa lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ atswa shi shiŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I put four or five corn seeds together in one hole so I get more plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli bɔni afee ni maná tsei babaoo?

english: When too many seeds share one hole, the young plants fight each other for water, light, and soil food. This competition makes all of them weak, resulting in thin stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei bibii wuɔ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ ha amɛ fɛɛ amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do some of the corn seeds I planted in the soil fail to germinate and come up at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ ni amɛdaraaa lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in the soil, if the soil is too dry, or if soil insects and birds ate them before they could grow roots.
ga: Dumɔwui ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ lɛ dani enyɛɔ ekwɛɔ shishifãi.

english: Why is it dangerous to leave weeds growing next to my young corn plants during the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi jwɛi lɛ yɛ afã? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-baby corn tsei ni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ yɛ oshara.

english: Weeds grow faster than young corn and quickly steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your crop needs. Clearing weeds early ensures your corn gets all the nourishment to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmãa, kɛ hulu la ni tsei taoɔ lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-ŋmã lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my corn leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii feɔ ŋmãa baa mli ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the center whorl of the corn plant during the day and chews on the tender leaves as they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii kɛ́ amɛgbele.

english: Why do some of my corn cobs have missing grains and large empty patches on them when I peel the husk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii lɛ elaaje kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni nɔ ko bɛ mli beni mifoɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when the plant does not pollinate properly. If the weather is extremely hot and dry when the corn produces silks and tassels, pollen dries up before it can fertilize every grain site on the cob.
ga: Nibii ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ awo tsei amli pollen yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ Beni ŋmãa lɛ feɔ siliki kɛ ŋmeii Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani abaanyɛ awo dumɔwui komɛi awo ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell exactly when my corn is ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Your corn is ready to harvest for dry grain when the green leaves and husks turn completely brown and papery, and the silk thread at the tip of the cob is dark brown and dry.
ga: Oŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi beni baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ tsɔ ŋmãa kwraa ni efee tamɔ wolo lɛ. ni siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ naagbee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after I finish harvesting my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni migbe ŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Corn feeds heavily on soil nutrients and leaves the land tired. Planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts good nitrogen back into the soil naturally, refreshing your farm for the next season.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kpakpa kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛo kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants drying up and turning brown in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and holds soil moisture to protect the young trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi koni ebu tsei bibii ahe.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for soil food and water. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to put all its energy into producing large plantain bunches.
ga: Tsobii loo tsei krokomɛi kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee plantain tsei wuji.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives plants their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving powdery dirt inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tamɔ powder yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The caterpillars hide inside the leaf funnel during the day and feed on the plant, which can reduce your yield if not treated early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my maize field right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani ahum ni naa wa ko baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the crop roots into gutters and streams. Applying fertilizer when the soil is damp, but not during heavy downpours, ensures the plant roots can absorb the food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the stem color changes to a darker shade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. ni tso lɛ su lɛ tsakeɔ kɛfeɔ su ni mli edɔ

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Ni ato tsei ahe gbɛjianɔ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up poles into the sunlight to make food for the roots. Staking prevents leaves from rotting on wet soil and helps produce bigger tubers under the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛkɛha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Staking tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa bulbs wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomatoes produce fewer fruits if I plant them in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji midu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same soil repeatedly drains specific nutrients and allows tomato diseases and soil pests to build up in that field over time.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi afite, ni ebaaha tomato helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei ni baakwɛ̃ wɔsɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by the plant reacting to severe heat and water stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni feɔ amɛnii waa yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash soil nutrients away below where roots can reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. Intercropping them with maize enriches the soil naturally, helping your maize grow better while giving you an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ ehaa bo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni obaakpa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and drying up right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly during wet, damp conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes in my maize leaves with small caterpillars inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: Your farm is likely attacked by Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the growing center of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying targeted control measures directly into the central leaf funnel saves the crop from severe damage.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ miitutua oŋmɔ lɛ. Ni aaamɔ amɛ mra ni akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Ebaahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛjɛ fitemɔ ni mli wa mli.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the ground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water logs in the soil around them, causing fungal infections. Planting your cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain off, keeping the tubers safe and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu mɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct harsh sunlight and heat stress. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains next to young cocoa creates a humid, shaded shelter that keeps the young seedlings alive until mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he waa. releasing tall trees Shade loo dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe, ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ amɛdaramɔ.

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce large tubers underground. Lifting the vines onto stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, improves airflow to lower leaf diseases, and leads to a bigger harvest.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛba foliar hela he okadii lɛ shi. ni ekɛ kpamɔ ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap or fall over so easily when heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ fãa loo egbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches at the top, making them unstable during storms. Propping the main stem with strong bamboo poles supports the heavy load and keeps the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni jwɛi ni mli tse yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Destabilizes during storms Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa to tso wulu lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua muji ni tsii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Flower drop happens when crops experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Covering the soil with organic mulch keeps the ground moist and cool, helping the plant hold its flowers to form fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Nibii ni akɛ organic mulch woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I spread chemical fertilizer on my field immediately after a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Heavy rainwater carries fertilizer away in runoff or washes it deep into the ground beyond the root zone. Applying fertilizer when the soil is damp but not flooded ensures the roots can absorb the nutrients efficiently.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa kɛtsɔɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ loo efɔ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa he ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I keep some tall trees on my farm instead of cutting them all down before planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tsei lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Tall trees act like huge umbrellas that protect the cocoa from intense heat, hold moisture in the soil, and shield young plants from strong winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei kakadaji lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akpɔlɔi wuji ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni obu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient they need to build green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the farm and drown the plant roots, stopping them from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko mli nu ni eha tsei shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli. Ehaa onyɛɛɛ oye niyenii

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to hide and eat inside the center leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they crawl into the tight center leaf roll (the whorl) because it is soft, hidden from birds, and full of fresh tender growth to eat.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Efoɔ kɛboteɔ baa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni mli wa lɛ mli (rings) ejaakɛ eyɛ blɛoo, ehiɛ okpoi adɛŋ, ni eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni eyeɔ.

english: How do I know which direction to point cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ matsɔɔ mi-cassava niji lɛ beni mikɛ amɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You must plant cassava cuttings with the tiny leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stem has to bend itself around to grow upward, which wastes the plant's energy and results in smaller cassava roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmeii bibii adu ŋmeii niji lɛ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Esa akɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ abɔle ehe koni ekwɛ̃. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Raising the leaves off the damp ground keeps them healthy, stops soil diseases from infecting them, and helps the plant produce large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni biɔ ni agbɛ baai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Tsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or dry soil. Without enough water or under high heat, the plant loses energy and drops its flowers to save itself rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ loo yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi lɛ Tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛtsa ehe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny invisible pests like mites or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves. As the damaged leaves try to grow, the wounded parts shrink and cause the leaf to warp and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi Beni baai ni efite lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara lɛ Fã ni epila lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it wrong to put chemical fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii? No hewɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ ejaaa?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so crop roots can drink it in. If you put fertilizer on dry soil in hot weather, the strong undissolved chemicals will draw water out of the roots and scorch or kill the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ wo mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Concentrated, tsofai ni nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli lɛ baajie nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ebaashã loo egbe tso lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It blocks the hot sun from hitting the bare earth directly, which keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Planting maize in the same spot every year sucks out the specific nutrients maize needs and lets maize-loving pests build up in the soil. Switching to legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas refreshes the soil by putting nitrogen back into it naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, ebaaŋɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. ni oha kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do all my maize plants produce corn at the exact same time instead of spreading out over several months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã nyɔji babaoo amli lɛ?

english: Maize plants sown together react to the same weather and sunlight cues, causing them to mature simultaneously. To avoid having all your harvest ready at once when market prices might drop, you can plant your fields in small batches two weeks apart.
ga: Abele ni adu yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ hulu la he nii nakai nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ekome kɛdaraa. Enɛ ji koni akakpa nibii fɛɛ shikome beni jara nɔ jara baanyɛ aba shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kui bibii amli. otsii enyɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and spoil within just a few days of picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni mikpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and ripen after harvest. Exposure to intense heat and rough handling during harvesting speeds up decay, causing them to rot rapidly if not kept in a cool, shaded environment.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekwɛɔ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nitsumɔ ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii Yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, enɛ baaha efite oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛtooo he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start rotting in the barn even when they appeared healthy at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ beni akpa amɛ lɛ moŋ?

english: Small scratches or bruises from harvesting tools allow fungi and bacteria to enter the yam. Poor airflow and heat inside the storage barn cause these germs to multiply quickly and rot the tuber from within.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ bibii loo ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ aba sweet potato lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ haa nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ faa oya ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds turn into powder with tiny holes after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powder ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Weevil insects often lay microscopic eggs inside the pods while the crop is still in the field. After harvest, these eggs hatch into tiny pests that eat the seeds from the inside out, damaging their quality.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ewui bibii ni anaaa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. ni yeɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ ni fiteɔ su kpakpa

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers during intense heat and water shortages to conserve energy and survive. Without steady soil moisture, the plant drops blossoms before they can develop into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do some of my cassava roots grow very large while others stay tiny on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi daa waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu ji bibii lolo yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose soil and physical space to swell. If plants are spaced too closely or grown in hard, unplowed soil, they compete for nutrients and water, producing small and uneven roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛfu. Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small fruit bunches when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: Overcrowded plantain trees shade each other's leaves and fight underground for soil nutrients. Without enough sunlight and plant food, the trees lack the energy needed to form large, heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛhe baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ hulu la kɛ tsei niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ hu bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat combined with dry winds or irregular watering stresses tomato plants, causing the flower stems to weaken and drop off before pollination occurs.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni bɛ be fɛɛ be fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani pollination baa.

english: Why do my neighbor's maize seeds mature a month earlier than my local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ mra nyɔŋ kome fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Certain maize varieties are bred to complete their life cycle faster using less water. These early-maturing varieties allow farmers to harvest quickly before dry spells or market gluts occur.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi koni amɛgbe amɛwala shihilɛ naa oya kɛtsɔ nu fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra nɛɛ haa okwaafoi kpaɔ nii oya dani hɔmɔ shihilɛi loo nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut tree turning brown and looking old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔ lɛ?

english: Coconut leaves naturally age over time as the tree grows. When leaves look old and dry, it means they have finished their work, and the tree needs to focus its energy on growing new leaves and fresh fruits.
ga: Kokoo baai lɛ daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Beni baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔ ni egbi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ agbe nitsumɔ lɛ naa. Ni ehe miihia ni tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai heei kɛ aduawai heei ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it necessary for me to cut off old leaves from my coconut trees?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni afolɔ baai momoi kɛjɛ ŋmei tso mli?

english: Yes, it is necessary to prune old leaves. Cutting them off helps the coconut tree direct its food and water to healthy green leaves and developing coconuts instead of wasting energy on dying foliage.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni afolɔ baai momoi lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmei tso lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli lɛ anɔ. ni amɛfee ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni miigboi lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to prune leaves from my coconut trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei baai lɛ?

english: You should prune your coconut tree whenever the leaves look old, yellowed, or fully dry. Regular pruning keeps the tree clean, healthy, and growing strong.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo o-coconut tso lɛ he be fɛɛ be ni baai lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔŋ, loo egbi kwraa. Tso lɛ he tsemɔ daa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ he tseɔ, ehiɛɔ hewalɛ, ni edaa waa.

english: Will trimming old leaves off my coconut trees really help them perform better?
ga: Ani ŋmeii momo ni afoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tso mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, removing old leaves helps the crop significantly. It allows more sunlight and air to reach the tree and ensures the plant's resources go directly into producing good yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai momoi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni akɛ tsei amli nibii atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.
