english: What should I do with the old coconut leaves after I cut them off?
ga: Kɛ́ mifo ŋmei baai momo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: Instead of throwing them away or burning them, you should stack the cut leaves on the ground around your farm. Stacking them helps protect and feed your soil.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ loo oshã Esa akɛ okɛ baai ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha niyenii.

english: Why do extension officers recommend stacking cut leaves on the farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ato baai ni afolɔ awo ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When you stack cut leaves on the ground, they slowly break down and rot. This returns all the nutrients that the coconut tree originally absorbed back into the soil for future growth.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni afolɔ lɛ to shikpɔŋ lɛ, amɛgboiɔ fiofio ni amɛgboiɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fɛɛ ni ŋmei tso lɛ ŋɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ wɔsɛɛ.

english: How do plants put back nutrients into the soil after taking them out?
ga: Te tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii beni ajie amɛ lɛ?

english: Crops take nutrients from the earth to build their trunks, leaves, and fruits. When old leaves are cut and stacked on the soil to decay, those stored nutrients are released back into the ground.
ga: Tsei kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ tsei ashishifãi, baai, kɛ aduawai. Afoɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni atoɔ shikpɔŋ koni amɛgboi. No sɛɛ lɛ, abaajie nakai niyenii mli nibii ni ato lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Can stacking old leaves on my farm replace some of the nutrients my soil loses?
ga: Ani baai momoi ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsake niyenii mli nibii ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ miifite lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Yes, piling up cut leaves allows them to act as natural mulch. As they rot, they give back the natural food and minerals that the crop absorbed during its growth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, baai ni afolɔ ni atoɔ lɛ haa amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ mineral ni tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Does leaving pruned coconut leaves on the farm harm the crop's roots?
ga: Ani ŋmei baai ni afolɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ náa tsei lɛ ashishifãi anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo ko?

english: No, it actually benefits the crop. Stacking pruned leaves covers the soil, traps moisture, and enriches the earth as the leaves rot, giving back food to the tree's root system.
ga: Dabi, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he diɛŋtsɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Baai ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni abua naa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii be mli ni baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Ehaa niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my coconut tree seem to grow better after I clear out the dry leaves and stack them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso lɛ feɔ fɛo beni mibua baai ni egbi lɛ anaa ni mikɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Trimming old leaves frees up the plant's energy, while stacking the cut leaves on the ground returns valuable nutrients to the soil, giving the crop a healthy boost from top to bottom.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai momoi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ atsu nii. yɛ be mli ni baai ni afo lɛ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa niyenii ni jara wa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi kɛyashi shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, harsh sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving some tall trees creates a cool, humid environment that helps young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ. Ebaaha shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava sticks so that I get big tubers at harvest time?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu amɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni aná bulbs wuji kɛji kpamɔɔ be lɛ shɛ?

english: Planting cassava sticks about 1 meter apart gives the roots enough space to spread out underground and absorb nutrients without competing with neighboring plants, leading to larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ. ni kɛ yitso ni da baa

english: How do I choose the right suckers from my plantain tree to start a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni sa kɛjɛ plantain tso mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for 'sword suckers,' which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. They grow much faster, produce stronger stems, and yield larger plantain bunches than 'water suckers,' which have wide, leafy tops early on.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni shishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa. Bɔɔ tso lɛ tso ni mli wa ni ofee plantain tsei lɛ agbo fe ‘nu-nu-nu-nu-nu-ŋmei’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ yɛ shishijee lɛ

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ ni Akɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. The worms eat the young growing leaves, which slows the plant's growth; applying recommended neem extracts or insecticides early in the morning directly into the leaf funnel helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ baai bibii, ni no haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ wo tso lɛ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the plant sap and spread viruses. Controlling these pests early with neem oil spray keeps new leaves healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai heei lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize field so it does not waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekafee yaka?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, such as right after a light rain or early in the morning. Avoid applying just before heavy rains, as floodwaters will wash the fertilizer away from the crop roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, tamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ loo leebi maŋkpa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Ejaakɛ nu afua lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli.

english: How can I improve soil that has become hard and dry so my crops can grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi lɛ aya hiɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Adding organic matter like well-rotted animal manure, compost, or decayed leaves softens hard soil, helps it hold water longer, and provides essential food for crop roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi aŋmei ni egbo, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo baai ni egboi fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei shishifãi

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, sunken spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii ni ebote shishi dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the plant. Keeping the soil consistently moist rather than letting it dry out completely helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ lɛ daa loo calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbi kwraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium ni sa.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight on their leaves to produce energy for growing tubers underground; staking holds the leaves up toward the sun and keeps them off the wet soil where they could rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu lɛ he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni baanyɛ afite.

english: Why does letting grass grow around my young crops slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ahaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔleɔ he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ miiha amɛdalɛ miiba shi?

english: Weeds and grass steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and build leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the planting season helps keep the leaves healthy and increases your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei ahe tsei lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have microscopic helpers in their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When you rotate them with crops like maize, they leave behind natural plant food for the next planting season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ yelikɛbualɔi bibii ni anaa yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa tsake amɛ lɛ, eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: This pattern is caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny flying insects called whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and using clean stem cuttings helps keep your farm safe.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa loo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ Oduɔ ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔ lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: What is causing the young leaves on my pepper plants to wrinkle and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Wrinkled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves. Spraying your crops with neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticides removes these pests so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do flowers keep falling off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by too much heat, shade that is too thick, or attacks by tiny insects like mirids. Pruning extra tree branches to let in light and managing sap-sucking pests helps flowers stay on and form healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Shade lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ashwishwɛi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni akɛwo la mli ni akɛtsa kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Should I leave all the young suckers growing around my main plantain stand?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi mibii lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ? Ani eji mi-plantain titri lɛ?

english: No, leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for water and soil nutrients, leading to small plantain bunches. Cut away extra suckers and keep only two or three healthy ones at different ages alongside the parent plant.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa plantains lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ masɛi.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines up off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage into the air and prevents rainy ground moisture from causing leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekaha baai lɛ fite.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together cause thin stalks and small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for water, air, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and nutrients to develop strong stems and big fruits.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ waa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why are my growing tomatoes getting black, rotten spots at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miida lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egboɔ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. Watering your garden regularly and mixing organic manure or lime into the soil prevents this from happening.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli. Okɛ nu awo abɔɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ organic fertilizer loo lime afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni enɛ akafee.

english: Why does my harvested corn get ruined by insects and mold so quickly after storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni akɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain rots and attracts insects when it is put into storage before drying completely. Sun-dry your maize until the kernels are hard, and store them in clean, airtight sacks or treated storage containers to prevent mold and pests.
ga: Ŋmãa fiteɔ ni egbalaa kooloi kɛji akɛ akɛto dani egbi kwraa. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku loo nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi akabote mli.

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for nutrients, causing the plants to grow tall, thin stems with very small tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ efee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Ni eshishifãi lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulb bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shishi.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans on the same farm plot together with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpeas loo beans yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is beneficial because beans trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and improves crop yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa ŋmãa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Yellowing bottom leaves show that the soil lacks enough nitrogen, forcing the plant to pull stored nutrients from its older lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops produce lush green leaves when I apply poultry manure, but delay in bearing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo kooloi amli lɛ? Shi nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ?

english: Poultry manure is high in nitrogen, which builds leaves and stems, but crops need additional nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to move from leafy growth into flowering and fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo yɛ kooloi ashishifã mli. ni feɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii Shi tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium. Koni ejɛ baa lɛ dalɛ mli kɛya fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves burn and drop off during the bright sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight; harsh light burns their sensitive leaves and dries out their roots unless they are protected by temporary shade plants like plantains.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. La ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. ja tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ebu he

english: Why is my maize crop producing small, half-filled cobs during a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni dalɛ ji fã yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize requires steady water during flowering to produce pollen; drought stress at this stage prevents complete fertilization, leaving cobs poorly filled with grains.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmã daa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli koni ekɛ pollen aba. Hɔmɔ he haomɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ fɔmɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ naa. Ni aaashi ŋmei lɛ ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ lɛ ehiii.

english: Extreme heat and inconsistent water stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to conserve energy and water rather than producing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Should I cut off the small extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Ani plantain lɛ shishi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Yes, removing extra shoots (suckers) leaves only one or two strong stems, preventing them from competing with the main mother plant for food and water so you get larger plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine (ŋmeii) ni ooojie lɛ baaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkɛ tso nyɛ titri lɛ akabɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ koni amɛha bo jwɛi wulu.

english: Why do weeds appear to grow much faster than my crops immediately after the major rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshinii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit ready in the topsoil and absorb water instantly, allowing them to sprout and steal soil nutrients before young crop seeds can fully establish their roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmɔɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni ejuɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani dumɔwui bibii lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifãi kwraa.

english: Why do the growing centers of my young maize plants look chewed up with dirt that looks like sawdust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hei ni miida yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which burrow into the center funnel of the plant and chew on fresh leaves, leaving waste that resembles wet sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Shĩ jwɛi ni tamɔ tsei ni efɔ lɛ ashwie.

english: Why should I plant only one maize seed per hole instead of dropping three or four seeds together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwu kome pɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, nyɛɛ du wu etɛ loo eywiɛ kake.

english: Planting one seed per hole gives the seedling full access to soil food, water, and sunlight without competing with neighboring plants. This creates a stronger stalk and produces larger, fuller cobs instead of many small, weak ones.
ga: Dumɔwu kome ni aduɔ yɛ bu fɛɛ bu mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kwraa. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahe wa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ najiaŋ. mɛi babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: If I plant my cassava crops very close to each other, won't I harvest more food from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe Ani minyɛŋ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When cassava plants are too close together, their roots fight for space and nutrients under the soil. Giving them proper spacing ensures each plant has enough room to develop thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs ni mli wa ni tsii baa.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings droop and die when I move them from the nursery to the field in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: The strong afternoon heat causes fresh seedlings to lose water faster than their young roots can absorb it. Transplanting early in the morning or late in the evening gives the roots cooler soil and time to settle.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa dumɔwui heei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛ be ni amɛkɛbaahi shi.

english: What is the benefit of digging small soil basins around my crop roots instead of leaving the farm flat?
ga: Nubu bibioo ko ni atsaa Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Small soil basins help catch rainwater and hold moisture directly around the root zone. They also keep heavy rains from washing away topsoil and nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii buaa nugbɔ nu naa ni amɛhiɛɔ nu ni mli edɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting choked by too much water in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When crop roots stay submerged in waterlogging soil for too long, they cannot breathe. The leaves will start turning pale yellow and the plant will stop growing even though there is plenty of water.
ga: Kɛ tso shishifãi hi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ ohe awo mli Baai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni tsei baakpa kwɛ̃mɔ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ po.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil between my young vegetable crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) shades the earth from direct heat, keeps moisture in the soil longer during sunny days, and prevents weeds from popping up easily.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo gbii amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni jeɔ kpo oya lɛ naa

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that provide natural shade and protect the cocoa plants until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛhaa kookoo tso lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster than my food crops when the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie hidden in the soil waiting for moisture. Removing them early while your main crops are small stops the weeds from stealing water and nutrients from your crop roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Be mli ni otso titri lɛ ji bibioo lɛ Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli.

english: Why should I place dry palm fronds over my vegetable seedbed before the seeds sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tsei ni egbi awo mi-vegetables saatso lɛ nɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Palm fronds shade the delicate soil from heavy raindrops that wash seeds away and protect the seedbed from drying out under the hot sun until germination happens.
ga: Palm baai buɔ shikpɔŋ ni waaa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hoɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛyaa lɛ he. ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ

english: Why is it better for us farmers in the village to join a group to learn new farming methods together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ wɔ akrowa mli okwaafoi lɛ baafata kui ahe ni wɔfee ekome kɛkase okwaayeli gbɛ̀i heei lɛ?

english: Working in a group allows extension officers to demonstrate techniques easily, makes it cheaper to buy seed and fertilizer together, and lets farmers share labor and experiences to fix farm problems.
ga: Nitsumɔ yɛ kui amli lɛ haa mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ jieɔ ŋaa gbɛ̀i akpo. easily Enɛ haa dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfeɔ ekome lɛ he jara waaa. ni ehaa okwaafoi lɛ jaa nitsumɔ kɛ niiashikpamɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli naagbai ahe nitsumɔ mli.

english: How long must I wait after spraying pest chemicals on my vegetables before I can harvest and sell them?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani akpa amɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Every chemical has a safety period called a pre-harvest interval. You must wait a specific number of days or weeks for the chemical to break down naturally in the sun so the crops become safe for human consumption.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa yɛ be ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɛɔ lɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ. Esa akɛ omɛ gbii loo otsii babaoo dani tsofai lɛ afite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulu la mli. Koni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai niyenii

english: Can applying too much chemical fertilizer at once actually scorch or kill my crops?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã loo efite?

english: Yes, applying excess fertilizer causes salt to build up in the soil, which pulls water away from plant roots rather than letting them drink. This burns the roots and causes leaves to dry up and wither.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei buaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha enu. Enɛ baashã shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛgbi.

english: Why does using the exact same pest chemical over and over stop killing insects on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ haaa agbe kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects adapt quickly. When you use the same chemical continuously, the few pests that survive pass their strength on to their young, making the chemical useless over time. Rotating different chemicals prevents this resistance.
ga: Kplukai tsakeɔ amɛhe oya Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii be fɛɛ be Kplukai fioo ni yeɔ wala lɛ baaha amɛhewalɛ lɛ aha amɛbii lɛ. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa yɛ be ni sa mli. Tsofai srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nɛkɛ shitee-kɛ-woo nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves dry up and turn brown during the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees naturally prefer shade. Direct harsh sunlight causes heat stress and scorches their leaves because their small roots cannot pump up water fast enough to keep the plant cool.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔ hulutsoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa ni eshãa baai kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ. Amɛ nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ nu nɔ oya bɔ ni sa ni eha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn pale yellow after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them. Without nitrogen, maize plants lose their green color and struggle to make food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfee niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without growing into peppers when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to save energy and moisture. High temperatures can also damage pollen, preventing fruits from forming.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafite. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa hu baanyɛ afite pollen. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and get light yellow patches during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellowish patches usually indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus damages the leaves so the plant cannot create enough energy to expand its roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ yucca mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Leaf blight virus lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the day even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ani nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo?

english: This is often caused by bacterial or fungal wilt in the soil. The disease blocks the tiny tubes inside the plant stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves even when the ground is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ muawai loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Hela lɛ tsiɔ tsɔnei bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa, ni no haaa nu ayashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do many tiny black pods on my cocoa tree die off before growing into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cocoa ŋmeii bibii Ani mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gboiɔ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees naturally shed excess young pods they cannot afford to feed with available water and nutrients, though fungal diseases like black pod can also cause it.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aha amɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods hu baanyɛ aha amɛba moŋ.

english: How does pruning branches from my cocoa tree help me get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ?

english: Pruning removes dead or non-producing branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This directs the tree's energy into producing healthy pods while reducing moisture that causes fungal rot.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egboi loo ni wooo yibii lɛ ajieɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba, yɛ be mli ni ebaa ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ shi.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often only wets the top layer of soil without deep moisture. If a hot, dry spell follows immediately, the germinating seeds dry out and die before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni mli edɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot survive under harsh, direct sunlight or hot winds. Shade trees protect them from burning and help keep soil moisture high until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shãaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. This often happens in poor soil or when heavy rains wash nutrients down below the root level.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi kɛyashɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishi.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes in the soil for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tso kakadaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce food, which is then stored underground to form tubers. Staking keeps leaves off the ground, maximizing sunlight and increasing your yield.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee ŋmeii. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to high temperatures, uneven watering, or lack of pollination. When conditions are too hot or dry, the plant sheds flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Nɔ titri ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa ji hulutsoo ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoot suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around a plantain tree, they steal water and food from the mother plant. Leaving only two or three healthy suckers ensures the main plant grows a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable crops with dry leaves or grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct heat from the sun, trapping soil moisture and preventing weed growth around your crop's roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and shrink into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or viruses spread by them. These pests drain sap from new leaves, causing them to twist and stop growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai heei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛtsiɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inner leaves inside the middle of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on young maize leaves. The hatched caterpillars crawl deep inside the central whorl of the plant where it is dark and moist to feed safely.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii baai bibii anɔ lɛ. Kplukai ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye nii shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully mature and ready for harvest under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants show maturity when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a tuft of green leaves at the top. You can also carefully dig around one plant base to inspect tuber size.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni amɛshishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ashi baai eŋɔlii akuu ko yɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Kwɛmɔ tso kome shishi jogbaŋŋ koni ona bɔ ni eyitso lɛ da ha.

english: Why do older farmers always tell me to plant groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛɔ mi be fɛɛ be akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts act like natural soil helpers. They pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, which feeds the hungry maize plants. Planting them together gives you two crops from one field while keeping the soil healthy.
ga: Peanuts tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ yelikɛbualɔi. Amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ wo he kome lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land stop producing good cassava if I plant it in the same spot three times in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kpaɔ ŋmei kpakpa kɛji midu yɛ he kome shii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava takes specific nutrients out of the soil every season. If you keep planting it in the exact same spot without giving the soil a break or planting a different crop like beans, the soil becomes completely empty and tired.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ he kome ni ogbalaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo oduuu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: If I trim away too many branches from my cocoa tree, will it affect the cocoa pods?
ga: Ni kɛji mifolɔ kookoo niji babaoo hu? Ani ebaana kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes. Leaves act like small food factories that use sunlight to nourish the tree. If you cut off too many leaves and branches, the tree loses its ability to feed itself, causing young pods to dry up and drop off.
ga: Hɛɛ. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii afeemɔ hei bibii. ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa tsei niyenii Kɛji ofolɔ baai kɛ niji babaoo Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii dɔŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: What happens to my maize if I put too much chemical fertilizer on the land thinking it will grow faster?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni misusu akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ oya?

english: Too much fertilizer can burn the roots of your crops, similar to putting too much salt in a small pot of soup. Instead of growing faster, the leaves will turn brown and dry out, which can kill the whole crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Etamɔ ŋoo babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shwiili bibioo ko mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaada oya lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. ni baanyɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii muu fɛɛ

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or tiny insect attacks. Keeping the soil moist and protecting the crop from pests encourages the flowers to stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa lɛ lɛ hao tso lɛ. Ehe hia ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni abu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui ahe. Ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi daa ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yam tubers from underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the leaves and vines above the ground naturally turn yellow and dry up, it means the yam tuber has finished growing. Digging them up too early leaves you with soft, small yams, while leaving them too long exposes them to rotting.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ egbe naa. Tsɔɔmɔ mra tsɔ ni obaagbe naa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo. yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha egbo.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers or cocoa seedlings wither when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui loo cacao tsei lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young plants have delicate roots that cannot pull water from deep in the ground yet. Strong direct sunlight dries out their leaves quickly, which is why providing temporary shade helps them survive their early months.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ha lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild and tough, meaning they naturally steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops the room and food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ gbeyei ni amɛhe wa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei ni miida lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it up. Curling leaves is the plant's way of reducing its surface area to save water, and covering the soil with dry grass helps keep root moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why did some of the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their life if they were stored in warm, damp places or attacked by hidden insects. Storing well-dried seeds in sealed containers keeps them healthy and ready to sprout when planted.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ agbo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni edɔ loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛ́ adu amɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant my crops in straight lines with specific spacing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ adu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ krɛdɛɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines with proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients to grow strong, while also making weeding and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Certified seeds are specially tested to grow faster, give higher yields, and resist local pests and diseases much better than seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛdara oya. Ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fe dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How can I increase the amount of maize I harvest from my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmãa ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: To get a bigger harvest, you need to use good quality seeds, space your plants properly so they don't fight for light, apply the right fertilizer at the right time, and clear weeds early.
ga: bɔni afee ni okpa nibii babaoo Ehe miihia ni okɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ atsu nii. Tsɔɔmɔ otsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ koni amɛkatswa la he akaŋ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ mra.

english: Why are weeds so harmful to my growing crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly away from your crops. If you let weeds grow, your crops will stay weak and produce a very small harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji oha jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii fioo.

english: What causes my crop leaves to turn yellow and get dark spots on them?
ga: Mɛni miiha mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yellow leaves and spots are usually caused by crop diseases, tiny insects feeding on the plant, or a lack of proper nutrients in the soil. wet weather and crowded plants can make these diseases spread faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ tso helai, koolooi bibii ni yeɔ tso lɛ, loo niyenii kpakpa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha helai nɛɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: How can I stop diseases from spreading and destroying my tomato crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite mi-tomato tsei lɛ?

english: You can protect your crop by removing infected plants immediately so they don't infect healthy ones, avoiding planting tomatoes in the exact same spot every year, and following recommended treatment steps early.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie oya koni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akahe hela lɛ nɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tomato ni ooodu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ he. ni onyiɛ tsofafeemɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ asɛɛ mra.

english: Why does rain sometimes cause more diseases to show up on my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ kɛ helai babaoo baa mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Many plant diseases are caused by fungi and bacteria that thrive in moisture. Heavy rain splashes these germs from the soil onto plant leaves and keeps the foliage wet, allowing diseases to grow.
ga: Fungi kɛ bacteria ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ kɛ tsei ahelai babaoo baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ. ni eha tso lɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba

english: What is a starter fertilizer, and why should I use it when planting?
ga: Mɛni ji shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Starter fertilizer is a small amount of nutrients placed near the seed at planting time. It gives young seedlings quick access to food so they can build strong roots early and grow much faster.
ga: Starter fertilizer ji niyenii fioo ko ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwu lɛ masɛi yɛ dumɔ be mli. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ náa niyenii oya. Koni etswa shishifãi ni wa mra ni edara oya

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every year drains the same nutrients continuously and lets crop-specific pests and diseases build up in the ground. Changing crops restores the soil and starves the pests.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei komekomei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my crops at the start of the rainy season rather than late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu nibii mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting early in the rainy season ensures your young crops get consistent water when they are growing fastest. If you plant late, the rains may stop before the plants finish producing their crop.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa otsei bibii lɛ náa nu ni hoɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa oya fe fɛɛ lɛ. Kɛji odu sɛɛ Nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa dani tsei lɛ agbe amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afeemɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither if I plant them in an open field without any shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby provides a protective canopy that reduces heat stress and preserves essential moisture in the soil for the young cocoa roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaha ŋwɛitsu ni buɔ mɔ he ni baaha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Leaf rolling is a survival mechanism where the maize plant reduces its leaf surface area exposed to the sun, helping it trap moisture and prevent water loss through evaporation during extreme heat.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Abɛi lɛ baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa nu lɛ afite kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants look wilted in the hot afternoon sun even when the dirt around their roots is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli edɔ lolo po.

english: During peak heat, pepper leaves lose water through transpiration faster than the roots can pull moisture from the ground, causing temporary wilting until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cashew trees shed so many of their early flowers before any nuts begin to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi mra dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cashew trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support as fruit. When faced with hot, dry winds or water stress, the tree voluntarily drops weak flowers to save energy and water for surviving heat.
ga: Cashew tsei woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ adebɔɔ naa moŋ fe aduawai. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu he haomɔ kpe lɛ Tsei jɛɔ amɛsuɔmɔ mli amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape along the middle line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ teŋgbɛ ŋta lɛ he lɛ?

english: A V-shaped yellowing starting from the tip of older, lower maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency, showing that the plant is starving for essential nutrients needed to build green leaf matter.
ga: V-shaped yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baa ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ naagbee lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce big bushy green leaves above ground but only thin, weak roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shishi?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing and enriching the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize that follow them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni nyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and slender and easily fall over in the wind when I put many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Overcrowding forces seedlings to compete intensely for light, causing them to stretch rapidly upward into thin, weak stalks with shallow root systems that cannot support the weight of the plant.
ga: Nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ tsɛɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ tso lɛ muji lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do fall armyworms concentrate inside the central funnel leaf of my young maize instead of eating the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa mi-baby corn lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ baa lɛ?

english: The central funnel, or whorl, contains the youngest, softest, and most nutrient-dense tissue of the plant, making it the easiest place for young caterpillars to feed and hide from direct sunlight and predators.
ga: Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa, loo whorl lɛ ji he ni tso lɛ mli fãji bibii fe fɛɛ, ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ he ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna niyenii ni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the cocoa pods on my trees start turning dark brown or black during periods of heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungal pathogen that thrives in high humidity and wet weather, spreading rapidly across pods through rain splashes and stagnant moisture trapped under thick canopy shade.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ pods nɔ kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekã shi ni emɔ ŋwɛitsu ni mli tse lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: How does the quality of my soil affect the total yield I harvest from my crops?
ga: Te bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ saa yibii fɛɛ ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The soil acts as the primary food store for your crops. Everything the plant produces comes from the nutrients and water it draws from the ground, so healthy soil directly leads to bigger harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ji nɔ titri ni haa onibii lɛ náa niyenii kpakpai. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni tsei feɔ lɛ jɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ kpamɔ babaoo baa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do my crops take up food from the ground to grow strong?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Crops use their roots to absorb water and tiny nutrient particles from the soil. These nutrients travel up through the stem to help the plant build leaves, strong stems, and healthy fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii bibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛi nɛɛ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛ wo baai ni wa, ashishifãi lɛ ashishifãi, kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do two farms planted with the same seed yield differently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji enyɔ ni akɛ dumɔwu kome du lɛ woɔ yibii sɔrɔtoi lɛ?

english: A crop only performs well if it receives good care. Factors like regular soil feeding, weeding, proper spacing, and watering determine whether a crop reaches its full harvest potential.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ pɛ kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, nibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni sa Ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ ekpamɔ he hewalɛ ni sa lɛ he.

english: What is the difference between my local crop seeds and the 'agric' seeds sold in stores?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ mimaŋ tsei ahe dumɔwui kɛ ‘kwaayeli’ dumɔwui ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Agric' seeds are improved varieties bred to grow faster, sprout more reliably, and give higher yields than traditional local seeds, though they often require good soil care to thrive.
ga: Okwaayeli’ dumɔwui ji dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛdara oya. amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe blema maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa koni amɛshwere moŋ.

english: Why do some crop varieties sprout out of the ground much faster than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi jeɔ kpo oya fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different varieties have different natural growth speeds. Improved seeds are often bred with stronger seed energy, allowing them to sprout quickly and establish roots before weeds take over.
ga: Srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, akɛ dumɔwui ahewalɛ ni mli wa fɔɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛtswaa shishifãi dani jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ.

english: Is an improved 'agric' seed variety always better for my farm than my traditional local variety?
ga: Ani ‘kwaayeli’ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be fe mi maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Improved varieties generally give higher yields in shorter times, but they perform best when given good soil management and care, whereas traditional varieties might be more tolerant of low-care conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ aha amɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa. yɛ be mli ni blema henɔi lɛ baanyɛ akpɛlɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my crops shoot up new stems right from the base near the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miikwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛmiijɛ shishitoo ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Many plants naturally produce side shoots or suckers from their lower base as a way to spread out, store backup energy, or multiply new growth.
ga: Tsei babaoo fɔɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Too hewalɛ ni ato loo okɛ dalɛ hee afata he

english: Why do some crop stems stand straight and strong while others fall over easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ja ni amɛhe wa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi gbeeɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: A plant stands straight when it gets enough stem-strengthening nutrients from the soil and plenty of direct sunlight, helping it develop a rigid trunk that resists wind.
ga: Tsei baadamɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ amɛná niyenii ni wajeɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni wa ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: How are some seeds able to sprout even when the ground looks dry and hard?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui komɛi nyɛɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni ewa po lɛ?

english: Certain resilient crop varieties have strong shoot energy that allows them to break through tough soil crusts and tap into hidden moisture stored deeper underground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ashwieɔ shi lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii ahe hewalɛ ni haa amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli ni amɛboteɔ nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Should I cut off the extra shoots sprouting at the base of my crop, or let them grow?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli loo maha amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Removing extra base shoots usually helps the plant send all its food and water to the main stem, resulting in larger, healthier crops rather than many small, crowded ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ eniyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ yaa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ feɔ tsei bibii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why did my land give me very big harvests for the first two years, but now the crops are weak and failing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi amrɔ nɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee nɔ ko?

english: When you clear fresh land, the soil has natural nutrients built up over time. After two years of continuous farming, the crops pull out those nutrients, leaving the soil exhausted unless you restore it with fertilizer, manure, or crop rotation.
ga: Kɛji ojie he ko hee lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni abua naa yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ afii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ mli. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ saa ehe.

english: What happens to my farm if I keep planting the exact same crop on the same plot without giving the land a rest?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mihaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil, causing yields to drop lower each year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi

english: Why do my crops grow tall and strong at first, but then suddenly fall over to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwere ni ehiɛ wa yɛ shishijee mli, shi trukaa lɛ egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Crops usually fall over because their root systems are weak or damaged underground by pests, diseases, or waterlogging. As the top of the plant grows heavy, weak roots can no longer hold it upright in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efite amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ bafee tsii Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ amɔ lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling down even when there is no heavy storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miigbee shi lɛ? He ni ahum ni naa wa bɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that are easily eaten by underground pests like root nematodes or stem borers. Without strong roots anchoring them to the ground, the heavy weight of the plantain bunch causes the whole tree to tip over.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers yeɔ amɛ oya. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni akɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ baaha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ agbee shi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak stems that collapse easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fãa oya lɛ?

english: If seeds are planted too close together, the plants stretch upward rapidly to search for sunlight. This makes them grow tall, thin, and weak, causing them to fall over under their own weight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛtao hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɔ, amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛgbɔjɔ, ni no haa amɛkuɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsiimɔ shishi.

english: Why do my fruit tree branches break when they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii niji lɛ fãa kɛ amɛbɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Trees break under heavy fruit loads if the wood lacks strength from nutrients like potassium, or if the tree was not pruned to build strong, thick branches capable of carrying heavy yields.
ga: Tsei baafo kɛjɛ aduawai babaoo mli kɛji akɛ tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium mli, loo kɛji akɛ afolɔɔɔ tso lɛ mli koni ekɛfee niji ni mli wa ni mli wa ni baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops yield poorly if I plant a few weeks after the main rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai kɛji midu amɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni nugbɔ wulu lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: The early rains cause a natural release of nutrients in the soil called a nitrogen flush. Planting late means your crops miss this natural boost of nutrients and may not get enough rainfall to mature fully.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen flush. Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ naaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni ekolɛ amɛnaŋ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara.

english: How do I know if I missed the right window to put my seeds in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mifo samflɛ ni sa ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: If the rains have been falling for weeks, weeds are established, and the soil has cooled down, the prime planting window has likely passed. Seeds planted late struggle against weeds and miss peak moisture.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ otsii babaoo lɛ Jwɛi miije kpo ni shikpɔŋ lɛ miiho, ni tsɔɔ akɛ be ni he hiaa waa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ eho. Dumɔwui ni adu sɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ jwɛi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛ naaa nu babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade from plantains or shade trees when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ he hiaa ni ekɛ plantain loo tsei krokomɛi ni haa tso lɛ aná hulutsoo be mli ni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight and short roots that dry out quickly. Shade trees protect them from intense heat and keep the surrounding soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ, kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my healthy crops suddenly turn yellow and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Leaf yellowing is a sign that the plant is stressed, usually caused by a lack of nitrogen in the soil, root rot from wet soil, or severe dry spells stopping the roots from taking up food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye nii.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is its main food. The plant is pulling nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves and growing corn ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tso lɛ miigbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves. They suck the sap out of the young leaves, causing them to twist, dry out, and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. Severe heat sterilizes the pollen inside the flower, so fruit cannot form, causing the plant to shed the useless bloom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbeɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai efeee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he.

english: When soil has too much rich manure or nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers in the soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni efee bulbs ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut away extra shoot suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: If you leave too many suckers attached to the mother stem, they will steal water, light, and soil food from the main plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one strong stem to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ nyɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ plantains wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Yam leaves need to be lifted high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the tuber. Staking also keeps leaves away from damp ground heat and soil diseases that rot the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ awo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la babaoo aná bɔ ni aaanyɛ ni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking hu buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni haa tso lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last maize harvest produce smaller crops than the hybrid seed packages I buy from the agricultural shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields, but their special power only lasts for one planting. Saving seeds from that harvest causes the next generation to lose its strength, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ dumɔ kome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abaabu kɛjɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ baaha yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ahewalɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow much better when I plant them in the same field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes nitrogen out of the dirt, but cowpeas put natural nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Rotating these crops naturally restores soil fertility without needing extra expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shi cowpea kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii nɛɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade from larger trees or plantains to shield their soft leaves and keep the soil moist until their root system is fully established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli koni amɛbu baai bibii ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbe naa.

english: Why do my mature tomato fruits crack open right before they are ready for picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split open when there is a sudden heavy rain after a long dry spell. The plant drinks up water too fast, swelling the inside of the tomato faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to tear open.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei nuɔ nu oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa tomato lɛ mli lɛ fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji hewolo lɛ mligbalamɔ.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant save moisture and survive extreme heat.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni baa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells to conserve water. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss and protects its underground tubers until rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ haa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni amɛbuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle and burn after I clear all the large forest trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshãa beni mijie koo mli tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees do not have strong root systems yet and cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight. They require shade trees or plantain plants to protect them from heat and soil drying.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli wa lolo, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my tomato crops are getting too much water from the heavy rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Too much water turns crop leaves pale yellow, causes stems to look weak or soft, and causes root rot because wet, waterlogged soil deprives roots of the oxygen they need to breathe.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha tso lɛ baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo eyɛ blɛoo. Ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni he hiaa shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu lɛ.

english: Why do small, ragged holes appear in the leaves of my young corn plants as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by pests like Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on the soft, inner leaves of the plant before they fully open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm caterpillars ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli baai bibii lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ kwraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii amli.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster and stronger than my main crops without any special care?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitso titri lɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii krɛdɛɛ ko lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep roots adapted to quickly steal available soil nutrients, water, and sunlight before your domestic crop plants can use them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ, ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju sũ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ oya dani omaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: What happens to my maize yield if I plant my seeds very close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes plants to crowd each other out. They compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak stalks and smaller corn ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee ekome. Amɛshiɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ atoi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or crop leaves help them grow better?
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry organic matter (mulching) keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, stops weeds from growing, and improves soil fertility as it decays.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi (mulching) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya Ehaa jwɛi shwereɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.
