english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before they can grow into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination, causing the plant to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ye dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he amanehulu. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni bɛ Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the soil better for the maize I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen naturally from the air and trap it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees keep dying when I clear away all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive strong, direct sunlight and hot winds. Leaving larger shade trees or planting plantains nearby creates shade and keeps the air cool, acting like an umbrella while the cocoa plants are young.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta be mli ni cacao tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the dirt. This competition leaves you with thin, weak plants and very small maize cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa.

english: How do I know which food crops are best to grow on my plot of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops prefer different types of soil and water amounts. Looking at how well water drains on your land and testing the soil will tell you if your ground is better suited for root crops like cassava or grains like maize.
ga: Tsei biɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu babaoo. Kɛ́ okwɛ bɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ehaa ni ofee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ bo kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shishifãi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt and lets crop-specific pests multiply. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts puts good nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for leaves, or that excess rain is washing the nutrients too deep down into the ground where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ miifɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: What causes armyworms to suddenly appear and destroy my maize leaves so quickly?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo ni amɛfiteɔ mi-abele baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay thousands of eggs that hatch right when warm weather and fresh rains begin. The young caterpillars grow fast because they have soft, tender green leaves to eat continuously.
ga: Caterpillar ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii akpei abɔ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ. Kplukai lɛ daraa oya ejaakɛ amɛyɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii daa.

english: How long should I wait after the first rain falls before I start planting my seeds?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: It is best to wait until two or three good rains have soaked the ground deeply. Planting after just the very first light rain can cause seeds to dry up and die if heat returns for a few weeks.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi kpakpai enyɔ loo etɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji latsaa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally better at stealing light, water, and soil food. Clearing them early gives your planted crops the head start they need to grow taller than the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii ni odu lɛ aná yitso ni ehe baahia ni amɛdara fe jwɛi.

english: Why do small insects attack and spoil my dried maize even when I tie it inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛfi lɛ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku mli moŋ.

english: Weevil insects can lay invisible eggs on the grain in the field or hide in damp bags. Drying your maize thoroughly under the hot sun until it is completely hard kills these insects before you store the grain.
ga: Kpɔŋɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo ewui ni anaaa lɛ yɛ dumɔwui anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo ekɛtee kotokui ni mli efɔ mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ewaa akɛ ooogbe kooloi bibii nɛɛ dani okpa ŋmãa lɛ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested tomatoes from getting soft and rotting before I reach the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tomato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite dani eyashɛ jara nɔ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly when exposed to heat and rough handling. Harvesting them early in the cool morning, packing them in smooth crates instead of heavy sacks, and keeping them in the shade protects their quality until sale.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo la mli ni akɛtsu nii waa. Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa ni hulutsoo be mli Akɛwoɔ adekai ni mli tse amli yɛ kotokui ni tsii najiaŋ. Ni kɛ́ okɛto hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaabu bɔ ni ehi ha lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect them from direct sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides natural cover that retains soil moisture and keeps the young cocoa trees cool during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he. Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ Ehaa adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: What is causing the small holes in my maize leaves and ragged edges on the growing shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛi ni ekumɔ lɛ amli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the young leaves and inner whorl of maize plants. Checking your fields early and applying recommended biological or chemical sprays inside the leaf funnel can effectively control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is often caused by bacterial wilt or fungal root diseases, which block the water-carrying tubes inside the stem. Rotating your tomato crops with non-solanaceous plants and using disease-resistant seeds helps prevent this soil-borne issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt loo fungal root hela ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ baa. ni tsiɔ nu tsɔne ni akɛyaa tso lɛ mli lɛ naa Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee monoculture ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii kɛ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagbai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I avoid planting my cassava stems too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Planting cassava too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, thin stems and small tubers. Proper spacing gives the roots enough space to expand and form large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulb bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Staking exposes more yam leaves to sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more energy for larger underground tuber growth. It also keeps the leaves off wet soil, reducing the spread of fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a short dry spell, which can dry out the upper soil layer and kill newly germinated seeds. Waiting for continuous, reliable rains ensures that young seedlings get steady moisture to establish strong roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ni aaamɛ lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is running low on nutrients before my crops start to die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ajeɔ gbele shishi?

english: Slow plant growth, pale or yellowing leaves (especially on older foliage), and weak stems are early signs of nutrient deficiency. Observing leaf color changes helps you identify which nutrient is missing so you can apply organic compost or fertilizer early.
ga: tso lɛ daalɛ blɛoo Baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ (Titri lɛ yɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ) kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa. Kɛ́ okwɛ bɔ ni baai lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ole niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts partner with natural soil bacteria to take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food stored in their roots. When the plant roots decay, this natural nitrogen stays in the soil to feed crops like maize planted next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee tsei aniyenii ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for essential resources like soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. When weeds are allowed to spread, they steal water and plant food away from your crops, stunting their development.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la. Kɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi lɛ gbɛ eshwa lɛ, Ebaaju nu ni ebaakwɛ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli. ni ha amɛyiwalaheremɔ ba shi lɛ

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper yibii ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to stress, such as severe heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Mulching the soil to keep it cool and keeping moisture levels consistent helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: If I harvest seeds from my strongest maize stalks, will the new crops grow just as strong as the parent plant?
ga: Kɛji mikpa dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa tsei ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ Ani tso hee lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ?

english: Healthy parent plants pass good traits like disease resistance and high yields down to their offspring seeds. However, if the seed was a hybrid, the next generation might not behave exactly like the parent plant.
ga: Nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baajie sui kpakpai tamɔ helai ni nyɛɔ etswaa kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ kpo etsɔɔ ebii lɛ dumɔwui lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ, Ekolɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ efeŋ amɛnii tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do seeds taken from a diseased cocoa pod often grow into weak seedlings that get sick easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ daa kɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni hela baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Just like parents can pass traits to their young, diseases carried inside a seed pod are inherited by the new seedling, causing it to start life weak and susceptible to pests.
ga: Taakɛ fɔlɔi baanyɛ amɛkɛ sui aha amɛbii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Helai ni etsi dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui heei amli kɛbaa. Enɛ haa ejeɔ shihilɛ shishi ni egbɔjɔ ni enuɔ he akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cassava and sunflower leaves turn to face the sun as it moves across the sky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei kɛ hulutsoo tso lɛ baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ beni etsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Crops actively move towards sunlight because light is their source of energy to make food. Turning leaves toward the sun allows the plant to catch as much sunlight as possible during the day.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ miishɛɛ yaa hulu la lɛ he ejaakɛ la ji hewalɛ jɛɛhe ni akɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ hulu lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa hulu la babaoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of some weeds fold up completely as soon as my boot or cutlass touches them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi komɛi ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa kɛji mi-boot loo mi-dagger lɛ kɛ amɛ kpe pɛ lɛ?

english: Certain plants have a quick defense movement triggered by touch. Closing their leaves makes them look dead or unappetizing to grazing animals and helps deter pests.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ hebuu nifeemɔi ni yaa oya ni kɛ́ mɔ ko ta he lɛ, ekanyaa amɛ. Kɛ́ oha baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi loo kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ sumɔɔɔ amɛ niyenii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa

english: Why do my groundnut and cowpea plants fold their leaves closely together every evening when night falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts kɛ cowpeas lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe daa gbɛkɛ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ shɛ lɛ?

english: Closing leaves at night is a natural resting behavior that helps the plant protect delicate leaf tissue from cool night air and conserve water until daylight returns.
ga: Baai ni agbeɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ su ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ he, ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulu la lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my yam vines naturally start wrapping themselves tightly around wooden stakes placed beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miije shishi amɛmiifee ekome kɛ tso ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines have touch-sensitive growing tips that actively search for nearby structures to cling to, allowing the crop to lift its leaves higher off the ground to reach sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei yɛ teemɔŋ sane ko ni haa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Amɛtaoɔ tsũi ni bɛŋkɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe akpɛtɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ.

english: Why do sweet potato vines sprout new roots wherever their stems trail along damp soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ shishifãi heei shwereɔ ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji tso lɛ shishifã lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ loo etsɔɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Sweet potato stems naturally search for moist soil to anchor themselves, using extra roots to gather water and produce additional food tubers across the bed.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni amɛ ma amɛhe. Ekɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbuaa nu naa ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ saatso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl inwards and look droopy during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a survival behavior crops use during extreme heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and prevent moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Leaf curling ji wala yibiiwoo su ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flower buds when the dry season heat lasts too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ beni latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, a crop will drop its flowers to protect itself. It sacrifices future fruits so it can save remaining moisture to keep its roots and main stem alive.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baashi fɔfɔi yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Ekɛ wɔsɛɛ aduawai shaa afɔle koni enyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my maize crops turn pale yellow and stop growing after heavy rainfall floods the field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Flooded soil suffocates plant roots, preventing them from taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the crop to show stress through yellowing leaves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaaa enine ashɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen nɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ jieɔ haomɔ he okadii akpo kɛtsɔ ebaai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight because their leaves lose water too fast. They require shade trees or plantains to shield them from the sun during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planted too closely, maize plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, thin stalks that produce very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: adu ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Abele kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ŋmeii ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I leave all the shoots growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ.

english: Excess young shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the mother plant. Cutting back extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the main plant gets enough nutrients to produce large bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii loo tsei bibii babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up around them and cuts off oxygen to the root system. Planting cassava on mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled and twisted leaf growth is usually caused by tiny pests like whiteflies or aphids sucking sap from young leaves and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ baa bibii amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why do my yam tubers get smaller every year if I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams feed heavily on soil nutrients. Planting them on the same field every year drains those specific nutrients and allows yam pests to build up in the soil over time.
ga: Sweet potatoes yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ, nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni sweet potato mli ŋmeii lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to be harvested from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up, and the inside of the shelled pod shows dark brown veins instead of a pale white color.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmɔtɔ ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why did my vegetable seeds fail to sprout after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep, if the soil is kept too dry, or if hot weather bakes the soil surface and prevents young shoots from pushing through.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsĩɔ ŋmeii bibii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ mli.

english: Why are the roots of my maize plants coming out of the ground above the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: These are called brace roots. They sprout from the lower stem to anchor tall maize plants against strong winds and heavy rainstorms while gathering additional moisture and nutrients from the topsoil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ shishifãi. Amɛdaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmãa tsei kakadaji ni teɔ shi woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ ahum ni naa wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuaa nu kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short and twisted even though the surface soil looks soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ? Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo?

english: Beneath the loose topsoil, there is often a hard, compacted soil layer called a hardpan. Yams need deep, well-tilled mounds or ridges so the roots and tubers can push down smoothly without hitting hard ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli etse. Bei pii lɛ, sũ ko ni wa ni ebɔle ehe ni atsɛɔ lɛ hard pan lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Sweet potatoes he miihia gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ shi mlɛo ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa.

english: Where exactly should I place fertilizer around my pepper plants so it works well?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe koni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba?

english: Never place fertilizer directly against the stem, as it can chemical-burn the plant. Instead, dig a small hole or shallow ring about 5 centimeters away from the base where the active roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Kaaha ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ejaakɛ ebaanyɛ eha tsei ashã kɛjɛ tsofai amli. Tsɔmɔmɔ bu bibioo ko. loo shallow ring Ha ehi shi aaafee sɛntimitai 5 kɛjɛ shishigbɛ, he ni shishifãi ni tsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: How do I know if my sick soil needs animal manure or chemical fertilizer to fix crop growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ ni hela mɔ lɛ he miihia kooloi aŋmei loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli koni akɛsaa tsei lɛ adalɛ?

english: If leaves turn pale yellow and plants stay small despite watering, the soil is lacking nutrients. Animal manure builds long-term soil structure and moisture holding capacity, while chemical fertilizer provides a quick nutrient boost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ tee nɔ efee bibioo yɛ nu ni awo lɛ sɛɛ po lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa he oya.

english: Why are my traditional planting months no longer working for my rain-fed crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kusum naa dumɔwui nyɔŋ lɛ yɛ srɔto lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ kɛha tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ amɛmli lɛ.

english: Shifting weather patterns in Ghana have changed rainy season start dates, making old calendar rules unreliable. Switching to early-maturing crop varieties and tracking weather forecasts helps prevent crop loss.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ eha atsake gbi ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ kalanda mlai momo lɛ anɔ. Tsakemɔ kɛmiiya tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he akɔntaabuu sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: Why does clearing and burning my farm before planting seem to dry out the soil faster nowadays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãa dani aduɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya bianɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the protective organic layer that retains water in the soil. Leaving dry crop remains on the field as mulch shields the ground from direct sun and keeps soil moist longer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he ni hiɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up and droop during hot sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Plantains roll their leaves during peak afternoon heat to shrink the leaf area exposed to the sun and stop water from evaporating too quickly. They naturally unroll once temperatures cool down.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ plantain baai lɛ yɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ebaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ lɛ shi ni eha nu lɛ akaho oya tsɔ. Ebaajie ehe kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their tiny young pods before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo dani amɛdara kwraa?

english: This shedding process, called cherelle wilt, is natural. The cocoa tree sheds extra young pods when it senses it lacks enough water or soil nutrients to carry every pod to full size.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ cherel wilt ni ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ. Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii ni fa lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛnu he akɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ atere ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kɛyashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Lower leaves age first and receive less light, but rapid yellowing usually means soil-borne fungal spores are splashing onto the bottom leaves during heavy rain or watering.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baagbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni amɛnaŋ la fioo. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni baa oya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ baagbɛ ashwã baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ mli.

english: How do cassava plants manage to stay green and survive through long dry seasons?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Cassava drops its older outer leaves to limit water loss and uses deep feeder roots to draw water from far beneath the surface until the rains return.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ kponɔgbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa. ni ekɛ eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛgbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over and lay on the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Crops fall over—a condition called lodging—when their stems are too weak or their roots are too shallow to hold them upright. This is usually caused by strong winds, poor soil nutrients, planting too close together, or root damage from pests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbee shi Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ shĩa. Beni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ loo shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo shishifãi ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite lɛ.

english: How can I prevent heavy crops like tomatoes or peppers from falling over as they grow big?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ akagbee shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: You can support heavy plants by staking them, which means tying the main stem loosely to a strong wooden stick driven into the ground. This gives the plant extra strength to carry heavy fruits without bending or breaking.
ga: Obaanyɛ oye obua tsei ni tsii kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oookɛwo tso nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akpɛtɛ tso titri lɛ he kɛya tso ni wa ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kroko ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai ni tsii ni efoŋ loo efoŋ.

english: Why do farmers heap soil around the base of crop stems during the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi buaa sũ naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heaping soil around the stem, known as earthing up, buries the roots deeper and gives the plant a wider, stronger base. This anchor protects crops like maize and cassava from being pushed over by rainwater or wind.
ga: heaping dirt around Ale tso lɛ hu akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsakpaa. Eshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. ni ehaa tso lɛ náa shishitoo ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa Ankɔ nɛɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa he. Kaaha nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa yɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I stop weeding my farm for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikpa miŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: When you stop weeding, aggressive wild plants quickly steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil. This starves your crops, making their stems thin and weak so they eventually collapse and die.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa jwɛi shwiemɔ Ko mli tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkuɔ shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ.

english: If I leave my ripe crops in the field without harvesting them immediately, will they suffer?
ga: Kɛ mishi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni mikpako amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ani amɛbaana amanehulu?

english: Yes, leaving ripe crops unharvested makes them overly heavy, causing the plants to fall to the ground. Once on the wet soil, the produce will quickly rot or be eaten by insects and rodents.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ ashi tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni akpaaa amɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshwere fe nine. ni haa tso lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, nibii ni anáa lɛ baafite oya loo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baaye amɛ.

english: Why is it risky to abandon farm work halfway through the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ be lɛ fã mli lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Crops need continuous care at every stage of growth. If you pause work mid-season, pests and weeds quickly takeover, destroying the investment and labor you already put in during the early weeks.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛdalɛ fãi fɛɛ amli. Kɛji okpa nitsumɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ jwɛi baaye nɔ oya. Efiteɔ shika ni okɛwo mli kɛ nitsumɔ ni okɛwo mli momo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain bend my young crops down into the mud?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ miiho kɛmiiya muji lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain softens the soil around the roots while adding heavy water weight to the leaves. If the soil becomes too muddy, the root system loses its grip and the whole plant tilts into the mud.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ muji fa tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala amɛhe ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa muji lɛ mli.

english: Is it harmful to leave an overgrown, unmaintained plot of land right next to my active farm?
ga: Ani ebaafee oshara akɛ mashi shikpɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, an abandoned or overgrown farm becomes a breeding ground for pests, plant diseases, and bush rodents. These problems will easily cross over into your clear farm and attack your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔji ni ashi loo ni ashi amɛ lɛ bafeɔ hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tsei ahe helai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Naagbai nɛɛ foɔ mli oya koni amɛjie ŋmɔji amli ni amɛtutua oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What happens if I plant crops on land that wasn't fully cleared of tree roots and stumps?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajieko tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ kwraa lɛ nɔ?

english: Old roots and tree stumps prevent your crops' root systems from spreading deep into the earth. Shallow roots make plants weak and easily knocked over by rain or wind.
ga: Shishifãi momoi kɛ tsei bibii tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ oya.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my land, will the crops grow well?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ hu? Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight each other for sunlight. They will grow tall, thin, and spindly, making them weak and prone to falling over long before harvest time.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ, ni amɛbaadara, amɛbaatsɔ shwiili, ni amɛhe wa, ni no baaha amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagbee shi be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why can't I just plant my cassava and maize together on the exact same spot without leaving space between them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome ni mishiŋ gbɛ yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: Different crops compete for the same nutrients, water, and sunlight in the soil. Giving each crop its own proper space or planting them in organized rows ensures both crops get enough resources to produce a healthy harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kome ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he ko ni sa loo adu amɛ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, won't I harvest more food because there are more plants on the farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani abaakpa niyenii babaoo ejaakɛ tsei babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes overcrowding, where the plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo baa. Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the trees and plant them under the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni miduɔ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight in their early stage. They require shade crops like plantain to protect their leaves from sunburn and keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ shishijee mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants turn yellow and rot when I water them as heavily as I water my rice field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli babaoo lɛ? Ni nu ni akɛhaa ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Different crops have different water needs. Rice thrives in flooded, standing water, but tomato roots need air and clear drainage; too much water rots tomato roots and causes fungal diseases.
ga: Nu he hiamɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ahe. Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Shi kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he miihia tomato shishifãi. Nu babaoo haa tomato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa.

english: Why is my cassava yield getting smaller every year even though I plant on the exact same piece of land each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mifeɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Ni miduɔ nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ mli?

english: Growing the same crop on the same spot continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating crops or planting leguminous crops like cowpeas helps replenish the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cowpea seeds during the heaviest part of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tsina ŋmei dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Cowpea seeds easily rot in waterlogged soil before they can sprout. They prefer moderate moisture to germinate and dry conditions when producing pods.
ga: Cowpea dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Amɛsumɔɔ hulutsoo ni mli wa koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ he ni egbi koni amɛfee pods.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow huge leafy branches after I apply fertilizer, but produce very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ niji kɛ baai wuji yɔɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli sɛɛ lɛ? Shi ehaa chili fioo ko pɛ?

english: Using fertilizer high in nitrogen encourages the plant to make leaves instead of flowers and fruits. Crops need different types of nutrients at different growth stages to yield well.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo baai yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niyenii srɔtoi he miihia tsei. yɛ dalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli kɛha yibii kpakpai

english: Why do I need to prune or cut off some branches from my tomato plants when they start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo majie niji komɛi kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ beni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches so the plant can focus its energy and nutrients on growing bigger, healthier fruits rather than feeding unnecessary leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii yɛ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha tso lɛ yibii ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do insects destroy my pepper farm faster when I grow only peppers, compared to when I mix them with onions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ oya fe be mli ni miduɔ pepper pɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be ni mikɛ ŋmeii futu mli lɛ he.

english: Large areas of a single crop make it easy for specialized pests to find food and spread quickly. Planting strong-smelling crops like onions nearby confuses pests and deters them naturally.
ga: Hei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi lɛ naa niyenii ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya. Tsei ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa tamɔ sabolai ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baafutu kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds reduce my yam yields so drastically even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi sweet potato yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are aggressive, stealing essential soil nutrients and light away from the yam plants, which stops the tubers underground from swelling and growing large.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ejuɔ la kɛjɛɔ sweet potato tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, or the ground may simply need organic manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo ekolɛ ehe baahia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ atsu nii.

english: Too many shoots compete with the main plant for food, water, and sunlight from the soil. Removing the extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main plant grows big bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni tso titri lɛ akwɛ plantains babaoo.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves to save water when the soil dries out and the air gets hot. Dropping leaves reduces water loss, helping the root tuber stay alive under the soil until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting like paper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ wolo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from under the leaves. Controlling these small pests early stops the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the fruit as it grows. It often happens when watering is irregular or during sudden dry spells when roots cannot absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the energy required to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sun, preventing leaf rot and increasing tuber size.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ehaa yitso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant groundnuts on my farm before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmeii yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can draw nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When groundnut roots rot after harvest, they leave natural food behind that helps the following maize crop grow strong.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ agbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii koni eye ebua ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ nɛɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize crop develop tassels on top and silks on the cob at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛ siliki yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: The tassel at the top sheds powder called pollen, which is carried by the wind to land on the soft silks growing out of the cob. Each silk leads to a single grain, so this process is necessary to fill the whole cob with maize kernels.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ powda ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollen. ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ ni egbeeɔ siliki ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwu kome pɛ yɔɔ siliki kpãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛ nɛɛ he miihia koni akɛ ŋmãa awo ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my garden egg leaves droop and go soft during the hot afternoon sun even if I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can drink it up from the soil. Drooping is a natural defense that reduces leaf surface exposure to sunlight to keep the plant from burning until the evening cool arrives.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Defoliation ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni haa hulu la ni baa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ ashã kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when I plant them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or Gliricidia trees above them to block harsh sun rays and keep the soil moist while they build strength.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo gliricidia tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Koni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛtswaa hewalɛ amɛmaa shi lɛ.

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tuber through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch more light and airflow, preventing rot and directing maximum energy down into growing a large tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo atsɔ mli. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa bulbs wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which suckers to cut away from my plantain bush to get bigger bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni esa akɛ mafo plantain tso lɛ mli koni maná niji wuji?

english: A plantain mother plant shares water and food with all the suckers growing around it. You should keep only one strong 'sword sucker' (a sucker with narrow, pointy leaves) to replace the main plant, and cut down the water suckers (broad-leaved suckers) so energy stays focused on producing big fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ jaa nu kɛ niyenii. Esa akɛ okɛ 'klante tu' kome pɛ ni mli wa ahi shi. Akɛ nu mli ŋmeii (ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ) yeɔ tso titri lɛ najiaŋ ni ajieɔ nu mli ŋmeii (baai ni mli kwɔ) lɛ shi bɔni afee ni anyɛ akɛ hewalɛ atsu nii yɛ yibii wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants and leaving behind sawdust-like powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the central funnel of maize plants to feed on soft new leaves. The sawdust-like material is their waste, and catching them early with recommended sprays or organic neem treatments stops them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni eye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Nibii ni tamɔ ŋmei ji jwɛi. kɛ amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛ tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ he nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, neem baaye abua ni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and develop brown spots during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive moisture and splash from raindrops spread fungal diseases like late blight from the soil onto the leaves. Spacing plants further apart, staking them, and trimming bottom leaves near the wet soil helps reduce humidity around the plant and prevents blight.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ sũ-kɛ-bai amli tsɛŋemɔ baa. Tsei amli gbalamɔ, amɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli, kɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afolɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni eha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aba shi. tsei ahe ni atsĩ blight hela naa

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, very dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like calcium and nitrogen. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and feeding the soil helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium kɛ nitrogen ni faaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ niyenii ha shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I place fertilizer in a small ring around my crop instead of pouring it right against the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii bibii awo ŋmeii amli lɛ? ebɔle ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni eeeshwie nɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Putting concentrated fertilizer directly on the stem burns the plant's skin and primary tissue. Placing it a few inches away in a ring puts the nutrients right where the underground feeding root tips are searching for water and food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ fãji titrii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi he ni shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtaoɔ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria in their roots that suck nitrogen gas out of the air and turn it into natural soil fertilizer. When the legume roots rot after harvest, they leave this free nitrogen behind for the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni shwieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji legume shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava tubers turn dark and spoil within just two or three days of digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli beni atsa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is pulled from the ground, its roots breathe rapidly and react with oxygen in the air, causing internal discoloration and decay. Processing cassava quickly into gari or flour, or keeping tubers submerged in clean water, slows down this decay process.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajieɔ ŋmei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ muɔ oya ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa mligbɛ su tsakeɔ ni efiteɔ. Kasava ni akɛtsuɔ nii oya kɛfeɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ loo yitso ni akɛwoɔ nu ni mli tse mli Ebaaha fitemɔ nifeemɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why does paddy rice grow well in flooded mud while my maize crop turns yellow and dies in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ muji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Beni mi ŋmãa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems that pipe oxygen down from the air to their roots under water. Maize roots do not have these air tubes, so standing water drowns them by suffocating their roots.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an important food crop plants need to stay green and build strong stalks. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure feeds the soil so the leaves can become green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa, ni esa akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ aya hiɛ koni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my young vegetable plants with dried grass make them survive longer during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective shade over the ground. It traps water in the soil so it doesn't dry out quickly under the hot sun and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yam plants rely on their leaves catching direct sunlight to manufacture energy, which is then sent down to build big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they get full sun and don't catch soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ baa ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛ na hewalɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsu lɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tuber agbo ko. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulutsoo be fɛɛ ni amɛha helai akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do groundnut plants produce their nuts underground when the flowers bloom up in the air?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ fɔfɔii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli?

english: Once groundnut flowers are open and pollinated in the air, they drop their petals and send out long stems called pegs. These pegs grow downward, push into the soft soil, and then swell into groundnut pods underneath the ground.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ gbele amɛhe ni amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ejieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​ŋmei kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg lɛ. Nɛkɛ pin nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shi. Tsi kɛya shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ ni efuu ni etsɔ ŋmei ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in standing water while my maize crop dies if water sits on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air channels inside their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots underwater. Maize plants do not have these channels, so their roots suffocate and rot when buried under standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi tsei bɛ nɛkɛ gbɛi nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ afu amɛ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo shishi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their tiny flowers before they can turn into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi bibii dani amɛtsɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel heat stress, usually caused by extremely hot sun, lack of water, or sudden changes in soil moisture. Giving plants steady water and light shade during hot peaks helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnu dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i tsakemɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu ni aha lɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my bearing plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallow in the ground and the tree becomes top-heavy when bearing fruit. Tiny worms in the soil can also weaken the roots, so supporting the stems with bamboo props keeps wind from pushing them down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni tsei yɛ ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo kɛ́ amɛwo yibii. Kplukai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ he lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akatswa lɛ shi.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if the weather gets too hot and dry, or if there are no small insects around to transfer pollen between flowers. Keeping shade trees on the farm protects flowers from heat and provides a habitat for insects to pollinate.
ga: Cocoa tsei baafɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii komɛi bɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe ni baajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ buɔ fɔfɔi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa kooloi ni feɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa shihilɛhe.

english: Underground cassava rot happens when water stays trapped around the roots in heavy soil during rainy periods. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain off so the roots do not rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by viruses spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies. Keeping whiteflies away by using insect nets on nursery beds or spraying natural neem oil helps protect new growth from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ atsĩ ŋmeii yɛji anaa kɛtsɔ saatso nɔ ŋmeii loo adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ ŋmeii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmeii.

english: This usually shows that your soil is low in nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. The maize plant automatically moves nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baa heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on my farm before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which catches nitrogen gas from the air and puts it into the soil. When you plant maize after them, the maize uses this natural plant food to grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ ŋmãa kɛ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Heavy rainfall washes away the fertilizer before plant roots can drink it. The water washes the nutrients off the surface or pushes them too deep into the dirt where your crops cannot reach them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Nu baaho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe loo ebaatsi amɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni oŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Cocoa plants drop their leaves during dry hot seasons to save water. Without enough shade and soil moisture, the leaves dry up quickly, and the tree sheds them to protect its main stem.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly. The plant gets stressed by extreme heat or dry soil and discards flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ eha tso lɛ ehao. ni oshɛrɛ fɔfɔi oshwie koni okɛbu hewalɛ he

english: Why do my cassava roots go bad and rot underground when water collects in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the dirt to stay healthy. When excess water sits around the roots for too long, it cuts off air supply and attracts soil fungi that rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa lɛ mli ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the wet ground helps them catch maximum sunlight and protects the leaves from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa wein tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Extra suckers steal food, sunlight, and water from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree has enough strength to produce a larger, heavier bunch.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from the underside of leaves, or by viruses spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for survival. They aggressively pull away water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhi shi. Amɛjieɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the lower leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, and when the soil lacks it, the plant moves available nutrients from older leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni baai heei ahi nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many bushy leaves, but give me tiny tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi ani oooha bulb lɛ afee bibioo kɛ́ ookpa nii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do people advise planting legumes like beans or groundnuts alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes have special bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally enriches the soil with free nutrients that help the maize grow better.
ga: Legumes yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa abɛi lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering. The plant sheds flowers to save water and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni afɔɔɔ amɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are my cocoa leaves burning and drying up when I plant them in an open field without tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain plants to filter the light, the intense heat burns their delicate leaves and dries out root moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo plantains ni baaha la lɛ atsɔ mli lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ agbi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing green tomatoes turn dark brown and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by calcium deficiency in the fruit. It usually happens when watering is inconsistent, making it difficult for the roots to draw calcium from the soil into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbala calcium kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli.

english: What causes tiny ragged holes and dirt that looks like sawdust inside the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central whorl (funnel) of the maize plant during the day, eating the tender leaves and leaving behind frass (caterpillar waste) that looks like sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ whorl (cone) lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii (worm bits) ni tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over during windstorms even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, and pests like root nematodes or stem borers weaken underground tissues. When roots rot or get eaten, the plant cannot anchor itself properly under the heavy weight of a fruit bunch.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers. Ebaaha fãji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbo loo aye lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atswa ehe jogbaŋŋ yɛ aduawai akutsei ni tsii lɛ ashishi.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines on long sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward the sun so they can manufacture more food for the underground tuber. It also keeps leaves off wet ground, reducing fungal diseases caused by humidity and soil contact.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he bɔni afee ni niyenii babaoo aba aha ŋmeii lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu shwieɔ shi. Tsɔɔmɔ fungal helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ shi.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply chemical fertilizer on my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo miŋmɔji amli?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the soil is moist and the sun is gentle. Applying fertilizer during hot sunshine can burn the plant leaves and roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji leebi loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni hulu la fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baa kɛ shishifãi ashã.

english: How do I know that my rice crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains turn a golden-yellow color and feel hard when you bite them. Delaying harvest causes ripe grains to drop to the ground or get eaten by birds, while harvesting too early leaves you with small, undeveloped grains.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔtɔ. ni enuɔ he akɛ ewa kɛji emɔ Nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbee shikpɔŋ loo okpoi aye amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha oná dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛko.

english: How long can mature rice stay on the stalk in the field before it starts losing quality?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baanyɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Ripe rice should be harvested within 5 to 7 days after reaching maturity. If left too long under the hot sun, the grains dry out excessively on the stalk, causing them to crack easily during threshing and milling.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ gbii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo mli kɛjɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ŋmaa lɛ baagbi tsɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fãa oya yɛ be mli ni ashwieɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔmɔ mli lɛ.

english: How many days should I leave my harvested rice in the sun to dry properly?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Under good sunshine, rice typically takes 2 to 3 days to dry evenly. You can test dryness by cracking a grain with your teeth—if it snaps cleanly without bending, it is dry enough for bagging and storage.
ga: yɛ hulu kpakpa shishi lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa heɔ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 dani egbiɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni egbi lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ onyanyɔji ni okɛbaatswa ŋmaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ehiɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni efoŋ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ awo kotoku mli ni akɛto.

english: Why should I dry my harvested crops on a plastic sheet instead of directly on bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mikpamɔ lɛ yɛ plastic woji anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Drying crops directly on soil exposes them to ground moisture, dirt, stones, and animal waste. Using a tarpaulin or drying sheet keeps the grains clean, raises their market value, and speeds up drying by keeping ground dampness away.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ, muji, tɛi, kɛ kooloi ashwiei amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tarp loo tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe tseɔ. eha jara nɔ jara aya hiɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi oya kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my harvested crop if I leave damp grains heaped together in a pile?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi ŋmaa ni mli efɔ yɛ ŋtayaa mli?

english: Leaving wet or freshly harvested crops in a large heap traps heat and moisture inside. This heat causes mold to grow rapidly, creates heat-damaged grains, and can even cause the seeds to start sprouting in the pile.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ loo ni akpa ehee yɛ ŋtayaai agboi amli lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa oya. Ehaa dumɔwui ni dɔlɛ efite lɛ feɔ ekoŋŋ. Ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ hu abɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli.

english: Why does my stored rice spoil or smell bad when I pack it into bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ fiteɔ loo eŋɔɔɔ kɛji akɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Rice spoils in storage bags when it is bagged before reaching the correct dryness. Trapped moisture inside airtight or woven bags encourages fungal growth and insects, which rot the grain from the inside out.
ga: Omɔ fiteɔ yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli kɛ́ awo kotoku mli dani eshɛ he ni egbi jogbaŋŋ. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ vacuum loo mama kotokui amli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii daraa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my rice grains break into small pieces when taken to the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ fãa bibii bibii kɛ akɛwo ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: Grains break during milling mainly because they were dried too rapidly under harsh midday heat or harvested when over-ripe. Drying rice gradually in moderate sun helps maintain grain strength during processing.
ga: Afoɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ. Nɔ titri ni haa enɛ baa ji bɔ ni egbiɔ oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni yɔɔ gbi lɛ mli lɛ shishi lɛ. aloo akpaa beni ekwɛ̃ tsɔ Omɔ ni agbiɔ fiofio Hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni omɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my rice plants turn yellow as the crop approaches maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni tso lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are a natural sign that the plant is finishing its growth cycle. It is redirection of energy—the plant pulls remaining nutrients from its leaves and sends them directly into the developing grains to make them full and heavy.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso ko miiba edalɛ be lɛ naagbee. Eji hewalɛ ni akɛtsɔɔ gbɛ kroko nɔ. Tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni ekɛmajeɔ dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni eha eyi obɔ kɛ muji.

english: Why do crops planted on one side of my field mature faster than crops on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ afã kroko lɛ?

english: Crops grow at different speeds across the same field due to variations in soil fertility, water retention, and shade. Areas with better soil nutrients and adequate moisture allow plants to develop and ripen faster.
ga: Tsei baakwɛ̃ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ahiɛɔ lɛ mli fɔmɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔlɔi srɔtoi lɛ ahewɔ lɛ Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ adara ni amɛdara oya.

english: How can I schedule my planting dates so I do not get overwhelmed during harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato gbi ni mikɛbaadu nii lɛ koni akawo mihe tsɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Staggering your planting over a few weeks divides your farm into manageable sections that mature at different times. This prevents your entire crop from ripening all at once, giving you enough time and physical energy to harvest and dry each section properly.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli lɛ baajara oŋmɔ lɛ mli awo fãi srɔtoi amli. ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ, ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli Enɛ baatsi oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ shikome. Enɛ haa onáa be kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛkpaa fã fɛɛ fã jogbaŋŋ ni okɛgbi.

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, a key nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni etsɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.
