english: How does planting cowpeas together with my main crops help improve my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen out of the air and puts it directly into the dirt. They act as a natural fertilizer supplier, leaving behind richer soil for crops planted alongside or after them.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔi. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni ashiɔ ahaa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ nɔ. loo no sɛɛ

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars feeding inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Hiɔ shi yɛ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds heavily on young maize leaves. Catching them early and applying approved insecticides or neem oil extracts helps protect the growing crop before the leaves are destroyed.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii babaoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ afite.

english: What causes the bottom end of my tomatoes to turn black and soft while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the fruit. It is usually caused by irregular watering during hot periods rather than an infectious disease.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Yɛ hela ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ najiaŋ

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for a long time, encouraging fungal decay. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop small, shriveled green pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Ani egboɔ dani edaa?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt, which occurs when the tree lacks enough water or nutrients to feed all its developing pods at once, or when sap-sucking insects like mirids attack the tree.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua eshishifãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ fɛɛ shikome. aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids lɛ tutua tsei.

english: Should I allow all the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem to stay?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃? Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he Ani mi plantain tso titri lɛ baahi nɔ?

english: No, letting too many suckers grow forces them to steal water and food from the main mother plant, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. Prune extra suckers away so only one or two healthy ones remain to replace the main stem after harvest.
ga: Dabi, ha ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃, ni enyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni baaye ŋmeii titri lɛ najiaŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to generate energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up into the light and keeps them off wet ground, where diseases spread easily.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo bulbs wuji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ la mli ni ehaaa tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Biɛ ji he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my pepper plants with dried grass help them grow?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te pepper tsei ni jwɛi ni egbi yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dried plant materials is called mulching. It keeps the blazing sun from drying out the soil, blocks weeds from taking over, and keeps the soil cool for the pepper roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsei ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi

english: Why don't seeds saved from my previous hybrid maize harvest produce as much food as newly bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ mi tsutsu ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mikɛwo mli lɛ mli lɛ wooo niyenii babaoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni ahe ehee lɛ?

english: Commercially produced hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yield in their first generation only. The seeds you collect from those harvested crops lose those special traits, leading to smaller yields if replanted.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee jarayeli nibii sɔrɔtoi lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni obua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ baafite nakai nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo fioo kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my carrots growing bent and twisted under the soil instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi karɔt lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Carrots need soft, loose soil to grow straight down. When carrot roots hit hard dirt, rocks, or heavy clay, they split or bend as they try to push through the ground.
ga: Karɔt he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji karɔt shishifãi lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni wa, tɛi, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ, karɔt shishifãi lɛ baafo loo amɛbaakoto beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend making soil ridges or mounds before planting root crops like carrots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii dani adu shishifãi tamɔ karɔt lɛ?

english: Building raised mounds loosens the topsoil so roots can easily swell and grow deep underground, while also helping excess rainwater drain away so the roots do not rot.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishifãi lɛ fũuɔ oya ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo.

english: Can carrot crops actually grow well in our warm weather here in Ghana?
ga: Ani karɔt tsei baanyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ wɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Yes, carrots can produce good harvests in Ghana if planted in loose, well-draining soil and given regular watering, especially during the cooler morning and evening periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, karɔt baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai yɛ Ghana kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. kɛ nu daa Titri lɛ yɛ leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: How deep down am I supposed to bury small seeds when I plant them in the ground?
ga: Esa akɛ mafu dumɔwui bibii lɛ. Te okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ohaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ oodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: A general rule is to plant seeds at a depth equal to two times their size; small seeds like carrots only need a tiny dusting of fine soil over them so they can push up easily when they germinate.
ga: Mla ni yɔɔ ji ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ yeɔ egbɔ. Dumɔwui bibii tamɔ karɔt lɛ he miihia ni akɛ sũ bibioo ko pɛ aha nɔ ni ŋã kpakpa yɔɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni anyɛ ashɛre amɛ kɛya ŋwɛi mlɛo kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are the green leaves on my crops turning pale and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or when too much standing water in the soil is suffocating the roots so they cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ miitao niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛna niyenii.

english: Why are my vegetable plants producing flowers very early when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛji bibii lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: When a crop gets stressed by intense heat or a lack of water, it rushes to produce flowers and seeds quickly to reproduce before it dries up and dies.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei hao lɛ, Ebaawo fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui oya koni ekɛfɔ dani egbi ni egbo.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables in the hot afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to soak up water before the hot afternoon sun evaporates it, giving your plants moisture to survive the heat of the day.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi maŋkpa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu dani etsɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli. Ha otsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli.

english: Do all vegetables need full heat from the sun all day to give a good yield?
ga: Ani hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni yeɔ emuu he miihia aduawai fɛɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: No, while crops like corn like full direct sun, tender crops and young seedlings can get scorched by intense sunlight and grow better with light shade during the hottest hours.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sumɔɔ ŋmãa sumɔɔ hulu ni eyi obɔ moŋ. Hulu la ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ dumɔwui bibii ahe. ni edaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops stay small and produce very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miifee bibioo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight from the soil that your main crops need to grow strong, leaving your crops weak and malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa onibii titri lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ hewalɛ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ hu bɛ.

english: How will I know that crops growing underground like carrots are ready for harvesting since I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso ko ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ karɔt lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ ejaakɛ minyɛɛɛ mana lɛ?

english: You can tell root crops are ready when the top ring of the root starts poking slightly above the soil surface, or by checking the age of the crop based on the recommended weeks after planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ efee klalo beni shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jeɔ shishi ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ afii ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye lɛ kwɛmɔ nɔ yɛ otsi ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural canopy that shields the young trees and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa tree usually take to start bearing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruits within 2 to 3 years under good care, while older traditional varieties may take 4 to 5 years to produce pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi. Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the soil is running low on vital nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is trapping air around the roots. Adding compost or proper fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nu mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my neighbor's crops to grow faster and bigger than mine on the same type of land?
ga: Mɛni haa mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe minɔ̃ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ kome nɔ?

english: Crops grow slowly when they have to compete with weeds for soil nutrients, or when plants are spaced too close together. Clearing weeds regularly and maintaining proper planting distance lets crops get full nourishment.
ga: Tsei lɛ daa blɛoo kɛ́ ehe bahia ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa kɛ dumɔ he ni sa ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: When crops lack water, their leaves droop during the hottest part of the day, turn yellow at the edges, or drop early. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass helps retain moisture.
ga: Beni tsei bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly humid conditions. Keeping the farm clear of weeds and removing infected pods stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, no haaa jwɛi lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: How do tiny bugs cause the leaves on my crops to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii aha baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ lɛ abɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpa shweremɔ?

english: Small sap-sucking insects like pests feed on young shoots and leaves, stealing the plant's food and injecting harmful fluids that cause leaves to curl and stunt plant growth.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ baai. juɔ tso niyenii ni ekɛ nu ni yɔɔ oshara woɔ mli Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa tso lɛ ada.

english: It is natural for cocoa trees to produce more flowers than pods, but heavy flower loss is often caused by severe dry weather, poor soil nutrition, or a lack of beneficial insects that pollinate the flowers.
ga: Eji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ akɛ cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe ŋmeii. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii wuji ni laajeɔ lɛ baa. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni bɛ

english: Cassava roots spread aggressively and suck up a lot of nutrients and water from the soil, which starves young cocoa trees. Plantains or cocoyams are safer companions for young cocoa.
ga: Cassava shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛmuɔ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ kookoo tsei bibii. Plantain loo kookoo ji nanemɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe kookoo ni mli jɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off branches from my cocoa trees when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo niji be mli ni tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach the inside of the tree. This helps prevent fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ejieɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce new flowers in November right after I finish harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ yɛ November mli beni mikpa amɛ pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally start a new flowering cycle around November to prepare for the minor harvest. Even after a major harvest, the tree naturally restarts its growth process as part of its annual cycle.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ November aaafee lɛ mli koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ bibioo ko. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kpeteŋkpele lɛ sɛɛ po Tso lɛ baaje dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ shishi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ e-afii sɛɛkuu lɛ fã.

english: Is it normal to see fresh buds coming out on my cocoa trees late in the year?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa akɛ mana ŋmeii heei yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee?

english: Yes, around November and December, healthy cocoa trees form fresh buds on their trunks and main branches, which marks the beginning of the next pod-producing phase.
ga: Hɛɛ, aaafee November kɛ December. Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ tsei heei yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji wuji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji pod feemɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ shishijee.

english: Why does my cocoa farm seem to start its fruiting process all over again every November?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi ekoŋŋ daa November lɛ?

english: Cocoa produces crops in overlapping cycles throughout the year. As the main harvest winds down around October and November, the tree automatically triggers new flowers to begin the mid-crop cycle.
ga: Akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ yɛ bei ni feɔ ekome mli yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Beni kpamɔ titri lɛ baa naagbee yɛ October kɛ November he lɛ. Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baawo fɔfɔi heei hewalɛ koni amɛje tsei lɛ ateŋ shweremɔ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees flower every year around November even when the weather turns dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi daa afi yɛ November beaŋ eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow internal timing and seasonal environmental cues late in the year, which naturally signal the tree to open its flower buds regardless of slight changes in rain.
ga: Cacao tsei nyiɛɔ amɛmli gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ be mli shihilɛ sɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi ekɔɔɔ tsakemɔi fioo ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ he.

english: Should I cut off the new flowers that appear on my cocoa trees in November?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ fɔfɔi heei ni jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ November mli lɛ?

english: No, you should leave those flowers untouched. Those November flowers will grow into the young pods that give you your minor cocoa harvest later in the year.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ oshi nakai fɔfɔi lɛ ni okataa he. Nɛkɛ November fɔfɔi nɛɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni baaha oná kookoo bibioo ko yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: How do I avoid damaging new buds when picking ripe pods late in the harvest season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmeii heei ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe beni mikpaa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Harvest mature pods carefully using a sharp hook or cutlass without scraping the trunk bark, because new November flowers grow directly on the flower cushions where old pods were attached.
ga: Kpaa pods ni eda lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ hoo loo dagger ni naa wa nɔ ni okɛ tso lɛ yibii akafolɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi heei ni jeɔ kpo yɛ November mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akutso lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii momo lɛ ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ.

english: Is it harmful to the cocoa tree if it starts budding immediately after I pick all the main pods?
ga: Ani ebaaye cacao tso lɛ awui kɛji akɛ ebɔi shweremɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa ŋmeii titrii lɛ fɛɛ?

english: It is not harmful at all. Cocoa trees are naturally built to bud and flower continuously as long as they are healthy and have enough nutrients in the soil.
ga: Ebɛ oshara kwraa. Abɔ cacao tsei yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛya nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi be fɛɛ be ni cacao tso lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Does seeing new flowers on my cocoa trees in November mean I will harvest again soon?
ga: Ni minaa fɔfɔi heei yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ November mli lɛ, ani no tsɔɔ akɛ etsɛŋ ni makpa ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, flowers that appear in November will take about five to six months to mature into harvestable pods, giving you pods for the mid-year crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, fɔfɔi ni jeɔ kpo yɛ November mli lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa. Enɛ haa onáa pods kɛha afi teŋ dumɔ.

english: What kind of care should I give my cocoa farm when new buds show up in November?
ga: Te esa akɛ makwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ tɛŋŋ beni eyɛ ŋmeii heei yɛ November mli lɛ?

english: Clear surrounding weeds, manage shade levels to let in adequate light, and ensure good soil nutrients so the tree has enough energy to feed the new November buds into full pods.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni shade lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ koni ona la ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni okwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni niyenii kpakpai ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji koni eha tso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛha ŋmeii heei lɛ niyenii yɛ November mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why are some cocoa trees flowering in November while others on the same farm are not?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ November mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni jeee kookoo tsei fɛɛ fɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Different cocoa trees flower at slightly different rates based on their age, health, individual shade exposure, and how much energy they used up during the previous harvest.
ga: Cacao tso fɛɛ tso baawo fɔfɔi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo nɔ, ni enɛ damɔ tso lɛ afii, hewalɛnamɔ, kɛ hulutsoo nɔ. kɛ hewalɛ ni cacao tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and build leaves, or when too much water around the roots prevents them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛfee baai. aloo be mli ni nu ebɔle Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer right against the stems of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against tender plant stems can burn the plant's skin and roots. Fertilizer should be placed a short distance away so the expanding roots can absorb it safely without getting damaged.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni ekɛ nɔ ko akafite.

english: Why do my crops look weak and produce smaller yields when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Because no single plant gets enough, they all remain small and produce fewer fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ejaakɛ tso kome po pɛ baafee nɔ ni fa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei fɛɛ daraaa ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves, drink the plant's juices, and transmit plant diseases that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. enuɔ tsei amli nu ni ekɛ tsei ahe helai ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves with sawdust-like dirt inside the growing tops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ he ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center of young maize plants during the day to feed on the tender new leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked in water for too long, creating conditions for harmful soil fungi to attack and decay the underground tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua amɛ ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agboi lɛ baa.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from long dry spells, attacks by mirid pests, or a lack of tiny insects called midges that are needed to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ he. Naakpɛɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midge, ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔmɔ nii lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and rotten while still hanging on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, usually because watering has been irregular.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun but recover completely by early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ená hewalɛ kwraa leebi?

english: Under intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. Overnight, when temperatures cool down, the roots catch up and replenish the plant's water balance.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Shishifãi baaje kpo ni amɛbaawo tso lɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during rains even when the wind is not very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa tsɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by underground pests like nematodes or stem borers. When these root systems are damaged, the heavy top weight causes the plant to fall easily in wet soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers baanyɛ afite. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fite lɛ Nɔ ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baaha tso lɛ akumɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ oya.

english: How long does it usually take for my young crop to mature and start producing properly?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Many long-term crops take around three years to mature fully. During this initial growth period, the plant focuses its energy on developing strong roots and stems before producing full yields.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii etɛ dani eshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Yɛ nɛkɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ fã nɛɛ mli lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛ hewalɛ maa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Is it normal for my plants to take a few years before giving a good yield?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mitsei lɛ baahe afii babaoo dani amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Yes, it is completely normal. Crops need time to establish themselves in the soil, build strong branches, and reach maturity before they can consistently yield high-quality fruit or seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kwraa. Be he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛma shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔɔ niji ni mli wa ni amɛdara dani amɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are my young crops not producing any seeds for me to harvest yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ wooo dumɔwui ko ni mikɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Young plants spend their early years building strength and foliage. They must reach full maturity, which often takes up to three years, before they are strong enough to form healthy seeds.
ga: Tsei bibii yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Bɔni afee ni afee hewalɛ kɛ baai Esa akɛ amɛdara, ni bei pii lɛ amɛheɔ afii etɛ, dani amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni mli wa.

english: Where can I get good seeds or seedlings to plant on my farm?
ga: Matao dumɔwui loo dumɔwui kpakpai komɛi. Nɛgbɛ manyɛ makwɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can get planting material by saving seeds from your own healthy, mature harvest, buying certified seeds from sellers in the local market, or getting seedlings from commercial nurseries.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona nibii ni akɛduɔ nii kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni oookɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Hemɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelɔi adɛŋ. Aloo ná dumɔwui kɛjɛ jarayeli dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko.

english: Can I just collect seeds from my current harvest to plant for the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, once your crops reach full maturity and produce healthy yields, you can select the best seeds from your own harvest and keep them to replant for the next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai lɛ. Obaanyɛ ohala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli ni okɛto koni okɛdu ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to buy planting seeds from sellers in the market?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahe dumɔwui kɛjɛ jarayelɔi adɛŋ?

english: Buying market seeds is common, but you must ensure you purchase from reputable vendors who sell healthy, undamaged seeds that are suitable for planting in your area.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi ehe miihia ni okwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ohé kɛjɛ nihɔɔlɔ ko ni ehe gbɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni efiteee ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ dɛŋ.

english: Should I buy new seeds from the market or just replant seeds from my own farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ jara nɔ loo madu dumɔwui kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli ekoŋŋ?

english: Using your own seeds saves money if your crops are strong and healthy, but buying certified seeds from the market can sometimes give you improved varieties that yield better or resist pests.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ odumɔwui tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha okɛ shika akafite kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa. Shi bei komɛi lɛ, kɛ́ ohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase yɛ jara nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha oná dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii kpakpai loo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: How do I know which of my harvested crops are best to take seeds from for replanting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli?

english: Wait until your crop has reached full maturity and select seeds from the healthiest, highest-yielding plants that showed no signs of disease during the season.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi oŋmɔshi nii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ohala dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni hela he okadi ko bɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do some farmers choose to use their own saved seeds instead of buying from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi halaa akɛ amɛkɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛdumɔwui ni amɛto lɛ baatsu nii moŋ fe ni amɛbaahe kɛjɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Replanting seeds from your own farm saves money on buying input materials, and it allows you to reuse seeds from plants that have already proven they can grow well in your farm's soil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ooodu kɛjɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha okɛ shika akafite yɛ nibii ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ ahemɔ mli. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni ena akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the benefit of starting my farm with seedlings instead of direct seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shishi kɛ dumɔwui moŋ fe dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Starting with seedlings gives your young plants a head start in a protected environment, ensuring they are strong and mature enough to survive harsh field conditions when transplanted.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui je shishi lɛ, ehaa otsei bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wa lɛ amli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ.

english: When is the main cocoa harvest season in Ghana, and why does it start around September or October?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji kookoo kpamɔ be titri yɛ Ghana? Ni mɛni hewɔ ejeɔ shishi yɛ September loo October aaafee lɛ?

english: Ghana's main cocoa harvest runs from October to February because the heavy rains stop, giving way to sunny weather that allows pods to mature fully and beans to be dried under the sun without rotting.
ga: Ghana kookoo ŋmaa titri jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ Alemle kɛyashi Oflɔŋ. Ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kpa. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli atse Ha pods lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ. kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni egbooo

english: Is cocoa harvested only once a year in Ghana, or can I harvest pods at other times too?
ga: Ghana kpaa lɛ shikome pɛ yɛ afi mli. Aloo manyɛ makpa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ be kroko mli?

english: Cocoa has two harvest periods each year in Ghana: the main crop season from October to February (which gives the largest yields) and a smaller mid-crop season from May to September.
ga: Cocoa yɛ kpamɔ bei enyɔ yɛ afi mli yɛ Ghana: be titri ni ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ October kɛyashi February. (ni ji nɔ ni woɔ yibii fe fɛɛ) kɛ be bibioo, ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni daa kɛjɛ May kɛyashi September.

english: How does the government decide when cocoa buying season officially opens for farmers?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ ekpɛ eyiŋ yɛ be mli ni abaagbele kookoo hemɔ be lɛ naa aha okwaafoi lɛ?

english: The Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) monitors weather patterns and crop maturity across regions to announce official opening dates so all farmers get a fair fixed price and buyers collect quality beans.
ga: Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) lɛ kwɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ lɛ anɔ. Koni atswa gbi ni akɛgbeleɔ nitsumɔ lɛ naa lɛ he adafi Koni akwɛ koni okwaafoi fɛɛ ana jara ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni ja ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ ana kɔfi ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and care for my farm in January if harvesting only happens late in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ January mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ kpamɔ lɛ ba yɛ afi lɛ naagbee pɛ

english: Cocoa trees need year-round care because early-year work like pruning and weeding removes pests, conserves soil moisture, and prepares the tree to produce strong flowers during the rainy season.
ga: Cocoa tsei biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Nɔ ni ha ebalɛ nakai ji nitsumɔi ni atsuɔ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli tamɔ tsei akwɛmɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ hewɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie kooloi bibii ni woɔ mɔ mii la lɛ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni osaa tsei lɛ ahe kɛha fɔfɔi ni mli wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Will pruning and cutting off branches from my cocoa trees harm my harvest?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei aniji ni afoɔ ni afoɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Proper pruning actually increases your yield because removing dead or overcrowded branches lets sunlight and air reach the main trunk, which encourages more flowers and pods to grow.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season affect my growing cocoa trees?
ga: Te harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ saa mi-kokoo tsei ni miida lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Harmattan winds dry out the air and soil, causing young cocoa trees to lose water quickly and shed leaves; providing shade trees and mulching helps protect them from dying.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shading kɛ mulching buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ gbele he.

english: Trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress, lack of nutrients, or poor pollination by tiny insects called midges, which need shade and moist leaf litter to survive.
ga: Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji nu mli haomɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛ baai ni mli efɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How many years after planting will a new cocoa tree start giving me pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu cacao tso hee lɛ, ebaaje shishi eha mi ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties take 4 to 5 years to fruit, but modern hybrid seeds provided by extension services can start producing cocoa pods in just 2 to 3 years.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi amli kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani ewoɔ yibii, shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni extension service lɛ kɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ aje kookoo ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli.

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod is completely ripe and ready for picking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: A ripe pod turns from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange-yellow, and makes a hollow sound when you tap it because the seeds inside have detached from the outer shell.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. loo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ-ɔranji nɔ. Ni efeɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ otswa lɛ ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ he.

english: Why can't I sell my cocoa beans to buyers right after I harvest the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ maha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa beans must undergo fermentation under plantain leaves for about 6 days and then be sun-dried to develop the true chocolate flavor and prevent mold during storage.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afee cocoa ŋmeii heei lɛ awo plantain baai ashishi aaafee gbii 6, ni no sɛɛ lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛná amɛ tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ. ni otsi ŋmɔtɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the nutrient that helps plants build green leaves and grow big. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed nutrients out of the topsoil or if the soil is soaked with too much standing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nu ni ekã shi.

english: Is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas or beans together on the same farm with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans or cowpeas with maize is very good for your soil. Legumes like beans can pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which helps feed the maize plants naturally and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ agbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ yeɔ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving green-brown dirt in the middle of the plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves (the whorl) of the maize plant during the day and eat the young leaves, leaving behind droppings that look like saw-dust. You need to apply recommended neem extracts or insecticides early in the morning or late evening when they feed.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai (rings) lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni amɛshiɔ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa. Esa akɛ okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ atsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotten before they even get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often because the water supply is uneven—such as alternating between very dry soil and sudden heavy watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa trukaa lɛ ni tsakeɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Should I plant my crops immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rainy season has fully established. The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which can scorch and dry out young seeds or shoots that have just sprouted in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baagbe naa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã ni egbi dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ehee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not carry it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours. It is best to place fertilizer slightly into the soil near the crop's root area and cover it with a little soil so rain does not wash it off the surface.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo baafata sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ kɛjɛ nɔ.

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and make food for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can get maximum sunlight and avoid rotting or catching diseases from wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli fitemɔ loo helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees dropping their flowers before any cocoa pods start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani cacao ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are under stress, such as during dry spells when there is not enough moisture in the soil, or if pests like mirids are attacking the tree. Ensuring good shade and soil moisture helps the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛmiihao, tamɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋulamiiaŋ sũ lɛ tutua tso lɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ hiɛ hulutsoo kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves starting to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem may begin to crack as the expanding tubers push up from underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaayɔse akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I cut them down with my cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds with a cutlass leaves the roots intact under the ground, and it exposes hidden weed seeds in the soil to sunlight and moisture, which causes them to germinate almost immediately. Covering the bare ground with crop residues or mulch helps slow them down.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei jieɔ jwɛi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. ni ehaa hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa jwɛi dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ aaafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shweremɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why did my crop yield a full harvest during the major rainy season, but fail during the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli lɛ? Shi eyeee omanye yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli?

english: In regions like Ashanti, the major rainy season brings steady and prolonged rainfall, whereas the minor season is shorter and more unpredictable. Crops planted in the minor season often experience dry spells, which prevent proper flowering and fruit development unless supplemented with irrigation.
ga: Yɛ kpokpai tamɔ Ashanti lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, be ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ kuku ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni esaaa baa. ja nu kroko ni akɛfataa he yɛ

english: How do I know when the soil has enough moisture for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil from your farm into a ball. If it holds its shape without dripping excess water and crumbles easily when squeezed gently, the soil has the right moisture balance for seed germination.
ga: Nyɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ko ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu ni fa fe nine shwieee shi ni efoɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ blɛoo lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm take several years after planting before I see any pods?
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani anaa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Perennial crops like cocoa focus their early years on establishing deep root systems and developing strong stems. Pod production only begins when the tree reaches structural maturity and can safely support heavy fruit loads.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ. Pod feemɔ jeɔ shishi beni tso lɛ eda kwraa ni ebaanyɛ eye ebua aduawai babaoo shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the leaves on my young crop seedlings burn and dry up during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow root systems and thin leaf surfaces that lose water rapidly under intense sunlight. Providing temporary natural shade, such as intercropping with fast-growing foliage crops, protects tender leaves from heat stress.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni nu lɛ laajeɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei ni baa tsei ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: If I plant my maize seeds close together, will I get a larger harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in weak stalks and smaller, lower-quality yields rather than more food.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baa shi ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi yɛ niyenii babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb fertilizer and water faster than cultivated crops. They also block sunlight, effectively starving your main crops of the essentials needed for steady growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Etsĩɔ hulu lɛ hu naa. Enɛ haa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ náaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crop turning light yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of older, lower leaves usually signals a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newest upper leaves to keep growing, causing the older leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni edako ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Ehaa baai momoi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow well in one part of my field but remain small and yellow in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi eji bibioo lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fã kroko mli?

english: Soil quality varies across the same piece of land due to differences in drainage, shade, or nutrient levels. Soil in lower or eroded areas may lack nutrients or hold too much water, causing uneven crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ jɛɔ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ nu ni hoɔ, hulutsoo loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi loo hei ni efite lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli loo ehiɛ nu babaoo mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for one high-yielding generation. Planting seeds harvested from that crop results in offspring that lose their strength, leading to uneven growth and significantly lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa seshibii lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi waa.

english: Why do my harvested cassava tubers start spoiling within just a few days of digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots are cut from the living plant, rapid cell breakdown begins as air enters the exposed tissue. Processing or consuming cassava shortly after harvest prevents this natural spoilage.
ga: Beni afoɔ ŋmei shishifãi kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka mli. Cell lysis ni yaa oya lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ bote fãji ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ amli. Cassava ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ayeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ tsiɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: How deep should I bury my coconut seedling when I plant it in the farm?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, te esa akɛ afu ŋmei tsei lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: You should not push coconut seedlings too deep into the soil. Plant it so the base of the shoot stays near the surface level; burying it too deep suffocates the plant, causes rot, and slows down its initial growth.
ga: Esaaa akɛ ashɛɔ ŋmei tso lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ. Dumɔ ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. kɛ fitemɔ baa ni ehaa dalɛ baa shi yɛ shishijee mli

english: What happens if I push my crop cuttings or seedlings too deep into the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ tso ni afo loo dumɔwu ko wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ?

english: When seedlings or cuttings are planted too deep, their shoots struggle to reach sunlight and may rot in excessive wet soil before they can establish healthy green leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná hulu la ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine nɔ dani amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die right after I pull them up and replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni migbala amɛ ni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seedlings are pulled out roughly, their small feeding roots snap. This root damage prevents the seedling from taking up water, causing it to suffer severe transplant shock and die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii ni yeɔ E-nibii lɛ baakumɔ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ nɛɛ haaa dumɔwu lɛ aná nu. Enɛ kɛ graft piŋmɔ ni naa wa kɛ gbele baa.

english: How can I tell if a seedling root is healthy enough to be planted in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy seedling roots are firm and light-colored. If the roots are soft, black, or snap off too easily when handled, they are damaged or diseased and will struggle to survive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ ediŋŋ, loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya tsɔ kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ efite loo hela emɔ amɛ. ni esa akɛ ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehi shi

english: What is the best time of day for me to move my young crops from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaajie ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔ mli?

english: It is best to transplant in the cool late afternoon or on a cloudy day so the strong sun does not dry out and stress the fresh seedlings before their roots settle.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsake yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ akagbi ni ekɛ haomɔ aba dumɔwui heei anɔ dani shishifãi lɛ atswa.

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stems and small yields.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava cuttings when I insert them into the earth?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni atsɔɔ yucca niji lɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ akɛmiifata shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to curve around to find light, wasting energy and reducing yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛna la. Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa nitsumɔ baa shi.

english: Why are my tree crops taking so long to sprout new leaves after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ baai heei beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If a tree seedling is buried improperly—such as covering the growing point with dirt—the plant spends all its energy trying to break through the soil rather than growing new leaves and roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu tso dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kɛtsɔ sũ ni akɛhaa he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni ebaakwɛ baai kɛ shishifãi heei.

english: Why does the soil around my newly planted crops dry out so quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei ni midu ehee lɛ he lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture fast under direct sunlight. Covering the base of your plants with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the root zone shaded, cool, and moist.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) ha otso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ hulutsoo, ehaa edɔɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, which the plant needs to build strong green leaves and produce good ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa aba ni ekɛ toi kpakpai aba.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving some forest trees protects young cocoa until it is mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow before the corn is even ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ po feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to stay healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea when the crops are young keeps the leaves green and helps form big corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii tso titri ni he hiaa kɛha hewalɛnamɔ kpakpa Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ baaha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eye ebua ni efee ŋmãa ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped in the soil, preventing air from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows rainwater to drain off so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: How do I know the right time to put my seeds into the ground when the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets a deep soak from two or three heavy rains, rather than planting right after the first light drizzle. This ensures there is enough moisture stored in the ground for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ hewɔ. Mohu ɔ, duɔ amlɔ nɔuu ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se. Enɛ haa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: What causes small worms to eat holes in the leaves inside the whorl of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ni ayeɔ bu yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ a-rings lɛ amli lɛ mli?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hatch from eggs laid by moths on young corn. Checking your field early and spraying neem extract or recommended insecticides into the center of the plants stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: No, crowding plants causes them to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with small yields. Giving crops correct spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to grow large.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni fa babaoo lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ he ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaadara.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without growing into fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry up before they can be fertilized and set fruit. Watering your plants at the base and covering the soil around them with dry grass helps keep the roots cool and prevents flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛwoɔ fɔmɔ nii ni amɛwoɔ aduawai. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli yɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Having too many shoots causes them to steal food and water from the main mother plant, making the plantain bunch small. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems to produce healthy, heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo baaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ha plantains akuu lɛ afee bibioo. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii 1 loo 2 pɛ ahi shi kɛha ŋmeii ni wa ni tsii.

english: How do weeds in my field hurt the growth of my main crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ adalɛ he yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and take away vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that your main plants need. Clearing weeds during the first few weeks after planting lets your crop grow strong without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛheɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ he hiaa lɛ. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ ada waa ni akaŋshii ko bɛ he.

english: Why is it bad to put chemical fertilizer on dry soil when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need moisture to dissolve into a form that roots can absorb. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn the plant roots and cause the fertilizer to waste away into the air without helping the crop.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are some rice farmers in Ghana harvesting much more grain now than they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miikpa omɔ babaoo fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Farmers are harvesting more rice now because many have switched to improved seed varieties, proper fertilizer application, and better field water management techniques rather than relying on outdated farming practices.
ga: Okwaafoi miikpa ŋmãa babaoo bianɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi babaoo miitsake kɛmiiya dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nu mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔ mli nu he ŋaai ni hi jogbaŋŋ Yɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni etsɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young crop plants turn yellow and stop growing early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the ground is improperly watered. Adding the right fertilizer and managing field moisture helps the plants grow green and strong again.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does rice grow so much better in lowland swampy areas than on dry hillside farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ fe ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ gɔŋji ni nɔ egbi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Rice naturally requires a lot of water to absorb nutrients properly. Lowland valleys hold rainwater and moisture naturally, which gives rice roots the constant water supply they need to thrive.
ga: Omɔ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, nu babaoo he miihia lɛ koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. Jɔɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ toɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do crops dry up and fail even when it rains once every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii gĩɔ ni amɛfiteɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ shikome yɛ otsi mli moŋ lɛ?

english: If soil lacks organic matter or proper earth bunds to trap moisture, rainwater runs off or evaporates in the hot sun quickly before plant roots have enough time to drink it.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ loo etsɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli oya dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know if the seed rice I buy from the local market will give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai?

english: Grains bought from the food market are meant for eating and often sprout unevenly. Certified seeds from registered agricultural dealers are specifically tested to sprout reliably, resist local diseases, and yield more harvest.
ga: Akɛ ŋmaa ni aheɔ yɛ niyenii ajarayelihei lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛye ni bei pii lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ akwɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ babaoo

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop seedlings right after I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to jump up and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before young crop seedlings can establish deep roots, which is why early weeding is critical.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni sa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛtu kɛya ŋwɛi ni amɛju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani dumɔwui bibii lɛ anyɛ atswa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Why do my harvested rice grains break into tiny pieces when they go through the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli fãi bibii lɛ? Beni oootsɔ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice grains crack and break during milling if they are harvested too late after drying out on the stalk, or if they are dried too fast under harsh midday sun instead of slow drying in the shade.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa baagbala ni ebaakumɔ yɛ be mli ni akpaa lɛ kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ beni egbi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ gbi lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeegbi fiofio yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How do I tell the exact right time to harvest my rice field so I don't lose my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ, ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni laajeɔ lɛ bɛ?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the plant head turn a golden yellow color, while the stem underneath still retains a slight green shade.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo lolo lɛ.

english: Why does locally produced rice sometimes have a different smell or taste compared to imported rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmãa ni afeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmãa ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ he lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested local rice retains its natural flavor and aroma, whereas imported rice may sit in shipping containers and warehouses for years before reaching store shelves.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli omɔ ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ebɔɔ su kɛ eŋɔli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, omɔ ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ baanyɛ ahi tsɔnei ni akɛmajeɔ kɛ nitoohei amli afii babaoo dani eshɛ shwapoi amli.

english: Will market women and local buyers actually buy my locally grown rice over foreign imported rice?
ga: Ani jarayeli yei kɛ maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ heɔ mi maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ moŋ fe ŋmãa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ?

english: Yes, local buyers increasingly prefer locally grown Ghana rice because modern milling leaves it clean, stone-free, and much fresher than foreign rice that has travelled long distances.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ Ghana omɔ ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ fe tsutsu lɛ. Yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa ni akɛshãa ŋmãa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli tse, tɛ bɛ mli, ni eyɛ ehee fe ŋmãa ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ni efã gbɛ kɛtee shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the topsoil. Leaving a few large trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa creates a shade canopy that protects the young seedlings until they are strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei fioo komɛi ni eda loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize stem usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize uses to make leaves green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting leguminous crops like cowpeas before planting maize restores this essential nutrient.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛha ebaai lɛ afee eŋɔli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmãa dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests to live and multiply in the dirt. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans helps fix food back into the soil and breaks the cycle of crop diseases.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekpaa tsei ahe helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ.

english: How should I stick my cassava stem cuttings into the ground so I get large tubers?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ odu ŋmei ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni onine ashɛ ŋmei wuji anɔ?

english: Cassava stems should be planted slanting at an angle or horizontally covered with soil, with the growing buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them right side up encourages strong root development where the large cassava tubers grow.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ loo awo nɔ mulch yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. ni ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa ŋwɛi Dumɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa shishifãi ni mli wa yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmei shishifãi wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central fold of the maize plant to eat soft young leaves. Catching them early and applying recommended pesticides or neem oil sprays late in the evening helps kill the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking pests like whiteflies or aphids spreading a plant virus. Controlling these small insects with soaps or recommended insecticides keeps the leaves flat so the plant can grow and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ye nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ada ni ewo yibii.

english: When too many young shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal water, soil food, and sunlight from the main stem. Leaving only two or three strong shoots ensures the main plant grows big and produces heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Plantain kome pɛ baaju nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to manufacture energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground where they can catch maximum sunlight and protects the leaves from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni ebuɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients. Giving your plants steady moisture at the root level and mulching the soil keeps the plant calm so flowers can develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni akɛ nu haa tsei lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfeɔ kpoo. Kɛkɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ tomato.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the hot afternoon or in the cool morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso loo leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso?

english: Watering in the cool early morning is best because the plant roots can soak up moisture before the hot sun evaporates it. Afternoon watering can shock hot plants and create damp conditions that cause fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani enyɛ etsɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ he akpokpo ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba lɛ aba.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons as a natural defense mechanism to reduce their surface area, trapping moisture and preventing water from evaporating too fast during heat stress.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi, ni ekɛtsiɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal organism that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions. Damp leaves and cool rain help the spores spread rapidly from pod to pod.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo fe nine. Baai ni mli efɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni mli ejɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa pod kroko mli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young cassava plants when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei bibii amli lɛ?

english: Young cassava stems grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for essential soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, which stunts their early root development.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ nu. Enɛ baatsi eshishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Plantains should be planted about 3 meters apart so that their massive leaves have enough room to capture sunlight without shading neighboring plants or competing for soil moisture.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantains aaafee mitai 3 kɛjɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni baai wuji lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni amɛtsĩii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anaa loo amɛkashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new green growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yaa ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience temperature stress, prolonged dry spells, or irregular watering, which prevents proper pollination.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo hulutsoo be mli haomɔ mli. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce plenty of flowers but fail to form heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi ewooo aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ?

english: Oil palm fruit formation requires successful transfer of pollen from male to female flowers, which depends heavily on tiny pollinating insects or wind; without them, flowers wither without producing fruit.
ga: Mu tso yibii lɛ afeemɔ biɔ ni ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei amli. Enɛ damɔ kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmeii anɔ. Kɛ́ amɛbɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why do my tomatoes get a dark, flattened rotten patch on the bottom end of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when water supply to the plant is uneven during fruit growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ lɛ ejaaa yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell underground cassava roots are fully grown and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves dry out and shed, the main stems turn woody, and visible cracks appear in the soil near the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ dalɛ he kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso. ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines dry up and turn brown at the end of the rainy season?
