ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally die back when the plant finishes its lifecycle, shifting all its remaining energy into storing nutrients within the underground tuber before going dormant.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ gbe ewala shihilɛ naa. Amɛbaatsake hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛbaafite.

english: What should I do if I find tiny clusters of eggs on the underside of my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina ŋmeii bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ tso baai lɛ ashishi?

english: Those eggs are laid by insects that will hatch into hungry caterpillars or bugs. You should crush them by hand or remove the infected leaf and destroy it so the pests never get the chance to hatch and eat your crop.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii ni baatsɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ woɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ oniji atswa lɛ loo ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkaná hegbɛ ni amɛfɔ ni amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How long does it take for insect eggs laid on my plants to hatch into harmful pests?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kooloi bibii ni akɛwoɔ mi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ afɔ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ oshara?

english: Depending on the type of insect and the temperature, eggs can hatch anywhere from a few days to several weeks. Checking your field regularly helps you spot and destroy eggs before they turn into damaging pests.
ga: Wɔɔji baanyɛ afɔ kɛjɛ gbii fioo kɛyashi otsii babaoo. Edamɔ kooloo lɛ henɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona ŋmeii ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ dani amɛbatsɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni fiteɔ nii.

english: Why do pest numbers increase so quickly on my farm in just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ etee hiɛ oya yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: A single insect can lay dozens or hundreds of eggs at once. When those eggs hatch around the same time, a small problem of just a few bugs quickly turns into hundreds of pests feeding on your crops.
ga: Kooloo kome baanyɛ awo wuji nyɔŋmai abɔ loo ohai abɔ shikome. Kɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ, naagba bibioo ko ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii fioo komɛi pɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ oya kɛfeɔ kooloi ohai abɔ ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do insects prefer laying their eggs on young crops instead of mature ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ moŋ fe tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Young crop plants are soft, tender, and easy for newly hatched insects to chew and digest, giving the young pests the best chance to survive.
ga: Tsofai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe jɔ, ni ewaaa akɛ koolooi ni efɔ ehee lɛ baaye ni amɛye. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii Naa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi

english: Why is it important to pick insect eggs off my crops and throw them far away from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anaa ni mashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie he ko ni kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ?

english: If you simply knock eggs off onto the soil near your crops, many can still hatch and crawl right back onto your plants. Throwing them far away or burning them ensures they are completely destroyed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otswa ŋmeii lɛ oshwie shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ. Akpɔlɔi babaoo baanyɛ afɔ lolo ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba otsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie loo ashã amɛ lɛ, ebaaha akpata amɛhiɛ kwraa.

english: Can I remove pest eggs from my crops without spending money on chemical sprays?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋmeii kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, manual hand-picking, crushing egg clusters, or washing leaves with a simple soapy water mixture are effective, low-cost ways to control pests before they hatch.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni akɛ niji buaa naa Akpɔlɔi babaoo ni atswaa loo baai ni akɛ nu ni mli ewo saamɔ folo tsuɔ he nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni shika helɛtemɔ he ehiaaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfɔɔ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check for pest eggs or plant damage?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsei efite?

english: It is best to inspect your farm at least twice a week. Early detection allows you to remove egg clusters before they hatch and spread across the entire field.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. mra ni anaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ ŋmeii akui kɛjɛɔ mli dani amɛfɔɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why should my neighboring farmers and I clear insect eggs from our fields at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi kɛ okwaafonyo ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ abua kooloi awuii anaa yɛ wɔŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Insects fly easily between fields. If you clean your farm but your neighbor does not, the pests that hatch next door will eventually migrate straight into your healthy crops.
ga: Kplukai fãa yɛ ŋmɔji ateŋ oya. Kɛji otsumɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okutsoŋbii lɛ etsuuu he lɛ, yɛ naagbee lɛ, kooloi ni fɔ̃ɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baafã kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can an extension officer help me when I notice strange eggs or bugs on my farm?
ga: Te extension nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mina ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ? Yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extension officers can help you identify the specific type of insect, tell you how dangerous it is, and teach you the safest, cheapest ways to protect your crops.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oyoo kooloo lɛ henɔ. Kɛɛmɔ bo bɔ ni eyɔɔ oshara ha. ni etsɔɔ bo gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni jara waaa fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ obu onibii ahe.

english: What should our farming community do if we notice a widespread pest outbreak across our area?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ wɔ okwaayeli akutso lɛ afee kɛji wɔyɔse akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa wɔ akutso lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: You should immediately inform your local agricultural extension officer and organize community farm clean-ups so everyone can control the pests together before they destroy the whole harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ oha okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ ale amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni ato akutso lɛ mli ŋmɔ mli saamɔ he gbɛjianɔ koni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ afee ekome kɛye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce heavy fruit bunches during the wet season but stop producing much in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli shi ekpaa yibii babaoo womɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees need a massive amount of water to develop fruits. During the rainy season, the abundant water allows the tree to form and fill large fruit bunches, while dry weather forces the tree to conserve water and delay flower and fruit development.
ga: Mu tsei biɔ nu babaoo dani amɛyibii lɛ aya hiɛ. Yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, nu babaoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai akui wuji ni amɛyiɔ amɛmli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhaa fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants blossom above the ground when the nuts themselves grow inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ miikwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated in the open air, they produce long stems called pegs. These pegs naturally bend downwards and push themselves into the soil, where the actual pods form and mature in the dark.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli sɛɛ lɛ, tso kakadaŋŋ ni atsɛɔ lɛ pin lɛ baafee. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baakoto amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni pods diɛŋtsɛ lɛ feɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ duŋ mli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize is short on nitrogen, an important food for growth. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves nutrients from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen lɛ Tsei tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites feeding on leaf sap, or by viruses they spread. Damaged leaves cannot convert sunlight into energy properly, which starves the developing pepper fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni yeɔ baa mli nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsake hulu la lɛ amɛfee hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye pepper aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do my soybean plants grow tall with bright green leaves but end up with empty pods without seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tso lɛ daa kɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ shi egbeɔ naa kɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Empty pods often occur when plants lack sufficient phosphorus in the soil or experience water stress and extreme heat during the flowering stage, preventing the seeds inside from filling out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo ni enaa haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyimɔɔɔ obɔ.

english: Why do so many flowers on my cocoa trees fall to the ground without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of blossoms, but only flowers pollinated by tiny insects called midges will turn into pods. The tree naturally sheds unpollinated flowers so it can direct its energy into growing the pods that did set.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi pɛ yɔɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ tsɔɔ pod pɛ. Tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akudɔ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom tips of my tomato fruits turn black and rotten before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ he ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when rainfall or watering is irregular, making it difficult for the plant roots to draw up calcium evenly from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso yibii ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ loo nu hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots inside the barn even when kept dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto he ni amɛgbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living storehouses that naturally go into a short resting stage after harvest. Once that dormancy period ends, the tuber automatically uses its internal water and energy reserves to grow shoots for the next season, even without soil.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji nitoohei ni hiɛ ka ni boteɔ wɔɔhe be kuku mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. kpamɔ sɛɛ Beni wɔɔhe be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Bulb lɛ kɛ emli nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ko bɛ po

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil and turn dark inside within just two days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ duŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once cassava is harvested, cutting it off from the living plant triggers a natural chemical reaction to air and moisture loss. This causes rapid breakdown and discoloration of the flesh within 48 to 72 hours.
ga: Beni akpaa ŋmei Tso ni hiɛ ka lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa loo lɛ fãa oya ni etsakeɔ ehiɛ su yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli.

english: Why do small extra shoots grow around the base of my main plantain stem, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: Those extra shoots are called suckers, and they compete directly with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing most of them and leaving just one or two strong ones ensures the main stem gets enough food to produce a large plantain bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Ni amɛkɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee plantains akuu agbo ko.

english: Yellow lower leaves are usually a cry for nitrogen, a key nutrient plant food. When the soil doesn't have enough nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has to new top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ biɔ nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni ji niyenii titri ni haa mɔ he waa Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do groundnuts make my soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have special roots that grab natural plant food (nitrogen) from the air and put it into the ground. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpaa lɛ Niyenii ni ekã lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stick stems at an angle instead of straight down into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree angle helps the roots spread out wide near the top layer of rich soil, which gives you bigger, thicker tubers than planting them straight down.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji 45-degree lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha oná bulbs ni dara ni mli wa fe kɛji akɛ odu shi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and fresh air reach the trunk of the tree. This stops damp fungal diseases like black pod from growing and forces the tree to put its strength into growing cocoa pods.
ga: Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ akakwɛ̃. kɛ tsei lɛ ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛha amɛhewalɛ aya hiɛ koni amɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines onto tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Lifting the vines up on tall sticks keeps the leaves spread open to the sun and protects them from rot on the hot ground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛhere hulu la lɛ atuu, ni ehaaa amɛfite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool and wet for longer during hot dry days, and stops unwanted weeds from growing near your crop.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be babaoo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too fast. The plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save its own life.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Tso lɛ hao ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillar droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii afɔfɔi yɛ mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center whorl of young maize leaves to eat the tender growth away from heat and natural predators.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ amli koni amɛye tsei bibii ni kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small even when I plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crops underground and above ground. Your crops end up starving because the fast-growing weeds get to the water and soil nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ fɛɛ. Hɔmɔ baaye onibii ejaakɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baaná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot when heavy rain stays on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like people do. When rainwater sits on your farm without draining away, it fills all the tiny air pockets in the dirt, causing the roots to drown and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛtee. Eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why should I grow fresh vegetables around my home instead of only buying them from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ aduawai heei yɛ mishia lɛ he moŋ fe ni mahe yɛ jara nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Growing vegetables around your house gives you immediate access to fresh, healthy food, saves money on daily household expenses, and ensures your family has a reliable food supply even during market shortages or emergencies.
ga: Aduawai ni ooodu yɛ Shia lɛ he lɛ haa onine shɛɔ niyenii hee ni haa mɔ he waa nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Okɛ shika ato daa gbi shia shika he nyɔmɔwoo he. ni oye obua ni oweku lɛ aná niyenii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ jarayeli he nibii ni faaa loo oyaiyeli bei amli po.

english: Can vegetables like peppers and garden eggs grow well in a small backyard space in town?
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛgbɛ he bibioo ko. Yɛ maŋ lɛ mli loo daabi?

english: Yes, many vegetable crops have short root systems and do very well in limited spaces, small backyard patches, or even inside recycled bags and containers placed around the house.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai babaoo yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, sɛɛtsu bibii amli, kɛ kotokui kɛ tsɛnsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ shia lɛ he lɛ po amli.

english: Which vegetable crops can I plant at home that will yield food quickly for my family?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai manyɛ madu yɛ shia koni manyɛ mahã miweku lɛ niyenii oya?

english: Leafy green vegetables like spinach, Gboma, and kontomire grow very fast and can be harvested in as little as three to four weeks, providing quick food for the home.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli tamɔ spinach, burdock, kɛ contomire lɛ daa oya waa, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ eji niyenii ni ayeɔ oya yɛ shia.

english: Why do my backyard vegetable plants grow tall and thin without producing good leaves or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishia sɛɛ aduawai lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee mlɛo ni amɛwooo baa loo aduawai ko lɛ?

english: Vegetables need direct sunlight to make their food. When planted under dark shade or close to tall walls, they stretch upward searching for light instead of growing strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Hulu la he hiaa aduawai tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhoo. Kɛ́ adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ewo duŋ shishi loo yɛ gbogbo ko ni nɔ kwɔ masɛi. Abaakpã mli koni ena la lɛ Moŋ lɛ ebaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do my green vegetable leaves droop down during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-green lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leafy vegetables lose water rapidly through their leaves in high heat. Drooping is the plant's natural way of reducing water loss, and they usually bounce back once the sun goes down or after watering.
ga: Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Foliation ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛyaa sɛɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi loo kɛ́ afɔ lɛ nu sɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my newly planted vegetable seedlings are getting enough sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-vegetable dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ miiná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Healthy seedlings getting enough sunlight will have deep green leaves and thick, sturdy stems that stand upright rather than pale, weak stems leaning toward one side.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baaná baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ, yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa he kome lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant different kinds of vegetables together in the same small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu aduawai srɔtoi? No hewɔ lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ afee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo kome nɔ?

english: Mixing different vegetables confuses crop pests, reduces the spread of diseases, and allows different plants to share soil nutrients efficiently without competing with each other.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ aduawai srɔtoi futu mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee basabasa. Ehaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei srɔtoi Ajaraa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How often should I water my newly sown vegetable seeds so they sprout properly?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-vegetable dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Vegetable seeds need constant soil moisture to wake up and germinate, so they should be watered lightly once in the early morning and once in the cool evening until they sprout.
ga: Aduawai dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afɔ nɔ nu fioo. Shikome leebi maŋkpa kɛ shikome yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do insect pests seem to prefer eating my home-grown vegetables over the weeds growing nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ sumɔɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ shia fe jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Vegetable leaves are soft, tender, and rich in water and nutrients, which attracts insects, whereas many wild weeds have tough leaves or strong smells that naturally push bugs away.
ga: Aduawai ahe baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ mlɛo ni nu kɛ niyenii ni haa kooloi bibii baa lɛ fa babaoo yɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni koo mli jwɛi babaoo yɛ baai ni wa loo ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii lɛ,

english: How can I improve my home garden soil to help my crops grow without buying expensive fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishia abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni miheee ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa?

english: You can mix decomposed kitchen food scraps, dried leaves, and animal manure into your soil to create natural compost, which feeds the crops and helps the soil hold moisture longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shĩa mli nibii ni efite, baai ni egboi, kɛ kooloi amli ŋmeii ni egboi afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ofee adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmeii amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is my harvested cassava hard and difficult to pound into smooth fufu?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni akpa lɛ mli wa ni ewa akɛ aaatswa lɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Different cassava varieties have different water and starch contents. Varieties meant for processing into gari or industrial starch often have less moisture and higher dry matter, which makes them tough when boiled, whereas soft 'boiling' varieties pound easily into smooth fufu.
ga: Esoro nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli. Nibii srɔtoi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni akɛfee gari ashikiŋsha loo nitsumɔhe ashikiŋsha lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ fioo kɛ nibii ni egbi babaoo. ni haa ewaa kɛ́ ahoo lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ atswa ‘hoomɔ’ henɔi ni mli jɔ lɛ oya ni efee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I use the same cassava variety from my farm to make both fufu and gari?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ afee fufu kɛ gari fɛɛ?

english: Yes, while some cassava varieties are specially bred for high gari yield and others for soft boiling, many dual-purpose varieties can be used for both depending on how you process them.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ akwɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo moŋ. kɛ henɔi komɛi kɛha soft boiling Shi abaanyɛ akɛ henɔi babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo atsu nii kɛha enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Edamɔ bɔ ni otsuɔ he nii ohaa lɛ nɔ.

english: What is cassava 'sunsum' and how do I get it when processing cassava?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘Sunsam’ Kasa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maná kɛji mitsuɔ ŋmei he nii?

english: Sunsum is the fine starch sediment settled from the liquid squeezed out of grated cassava during gari making. Once dried, this starch can be used for baking, cooking, or industrial uses.
ga: Sunsum ji sũ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sũ ni jɛɔ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ni atswa lɛ mli lɛ mli be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ mli. Kɛji egbi lɛ Abaanyɛ akɛ ashikishaŋ nɛɛ ashã niyenii, ahoo nii, loo akɛtsu nii yɛ nitsumɔhei.

english: Why does my harvested cassava rot or turn black within just three days of digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ fite loo etsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ gbii etɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not store well once removed from the ground because they lose water quickly and react with oxygen. To prevent loss, you must process the roots quickly into dry goods like gari or flour.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ etooo amɛhe jogbaŋŋ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya, ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii. koni akafite Ehe miihia ni okɛ shishifãi lɛ atsu nii oya ni ofee nɔ ko ni egbi tamɔ ghari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: How do I know if the cassava on my farm is a one-year crop or a two-year crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji afi kome ŋmãa loo afii enyɔ ŋmãa?

english: Early-maturing cassava varieties reach full growth between 9 to 12 months, while late-maturing varieties take 18 to 24 months. You should ask the extension officer or seed supplier for the maturity timeline of the specific stem variety you purchased.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni shwereɔ oya lɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he, yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ nyɔji 18 kɛyashi 24. Esa akɛ obi o-extension agent loo seed supplier lɛ be ni fɔlɔ srɔtoi ni oheɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ he sane.

english: What happens if I harvest a one-year cassava crop too late, like after two years?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa ŋmei afi kome sɛɛ tsɔ, ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, yɛ afii enyɔ sɛɛ?

english: If you leave early-maturing cassava in the ground too long, the tubers become woody, fibrous, lose their floury texture, and may begin to rot from pest damage or excess rains.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmei ni shwereɔ mra lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ bafeɔ tso, efeɔ ŋmei, ni ehiɛ ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eje shishi egbo yɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hewɔ.

english: Is it safe to leave cassava in the ground for up to two years without digging it up?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli kɛyashi afii enyɔ ni akuuu mli?

english: Yes, but only for specific late-maturing or hardy varieties. These cassava plants act as natural storage in the ground, allowing you to harvest tubers gradually when you need food or money.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi kɛha ŋmeii ni shwereɔ sɛɛ loo ŋmeii ni wa lɛ pɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmei tsei nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nutoohei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ye obua bo fiofio ni Ohiɛ oyitso nɔ beni niyenii loo shika he miihia bo lɛ.

english: Should I plant one-year cassava or two-year cassava on my land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmei ni yeɔ afi kome loo ŋmei ni yeɔ afii enyɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: If you need quick food or fast cash sales, plant one-year varieties. If you want a crop that stays safe in the ground as an emergency food reserve over a long dry season, plant two-year varieties.
ga: Kɛji niyenii ni ayeɔ oya loo shika ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ oya he miihia bo. Dumɔ tsei srɔtoi ni eye afi kome. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he miihia bo akɛ oyaiyeli niyenii ni akɛtoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Dumɔ tsei srɔtoi ni eye afii enyɔ.

english: Can I identify which cassava stems are best for gari just by looking at the leaves of the plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ male ŋmei tso ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha gari kɛtsɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ?

english: No, leaf shape and color do not reliably show tuber quality. You should get certified stems from agricultural extension agents or reliable growers who track specific cassava variety traits.
ga: Dabi, baa lɛ su kɛ ehiɛ su ejieee bɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ kpo yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Esa akɛ ona he ni ojɛ lɛ he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo okwaafonyo ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ enɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmei sui lɛ anɔ lɛ dɛŋ.

english: Why do some cassava plants produce large tuber yields faster than other plants on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji oya fe ŋmeii tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Fast growth usually comes down to stem variety and soil nutrients. Improved early-maturing varieties are specifically bred to form heavy roots quickly compared to traditional, slow-growing stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni yaa oya lɛ damɔ tso lɛ yibii srɔtoi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii mli nibii anɔ. Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ titri koni amɛná shishifãi ni tsii ni yaa oya kɛ akɛto blema tsei ni daa blɛoo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my sweet improved mangoes produce small, sour fruits when I plant their seeds directly in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi Sweet Improved Mango lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni mli edɔ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Mango seeds do not grow true to the parent fruit because they carry mixed traits from insect pollination. When you plant a seed directly, the tree usually reverts to its wild or local ancestor, losing the sweet taste and big size of the original fruit.
ga: Mango dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ kɛjɛ fɔlɔ aduawai lɛ mli ejaakɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ amɛ feɔ ekome. Kɛji odu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ Bei pii lɛ Tsei kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa adebɔɔ mli loo maŋ lɛ mli blematsɛmɛi aŋɔɔ. Ekɛ shishijee aduawai lɛ amli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ elɛɛmɔ ni da lɛ baa shi.

english: What is the main benefit of starting my fruit trees in a nursery instead of planting seeds straight on the farm?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ aduawai tsei ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he?

english: A nursery provides a controlled environment where fragile young seedlings can be sheltered from harsh heat and pests while being properly grafted, ensuring they keep high-quality fruit traits before being moved to the field.
ga: Gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ haa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ. He ni abaanyɛ abu dumɔwui bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɛɔ aduawai ahe su ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli dani ajieɔ amɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested improved crops to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ tsei ni asaa amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving seeds from improved or hybrid fruit varieties often leads to poor harvests because the second-generation seeds lose the special qualities of the parent plant and frequently go back to lower-quality local traits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ aduawai srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo aduawai ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he lɛ haaa akpaa nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ mli nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli sui ni baa shi lɛ anɔ

english: Why do extension officers recommend grafting fruit trees like mangoes instead of just growing them from seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ, ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, aŋɔ mango awo mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ dumɔwui kɛkɛ baakwɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Grafting attaches a branch from a sweet, high-yielding tree onto a strong rootstock. This guarantees that your new tree produces the exact same high-quality fruit as the branch source, which seed planting cannot guarantee.
ga: Tso ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ niji ni jɛ tso ni ŋɔɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ fĩɔ shishifã ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he. Enɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ otso hee lɛ baawo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ nɔ ni jɛ he ni afo lɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni nyɛŋ aha dumɔwui adumɔ aba

english: Why do grafted trees bought from a nursery start bearing fruit so much faster than trees grown straight from seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛwo amɛhe ni ahe kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa fe tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Grafted seedlings use shoots taken from mature, adult fruit-bearing trees, so the new tree skips the long childhood stage and can start producing fruit in 2 to 3 years instead of waiting 7 years or more.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni eda ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ tsei heei foɔ gbekɛbiiashi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaamɛ afii 7 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: What makes an improved tree variety different from our traditional local variety?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ wɔmaŋ tsei srɔtoi lɛ ahe?

english: Improved varieties have been carefully selected to produce larger fruits, sweeter taste, and higher yields, whereas local varieties are hardier but usually produce smaller, fiber-filled, or sour fruits.
ga: Ahala tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii wuji. E ŋɔɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, akutseiaŋ tsei srɔtoi lɛ wa shi amɛfɔɔ yibii bibii, ni yɔɔ fiber babaoo, loo ni citrus-flavored yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do young tree seedlings die easily if I plant seeds directly in the field during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii gboiɔ oya kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Directly planted seeds grow tender shoots that lack strong root systems and burn quickly under full tropical sun. A nursery protects them under shade until their stems and roots are tough enough for the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ shishifã ni mli wa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ aba. He ni akwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ baabu amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo shishi kɛyashi be mli ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔ wulu lɛ.

english: Why do two seeds taken from the exact same sweet fruit end up growing into trees with different tasting fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui enyɔ ni ajie kɛjɛ tso yibii ni ŋɔɔ kome mli lɛ daa kɛfeɔ tsei ni tso yibii lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Seeds inherit traits from both the mother flower and pollen carried by bees from neighboring trees, causing each seed to have a unique genetic mix, much like children from the same parents do not look identical.
ga: Dumɔwui náa amɛsui lɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi ni ŋmeii kɛyaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ fɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa wala yibii ni yɔɔ srɔto. Taakɛ gbekɛbii ni jɛ fɔlɔi kome mli lɛ tamɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can I make sure that all the fruit trees in my farm mature at the same time and produce identical fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni aduawai tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ekome kɛkwɛ̃? amɛfee ekome ni amɛha nɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ aba

english: To get identical fruits and uniform harvesting times, you must use vegetatively propagated seedlings like grafted nursery plants from one trusted source, rather than growing unpredictable seedlings from mixed seeds.
ga: Koni aná aduawai abɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ ni aná kpamɔ be ni yaa nɔ daa. Esa akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsei shwieɔ shi, tamɔ tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ni jɛ he kome ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu dumɔwui ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni efutu mli lɛ.

english: How do I safely prepare my young seedlings in the nursery so they don't die when I move them to the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweshweeshwe? Enɛ ji koni amɛkagboi kɛ́ amɛfã kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: You must harden off the seedlings by gradually reducing water and introducing them to direct sunlight a few weeks before planting, then carefully move them with the soil around their roots intact to prevent root shock.
ga: Esa akɛ oha dumɔwui lɛ afee mlɛo fiofio. Okɛ nu lɛ aba shi ni okɛwo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ otsii fioo komɛi dani odu, no sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo he kroko blɛoo, ni oshi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ akatswa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Tall shade trees like plantains or timber trees act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa plants can build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains loo boxwoods tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo tso lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves their green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloi ashishifã ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the space after the maize is cleared.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: These holes are typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing funnels of young corn plants. Catching them early by inspecting your farm allows you to apply recommended pest control before they destroy the entire crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaa lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do people cover the soil around vegetables with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, protects the soil from direct sunlight. It traps water in the ground, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves get maximum light and prevents wet soil from rotting the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha tso lɛ baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ la ni fa babaoo mli ni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite baai lɛ.

english: How can I tell which plantain suckers are best to cut and plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male plantain tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best plantain suckers are 'sword suckers', which have narrow, blade-like leaves and a broad base. They have stronger root reserves and grow faster than suckers with wide leaves.
ga: Plantain tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ‘sword shoot’, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei ni shishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni ji enyɔ ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long hot dry spell before regular rains start. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then scorch in the dry soil from lack of steady water.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛjɛ nu ni bɛ daa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat or irregular watering. Giving tomato plants consistent moisture helps the flowers stay on the plant and form healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛmiifee nɔ ko, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Kɛ́ okɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ wo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is already moist after rain, but not during heavy downpours. Moist soil helps plants absorb nutrients safely, whereas heavy rain can wash the fertilizer away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai lɛ shweshweeshwe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛya.

english: Is it true that harvesting medicinal leaves early in the morning before sunrise makes them more potent?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ tsofafeemɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ leebi dani hulu lɛ ateshi lɛ baaha amɛhe awa waa?

english: Yes, gathering leaves early in the morning before the sun gets hot helps the plant retain its maximum moisture, essential oils, and natural chemical properties that hot sunlight can break down.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni ajieɔ leebi dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ hulutsoo be ni fa fe fɛɛ mli. mu ni he hiaa waa kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite lɛ

english: Why can some health-boosting crops like ginger or garlic be consumed raw while others must be cooked?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abaanyɛ aye tsei komɛi ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ ŋmei loo galiki lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa ni ahoo tsei komɛi lɛ?

english: Raw plants retain fragile active compounds and juices that heat from cooking can destroy, though some heavy roots require light boiling to make them digestible.
ga: Tsei ni ahoo lɛ hiɛɔ nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni waaa kɛ nu ni nihoomɔ mli dɔlɛ baanyɛ afite. Shi kɛlɛ, ehe miihia ni ahoo shishifãi ni tsii waa lɛ ekomɛi yɛ la ni mli edɔɔɔ nɔ koni amɛtsɔ mli.

english: How long can I store freshly squeezed plant juices before they lose their health benefits?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ tso mli nu ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ ato dani sɛɛnamɔi ni eyɔɔ kɛha hewalɛnamɔ lɛ afite?

english: Fresh plant juices begin to ferment and lose vital nutrient strength within hours at room temperature, so it is best to extract and consume them immediately or keep them cool.
ga: Aduawai kɛ aduawai amli nu ni afee ehee lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔtɔ ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baaje mli yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli yɛ ŋwɛi fɛ̃i mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie ni oye amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo okɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my moringa plants turn yellow and drop off during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi Moringa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Moringa plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to conserve water inside their stem and roots, but they quickly sprout fresh leaves once watered.
ga: Moringa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛ nu ato amɛshishi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Shi baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu pɛ.

english: Why does bitter leaf grow back so fast even after I cut all the branches down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ Afolɔ niji lɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Bitter leaf has a deep root network that stores food energy, allowing it to send up strong new shoots rapidly after harvesting to rebuild its leaf canopy.
ga: Baai ni mli edɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ niyenii hewalɛ toɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atsuɔ ŋmeii heei ni he wa oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni akɛsaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my tiger nut plants take much longer to mature during cloudy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tiger nut tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji ni atatu yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Tiger nuts rely on intense sunlight to manufacture plant sugars and build tubers underground, so cloudy days slow down their natural growth cycle.
ga: Tiger ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛfee tsei amli sugar ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, gbii ni atatu yɔɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli dalɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the fleshy leaves of my aloe vera plants turn soft and dark when I give them water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aloe vera lɛ baai ni yɔɔ loo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ediŋ waa kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo mli daa gbi lɛ?

english: Aloe vera naturally holds water inside its thick leaves and requires very little moisture; overwatering suffocates the roots and rots the plant from the base.
ga: Aloe vera lɛ toɔ nu yɛ ebaa ni mli tse lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehe ehiaaa ni ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ ahi mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha tso lɛ agbo kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ.

english: Does planting crops in heavy clay soil lower the strength of their medicinal roots?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi?

english: Hard clay soil restricts root expansion and traps excess water, which can stunt underground growth and lessen the concentration of active juices in medicinal roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ehiɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. ni baanyɛ atsĩ shikpɔŋ shishi dalɛ naa ni eha tsofa aduawai amli nu ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ aba shi.

english: How does adding compost manure to my soil improve the strength of my health crops?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ hewalɛ kɛha hewalɛnamɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic compost releases balanced nutrients slowly into the soil, giving plants the steady nourishment needed to develop strong leaves, roots, and natural health compounds.
ga: Organic compost lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni sa lɛ fiofio kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ daa koni amɛná baai, shishifãi, kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do fruits on my pawpaw trees taste sweet during the sunny season but watery after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yibii ni yɔɔ mi-pawpaw tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shi amɛfeɔ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sunlight helps the tree convert nutrients into concentrated natural sugars, whereas excessive rainwater dilutes the sugar concentration inside the growing fruit.
ga: Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli sugars ni mli eyi obɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa sugar ni yɔɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know if a cassava stem cutting is healthy enough to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso ni afo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Choose cuttings from mature, healthy plants that are 8 to 10 months old. Look for stems with close nodes and healthy buds, and avoid stems showing rot, insect holes, or signs of disease.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 10 lɛ mli tso ko ni afolɔ. Taomɔ tsei ni yɔɔ nodes ni agbe naa kɛ buds ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni fiteɔ, kooloi bibii, loo hela he okadii ahe.

english: Yam plants need their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the wet ground, preventing leaf rot and disease.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ helai anaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to build strong, food-producing green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores color and vigor to the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa awo baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ niyenii jɛɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná su kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like cowpeas restores nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of small holes and chewing damage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni nɔ ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli?

english: This chewing pattern is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf funnel. Catching them early is important so they don't eat the main growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baa. Ehe miihia ni amɔmɔ amɛ mra koni amɛkaye tso lɛ mli fãi titrii lɛ.

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your main crops need to grow strong. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to food and moisture.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot, dry spell before the actual rainy season stabilizes. Seeds planted too early may germinate and then scorch and die in dry soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ be ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baa shi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛshã ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt and drop their flowers when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomatoes, causing leaves to lose moisture faster than roots can draw it up. High temperatures also heat up pollen, preventing flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ hu haa pollen lɛ mli dɔɔ. Tsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers compete directly with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Planting maize on the same plot continuously drains specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, leading to poorer yields each season and allowing maize-specific pests and diseases to settle in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli. ni eha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans alongside my maize helps the crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans absorb nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow near maize, they release this natural nitrogen into the soil, acting as a free, organic fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei shwieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa Amɛjieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ehe.

english: Why do I need to build big soil mounds before I plant my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ agbo dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand underground and require soft, loose soil to grow long and thick. Soil mounds give the tubers enough space to grow freely while ensuring excess rainwater drains away so the yams do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ koni amɛdara kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Muji ni abua naa lɛ haa bulb lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade, cooler air, and soil moisture during its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo shade ni mli tse, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with tiny yields when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete directly against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving the plant with very little energy to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hewalɛ fioo pɛ tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaawo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why are the center leaves of my young maize plants full of holes and dark, sawdust-like dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This is a signature sign of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar crawls into the center heart of the maize plant, eating the tender leaves before they fully open and leaving behind its waste.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ he okadi krɛdɛɛ ko. Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Ye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛfɔ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni oshi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up, shrinking, and turning yellow with green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant sap. The virus stops the plant from making food properly, which stunts the plant and shrinks the harvestable roots.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa shishifãi ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: This is usually bacterial wilt or root rot. Microscopic organisms in the soil invade the plant's roots and clog the stem's internal water pipes, preventing water from reaching the leaves despite moist soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ. Nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli ni amɛtsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees snap at the base or fall over during moderate rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Underground pests, such as banana weevils or root nematodes, bore into the stem bulb and eat the roots. This destroys the anchor system holding the heavy tree securely in the dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ Boreɔ amɛboteɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋshɔŋloo gbɛjianɔtoo ni ŋmɛɔ tso ni tsii lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by severe midday heat, long gaps between watering, or tiny insects like thrips eating the flower joints.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli kɛ enɛ baa. Gbɛ kakadaŋŋ ni kã nu ni akɛhaa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ahe fãi lɛ ateŋ

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight or high heat. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside young cocoa creates a canopy that shields them from scorching heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Enɛ kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Does it matter which direction I stick my cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava stem buds point upward toward the sky. If you plant the cutting upside down, the shoots must bend unnaturally underground to find light, which drains the plant's energy and produces small, poor-quality tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cassava tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ nine lɛ hiɛ lɛ Esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔle amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ koni amɛna la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni ehaa bulb bibii ni ehiii kwraa lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for growth. Staking prevents the leaves from rotting on damp soil and helps the plant direct its food down into expanding the yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛshwere. Staking tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii baa shi koni amɛgbala sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: Why are my maize stalks growing tall and thin without producing big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɛɛ toi wuji lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for light, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows each plant enough room and sunlight to produce strong stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la mli akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my plantain mats produce smaller fruit bunches after the second year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii bibii yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants continuously produce extra young shoots called suckers. If you do not cut off excess suckers, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem, causing the mother plant to yield smaller bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii be fɛɛ be. Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Ha tso nyɛ lɛ awo ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn crops turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that the soil is overly waterlogged. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore leaf health and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baa lɛ aya hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes in them as soon as they shoot up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the leaves are commonly caused by early-stage caterpillar pests, such as Fall Armyworm, feeding inside the plant whorl. Early monitoring and targeted treatment stop them before they destroy the crop's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ mra be mli, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fãa yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ mra kɛ tsamɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ Kpa amɛ dani amɛfite hei ni onibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before any tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani tomato lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulching helps protect the blossoms so fruit can set.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ okɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to multiply. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts naturally restores nitrogen and keeps soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛfɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aba ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even when my crops are already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo lɛ?

english: Weed roots spread aggressively underground and steal water and nutrients from the soil long before your crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds early ensures all soil nutrients go directly to feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How many maize seeds am I supposed to put in one hole when planting my field?
ga: Abele dumɔwui enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛwo bu kome mli kɛ́ midu yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When you have good quality seeds, you should put only one seed in each hole. Putting one strong seed per hole gives the plant enough room and soil nutrients to grow strong and produce big ears of maize.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ Esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui 1 pɛ awo bu fɛɛ bu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwu kome ni hi jogbaŋŋ fata bu kome he lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi wuji aba.

english: If I am worried that my maize seeds are not very good, should I put extra seeds in each hole?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ohao akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ehiii. Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo afata bu lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he?

english: Yes, if your seeds are of lower quality or older, planting two seeds in a hole acts as a safety net. This ensures that at least one plant will survive in that spot even if the other seed fails to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ odumɔwui lɛ ji nɔ ni baa shi loo nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ. Dumɔwui enyɔ ni aaadu yɛ bu lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii akɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ tsɔne. Enɛ haa kɛ hoo lɛ, tso kome hiɔ shi yɛ nakai he lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwu kroko lɛ kwɛɛɛ po.

english: How does planting only one seed per hole save me money during the farming season?
ga: Bɔ ni dumɔwu kome pɛ ni miduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa mináa shika yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Planting one good seed per hole means you use fewer seeds to cover your entire field. This prevents you from wasting expensive, high-quality seeds and avoids the need to spend extra labor pulling out crowded plants later.
ga: Dumɔwu kpakpa kome ni ooodu yɛ bu kome mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ okɛ dumɔwui fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii ni okɛhaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ baatsi bo gbɛ koni okafite dumɔwui ni jara wa ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Ni nitsumɔ kroko he ehiaaa koni akɛjie tsei ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What is a germination test, and why should I do it before planting?
ga: Mɛni ji shweremɔ he kaa? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee dani adu lɛ?

english: A germination test is a simple trial where you plant a small batch of seeds in wet cloth or soil to see how many sprout. Doing this tells you if your seeds are healthy and alive before you spend time and labor planting the entire field.
ga: Kaa ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Oduɔ dumɔwui akuu bibioo ko. yɛ mama loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ mli koni ana dumɔwui enyiɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Enɛ baatsɔɔ bo kɛji odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɛ wala mli dani okɛ be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I test the seeds I saved from last harvest to see if they will grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ kɛji amɛbaakwɛ̃?

english: Take a sample of 10 or 100 seeds, place them on a wet cloth or in a small bowl of damp soil, and keep them moist for a few days. Count how many sprout to easily see what percentage of your saved seeds are still healthy.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui 10 loo 100 afee nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, ni okɛwo mama ni mli efɔ nɔ loo yɛ tsɛnsi bibioo ko ni sũ ni mli efɔ mli lɛ mli, ni oha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi gbii fioo komɛi. Kanemɔ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ayibɔ koni ona dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa enyiɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ lolo.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer tells me my seeds have '98% viability'?
ga: Beni sɛɛkuu nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midumɔwui lɛ ji Mɛni ji ‘98% viability’ shishi?

english: It means the seed quality is excellent, and out of every 100 seeds you plant, around 98 of them will successfully sprout into strong, healthy plants.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ, ni yɛ dumɔwui 100 fɛɛ 100 ni obaadu lɛ mli lɛ, aaafee 98 baatsɔ tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: If my sprout test shows that only half of my seeds grow, what should I do when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ shweremɔ he kaa lɛ mli saji lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ fã pɛ kwɛ̃ Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji midu?

english: If only half of your seeds grow in a test, your seeds have low viability. You should either buy fresh, tested seeds or plant two seeds in every hole so you do not end up with empty spots across your field.
ga: Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ daraa be lɛ fã pɛ yɛ kaa lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni baa shi. Esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei ni aka amɛ akwɛ. Aloo dumɔ dumɔwui 2 yɛ bu fɛɛ bu mli. koni he ko akafee shwɛm yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do my maize plants look weak and thin when I put three or four seeds in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe efee shoo kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When multiple seeds sprout in the same hole, the young plants fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This competition leaves all of them weak, thin, and unable to produce large maize cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei bibii kɛ amɛhe baawu koni amɛná nu. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ, amɛhe feɔ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmãa ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant fail to sprout out of the ground completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yeee omanye kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are damaged by insects, spoiled by bad storage conditions, planted too deep, or if the soil lacks enough moisture during planting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji kooloi fite amɛ. Efiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nitoohe shihilɛ ni ehiii ni adu mli tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ dumɔ be mli

english: How does using a seed-planter machine help my maize farm compared to hand planting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛduɔ lɛ he?

english: A seed planter automatically drops the precise number of seeds needed—such as exactly one seed per hole—at a uniform depth and distance, making planting faster and ensuring an even crop growth across your field.
ga: Dumɔwui adumɔ tsɔne lɛ diɛŋtsɛ duɔ dumɔwui ayibɔ ni he hiaa lɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui kome yɛ bu kome mli. yɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ daa Enɛ haa dumɔ yaa oya ni ehaa tsei po daa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and fragile root systems that easily dry out under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa shields the young trees from heat and retains soil moisture until the cocoa is mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ egbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulutsoo be muu lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. Applying balanced fertilizers, compost, or animal manure helps restore nitrogen to the soil and turns the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ he miihia koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and causes crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa babaoo Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce a strong yield.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the soil before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays overly wet and cannot drain properly after rain. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water flow away from the roots, preventing rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa

english: Why do weeds make my crops weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and steal valuable nutrients, fertilizer, and sunlight from the soil. Keeping the farm clear of weeds leaves all the soil nutrients for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni jara wa, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni baaye abua ni onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing hole patterns into the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are often Fall Armyworms, which attack the growing central shoot of young maize plants. Early detection and applying recommended organic or chemical controls early in the morning or evening can save the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmei tsei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛbaatsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do people advise me to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Removing dead or overcrowded branches, known as pruning, allows sunlight and air to move freely through the tree canopy. This reduces dampness that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Ale tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ hu akɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Mulching around the base keeps the soil moist and cool, helping flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ye dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Mulching around Shishitoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce small and uneven yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for one powerful harvest. If you replant seeds saved from that crop, they lose their special strength, resulting in weak plants and lower yields compared to buying fresh certified hybrid seeds.
ga: Afɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwu ni ahere lɛ kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Does strong sunshine hurt my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ mi kokoo tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, direct and excessive sunlight can scorch the delicate leaves of young cocoa trees, dry out the surrounding soil, and cause severe stress that stunts their growth or kills them.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã cacao tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli agbi ni ekɛ haomɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ aha dalɛ afee mlɛo loo gbele aba.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are suffering from too much sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: When cocoa trees get too much sun, their leaves turn yellow or brown at the edges, dry up, and drop off early, leaving the branches bare and weak.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ asɛɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Egbi ni egbee shi oya Enɛ haa niji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Will big shade trees steal water and nutrients from my cocoa crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli?

english: While shade trees do use soil resources, their deep roots pull nutrients up from lower soil levels and their falling leaves create rich compost, which actually feeds and protects your cocoa crops in the long run.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ, Shi shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Ni baai ni egbee shi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Ehaa o-cocoa tsei lɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ ni ebuɔ amɛhe yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings lack strong root systems and thick leaves to survive harsh sunlight and heat; without temporary shade crops to shield them, they quickly dry out and die.
