ga: Cocoa dumɔwui bɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ baai ni mli wa ni baaha amɛhi shi yɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ mli. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ lɛ, Amɛgbiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains together with new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei duɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that create temporary shade, keeping the air cool and soil moist so young cocoa seedlings can establish strong roots.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Bɔni afee ni kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ anyɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why are my newly planted plantains drying up and dying on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni midu ehee lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Newly planted plantain suckers usually die if they are planted during extended dry spells without enough moisture in the soil, or if the soil lacks organic matter to hold water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ gboiɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha nu ahi mli

english: Why are my new crops struggling to grow where old cocoa trees used to be?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ miitao ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ cacao tsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Old farms often have depleted soil nutrients and hidden pests or diseases in the ground from the previous trees, which makes it harder for new seedlings to take root without soil treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni etsɛ waa lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni jɛ tsei ni eho lɛ amli ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui heei akɛ amɛaawo shishifãi kɛji atsuuu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii.

english: Should I cut down all the big trees on my land before planting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo ŋmɔ hee?

english: No, cutting down all big trees exposes your soil and young crops to harsh sun and heavy rain; it is better to leave selected, beneficial shade trees to protect the farm.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaha hulu ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aná oshikpɔŋ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ koni obu ŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce fewer pods now compared to when I planted it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo fe beni midu lɛ afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past their peak, their productivity naturally drops due to worn-out branches, tired roots, depleted soil nutrients, and accumulated pests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ fe afii ni eshɛɔ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ niji ni efite lɛ ahewɔ. shishifãi ni etɔ Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni efite kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ebua amɛhe naa

english: Is it better to replace an old cocoa farm all at once or bit by bit?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaatsake kookoo ŋmɔji momoi lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo atsake amɛ fiofio?

english: Replanting in phases allows you to maintain continuous income from the remaining old trees while giving young trees time to grow under controlled shade and care.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ekoŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ onáa shika ni yaa nɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei momo ni eshwɛ lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ be koni amɛdara yɛ hulutsoo kɛ kwɛmɔ ni akudɔɔ shishi.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer gives the leaves the food they need to turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting beans together with my maize help my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special because they pull natural fertilizer from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the maize growing next to them without extra cost.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji nɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛgbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ ni shika kroko fataaa he

english: What happens if I plant my cassava stems too close together?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and very small tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ baa.

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three heavy rains so the soil is wet deep down, rather than planting right after the very first light shower which can dry out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa. Mohu ɔ, duɔ amlɔ nɔuu ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ ɔ nɛ ma nyɛ maa gbi ɔ se.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get extremely high, when the soil becomes too dry, or if insects have not visited to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi baaa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up and look droopy during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves and save water, and they usually bounce back once the afternoon cools down.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he. Ni amɛfɔɔ sɛɛkuu be mli ni shwane lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I grow pepper on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing pepper in the same soil year after year allows pests and diseases that attack peppers to hide in the ground and build up, making future harvests weaker.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛbua amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ baa shi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the roots, which helps the yam tubers under the soil grow long and fat.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce much smaller yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm—they quickly soak up the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your crops need to produce good food.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ mɛi ni juɔ niyenii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpa lɛ oya.

english: What causes small holes and caterpillar droppings inside the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the center shoot of young maize plants and eat the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli ni eyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow starting from the tip and moving down the middle, your maize is lacking nitrogen. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the leaves stay green and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaagbee shi kɛtee teŋgbɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: How does spreading dry leaves and animal manure around my crops help my farm?
ga: Baai ni egbi kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry leaves and manure break down into organic matter, which acts like a sponge in the soil. It traps rainwater, keeps the soil cool during hot days, and slowly releases natural food to your crops.
ga: Baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Emɔɔ nugbɔ nu, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii fiofio kɛyaa onibii amli.

english: How do I choose the right stem to cut when planting new cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso ni sa ni mikɛduɔ ŋmei hee?

english: Select mature stems from the middle part of a healthy plant, about 20 to 30 centimeters long with visible buds. Avoid using the very soft top tips or the woody bottom bases, as they sprout slowly and produce weaker plants.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda kɛjɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ teŋgbɛ. Amɛkɛlɛ aaafee sɛntimitai 20 kɛyashi 30 ni amɛyɛ hiŋmɛii ni anaa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi naagbee ni yɔɔ blɛoo waa loo shishigbɛ ni akɛ tso fee lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa blɛoo. ni ebaaha tso lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ

english: Which kind of sucker should I select when I want to start a new plantain farm?
ga: Mɛɛ sucker henɔ esa akɛ mahala kɛ́ miisumɔ ni mabɔi plantain ŋmɔ hee?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which have narrow leaves and a large bulb at the base. Avoid 'water suckers' with broad leaves, because they grow into weak plants that yield small, light bunches.
ga: Halamɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni yɔɔ baai bibii kɛ bulb agbo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘sucker shoot’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ he, ejaakɛ edaa ni etsɔɔ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii bibii ni tsiimɔ waaa.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn under strong direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a canopy that protects young cocoa trees from the harsh sun while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛkɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shãa amɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward the sun. Proper staking helps the leaves catch more sunlight to feed the plant, which results in much larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ wo tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni ekɛhaa tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juice from young leaves, or by a virus spread by aphids. Spraying neem oil early or using safe insecticidal soaps helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni aphids gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Neem fɔ ni oooshwie nɔ mra Aloo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving sawdust-like powder in the stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ anɔ Ni ashi powda ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day, so applying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening reaches them best.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni akɛtsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. Watering regularly at the soil level during dry periods keeps the soil moist and helps fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ he.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize affect my crop growth?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baaná tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Planting beans with maize is actually beneficial. Beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil, which helps naturally fertilize your maize while giving you two harvests from one land area.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Beans gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha o-corn lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji shii enyɔ aba kɛjɛ he kome.

english: What type of crops should I plant if my farm is in an area that does not get much rain?
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ adu?

english: You should plant fast-growing bean varieties like 'Favour' or 'Fever', as they mature quickly within 90 to 110 days and can produce a good harvest before the moisture runs out.
ga: Esa akɛ odu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni daa oya tamɔ ‘Favour’ loo ‘Fever’ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya yɛ gbii 90 kɛyashi 110 mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baaho.

english: Why are many farmers across Ghana switching to new bean varieties like 'Favour'?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ miitsake kɛmiiya ŋmeii srɔtoi heei tamɔ ‘Favour’ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Farmers across Ghana are adopting varieties like 'Favour' because they grow fast, withstand low rainfall areas, and produce high crop yields.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ miiye ŋmeii srɔtoi tamɔ ‘Favour’ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hei ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: How long does the 'Favour' bean variety take from planting until harvest time?
ga: Be enyiɛ ‘Favour’ ŋmeii lɛ heɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ mli?

english: The 'Favour' bean variety takes between 100 to 110 days to mature fully, giving you enough time to harvest high yields.
ga: Favour’ ŋmeii lɛ heɔ gbii 100 kɛyashi 110 dani eshɛɔ ŋmeii ahe. Enɛ haa onáa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛkpaa yibii babaoo.

english: What does it mean when a bean crop is described as fast-maturing?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛ́ atsɔɔ ŋmei tso ko mli akɛ edaa oya?

english: Fast-maturing means the crop completes its growth cycle quickly, reaching harvest readiness in as little as 90 days so you get your produce faster.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ mra lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbeɔ amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa oya. Eshɛɔ kpamɔ he he saamɔ he yɛ gbii 90 pɛ mli, no hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ onine ashɛ okpamɔ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: How can I make sure my crop fully grows before the short rainy season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ aba naagbee?

english: By choosing quick-maturing varieties like 'Fever' beans that ready in 90 days, your crop completes its growth cycle before the rain stops completely.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra, tamɔ ‘Fever’ ŋmeii ni feɔ klalo yɛ gbii 90 mli lɛ ni ooohala lɛ nɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa dani nugbɔ lɛ baakpa kwraa.

english: Can bean crops still grow well if the rains are short and irregular this year?
ga: Ani ŋmeii tsei lɛ baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lolo kɛji nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni ebɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ afi nɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting short-duration crop varieties allows the plants to establish and grow rapidly within places that don't receive high amounts of rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli dumɔ haa tsei daa ni amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ hei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ tsɔ lɛ.

english: How can I increase the amount of harvest I get from my bean farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã ŋmɔshi nibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-bean ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Planting improved bean varieties such as 'Favour' can significantly increase your total yield while still maturing in a relatively short timeframe.
ga: Bean henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ‘Favour’ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baanyɛ aha onibii fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ waa yɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ lolo yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Are there bean crops that don't take long to mature but still give a heavy harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei komɛi yɛ ni heɔ be kuku dani amɛdaraa shi amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lolo?

english: Yes, varieties like 'Favour' take only 100 to 110 days to mature while still giving farmers very high yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi tamɔ ‘Favour’ lɛ heɔ gbii 100 kɛyashi 110 pɛ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa okwaafoi lɛ yibii babaoo waa lolo.

english: Why should I choose a 90-day bean variety over traditional longer-season crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yeɔ gbii 90 fe blema ŋmeii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: A 90-day bean variety like 'Fever' allows you to harvest much quicker, helping you avoid dry weather damage while freeing up your field sooner.
ga: Bean henɔi ni yeɔ gbii 90 tamɔ ‘Fever’ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa oya. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ nibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he, ni ehaa he ko feɔ mlɛo oya.

english: Which bean varieties perform well in dry zones while still providing good food for my family?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu bɛ shi amɛhaa miweku lɛ niyenii kpakpa lolo?

english: Varieties like 'Favour' and 'Fever' are ideal for dry zones across Ghana because they mature quickly within 90 to 110 days and yield plenty of produce.
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ ‘Favour’ kɛ ‘Fever’ lɛ hi kɛha hei ni nu bɛ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, edaa oya yɛ gbii 90 kɛyashi 110 mli, ni ewoɔ nibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. It can also happen when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do people plant plantain trees in a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi miidu plantains yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that provide vital shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees are young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daraa lolo lɛ.

english: Too much rain fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. This wet condition encourages fungal diseases to grow and attack the tubers, causing them to decay.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ nɛɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ.

english: What causes the small worms that eat the leaves inside the whorl of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ a-rings lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid on the leaves by adult moths. They hide inside the central leaves of young corn plants to feed on the tender leaf tissues.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ afɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye baa bibii lɛ amli fãji lɛ.

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil nutrients, especially nitrogen. Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, restoring fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Heat stress stops the flowers from pollinating properly, so the plant drops them to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Heat haomɔ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crops help them survive dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry grass acts as a protective blanket over the soil called mulch. It blocks the hot sun from directly hitting the earth, preventing soil moisture from evaporating quickly and keeping root temperatures cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ ni ale lɛ akɛ mulch lɛ he. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch sunlight so their leaves can produce food for growing tubers. Staking keeps the leaves dry and off the ground, which also prevents foliage diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai hu anaa.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds when my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, weak root systems. Weeds grow faster and will steal the available water, sunlight, and soil fertilizer before your young crops have a chance to feed and grow.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu ni yɔɔ, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Dani oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baaná hegbɛ amɛye nii ni amɛdara

english: What makes cocoa pods turn dark brown or black during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, cold, and humid conditions. High moisture and thick canopy shade allow the water mold to travel easily from pod to pod.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ ŋwɛi ŋmɔlɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa pod kroko mli mlɛo.

english: How does fertilizer actually work to increase my crop yield?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ koni eha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for plants. Just as good food helps a child grow strong, fertilizer supplies missing soil nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, allowing crops to grow larger fruits, leaves, and seeds so you harvest much more.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei aniyenii. Niyenii kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa gbekɛbii ni amɛdaraa kɛ hewalɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ aduawai, baai, kɛ dumɔwui wuji. no hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa babaoo

english: How do I know if my soil is missing nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops are growing slowly, look weak, have pale green or yellowing leaves, or produce small yields despite getting enough rainfall, your soil is likely out of essential food and needs fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo, etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ, eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ loo yibiiwoo fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia lɛ.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer in the soil when planting or after the crops sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ be mli loo beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Feeding plants in stages gives the best result. A little fertilizer at planting helps young seeds build strong roots, and a second application once the plant is actively growing provides the boost needed for a rich harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii ha tso lɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo fata odumɔ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa. Ni kɛ́ akɛtsu nii shii enyɔ beni tso lɛ miida waa lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmaa babaoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When soil becomes flooded with heavy rain, water washes away nitrogen and drowns root system, preventing plants from breathing. Without air and nitrogen, crops cannot maintain their healthy green color.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nitrogen bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu nyɛŋ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants slow down and stop growing during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants use water from the soil to carry nutrients up into their stems and leaves. When water is scarce, the plant goes into survival mode, slowing its growth to conserve moisture until rain returns.
ga: Tsei kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Tso lɛ baaya wala shihilɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ dalɛ ni abaaha eya shi fioo koni akɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with poor yields if I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo faaa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil moisture, and food. They stretch upward to reach light, becoming weak and thin instead of strong and full of crop yield.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ, amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshɛɔ la lɛ he. baafee mɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee mɔ ni he wa ni ewo yibii kwraa

english: Why do weeds on my field seem to grow much faster than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are aggressive at stealing nutrients, water, and sunlight from the soil. They grow quickly and will starve your main crop if they are not cleared away early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛbaahã hɔmɔ aye onibii titrii lɛ kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: What makes cassava plants grow thick green leaves but leaves very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ baa eŋɔli ni mli tse shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the plant spends all its energy building leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients below to expand the cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛba shishi koni ekɛdu ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do tomato flowers fall off my plants before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Providing good soil nutrients and moisture helps the flowers stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot under the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when rain water sits around the roots in flat, poorly drained soil, encouraging soil fungi and diseases. Raising the soil into high mounds lets extra water drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ebɔle amɛhe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmeii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ helai srɔtoi baa. Shikpɔŋ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛfeɔ gɔŋ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops take 6 months to mature when other farmers harvest theirs in just 4 months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ nyɔji 6 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Beni okwaafoi krokomɛi kpaa nii yɛ nyɔji 4 pɛ mli?

english: Crop maturity speed depends on the seed variety and soil nutrition. Improved, early-maturing seed varieties combined with proper fertilizer can reduce crop growth cycles significantly compared to traditional seeds.
ga: Tso dalɛ oyaiyeli damɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra ni atsake amɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ afee kuku kwraa kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ahe.

english: How can early-maturing seed varieties help me get my produce to market faster?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mikɛ minibii lɛ aya jara nɔ oya?

english: Early-maturing seeds are bred to complete their life cycle in fewer days, allowing you to harvest early, beat peak market gluts, and sell your produce when market demand and prices are high.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ koni amɛgbe amɛwala shihilɛ naa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa nii oya. Ye jara nɔ nibii ni ataoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ kunim ni ohɔ̃ɔ onibii lɛ be mli ni jara nɔ nibii ni ataoɔ kɛ jara lɛ nɔ kwɔ.

english: How does adding fertilizer or manure help my crops grow faster?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: Just like food feeds a growing animal, fertilizer provides essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that plants need to build strong stems, green leaves, and big produce rapidly.
ga: Nakai eji yɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa kooloi ni miida lɛ hu he. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ awo ŋmeii ni wa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ yibii babaoo oya.

english: Why do my crops look pale and weak even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for crops to grow well. Pale leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, so adding organic compost or fertilizer gives the plant the nourishment required to turn deep green and strong.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa koni tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds and mulch my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi awo mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds removes aggressive competition for light and nutrients, while mulching covers the ground to trap moisture and protect seeds, creating ideal conditions for rapid early growth.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni naa wa kɛha la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Yɛ be mli ni mulching haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha dalɛ oya baa shishijee mli.

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crops to fight over sunlight, soil water, and nutrients, which results in tall, weak plants with small yields instead of healthy, full produce.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ kɛhaa hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii, ni no haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa lɛ baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona nɔ ko ni yeɔ emuu ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when my produce is ready to harvest for buyers coming from Accra?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛjɛɔ Accra lɛ?

english: For distant buyers, harvest crops like tomatoes or vegetables when they reach full size and firm maturity but before they fully soften, ensuring they survive transit without spoiling.
ga: Kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ Kpamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato loo aduawai. Beni amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa. Shi dani ebaagbɔjɔ kwraa Enɛ ji koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ gbɛfaa lɛ mli ni amɛfiteee.

english: Which short-term crops can I plant if I need quick cash within a few months?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ madu kɛji shika he miihia mi oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Vegetable crops like okra, cucumbers, and leafy greens mature within 2 to 3 months, making them reliable options for quick cash flow compared to long-term tree crops.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ okra, kukumba, kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni no baaha amɛfee nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha shika ni baa oya. kɛ akɛto tsei ahe yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: How can I protect my young seedlings from dying under heavy heat and sunshine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hulu la shishi?

english: Young seedlings have tender leaves that dry out easily; providing temporary shade with palm fronds or intercropping with broad-leaf shade plants shields them from harsh heat until their roots are strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbiɔ oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo aduɔ lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Leaf curling is usually a sign of insect pests like whiteflies or disease; using disease-resistant cassava stems and managing pests early keeps the leaves healthy so the roots can swell properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii loo helai ahe okadi. Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ afu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients to the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight during their early years. Shade trees act as natural umbrellas that keep the air cool and conserve moisture until the cocoa plants grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulutsoo ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yam plants store energy in their underground tubers through their leaves catching sunlight. Lifting the vines up on stakes allows the leaves to spread out and capture more sunlight, resulting in bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni hulu la babaoo shɛɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them for too long due to poorly drained soil during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell that dries out the hot soil. If seeds start germinating without follow-up rains, the young roots dry up and die before the major rains fully establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli gbiɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli. Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruits start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches, making them top-heavy. As the fruit bunch grows, wind can easily pull the plant down unless you prop it up with strong wooden poles.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛyɛ jwɛi ni mli tse, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ dara lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ agbala tsei kɛba shi mlɛo. Ja okɛ tso ni wa miitsu nii kɛmiifi sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without producing fruit during periods of extreme afternoon heat or dry spells, which damages the pollen. Giving the plants consistent water during flowering helps them set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa loo hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli. ni fiteɔ pollen Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my cowpea plants producing lots of leafy green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpea plants to focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of flowers and pods. Tiny insect pests like thrips can also attack and destroy the flower buds before they turn into pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Nibii bibii tamɔ thrips hu baanyɛ atutua fɔfɔii ashishifãi ni amɛfite amɛ dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my harvest if there is plenty of soil for everyone?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and water required to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How long does it usually take for short-season crops like maize or vegetables to mature and be ready for harvest?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai. Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani ekwɛ̃ ni efee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ?

english: Many fast-growing crops like maize, peppers, and leafy greens mature in about three months (90 days). This short cycle allows farmers to plant and harvest multiple times in a year if water is available.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ baai lɛ, shwereɔ yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ (gbii 90) mli. Nɛkɛ sɛɛkuu kuku nɛɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ duɔ nii ni amɛkpaa nii shii abɔ yɛ afi mli kɛji nu yɛ.

english: Why do large commercial farms manage to harvest so much more food from their land than small farms using simple hand tools?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔji bibii ni kɛ nine nitsumɔ dadei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Commercial farms use machinery for deep plowing, precise seed placement, and efficient harvesting, along with improved seed varieties and balanced fertilizers, which allows them to produce much higher yields per acre.
ga: Jarayeli ŋmɔji kɛ tsɔnei tsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ. Dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Kɛfata dumɔwui afɔmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kwraa yɛ acre kome mli.

english: Why do crops like cocoa and plantain grow better in southern forest regions than in drier northern regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ kookoo kɛ plantain kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ amli fe hei ni nu bɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops have different moisture and climate needs. Southern regions offer higher rainfall and natural shade suitable for cocoa and plantain, while northern regions have drier climates better suited for grains like sorghum, millet, and cowpeas.
ga: Tsei yɛ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ, ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo, ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo kɛ plantain. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ tsina ŋmei.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or poor drainage causing waterlogged roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni haa shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has run out of nutrients before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ efo mli dani mibɔi dumɔwui?

english: If crops from the previous season grew slowly, had pale leaves, or produced very small yields, your soil is likely low in nutrients and needs organic manure, compost, or fertilizer before planting again.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ daraa blɛoo, amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hu faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni okɛ humus, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani odu ekoŋŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in thin stalks and smaller tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii kɛ yitsei bibii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops whenever the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local soils, allowing them to absorb rainfall and nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds, which need time to establish delicate roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu, ni he hiaa be dani amɛfee shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do young seedlings often wither and die when transplanted directly into full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have fragile root systems that cannot absorb water fast enough to replace moisture lost through their leaves under harsh direct heat. Providing temporary shade helps them survive until their roots grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛto nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ najiaŋ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli waa.

english: Why do pests like armyworms suddenly appear in large numbers right after the first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ jeɔ kpo babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Warm weather and humidity right after early rains create ideal conditions for pest eggs to hatch simultaneously, leading to sudden outbreaks that target young, soft crop leaves.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa mra be mli nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔfɔi yɛ be kome mli, ni ekɛ helai ni baa trukaa lɛ baa ni amɛtutuaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do harvested vegetables rot quickly if I leave them stacked in direct sunlight after picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛwo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ beni mikpa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested crops continue to breathe and lose water. Direct sunlight heats up the produce, speeding up water loss and softening tissues, which allows mold and bacteria to spoil the harvest quickly.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛnuɔ nu. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha nibii ni adu lɛ mli adɔ. Ehaa nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ yaa oya ni ehaa fãji lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni adu lɛ oya.

english: Can groundnuts grow well on my farmland here in Ghana, or do they only grow in neighboring dry countries?
ga: Ani ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ? Aloo ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni egbi lɛ pɛ amli?

english: Groundnuts grow very well in Ghana, especially in areas with warm weather and well-drained, loose soil. The same climate conditions that allow neighboring countries to produce groundnuts exist across many regions in Ghana.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni haa maji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ Ghana kpokpai babaoo anɔ.

english: Do groundnut crops require a lot of continuous heavy rainfall to yield a good harvest?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni naa wa ni yaa nɔ waa he miihia ŋmei tsei koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: No, groundnuts do not need flooded fields and actually prefer moderate rainfall with good sunlight. Excessive water can cause groundnut pods to rot in the soil before harvest.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni nu ashwie ŋmeii anɔ ni yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, amɛsumɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ kɛ hulu la ni baaa tɛ̃ɛ. Nu babaoo baanyɛ aha ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa.

english: Why do groundnut flowers bloom above the ground if the actual nuts grow underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Once the flower on top of the plant is pollinated, it grows a long stem called a peg that bends downward and pushes itself into the soil, where the groundnut pods mature underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ shwie shi lɛ Eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why must the soil be kept soft and loose while my groundnuts are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Loose soil allows the stems from the flowers to easily push underground into the earth to form nuts; hard, packed soil prevents these stems from digging in, leading to fewer nuts.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsiɔ tsei nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkabote mli, ni no haa ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young groundnut plants turning yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Early yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nutrients, water is sitting around the roots due to poor drainage, or the plant has a fungal leaf disease that needs attention.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Aloo tso lɛ yɛ fungal leaf hela ko ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will growing groundnuts weaken my soil or drain all its nutrients for future crops?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ loo ebaajie niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts actually improve soil health because they are legumes, which take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, leaving useful nutrients behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ejaakɛ eji ŋmãa. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shi niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my groundnut crop early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni bɔle mi-peanut tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light and nutrients from young plants, and dense weeds physically block the growing flowering stems from reaching the earth to form nuts.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Ni jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Can I plant regular groundnuts bought from the local market as seeds on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ daa akɛ dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Market groundnuts may not germinate well because they might be old or damaged; using certified seeds meant for planting ensures strong growth and better yield.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ kwɛŋ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ amɛgbɔ loo amɛfite. Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli tsu nii kɛdu lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ waa ni eha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me if I want to start growing groundnuts?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛji miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmeii ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: An extension officer brings practical knowledge directly to your farm, helping you choose the right seed varieties, prepare your land properly, detect crop diseases early, and apply modern farming methods.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi kɛ nilee ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ye obua bo ni ohala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni sa. Saamɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai mra. ni amɛkɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi atsu nii

english: When is the best time for me to plant groundnuts during the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ nugbɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Groundnuts should generally be planted right after the major rains begin and the soil stays consistently moist, allowing the seeds to germinate quickly and grow before dry spells set in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛdaraa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or the ground has too much standing water. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea and ensuring water can drain away helps them turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmãa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛaawo mli kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ nu lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my tomato plants are getting too much water or not enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: If tomato plants lack water, their leaves turn dry, curl up, and drop flowers. If they get too much water, the leaves turn soft and pale yellow, and the roots rot because there is no air in the soggy soil.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ otato tso lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ baagbi, amɛbaakpã, ni amɛbaafɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu babaoo ba enɔ. Baai lɛ baatsɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ sũ ni efɔ lɛ mli.

english: Which direction should I push my cassava stem cuttings into the ground when I am planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ ashɛre ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Always plant cassava stem cuttings with the small growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward first before turning up, which wastes the plant's energy and leads to small, weak tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ dani amɛje kpo. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa bulb bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi edaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers mainly when they face extreme heat stress, dry soil, or lack nutrients. Providing steady water at the root level and light shade during the hottest hours helps the flowers stay on the plant to turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ titri kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ mli lɛ kpe. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I not put chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mitsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ he?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem can burn and kill the skin of the plant. Instead, place the fertilizer in a circle or line a few inches away from the stem so the roots can reach out and absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hewolo lɛ ashã ni egbe amɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo kooyigbɛ loo 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ he koni shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he ni amɛŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Does leaving dead pulled-up weeds on top of my soil hurt my growing crops?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni egboi ni mishiɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ awui?

english: Leaving dead weeds on top of the soil as mulch actually protects your crops. It keeps the soil cool, traps moisture from evaporating in the sun, stops new weeds from coming up, and turns into rich organic food for your soil as it rots.
ga: Shi jwɛi ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii buɔ onibii ahe diɛŋtsɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Tsi jwɛi heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ebatsɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars and fall armyworms destroy my maize mostly at night instead of during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fiteɔ mi-abele lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ moŋ fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide deep inside the center leaves or soil during the hot daylight hours to protect themselves from the sun and heat. They come out at night when it is cool and moist to feed heavily on the leaves.
ga: Asraafoi akuu mli ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai loo shikpɔŋ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ dɔlɛ he. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso ni edɔ koni amɛye baai lɛ waa.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground when I plant them in lowlands that flood during rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔji ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, well-draining soil to breathe and expand. When soil stays flooded with water for a long time, air cannot reach the roots, allowing rot bacteria to invade and spoil the tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛmu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: If I save seeds from the hybrid maize I harvested this year, why won't they produce a good harvest next season?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn ni mikpa afi nɛɛ mli lɛ to lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ amɛnáaa ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially created by crossing two specific parent plants to produce a high yield for one generation only. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities, resulting in mixed plant sizes and much smaller harvests if replanted.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛha yinɔ kome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛi kɛ yibiiwoo ni futuɔ amɛhe lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because full sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting shade crops like plantains or keeping larger trees creates a protective canopy that reduces heat stress until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni eda lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating with other crops gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ abɛi pɔtɛɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei krokomɛi tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts to help my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmeii koni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leguminous crops like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally enrich the soil with free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and lose their starch when harvested during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ starch kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During intense rain, cassava plants absorb excess water into their root tubers, which lowers the starch concentration and makes the tubers spoil faster after harvest.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛyaa shishifã lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is waterlogged, which prevents roots from absorbing essential plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I let all the shoots grow around the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwereɔ kui bibii waa beni mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain stem creates heavy competition. The suckers steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant, resulting in smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain kome he lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa. Suckers juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii.

english: Why do I need to put tall stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves open to sunlight. Maximum sunlight exposure helps the plant make food to grow large tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ niyenii ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages their pollen, causing the plant to drop its flowers to preserve moisture instead of developing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen lɛ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, so they quickly absorb the fertilizer, water, and space meant for your crops before the crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ he ni okɛbaakwɛ onibii lɛ oya dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together cause them to grow tall and slender with low yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ shwiili ni amɛfeɔ shwiili ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete aggressively for sunlight, stretching upwards to reach light instead of using their energy to grow strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni oooshɛ nɔ koni enine ashɛ la nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ kɛkwɛ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ,.

english: Yellow leaves on lower maize stems usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for leaf growth. When nitrogen in the soil runs low, the plant pulls whatever nutrients it has left from its oldest outer leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛhaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to conserve moisture. When the midday sun gets too hot, pepper leaves curl inward to reduce their surface area, slowing down the amount of water escaping into the air.
ga: Baai akumɔ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi. Ehaa nu ni shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with broad leaves but produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from the soil or wet weather, it spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in its root tubers below ground.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmei lɛ naa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ woɔ shishifãhi a mi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my young crop stems grow thin and fall over when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, seedlings compete heavily for sunlight. Each plant stretches rapidly upwards to reach the light, making its stem tall, thin, and too weak to support its own weight.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋshii mli waa. Tso fɛɛ tso shwieɔ ehe oya kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ, eyɛ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsitsinɔnii lɛ nɔ.

english: Staking gets yam leaves up off the hot soil, allowing them to spread out and catch maximum sunlight to make food. It also improves airflow around the leaves, which prevents fungal diseases from spreading in wet soil.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni no haaa ŋmeii helai agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their blossoms without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from moisture stress, sudden high temperatures, or lack of insect pollinators like tiny midges. If the tree feels stressed, it drops flowers to save its energy for simple survival.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ he haomɔ hewɔ. trukaa hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ loo kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni bɛ Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi ashwie shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ ato.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots on the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi diji dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant cannot draw up enough calcium from the soil while the fruit is forming, often caused by irregular watering or dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai miifee lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo hɔmɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do small holes appear in the heart of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛkɛ kome?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central whorl of the leaf funnel during the day and feeds on soft leaf tissue at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. ni kɛ ehe teeɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ shwane mli ni eyeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji bibii gbɛkɛ

english: Why does putting fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop burn the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is made of salts that absorb water. If placed right against a tender plant stem, it draws moisture directly out of the stem tissue, causing the plant to dry out, scorch, and die.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ nu lɛ feɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he lɛ, ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi fã lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, amɛshãa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow root systems near the topsoil. When heavy rains soften the dirt, strong winds can easily pull those shallow roots right out of the wet ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ shishifã nɛ mi kuɔ we nɛ e kɛ zugba a yi mi tɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. mɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ oya lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is a major food source for leafy growth. It can happen when the soil is poor, when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients, or when fertilizers were not applied on time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa Ebaanyɛ eba mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ. aloo be mli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli yɛ be naa

english: Why do my maize plants produce thin stalks and tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them correctly ensures every plant gets enough resources to grow strong stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni he wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the warm afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks water from traveling up from the roots into the stem. Even though there is water in the ground, the plant cannot drink it, so it wilts under hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji shikpɔŋ hela ko ni haaa nu akajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya tso lɛ shishi. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu. No hewɔ lɛ, egboɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for a long time, especially in heavy clay or poorly drained land. Fungus grows in wet soils and attacks the roots, causing soft, smelly rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Fuŋ lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ ni etutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa egboɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites that feed on the soft underside of young leaves. Their feeding damages the leaf veins, causing them to twist and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Ha etsɔ ni ebɔle ehe.

english: Why do insect pests attack my cowpea field mostly when the crop starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ babaoo beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Insects like flower thrips are attracted to cowpea flowers because they contain sweet nectar and protein-rich pollen. The pests come to feed on the tender flowers, which can cause the flowers to fall off before forming pods.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ sumɔɔ cowpea fɔfɔii yɛ amɛmli nu ni mli eyi kɛ protein ni fa babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baaye. Enɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ afee.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, drought, or insect damage to the flower cushions. If the tree does not have enough moisture or nutrients, it sheds flowers to protect itself.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ akushin lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the fruit bunch becomes heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akutsei lɛ bafee tsiimɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that can easily be damaged by soil pests like root nematodes or stem borers. Weak roots cannot support the heavy weight of the fruit bunch, causing the tree to collapse in high wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akuu lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko ba.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and prevents leaf diseases caused by sitting on damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni ekɛtsi baai lɛ ahe helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni amɛtaraa lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my vegetables grow tall and thin with few fruits when I plant them under shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make food and form fruits. When grown under heavy shade, plants stretch upward searching for light, making them tall and weak, leaving them with little energy to produce fruit.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehe koni etao la. ha ekwɛ ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ ewoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni oye obua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava grow huge leafy stems but produce very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are too shaded, cassava puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ ehiɛ hulutsoo tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upward and look wrinkled during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites living under the leaves, but plants also curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much moisture in intense heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shi tsei hu shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkafite ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too hot, when soil moisture changes suddenly between very dry and very wet, or when insects fail to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why are the bottom ends of my ripening tomato fruits turning black and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efo mli lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering routines.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why is Striga weed spreading across my maize field and stunting my crop growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miigbɛ eshwa mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni eha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches directly to maize roots to steal water and food. It thrives in worn-out soils that have low fertility and lack organic matter.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite ni ŋmɔshi nibii faaa yɛ nɔ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants yield fewer pods when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cowpeas are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, space, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow long, weak vines with fewer flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsina ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ wain tsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why did my maize seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting after the rains came?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when the soil is overly soaked with water and lacks air, or if seeds are planted too deep in heavy soil where soil fungi can attack them before they sprout.
