ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ nu babaoo ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ tsɔ he ni shikpɔŋ mli ŋmeii baanyɛ atutua amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and growing thin in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni miifee bibioo yɛ mi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams sprout naturally when exposed to warmth and light after their dormant period ends. As the sprout grows, it drains water and nutrients out of the yam tuber, causing it to shrink.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ amɛwo hulutsoo kɛ la mli yɛ be mli ni wɔɔhe be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ sɛɛ. Beni sweet potato tso lɛ da Enɛ baajie nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sweet potato tuber lɛ mli lɛ. ha egbɔjɔ

english: Why do my maize and bean crops seem to grow much better when I plant them together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ fɛo waa kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ fee ekome yɛ saatso kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize. In return, the tall maize stalks give climbing bean vines physical support to grow upwards.
ga: Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do experienced farmers leave the roots of harvested bean plants inside the soil instead of pulling them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shiɔ amɛ ŋmei tsei ni amɛkpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛbaagbala amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bean roots have tiny bumps called nodules that hold stored nitrogen. Leaving the roots to decompose in the ground releases this natural fertilizer to nourish whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Bean shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ nitrogen ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a signal that the plant lacks nitrogen or is sitting in waterlogged soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving water drainage will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii loo nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to conserve moisture. By rolling up its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to stop water from evaporating too fast.
ga: Baai akumɔ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbu nu he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ.

english: My bean plants are producing plenty of flowers, so why are the blossoms dropping off without forming pods?
ga: Mi bean tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Bean flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from high midday heat or a lack of water during the critical flowering stage. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto flowers and make pods.
ga: Pea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ efɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni efee ŋmeii.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with very small or empty maize cobs instead of a larger yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Yɛ nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ najiaŋ

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases specific to maize to build up in the ground, lowering your yields over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What causes the middle leaves of my young maize plants to look like ragged holes were chewed through them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni atsɔ mli awo bu ni mli ewo muji mli?

english: This ragged damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls deep inside the center funnel of the maize plant and eats the leaves while they are still rolled up inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ ni efite nɛɛ baa. Efoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni eyeɔ baai lɛ be mli ni amɛkpã mli lolo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than my crops right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep root systems adapted to survive dry seasons. When the rains start, they absorb water immediately and grow rapidly, competing with your seeds before they even sprout.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ Amɛmɔɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya. Ekɛ odumɔwui lɛ yeɔ akaŋ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ po.

english: How can I tell that my maize is fully mature and ready to harvest so it won't spoil in my storehouse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize is mature when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and a tiny dark mark called a 'black layer' forms at the bottom tip of the corn kernels where they meet the cob.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ batsɔ ŋmãa ni egbi kwraa. Ni ŋmei bibioo ko ni tsuɔ nii ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘black layer’ lɛ baa ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ ashishigbɛ naagbee yɛ he ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ mli egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain trees grown alongside them to shield their delicate leaves until they are mature and strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ koni ebu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dried leaves or grass help them stay alive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, also known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, and prevents weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni otsĩ jwɛi ni yeɔ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is missing vital food in the soil, especially nitrogen, or that the ground is too soaked with water. Adding manure or the right fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmã tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get a steady supply of water, or when the soil lacks proper nutrients needed to support fruit development.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni he hiaa koni aduawai akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ madu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This results in weak, thin stalks and tiny corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa.

english: Why do crops grow much slower when I leave weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa blɛoo babaoo kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, leaving your plants hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: This damage is commonly caused by pests like the fall armyworm, which burrow into the central leaves of young maize plants and feed on them before the leaves unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ dani baai lɛ gbeleɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by flying insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii ni foɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in heavy soil for too long without proper drainage. When the roots stay completely waterlogged, they cannot breathe and begin to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ kwraa lɛ. Amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu ni amɛbaabɔi fitemɔ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant immediately, your seeds will sprout but then dry up and die before the regular rain pattern begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Odumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water and plant food in the soil, and their leaves block sunshine from each other, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋshii mli ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce the energy needed to grow large, healthy yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Baai ni hulu lɛ ewo mli lɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest since the tubers are hidden underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ejaakɛ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava lets you know it is mature when its lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, the main stem turns woody, and the ground around the stem base begins to crack open.
ga: Yucca haa oleɔ akɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso titri lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ tso. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, which is usually caused by excessive heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: What is making holes in the center of my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt behind?
ga: Mɛni haa bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ waa yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the maize plant during the day and feeds on the soft inner leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: This is often caused by soil diseases like bacterial wilt, which attack and block the plant's internal water pipes, preventing water from reaching the upper stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tamɔ bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni tutuaa ni etsĩɔ tsei amli nu paipii lɛ anaa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋwɛi tso lɛ he.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the hot sun will dry out the soil and kill the young germinating seeds before the real rainy season starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly if I leave them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors; they steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving your plants weak and hungry.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my farm growing so small this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa nɛkɛ afi nɛɛ?

english: Small crop sizes usually mean the plants are not getting enough nutrients from the soil or sufficient water during their pod-building stage. Soil testing, proper weeding, and organic manure can help your trees produce bigger pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu mli yɛ be mli ni afeɔ pod lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ kaa, kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete heavily for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough light and food to grow large crops.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii he akaŋshii mli waa. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso agbo ko akwɛ̃.

english: Why do crops on one section of my land produce smaller yields than crops on another section of the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soil quality and water holding capacity often vary across the same piece of land. Areas with thinner topsoil or poor drainage will yield smaller crops unless enriched with compost or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ bɔ ni nu lɛ baanyɛ ahi mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli tseee loo nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii aba. ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting enough rainfall during the growing season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ená nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can monitor your crops by checking their leaves; if leaves curl, turn yellow, or wilt in the early afternoon, they lack water. Moist soil a few inches deep indicates adequate moisture for healthy growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ onibii lɛ kɛtsɔ ebaai ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ, amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ. loo egbo yɛ shwane mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo mli Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli kwɔ inchi fioo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni mli ewo fɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do changing rainfall patterns affect the best time for me to plant my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ saa be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When rainfall timing changes, planting too early can cause seeds to dry up in the soil, while planting too late prevents crops from maturing before the dry season. It is best to wait until the first main, consistent rains settle in before planting.
ga: Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni aduɔ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baanɛ dani odu.

english: Will applying fertilizer give me bigger crop yields if the rainfall is very low?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo kwraa?

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve so roots can absorb it. Applying chemical fertilizer during a dry spell without enough rain can burn crop roots and waste your money.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight without shade. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shelter that keeps the soil cool and protects young cocoa roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ nɔ kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adumɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and fresh air to reach lower branches. This prevents fungal diseases and ensures the tree directs its energy into growing larger, healthier fruit rather than excess leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe baai ni fa fe nine.

english: How can I tell if my crops are failing because of poor soil or bad weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite?

english: Poor soil usually causes slow, stunted growth and pale yellow leaves across the entire season, whereas bad weather like a sudden drought causes previously healthy leaves to quickly wilt or drop off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni ehiii kwraa kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsutsu lɛ shwieɔ oya loo amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How can I distinguish between crop damage caused by insect pests and damage caused by dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛbaa kɛ nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Pests leave physical signs like holes in leaves, chewed stems, or visible insects, whereas dry weather causes uniform wilting, browning of leaf edges, and dry, cracked soil throughout the plot.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii, tamɔ bu yɛ baai amli, tsei ni atswa, loo kooloi bibii ni anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ uniform wilting baa. Baai lɛ ashishi ji asarasu. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops keep catching diseases even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛheɔ helai eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Just like a dirty house makes people sick, leaving weeds, infected leaves, and trash in your field allows pests and fungal diseases to multiply and attack your crops.
ga: Taakɛ shĩa ni mli ewo muji haa mɛi yeɔ hela lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. jwɛi ni baa ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ Kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ oyale mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa ni amɛtutuaa onibii.

english: Is it really necessary for me to clear rotten pods and dead branches away from my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni majie ŋmeii ni egboi kɛ tsei niji ni egboi kɛjɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, leaving rotten plant material on the field carries germs that spread to healthy crops. Removing them keeps the environment clean and stops diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baagbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaha shihilɛ lɛ mli atse, ni ebaaha helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Why shouldn't I use dirty or standing pond water to irrigate my young vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji loo ŋshɔ mli nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa mibii aduawai lɛ nu lɛ?

english: Stagnant or dirty water carries harmful germs and fungi that infect plant roots and leaves, causing rapid rotting and poor growth.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi loo ewo muji lɛ mli helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa efiteɔ oya ni edaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my crops in neat rows instead of scattering seeds all over the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Organizing crops in rows keeps the farm arranged, allows air to flow freely between plants, and stops crowded roots from competing for food and getting diseased.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atoɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. ni atsĩ shishifãi ni eyi obɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii kɛ hela he akaŋshii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get infected when they touch the wet ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ náa hela kɛ́ amɛta shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil contains dirt and fungal germs that easily transfer to plant leaves when wet; keeping plants elevated off the ground protects them from soil-borne sickness.
ga: Muji kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ahe baai amli oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji edɔ. Tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops suffer when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ awui kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overcrowded crops trap excess moisture and heat between their leaves, creating a damp environment where pests and diseases thrive and ruin the harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil so quickly when I dump all of it together in a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ fɛɛ wo tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Piling fresh produce tightly in an unventilated room traps heat and moisture, which spoils the grain and causes mold to grow rapidly.
ga: Nibii heei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsu ko mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmaa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ daa oya.

english: How does sweeping and cleaning my grain storage shed stop insects from eating my harvest?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi dumɔwui atoohe lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye midumɔwui lɛ?

english: Storage insects thrive in dark, dirty spaces with old food scraps. Keeping the storage room clean and dry deprives pests of hiding spots and starves them.
ga: Shed bugs yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, muji ni niyenii momo ni eshwɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oha he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ mli tse ni egbi lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ akatee amɛhe ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ.

english: Why should I stack my sacks of farm produce neatly on wooden stands instead of leaving them on the bare floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ ama tso nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Bare ground transfers moisture into your crop sacks, while organizing produce on one side on wooden stands keeps everything dry and prevents damp rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii kotokui lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo yɛ tso ni akɛdamɔ shi lɛ fã kome lɛ baaye abua ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers rot faster when damaged ones are mixed in with good ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ futu mli lɛ?

english: A damaged or decaying crop carries germs that quickly pass to healthy neighbors; sorting and separating bad produce protects the rest of your harvest.
ga: Tsei ni efite loo egboi lɛ hiɛɔ helai ni baanyɛ atsɔ oya kɛya akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Nibii gbohii ni ooojie ni ojara mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does some harvested rice become soft and sticky when prepared while other types stay firm and separate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa komɛi ni akpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ asaa he yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛmli gbalaa lɛ?

english: Different rice varieties contain different types and amounts of natural starch. Varieties with low starch amylose absorb more water during processing and stick together into lumps, while high-amylose varieties stay firm and separate easily.
ga: Omɔ henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei henɔi kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ srɔtoi. Starch henɔi ni amylose faaa lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ, ni amɛbua amɛhe naa. yɛ be mli ni amylose henɔi ni fa babaoo lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛmli gbalaa oya.

english: Why does a new high-yielding seed variety sometimes get lower prices in the local market than my old traditional variety?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jara baa shi yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ fe mi kusum mli dumɔwui momo lɛ?

english: High yield does not always mean good grain quality for buyers. Newer varieties might grow faster or yield more, but if consumers do not like their texture, thickness, or appearance when cooked, local buyers will pay less for them compared to familiar traditional varieties.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mɔ ni heɔ lɛ. Hei srɔtoi baanyɛ adara oya loo amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi kɛji akɛ nihɔɔlɔ lɛ sumɔɔɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɔɔ ha, bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha kɛ́ ahoo lɛ hu? Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ baawo nyɔmɔ fioo kɛ akɛto blema nibii srɔtoi ni ale lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested grains break and turn into small pieces when processed at the mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni akpa lɛ akumɔ ni etsɔ bibii bibii lɛ? Be ni atsuɔ he nii yɛ ŋtayaa he lɛ?

english: Grains crack inside if they are dried too quickly under harsh, direct midday sun or left too long in the field before harvesting. Drying your grains slowly on clean tarps in light shade keeps the grain structure solid so it mills into whole pieces.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ baagbala yɛ mli kɛji amɛgbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi. aloo ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa Dumɔwui lɛ ni egbiɔ blɛoo Yɛ tarp ni he tse ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, akumɔ fɛɛ mli bibii bibii.

english: How does leaving water in my rice field close to harvest time affect the final quality of the grain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mishi mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli nu lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ, ebaana ŋmãa lɛ naagbee su lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Leaving standing water in the field right up to harvest causes the plants to continuously soak up excess moisture. This leads to heavy, soggy grains that spoil faster and produce a thick, mushy texture after harvesting.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa ŋmaa ni tsii, ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop grains look thick and big on the plant but feel light and empty after threshing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ? Shi enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ mlɛo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli beni eshɛre ŋmãa sɛɛ?

english: Thick but light grains happen when the crop lacks key nutrients like potassium or suffers from heat stress during the grain-filling stage. The hull grows to full size, but the inside fails to fill up completely with solid starch.
ga: Afeɔ ŋmaa ni mli tse shi eyɛ mlɛo beni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo amɛnaa piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛ ŋmaa lɛ woɔ mli lɛ. Lɛlɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyashɛɔ elɛɛmɔ fɛɛ he. Shi anyɛɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa awo mli.

english: Why does my stored grain develop moisture and mold inside the bag even though I dried it before bagging?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ lɛ dani mikɛwoɔ baagi mli moŋ.

english: Even if the surface of the grain feels dry, moisture can remain trapped inside the core. When stored in sealed bags, this internal moisture escapes, creates water droplets on the bag lining, and causes mold to grow.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa lɛ hiɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi moŋ Shi ŋmɔtɔ ehi ŋmãa lɛ mli lolo. Kɛ akɛto kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli Nɛkɛ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ baajo foi. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ kotoku lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii shwereɔ

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my grain crop so it does not lose its quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni su akafite?

english: You should harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the field has turned golden brown and the grains feel hard when pressed with your thumbnail. Harvesting too early leaves watery grains, while harvesting late causes grains to crack and drop to the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmaa lɛ beni aaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛ́ okɛ oshishifa lɛ nyɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ahi dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akumɔ ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my recent high-yielding crop to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mitsei heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ dumɔwui lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved and hybrid seeds lose their special qualities after the first harvest. Planting saved seeds from these crops leads to uneven growth, unpredictable grain textures, and lower overall yields compared to buying fresh certified seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ srɔtoi lɛ laajeɔ amɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei nɛɛ amli lɛ kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa. Anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ bɔ ni ŋmaa lɛ yɔɔ ha. Ni yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why do crops harvested from one side of my field feel different in texture from crops harvested on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fa kome lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛsoro amɛhe fe tsei ni akpa yɛ fa kroko lɛ?

english: Uneven soil nutrients, patchy water drainage, or shade across a single field make plants mature at different rates. This leads to a mixed harvest where some grains are fully mature and dry while others are still immature and hold excess water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee Nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli etse. Aloo hulutsoo yɛ jɛmɛ fɛɛ. ni haa tsei daa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ Enɛ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni futuɔ he ni dumɔwui komɛi ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni amɛgbi lɛ baa. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui krokomɛi Amɛshɛko lolo ni amɛhiɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine.

english: Why do small sap-sucking insects in my field ruin the final texture and appearance of my grain harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ yɛ miŋmɔji amli, ni no fiteɔ miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ mli bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha kɛ naagbee bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Insects like paddy bugs suck out the liquid milk inside young developing grains. This damages the internal starch buildup, leaving behind discolored, misshapen, or chalky grains that perform poorly during processing and cooking.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ dumɔwui bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ starch ni ebua ehe naa yɛ mli lɛ. Shĩ dumɔwui ni ehiɛ su, ni efite, loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii kɛ be mli ni ahoɔ lɛ ashwie.

english: Why does it take researchers so many years to test and release a new crop seed to us?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ niiamlitaolɔi afii babaoo dani amɛkaa dumɔwui heei amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛjieɔ amɛhaa wɔ lɛ?

english: Researchers need to grow and watch a new variety across several years and seasons to make sure it can handle different weather conditions, pests, and soil types before it is safe for farmers to rely on.
ga: Ehe miihia ni niiamlitaolɔi akwɛ tsei heei ni amɛkwɛ nɔ. yɛ afii babaoo kɛ be mli koni ekwɛ akɛ ebaanyɛ etsu kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi ahe nii dani okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe afɔ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does the same crop variety grow tall on my neighbor's land but stay short on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ miiya hiɛ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ebɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops react to tiny differences in soil food, sunlight, and water. Even if it is the exact same variety, richer soil or better moisture on one plot will make the plant behave differently.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ srɔtofeemɔi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli niyenii, hulu la kɛ nu mli lɛ ahe nii, yɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ amli po. Shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo loo ni mli edɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers insist I use exact measurements for spacing when planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Measuring proper distances stops plants from fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, ensuring every individual plant gets enough food to produce large ears of corn.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ asusuɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haaa amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I plant them deep inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deep exhaust all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil before they ever reach the sunlight, causing them to die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of leafy branches but fail to show any flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ ejie fɔfɔi loo aduawai akpo lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to spend all its energy growing big green leaves instead of making flowers and tomatoes.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ tomato najiaŋ

english: Why do my cocoa trees keep dropping their flowers before the small pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii bibii feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, dry soil, or lack of shade. Providing living shade trees keeps the air cool and helps the flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo hulutsoo bɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves naturally when it gets dry to save water in their stems, protecting themselves until the rain returns to push out new growth.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛgbi koni amɛkɛ nu ato amɛtso lɛ mli. Buu ohe he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba koni ekɛtsi tsei heei kɛje kpo.

english: How do I know the correct measurement of fertilizer to give each plant so I don't spoil my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha tso pɔtɛɛ ko? Bɔni afee ni mikafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Using a fixed measure, like a small tin or bottle cap per plant, ensures the crop receives just enough food without the concentrated chemicals burning the plant's roots.
ga: Kɛtsɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa tamɔ kans bibii loo tɔ mli tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ tso fɛɛ tso mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni tsofai ni mli wa ni shãa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper crops stop growing well whenever weeds fill up the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni jwɛi eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like stubborn food thieves that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil fertilizer away from the roots of your pepper plants.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ niyenii julɔi ni yitsoŋ wa, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei ashishifãi amli.

english: Yam tubers rot inside the mound when heavy rains settle in poor-draining soil, creating stagnant water that allows fungal diseases to attack the yam.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji fungal lɛ tutuaa sweet potatoes lɛ baa.

english: My cocoa trees are getting sick, so why can't I just spray chemical medicine to cure them?
ga: Mi cacao tsei lɛ miihe hela. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ tsofai awo cacao tsei lɛ amli koni mikɛtsa cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Some cocoa diseases are caused by viruses that live inside the tree's system where chemical sprays cannot reach. Once a tree gets a viral disease, spraying won't cure it, so removing the sick tree is the best way to save the rest of your farm.
ga: Virus ni hiɔ tso lɛ mli he ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo helai komɛi baa. Kɛji hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ye tso ko nɔ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsaaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oye obua oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why does the government extension service ask us to cut down our infected cocoa trees instead of treating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ extension agency lɛ biɔ ni wɔfolɔ cocoa tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni wɔbaatsa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting down sick cocoa trees removes the disease completely from your farm so insects cannot spread it to healthy plants. Clearing out the old infected trees gives you a fresh start to grow strong, healthy new cocoa.
ga: Kakao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baajie hela lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kɛji ojie kookoo tsei momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, obaanyɛ oje kookoo tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ shishi.

english: Can crop diseases spread from tree to tree in the same way human sicknesses spread among people?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni gbɔmɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa gbɔmɛi ateŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, plant diseases can spread much like human viruses. Tiny insects act like carriers, sucking sap from a sick tree and transferring the infection to healthy neighboring trees when they move around your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tamɔ gbɔmɔ mli helai. Kplukai bibii tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Amɛmuɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli beni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛbɔleɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ.

english: If I cut down my diseased cocoa trees and plant new seedlings on the same land, will the new ones get sick too?
ga: Kɛji mifo kookoo tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ ni midu dumɔwui heei yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ani kookoo tsei heei hu baaná hela?

english: If you completely destroy the old diseased stems and roots before replanting, the new cocoa seedlings will grow healthy without being affected by the old disease that was on the land.
ga: Kɛji okpãtã tsei kɛ shishifãi momoi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ dani odu ehee lɛ, Kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa ni helai momoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ enaŋ amɛnɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant young cocoa seedlings right next to my old, dying cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi? Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni miigboi

english: No, planting young seedlings next to sick old trees is risky because insects on the old trees will quickly jump to the new seedlings and infect them. It is best to clear the old trees completely before planting new ones.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ yɛ tsei ni egbɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ tsei momo anɔ lɛ baaho oya kɛya dumɔwui heei anɔ ni amɛgbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie tsei momoi lɛ fɛɛ dani odu eheei.

english: How do I know it is time to cut down my old cocoa farm and start over with new trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mafo mi-kokoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ mli ni mije tso hee shishi?

english: When your cocoa trees stop producing good pods, show widespread leaf yellowing or swollen branches, and do not respond to regular care, it means disease or old age has taken over, and replanting new trees is the best step.
ga: Beni o-cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpai lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo niji ni efuu babaoo yɛ. ni etsuuu daa kwɛmɔ he nii No tsɔɔ akɛ hela loo onukpayeli eŋɔ nɔ. Ni tsei heei ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Where should I get new cocoa seedlings to make sure they do not easily catch diseases?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maná kookoo dumɔwui heei koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ hela lɛ emɔɔɔ amɛ oya?

english: You should get certified hybrid seedlings from official government seed gardens or authorized extension nurseries, as these varieties are specially bred to resist common local diseases and yield more pods.
ga: Esa akɛ onine ashɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli nɔ kɛjɛ nɔyeli dumɔwui abɔɔ ko ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli loo dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko ni aŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, atsɔse nɛkɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi nɛɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How can I continue earning money if a major disease outbreak hits my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maya nɔ maná shika kɛji hela ko ni naa wa ba mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When facing a major cocoa disease, farmers can cut down infected sections in phases while planting fast-growing food crops like plantain or cassava on the cleared land to generate continuous income while new cocoa grows.
ga: Yɛ kookoo helai wuji lɛ ahiɛ lɛ Okwaafoi baanyɛ afo hei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. yɛ be mli ni aduɔ niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantain loo cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ koni aná shika ni yaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo hee lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Can dirty cutlasses and farm tools spread diseases across my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli nibii ni afolɔ kɛ muji baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã mi-kokoo tsei lɛ fɛɛ amli?

english: Yes, using the same cutlass or pruner on a sick tree and then on a healthy tree can transfer infected sap. Cleaning your farming tools with soap or sanitizer prevents you from spreading diseases around your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ tsɔne loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ yɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie nu ni hela emɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ helai tsu oŋmɔ mli nibii ahe nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ helai akagbɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What can I do to keep disease from moving into my healthy farm if my neighbor's cocoa farm is sick?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni hela akabote miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli kɛji hela mɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You can create a boundary buffer zone by clearing cocoa trees along the farm border or planting a barrier of plantains, which makes it harder for disease-carrying insects to cross from your neighbor's farm into yours.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee buffer zone kɛtsɔ cocoa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe lɛ ni oootsi loo gbɛtsii nii dumɔwui ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa waa kɛhaa kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ akɛ amɛaafo kɛjɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛba bo ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade from larger trees or plantain plants to act as living umbrellas, the harsh heat burns their young leaves and dries out the soil before their roots can establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei wuji loo plantains he hulutsoo be ko bɛ ni baaha etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai bibii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for dark green growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize the energy it needs to make strong, green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ daa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔji amli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the daytime heat gets too high or when the plant experiences water stress. Giving the plants consistent water and applying mulch around the base keeps the roots cool so the flowers can set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Ha tsei lɛ nu daa ni okɛ sũ awo amɛhe. Konii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water collects around them and starves the soil of air. Building raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain away easily so the tubers stay healthy underwater.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua amɛhe naa. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu shishi.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves. Spraying the plants with neem leaf extract or mild soapy water helps control these insects so normal leaf growth can return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ neem baa mli nu loo nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ. Koni ebaaha baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: When too many young shoots grow around the main plantain stem, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Leaving only two or three healthy shoots allows the main plant to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii daraa kɛbɔleɔ Plantain tsei wuji babaoo tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Cowpea plants have tiny nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When you harvest the cowpeas, that trapped nutrient stays behind in the ground to feed your next crop naturally.
ga: Cowpea tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni okpaa tsina ŋmei lɛ Niyenii nibii ni amɔmɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves up high to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the wet ground where leaf diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baa lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni baa helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants look wilted in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the intense heat of the afternoon, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. As long as the soil remains moist, the leaves will recover their strength once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ Baai lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ be mli ni gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow short and thin if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee kuku ni efee mlɛo kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks ensures your crops get all the soil nutrients needed to grow tall and produce a strong yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni otsei lɛ náa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning pale yellow starting from the middle of the leaf down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant is short on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base will help the maize regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my land help the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that stored nitrogen remains behind, acting as free natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ baakã he ahi shi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slanting angle instead of straight up and down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mawo ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanting angle keeps more stem nodes buried close to the surface, which encourages the plant to form multiple strong roots. More buried roots give the plant a better chance to produce a higher yield of large tubers.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa anyɛɔ afuɔ nodes lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shishifãi babaoo ni wa. Shishifãi babaoo ni afu lɛ haa tso lɛ naa hegbɛ kpakpa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible to make energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where they could rot or get diseased, allowing the tubers below ground to grow much larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo hela aba amɛnɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the plants compete heavily for root space, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives each maize plant enough food and sunlight to build a thick stalk and support large, fully filled corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shishifãi amli he ko, nu, kɛ hulu la mli waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ náa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa tsei wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantain trees planted next to them in the first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have very tender leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings the gentle shade and humidity they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo blɛoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the air gets too hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells without water. Mulching the soil to keep it cool and watering the plants regularly helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Aloo beni tomato tsei lɛ egbi trukaa ni nu bɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ kɛ nu ni awoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and look dead during the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni gboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni amɛgbooo lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil, causing the plant to wilt temporarily to protect itself. As temperatures cool down in the evening, the leaves will naturally stand back up.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baadamɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the underside of the leaf. Spraying the plants with a soapy water solution or neem oil clears these insects so new leaves can expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ajie amɛhe. koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly if I leave weeds in the farm during the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mishi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli beni midu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop roots are small and easily overwhelmed by aggressive weeds that steal water, light, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops full access to the soil's resources when they need it most.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraaa ni jwɛi ni juɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtutuaa amɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa onibii bibii lɛ naa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that scorch easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains or bananas alongside cocoa creates shade umbrellas that protect the delicate seedlings and keep the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Which specific part of a cassava stem should I cut and plant to get a healthy crop?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mafo ni madu koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should cut pieces from the mature, woody middle section of the stem, about 20 to 30 centimeters long with at least 4 to 6 visible nodes. Avoid using the soft, green top section because it dries out quickly and rarely produces strong roots.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ mli bibii bibii. Kɛjɛ tso ni eda ni tamɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli. Ekɛ aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eyɛ ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni anaa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi fã ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ he ejaakɛ egbiɔ oya ni efɔɔɔ shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my field is moist enough to plant seeds after the first rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔji lɛ amli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pick up a handful of soil from a depth of a few inches and squeeze it in your fist. If it forms a soft ball that holds together but easily crumbles when pressed gently, it is ready; if water drips out, it is too wet, and if it crumbles into dry powder, you need to wait for more rain.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ji inchi fioo ko ni okɛmimɔ otsitsi mli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kpɛtɛɔ he shi efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ fioo lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo. Kɛji nu ho lɛ, no lɛ edɔ tsɔ. Ni kɛji akɛ egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ powda ni egbi lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ babaoo.

english: Yam tubers grow large deep underground and need loose, soft soil to expand without resistance. Building mounds creates deep, well-drained topsoil that lets the tubers grow easily while preventing waterlogging, which causes yam rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa, ni amɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. ni ehe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa ni nɔ ko akatsi enaa. Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya, ni ehaa nu shwieɔ amɛnɔ. ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: What can I do to make my farm soil richer if I cannot afford chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: You can make natural fertilizer by mixing dried leaves, crop waste, weed scraps, and animal manure in a pile with a bit of water and letting it decompose into rich, dark compost. Spreading this organic matter over your soil feeds your crops naturally and helps the ground trap water during dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse, jwɛi ni eshwɛ, kɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni okɛ nu fioo baafutu mli lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ashiɔ lɛ koni egbo ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ogbala nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the roots will help the plant regain its bright green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kpɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground. Rotating your maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck sap from the undersides of leaves, or by viruses carried by these pests. Spraying your crops with neem oil or a mild soapy water solution helps kill these insects before they damage the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe nibii ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Ye obua ni agbe tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to stress from high heat, sudden dry soil, or irregular watering. Mulching the base of your plants with dry grass and watering regularly at the roots keeps the plant cool and stable so the flowers can develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Trukaa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi. loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi ni akɛ nu awo shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ atsɔ tomato.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if I leave them growing together in the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miha amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds act like food thieves by aggressively stealing soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your main crops need to grow strong. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your crops full access to food and light, leading to a bigger harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ niyenii julɔi kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni he hiaa tsei ni okɛ amɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii kɛ la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ kɛ kpamɔ babaoo baa.

english: If my cassava crops recovered from leaf disease last season, can that same farm get infected with the disease again?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ ehiɛ edɔ kɛjɛ nyɔŋ ni eho lɛ mli baa hela lɛ mli lɛ, Ani ŋmɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ baaná hela nɛɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, crops can get infected again. Unlike humans, plants do not build permanent immunity to viruses. If healthy-looking plants get stressed or if insects bring the virus back from a neighboring field, the disease will return.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aná hela ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ adesai lɛ, tsei bɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ helai anaa daa. Kɛji tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ miihao loo kɛji akɛ kooloo lɛ kɛ hela lɛ ku esɛɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Hela lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is there sticky liquid or ooze coming out of the bark of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ? Aloo nu ko miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cacao lɛ mli?

english: When liquid or sap oozes out of a stem, it usually means bacteria or fungi have infected the inside of the tree. The tree leaks fluid as a natural reaction to the internal damage and infection.
ga: Kɛ nu loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ helatsɛmɛi loo ŋmeii ebote tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ jieɔ nu akɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ kɛji emli nibii efite kɛ helai eba.

english: Can I spray chemical medicine to completely cure a viral disease on my pepper plants once they get sick?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo tsofai ni baatsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli lɛ amli kwraa yɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hela mɔ amɛ?

english: There is no chemical spray that can cure a plant once it has a virus. Chemical sprays only kill the insects like whiteflies or aphids that spread the virus, so removing infected plants early is the best way to protect the rest of your farm.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni baanyɛ atsa tsei ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ mra. No hewɔ lɛ eji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ obu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees keep showing swollen branches even after I cut off the sick parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso momo lɛ niji ni efuu lolo yɛ be mli ni mifo fãi ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Swollen shoot disease is caused by a virus that lives inside the entire sap system of the tree, including the trunk and roots. Cutting off branches leaves the virus alive inside the rest of the tree, so it will keep showing symptoms until the entire tree is removed.
ga: Virus ko ni hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ bud swollen hela lɛ baa. Nɔ ni fata he ji tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Niji ni afoɔ lɛ haa helatsɛ lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaaya nɔ ejie hela lɛ he okadii akpo kɛyashi abaajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does a crop disease keep coming back on my land year after year even when I clear the farm and plant new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni midu dumɔwui heei moŋ.

english: Many disease germs and fungal spores can survive hidden in the soil or in leftover crop waste for several seasons. When you plant fresh crops, these soil germs wake up and infect the new plants.
ga: Fungal pathogens kɛ spores babaoo baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ sũ mli loo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli bei babaoo. Beni oduɔ tsei heei Nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai nɛɛ teɔ shi ni amɛhaa tsei heei yeɔ hela.

english: Why do my tomato plants seem to catch diseases suddenly when a long dry spell or heat starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni hɔmɔ loo latsaa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ yeɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: When plants do not get enough water, their natural defense system becomes very weak. Just like a hungry or tired person gets sick easily, water-stressed plants allow hidden or mild infections to quickly take over.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kwraa. Taakɛ mɛi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ loo etɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná hela oya lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo okadii bibii anɔ oya.

english: If my cassava plant survived a disease and looks healthy now, can I safely cut stems from it to plant next season?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ ye hela lɛ nɔ kunim ni amɛfee tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bianɛ. Ani manyɛ mafo mi-cassava tso lɛ shweshweeshwe koni madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is risky because plants can carry viruses inside them without showing severe symptoms. Using stem cuttings from a plant that was previously sick can transfer the hidden virus straight into your new farm field.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ hela lɛ awo mli ni amɛjieee okadii ni mli wa kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ tsutsu lɛ amli ŋmeii ni afo lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ aya oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do crops that do not get enough fertilizer get sick faster than crops that are well-fed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ hela mɔ amɛ oya fe tsei ni awo amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer provides essential nutrients that build a strong physical structure and defense system in crops. Without proper feeding, crops grow weak, making it easy for diseases to attack and spread.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ kɛ hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo baa ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛji akɛ ahaaa niyenii ni sa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ. kɛ helai srɔtoi baa Etutuaa mɔ oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: If my neighbor's farm has a plant virus, can it spread to my farm even if our crops do not touch?
ga: Kɛji mikutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei ahe hela ko yɛ Ani ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji wɔŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etaaa amɛhe po?

english: Yes, insect pests like mealybugs, aphids, and whiteflies feed on infected crops, carry the virus in their bodies, and fly or drift over to feed on your healthy farm, spreading the disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi tamɔ mealybugs, aphids, kɛ whiteflies yeɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ. Virus ni akɛbaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli ni efoɔ loo efoɔ koni eye nii yɛ oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli. ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ

english: How can I tell if my plant leaves are curling because of hot weather or because of a virus infection?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miihoso yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hewɔ loo hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Leaves curling from heat will usually relax and uncurl during the cool evening or after watering. If the curling is caused by a virus, the leaves stay permanently twisted, thick, and often turn yellow regardless of water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ latsaa lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ jɔɔmɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli loo beni awo amɛ nu sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ hela ko ji nɔ ni kɛ curl lɛ ba lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi daa, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni bei pii lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nu kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Why shouldn't I plant as many maize seeds as possible in my field to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting too close together forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of many big, healthy cobs, you end up with weak stems that produce tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, yɛ ŋmeii wuji babaoo ni mli wa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbɔjɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: When cassava plants are overcrowded, their roots compete under the ground for food and space. This causes the plants to yield thin, small tubers instead of large, heavy roots that sell well at the market.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ he ko. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shishifãi wuji ni tsii ni ahɔ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Is it better to have fewer healthy plants or many small crowded plants on my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooona tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ loo tsei bibii? Dense yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Having fewer, properly spaced, healthy plants gives you a bigger and better harvest. Properly spaced crops produce larger fruits or grains, while overcrowded plants stay small and struggle to produce.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni sɛɛ jɛkɛmɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ooona lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa bo ni okpaa nii babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii loo ŋmaa wuji. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo lɛ baafee bibii ni amɛbaaná nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ ahe naagbai.

english: What is plant competition and how does it affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei ahe akaŋshii? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Plant competition happens when too many crops share the same small area. They end up fighting over limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, which slows down their growth and lowers your overall yield.
ga: Tsei ahe akaŋshii baa kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ he bibioo kome tsu nii. Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dalɛ baa shi ni ehaa nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin when they are crowded together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo waa kɛji akɛ abua naa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another. The plants stretch rapidly upward toward the sky searching for light, making them thin and easy for wind to blow down.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Tsei lɛ shwie amɛhe oya kɛtee ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Ha efee mlɛo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akatswa kɛba shi.

english: How does planting too many crops close together affect the fertilizer I apply?
ga: Te tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When you have too many plants in a small space, they all grab for the same fertilizer at once. No single plant gets enough nutrients to grow well, meaning your investment in fertilizer gets wasted.
ga: Kɛji oyɛ tsei babaoo yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ Tsei fɛɛ baamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ shikome. Tso ko bɛ ni nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafee yaka.

english: Why do my crops dry up faster during a short drought when they are crowded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli beni mɛi babaoo eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Too many plants packed tightly together drink moisture out of the soil very quickly. When the rains pause, the overcrowded soil runs dry much faster, causing your crops to wilt rapidly.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni atswa lɛ baagbi oya kwraa. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why do diseases spread faster in my farm when crops are planted very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crowded crops trap damp air between their leaves and prevent breeze from passing through. This wet, warm environment allows plant diseases and fungi to grow fast and jump easily from plant to plant.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ akatsɔ mli. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni mli edɔ nɛɛ haa tsei ahe helai kɛ ŋmeii daa oya ni amɛjoɔ foi kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why should I remove some young seedlings if too many come up close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kɛji amɛfa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Removing extra seedlings, called thinning, gives the remaining plants enough room, light, and soil food to grow strong. If you leave all of them, every single plant will remain weak and unproductive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni fa fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ thinning. Enɛ haa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ naa gbɛ, la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji oshɛrɛ amɛ fɛɛ oshwie lɛ Tsei fɛɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why do weeds seem to destroy my crops faster when my crops are planted too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛ́ adu miŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overcrowded crops are already weak from fighting each other for food and water. This makes it very easy for aggressive weeds to take over and steal the remaining nutrients from your crops.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ momo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo waa akɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ baaju niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean your maize plant is stressed. This happens when the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, isn't getting enough water, or is being attacked by pests like Fall Armyworm that eat the leaves from the inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ miihao. Enɛ baa kɛji tsei bɛ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ tutuaa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, strong sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the topsoil around their shallow roots. Keeping shade trees or intercropping with plantains creates a cool environment that protects the cocoa until it grows strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni bɔle shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ ahe lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ wo hulutsoo mli loo akɛ plantains wo mli lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa.

english: What causes my cassava roots to remain very thin even after a full year in the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo tamɔ nɛkɛ beni mikɛ afi muu fɛɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin if the soil is packed too hard for them to expand, or if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium. Tilling the soil well to loosen it and planting in fertile ground gives the roots room to swell and grow thick.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni enyɛŋ egbɛ eshwa.
