Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootsu he nii jogbaŋŋ koni eha egbɔjɔ ni odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii nɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛfu ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually stop them from growing well?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akpa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and fertilizers from the soil before your crop's roots can reach them. They also grow tall quickly, blocking sunlight that your crops need to make their food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Amɛ hu amɛdaraa oya. Etsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa onibii lɛ koni amɛhoo amɛ niyenii lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die so quickly right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains flood the soil and reduce air around the root system, allowing soil diseases like fungal or bacterial wilt to infect the roots. Once infected, the plant's internal water pipes get blocked, causing it to wilt rapidly even when the soil is wet.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai tamɔ fungal wilt loo bacteria wilt lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ Nu paipii ni yɔɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ mli lɛ etsi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ sũ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ, tso lɛ gboɔ oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my crop roll up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense to save water during high heat. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun and wind, preventing water from evaporating out of the plant too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ baa shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight with each other for light, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and leaves, resulting in larger, healthier crops and a bigger total harvest.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni okpa nii babaoo

english: Why does my land become hard and produce fewer crops after I burn the bush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa beni mishã mi jwɛi lɛ dani midu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning bush destroys organic matter and kills helpful living organisms that keep soil soft and rich. Over time, the heat bakes the bare soil, making it hard like concrete so water runs off instead of soaking in to feed your crops.
ga: Tsoi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, latsaa lɛ baashã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ. Ha efee nɔ ni wa tamɔ kɔnkrit. No sɛɛ lɛ, nu hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ mli koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant grow leaves instead of fruit. It can also happen if there are no bees or insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi krokomɛi bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully grown and ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts show maturity above ground when their main leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. You can check readiness by pulling up one plant; if the inside of the pods has dark markings and the nuts fill the shell tightly, they are ready for harvest.
ga: Peanuts daa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ beni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ hesaamɔ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ okadii diji ni ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa.

english: How does knowing the amount of rain that fell help me decide when to plant my maize?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni mile lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni makpɛɔ miyiŋ yɛ be ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa lɛ he?

english: Tracking rainfall levels lets you know when the soil has absorbed enough moisture to support seed germination, preventing your seeds from drying out and dying due to a false start of the rainy season.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛdii yeɔ ebua bo ni oleɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ eŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ. Etsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee ni ejaaa hewɔ.

english: Why do my crops wither and stop growing when rainwater collects and stands on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ beni nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni edamɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air in the soil to survive. When water collects and cannot drain, it drowns the roots, stopping them from absorbing nutrients and leading to rot.
ga: Tse shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu buaa ehe naa ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Etsiɔ enaa koni ekaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ekɛ fitemɔ aba.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) shades the soil from the hot sun, which reduces water evaporation, keeps the root area cool, and maintains soil moisture for longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when they are exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, thin leaves that cannot handle direct heat. They require partial shade from nurse crops like plantains during their first few years to protect them from intense heat and moisture loss.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he.

english: Why do plants grown under heavy tree shade grow tall and weak with very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Plants use sunlight to make food. When they are in deep shade, they stretch upward searching for light, spending all their energy growing tall stems instead of producing strong branches and fruit.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Ekpãa ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Okɛ ohewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni okɛkwɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ moŋ fe ni ooofee tsei niji kɛ aduawai ni mli wa.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same nutrients and water in the soil while their leaves fight for sunlight, resulting in thin plants with small tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulb bibii baa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to local soils and have strong root systems that absorb water and soil nutrients instantly, allowing them to grow faster than newly planted crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ ehe kɛyaa he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is not getting enough nitrogen from the soil, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy, green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ naaa nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme atmospheric heat, dry soil, or irregular watering, causing the plant to protect itself by shedding flower growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa tsei buɔ amɛhe kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛhaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize plants while growing beside them.
ga: Cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tso lɛ niyenii be mli ni edaa yɛ emasɛi lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to harvest cassava leaves to cook, or will taking the leaves stop the tubers underground from growing big?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaabua ŋmei baai anaa koni akɛhoo nii? Aloo obaakɛ baai lɛ atsu nii ni okɛtsi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara?

english: Harvesting a few leaves occasionally is fine, but plucking too many leaves deprives the plant of sunlight energy, which slows down root development and results in smaller cassava tubers.
ga: Ehi akɛ oookpa baai komɛi yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Shi kɛ́ ajie baai babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hulu la hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmei shishifãi bibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava crop turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow and curled cassava leaves usually indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Uprooting and destroying infected plants early helps stop the disease from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ yucca mosaic hela. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ashishijee kɛ amɛkpatamɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean the plant is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miigbo?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of saving water to survive drought. The plant is not dead; its roots remain alive underground and will shoot fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with bushy green leaves but produces tiny underground roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen manure. Excess nitrogen forces the crop to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of building fat, starchy tubers below.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ fa babaoo. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tuber nɛ fɔ kɛ starch ngɛ sisi.

english: Which direction should I push my cassava stem cuttings into the ground so that they sprout properly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ ashɛre ŋmei nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Plant cassava stems slanted at a 45-degree angle with the growing buds pointing upward toward the sky; planting them upside down prevents the buds from sprouting correctly.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ji digrii 45, ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I leave fallen cassava leaves on the soil around my crops, or will they harm the field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmei baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ? Aloo ebaafee oshara kɛha ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Healthy fallen leaves act as mulch that protects soil moisture and rots into free natural fertilizer. However, if the leaves fell due to disease, you should clear them away to prevent spreading sickness.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni ehaa efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko. Shi kɛji akɛ hela hewɔ lɛ baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Esa akɛ ashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie koni hela akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How should I handle my freshly harvested cassava roots so they don't spoil before I reach major markets like Techiman?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsu ŋmei shishifãi ni akpa ehee lɛ ahe nii koni amɛkafite dani amɛyashɛ jarayeli hei wuji tamɔ Techiman?

english: Cassava rots within two to three days after harvest. Keep harvested roots shaded from direct sunlight, leave a short stem attached to prevent open wounds, and transport them to the market as quickly as possible.
ga: Cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Ha shishifãi ni akpa lɛ ahi he ko ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shi tso kuku lɛ ni ehi shi koni pilamɔi ni agbele lɛ akafee nɔ ko. ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ jara nɔ oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to harvest food crops from my farm before packing them for sale?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani akɛwo kotoku mli koni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Harvest crops early in the cool morning or late in the evening. Harvesting in the hot afternoon heat causes produce to lose water quickly, wilt, and rot faster during transport.
ga: Kpaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli loo gbɛkɛ mli. Nikpamɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, egbɔjɔɔ ni egboɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do snails thrive better under leafy crops like plantain and cassava compared to open farm fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ plantain kɛ cassava shishi lɛ? Kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ ahe

english: Snails lose water quickly and dry out in heat. Broad crop leaves create shade and high humidity, keeping the soil damp and safe for snails to feed and grow.
ga: Snails lɛ fiteɔ nu oya ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be mli. Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii yeɔ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Can I feed cassava peels and leftover leaf scraps to farm-raised snails?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, snails feed well on crop waste like papaya leaves and cassava peels, but fresh bitter cassava peels should be dried or fermented first to remove natural toxins before feeding.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii le jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ tamɔ papaya baai kɛ ŋmei hewolo lɛ yeli mli. Shi esa akɛ agbi ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ loo afee amɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ajie adebɔɔ mli tsofai fɔji lɛ dani aha amɛ niyenii.

english: What is the best way for me to clear my land before planting without ruining the soil quality?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu nii ni mifiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii?

english: Clearing land by burning destroys good nutrients and beneficial organisms in the soil. Slashing weeds and leaving them on top of the ground as mulch protects the soil from the hot sun, keeps moisture in the ground, and feeds the soil as the plant material decays.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛtsɔ shãa nɔ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni afoɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii kɛshiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛji tsei amli nibii fite.

english: How should I prepare my field so that my crops do not dry out too fast during hot weather?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Loosening the soil properly and mixing in organic matter like animal manure or compost helps the ground hold onto rainwater much longer. This keeps your crop roots cool and moist even during hot, dry stretches.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ mli. Ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i, yɛ be mli ni edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei po.

english: Why should I plant my crops in neat straight rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni ja lɛ? Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, agbɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashwãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa.

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every crop gets equal space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko, hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: How deep into the soil should I plant my seeds to make sure they sprout properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: As a general rule, seeds should be planted at a depth about two to three times their size. If you bury them too deep, the seedling runs out of energy before reaching the surface; if planted too shallow, birds or heat will destroy them.
ga: Taakɛ eji mla lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee amɛdalɛ toi 2-3. Kɛji ofu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwu lɛ hewalɛ baaho dani eshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, okpoi loo latsaa baafite lɛ.

english: How can I check my crops regularly to spot diseases before they spread across my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli daa koni mana hela dani egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Walk through your farm a few times a week to check the leaves and stems for strange yellow spots, wilting, curling leaves, or unusual holes. Catching these early signs lets you remove sick plants before the disease spreads to healthy crops.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli ni okwɛ baai lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, ŋmɔtɔ, baai ni ebɔle amɛhe, loo bu ni yɔɔ srɔto. Kɛ́ omɔ mra be mli okadii nɛɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow, and what does it mean for their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni mɛni ji amɛshweremɔ lɛ shishinumɔ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is stressed—either from a lack of soil nutrients like nitrogen, too much or too little water, or pests feeding on the sap underneath the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Kɛji akɛ ejɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ nitrogen, nu babaoo loo nu fioo. loo kooloi ni baa koni amɛbanu nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: What steps can I take to protect my harvested grains from getting ruined by insects while in storage?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mabu midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ahe koni kooloi akafite amɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ he lɛ?

english: Thoroughly dry your harvested grain under the sun until it is hard before storing it. Store the grain off the bare floor in clean, sealed bags or raised granaries to keep out moisture, insects, and rats.
ga: Gbimɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛto. Kɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ato kotoku loo ŋmɔ mli ni he tse ni atsĩ naa koni ebu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ makwɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly allows soil pests and diseases to build up in that spot, and drains the soil of specific nutrients. Changing your crop type each season breaks disease cycles and keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe tsakemɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some crops grow better when planted together on the same plot while others do poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi daaa lɛ?

english: Some crops companion well together because one protects the other from sun or pests, or feeds the soil—like beans adding nitrogen for maize. Other crops compete for the exact same nutrients or share the same diseases, making them poor neighbors.
ga: Tsei komɛi hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ eko buɔ ekroko lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui ahe. Aloo ha ŋmeii ni tamɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ nɔ. Tsei krokomɛi kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ loo amɛyɛ helai ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. Feemɔ akutsoŋnyo ohiafo

english: How does joining a local farmers' group help me manage diseases and get better yields on my own farm?
ga: Bɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akuu ko ni mikɛ mihe wo mli lɛ eye ebua mi ni makwɛ helai anɔ ni maná yibii kpakpai yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Working with neighboring farmers allows you to share early warnings about pest outbreaks moving through the area, share knowledge on best farming practices, and pool resources together to buy supplies at lower costs.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa okɛ kɔkɔbɔɔi ni kɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa ni tsɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he lɛ haa mra. Jaa nilee ni kɔɔ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ he. ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ afee ekome koni akɛhe nibii ni jara waaa.

english: You must check the tiny bumps or 'nodes' where leaves used to grow on the stem. Make sure these nodes point upward toward the sky. If you plant the cassava stem upside down, the roots and shoots will struggle to grow, leading to poor yield or total crop failure.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii loo ‘nodes’ yɛ he ni be ko ni eho lɛ baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ nodes nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋmei tso ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ shi lɛ Shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baawa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo ni ehiii loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Should I leave all the small plantain shoots growing around the main stem or remove some?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashɛ plantain tsei bibii lɛ ashwie? ni kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔleɔ Tso titri lɛ he loo ajie fãi komɛi?

english: You should trim away most of them and leave only one or two strong suckers. If you leave too many shoots, they will fight with the main plant for food and water, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo amɛteŋ babaoo ni oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ Ekɛ tso titri lɛ baabɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food, or the soil has too much water drowning the roots. Adding proper fertilizer like NPK or manure usually helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there are no insects around to pollinate the flowers. Keeping the soil consistently moist can help save the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do I see small holes in my corn leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the top part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ mli lɛ anɔ

english: This is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that eats young corn leaves from the center of the plant. Treating the plants early with recommended organic or chemical sprays will stop them before they ruin the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper plants in the hot afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. Watering in the hot afternoon causes the water to evaporate before roots can drink it, and cold water on hot leaves can stress the pepper plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni nu ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha pepper tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to grow maize on the exact same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously removes the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the sun and keeps them off the hot ground, preventing disease and increasing your harvest size.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ he. Tsi helai anaa ni oha okpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a gentle rain, during the cooler parts of the day. Placing dry fertilizer on dry soil under hot sun can burn the plant roots and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: How does clearing my land with a tractor help my corn grow better than using a traditional hand hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ trakta tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe blema ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Tractors loosen the soil much deeper than hoes can, which allows crop roots to spread easily, absorb deeper soil moisture, and access more nutrients for stronger plant growth.
ga: Trakta baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kwraa fe ŋmei. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni anáa koni tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: If I use a heavy tractor on my land, will it stop my crops from growing well?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ trakta ni tsii tsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani ebaatsi miŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Heavy machinery can compact the soil if used repeatedly or when wet, making it hard for crop roots to breathe and push through, which can stunt plant growth.
ga: Nibii ni tsii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ akɛtsu nii shii abɔ. loo kɛ́ edɔ Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaamu ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei aka amɛdalɛ.

english: Does ploughing my farm with a machine make the soil dry out faster during dry weather?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Deep ploughing exposes wet underground soil to the air and heat, causing water to evaporate faster, so crops may need mulch to keep the soil moist.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ baa. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya No hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ ehe baahia ni awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young crops wash away easily after heavy rain on land cleared by a tractor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni traktɔi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Machine clearing removes all root cover and loosens topsoil, making it easier for heavy rain to wash away the fertile top layer along with small plants if soil barriers aren't built.
ga: Mashiŋ ni akɛfɔɔ nii ahe lɛ jieɔ shishifãi fɛɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho ŋwɛi ŋta ni baa nii lɛ kɛ tsei bibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ gbɛtsii nii ko bɛ ni abɔ

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bigger when the ground is deeply loosened before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa waa beni ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ lɛ?

english: Soft, deeply tilled soil gives root crops free space to expand without pressing against hard dirt, allowing the tubers to grow longer and thicker.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkumɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa yitso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my seeds taking so long to sprout after planting them in soft, ploughed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If seeds sink too deep into freshly ploughed soil, they run out of energy trying to push up to the surface before they ever reach sunlight.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bote shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ehee lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, Ehewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be mli ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ egbɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do weeds sprout so quickly right next to my crops after I plough the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe beni mitsu he nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Ploughing turns over the soil and brings old weed seeds up to the surface where sunlight and rainwater trigger them to grow quickly alongside your crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ kɛ jwɛi dumɔwui momo ni okɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la kɛ nugbɔ woɔ amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara oya kɛfata oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava in straight rows instead of scattering them like I used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja mli yɛ ŋmei ni makwɛ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Straight rows ensure every crop gets equal sunlight and air, stops roots from fighting for space, and makes it easy to weed without stepping on plants.
ga: Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Etsiɔ shishifãi anaa koni amɛkaye he ko he akaŋ. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni anaa tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even though I prepared the land with modern machinery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsɔnei esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, which tilling alone cannot add; crops still need fertilizers or manure to stay green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. ni ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ nyɛŋ aha eya hiɛ. Dumɔwui hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: Can I still plant beans together with my maize if I prepare the land with a tractor?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ trakta saa shikpɔŋ lɛ Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa lolo?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is great because beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil to help your maize grow.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua oŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which acts like food for the plant, or that the soil is waterlogged and choking the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer will help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the vegetables I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe aduawai ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally tough and strong. They can absorb water and food from the soil much faster than domesticated crops, which is why you must clear them early so they do not starve your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ tsei ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ojie amɛ mra lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshinii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and wither when there is full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight because their roots are not deep enough to draw sufficient moisture. Planting food crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture, protecting the young trees until they grow strong.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to manufacture food for the developing tubers beneath the soil. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight while keeping them off damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ekɛ ehe akabɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in the middle from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip in an inverted 'V' shape indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost around the base of the maize will restore its green color and health.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ ‘V’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ Abɛi tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaha abɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Why did my fertilizer burn and kill my crops after I placed it right next to the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-fertilizer lɛ shãa ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is high in salts, which can pull water out of plant stems and roots if touched directly. Fertilizer should always be applied in a ring or line a few inches away from the stem so roots can absorb it safely through the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmei fa babaoo. ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi amli kɛji amɛbashɛ he tɛ̃ɛ Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋwɛi loo line mli ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller maize harvests every time I plant on the same plot without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops like maize continuously pull specific nutrients out of the soil. Planting maize repeatedly without adding compost or rotating with leguminous crops, like cowpeas or groundnuts, exhausts the soil's nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite.

english: Why did a high-yield seed variety perform poorly on my land even though it worked well on a demonstration farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔji amli moŋ.

english: Seed performance depends on specific soil conditions, rainfall, and management. A new seed variety may fail if your field has different soil fertility or water levels, which is why testing a small patch first helps you learn if your land needs soil improvements.
ga: Dumɔwui anitsumɔ damɔ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nifeemɔi pɔtɛɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui heei baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse loo nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ srɔtoi. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni aka hei bibii akwɛɔ Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ehe ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when we get heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and starves the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small worms inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ yɛ bu komɛi. Yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which hides inside the leaves and eats the growing heart of the maize plant. Applying recommended organic or chemical treatments directly into the plant's central funnel early in the morning destroys them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ baai lɛ amli ni eyeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ wo mli leebi lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Extreme heat and erratic watering stress tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to survive. Giving tomatoes consistent water at the root level and protecting them during intense heat periods helps flowers develop into healthy fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛbai lɛ amɛshwie shi koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni abu tomato lɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and produce small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, competing directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to yield heavily.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni jieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to build healthy leaves. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient out of the soil, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma baai ni wa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná su ni ji eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help the next crop I plant grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have a natural ability to trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest the cowpeas and leave the roots to decay, that trapped nutrient remains in the ground to feed your next crop naturally.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa tsina ŋmei ni oha shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, Niyenii nibii ni amɔmɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen but lacks nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leaves instead of food below ground. Using balanced soil nutrients encourages the plant to feed its roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji moŋ fe ni eeeha niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Niyenii mli nibii ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛshishifãi akwɛ̃.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot in the ground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when rain water collects around the roots in heavy soil without draining away, creating a damp environment for fungi to attack the tuber. Planting yams on high, well-drained mounds helps water flow away from the roots.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni efooo. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa koni ŋmeii lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu akabote shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding extreme dryness helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects. Checking under the leaves regularly and applying basic pest control remedies keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa kɛ shishijee gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my watermelons crack open on the farm before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when they receive a sudden, heavy soak of water after a long dry period. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, so giving your farm steady, regular water prevents this splitting.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo nu mli trukaa, ni kɛ́ egbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa, ni afeɔ daa lɛ baatsi mligbalamɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and wither when planted in open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot endure harsh, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade plants—such as plantains—to shield them from the sun and keep the surrounding air cool until their roots are strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsi hulu lɛ naa ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ajɔɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily before the bunches finish maturing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can be damaged by underground pests like nematodes or weakened by wet soil during heavy storms. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo stakes helps hold the plant upright under the weight of heavy fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes baanyɛ afite amɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ aduawai ni tsii ni tsii lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the tips of my rice leaves turning brown and drying out during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Brown, dry leaf tips indicate that the rice plant is losing water faster than its roots can take it up from the soil. Maintaining proper water levels in your rice field prevents drought stress and keeps the leaf tips green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu miifite ŋmãa tso lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni sa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hɔmɔ he haomɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ eŋɔli.

english: Young cocoa plants do not like harsh direct sunlight because their roots are weak and leaves dry out easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts as a shelter, keeping them cool and moist until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii sumɔɔɔ hulu la ni naa wa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbaai lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ Ha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Which crops are easier for my family to manage without needing to hire outside workers every week?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha miweku lɛ akɛ amɛaakwɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe nitsulɔi ni jɛ kponɔgbɛ daa otsi?

english: Root crops like cassava and sweet potatoes require heavy work mainly during planting and harvesting, but need very little daily maintenance once established. This makes them much easier to manage with family labor compared to sensitive vegetable crops.
ga: Shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei biɔ nitsumɔ ni wa babaoo yɛ dumɔ kɛ ŋmãa be mli. Shi kɛ́ adu lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa gbi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ akɛ weku nitsumɔ baatsu he nii kɛ akɛto aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe tsutsu lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my maize crops even when I clear the farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-abele tsei lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu nii moŋ.

english: Weeds are natural wild plants adapted to quickly steal water and food from the soil faster than domestic crops can. If you do not clear them early, they will starve your young maize plants and prevent them from developing strong stems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe shia tsei. Kɛji okɛ nibii tsuuu nii mra. Amɛbaahã hɔmɔ aye o-corn tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛbaatsi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in the same farm with my maize make the maize produce better yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa yibii kpakpai baa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has a natural ability to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This nitrogen acts as a free, natural fertilizer that feeds the surrounding maize plants.
ga: Cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam vines use their leaves to capture sunlight and convert it into food stored in the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground so they catch full sunlight and stay free from rot and ground bugs.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei amli. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: What happens if I leave my cassava in the ground for a long time past its normal harvest season?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava tubers will continue to absorb water and grow bigger, but the inside will become tough, woody, and lose its starchy texture, making it less soft for cooking and less valuable at the market.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baaya nɔ aŋɔ nu ni amɛdara. Shi emli lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa, tso ni ehiɛ powder lɛ sɛɛ baafo. Ehaa efeɔ blɛoo yɛ nihoomɔ mli, ni ejara waaa yɛ jara nɔ

english: Why do caterpillars attack the center leaves of my maize plants during the dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms target the tender, growing heart of the maize plant where the stem is softest and protected from heat. Warm weather helps their eggs hatch faster, leading to quick damage if not caught early.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ nɔ, he ni ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa wɔji ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya. Ekɛ fitemɔ baa oya kɛji akɛ amɔɔɔ lɛ yɛ be naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many yellow flowers but then the flowers drop off without giving tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo shi amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit if the weather is too hot, if there is a dry spell, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Flowers need moderate heat and gentle movement from wind or bees to turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, edɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni fa fioo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo ŋmeii ni tsiɔ amɛhe blɛoo lɛ he miihia fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: If I plant my crop seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of a larger harvest, you will end up with many thin, sickly plants that yield small or unusable fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookpa babaoo Obaagbe naa kɛ tsei babaoo ni hela mɔ amɛ ni egbɔjɔ ni woɔ yibii bibii loo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii.

english: Why am I advised to cut off extra shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, drain water and nutrients away from the main mother plant. Cutting off all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree keeps all its strength to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii loo suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ ashishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hiɛɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ mli ni ekɛwoɔ tsei agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when planted in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—their leaves burn easily and their roots are too weak for full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates a living umbrella that shields the cocoa from heat and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni fa. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize ears come out small and poor when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots compete fiercely underground for food and water, while their leaves block light from each other. Proper spacing gives every plant enough sunlight and soil nutrients to yield large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋshii mli waa. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ naa Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai ni miida lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, a critical nutrient that plants need to stay green and produce food. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores this nutrient to help the crop grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Groundnuts and beans are leguminous crops that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally feeding and restoring the soil for future crops.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ehe hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Holes in the center leaves of young corn are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the plant whorl. Spotting them early allows you to apply recommended remedies before the central growing shoot is completely destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ tso lɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii dani tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ akpãtã kwraa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When land stays flooded or waterlogged for too long, oxygen gets cut off, allowing soil fungus to attack the tubers and cause them to soften and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does placing dry grass around my tomato plants help them survive the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-tomato tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the sun off the soil, preventing water from evaporating so roots remain cool and hydrated.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni okɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulu la shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to sudden heat stress or a lack of water. Ensuring consistent soil moisture during flowering prevents the plant from shedding its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafo baai.

english: Multiple shoots growing around one plantain stem share the same root system and compete for nutrients. Removing the extra shoots leaves just one strong replacement sucker, ensuring the main plant produces big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ shishifãi kome ni amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome pɛ ni he wa ni baaye najiaŋ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce poor yields even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa yibiiwoo aba miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and have aggressive roots that steal water and nutrients from the soil. If weeds are left in the field, they consume the fertilizer meant for your crops before the crops can use it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji jwɛi ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Keeping some tall shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from heat stress while it grows.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ cocoa plantain lɛ ni oooha amɛ shade loo amɛdu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars chewing holes in the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender leaves in the heart of the maize plant. Inspecting fields early and using neem extracts or recommended safe pesticides will prevent them from damaging the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baatsi nɔ ni baafite he ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key food for growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer early in the season will keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans together with my cassava help my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving neighboring crops like cassava free plant nutrients without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Feemɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ tsei amli niyenii ni ŋmei bɛ mli. ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fataaa he

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy, soggy soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: How do I know it is safe to sow my seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Seeds should be planted only after the soil receives a few steady, heavy rains rather than after the very first light shower. Sowing in properly soaked ground ensures the seeds germinate instead of drying up in hot soil.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fioo be fɛɛ be lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: When maize is planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes the stalks grow tall and weak, resulting in very small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plantain stalk produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha plantain tso titri lɛ awo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen. Providing consistent moisture and gentle shade during peak heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli Ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to produce food that grows large tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves into the air to catch sunlight and prevents wet soil from giving the leaves fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛyamɔ hulu la lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa baai lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops when the rains are no longer predictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ be mli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni baa lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops need consistent moisture to germinate and establish strong roots. Planting after a single light rain can cause seeds to dry up and die, so it is best to wait until the soil is thoroughly soaked and the rainy season has fully settled in.
ga: Tsei hia nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ebote mli kwraa.

english: If there is very little water this season, how can I make sure the small amount I get actually helps my crops survive?
ga: Kɛji nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ nu fioo ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛhi shi?

english: Applying water directly to the root area of the plant early in the morning or late in the evening reduces evaporation from the sun, allowing the roots to absorb maximum moisture and help the plant get through dry periods.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu babaoo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up into tight tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural self-defense behavior to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve water and prevent itself from drying out in high heat.
ga: Abɛi baai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ he, ni ehaaa egbi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Most food crops need direct sunlight to make energy for fruiting. Under heavy shade, a plant stretches upward seeking light, using up energy it would normally use to grow big, healthy fruits.
ga: Niyenii tsei babaoo he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo yibii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛna la. Ekɛ hewalɛ ni kulɛ akɛbaatsu nii kɛkwɛ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow and falling off even though I am watering them constantly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Too much water fills up all the air pockets in the soil, effectively suffocating the roots. Without air, the roots cannot take up nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ayi obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if the soil becomes very hard and dry during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa waa ni egbi yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil makes it physically difficult for cassava roots to expand underground, resulting in thin, small tubers rather than thick, heavy ones.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haa ewaa yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ yitso ni mli wa ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop consumes the same nutrients from the soil year after year, leaving the soil drained and hungry. Changing crops each season gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Eheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛsaa ehe.

english: Why do my vegetable plants drop their flowers before any fruit actually starts to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat or sudden dry spells, because they do not have enough water or energy to sustain fruit development.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaha aduawai lɛ ada.

english: How does putting dried grass around the base of my crops help them stay alive during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass acts like a blanket that shades the ground, keeping the soil cool and locking in moisture so water does not evaporate quickly into the air.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: If I plant my seeds very close to each other, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete aggressively with one another for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, leading to crowded, weak plants that produce fewer and smaller fruits overall.
ga: Amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsei bibii kɛ bibii fɛɛ baa.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing much fewer pods now than they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo kwraa fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 30 years, their natural productivity declines, and they become more vulnerable to soil depletion and diseases. Replacing old, low-yielding trees gradually with modern varieties helps restore high pod yields on your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, nɔ ni ewoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baa shi. ni amɛyɔɔ oshara babaoo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite kɛ helai baa amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ tsake tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ fiofio lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha pod yibii babaoo aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so I don't spoil the beans?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akafite

english: Cocoa pods are ripe when their color fully changes—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting too early yields flat, undeveloped beans, while waiting too long causes beans to germinate inside the pod.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ kɛji amɛtsake amɛhe su kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuru lɛ baatsake ni etsɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in open sunlight without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under intense tropical sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa protects them from heat stress until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow direct light and airflow, which prevents damp conditions where fungal diseases thrive. It also forces the tree to direct its energy into producing more flowers and pods rather than excess leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akabɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ada yɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ hu koni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená baai babaoo tsɔ

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy periods in heavy shade. Clearing excess shade, weeding regularly, removing infected pods, and applying approved fungicides help control the rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shade ni fa fe nine lɛ jiemɔ Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. Jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ ŋmeii.

english: How far apart am I supposed to plant my cocoa seedlings when starting a new farm?
ga: Kɛji mije ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ Te esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni kɛ mi teŋ jɛkɛ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees should generally be planted about 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet) apart. This spacing allows roots and branches enough space to absorb nutrients and sunlight without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3 (naji 10 x naji 10). Nɛkɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa shishifãi kɛ tsei niji lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain on the same plot where I just planted young cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu kookoo bibii amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping young cocoa with food crops like plantain or cocoyam is beneficial because it provides temporary shade and food income. However, avoid aggressive spreading crops like cassava too close to the young cocoa stems so they do not compete for soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ni akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo kookoo duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ehaa hulutsoo kɛ niyenii he shika baa be kukuoo mli. Shi kɛlɛ, tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa, tamɔ ŋmei, ni ooogbɛ ashwã kookoo bibii lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni akatswa akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he

english: Why is it better to buy certified hybrid seeds instead of planting seeds from my own farm harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high yields, disease resistance, and early fruiting within 2 to 3 years. Seeds saved from your own harvest often lose these improved qualities and produce weaker trees.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii mra yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ sui kpakpai nɛɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What can I do to keep my young crops from drying up during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni midumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: Applying mulch—such as dry grass or fallen leaves—around the base of young plants traps moisture in the soil and keeps roots cool. Maintaining overhead shade trees also buffers young plants against harsh, dry winds.
