ga: Mulch, tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ bɔleɔ tso lɛ he. Tso bibioo lɛ shishi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ. Tsei ni akɛhaa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ hu buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow even though there are no pests on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or poor soil drainage around the roots. Adding recommended organic compost or specialized cocoa fertilizer can replenish the soil and restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil, or that the ground is waterlogged. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: How do cowpeas or beans help make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aha tsina loo ŋmeii aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot in the ground, they leave behind free plant food that feeds the next crop you plant, like maize or cassava.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shĩɔ tsei niyenii koni amɛkɛye tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them without draining, especially during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to run off easily and prevents root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. ni nu hoɔɔɔ mli Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya ni ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Tomato leaves curl mostly because of a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or due to extreme heat and dry soil. Controlling whiteflies early and keeping the soil moist helps protect the plants.
ga: Nɔ ni haa tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi hewɔ Mra Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put wooden stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso ama sweet potato tso masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves in full sunlight. Staking keeps the vines off the damp ground where they could catch diseases and ensures the leaves get enough sun to feed the growing yam tubers underneath.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Staking haa wain tso lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela baanyɛ aba lɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know which suckers to remove from my plantain trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmeii ni esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mi-plantain lɛ mli?

english: You should leave one or two strong 'sword suckers' with thin, narrow leaves because they will grow into healthy, fruit-bearing trees. Remove 'water suckers' with wide, broad leaves because they take food from the main tree without producing good plantains.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi ‘tso’ kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɔɔ mli ejaakɛ amɛbaada ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni he wa ni woɔ yibii. Jiemɔ ‘suckers’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛjɛ ohe be mli ni amɛnuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛwooo dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper flowers falling off the plant during hot weather without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ ni etsakeee pepper lɛ?

english: When pepper plants experience excessive heat and lack of water, they drop their flowers to save energy and survive. Mulching the base of the plant with dry grass and watering regularly keeps the soil cool and helps the flowers stay on.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do flowers fall off my young cocoa trees without producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop if the tree is stressed by drought, lacks shade, or is attacked by insect pests like mirids. Keeping young cocoa under partial shade from trees or plantains protects the delicate flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hɔmɔ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen tutua tso lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ wo tsei loo plantains he hulutsoo fioo ko shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and give a small harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds during the early growth stage ensures your main crop gets all the resources it needs to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ onibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ shweremɔ shishijee bei amli lɛ haa onibii titri lɛ naa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ agbo ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant my cabbage seeds in a small bed before moving them to the big farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu kaabii dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ dani mikɛya ŋmɔ agbo mli lɛ?

english: Cabbage seeds are tiny and vulnerable to heavy rain and hot sun. Starting them in a sheltered nursery bed lets you care for the fragile seedlings until they are strong enough to survive being moved to the main field.
ga: Cabbage dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ. Kɛ́ oje shishi kɛ ŋmɔ mli saatso ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and soft leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living umbrellas that protect the trees from harsh heat and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Pruning removes excess branches so that air and sunlight can pass through the tree canopy freely. This keeps humidity low to stop diseases from growing and directs the tree's strength into growing bigger cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli oya. Enɛ baaha hulutsoo be lɛ aya shi koni helai akakwɛ̃ ni ewo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ kookoo ŋmeii ni mli wa moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai babaoo baafata he.

english: Why do buyers care so much about how well I ferment my cocoa beans after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ susuɔ bɔ ni mikɛ mi-kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ he waa lɛ?

english: Fermentation develops the chocolate flavor and proper fat content inside the cocoa bean. Good fermentation changes the bean color from purple to rich brown and reduces bitterness, which makes the cocoa high quality and valuable to chocolate makers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ kɛ fɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa shi, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ejara wa kɛhaa mɛi ni feɔ tsokolate lɛ.

english: Why should I dry my cocoa beans on raised wooden mats instead of on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi kookoo ŋmeii yɛ tso nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying beans on raised platforms lets air circulate underneath, which dries them evenly and prevents mold. Placing beans on the bare ground exposes them to damp dirt, insects, and animals, which ruins the quality of the cocoa.
ga: O-beans lɛ ni ooogbi yɛ kpoku ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ amɛshishi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa. Kɛ́ akɛ kɔfi ŋmeii fɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa muji ni mli ewo fɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ shɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni no baanyɛ afite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting when pods are fully yellow ensures the beans inside have reached maximum size and fat content without germinating inside the pod.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Nikpamɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ kɛ fɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he ni amɛkwɛɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease known as Black Pod, which spreads quickly in dark, wet conditions. Clearing heavy weeds and picking off infected pods right away stops the fungal spores from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ waa kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ oya lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees suddenly look burnt and withered during the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by small insects called capsids or akate. They suck sap from young branches and leaves while injecting poison that makes the leaves shrivel and look like they were scorched by fire.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo akates lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei niji bibii kɛ baai amli lɛ ni amɛkɛ tsofa fɔŋ woɔ mli ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its strength to feed my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: When soil becomes weak, crops grow very slowly, their leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green, and the yield drops year after year. Adding organic compost or the right crop fertilizer puts missing nutrients back into the ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo waa. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛ́ akɛ organic compost loo tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting maize in the exact same spot every season result in smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haaa yibii babaoo aba lɛ?

english: Maize pulls the same specific food out of the soil every single time it grows. Planting it continuously in one place drains the soil completely, so rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans helps restore the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ebaakwɛ̃. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu hoɔ kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does clearing weeds around the base of my crops help them grow bigger fruits?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai wuji?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer that your main crops need to grow. Keeping the base of your crops clear ensures that all the nutrients in the soil go straight into feeding your main plant.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa onibii titrii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ oha tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa otsei titrii lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a major food source crops need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain stays on the field for too long and drowns the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and ensuring maximum sunlight exposure.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi helai anaa ni oha hulu la ni fa babaoo aba.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts pull natural food (nitrogen) from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps feed your maize plants without buying extra chemicals.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts gbalaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni eha ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe tsofai krokomɛi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the juices from the leaves and spread plant sicknesses. Spraying neem oil or recommended organic sprays early helps clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa lɛ Akɛ neem fɔ loo organic spray afɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛya.

english: Why should I wait to plant my crops instead of planting right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimɛɔ koni madu tsei moŋ fe ni madu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can scorch delicate young sprouts. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so your seeds don't dry up and die in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil lacks water, or when there are no insects around to shake the pollen inside the flower. Keeping the soil moist and avoiding heavy chemicals helps.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he lɛ Ha wɔfolɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems from my old farm to plant on a new piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that produced big tubers and showed no yellow or twisted leaves. Cut pieces from the strong middle part of the stem, about the thickness of a finger, with clear stem buds.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni wa ni eda kɛjɛ tsei ni woɔ bulbs wuji amli. ni baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ loo efite bɛ mli lɛ, afolɔ mli bibii bibii kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni mli wa lɛ mli. Eshɛɔ tamɔ nine bibioo ni eyɛ tso ni mli tse.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even if I give my crops enough water and fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds act like greedy thieves. They grow much faster than your crops and quickly steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops have a chance to take them up.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ Amɛdaraa oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la oya dani onibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why is my farm land giving me smaller harvests now than it did three years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii etɛ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops without putting manure or compost back into the ground, you remove goodness from the soil. Over time, the soil gets tired and hungry, so plants cannot grow as big as before.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ awooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Obaajie kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye lɛ. Tsei nyɛŋ adara tamɔ tsutsu lɛ.

english: How do I know how much land I need to clear to make a good profit from growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male shikpɔŋ enyiɛ ni esa akɛ mafo mli koni maná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ mli?

english: To make a profit, you must match your land size to what you can afford to manage with seeds, fertilizer, and weed control. Starting with one or two well-cared-for acres often yields more food and money than clearing a huge plot you cannot maintain.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni oná sɛɛnamɔ Ehe miihia ni okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ ato nɔ ni obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ atsu he nii lɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome loo enyɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ je shishi lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika babaoo fe shikpɔŋ wulu ko ni onyɛɛɛ okwɛ nɔ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow strong in one part of my farm but stay weak and stunted in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ fã kroko mli?

english: Soil quality changes across the same field. One area might hold water and natural organic matter better, while another spot may be hard, sandy, or lacking nutrients, which prevents crop roots from taking up food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su tsakeɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ekolɛ he kome baanyɛ ahi nu kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni ekroko hu baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is healthy enough for planting without paying for expensive laboratory tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ ni miwooo laboratori mli kaai ni jara wa lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ?

english: You can judge soil health by its color, smell, and life. Soil that is dark brown or black, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture, and contains living earthworms is fertile and ready for crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ha lɛ kɛtsɔ ehiɛ su, eŋɔli, kɛ ewala be nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ, ni fãa oya yɛ nine mli lɛ, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka yɛ ni Ewoɔ yibii ni esaa ehe kɛha dumɔ.

english: What can I do to improve my hard, worn-out soil before planting so my crops grow properly?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mafee shikpɔŋ ni wa ni efite lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu nii koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: You can improve hard soil by breaking it up with a plow or hoe and mixing in animal manure, compost, or leftover crop stalks. This loosens the dirt so roots can spread and helps the ground store rainwater.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaakumɔ mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ahe ŋmeii baafutu mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa muji lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and stop growing even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots without draining away. When roots stay trapped in waterlogged soil, they suffocate and cannot feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo nu yɛ he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. shishifãi ni nu hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo Kɛji shishifãi lɛ efo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli Amɛfoɔ amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye tsei.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even after leaving them in the ground for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ni fe afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose soil and plenty of potassium to swell up. If your soil is compacted tightly or missing nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall leaves on top instead of big roots underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ potassium babaoo he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛfu. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji yɛ ŋwɛi moŋ fe shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How does changing the crop I plant on my field every season keep my farm productive?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mitsakeɔ daa be lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ewo yibii?

english: Rotating crops keeps soil healthy because different crops feed in different ways. Planting beans or groundnuts after maize puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally, which feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ahaa tsei srɔtoi niyenii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni haa niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Will using a tractor to plow my field harm my crop roots or help them grow better?
ga: Ani trakta ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Plowing with a tractor opens up deep soil so crop roots can easily grow deep into the earth to search for water and nutrients. However, plowing when the ground is too wet can create a hard layer underneath that stops root growth.
ga: Trakta ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ gbeleɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛtao nu kɛ niyenii. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishigbɛ nibii ni wa aba ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ.

english: What machines can help me clear and prepare my overgrown land faster than using a cutlass and hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ tsɔne baanyɛ aye abua mi ni majie muji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii kɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii?

english: Motorized weed cutters clear bushes quickly, walking tractors help till small vegetable plots, and heavy tractors with disk plows turn over big fields rapidly, saving you weeks of manual labor.
ga: Motor ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ajieɔ brɔshi lɛ oya. Trakta ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduɔ aduawai bibii. kɛ traktɔi wuji ni akɛ diski ŋmɔji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji wuji amli oya. Ekɛ otsii babaoo ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ omanye.

english: How can government agricultural extension services help a small farmer like me access tractors for my land?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ nitsumɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua okwaafonyo bibioo ko tamɔ mi ni ená trakta kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Government agricultural programs establish local Mechanization Service Centers where small farmers can register to hire tractors, plows, and shellers at affordable, subsidized rates without needing to purchase the machines themselves.
ga: Nɔyeli okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo ko toɔ maŋ lɛ mli tsɔnei ahe nitsumɔhei ni okwaafoi bibii baanyɛ aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo mli koni amɛhe traktɔi, traktɔi kɛ shelɛi yɛ jara ni waaa ni akɛyeɔ abuaa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe tsɔnei lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so fast if I leave them in the sun for two days before transport?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii enyɔ dani mikɛmaje lɛ?

english: Tomatoes produce moisture and trapped heat after harvest; keeping them under direct sunlight speeds up natural decay and decay bacteria, causing them to go soft and rot within 24 to 48 hours.
ga: Tomato haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ehiɛɔ dɔlɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss from heat and evaporation when the ground is dry during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my cassava so the roots grow thick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei koni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Cassava needs reliable water when first planted so its stem cuttings can grow strong roots; planting at the start of the rainy season gives the roots the moisture required to expand into big tubers.
ga: Nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ he miihia cassava kɛ́ adu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean the soil is short on nitrogen. The plant copes by pulling nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsuɔ enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai ni miida lolo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Extreme atmospheric heat or dry soil stresses the plant, causing the flowers to dry up and drop before insects can pollinate them or before fruit can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani kooloi bibii nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ amɛ loo dani amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: What causes my yams to decay so quickly after I dig them up from the soil?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When yams get bruised or cut during digging, rot-causing fungi and bacteria easily enter the wounds, especially if the yams are stacked in warm, unventilated spaces.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atswa sweet potato loo afo lɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ, Fungus kɛ bacteria ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ pilamɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ato ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my garden crops stay short and produce small leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ afee kukuji ni amɛyɛ baai bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil food, stealing nutrients away and leaving your crops starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni oooju kɛya ni oha hɔmɔ aye onibii ni ogbɔjɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under direct sunlight; they need shade trees or plantains to protect them from direct heat during their first two years.
ga: Cacao bibioo lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa tɛ̃ɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are there small round holes all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabe baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually made by hungry caterpillars or beetles feeding on the leaves, which weakens the plant's ability to make food from sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bulɛ baa kaabeji baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it good for me to water my vegetable crops in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate before roots can drink it, and hot water drops left on leaves can scorch the plant; early morning or late evening is best.
ga: Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ. Leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are my crops getting sick now when this same seed variety used to grow easily without any disease years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ bianɛ lɛ? Beni nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ nɔŋŋ kwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo ni hela bɛ mli afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Over time, disease-causing germs and pests adapt to crop varieties, and changing weather patterns can weaken the plants, making crops that were once strong vulnerable to new infections.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, helai ni kɛ helai baa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei srɔtoi lɛ amli. Ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsutsu lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ helai heei baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my crops look green and healthy at first, but then suddenly dry up and die before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli, shi trukaa lɛ egbiɔ ni egboɔ dani akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Some diseases and pests attack plant roots invisibly underground while the crop grows; once the plant tries to produce fruits or leaves under heat, the damaged roots cannot support it, causing a sudden collapse.
ga: Helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi tutuaa tsei shishifãi ni anaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ tso ko bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii loo baai yɛ latsaa shishi Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua lɛ. ni kɛ gbee shi trukaa baa

english: If one corner of my crop field catches a disease, will it spread to the rest of my farm?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli koŋ kome he hela lɛ Ebaagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, crop diseases spread quickly through wind, splashing rain, farm tools, and insects moving from sick plants to healthy ones if the infected plants are not removed early.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ okwaayeli nibii anɔ. kɛ kooloi ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛji ajieee tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ mra.

english: When people say a crop variety is 'hardy', what does that actually mean for my farm?
ga: Kɛji mɛi kɛɛ tso henɔ ko ‘wa’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni no tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: A hardy crop variety is specially bred to survive tough conditions like poor rainfall, heat, or local pests better than regular crops, giving you a better chance of harvesting even in bad seasons.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni wa lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ, dɔlɛ loo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei foloi. Enɛ haa onáa hegbɛ kpakpa ni okɛkpaa nii yɛ be ni ehiii po mli.

english: Should I replace my traditional seeds with the new improved crop varieties being recommended?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsei srɔtoi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ atsake shishijee dumɔwui lɛ?

english: New improved seeds are usually bred to handle current challenges like new diseases and dry spells better than older seeds, though it is wise to try them on a small plot first to see how they perform on your land.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ naagbai tamɔ helai heei kɛ hulutsoo bei lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni etsɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ oooka yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ koni ona bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why am I seeing strange new insects and leaf damage on my crops that I never saw on my farm in the past?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ kɛ baai ni efite yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli ni minako yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be ko ni eho lɛ?

english: As local weather and rainfall patterns change, new types of insects move into new areas or multiply much faster in warmer temperatures, bringing new pest problems to your farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi tsake Kooloi ahenɔi heei Amɛbaafã kɛya hei heei loo amɛbaafɔ oya kwraa yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai heei baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: How can I protect my crops now that the rainy season has become so unpredictable in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ́ nugbɔ be ni baa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ bafee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ?

english: You can protect your yield by planting fast-maturing crops that grow quickly before the rain stops, or by choosing drought-tolerant crop varieties designed for low water.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni baakwɛ̃ oya dani nugbɔ lɛ baakpa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni afee aha nu ni baa shi lɛ ni amɛhalaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops seem to get attacked by diseases much more easily now than when I first cleared this land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni helai yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ oya fe beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Farming the same land continuously wears out the natural nutrients in the soil. Underfed, weak plants have a low immune system, making them easy targets for diseases.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be. Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni niyenii faaa lɛ bɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ. ni ehaa efeɔ nɔ ni helai baanyɛ atswa lɛ mlɛo

english: If a crop yielded well on my land last season, why shouldn't I plant that exact same crop in the same soil again?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ nakai tso lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously in the same soil allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific plant to multiply in the soil, causing worse outbreaks in the next season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ kɛ hela ni ehiii fe no po baa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my old methods of protecting crops from pests no longer working like they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛi momo ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mibuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Pests can build resistance to the same chemicals or control practices over time, which means you need to rotate your control methods and combine sprays with good field sanitation.
ga: Tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ama hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ loo nifeemɔi ni akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni otsake gbɛi ni otsɔɔ nɔ okɛ spray lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ ni okɛ hetsemɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afutu mli.

english: Why is it better to start my crop seeds in a nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mabɔi mi tsei lɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery acts like a sheltered room for young seedlings, protecting them from hot sun, heavy rains, and pests while they are weak so they can grow strong roots before moving into the open field.
ga: Nursery lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsu ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha dumɔwui bibii. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛgbɔjɔ lolo lɛ koni ewaje amɛshishifãi lɛ dani okɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli.

english: How does creating a temporary shade cover protect my young plant seedlings?
ga: Te be kukuoo mli hulutsoo he ko ni mafee lɛ baanyɛ abu mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A shade canopy acts like an umbrella that blocks harsh sunlight and keeps the soil cool and moist, preventing delicate young plants from drying out and dying.
ga: Shade tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Etsiɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: What are those tiny lines running through the leaves of my crops, and what do they do?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai ŋmeii bibii ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni etsuɔ?

english: Those lines work like small water pipes running through the leaf. They transport water and food back and forth between the stem and the leaf so the plant stays healthy.
ga: Linei lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nu paipii bibii ni tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli. Amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii yaa tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ ateŋ. Koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: What is the main work that roots are doing underneath the soil for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nitsumɔ titri ni shishifãi tsuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Roots act like an underground anchor holding the plant firmly in the dirt, while also spreading out like wires to suck up water and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋshɔŋlooi ni fiɔ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa tamɔ waya koni ekɛmu nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do cassava plants store so much food underground in their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants build up reserves underground to save water and nutrients for survival during dry periods, which creates the large starch tubers we harvest.
ga: Cassava tsei toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ starch ni wɔkpaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do tree crops like cocoa need a big spread of leaves overhead to form a canopy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa amɛyiteŋ koni amɛfee ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ?

english: A broad leaf canopy catches maximum sunlight for the tree to make food, while also shading the ground below to stop weeds from growing and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ ji he ni hulu la lɛ naa fe fɛɛ kɛha tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do vine crops like yams need wooden stakes to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wain tsei tamɔ sweet potato he hiaa tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Stakes hold the plant's stems up into the air like a frame, lifting the leaves off the damp ground to reach sunlight and prevent leaf rot.
ga: Tsoi lɛ fiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ asɛɛ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli tamɔ frem. Wo baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ ni akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why should I cut fruits and vegetables off the plant with a sharp tool instead of twisting or pulling them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ afo aduawai kɛ aduawai kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi loo ogbala

english: Cutting cleanly prevents tearing the plant's outer skin and damaging its inner stem channels, allowing the plant to heal quickly without inviting diseases.
ga: Kpojiemɔ ni he tse lɛ tsiɔ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ mligbalamɔ kɛ mligbɛ tsɔne lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ fitemɔ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ tsaa oya ni amɛkɛ hela baaa.

english: Why do I need to cut off dead or diseased branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni egboi loo hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Removing dead or sick branches cuts off the pathway for diseases to travel through the tree, allowing the plant to direct its energy into healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ foɔ gbɛ ni hela tsɔɔ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to leave space between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that the underground root systems and overhead leaves of neighboring plants do not fight each other for sun, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛ amɛyiteŋ baai lɛ akatswaa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii he akaŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong stems and green leaves, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm help my soil produce better crops later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny root nodules that capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi bibii. No mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight; plantains grow fast and provide tall, broad leaves that shade the young cocoa from intense sun and retain soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be trained on wooden stakes to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsɔse mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ koni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make energy for building big underground tubers; staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they can catch sunlight efficiently and stay safe from rot and pests.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔ hulu la jogbaŋŋ ni amɛha amɛhe akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long because the roots drown without air, creating conditions for harmful fungi and bacteria in the wet soil to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho nu mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why can paddy rice survive standing in flooded water when my maize would die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ je nu afua lɛ mli lɛ? Mɛɛ be ŋmãa gboɔ?

english: Rice plants have hollow air tubes in their stems and roots that pump oxygen down from the air, allowing their roots to breathe underwater while other crops drown.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ yɛ nu shishi yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi shwieɔ nu lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaves, which damages the leaf tissue and can pass viruses to the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ baa fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ muawai eshwã tsei amli.

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a water mold that thrives in cool, damp weather, spreading quickly from pod to pod when rain droplets bounce off infected soil or plants.
ga: Black pod ji hela ko ni nu mli ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔi shwie shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or dry, or if the soil lacks phosphorus, causing stress that forces the plant to abort the flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. aloo kɛji akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛfo fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during high winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can be weakened by underground pests like root nematodes or stem borers, leaving the heavy tree without an anchor when strong winds blow.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ shishifãi nematodes loo stem borers baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiiɔ, ni ebɛ sɛkɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up and turn yellow during long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up like tubes to reduce surface area and protect themselves from losing water in hot weather. Yellowing happens because dry soil prevents roots from taking up essential nutrients needed to keep leaves green.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ paipii amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni nu akafite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Yellow baa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off before producing fruit when the heat increases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes heat stress in pepper plants. To survive and conserve water, the plant sheds its flowers rather than using energy to develop heavy fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi ni amɛbu nu he lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafite hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why are my cassava tubers very small even though the leafy tops look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa?

english: When soil has plenty of nitrogen but lacks potassium, cassava plants focus all their energy on growing big leaves above ground instead of storing starch and expanding the roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ. Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai agboi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔɔ ngmlɛfia kɛ toɔ sisi nɛ e haa nɛ e sisi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do cocoa flowers drop off the tree instead of turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if the soil lacks sufficient nutrients, if water is scarce, or if there are not enough tiny midges (pollinating insects) around to fertilize the blossoms properly.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu bɛ, loo kooloi bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ (pollinators) lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of putting energy into producing large cobs, they stretch upwards to fight for light.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛwu amɛha la lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Beans belong to a family of plants that can pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby maize plants.
ga: Beans fata tsei ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell if the maize seeds I stored from my last harvest are still good enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: You can do a simple germination test by wrapping 10 seeds in a wet rag for 3 to 5 days. If 8 or more sprout roots, your stored seeds are healthy and strong for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni akɛbaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 nɔ. Kɛji shishifãi 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, dumɔwui ni okɛtoɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni ebaahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves and spread so quickly after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the lower leaves. The moist conditions allow the fungus to grow rapidly, creating spots and causing leaves to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ daa oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii baa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves get full of tiny holes even when I do not see large insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni bu bibii eyi kaabaji baai amli eyɛ mli akɛ anaaa kooloi wuji komɛi ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ?

english: Tiny caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae feed on the undersides of leaves during cool hours or at night, leaving 'window pane' holes without easily being seen during hot daytime hours.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ diamondback moth larvae lɛ yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi gbɛkɛ loo gbɛkɛ. ni eshiuuu bu ko ni anaa Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooofee ‘samflɛ’ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly in the barn before I can take them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if they receive small cuts or bruises during digging, or if they are stored in warm, poorly ventilated spaces where heat and moisture let rot-causing fungi thrive.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛná fãji bibii loo fãji bibii yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ adara.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. It often happens when the soil is poor or when heavy rains wash the nutrients deep beyond the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Bei pii lɛ ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ kɛha shishifãi lɛ.

english: How does spreading dried manure from farm animals on my plot help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi amli lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure improves soil health by slowly releasing rich nutrients and building up organic matter. This helps the soil retain water longer and provides a steady source of food for crop roots.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii mli nibii ni jara wa ni ejieɔ lɛ kpo fiofio lɛ nɔ. ni ebɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛha tsei shishifãi.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and easily scorched by direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that block direct heat, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Bɔni afee ni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves twist up into small curls and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni ekpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids that feed on leaf juices, or by viruses they spread. These pests stunt the plant's growth by damaging its tender growing shoots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ mli Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa kɛtsɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers dry up and fall off when temperatures get too high or when plants don't receive regular water. Extreme weather stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu daa. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ ashi efɔfɔi lɛ koni ebu ehe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers soft-rot underground when we get continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, the roots drown from a lack of air, allowing fungi and rot bacteria to invade the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of trailing on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeenyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves lifted off the wet ground, exposing them to light while preventing leaf rot diseases.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potatoes yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni eeeha ená la ni ekɛtsi baa ni fiteɔ hela lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on a field before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmei yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, the stored nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next maize crop naturally.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpaa Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to yield smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Because weeds grow aggressively, they steal vital resources away from your main plants, leaving them weak and small.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli yɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ hewɔ No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ otso titri lɛ mli. Shi amɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛfee bibii.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly start eating the center of my maize plants during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bɔi mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ yeli trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be kuku ko mli lɛ?

english: Dry and warm conditions speed up the egg-hatching cycle of pests like the Fall Armyworm. The young caterpillars seek shelter and moisture inside the tender inner leaves of maize plants, where they feed rapidly.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ fɔɔ oya. Kplukai bibii naa wɔɔhe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli he ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii oya yɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai ni wa, eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, known as mulching, helps keep the soil moist during hot days, cools the plant roots, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat spell that can dry out the ground and destroy germinating seeds; it is safer to wait until the rains become steady.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm, which hide inside the plant's growing funnel and feed on tender leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. ni kɛ ehe teeɔ tsei lɛ agbɛi ni miida lɛ amli ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering, which prevents proper pollination and causes the plant to drop its blooms to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. ni ehaa tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots compete for water and nutrients in the soil while their leaves block each other from getting sunlight, leading to lower yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: How do I choose the best part of a cassava stem to use for planting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni hi fe fɛɛ ni adu?

english: The middle section of a mature stem is best because it has healthy buds and strong reserves, while the woody base is too dry and the top tip is too weak to sprout well.
ga: Tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ eyɛ fɔfɔii ni mli wa, ni eyɛ he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ hu ni ekɛtoɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ egbi tsɔ ni ŋwɛi naagbee lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry out and die when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that easily burn under direct hot sun, so they need shade crops like plantains to protect them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible, which helps the plant produce energy to swell the yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow slowly when I leave weeds growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital food, water, and sunlight from your crops, effectively starving the crop plants and preventing them from growing strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkadara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and curling even after I sprayed the recommended chemical correctly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ efɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Chemicals target specific pests or fungi, but if the crop was already damaged internally or is suffering from nutrient deficiency or water stress at the same time, spraying alone will not automatically bring the plant back to normal health.
ga: Tsofai lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi loo ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ mligbɛ efite momo loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo nu he haomɔ miipiŋ yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ hu? Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ haŋ tsei lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba hewalɛ kpakpa mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How does swollen shoot disease actually change the way my cocoa tree grows?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bud swollen hela lɛ tsakeɔ kookoo tsei lɛ adalɛ?

english: Swollen shoot is a virus that damages the tree's internal vascular system. This causes the stems and roots to swell, leaves to turn red or yellow, and ultimately stops the tree from producing pods before killing it.
ga: Top swelling ji hela ko ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli lá fãji lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ fuɔ. Baai lɛ feɔ etsuru loo ŋmɔŋ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani egbeɔ lɛ.

english: What should I do if I strictly follow your spraying schedule but my farm still shows signs of plant sickness?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mikɛ be ni okɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ nyiɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ? Shi miŋmɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ahela he okadii lolo?

english: When a recommended treatment regimen fails, it usually means a different disease or pest is present, the plant is stressed by soil/weather conditions, or the pest has developed resistance, requiring an officer to inspect and adjust the regimen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofafeemɔ gbɛ̀i ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela kroko yɛ. Shikpɔŋ/kɔɔyɔŋ shihilɛ haa tsei haoɔ. loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ eha amɛhewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ etee hiɛ Kɛtsɔ ni amɛbiɔ ni onukpai lɛ akwɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsaa hela lɛ mli ni amɛtsake mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Does a crop disease only destroy the leaves, or can it change how the fruit tastes and looks too?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ afite baai lɛ pɛ loo amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsake aduawai lɛ amli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha?

english: Diseases affect the entire plant system. By interrupting nutrient flow and photosynthesis, diseases can cause fruits to grow deformed, ripen prematurely, turn hard, or taste bitter.
ga: Helai saa tso lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo muu lɛ fɛɛ he. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ fotosintɛsis ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, helai baanyɛ aha aduawai lɛ afite, amɛshwere oya, amɛwa, loo amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: If I buy high-yielding cocoa seeds, will they always give me a good harvest even if my farm gets sick?
ga: Kɛ mihe kookoo yibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo Ani kookoo yibii baawo yibii kpakpai be fɛɛ be kɛji hela mɔ miŋmɔ lɛ po?

english: Good seeds give the plant the potential for high yield, but environmental conditions and severe crop diseases can override those genetic traits and ruin the crop if proper care is not taken.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai haa tsei lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Shi shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ kɛ tsei ahe helai baanyɛ aye nakai fɔmɔ sui lɛ anɔ kunim ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I save seeds from my best pepper plants this year to plant next season and get the exact same results?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-pepper tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ ato afi nɛɛ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ni maná nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Not always. Diseases can hide inside saved seeds without you knowing, and natural cross-pollination in the field can alter the seed's genetics, causing the next generation to behave differently.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, helai baanyɛ ahi dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli ni oyɔseee. Ni adebɔɔ mli cross-pollination ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsake dumɔwui lɛ amli wala yibii. ni haa yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ

english: I applied all the fertilizer on time, so why are my cassava tubers still very small?
ga: Mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ be naa Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo lɛ?

english: Fertilizer supplies food to the soil, but hidden viral diseases (like cassava mosaic virus) or drought can prevent the roots from absorbing or converting those nutrients into tuber growth.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Shi helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ (tamɔ cassava mosaic virus) loo hɔmɔ baanyɛ atsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ loo amɛtsake nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ amɛfee ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do healthy-looking plantain suckers taken from an old farm sometimes produce tiny bunches on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ plantain tsei ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ woɔ tsei bibii yɛ ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers can carry invisible microscopic pests like nematodes or fungal spores in their roots from the old land, which attack the new plant quietly and stunt bunch growth.
ga: Plantain suckers baanyɛ aŋɔ kooloi bibii ni anaaa amɛ tamɔ nematodes loo fungal spores kɛya amɛshishifãi amli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋkukuji momo amli. ni tutuaa tsei heei dioo ni ehaa tsei akuu lɛ dalɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without fruiting when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and destroys the viability of pollen, forcing the tomato plant to drop its flowers as a survival mechanism to conserve moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do crops on one side of my farm grow tall and green while the same crops on the other side stay short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fa kome lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fa kroko lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ kuku lɛ?

english: Soil quality, water drainage, and hidden soil-borne diseases are rarely uniform across a whole field; patches with poor drainage or soil pests will cause crops to behave poorly compared to healthy areas.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ efɔɔɔ kaa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai baaha tsei lɛ afee amɛnii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to grow strong green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the soil the basic food crops need to thrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee shishijee niyenii tsei ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my field better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special roots that trap natural plant food from the air and fix it into the dirt. When the plant dies, that trapped food stays in the soil, acting as free fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei aniyenii mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo Niyenii ni ekpɛtɛ he lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun and can dry out and die. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that create living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist during its early months.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why should I bother using wood stakes to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tso he hiaa mi koni mikɛwo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves produce food, which flows down into the ground to build much bigger and heavier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe fe fɛɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Enɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii kwraa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground even though the leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: Root rot happens when heavy rainfall sits in flat soil and drowns the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the roots stay dry enough to remain healthy.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and plant nutrients away from the main mother tree. By removing most suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones, the main tree gets all the food it needs to yield large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ jieɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni eshwɛɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tso titri lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: What causes my pepper plant leaves to curl up tight and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from soft new growth. Spraying the leaves with simple soapy water or neem oil keeps these insects away so new leaves can unfold normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei heei ni eda ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ewo muji loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe. koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ ajie amɛhe kpo bɔ ni sa

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stem before any tomatoes can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani tomato lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too hot or lacks steady water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and putting dried grass mulch around the base cools the roots and helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ sũ ni egbi shwie shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai amli.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even if I put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the support and nutrients you put into the farm without sharing them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ náa yelikɛbuamɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ amɛ aha.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get full of holes and small insects a few weeks after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ? Otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects thrive inside harvested maize if the grains are still holding moisture. Thoroughly drying your harvested maize under the sun until the kernels are completely hard prevents insect eggs from hatching inside your stored grain.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli kɛji dumɔwui lɛ mli edɔ lolo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii akui ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants burn and die when I plant them in an open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and tender roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a living umbrella that keeps the soil cool and humid until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why should I plant my cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmei?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose earth so they can expand easily into large tubers. Raising the soil into mounds or ridges loosens the earth and allows heavy rainwater to drain away so the cassava roots do not rot in waterlogged soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji oya. Kɛ́ awó shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the nutrient boost it needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I place dry fertilizer directly against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that will chemically burn delicate plant stems and roots if applied directly against them. Leaving a small ring around the stem allows rain or watering to safely dissolve and carry the nutrients to the roots.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsofai ni baashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ loo nu lɛ atsɔ shweshweeshwe ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does the soil in my vegetable bed dry out so quickly just a day after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbi kome pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil leaves ground moisture completely exposed to the hot sun, causing water to evaporate very fast. Covering the exposed ground around your crop with dry grass or leaves—known as mulching—traps soil moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya waa Ehaa hei ni agbele ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔ onibii. Enɛ (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching) lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.
