english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every single season and allows pests that feed on maize to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nitrogen to the soil and starves out soil pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni eyeɔ ebuaa abɛi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni egbeɔ sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly and stop producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck plant sap and spread viral diseases. Controlling these small sap-sucking insects early keeps the leaves healthy and open so the plant can form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helai amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli waa ni egbeleɔ koni tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do small insects bore holes into my harvested corn after just a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Storage insects like grain weevils thrive when harvested corn is still moist or stored in non-airtight containers. Thoroughly sun-drying grains until they are hard before packing them into clean, airtight bags prevents insects from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ mli edɔ lolo loo akɛto tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaafee shiŋŋ dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui ni mli tse amli koni kooloi akafɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from high-yielding hybrid maize to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid maize seeds are specifically bred to give a high yield only in their first planting generation. Seeds harvested from that crop lose their special vigor, resulting in uneven growth and much lower yields if replanted.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra side branches growing out from my tomato plant stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Allowing too many side shoots to grow forces the tomato plant to waste valuable food energy on excess foliage instead of flowers. Removing extra side shoots directs energy into growing larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ yɛ afã lɛ, ehaa tomato tso lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Tso yibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa aduawai ni dara, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to keep or plant other trees on my farmland when growing cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makpa loo madu tsei krokomɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni miduɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense tropical sunlight and dry out quickly. Shade trees shield young cocoa from direct sun, maintain soil moisture, and create a cool climate that allows cocoa trees to thrive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oha kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni haa cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ aba.

english: Can I grow my cocoa in an open field with no trees at all?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli kwraa lɛ mli?

english: While cocoa might grow quickly in open sun at first, full sunlight stresses the plants over time, dries out the soil during the dry season, and shortens the lifespan of your farm compared to shaded cocoa.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shishijee lɛ, cocoa baanyɛ ada oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ moŋ, shi hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni no haa ŋmɔ lɛ wala be lɛ feɔ kuku kɛ akɛto kookoo ni akɛwoɔ shade mli lɛ he.

english: How does having the right amount of shade help my cocoa yield more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo be ni sa ni mikɛaaha lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Proper shade protects cocoa leaves from drying winds and extreme heat, keeping the trees healthy year-round so they have the energy to produce consistent pods.
ga: Shade ni sa buɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ehaa tso lɛ mli waa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ bɔni afee ni ená hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛha ŋmeii ni afeɔ lɛ

english: Is it better to keep existing wild trees for shade or plant new small ones?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaahiɛ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ amli kɛha hulutsoo loo aaadu tsei bibii heei?

english: A mix of both works well. You can keep existing wild trees that are beneficial, but planting fast-growing small shade trees helps cover open spaces where no large trees exist.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Obaanyɛ obu koo mli tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe. Shi tsei ni aduɔ koni ekɛha hulutsoo fioo Ekwɛ̃ɔ oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hei ni tsei wuji bɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I decide which large trees to keep on my land and which ones to cut down before planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ tsei wuji ni esa akɛ mahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe? Ni mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ afo dani adu kookoo?

english: Good shade trees have high canopy leaves that let in filtered light and do not host cocoa pests. Trees that block all light, spread diseases, or steal too many soil nutrients should be removed.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi ni haa la boteɔ mli ni amɛhiɛɛɛ kookoo mli tsɛŋemɔ helai. shade tree Esa akɛ ajie helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa loo niyenii mli nibii babaoo ni ajuɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Will big trees already standing on my land steal food and water from my young crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni damɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ midumɔ nii bibii lɛ amli?

english: Yes, if there are too many large trees, their heavy root systems will compete with your cocoa for soil nutrients and water, which is why unwanted trees must be removed before planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji tsei wuji babaoo yɛ Amɛshishifãi ni tsii lɛ kɛ kookoo yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei ni ataooo dani adu lɛ.

english: What is the very first step I should take when starting a fresh cocoa farm on uncleared land?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mije kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: The first step is clearing brush and selectively thinning out the existing forest so you leave only the best shade trees while removing unwanted trees and thick undergrowth.
ga: Nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni esa akɛ ofee ji ni ojie brɔshi lɛ ni ohala tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ bo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, jiemɔ tsei ni ataooo kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why does clearing huge existing trees take so much more labor than planting small new trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ajiemɔ he hiaa nitsumɔ babaoo fe tsei bibii heei ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Large trees have thick trunks and deep root systems that require heavy tools, chopping, or controlled killing to remove safely, whereas small trees only require digging a small hole in soft soil.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni biɔ ni akɛ nibii ni tsii atsu nii, afolɔ amɛ, loo agbe amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni akudɔɔ nɔ koni ajie amɛ shweshweeshwe. Yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu bibioo ko kɛkɛ lɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli pɛ

english: How do I safely remove large, unwanted trees without destroying my crop soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie tsei wuji ni ataooo lɛ shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee mitso lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Instead of chopping down massive trees that can fall and damage soil or crops, farmers often girdle or kill unwanted trees standing so they dry up slowly and drop leaves naturally.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofolɔ tsei wuji ni baanyɛ agbee shi ni efite shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi fĩɔ tsei ni ataooo lɛ ahe amɛhe loo amɛgbeɔ amɛ koni amɛha tsei lɛ agbi fiofio. ni egbee shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why is land preparation considered the most difficult phase of starting a cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ akɛ eji gbɛ ni wa fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajeɔ kookoo ŋmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Preparing fresh land requires intensive physical labor to clear dense bush, cut down thick branches, dig up heavy stumps, and organize shade canopy before planting can even begin.
ga: Shikpɔŋ hee lɛ he saamɔ bi nitsumɔ ni wa koni ajie jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ, gbee tsei bibii ni tsii, ni ofee tsei bibii lɛ ahe mfoniri koni amɛná hulutsoo dani obɔi dumɔwui.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing ripe pods earlier than the normal season this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ miikpa amɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ mra fe bɔ ni eji daa yɛ afi nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees can produce pods outside their normal season due to unexpected rainfall patterns, warm temperatures, or sudden increases in soil nutrients that trigger early flowering.
ga: Cocoa tsei baanyɛ awo ŋmeii yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ hewɔ. hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ trukaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni haa fɔfɔi baa mra.

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvesting when their color changes completely from green or dark red to yellow or orange. Pods usually take 5 to 6 months to mature after flowering.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ heɔ nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 dani amɛdaraa beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Flowers often drop without setting pods due to dry weather stress, poor insect pollination, lack of soil nutrients, or insect pest attacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahewɔ. Kplukai ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ ehiii kwraa. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa

english: What happens to my cocoa crop if heavy rain falls right when the trees are flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ tso lɛ fɔfɔi be mli?

english: Heavy rain can wash away pollen, reduce the movement of pollinating insects, and physically knock tiny flowers off the trees, which leads to fewer pods developing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ pollen lɛ he. Ha kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ agbɛfaa lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa fɔfɔi bibii shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is deep and fertile enough for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ kookoo nɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, crumbly, rich in leaf litter, and deep enough without hard rocks so tree roots can reach down easily to absorb water and food.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli. ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni tɛi ni wa bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ tso shishifãi nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya.

english: Why do some cocoa trees yield lots of pods while neighboring trees on the same farm produce almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ wooo nɔ ni miihe ashɛ eko kwraa lɛ?

english: Yield differences happen because of varying tree ages, uneven shade cover, unequal access to soil nutrients, or hidden root diseases affecting specific trees.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ baa yɛ afii srɔtoi ni tsei lɛ eye lɛ hewɔ. uneven shade Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni anáaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo shishifãi helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni saa tsei komɛi ahe.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy conditions, high humidity, or when the farm is too bushy and lacks airflow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli. hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ Aloo be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut off extra suckers and side branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ suckers kɛ sɛɛ niji ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes useless suckers and extra branches so the tree does not waste energy on leaf growth, allowing more nutrients to go directly into producing big, healthy pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa niyenii mli nibii babaoo yaa ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ afeemɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Do mature cocoa trees still need shade trees around them, or is shade only for young plants?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia amɛ lolo ni amɛná hulutsoo yɛ amɛhe, aloo eji hulutsoo kɛha tsei bibii kɛkɛ?

english: While young cocoa trees need dense shade to survive, mature cocoa trees still need moderate shade to protect the soil from drying out and to shield leaves from harsh sunlight.
ga: Nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii taoɔ hɔɔŋ ni mli wa koni amɛhi shi. Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be ni sa lolo koni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi, ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: For how many years can a cocoa tree keep producing good yield before I need to replant?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani ehe baahia ni adu lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: A well-cared-for cocoa tree usually produces high yields for 25 to 30 years, after which production begins to drop and the tree may need to be rehabilitated or replaced.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afii 25 kɛyashi 30, ni no sɛɛ lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa shi ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni asaa tso lɛ loo atsake eko.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and curling up in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Providing shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa trees from heat and dry winds until they develop stronger roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli waa.

english: Why do my crops shed their leaves and stop growing during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe baai ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of plants very quickly. Shedding leaves is a plant's natural way of saving water so that the roots and stem stay alive until rain returns.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli oya. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi kɛ tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Is it better to plant my cocoa trees close together so I can fit more on my farm?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ aaadu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni gbɛ babaoo ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting trees too closely forces them to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows trees to grow bigger, stay healthier, and produce more fruit per tree.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni owo yibii babaoo yɛ tso fɛɛ tso mli

english: What causes the green pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa?

english: This rot is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark conditions. Trimming excess branches to let in air and sunlight helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do tiny insects like mirids cause so much damage to my cocoa trees?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids lɛ afite mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Mirids bite into young shoots and pods to feed on sap, leaving open wounds. These wounds dry out the branches and allow diseases to enter, which can stunt or kill the tree if left untreated.
ga: Mirids lɛ ŋmɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii koni amɛye ŋmeii lɛ. kɛ pilamɔ ni agbele naa Pilamɔi nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ekɛ hela baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbo kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is losing its power to feed my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dɔŋŋ?

english: When soil runs out of nutrients, crop leaves often turn light green or yellow, plants grow very slowly, and fruit yield drops. Adding compost or the right fertilizer puts those essential plant nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa. ni aduawai ni anáa lɛ ba shi Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha nakai tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even when there is enough rain for everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your main crops. Keeping the farm clear of weeds ensures your crops get all the resources they need to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ onibii titrii amli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can support. Drought, lack of nutrients, or a lack of tiny pollinating insects can cause the tree to shed excess flowers to save its energy.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu he nii. Hɔmɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa. Aloo pollinators ni bɛ fioo lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Pruning dead or crowded branches helps the tree by directing its energy into healthy wood and fruit, while also allowing air and sunlight to pass through the tree to prevent diseases.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ tsei kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli koni helai akamɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why should I replace my very old cocoa trees if they are still producing a few pods every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake cacao tso ko ni egbɔ waa lɛ, be mli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lolo daa afi lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow old, their production drops significantly and they become easy targets for diseases. Replacing them with new, improved varieties will produce much higher yields in the long run.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa ni amɛfeɔ helai ni helai baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight or excessive heat. They need shade plants like plantains or Gliricidia growing nearby to protect them from the sun and keep moisture in the soil until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo glicidia, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy for expanding the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, which also prevents foliage diseases and increases your harvest size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni ehaa onibii ni okpaa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: When too many young shoots grow around the main plantain stem, they steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from the main crop. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree yields a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii daraa kɛbɔleɔ Plantain tsei wuji babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ niji agboi ni tsii akwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape starting from leaf tips is a clear sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure early in the season will keep the crop green and healthy.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark and rotting before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani tomato lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium, usually caused by uneven soil moisture. Watering your crop regularly and mulching the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni afɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by high heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Providing light shade, keeping the soil moist, and avoiding excessive fertilizers encourages flowers to turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. hamɔ hulutsoo fioo Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛbaafata he lɛ he, ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting, curling up, and developing yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties from certified sources is the best way to protect your farm.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ Adumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ odaseyeli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: What is eating the central leaves inside the whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji teŋgbɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ a-rings lɛ amli lɛ yeli?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a destructive caterpillar pest. Inspecting your farm early and dropping recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts directly into the plant funnels will control them before they destroy the stalk.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni gbeɔ mɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye amɛnɔ dani amɛbaafite tso lɛ shishifã lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my main maize crop benefit my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mi-fodder ŋmãa titri lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for maize. Their ground-covering leaves also prevent soil erosion and stop weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa. Baai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to build low earth bunds around my lowland rice field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa sũ ŋtayaa ko mabɔle mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Earth bunds are small soil ridges that trap rainwater and irrigation water in the field. Rice thrives best in flooded or saturated soil, which keeps the roots moist and smothers competing weeds.
ga: Gɔji ji shikpɔŋ bibii ni ŋmɛɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ.

english: Why do people say I should plant plantains on the same farm with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi kookoo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct heat from the full sun. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa shaded and the soil cool while the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa lɛ.

english: Leaving selected big trees provides shade to keep the soil moist, protects your crops from severe heat and strong winds, and drops leaves that decompose into natural food for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni eda ni ahala lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu onibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ni baai ni fiteɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii haa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for soil nutrients like nitrogen, or they are getting too much water around their roots. Adding the right fertilizer or improving drainage helps them get green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli loo aha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if a crop on my farm is getting sick, and what should I do first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hela mɔ amɛ? Ni mɛni esa akɛ mafee klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Look out for leaves that are curling, changing color, developing dark spots, or wilting when there is water. Treat a sick plant immediately with proper pest or disease remedies before the sickness spreads to the rest of the farm.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi, ni amɛhe su tsakeɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nu hiɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo helai ahe tsofa atsa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. dani hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi

english: Will pruning or cutting off branches from my mature cocoa tree hurt the yield?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ aniji ni afolɔ loo ajieɔ lɛ baaná yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: No, pruning healthy cocoa trees actually increases yield. Removing extra leaves and dead branches lets sunlight and fresh air reach the stems, which prevents pod diseases like black pod from developing.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ helai ni baa ŋmeii lɛ amli, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa.

english: Why does my cassava yield small tubers when I plant it in hard, compact soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose, soft soil so its roots can expand easily under the ground. Hard soil traps the roots and prevents them from swelling into large, healthy tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia cassava bɔni afee ni eshishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa amɛfu ni amɛfee bulbs agboi ni mli wa.

english: If seeds are planted too close, the growing plants will fight with each other for food, water, and sunlight. This results in weak, thin stalks that produce small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why is it beneficial for my land if I plant beans or groundnuts alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛji midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally feeds the soil and helps neighboring crops like maize grow bigger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow poorly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds early makes sure your crops get all the nutrients for themselves.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell before the main rains begin. If seeds sprout during that brief rain, the young shoots will wither and die when the sun returns.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ be ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbiɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or the ground is waterlogged. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving soil drainage helps the leaves turn dark green and stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Most crops need fertilizer in two main stages: a base application during planting to help roots establish, and a second application (top-dressing) a few weeks later when the plant is growing rapidly.
ga: Tsei babaoo he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ: Shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ dumɔ be mli koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛma shi. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli (ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli) yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni tso lɛ daa oya lɛ.

english: Why are little caterpillars chewing holes in the center leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the tender leaves in the heart of the maize plant. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tswaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. Heavy rains in flat, poorly drained soil drown the roots and cause fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need to grow under plantain shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwui ashishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct hot sunlight. Taller plants like plantains provide shelter, keep the soil moist, and protect young cocoa until it is strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains haa wɔɔhe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa kɛha hulu la ni naa wa.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's maize harvest yield less than new certified seeds from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their yield strength and vigor in subsequent generations. Certified seeds bought from agro-dealers are specially produced to give high yields and fight off diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aba ni ekɛ helai awuu.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ koni amɛshwere Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my main crops right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to local conditions and can absorb water and nutrients rapidly. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light, water, and fertilizer away from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ejie nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Mulching the soil and maintaining steady, even watering keeps the plants cool and helps flowers develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomatoi baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ miigba enaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ ekwɛmɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni eha tso lɛ mli ajɔ ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build strong leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or leaves the roots standing in water for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ ashi shishifãi yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow much better when the field is kept flooded with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ nu eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties are adapted to grow in wet conditions where water blocks oxygen from reaching weed seeds, stopping competing weeds from growing while keeping the soil continuously moist for the rice roots.
ga: Atsakeɔ ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ. Ekpaa jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛha ŋmãa shishifãi.

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies and cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Big shade trees protect young cocoa from sunburn, keep the soil cool, and maintain the moisture the young plants need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ekwɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I remove some of the suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main plant. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main stem to produce larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ afee ŋmeii ni da ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when the soil stays wet for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When soil is soaked with standing water for days, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to suffocate and attract fungal diseases that rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii babaoo lɛ, Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Amɛhaa mɔ mumɔ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ tuber rot baa lɛ.

english: Yam is a climbing vine, and lifting its leaves up into the air allows them to capture maximum sunlight to produce energy for the tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing soil-borne diseases.
ga: Atomɔ ji wain tso ni kwɔɔ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulb lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Koni akɛtsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ anaa

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences extreme water stress. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save its own strength rather than feeding new fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ ni naa wa. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛhe miiwo wu lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha yibii heei

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies that feed on the leaf juices and transmit viruses. Managing these insects early stops the leaves from twisting and crippling the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛhaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafite.

english: Why is covering the soil around my cabbage plants with dry grass helpful?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi baaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle kaabii tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil under the hot sun, prevents weeds from growing, and keeps the soil cool for healthy root growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ waa

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the plant harvest ends and the roots decay in the soil, that trapped nitrogen feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ba naagbee ni shishifãi lɛ gboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, No sɛɛ lɛ Nitrogen ni aŋã lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, a main nutrient maize needs to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows maize-specific pests to multiply. Rotating your land with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts builds soil nutrients naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ ayiɔ babaoo. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of direct sunlight to make energy for growing big underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, exposing the leaves to sun while keeping them safe from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni akɛwoɔ hulu la mli lɛ nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abuɔ he shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) compete with the mother plantain tree for soil nutrients, water, and space. Pruning away weaker shoots and leaving just one or two allows the main tree to direct its energy into producing large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo (tsobii) kɛ fɔlɔ dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛtsɔ tsei bibii lɛ ni efoɔ ni eshiɔ nine kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: It is best to water early in the morning when the sun is low. Morning watering allows water to soak deep into the soil before the afternoon heat evaporates it, and leaves dry off during the day, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nu lɛ leebi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani shwane mli la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni baai lɛ baagbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus transmitted by them. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil solution or mild insecticidal soap can manage these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni jɛɔ amɛmli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem mu ni akɛwoɔ mli loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft leaf tissues of growing maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended pest control sprays will prevent them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ kooloi amli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water collects around them in heavy or poorly drained soil during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua amɛhe naa. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high, when water levels in the soil fluctuate unevenly, or when there is a lack of calcium in the soil. Maintaining consistent morning watering helps keep the flowers on the vine.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo be mli ni calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees near my young cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees shields the young cocoa leaves from heat and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps bring back their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do cowpea crops actually improve the soil for the next crop I plant on the same land?
ga: Te tsina tso ko feɔ tɛŋŋ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have tiny organisms on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. When the cowpea plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava growing tall stems with lots of big leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai wuji waa, shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or water, it puts all its energy into growing leafy stems above ground instead of storing energy in the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly from very dry to very wet, which stresses the plant and prevents flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and dry up when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct harsh sunlight damages their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture too quickly before their root systems are strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over so easily during strong windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni tswaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that cannot easily hold up the heavy weight of a maturing fruit bunch during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with sturdy wooden props prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni ekwɛ̃ ni tsii lɛ anɔ mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fĩ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaf, or from a plant virus carried by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ji kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ amli

english: What causes my yam leaves to get dark spots and die off early if I let the vines trail on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji miha wain tsei lɛ nyiɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ?

english: When vine leaves touch wet soil, fungal spores easily jump onto the leaves and cause diseases like leaf spot. Staking vines elevates leaves into the air and sunlight where they dry quickly and stay healthy.
ga: Kɛji wain tso lɛ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpe lɛ, Fungal spores lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ oya ni ekɛ helai tamɔ leaf spot baa. Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ehaa onáa hewalɛ

english: Why does my maize crop fail to produce full kernels if rain stops for two weeks during flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ wooo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ otsii enyɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most sensitive stage for maize. Lack of water at this precise moment prevents successful pollination, causing ears to form with missing or underdeveloped kernels.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa. Nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. Enɛ haa toi lɛ náa dumɔwui ni elaaje loo edarako jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why can swamp rice grow directly in standing water while maize rots in waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have natural air passages inside their stems that transport oxygen down to their roots underwater, whereas maize roots lack these passages and suffocate without oxygen in soggy soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ gbɛi nɛɛ, ni amɛmuɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I successfully grow cocoa trees in the Northern Region of Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ kookoo tsei yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Traditional cocoa trees thrive best in warm, humid forest zones with abundant rainfall, which are typical of southern Ghana. The North is generally much drier and hotter, making it very difficult for standard cocoa crops to survive and produce high yields without heavy irrigation and climate protection.
ga: Kusum kakao tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ko ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ Ghana wuoyigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ egbi ni edɔ waa. Enɛ haa ewaa waa kɛhaa kookoo tsei ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ akɛ amɛaahi shi ni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛji nu ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hebuu bɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantain or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from heat stress and keeping the soil moist so the roots can establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods this season compared to past years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo yɛ be nɛɛ mli kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: A decline in pod production usually happens when soil nutrients are exhausted, trees grow too old, or when rainfall is unpredictable. Diseases like swollen shoot and black pod can also severely reduce crop yields if left unchecked.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pod ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa. Tso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ, helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu kɛ ŋmeii ni efee diŋ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes an entire farm of cocoa trees to start drying up and dying?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ ni kookoo tsei yɔɔ mli lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ?

english: Mass dieback on a cocoa farm is commonly caused by viral infections like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, severe drought, or heavy infestations of insect pests called capsids that feed on tree stems and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa tamɔ kookoo mli fũu kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ gbele babaoo baa yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli. Aloo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ capsid ni yeɔ tsei akutsei kɛ baai.

english: How do I know if my crop is suffering from poor soil or from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo hela?

english: If your crop is weak and pale across the whole farm even during rainy seasons, the soil likely lacks nutrients. If individual trees develop swollen stems, distorted leaves, or black rotting pods, a disease is usually the cause.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po. Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ ashishifãi efuu, baai ni etsake, loo ŋmeii diji ni egbo Bei pii lɛ, no ji nɔ ni kɛ hela baa.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree experiences stress from high temperatures, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Insect pests can also damage the small flowers before they are pollinated.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu baanyɛ afite fɔfɔi bibii. Dani pollination baanyɛ aba mli

english: What should I do if my old cocoa farm is continuously giving me low yields?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mi-kokoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii fioo?

english: You can revive a declining farm by pruning dead branches to let in light, applying the right fertilizers to restore soil fertility, and gradually replacing old, low-yielding trees with newer, disease-resistant cocoa varieties.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha ŋmɔ ko ni miiba shi lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni egboi ni ooofo koni ekɛ la aba lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni okɛ kookoo henɔi heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ awo tsei momo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ anajiaŋ fiofio.

english: How does bad weather like a long dry season affect crop behavior?
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ Te enaa tsei adalɛ subaŋ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extended dry periods cause crops to lose leaves to conserve moisture, stop flowering, and drop immature pods early to survive, leading to lower overall harvests.
ga: Gbimɔ be kakadaŋŋ haa ŋmɔshi nibii laajeɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kpaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni oshɛrɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛko lɛ oya koni onyɛ ohi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ nɔbaa.

english: How are hybrid cocoa trees different from the old traditional cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cacao tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɔɔ srɔto yɛ blema cacao tsei ahe?

english: Hybrid cocoa trees grow faster and begin bearing pods in about two to three years instead of five. They also produce higher yields, but they need proper soil nutrients and care to sustain heavy fruiting.
ga: Cacao tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ daa oya ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli, shi jeee afii enumɔ. Amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo hu. Shi shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ kwɛmɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛhiɛ amɛyibii ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: Does removing weeds around my crop help increase the yield?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ?

english: Yes, clearing weeds around your crops prevents them from stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your trees. It also keeps insect pests from hiding near your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni ooojie lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants grow leafy and green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa ni efeɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves. Spraying with neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticide gets rid of them so new leaves can grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ koni baa heei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know which way to push cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the tiny buds along the stem where leaves used to grow. These buds should point upward toward the sky like little arrows so the stems sprout easily out of the soil.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe ni be ko ni eho lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ akpɔlɔi bibii. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why is it important for me to tie my yam vines onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ makɛ sweet potato wain tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight and stay safe from ground heat and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani tomatoi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when it gets too hot during the day or when the soil gets too dry. Consistent watering during dry spells and keeping soil cool with mulch helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ edɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ oofɔ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Fertilizer works best when given in two stages: apply the first batch (NPK) two weeks after planting when shoots appear, and the second batch (Urea) at five weeks when the plant starts growing rapidly before flowering.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ awo mli yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ: Okɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã (NPK) lɛ awo mli otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ (urea) awo mli yɛ otsii enumɔ mli beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa oya dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my farm soil richer for the next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee nii babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen gas directly from the air and store it in the soil. When the crops are harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to feed your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Weed seeds are very tough and can stay asleep in dry soil for months, waiting for the first rains to explode with growth. Clearing weeds early ensures they do not steal water and nutrients away from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo. Mɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ni etswa be mli ni dalɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: How can I stop insects from destroying my harvested maize while it is stored in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Maize must be dried completely in the sun until the kernels are hard before storing. Keeping the dried grains in airtight bags or treating them with approved grain storage dust stops weevils from multiplying and eating your harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛto. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ awo vacuum kotokui amli loo okɛ sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ dumɔwui lɛ atsu he nii. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo ni amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I consider replacing a crop I have been planting on my land for over twenty years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ he?

english: Over decades, soil loses specific nutrients and pests build up; switching to long-term tree crops like rubber can restore soil balance and offer higher continuous financial returns based on current markets.
ga: Yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ rɔbɔt lɛ tsakemɔ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ shika ni yaa nɔ babaoo aba taakɛ jarayeli ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ lɛ.

english: What should I do to my soil before clearing my old farm to plant a new long-term tree crop?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ dani majie ŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni madu tsei heei be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You need to clear old roots, test or enrich the soil with natural organic matter, and map out wide spacing so the new seedlings have enough light and nutrients to establish strong roots.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi momoi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Kaa shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ loo okɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli. Ni ofee gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui heei lɛ aná la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: How long does a rubber tree take to start making money after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani rɔba tso ko jeɔ shika namɔ shishi beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Rubber trees usually take about six to seven years to mature before you can start tapping them for sap, but once mature, they yield income regularly for over twenty years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ aaafee afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo dani obaanyɛ obɔi amɛtswaa. Shi kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa lɛ, amɛbaaná shika ni amɛnáa be fɛɛ be nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ.

english: Why do young tree seedlings seem to grow so slowly during their first year in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the first year, young trees spend most of their energy underground building a deep root system to access water and nutrients, which supports rapid growth above ground later.
ga: Yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ, tsei bibii kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni mli kwɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. ni sɛɛ mli lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Does harvesting or tapping sap from a rubber tree hurt or kill the tree over time?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt ni akpaa loo atswaa kɛjɛɔ rɔbɔt tsei amli lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ awui loo egbeɔ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: No, proper tapping cuts only into the thin outer bark layer without damaging the vital wood underneath, allowing the tree to heal continuously while producing sap for decades.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ atswa tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, efoɔ tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã bibioo lɛ pɛ ni efiteee tso ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yaa nɔ etsaa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ nu afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: How can I tell if switching to rubber trees will bring me more income than my current farm crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kɛ́ matsake kɛya rɔbɔt tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha maná shika babaoo fe nibii ni miduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: You compare the upfront cost and waiting years of tree crops against their potential for regular continuous sales over 20+ years compared to seasonal single-harvest crops.
ga: Okɛ shika ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛ be ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ he lɛ toɔ bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eya nɔ ahɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni fe afii 20 daa lɛ he kɛ akɛto tso kome ni akpaa yɛ be mli lɛ he.

english: Why do market prices for harvested tree crop produce change from year to year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli jara ni akɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi lɛ?

english: Prices fluctuate based on global market demand, local processing factory capacity, and supply levels across different regions, which change regularly.
ga: Jara tsakeɔ yɛ bɔ ni jeŋ jarayeli nibii taoɔ lɛ naa. Nibii ni afeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɛ nibii ni akɛhaa yɛ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ ni tsakeɔ daa lɛ

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain on the same field while my rubber tree seedlings grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be mli ni mi rɔbɔt dumɔwui lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Yes, planting short-term food crops between young tree rows provides food and income in the early years and helps keep weeds from overtaking young seedlings.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, niyenii ni akɛyeɔ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ tsei bibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ. Ebaafee niyenii kɛ shika ni anáa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi akaye tsei bibii anɔ.

english: Rubber trees thrive in deep, well-drained soils in areas with steady warmth and high annual rainfall, conditions common in southern forest regions of Ghana.
ga: Rɔba tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɔɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo daa afi lɛ. Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ hei ni kooi yɔɔ yɛ Ghana wuoyigbɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to my harvest yields if I keep growing the exact same crop on the same plot indefinitely?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛya naanɔ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop consumes the same soil nutrients without rest and encourages specialized insects and diseases to multiply in the soil, causing yields to drop.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Esa akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ awo mli ni hejɔɔmɔ akafee nɔ ko. ni ewoɔ kooloi kɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi hewalɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and strength, so adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps green them back up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my maize grow better the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mi-ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to naturally feed your next maize crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants look droopy in the hot sun even when I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. They wilt temporarily to conserve moisture and usually stand back up when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when there is uneven watering. Shade from taller plants nearby and consistent soil moisture help keep the flowers cool so they can produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa be fɛɛ be. Tsei kakadaji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ahe hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and getting sticky underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Curling and sticky leaves are caused by tiny pests like mealybugs or whiteflies sucking sap from the plant. They leave behind a sweet, sticky waste that can attract black mold if left untreated.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa. Amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi. Eshiɔ nɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbala ŋmeii diji kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why do armyworms only seem to chew my maize leaves during the morning and evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hate the hot midday sun, so they crawl deep into the central leaf funnel of the maize plant during the hottest part of the day and only come out to feed when it is cool.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ nyɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ni ebaaje kpo koni eyatao niyenii pɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Planted too closely, cocoa trees compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Close spacing also blocks breeze from passing through, creating a damp environment where diseases like black pod thrive.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ hu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatsɔ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the extra branches growing on my cassava stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting off weak extra stems forces the cassava plant to send its energy down into growing big, heavy tubers underground instead of wasting food on excess stems and leaves above ground.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, enyɛɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ atsɔɔ ŋmei tsei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ a ngɔɔ tso ɔmɛ nɛ a he hiɛ ɔ ngɛ zugba a nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my green plantains are ready to harvest before they start ripening?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantains ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa dani amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Plantains are mature and ready to cut when the individual fingers swell up, lose their sharp angular edges, and become full and rounded.
ga: Plantains lɛ edara kwraa ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji nine fɛɛ nine shwie shi. Elaajeɔ ŋwɛigbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebafeɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛigbɛ

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce food that travels down to make the yam tuber under the ground grow big and thick.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Baai ni hulu lɛ ewo mli lɛ woɔ niyenii ni yaa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct sun. Planting them under fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them from harsh heat and keeps the soil moist while they build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: It is best to avoid heavy cassava planting near young cocoa because cassava roots grow fast and aggressive, stealing water and soil nutrients away from your growing cocoa trees.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei babaoo ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei ni miida lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, dark conditions. Trimming extra branches lets sunlight and airflow in, helping pods dry out and stay healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees look scorched and dry as if fire touched them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni shã ni egbi tamɔ nɔ ni la etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by small pests called capsids or mirids that suck sap from young branches. Applying approved organic or chemical sprays keeps these pests from destroying your trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo mirids ni nuɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite otsei lɛ.

english: Trees naturally drop excess flowers if they lack enough water, soil nutrients, or tiny pollinating insects. Proper feeding and watering help more flowers successfully turn into full pods.
ga: Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nu bɛ ehe. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli Loo ŋmeii bibii ni haa sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ fa. Niyenii ni sa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Is it harmful to pull cocoa pods off the tree trunk with my bare hands?
ga: Okɛ oniji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko agbala kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli Ani eyɛ oshara?

english: Yes, pulling pods damages the flower cushion on the tree trunk. That cushion is the exact spot where new flowers and pods grow every year, so damaging it reduces future harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ogbala fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔi lɛ akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Nakai kushin lɛ ji he ni fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ daa afi, no hewɔ lɛ nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ haa wɔsɛɛ be mli yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.
