english: Why do extension officers tell me to heap my harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves for six days before drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ ato plantain baai ashishi gbii enumɔ dani mikɛgbi lɛ?

english: This process is called fermentation. It heats the beans naturally, destroying the seed embryo and developing the chocolate flavor and dark brown color that crop buyers demand.
ga: Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ. efiteɔ dumɔwui amli fɔmɔ kotokui lɛ ni ehaa tsokolate kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it bad practice to dry my harvested cocoa beans directly on bare dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ aaagbi kookoo yibii ni akpa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spreading beans on the ground collects dust, mold, and animal waste. Using raised wooden mats keeps beans clean and dry, securing you a higher sale price.
ga: Kɛ́ agbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ, buaa sũ, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii anaa. Kɛ́ akɛ mat ni awo nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahe tseɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. ni haa bo jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ

english: Why should I cut off the long shoots growing straight out from the bottom of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei kakadaji ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots are called suckers or chupons. They steal water and food away from the main trunk, which leaves less energy for the tree to produce large pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupons. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsɔne wulu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ tso lɛ náa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has lost its richness and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiɛ edɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When farm soil loses nutrients, crop leaves turn light green or yellow, growth slows down, and trees yield far fewer pods than they used to in previous seasons.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli niyenii lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ. slow growth Ni tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kwraa fe be ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when water sits trapped on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates crop roots by cutting off oxygen. When water becomes stagnant, harmful substances like ammonia build up in the soil, rotting the roots and turning the crop leaves yellow.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nu damɔ shi lɛ, nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ammonia buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What happens to my maize crops if heavy rain leaves water stagnant in the farm without drainage?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ?

english: Trapped water becomes stagnant very quickly under the sun. This standing water builds up toxic gases like ammonia and starves the soil of oxygen, stopping the maize roots from absorbing nutrients and causing them to rot.
ga: Nu ni amɔmɔ lɛ feɔ ais oya yɛ hulu la shishi. Nu ni ekã shi nɛɛ feɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei tamɔ ammonia ni efiteɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I let irrigation water sit motionless in my crop gutters for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ hiɔ mitso lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Motionless water loses its oxygen and creates a breeding ground for harmful chemicals like ammonia to accumulate, which poisons crop roots instead of nourishing them.
ga: Nu ni bɛ nitsumɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ, ni ehaa tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ammonia buaa amɛhe naa, ni ekɛ tsofai fɔji woɔ tsei shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if the standing water on my farm has become dangerous for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: If the standing water smells bad, turns dark, or if your plants start wilting from the bottom up despite being in water, it means stagnant water has created toxic ammonia and root rot.
ga: Kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ ehiii lɛ tsakemɔ kɛya su ni tsuɔ waa Aloo kɛji otso lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ nu mli po. No tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa ammonia ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why should I drain the excess water immediately after transplanting my young rice seedlings out of the nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Draining the water right after removing young seedlings stops the water from turning stagnant. It protects the remaining soil health and allows fresh air to reach the ground so new roots can breathe.
ga: Beni ajie tsei bibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ akatsi ehe. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ he ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi heei anyɛ amu.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings die when water in the seedbed fails to drain after watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajɛ mli kɛji afɔ amɛ nu sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings have delicate roots that need drained soil. Standing water turns stagnant, creating a trapped environment where dangerous levels of ammonia build up and kill young roots.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ baafee dioo. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko ni mli wa baa. Ammonia ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa ehe naa ni efiteɔ shishifãi bibii.

english: Why is it important to empty out standing water in my plant beds right after removing young nursery crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ nu ni damɔ shi awo midumɔ saatsoi lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Removing young plants leaves behind broken root fragments. If left in stagnant water, these organic bits rot quickly and release toxic ammonia into the water, which damages any future crops planted there.
ga: Tsei bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shishifãi ni ekumɔ lɛ amli fãi shwieɔ shi. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli Nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛjieɔ ammonia ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛyaa nu lɛ mli. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can dirty, standing water in my vegetable bed actually poison my crops?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, as plant material decays in stagnant water without fresh air movement, it produces high levels of toxic ammonia, which burns plant roots and stunts crop growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei amli nibii fiteɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsiii ehe. No hewɔ lɛ, ejieɔ ammonia ni yɔɔ gbeyei babaoo kpo. Enɛ baa shã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eha tso lɛ kpa daamɔ.

english: How does draining water quickly after clearing small plants keep my soil healthy for the next planting?
ga: Te nu ni hoɔ oya beni ajie tsei bibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha midumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Draining the water prevents toxic ammonia build-up caused by rotting leftover organic matter, leaving the soil clean, rich in air, and healthy for the next crop.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ammonia ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni nibii ni eshwɛ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fitemɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ he atse Kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo yɛ. ni ehi kɛha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: If I grow crops in flooded fields or valley bottoms, why must I drain and refresh the water regularly?
ga: Kɛji midu nibii yɛ ŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli loo yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo mi nu lɛ mli ni mafee lɛ ehee daa?

english: Water that is left stagnant accumulates crop waste and naturally occurring ammonia, which spoils the soil quality and weakens crop roots over time.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ buaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli jwɛi kɛ ammonia ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli baa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn yellow when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and high heat. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees grown above them to shield their leaves and keep the air cool and humid while their root systems develop.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ koni ebu baai lɛ ahe ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant moves available nutrients from its older bottom leaves up to feed the newer growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Abɛi tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling and pale patches on cassava are typical signs of Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by small insects called whiteflies. The virus prevents the leaves from trapping sunlight properly, weakening the plant and shrinking the root yields.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni etsake yɛ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stems and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when it rains heavily for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up all the air spaces in the soil, preventing cassava roots from breathing. Without oxygen, the roots suffocate and become vulnerable to fungal rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafee oshara akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baafite.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help improve my soil for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer, leaving rich soil behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ashiɔ ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper blossoms often drop due to heat stress, erratic watering, or poor pollination. Keeping soil moisture steady and encouraging pollinators helps flowers stay on the plant and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo pollination ni ehiii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ pollinators ni awoɔ he hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell before the continuous rainy season begins. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the young seedlings will dry up and die from lack of moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli egbi lɛ amli Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and small even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can absorb them, depriving your main plants of essential nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii titri ni aduɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so it doesn't spoil in my storehouse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize is fully mature when the leaves and husks turn dry and brown, and a small black layer forms at the tip of each kernel. Harvesting at full maturity ensures low grain moisture, preventing mold growth during storage.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛji baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naagbee. Nikpamɔ yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade trees or food crops like plantain planted alongside them to block intense sun, keep the soil cool, and maintain moisture while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Ehe miihia ni amɛdu tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction are pollinated by tiny insects called midges. If there are not enough midges or if the tree is stressed by drought or lack of nutrients, many flowers will drop naturally.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii ji mɛi ni feɔ pollin lɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛji ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ loo tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli lɛ, Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color as they ripen. Green pods usually turn a bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. You can also tell a pod is ripe when it makes a hollow sound when tapped gently.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni pods tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Obaanyɛ ole hu akɛ pod ko egbɔ kɛji efee gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛji otswa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing at the base of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers or chupons, waste the tree's energy. They steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk and flowers, which reduces the amount of cocoa pods the tree can produce.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupon. Ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ afite. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it bad for my cocoa tree to have too many thick branches growing closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ baaná niji ni mli tse babaoo tsɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Dense foliage traps moisture and blocks sunlight from reaching the inner branches, creating an ideal damp environment for fungal diseases like black pod to spread. Pruning allows air and light to pass through the tree freely.
ga: Baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa. Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and dark conditions. Raindrops bounce water and soil onto low-hanging pods, spreading the fungal spores quickly across the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Fungal spores lɛ gbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: What causes the leaves on my cocoa tree to swell up and turn yellowish with red veins?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifu ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ?

english: This is a key symptom of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. The virus attacks the plant's food transport system, causing swelling and eventual decline of the tree.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi titri ko. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Virus tutuaa tsei aniyenii gbɛjianɔtoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fuuɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: What makes small brown patches and holes appear on my young cocoa stems and pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ okadii bibii kɛ buji baa? Su ni ji brown jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ kɛ mi-pods lɛ anɔ.

english: This damage is caused by mirid insects (capsids) that suck the sap from tender cocoa tissue. As they feed, they inject a toxic liquid that kills the plant tissue around the wound, turning it dark brown or black.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi babaoo (capsids) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo fã ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli lɛ. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛkɛ nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei woɔ mli koni ekɛfite tso lɛ mli fãji ni bɔle pilamɔ lɛ he lɛ, ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ.

english: Why must I heap my harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves for several days before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ toɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Heaping beans under plantain leaves creates heat for fermentation. This process kills the seed germ inside, stops it from sprouting, and develops the rich chocolate flavor and brown color that buyers look for.
ga: Okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato plantain baai lɛ ashishi koni ekɛ dɔlɛ aba kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Gbɛ nɛɛ gbeɔ muawai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Kpaa lɛ koni ekakwɛ̃ ni oná tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Why is cocoa considered such a special crop compared to other trees I can grow on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ kookoo akɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ? ni manyɛ mada yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Cocoa produces beans that are processed into cocoa powder and chocolate, which are valued globally not just for food, but also for health benefits like supporting heart health and general body vitality.
ga: Afeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ kookoo powda kɛ tsokolate. ni yɔɔ jeŋ muu fɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ Jeee kɛha niyenii pɛ Shi moŋ eyɛ hewalɛnamɔ he sɛɛnamɔi hu, tamɔ eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsui lɛ náa hewalɛ. kɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunshine because their leaves and roots are tender. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby acts like an umbrella, keeping the air cool and moist while protecting the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahewɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni aduɔ Amɛfeɔ ekome tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the stem during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess humidity and persistent rainwater allow a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread rapidly across cocoa stems. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and airflow into the farm, drying out moisture that the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo tsei lɛ amli oya. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni egbiɔ nu ni he hiaa ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning pale yellow even though we are getting enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a nutrient essential for leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach, requiring added fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Why does growing cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize help the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ewaa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with leafy branches but produce small tubers beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Eyɛ niji kɛ baai shi eyɛ yitso bibioo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava receives excessive leaf-growing nutrients or is planted too close to other crops, it puts all its energy into growing bushy leaves above ground instead of storing starch in its tubers below ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yaa hiɛ babaoo loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ starch baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves like solar panels to make food that builds the subterranean tuber. Staking the vines off the ground lifts the leaves toward sunlight and prevents foliage from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni akɛfeɔ niyenii ni feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ́ adu wain tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ hiɛ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut away small suckers growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Too many young suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and root space. Removing extra shoots ensures all the plant's food goes into producing one large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe he ko. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ baawo ŋmeii agbo kome ni tsii.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off before any fruit appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become excessively hot, during dry Harmattan winds, or when water supply is inconsistent. Keeping the plant roots consistently moist helps flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Yɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli loo be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli tse pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee tomatoi.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the leaves and central whorl of my young corn overnight?
ga: Mɛni miiha buji miifee yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the maize stem during the hot day and eat the tender leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my vegetable crops with dry grass help them survive warm dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around Mitsei lɛ ni mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi yeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Covering the dirt with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, creates a protective blanket that shields the ground from hot sun rays, preventing soil moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Efeɔ tsɔne ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plants twisting and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Twisted or curled leaves are often early signs of insect pests, viral infections, or plant diseases. Removing plants with these symptoms early prevents the problem from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni etsɔ loo ebɔle lɛ ji mra be mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai eba. Virus hela loo tso hela. Jiemɔ tsei ni yɔɔ okadi nɛɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi naagba lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What should I do if I see deformed leaves on a few of my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina baai ni efite yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi anɔ?

english: Pluck off the affected leaves or pull out the sick plant completely right away. Leaving infected plant parts on the farm allows disease to multiply and infect neighboring healthy crops.
ga: Jiemɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ loo jiemɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tso lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if a seedling is healthy enough to put in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look for bright, straight leaves and a sturdy stem. Avoid any seedlings with twisted leaves, dark spots, or unusual shapes, as these are signs of underlying disease.
ga: Taomɔ baai ni ja, ni kpɛɔ kɛ tsei ni wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni baai ekpɔtɔ, hei ni tsuɔ, loo henɔi krokomɛi ni ejaaa lɛ ahe. Ejaakɛ enɛɛmɛi ji hela ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ he okadii.

english: Why should I throw away sick-looking seedlings before planting them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashɛ dumɔwui ni tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ashwie dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sick seedlings carry diseases into your main field. Sorting and throwing them away beforehand ensures you only spend time, water, and fertilizer on strong crops that will yield a good harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ kɛ hela baaba oŋmɔji titrii lɛ amli. Kɛji ohala amɛ ni oshɛrɛ amɛ ashwie kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, no lɛ, obaafite be, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aba lɛ ahe.

english: What does it mean to 'clean' seedlings before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwui ni ‘atsumɔ’ dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ shishi?

english: Cleaning seedlings means inspecting your nursery plants and discarding weak, deformed, or diseased ones so that only healthy planting materials are brought to the field.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe saamɔ tsɔɔ akɛ obaakwɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli. ni oshɛrɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni efite, loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oshwie koni okɛ dumɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant weak seedlings alongside strong ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weak seedlings attract pests and diseases easily, acting as a bridge that brings sickness to nearby strong seedlings. Planting only healthy ones keeps the whole crop stand safe.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai oya, ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ blɔfo ni kɛ hela baa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: How do I stop a crop disease from spreading to the rest of my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei ahe helai anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã hei krokomɛi? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Regularly inspect your farm and immediately remove infected leaves or whole plants. Removing bad plants early cuts off the source of infection before wind, rain, or insects carry it to good plants.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni ojie baai loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsei gbohii ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baafo he ni hela lɛ jɛɔ lɛ mli dani kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why do crop diseases spread so quickly between plants that touch each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpeɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: When leaves of diseased and healthy plants touch, bacteria, fungi, and pests can easily crawl or wash over during rainy weather, spreading infection rapidly from plant to plant.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe baai lɛ ta amɛhe lɛ, helatsɛmɛi, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ loo amɛho amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ.

english: What is the safest way to throw away diseased leaves after plucking them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ashɛrɛɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ashwieɔ kɛji ajie amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burn or deeply bury diseased leaves far away from your farm. If you leave them on the ground near your crops, rainwater or insects can carry the infection back onto your healthy plants.
ga: Shã loo ofu baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Kɛji oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii Nugbɔ nu loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ hela kɛku sɛɛ kɛya otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important to separate damaged produce from good ones after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving even a few rotten or diseased fruits or leaves mixed in with your fresh harvest can cause the whole batch to spoil quickly during storage or transport to the market.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi aduawai loo baai ni egbo loo hela emɔ amɛ ni okɛfutu onibii heei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ afite oya yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ loo akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mifo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight and hot winds. High temperatures burn their tender leaves and dry out the soil, so they need shade trees to act as natural umbrellas and keep the air cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni edɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. This competition results in thin, weak stems and tiny corn ears instead of large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji ŋmãa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii yɛ ŋmãa wuji ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen nutrients. The plant automatically moves its remaining food from older bottom leaves to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen niyenii. Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to apply fertilizer on my land right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mawo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer away off the topsoil before the crop roots have enough time to drink it in, wasting your investment and leaving the plants without food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Eji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fitemɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the soil when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, it suffocates the roots, allowing fungal rots and bacteria to attack the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without fruiting when the weather becomes extremely hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when soil nutrients are low. High heat prevents the flower from pollinating itself properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tsei ahe loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do caterpillars hide deep inside the central funnel of my corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms hide inside the leaf funnel because it provides shelter from direct sunlight and predators like birds, while offering the softest, tenderest leaves for them to feed on.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai amli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi tamɔ okpoi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛbu amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha amɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ fe fɛɛ ni amɛye.

english: How do weeds growing around my pepper plants stop them from producing big peppers?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-pepper tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee pepper agboi?

english: Weeds have strong roots that aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight directly away from your pepper plants, leaving them starved and unable to grow large leaves or fruits.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ baai wuji loo aduawai.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the growing underground tuber. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing them to light and preventing soil-borne leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enaa la ni etsĩɔ sũ mli tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: Why should I remove some of the small sucker shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: The main plantain stem shares its water and food with every sucker attached to it. Removing extra suckers directs all the plant's energy into the main stem so it can produce a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Plantain tso titri lɛ kɛ suckers fɛɛ ni fata he lɛ jaa nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni afee dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: How often am I supposed to pluck cocoa pods from my farm during the main harvest season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ majie kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ mli?

english: You should harvest your cocoa pods regularly, typically once every month during the main season from October to January. However, if your trees are producing heavily, harvesting every two weeks is recommended to prevent pods from overripening.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ daa. Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ enɛ shikome yɛ nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ yɛ be titri ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ October kɛyashi January lɛ mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo lɛ, Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ akpa daa otsii enyɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ akakwɛ̃ fe nine.

english: What months of the year do cocoa trees produce the most harvest in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ kookoo tsei woɔ yibii fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: The main cocoa harvest season runs from October through January, which is when trees yield the highest quantity of ripe pods, followed by a smaller mid-crop harvest around May through July.
ga: Kookoo ŋmaa be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ Otukwajaŋ kɛyashiɔ Aharabata. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe fɛɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ akpamɔ yɛ May-July he.

english: Is it normal to harvest ripe pods multiple times from the exact same cocoa tree in one season?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ abaakpa kookoo tso kome nɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, cocoa pods on the same tree do not all mature at the same time. You will need to return to the same tree every few weeks throughout the harvest season to pick only the pods that have ripened.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jeee kookoo ŋmeii fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli. Esa akɛ oku osɛɛ oya tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ daa otsii fioo yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ koni oyajie ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ pɛ.

english: Can plucking my cocoa pods every two weeks instead of once a month hurt my farm?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii ni ajieɔ daa otsii enyɔ yɛ shikome yɛ nyɔŋ mli najiaŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ awui?

english: No, harvesting every two weeks will not hurt your farm. In fact, frequent harvesting helps protect your yield by removing ripe pods before diseases like black pod rot or farm pests can destroy them.
ga: Dabi, kpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ Otsii enyɔ yeŋ oŋmɔ lɛ awui. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ dani helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ loo ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: How long does it take for a cocoa flower to grow into a fully ripe pod ready for harvesting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: It takes about five to six months from the time a cocoa flower is pollinated for it to grow into a fully developed, mature, and ripe pod.
ga: Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni kookoo fɔfɔi ko shwereɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni edara kwraa, ni eda, ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are my cocoa trees not bearing heavy pods during early months like February and March?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ ewooo ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji tamɔ February kɛ March lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow natural yield cycles. February and March fall into a dry post-harvest period where the trees rest, shed old leaves, and build energy for the next flowering cycle.
ga: Cacao tsei nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ gbɛ ko sɛɛ. February kɛ March ji nyɔji ni nu bɛ yɛ nikpamɔ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ yaa wɔɔhe, eshwieɔ baai momo ni ehaa hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees mature their pods faster than others on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi daa oya fe cacao tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Pod maturation depends on factors like the variety of cocoa planted, the amount of sunlight and water the specific tree receives, and the health of the tree's leaves.
ga: Pod lɛ shweremɔ damɔ nibii tamɔ kookoo henɔi ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. Hulu la kɛ nu babaoo ni tsei náa kɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ baai lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: How do I know that a cocoa pod on my tree is mature enough to be plucked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie?

english: A cocoa pod is ready for harvest when its color changes completely—usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red/purple to orange, depending on the variety.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su etsake kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. loo kɛjɛ tsuru/purple ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: What happens to my cocoa beans if I leave ripe pods on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo lɛ nɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ hu?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the beans inside to start germinating or rotting. This destroys the quality of the beans and lowers the sale price you receive.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ni ehaa jara ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I cut the cocoa pod stem with a tool instead of twisting it off with my hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ dɛŋdade afo kookoo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ minine baatsɔ mli?

english: Twisting pods off by hand damages the flower cushion on the tree trunk. This cushion is where future flowers and pods grow, so damaging it reduces your future harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ oniji tsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔi lɛ akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Kushin nɛɛ ji he ni wɔsɛɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ɔ yɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, hiɛkpatamɔ lɛ haa nɔ ni obaafee wɔsɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without taller plants nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their young leaves burn easily. Planting them alongside fast-growing crops like plantains provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil to help the cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi koni eye ebua kookoo ni ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller yields every year when I plant them on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a large amount of nitrogen and nutrients from the soil. Continuous planting on the same spot without giving the land a break or rotating crops exhausts the soil nutrients, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he kome ni akumɔɔɔ jɛmɛ loo atsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa hu baa shi.

english: Why do people recommend that I plant groundnuts or beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legume plants like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the dirt. This naturally feeds the soil and helps nearby crops grow bigger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hidden inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee baai lɛ amli lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that eats maize leaves and stems. Catching them early by inspecting your field weekly and applying the correct control methods before they burrow deep into the plant is key to saving your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli kwɛmɔ nɔ daa otsi kɛ gbɛi ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ dani amɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ titri ni baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahere.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high moisture and shade. Pruning excess tree branches lets sunlight and breeze into your farm, drying out the pods and preventing fungal growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa kɛboteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants get twisted with yellow spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems during planting prevents this virus from stunting your crop.
ga: Baai ni etsilɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight so their leaves can make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking also lifts the leaves off the damp soil, protecting the plant from fungal rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Kɛji haomɔ ba Tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do my vegetable plants droop in the middle of the afternoon even when the soil is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Plants curl or droop their leaves in strong afternoon heat to reduce water evaporation from their leaves. As long as the soil has moisture, this is a normal self-defense mechanism and the leaves will stand back up in the cooler evening.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ aba shi. Be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afãa mɔ he. Ni baai lɛ teɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects around them for too long in heavy soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen or when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea near the base of the plants will help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nitrogen, tamɔ urea fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem before growing into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛmiitsɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil around the plant consistently moist and applying mulch like dry grass around the roots helps cool the soil and keep the flowers attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ feemɔ Tso lɛ mli edɔ be fɛɛ be. Ni kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is being attacked by Fall Armyworms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ etutua mi-abele lɛ?

english: You will notice ragged holes eaten into the leaves and dark, sawdust-like droppings inside the central leaf funnels of the plant. Inspecting your field early in the morning helps you spot the caterpillars inside the funnels before major damage happens.
ga: Obaana buji ni egbɛ eshwa ni aye yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ dani nɔ ko wulu ko abafite.

english: Why is it important to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving your maize plants extra nourishment without needing to buy as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa o-corn tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ krokomɛi ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and bent when I plant them in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight and thick only when the soil is soft and loose enough for the root to expand downward. Building high mounds or ridges with loose topsoil gives the tubers the space they need to grow long and heavy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ ashɛ shi. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni sũ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli etse lɛ, ehaa bulb lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to cut off the big leaves of a plantain sucker before planting it in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ plantain baai agboi dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Large leaves pull water out of the sucker faster than its young roots can absorb it from the ground. Trimming off the top leaves allows the plantain sucker to focus its energy on growing strong roots first.
ga: Baai wuji lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ amɛ nu mli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afo ŋwɛi baai lɛ, ehaa plantain suckers lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa lɛ ahe nii klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce smaller peppers after the first harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ pepper bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants use up a lot of soil nutrients to produce their first crop. Adding compost or top-dressing fertilizer after the first pick recharges the plant with the energy needed to grow large fruits for the next harvest.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa fata he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo yibii wuji kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetable crops curl inward during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense trick plants use to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun and cut down on water loss. Watering your crops deeply early in the morning ensures they have enough water to withstand afternoon heat.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. ni eha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo oŋmɔshi nibii amli jogbaŋŋ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛnáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ shwane latsaa lɛ naa.

english: Why do tiny beetles destroy my harvested maize grains when I store them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fiteɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ beni mikɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Weevils and grain beetles thrive inside grain bags when the maize is stored before it is completely dry. Drying your maize in the sun until a kernel cracks sharply between your teeth prevents insects from breeding inside the stored grain.
ga: Weevils kɛ seed weevils lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui kotokui amli kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baatswa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ akafa yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling just two days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots begin to deteriorate quickly once detached from the living plant because oxygen enters the cut ends and breaks down the flesh. Leaving roots unharvested in the ground until you are ready to sell or consume them keeps them fresh.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ boteɔ he ni afo lɛ naagbee lɛ, ni ehaa loo lɛ fãa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okpako kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaahɔɔ loo oye koni amɛkafee ehee.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing far fewer pods now than they did ten years ago on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo kwraa fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing cocoa continuously on the same soil for many years drains essential plant foods (nutrients) from the ground. Without replacing these nutrients, the soil becomes tired, causing older trees to produce fewer and smaller pods.
ga: Kookoo ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo lɛ haa tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa (nibii ni haa mɔ he waa) lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ atsakeee niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ etɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why does a piece of forest land produce heavy harvests for the first few years but then slowly lose its strength?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo ko mli fã ko woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ? Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, hewalɛ elaaje?

english: Newly cleared forest land contains years of rich, natural compost from fallen leaves. Once you start harvesting crops continuously, those stored nutrients are carried away in the harvest, leaving the soil empty unless you add organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Koo lɛ mli he ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni jɛ baai ni egbee shi afii babaoo lɛ amli. Kɛ oje ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ shishi be fɛɛ be lɛ, Nakai niyenii mli nibii ni ato lɛ yaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ mli. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee efolo lɛ nɔ Ja okɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he.

english: How can I bring life back to soil that has become tired from decades of cocoa farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ wala aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ kɛjɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni mikɛdu kookoo lɛ mli lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: You can restore tired soil by planting leguminous cover crops, letting parts of the farm rest (fallow), and applying well-rotted manure or compost to rebuild the natural plant food in the ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi ajɔɔ amɛhe (egbee shi) ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ atsu nii ni okɛfee adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my old cocoa farm needs to be cut down and replanted rather than kept alive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni afo mi-kokoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ mli ni adu ekoŋŋ moŋ fe ni mahã ehi shi?

english: If your trees are over 30 years old, produce very few pods despite good rainfall and fertilizer, or suffer from widespread diseases like swollen shoot, the trees are too old to recover and need to be replanted.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ eye fe afii 30 lɛ, ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po. loo helai ni egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he lɛ ahe naagbai, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efu lɛ miipiŋ lɛ, tso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni adu lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Extra branches and unwanted suckers (chupons) drink up the water and food that the main tree needs. Removing them allows the plant to send its energy directly into making flowers and growing cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo (chupons) lɛ nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso titri lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛfeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni kwɛɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under intense heat. They need shade trees to protect them from direct sunlight and keep moisture in the soil until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly when the farm is too wet, dark, and crowded. Clearing bush and pruning shade trees allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm and prevent the rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ ŋmɔji amli edɔ tsɔ, edɔ ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ. Afoɔ tsei ahe ŋmɔji kɛ tsei ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmɔji lɛ agbi ni akafite.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain on the same farm with my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni ŋmei tsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: You can grow plantain alongside young cocoa because plantain provides helpful shade. However, heavy feeders like cassava should not be planted too close to mature cocoa, as they fight with the cocoa roots for nutrients and water.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu plantains yɛ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, esaaa akɛ aduɔ tsei ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu.

english: Does cocoa grow well on every type of soil in Asanteman?
ga: Ani kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Asanteman lɛ anɔ?

english: No, cocoa requires deep, loose soil that drains water well while keeping enough moisture. Rocky soils stop root growth, and swampy waterlogged soils cause root rot, making both unsuitable for healthy cocoa.
ga: Dabi, kookoo biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baanyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa mli. Shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haaa efee nɔ ni sa kɛha kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small flowers but end up dropping them without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyi fa, shi amɛgbee shi ni amɛfeee pods?

english: Cocoa flowers drop without forming pods when there are not enough tiny insects (midges) in the farm to pollinate them, or when the tree is stressed by drought or lack of soil nutrients.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii beni kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee amɛ ŋmeii lɛ. aloo be mli ni hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ.

english: Why should I space my yam mounds far apart instead of packing them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ ahi he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni mikɛaabɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Yam tubers need plenty of underground room to expand and grow big. When mounds are placed too close together, the plants compete for soil nutrients, space, and moisture, resulting in smaller yams.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia ŋwɛi ŋtayaa babaoo koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, ŋwɛi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Is it good for my crop soil if I burn the bush after clearing the land?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi aha shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ kɛji mishã mi jwɛi lɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning gives a quick burst of ash nutrients, but it burns away the organic material and helpful soil organisms that keep soil fertile long-term. Leaving cleared vegetation to rot creates natural mulch that retains soil moisture and feeds crops.
ga: Shãa lɛ jieɔ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. Mohu ɔ, a tsakeɔ níhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a nɔ kɛ zugba a mi níhi nɛ a he hia nɛ haa nɛ zugba a peeɔ nɔ́ kpakpa ngɛ be kakadaŋŋ mi ɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ, ebaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoot to bend around to find sunlight, which weakens the stem and reduces tuber yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei heei lɛ akoto koni amɛna hulu la. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha tuber lɛ yibii lɛ aba shi.

english: If seeds are buried too deep, the shoot runs out of stored energy before it can break through the soil surface to reach sunlight, causing the seed to die underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow tall. Applying animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains nearby creates shade that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni baanyɛ ashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, crop leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. The leaves temporarily curl or drop to reduce water loss, usually recovering once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe loo amɛbaagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal light, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crop direct access to everything it needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa otsei titrii lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller when I plant the exact same crop on the same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that crop uses most and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating different crops helps balance soil nutrients and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ baaha sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii fe fɛɛ lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How do I stop my harvested yams from rotting before the transport vehicle arrives to take them to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite dani tsɔne ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ abashɛ?

english: Store harvested yams off the ground in a shaded, well-ventilated structure like a yam barn. Handle the tubers gently to avoid cuts and bruises, as broken skin lets in fungi and bacteria that cause quick rotting.
ga: Too sweet potato ni akpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, tamɔ sweet potato ŋmɔ mli. Okɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii blɛoo koni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hewolo ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni haa mɔ fiteɔ oya lɛ kpo.

english: How long does a plantain plant take from planting until the fruit is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Plantain plants typically take between 9 to 12 months to produce a full bunch ready for harvest, with the flower bunch first appearing around 6 to 8 months after planting depending on water and soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ akpa. Klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ baaje kpo aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Will my plantain tree produce another bunch of fruit after I cut it down during harvest?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii krokomɛi beni mifo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, a single plantain stem only fruits once in its lifetime. After harvesting, you cut down that main stem so that the young shoots growing at the base can take over and produce the next crop.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwu kome pɛ baawo yibii yɛ ewala shihilɛ mli. ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Ebaabi ni ofo nakai tso titri lɛ koni ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I dig up my plantain shoots and move them to a new piece of land if I lose access to my current farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ amli ni mikɛya shikpɔŋ hee nɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ hegbɛ kɛya ŋmɔ ni miyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɛɛ hu?

english: Yes, you can dig up healthy young shoots (suckers) from the base of the main plant, trim their leaves and roots, and safely replant them in a new plot where they will root and grow normally.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ (ŋmeii) kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ shishi. Kpãa ehe baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. ni okɛ amɛ aku sɛɛ adu amɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ saatso hee nɔ he ni amɛbaawo shishifãi ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain shoots droop and look weak right after I move them to new soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ?

english: Transplanted suckers experience shock because their roots were disturbed during digging. If you water them well and cut off extra leaves to reduce water loss, they will bounce back once new roots form.
ga: Suckers ni atsake amɛ lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa amɛhe yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛji okɛ nu ha otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ofolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ aba kɛji shishifãi heei eba.

english: Why do so many small shoots keep growing around my main plantain tree, and should I leave them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ. Midumɔwu titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mashi fɛɛ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantains naturally produce side shoots called suckers to reproduce. You should prune away extra suckers and leave only one or two strong ones so they do not steal water and nutrients from the main fruiting stem.
ga: Plantains woɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛkɛfɔ bii. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems. When the fruit bunch grows large, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a wooden or bamboo fork helps keep it upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei fɔk tsu nii kɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantains grow smaller bunches when I keep farming them on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbɛ amɛmiifee jwɛi bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Plantains draw heavy amounts of nutrients like potassium from the ground. Continuous farming without adding manure or resting the land exhausts the soil, leading to smaller yields over time.
ga: Plantains jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo, tamɔ potassium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli loo akɛjɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I plant other food crops like cassava or garden eggs on the same land with my plantains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-plantains lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant crops like cassava, maize, or vegetables between young plantain plants during their first few months before the plantain leaves grow big enough to shade the ground fully.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli. Dani baai lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ,.

english: How can I tell that my plantain bunch is mature enough to harvest before it starts to spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantain tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa dani ebɔi fitemɔ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits swell up and lose their sharp ridges, turning rounded, and the dry flower ends at the tips easily rub off.
ga: Plantain ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fũu ni esɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ naagbee ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my plantains ripen and soften so quickly after I cut them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains release natural gases that speed up ripening. Keeping them in a cool, shaded area with good airflow prevents them from overheating and ripening too fast.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Dare lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya lɛ kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkadɔ fe nine ni amɛkaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make green food. Applying organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizers early in the plant's life helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji tso ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ wala mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land is healthy enough to support a good vegetable harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa aduawai kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, breaks apart easily in your hands, holds moisture without becoming soggy, and contains beneficial creatures like earthworms that help create natural nutrients for crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli Ni nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ebuaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. This competition leaves you with tall, weak stalks that produce very small or poor-quality cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ tsei bibii waa loo ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating your maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts naturally rebuilds soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Ebaatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ema shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they are mature enough to pick?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafolɔ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, humid shade. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and dry air to reach the cocoa pods, keeping them dry and preventing the fungus from spreading.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ black pod hela baa. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shɛɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Tomato flowers fall off, or drop, when the plant experiences stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or insect pests like thrips. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from harsh afternoon heat prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni obu tsei ahe kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay tiny and short instead of growing tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ kuku yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ kakadaŋŋ ni efee hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted pepper plants are often a sign that soil is too hard for the roots to expand, or that tiny microscopic worms called nematodes in the soil are damaging the roots and blocking water absorption.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miifite shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmiitsi nu ni miibote mli lɛ naa.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally in hot weather to conserve water and protect its roots underground. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts fresh new leaves and continues growing normally.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plant leaves curl upward during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?
