english: Leaves curl in the afternoon heat to reduce the amount of surface exposed to the hot sun and prevent water loss. If the leaves uncurl when the evening cools down, the plant is simply protecting itself.
ga: Ha oyitsɔi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ ohe ni okɛtsi nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe.

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted to survive naturally in your climate, allowing them to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domestic crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from choking out your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential plant food. Maize needs nitrogen to grow deep green leaves and produce strong cobs, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Abɛi he miihia nitrogen koni ekwɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans helps make my farm soil richer for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni enáa ŋmei babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen acts as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nitrogen ni ato lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big shade trees from my new land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong sunlight and excessive heat. Shade trees shield young seedlings from burning under the hot sun and help keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa plants grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop flat black rotten spots on the bottom right as they start to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni egbo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? yɛ shishigbɛ ninejurɔgbɛ be mli ni ebɔi shweremɔ.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil moisture changes too drastically between dry and wet spells, preventing the plant from taking up enough calcium to build strong fruit walls.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ be ni hulu enyɔ shi kɛ be ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ teŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛma aduawai gbogboi ni wa.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but giving me tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or if plants are shaded too much, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and thick leaves instead of sending energy down to swell the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ ehiɛ hulutsoo tsɔ lɛ Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, atsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha yitso lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce much smaller bunches after the first harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain stems produce many side shoots called suckers that steal water and nutrients from the main stem. If you do not cut back extra suckers to leave just one or two, the main plant gets weak and yields small bunches.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ woɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii, ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, no lɛ eko loo enyɔ pɛ baashwɛ. Tso titri lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Yam plants use their leaves like solar panels to make food. Lifting the vines onto tall stakes spreads out the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to build big underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei feɔ niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ baaha etso lɛ baagbɛ eshwa koni ená hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the juice from fresh leaves, or by a plant virus carried by those insects. Controlling tiny pests early stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo tsei amli helai ni ji mɛi ni kɛ nakai kooloi lɛ baa lɛ Kɛ́ akwɛ kooloi lɛ anɔ fioo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akpa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my orange trees dropping young green fruits before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop fruit when they face stress from prolonged dry weather, or when pests like fruit flies puncture the young fruits to lay eggs inside, causing the fruit to rot early.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛyibii kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli haomɔ mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii, tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii, tsɔ aduawai bibii amli koni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my okra plants produce flowers that fall off without turning into okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ okra ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Okra flowers drop off without setting pods when the weather is extremely hot and dry, or when insects damage the insides of the flowers before bees can pollinate them.
ga: Roselle fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli dani ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ amɛmli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct harsh sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil. Planting plantains or leaving shade trees provides a shelter that keeps the young cocoa cool and moist until it gets strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ loo tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa anáa he ko ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in the same farm with my maize make the soil better for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the season ends, those roots rot in the ground and release natural fertilizer into the soil for the next crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛdu nii krokomɛi.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: No, planting cassava too close together makes the plants fight for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. This causes the plants to grow thin and produce small, weak tubers instead of big, thick roots.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni ewoɔ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's hybrid corn crop produce smaller ears than the seeds I bought from the dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo toi bibii fe dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ jarayelɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give a high yield only in their first generation. The seeds saved from that harvest lose their special strength, so they grow into weaker plants with smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni wooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten patches on the bottom while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ amɛshishi be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the plant or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the tomato plant take up calcium properly so the fruit grows clean.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa o-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni sa koni amɛwo yibii ni he tse.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and show yellow patches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is often caused by the Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties helps prevent the leaves from curling and losing their strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛbaa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing any peppers when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani eduɔ pepper lɛ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, making them drop flowers to save water and survival energy. Giving them extra water or light shade during very hot weeks helps them hold onto their flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Nu loo hulutsoo kroko ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to trim or prune the extra side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches removes leaves that waste the plant's food. This allows the plant to send its nutrients directly to developing big, healthy fruits instead of growing useless leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛbaakpa tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ajie baai ni miifite tso lɛ niyenii lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa aduawai wuji ni mli wa lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaakwɛ̃ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: Weed seeds naturally sit buried in the soil for years waiting for light. When you clear the bush, sunlight hits the ground and causes those wild seeds to germinate much faster than regular farm crops.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo, ni amɛmiimɛ la. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi lɛ mli lɛ, Hulu la lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa nakai koo mli dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kwraa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why should I clear and loosen the soil deeply before planting my cassava cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni mafolɔ mli jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmei ni afo lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers grow underground and need loose, soft soil to expand. Deep land preparation clears deep roots of wild weeds and creates space for heavy, healthy tubers to develop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni asaa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ koo mli jwɛi ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ. ni efee he ko ni bulbs ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to burn all the old grass and stems on my land before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei momo ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the living organisms in the soil and burns off valuable organic matter that keeps the soil moist and fertile for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wala ni eshãa nibii ni jara wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I clear fresh land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie he hee ko amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The soil stores hidden weed seeds that lie dormant until land clearing allows sunlight and rainwater to reach them, giving them a head start before your crop can establish.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ buaa jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ anaa. Kɛyashi be mli ni ajie jɛmɛ lɛ ha hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ bote mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi dani onibii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants rolling up during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense to conserve moisture when the air gets dry and hot. It reduces the surface area exposed to the sun so the plant doesn't dry out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ. Ebaaha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akagbi.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme midday heat or uneven watering. The plant sheds flowers to save energy until growing conditions stabilize.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna haomɔ kɛjɛ gbi teŋ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that burn under full, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from taller trees to protect them while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ amli kɛha hebuu be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop yields drop when I plant my seed cuttings very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots compete heavily for the same soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin stalks and smaller harvests.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings look weak and wilted for a few days right after I transplant them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi gbii fioo komɛi beni midu amɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Transplanting disturbs the plant's small roots, causing brief shock while it gets used to the new ground. Shade and evening watering help the roots settle into the new soil.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ ni akɛwoɔ he kroko lɛ gbaa tso lɛ naa, ni ehaa ekpokpoɔ fioo beni ekɛ ehe woɔ he hee lɛ mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shia mli kɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land for four seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei ejwɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests that feed on that crop to multiply in the ground over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if my soil is moist enough for planting right after the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball in your palm; if it holds together without dripping wet water or crumbling into dry dust, the ground is ready for seed germination.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu yɛ onine mli. Kɛji amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieee nu loo amɛgbalaaa amɛfeɔ sũ ni egbi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so when there is not enough, the plant steals nitrogen from its old bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure fixes this.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. No hewɔ lɛ kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why is my cassava crop growing tall with lots of green leaves but giving me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni ebaa eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing big leaves instead of underground tubers. Cassava needs soil rich in potassium—such as wood ash or balanced potassium fertilizer—to direct its energy into expanding root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Cassava biɔ shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ tso sũ loo potassium ni sa jogbaŋŋ. koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba koni ekɛgbala shishifãi lɛ amli

english: Why do cowpeas make my soil healthier for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that have small bumps on their roots containing friendly bacteria. These bacteria take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, leaving free natural fertilizer behind for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi ni helai ni haa mɔ feɔ naanyo yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ Helai nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Rolling leaves is the corn plant's way of protecting itself from losing water in extreme heat. By rolling up, less leaf surface is exposed to the hot sun and dry wind, conserving moisture inside the plant until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni ŋmãa tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo ŋwɛi lɛ, hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers dry up and fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme dry weather, high heat, or lack of soil moisture. Maintaining shade trees on your farm keeps the air cool and humid, helping flowers stay on the branches and set pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso nine lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ pods.

english: Upward leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from the undersides of young leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying neem oil or appropriate insect treatments stops these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anɔ Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa ni ebaatsi baai heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil. This is usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells that prevent the roots from moving calcium up to the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei diji ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo be ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie calcium kɛya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the main mother tree. By removing most suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones, all the food goes into producing a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ jieɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni eshwɛɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Niyenii muu fɛɛ woɔ plantains ni dara ni tsii.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up into the sunlight so they can manufacture food efficiently for the underground tuber. Keeping leaves off the damp ground also prevents fungal diseases from spreading across the farm.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii jogbaŋŋ amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my cabbage seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu kaabii dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting too close causes cabbages to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This competition prevents them from forming big, firm heads, resulting in small, soft, leafy cabbages.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa kaabii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná yitsei wuji ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kaaba lɛ baafee bibioo ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ.

english: Why do tree crops like cocoa draw so much water out of the soil compared to short crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ kookoo jieɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsei kukuji ahe lɛ?

english: Tree crops have deep and extensive root systems that reach deep underground to pull large amounts of water to support their big trunks, heavy leaves, and crop pods.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni ejie nu babaoo ni ekɛfi amɛshishifãi wuji, baai ni tsii, kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Will planting large trees on my farm dry out the ground and hurt my other crops?
ga: Tsei wuji ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awui. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Large trees do take water from the soil, but they also provide shade that keeps the ground cool and reduces water loss from sunlight, so choosing the right shade tree helps protect soil moisture.
ga: Tsei wuji nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ehaa hulutsoo hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa nu ni hulu la lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ohala tsei ni sa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: How do I know if my land has enough underground water to keep cocoa trees alive through the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha cacao tsei ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Land with rich, dark soil that stays damp a few inches below the surface during dry periods usually holds enough groundwater to sustain long-term tree crops like cocoa.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli ewo duŋ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi inchi fioo komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Bei pii lɛ, amɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo nɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why should I dedicate my land to growing cocoa when my family cannot eat it for food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii? Beni miweku lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhe niyenii?

english: Cocoa is a cash crop meant for market sale, which brings in income to buy staples like rice and maize, pay school fees, and fund family expenses that food crops alone cannot cover.
ga: Cocoa ji shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa shika ni akɛheɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Wo skul nyɔmɔ ni okɛtsu weku lɛ shika ni niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ atsu he nii lɛ he nii.

english: Can I grow food crops on the same plot where I am starting my new cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mije mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting temporary food crops like plantain or cocoyam alongside young cocoa trees provides food and income for your family while giving necessary shade to the young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni akɛyeɔ nii yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantain loo cocoa ni ooodu kɛfata cocoa tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaha oweku lɛ aná niyenii kɛ shika. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ hu náa hulutsoo.

english: Why do tree crops take several years to give harvest while cassava or maize produce in just months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei aheɔ afii babaoo dani amɛkpaa nii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa loo ŋmãa woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Food crops like maize grow quick, shallow roots to produce seeds in one season, whereas tree crops spend their first few years building a strong trunk and deep roots before they can produce fruit year after year.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa daa oya ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwui yɛ be kome mli. Shi tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛtswaa tsei ahe tsei ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Is it better for me to have multiple small farms spread out or just one large farm in one place?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ maná ŋmɔji bibii babaoo ni gbɛ eshwa loo ŋmɔ agbo kome pɛ yɛ he kome?

english: Having multiple smaller farms helps lower your risk, because if pests or bad weather affect one area, your crops on another piece of land can still survive.
ga: Kɛ́ oyɛ ŋmɔji bibii babaoo lɛ, ebaa oshara ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ shi. Ejaakɛ kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ ná he ko nɔ hewalɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ he kroko lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi lolo.

english: How does having farms in different locations affect the types of crops I can grow?
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ hei srɔtoi lɛ Te enaa ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Different locations often have different soil types and water levels, so one plot may be perfect for water-loving cocoa while another drier plot is better suited for cassava or cashew.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi kɛ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ko baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sa kɛha kookoo ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ dumɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ kroko lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei loo ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ.

english: Why do I need to dry my crop harvest thoroughly before taking it to town to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Drying removes excess moisture from crops like cocoa or maize so they do not spoil, mold, or rot during transport to town and storage at buying stations.
ga: Nibii ni agbiɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmãa mli. Enɛ ji koni ekafite, ekafee ŋmɔtɔ loo ekafite yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa maŋ lɛ mli kɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ yɛ nihɔɔmɔ he lɛ.

english: Why do buyers in town pay different prices for the same crop depending on how it was cared for on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋtiase mli lɛ woɔ jara srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome he lɛ? Edamɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ amɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Crops that receive adequate water, proper shade, and careful drying yield higher quality produce, which fetches better prices at town buying centers than poorly managed harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ haa hulutsoo ni sa Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa anáa yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha jara ni hi aba kɛjɛ maŋtiase mli jarayeli hei fe ŋmaa ni akpaaa ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings start turning yellow and dying when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava to protect them from heat and conserve soil moisture while their roots get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Enɛ ji koni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa trees when I am planting a new farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ abɔ he beni mikɛ ŋmɔ hee miidu lɛ?

english: Spacing cocoa trees about 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet) gives each tree enough room for its roots to gather soil nutrients and allows air and light to circulate without overcrowding.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã kookoo tsei ateŋ lɛ feɔ aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3 (naji 10 x naji 10), ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ abua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la tsɔɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli tsɔ.

english: Why do so many tiny flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo shwieɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support. Many drop off naturally due to lack of pollination by tiny insects like midges, or because the tree is saving energy during dry weather.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ fe bɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ. Tsei babaoo gbeeɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ ahewɔ, loo akɛni tsei buɔ hewalɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are some of my tiny green cocoa pods turning shriveled and black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni ji So mine lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree discards excess pods it cannot feed, but it can also be an early sign of fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii lɛ. Shi ebaanyɛ efee mra be mli okadi hu ni tsɔɔ fungal hela, tamɔ pods diji.

english: What causes the leaves on my cocoa trees to get dry brown patches and curl up?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔtɔ, ni egbi, ni ebɔle ehe?

english: This leaf damage is often caused by mirids (capsids), small insects that suck sap from young leaves and shoots, making the plant dry out especially during warm weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirids (capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ baa bibii kɛ tsei ashishi nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ baa. Ha tso lɛ agbi, titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm has been infected with cocoa swollen shoot disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Cocoa Bud Swollen Hela lɛ emɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for swollen sections on young stems or roots, red or yellow patterns along leaf veins, and smaller, rounded pods. Infected trees must be removed to protect the rest of the farm.
ga: Taomɔ hei ni efuu yɛ tso lɛ shishi loo shishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ. Ayɛ mfoniri tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ahe. kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni abu ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to apply fertilizer to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo kookoo tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Apply fertilizer at the beginning of the major rainy season when the soil is moist. This helps the roots absorb the nutrients quickly, whereas applying during a dry spell can waste the fertilizer or burn the roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii afite loo eha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around the base of my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and nutrients away from cocoa trees. Keeping the area around the tree trunks clean prevents weeds from competing with your crop and reduces places where pests can hide.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli. He ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Tsei akutsei lɛ ahe tsemɔ baatsi jwɛi ni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaye akaŋ lɛ naa. ni ajie hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ lɛ shi.

english: Pruning removes unwanted shoots (chupons) that suck food away from the tree, and opening up the canopy allows sunlight and air to pass through, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni ataooo (chupons) ni nuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. kɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ ni agbeleɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvesting when their skin color turns fully yellow or orange. Harvesting pods while they are still green means the beans inside will not be fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛhewolo lɛ su batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi be mli ni amɛji eŋɔli lolo lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛŋ kwraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the nutrients they need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure directly around my young tomato plants right after cleaning the coop?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee awo he fɛɛ he. Ani mi tomato tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ adara kɛji mitsumɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and hot for tender plant roots because it contains high levels of ammonia and salts that can burn the crop. You should let the manure sit and rot in a pile for a few weeks to cool down before applying it to your field.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee lɛ ehee lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ edɔ tsɔ kɛha tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eyɛ ammonia kɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii. Esa akɛ oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli otsii fioo komɛi koni edɔ dani okɛwo ŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why does mixing poultry manure into sandy soil help my crops stay green longer during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ashishifãi ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Poultry manure adds organic matter to sandy soil, which acts like a sponge that holds onto rainwater and soil nutrients. This organic sponge keeps moisture around the crop roots for a longer time during dry spells.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, emɔɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ organic sponge nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss through evaporation. This is a natural defense mechanism that allows the plant to go dormant and keep its underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa tsei wɔɔ shi. ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants droop during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil. The temporary drooping reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun to save water, and the plant usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ haa baa lɛ nɔ hulu la baa shi koni ekɛbu nu he. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he waaa amɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my tomato plants to curl up and turn yellowish green?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit a plant virus while feeding. Controlling sap-sucking insects early helps prevent the leaves from curling and damaging the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kplukai ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, lack of water, or excess nitrogen in the soil. When the plant feels stressed, it saves energy by dropping blossoms instead of spending energy to grow fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Beni tsei nuɔ he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa lɛ Ehereɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu aduawai.

english: Why are some kernels missing from my maize cobs when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi bɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when the silks on the maize cob are not properly pollinated by the dust from the flowers at the top of the plant. Drought or extreme heat during the flowering stage can dry out the pollen and leave gaps on the cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ sũ ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛɛɛ siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Hɔmɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I plant them in a field without any shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that easily burn under intense direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains next to cocoa provides cover and keeps the surrounding air cool while the young cocoa roots become established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ teeɔ shi ni ehaa edɔɔ be mli ni cocoa shishifãi bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to catch light instead of building thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ tsei lɛ amli tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ, amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la lɛ.

english: How do I know if a chemical medicine is officially approved for use on my cocoa farm in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ akpɛlɛ tsofa ko nɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: The Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) regularly tests and publishes a list of certified agrochemicals, such as Cocoa Set and Aseda. You can confirm approval by asking your local extension officer or checking for official COCOBOD certification seals on the package.
ga: Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) lɛ kaa tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ tamɔ kookoo kɛ aceda kui lɛ amli daa ni ekɛwoɔ wolo nɔ. Obaanyɛ oma nɔ mi akɛ okpɛlɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ nitsulɔ ni ooobi lɛ nɔ. Aloo kwɛmɔ COCOBOD he odaseyeli ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What should I do if a disease on my cocoa trees keeps coming back even after I spray it?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji hela ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ po sɛɛ?

english: Persistent symptoms usually mean the disease has become resistant to the current chemical or that the wrong product is being used. Switching to an officially recommended treatment and clearing away infected pods or branches helps stop the cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ he okadii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii amrɔ nɛɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu hela lɛ he nii loo akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ etsu nii. Kɛ́ mɔ ko tsake kɛtee tsofai ni maŋ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ anɔ, ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekpa hela lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just buy any cheap pesticide available in the market for my cocoa crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miheɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jara waaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ateŋ ekome kɛhaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ?

english: Unapproved or counterfeit chemicals can damage leaves, leave harmful residues in cocoa beans, reduce yield, and cause crop buyers to reject your harvest because they do not meet safety standards.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo amalei baanyɛ afite baai lɛ. Eshiɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ kookoo yibii amli, ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpooɔ okpamɔ lɛ ejaakɛ eshɛɛɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he mlai ahe.

english: Can I apply crop medicines directly onto the trunk and pods, or should I only spray the leaves?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsei ahe tsofai awo tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ baai lɛ pɛ nɔ?

english: Different treatments target different parts of the plant. Some chemicals work externally on the pods and leaves to kill fungi on contact, while others are absorbed through the trunk or roots to protect the plant from within.
ga: Tsamɔi srɔtoi lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ fãi srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. Tsofai komɛi tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛgbe ŋmeii lɛ kɛji amɛshɛ amɛhe. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai komɛi tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi lɛ amli koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ emli.

english: What is Cocoa Set and what does it do for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo set? Ni mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao lɛ he?

english: Cocoa Set is a COCOBOD-approved agrochemical formulated to treat and prevent common cocoa pod diseases, helping the tree recover strength and protect developing pods from decay.
ga: Cocoa Kit ji agrochemical fɔmla ko ni COCOBOD ekpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsaa helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ cocoa pod mli lɛ ni akɛtsiɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebuɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: What is Aseda chemical used for in cocoa farming?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofai Aseda kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Aseda is an approved treatment used by Ghanaian cocoa farmers to protect cocoa trees against fungal infections like Black Pod disease, ensuring pods remain healthy until harvest.
ga: Aseda ji tsofa ko ni kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ koni akɛbu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ he, ni ekwɛɔ koni kookoo tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn dark and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni amɛgboi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is typically Black Pod disease, caused by fungi that thrive in cool, moist conditions. Applying approved protective sprays and trimming thick branches to let in sunlight stops the rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni ofolɔ tsei lɛ amli waa koni hulu la lɛ akpa fitemɔ.

english: Can a disease inside the trunk of a cocoa tree show symptoms on the outside pods?
ga: Ani helai ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie okadii akpo yɛ kponɔgbɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, many crop pathogens live within the stem or vascular system of the tree and show symptoms on the leaves and outer pods. Proper treatments address both internal tree health and external pod protection.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei amli helai babaoo hiɔ tsei akutso loo lá fãji amli. ni etsɔɔ okadii yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ Tsamɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli hewalɛnamɔ lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Is it safe to mix two different crop medicines together to make them stronger?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsei ahe tsofai enyɔ baafutu mli koni amɛhe awa?

english: No, mixing unapproved chemicals can cause chemical reactions that burn your crop's foliage, render the medicines useless, or produce toxic fumes dangerous to the person spraying.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ko ni shãa tso lɛ baai lɛ aba. ehaa tsofa feɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa loo ekɛ lasu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ mɔ ni shwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ awui baa

english: How can I prevent fungal diseases from spreading across my cocoa farm during the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmeii ahe helai anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã kookoo ŋmɔji amli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Maintain good farm sanitation by pruning excess shade leaves, removing and burying infected pods, and applying COCOBOD-approved preventative sprays before heavy rains begin.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ kpakpa nɔ kɛtsɔ baai ni yɔɔ shade fe nine lɛ ni ooofo mli lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ ni ofu pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni okɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he ni COCOBOD kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aje shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to cover them, the intense sun burns their leaves and dries out the soil, causing the leaves to scorch and wither.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baaha hulutsoo lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni egboɔ.

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves usually means the maize lacks nitrogen, a key food plant needs to stay green. When nitrogen is short in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the newest leaves at the top to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays trapped around the roots for long periods, it drowns the roots and creates damp conditions where rot-causing fungus thrives.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by intense afternoon heat or lack of water. If the weather is too hot, the pollen inside the flower dies before it can form a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ dani etsɔɔ tomato.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam stems to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tsei kɛha sweet potato tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need sunlight to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground toward the sun, which keeps the leaves healthy and helps the plant build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni hulu la he hia koni eye niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ mli waa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I find caterpillars hiding deep inside the central funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm hide inside the leaf funnel because the tender inner leaves are soft to eat, and the funnel protects them from birds, direct sunlight, and rain.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teɔ amɛhe yɛ baai amli ejaakɛ baai ni yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni ŋɔɔ waa. Ni gbɛ lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he.

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil for nearby crops.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one main plantain stem, they steal food, water, and sunlight from each other. Removing extra suckers allows the main plant to grow a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ single main trunk Amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akwɛ̃ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even if the ground was moist in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During the hottest hours, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can drink it up. The leaves droop temporarily to protect themselves from losing more water, but they recover once the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni baafite ekoŋŋ lɛ he. Shi ebaahiɛ ahi ehe nɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my small vegetable seeds right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ aduawai bibii? Dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa

english: Heavy rains can wash away tiny vegetable seeds, bury them too deep in mud, or cause them to rot in pooled water before they have a chance to sprout.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo aduawai dumɔwui bibii lɛ, ni ekɛfu amɛ yɛ muji lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. loo egbo yɛ nu ni fata he lɛ mli dani ená hegbɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why does a crop disease start on just a few plants in one corner of my farm and then spread to the rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe hela ko jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tsei fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koŋ kome mli lɛ anɔ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa mɛi krokomɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Diseases often start in a small area because insects, wind, or rain carry fungi or viruses to nearby healthy plants. Dividing your farm into small sections and checking plants row by row helps you catch infected plants early before the sickness spreads across your whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela jeɔ shishi yɛ he bibioo ko. Enɛ ji akɛ, kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo nugbɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai baa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ooojara mli bibii bibii Ni okwɛ tsei lɛ amli yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Dani hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my farm and check individual plants instead of just looking from the edge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni makwɛ tso fɛɛ tso moŋ fe ni makwɛ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Diseases and pests usually hide under leaves or inside plant stems where you cannot see them from a distance. Inspecting your farm area by area allows you to spot early symptoms like leaf spots or insect damage before your whole crop is destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ashishi loo tsei ashishifãi amli he ni onyɛɛɛ ona amɛ kɛjɛ shɔŋŋ. Kpokpaa nɔkwɛmɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona mra be mli okadii tamɔ baa mli ŋmɔlɔ loo kooloi ni efite. Dani obaafite onibii fɛɛ

english: Why do I see holes in my crop leaves even when I do not see any insects on the farm during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Many crop pests, like armyworms and caterpillars, feed at night or hide inside the leaves and soil during the hot day. Inspecting under leaves and inside crop whorls section by section helps you catch them before they eat your entire field.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo ahe ji ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ loo amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli fã fɛɛ fã lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ dani amɛhe he fɛɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they are ready to be harvested?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shady conditions. It attacks pods individually, turning them dark, and spreads quickly to nearby pods if the infected ones are not removed from the farm immediately.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Ebaatutua pods lɛ ekomekomei. ha amɛfee duŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya kɛya ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli Kɛji ajieee ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree has swollen shoot disease before the whole tree dies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo tso ko ŋmeii efuu dani tso lɛ gbo?

english: Swollen shoot disease causes swollen joints on young stems, red vein patterns on leaves, and small, rounded pods. Inspecting your trees branch by branch helps you spot these signs early so the infected tree can be removed to protect surrounding healthy trees.
ga: Bud swollen hela lɛ kɛ fãji ni efuu yɛ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Linei tsuji yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo Kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ nine fɛɛ nine mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona okadii nɛɛ mra. No sɛɛ lɛ, abaanyɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛbu tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe. yɛ hewalɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow from the bottom leaves going upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow first, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The crop responds by moving whatever nutrients it has left to the newer leaves at the top to keep growing, leaving the older lower leaves to starve.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ haa hetoo kɛtsɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ekɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are crops in one area of my field growing very tall while crops in another section stay short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli he kome lɛ shwereɔ babaoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ he kroko lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ kuku ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Soil depth, water drainage, and nutrient levels vary across different parts of a field. Crops respond directly to their immediate soil environment, so plants in patches with rocky soil or poor drainage will grow much slower than those in rich, loose soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ amɛshikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ he nii tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ loo nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo fe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni sũ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When crops are crowded, they become weak and produce very small tubers because no individual plant gets enough food to thrive.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ bulbs bibii waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to trim off extra branches from my cocoa trees when I want more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mifo cacao tso niji ni fa fe nine lɛ mli be mli ni miitao ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches helps the tree send its food and water directly into growing pods rather than useless leaves. It also allows air and sunlight to pass through the branches, which prevents humidity from causing fungal diseases.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji amli, ni no haaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: Local weeds are wild plants that naturally adapted over time to survive in poor soil and dry weather. When rain falls, weeds steal water and nutrients faster than farm crops, which stunts your crop's growth if weeds are not cleared early.
ga: Native weeds ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ mra.

english: Why is March such an important month for me to start preparing my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ March ji nyɔŋ ni he hiaa mi koni mije mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahe saamɔ shishi lɛ?

english: March marks the critical transition period just before the major rainy season begins in Ghana. Preparing your farm during this time ensures your cocoa trees are healthy, clean, and ready to absorb rainwater and nutrients to produce a strong main crop.
ga: March ji tsakemɔ be ni he hiaa waa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana. Kɛ́ osaa oŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha o-cocoa tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ, amɛhe atse, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni mli wa.

english: Is there a specific time of year I should start getting my trees ready for the next harvest?
ga: Ani be ko yɛ afi lɛ mli ni esa akɛ mabɔi mitsei lɛ ahe saamɔ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, farm preparation should ideally start around March before the main rains arrive. Starting early gives the trees enough time to recover from the dry season and build up strength to support flowers and pod growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ aje shishi yɛ March aaafee, dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ aba. Kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ haa tso lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu nii kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni etswa hewalɛ ni eye ebua fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ

english: What does an extension officer mean when they tell me to 'prepare' my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ beni amɛkɛɛ mi akɛ ‘misaa’ kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Preparing your trees means clearing weeds from around the base, pruning dead or overcrowded branches, removing mistletoe parasite plants, and making sure sunlight can reach the middle of the tree canopy.
ga: Tso lɛ he saamɔ tsɔɔ akɛ abaajie jwɛi ni bɔle eshishigbɛ lɛ, ni abaafolɔ niji ni egboi loo ni egbɔjɔ fe nine lɛ. Mistletoe helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ hulu la ni ashɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: Pruning excess branches allows air and sunlight to pass freely through the tree. Good airflow keeps the farm dry and prevents fungal diseases, while sunlight encourages the tree to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la lɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are my cocoa trees tall and leafy but not producing many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai shi ebɛ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: When a tree has too many unattended leaves and branches, it spends all its energy maintaining that greenery instead of flowering. Preparing and pruning the tree redirects its food and energy into making strong cocoa pods.
ga: Beni tso ko yɛ baai kɛ niji babaoo ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii koni ehiɛ eŋɔli lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Tso lɛ he saamɔ kɛ ekpamɔ haa niyenii kɛ hewalɛ yaa kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: How often do I need to walk through my farm to check on my cocoa trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakwɛ kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: You should visit and inspect your cocoa trees at least once a week. Regular visits allow you to spot early signs of diseases, unwanted weeds, or insect attacks before they spread to the rest of the farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ oyasara ni okwɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli shikome yɛ otsi mli. Saramɔi ni ooofee daa lɛ haa onaa hela lɛ he okadii lɛ mra. jwɛi ni ataooo loo kooloi bibii ni baatutua amɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: What will happen to my cocoa trees if I leave them unattended for a few months?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ?

english: Neglect allows weeds to grow tall and steal nutrients from the soil, while pests like capsids and diseases like black pod quickly spread through the farm, drastically reducing your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids kɛ helai tamɔ black pods gbɛ eshwa ŋmɔji amli oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why should I clear the weeds around the base of my cocoa trees before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Clearing weeds around the tree trunk ensures that heavy rains wash soil nutrients straight to the cocoa roots instead of feeding the weeds. It also prevents excess moisture from building up around the trunk and causing root rot.
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa kookoo shishifãi lɛ anɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha jwɛi lɛ niyenii. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ he ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How does clearing dead pods and branches early in the year protect my cocoa from diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei aniji ni egboi lɛ ahe saamɔ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu kookoo he kɛjɛ helai ahe?

english: Fungal spores that cause black pod disease often survive the dry season inside old, dead pods and branches left on the tree. Removing them early stops diseases from spreading when wet weather returns.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli yɛ ŋmeii ni egboi kɛ tsei niji momo ni ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do I need to clean the ground around my cocoa tree before applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsumɔ he ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Cocoa tsei dani awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Removing dead leaves, weeds, and debris around the trunk base allows the fertilizer to sink directly into the soil where the shallow feeding roots of the cocoa tree can absorb it quickly.
ga: Ajieɔ baai ni egboi, jwɛi, kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Tso lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni kookoo shishifãi ni nuɔ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ oya

english: Why do agricultural extension officers recommend storing harvested groundnuts in cocoa bags instead of plastic bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ awo kookoo kotokui amli moŋ fe plastic kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa bags are made of natural jute fibers, which have a loose weave that allows fresh air to pass through easily. Plastic bags trap moisture inside, causing groundnuts to sweat, turn moldy, and rot.
ga: Akɛ adebɔɔ mli jute fibers ni afee lɛ mlɛo lɛ feɔ cocoa kotokui. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ oya. Plastic kotokui lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. Ha ŋmeii afee ŋmɔtɔ ni efite

english: What is the difference between a jute sack and a cocoa bag?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ jute kotokui kɛ kookoo kotokui ateŋ?

english: They are the exact same thing! 'Jute sack' is the general name for bags woven from natural plant fibers, but in Ghana, people commonly call them 'cocoa bags' because they are widely used to store and transport cocoa.
ga: Amɛji nɔ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ! ‘Jute sack’ ji gbɛi ni akɛtsɛɔ kotokui ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe tsɔi fee lɛ. Shi yɛ Ghana lɛ Bei pii lɛ Mɛi tsɛɔ kotokui nɛɛ akɛ ‘kokoo kotokui’ ejaakɛ akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo kɛtoɔ kookoo kɛyaa he kroko.

english: Can I store my harvested groundnuts in tightly woven plastic rice sacks if I don't have jute bags?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ awo plastic ŋmã kotokui ni akpɛ́ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli? Kɛji akɛ jute kotoku ko bɛ

english: Plastic sacks restrict airflow, which is risky. Groundnuts need continuous air movement to stay dry, so storing them in plastic traps dampness and speeds up spoilage unless they are completely dry.
ga: Plastic kotokui tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa, ni eji oshara. Peanuts biɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle ehe daa koni ehi shi ni egbi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii to plastic mli lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaafite oya, ja amɛgbi kwraa.

english: Why do my harvested groundnuts feel warm and damp when left inside a tightly closed bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts ni mikpa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku ko ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts continue to 'breathe' after being harvested, releasing small amounts of natural moisture and heat. Sealed bags trap this warm steam, creating a damp environment that causes crops to spoil quickly.
ga: Peanuts yaa nɔ ‘emuɔ’ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ fioo ko kpo. Baagi ko ni atsĩ naa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lasu ni mli edɔ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ oya.

english: Why is constant air movement so important for groundnuts after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa nɔ etsɔɔ mli lɛ he hiaa yɛ ŋmeii amli beni mifo amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly dug groundnuts carry a lot of hidden moisture inside their shells. Constant airflow carries away this dampness so the groundnuts dry out evenly and stay safe from internal decay.
ga: Peanuts ni atsa ehee Fɛ̃i babaoo yɛ etsitsi lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ oya lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ fitemɔ he.

english: What actually happens to groundnuts if air cannot pass through their storage containers?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmeii anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli?

english: Without airflow, moisture builds up inside the container. This humidity causes fungi and harmful mold to grow on the shells, reducing crop quality and making the groundnuts unsafe to eat or sell.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ, Fɛ̃i baabua ehe naa yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ anɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ahe nibii baa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔɔ.

english: Why do groundnuts spoil faster in humid weather if they are packed tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When tightly packed without proper ventilation, humid air gets trapped between the pods. Groundnuts need breathable materials to let fresh air pass through and flush out that trapped moisture.
ga: Kɛji akɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ. Nibii ni haa mɔ muɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmei koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do both cocoa beans and groundnuts use the same woven jute sacks for storage in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ kɛ jute kotokui ni akpɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii kɛtoɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Both groundnuts and cocoa beans are delicate post-harvest crops that spoil if kept damp. The woven jute fibers in cocoa bags protect the crops from physical damage while letting air pass freely to preserve their quality.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cocoa beans fɛɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. ni baafite kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ Jute tsɔji ni akɛwo kookoo kotokui amli lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ oya koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does using breathable jute bags help protect my groundnuts for next season's planting?
ga: Te jute kotokui ni haa mumɔ tsɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-peanuts lɛ he kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Breathable bags allow moisture to escape, keeping the groundnuts dry and cool. This prevents seeds from rotting or sprouting too early inside the bag, ensuring high germination when planted next season.
ga: Baagi ni haa mɔ muɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo. Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhe ajɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akafite loo amɛkakwɛ̃ oya tsɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni nɔ kwɔ baa kɛji adu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my stored groundnuts are getting enough airflow in my storehouse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mi-nitoohe lɛ?

english: If your storage bags feel dry on the outside, cool when you touch them, and have a natural earthy smell rather than a musty odor, it means fresh air is successfully passing through your breathable sacks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onitoo kotoku lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi yɛ kponɔgbɛ ni edɔ kɛji ota he Ni eŋɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ fe ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baanyɛ atsɔ okotoku ni okɛmuɔ nii lɛ mli yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when I put them in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani etsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ he ko?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the node buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to grow backward underground, resulting in weak stems and very small, poorly formed roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji lɛ esa akɛ odu amɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei aku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni shishifãi lɛ hu feɔ bibii waa ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes instead of just growing flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to lift their leaves off the ground and expose them to as much sunlight as possible. When vines lie flat on the hot soil, leaves get shaded, leaf diseases spread faster, and the plant cannot make enough food to produce big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni baaha amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛha hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Foliar helai baagbɛ ashwã oya. ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo bulb agboi.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more plants on my small farm?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni makwɛ nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli hu?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete against each other for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no grain at all.
ga: Amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛdumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build green, healthy leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time helps restore the green color and supports fast growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and its roots rot in the soil, they release this natural plant food for future crops like maize to feed on.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshishifãi lɛ egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ amɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa, koni amɛye.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into cups and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on tender leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and allows normal growth to continue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with powdery dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn ni yɔɔ sũ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baai lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day, eating the tender leaves before they unfold and leaving behind waste that looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛjie amɛhe kpo. ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei kpakpai.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making it impossible for the flower to form a fruit. When temperatures stay too high, the plant sheds its unpollinated flowers to save energy until cooler conditions return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo yibii Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct harsh sunlight and hot dry winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural leaf shield that traps soil moisture and blocks excessive heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa. Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe tsei ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ naa.

english: Why can paddy rice grow while sitting in flooded water for days, but my maize plants die if water stays on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu afua mli gbii babaoo lɛ? Shi ani mi-abele tsei lɛ baanyɛ agboi kɛji nu tee nɔ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli?
