english: Rice plants have hollow air passages inside their stems that carry oxygen from the leaves down into flooded roots. Maize plants lack these air tubes, so their roots drown and rot when underwater for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsuji ni mli ewo muji yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ. Abɛi tso lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ amɛhi nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green and strong. This can happen if the soil lacks nutrients or if heavy rains have washed the nitrogen away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I leave dry plant leaves on top of my field instead of burning them before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei ahe baai ni egbi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ dani madu?

english: Leaving dry leaves on the field creates a blanket called mulch. This blanket protects the soil from the hot sun, keeps water in the ground longer, and turns into free food for your crops as it rots.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Kuntu nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ni ebafeɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa onibii lɛ kɛ́ egbo.

english: Yam plants naturally like to climb so their leaves can catch as much sunlight as possible. When you stake your yam vines, the leaves get full sunshine to make food, which helps the tuber underground grow bigger.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, sweet potatoes sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɔ, no hewɔ lɛ amɛbaai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji ofo sweet potato wain tso lɛ Baai lɛ baaná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛhoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees keep dying when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in harsh sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing trees or plantains nearby creates shade that protects the cocoa trees until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni shwereɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or thrips are sucking the sap out of your plant leaves, or that a virus has infected the plant. Removing infected leaves early helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips he okadi. Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso baai amli loo hela ko yɛ ni miitswa tso lɛ Baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: What causes small ragged holes to appear in the leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ baai amli lɛ baa?

english: These holes are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the young leaves inside the plant funnel. Checking your farm early lets you clear them out before they destroy the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ojie amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: The very first rain can be a false start to the rainy season. If you plant right away and the rain stops for weeks, the hot ground will dry up and kill your newly sprouted seeds.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo lɛ, hei ni mli edɔ lɛ baagbi ni ebaafite dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground near the base of the stem begins to crack as the thick roots push against the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Will planting cowpeas together in the same field as my maize spoil the maize crop?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baafite ŋmãa lɛ?

english: No, planting cowpeas with maize is actually helpful. Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting like natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Dabi, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-corn lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant gets either too much or too little water. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ ná nu babaoo loo fioo pɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and wither when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides living shade that shields the seedlings from direct heat and keeps moisture in the ground while their roots mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Nurse tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the tops are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛyiteŋgbɛi lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plant leaves use to stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the roots helps the plant green up and produce full corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei ahe baai kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata he lɛ he. Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ewoɔ ŋmãa ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: What is eating tiny holes inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ cone lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow deep into the leaves at the top of the plant. Inspecting the field early and applying targeted neem oil treatments or approved pesticides into the plant funnels helps clear the infestation before it destroys the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ kɛyaa dani efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the tiny leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stalk wastes energy turning its sprouts upward, which leads to weak plants and much smaller cassava roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji adu lɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: Yam plants store energy in their underground tubers by absorbing sunshine through their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves lifted off the damp ground where they can catch maximum sunlight and avoids leaf rot diseases caused by soil contact.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ baai ni fiteɔ hela ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ he

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme dry heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently damp around the roots and ensuring proper spacing between plants helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I chop off the extra small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Small side shoots (suckers) steal water and nutrients from the main bearing plantain tree. Keeping only one strong stem alongside the mother plant ensures the main stalk grows thick enough to carry a heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso bibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛ (suckers) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akwɛ tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like brick just a couple of days after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ brikii yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Soil hardens quickly when it lacks organic matter, like decayed leaves and manure, which act like tiny sponges to hold water. Mixing organic material into the topsoil improves its texture so it remains soft and holds moisture much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji bibioo ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shi Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli futu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo, ni eha efee blɛoo ni eha nu lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan wind affect my field crops, and how can I protect them?
ga: Te Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Harmattan winds suck moisture rapidly out of plant foliage and dry out the ground. Covering the bare soil around your crop roots with dried grass or leaves (mulching) keeps water from evaporating fast during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ oya ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛbaabɔle ohe lɛ Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo otsei lɛ ashishi (mulching) lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ akafee oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or beans together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground. When planted alongside maize, they feed the soil and help neighboring maize grow stronger without needing extra bought fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni edara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why should I cut off some of the branches from my cocoa trees when they seem to be growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-kookoo niji lɛ ekomɛi? Etamɔ nɔ ni nakai niji lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lolo?

english: Cutting or pruning unwanted branches helps the tree direct its energy into growing healthy pods instead of extra leaves. It also allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree, which prevents dampness and diseases like black pod.
ga: Niji ni ataooo lɛ ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai baafata he. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu shɛɔ tso lɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji anaa.

english: Which specific branches am I supposed to remove first when caring for my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛɛ niji pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ majie klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ mikwɛ kookoo tso ko nɔ?

english: You should start by removing dead, diseased, or broken branches, as well as water shoots—which are straight, fast-growing green shoots that suck food away from the tree without producing any pods.
ga: Esa akɛ oje shishi kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni ekumɔ, ni nu mli ŋmeii fata he lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei eŋɔli ni daa oya, ni amɛmuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa.

english: How do I know the best time of year to prune branches on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to prune depends on your local weather, but generally, it is done right after the main harvest season or just before the rains start. This gives the tree enough time to recover and prepare for fresh flowering.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni okɛbaakpa tsei lɛ damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, afeɔ yɛ nikpamɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ loo dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ni esaa ehe kɛha fɔfɔi heei.

english: What will happen to my cocoa tree if I cut off too many branches at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mifolɔ niji babaoo shikome?

english: If you cut off too many main branches, you shock the tree and expose the main trunk to harsh sunlight. This sunshine can dry out the bark, reduce your pod harvest, or even cause the tree to die.
ga: Kɛji ofolɔ niji titrii babaoo tsɔ Tso lɛ he baakpãtã ni ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashɛ eshishifã titri lɛ he. Hulu la nɛɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ yibii lɛ agbi. Tsɔɔmɔ pod ŋmɔshi nibii loo ha tso lɛ po agbo.

english: What are those fast-growing straight shoots coming out near the root of my cocoa tree, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mihe?

english: Those shoots are called chupons or water shoots. They grow very fast and steal valuable water and nutrients from the main tree without giving you any fruit, so you should cut them off while they are still small.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ chupons loo nu ŋmeii. Amɛdaraa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛhaaa bo yibii ko kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ amɛ beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Why does my neighbor's pruning style look different from what works on my own cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tsei ni mifoɔ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning depends on your specific land and climate conditions. A farm under thick shade trees needs lighter branch trimming than a farm exposed to full sun, because every piece of land has different sunlight, soil, and moisture levels.
ga: Shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɔ ni oookpa lɛ damɔ. Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa ni tsii shishi lɛ biɔ ni afolɔ amɛmli fioo fe ŋmɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ fã fɛɛ fã yɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ kɛ hulutsoo be srɔtoi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle too much direct heat and bright sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains or temporary cover trees around them, their leaves burn because they lose water faster than their young roots can absorb it.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ni akɛhaa baai lɛ ahe be kukuoo ko bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baashã ejaakɛ amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa flowers and pods grow straight out of the thick branches and main trunk instead of small twigs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei niji ni mli tse kɛ tsei wuji amli moŋ fe niji bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are heavy fruits, so the tree naturally flowers on its thickest branches and main trunk where there is enough strength to support the weight of the growing pods until they are ready for harvest.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ji aduawai ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei niji ni mli wa fe fɛɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi wuji lɛ anɔ, ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishi kɛyashi be mli ni amɛbaafee klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ.

english: Why should I stop my cocoa trees from growing too tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mi-kokoo tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ tsɔ?

english: Tall cocoa trees make it very difficult for you to harvest pods, prune dead branches, or spray against pests. Keeping trees at a reasonable height encourages branches to spread sideways where you can easily reach and care for them.
ga: Cacao tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmeii. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ. Aloo ewa waa akɛ aaashwie tsɛŋemɔ helai. Tso lɛ ni oooha ehi shi yɛ he ni sa lɛ baaye abua ni niji lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya afãi lɛ. he ni obaanyɛ oya jɛmɛ oya ni okwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How does leaving too many thick leaves and branches on my trees cause my cocoa pods to rot?
ga: Baai kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse ni ajieɔ lɛ Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni nɔ ni fa fe nine yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ aha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbo?

english: When a tree has too many thick branches, air cannot move through and rainwater stays trapped on the leaves and pods. This wet, dark environment makes it easy for the black pod disease fungus to grow and destroy your crop.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ niji ni mli wa babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli. ni nugbɔ nu baakpɛtɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe Shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ haa ewaa akɛ ŋmeii diji lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to strong sunlight and dry winds. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of straight up or flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafee nɔ ni ja loo nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at an angle helps the roots grow deeper and spread evenly. This firmly anchors the plant against strong winds and gives the tubers enough space to swell properly.
ga: Yucca tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa bulb lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfuu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to grow healthy green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say I should plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts like natural fertilizer for your maize while also spreading across the ground to keep weeds from taking over.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu koni jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific soil nutrients and lets maize pests build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cassava lets the soil recover and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi hoɔ, ni ehaa abele mli tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Why must I put tall wood stakes next to my yam plants when the vines start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni wain tso lɛ jeɔ shishi edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch direct sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more energy the plant generates to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la lɛ naa baai lɛ, Babaoo ni tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ lɛ, babaoo ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ e-bulbs wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves—called mulching—stops the heat from drying out the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi dɔlɛ naa ni etsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and shoots from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni jɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches and weak shoots allows sunlight and air to move freely through the tree. This reduces humidity that causes black pod disease and forces the tree to put its energy into producing big pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when temperatures get too high, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when there is not enough phosphorus in the soil to support fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai akwɛ̃.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the leaf sap, or by a virus carried by those pests. Controlling the pests with proper sprays allows new leaves to grow back healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahe nibii ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha baai heei lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water collects around the roots in flat, heavy soil. Planting your yams on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni tsii nɔ. Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit if I bury them deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani dumɔwui woɔ yibii kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Burying a plantain sucker too deep smothers its root center, making it hard for the main shoot to push up and absorb nutrients. Placing the growing point just below topsoil level lets the plant spread roots quickly and produce fruit sooner.
ga: Kɛ́ ofu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso titri lɛ akɛ ebaatsi ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii. Kɛ́ okɛ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã oya ni ewo yibii oya.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of big green leaves, but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen—often from overusing animal manure—the cassava plant spends all its energy growing foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and black right on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark conditions. Clearing weeds around the base and pruning extra foliage lets sunlight and air dry out the trees, keeping the fungus away.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ ni afo baai krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi akakwɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow and curling up early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling early in maize growth usually indicates a lack of nitrogen nutrients in the soil or damage from Fall Armyworm pests eating the central shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shwereɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni shwereɔ mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nɔ ni fall armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ efite.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing and drop their leaves when the dry Harmattan winds start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds pull moisture out of plant leaves faster than roots can pull water from the soil, forcing the plant to shed leaves to survive. Covering the soil around the base with dry straw retains soil moisture during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei afɔse amɛ baai lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture changes drastically from dry to wet. Consistent morning watering helps the plant keep its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛtee nɔ ni edɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my watermelons crack and split open right before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miitswa ni amɛmiitswa dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack when a long dry spell is suddenly followed by heavy rain or excessive watering. The inside of the melon absorbs water and grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu hoɔ fe nine ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Watermelon lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest grow into smaller, weaker crops than packaged seeds bought from the agro-store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ dara ni amɛbatsɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ oshara fe dumɔwui ni awo mli ni ahe yɛ ŋmɔ mli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought seeds are often hybrid varieties specially bred for high vigor in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities in the next generation, resulting in smaller yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni atsɔse amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa mli eyɛ mli akɛ Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During the hottest part of the day, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. Wilting is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun and save moisture; the leaves usually bounce back once the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Wilting ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛba hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛbuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Baai lɛ fɔɔ sɛɛkuu kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why can sorghum survive long dry spells much better than my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum has a deeper and more extensive root system that can reach water far below the surface. Its leaves also have a waxy coating that traps moisture inside, and the plant can temporarily stop growing during severe heat without dying, unlike maize which dries up quickly.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ waa ni baanyɛ ashɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he. Ebaai lɛ hu yɛ nɔ ko ni tamɔ waxy ni haa ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ emli. Ni tsei baanyɛ akpa amɛdalɛ be kukuoo ko kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni mli edɔ waa mli ni amɛgbooo. Esoro lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ he.

english: Tomatoes crack when water intake is uneven, such as heavy rain after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit absorbs water rapidly and grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Tomato tswaa kɛji nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of young maize is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the nutrient that helps plants build strong, green leaves, and when there is not enough, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishi baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli. Ni kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family and have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When these plants die and decay, that nitrogen remains in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi ni amɛfite Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on all their leaves to make food and grow large tubers underground. Lifting the vines off the wet ground with stakes catches more light and prevents fungal diseases from spreading onto the leaves from damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei tsu nii kɛwo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa enáa la babaoo ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does paddy rice need to grow in shallow standing water while other crops die in flooded soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes in their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots under water so they do not suffocate. Holding standing water in the field also prevents weeds from growing and competing with the rice for food.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni mli ewo muji yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi koni amɛkagbɔjɔ. Nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu haaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ akaŋ koni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without growing into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects like midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower so fruit can form. If the weather is extremely dry, if bad weather drives the insects away, or if the tree lacks proper nutrients, the flowers fall off unpollinated.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii fioo komɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi amli kɛya fɔfɔi krokomɛi amli koni aduawai aba. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ehiii lɛ, shwiemɔ kooloi bibii lɛ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them in the field after the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains make the soil waterlogged, oxygen is blocked out, causing the roots to drown and allowing rot-causing fungi in the soil to quickly destroy the crop.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abaatsi oxygen lɛ naa. ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a strong storm hits, especially when carrying fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ? titri lɛ, kɛ́ ewo yibii

english: Plantain trees do not have a deep central taproot; instead, they have shallow roots that spread near the surface. When the heavy bunch of plantains grows at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy and easy for wind to uproot from wet soil unless supported with wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ, shi moŋ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Beni plantain lɛ da ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo yɛ ŋwɛi Tsei lɛ tsii ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ gbalaa amɛshishifãi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya. ja tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why is it important for me to plant my maize right after the first main rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting early with the first heavy rain allows your seeds to use the fresh nutrients released in the dry soil and builds strong roots before any mid-season dry spells occur.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ niyenii heei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. ni amɛma shishifãi ni wa dani hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be teŋgbɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize farm curl up like tubes when the sun gets very hot around noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ paipii yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much moisture in the heat. It is the plant's natural way of saving water until the temperature cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkafite ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I clear away all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct sunlight. Large canopy trees provide essential shade and keep the soil humid, protecting tender cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe koni akashã amɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually show that the plant is short on soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil around the roots is overly soaked with water, preventing the plant from feeding.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ sũ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aha niyenii

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as dry soil, very high heat, or irregular watering during the period when flowers are forming.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo latsaa ni naa wa kpe. loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why does my maize grow weak and thin when I leave weeds to grow close to the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ beni aŋmɛɔ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crop. When weeds are too close, your maize plants do not get enough food to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ waa. Beni jwɛi lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Oŋmãa tsei lɛ naaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why am I seeing tiny black insects clustering on the new shoots of my cowpea plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii diji lɛ? Abua mihe naa yɛ mi-cowpea tso lɛ tsei heei lɛ anɔ.

english: These insects are aphids that attack soft plant growth to suck the plant's sap. They target tender new leaves because they are rich in water and soft enough to pierce.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni tutuaa tsei bibii ni daraa lɛ koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Amɛtutuaa baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ejaakɛ nu babaoo yɛ mli, ni amɛhe yɛ blɛoo bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbote mli.

english: Why did many of the tomato seeds I sowed fail to sprout out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato dumɔwui ni midu lɛ babaoo ejeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep in the soil, if the soil dries out before sprouting, or if soil-dwelling insects eat the seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi dani ekwɛ̃ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off some of the extra branches on my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fata he ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning extra branches helps the plant direct its water and nutrient energy into growing larger, healthier fruits instead of wasting energy on excess leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts hidden under the ground are ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmeii ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ makpa?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the lower leaves of the bush turn yellow and drop off, and the inside of the harvested shell shows a dark, brownish coat when cracked open.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni jwɛi lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ni tso lɛ yitsɔi ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ yitsɔi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ efo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need partial shade because direct, harsh sunlight burns their leaves and dries out their stems. Keeping shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them until their root systems grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is essential for green leaf growth, and when it runs out in the soil, the plant moves available nitrogen from older lower leaves up to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. ni kɛ́ efo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava plant start producing branches and flowers instead of just growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ miibɔi niji kɛ fɔfɔi shweremɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Branching and flowering are natural signs that cassava is maturing. When the plant reaches this stage, it shifts its energy away from growing tall leaves and stems toward expanding its underground tubers.
ga: Niji kɛ fɔfɔi ni baa lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei miikwɛ̃. Kɛ tso lɛ shɛ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ Etsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida kɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ amli lɛ ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ amli.

english: Why do so many small shoots sprout around my main plantain stem, and should I leave all of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ Amɛteŋ babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ. mi tsɔne titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mashi fɛɛ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers, which grow from the main root. If you leave all of them, they compete with the main plant for water and food, resulting in small bunches. Removing most suckers and leaving just one or two allows the main plant to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifã titri lɛ mli Kɛji ashi lɛ emuu lɛ, ekɛ tso titri lɛ baabɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii, ni no baaha efee jwɛi bibioo ko. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of growing along the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso koni ekwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooda yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which helps them make energy to produce big tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off wet soil, preventing fungal diseases and leaf rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa enáa hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather temperatures become too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing unpollinated flowers to dry up and drop off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsake waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni awoko amɛmli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them first leaves natural fertilizer in the soil for the next crop to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsu nii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from young leaves, or by viruses carried by these insects. The feeding damage causes the leaf tissues to deform as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni niyenii yeɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do some of the small, young cocoa pods on my tree shrivel up and turn black while still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Ani mitso lɛ gbo ni etsɔ ediŋŋ beni eji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: This is a natural process called cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees naturally produce more young pods than they can feed, so the tree deliberately cuts off nutrient flow to some small pods so the remaining ones can grow big and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilting. Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni efoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hoɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why does lowland rice grow well in muddy, flooded soil while upland rice rots under water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa folo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties have special air passages inside their stems that send oxygen down to their roots even when submerged. Upland rice lacks these internal channels, so submerged roots starve of oxygen and rot.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ amɛbote nu mli po. Omɔ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ bɛ nɛkɛ mligbɛ gbɛi nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What is a net house structure, and how does it help my crops grow better than farming in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu ni akɛ tsei ewo mli lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe okwaayeli yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: A net house is a simple farm shelter covered with mesh net that allows sunlight and air in while blocking intense heat, strong winds, heavy rain, and destructive pests. This protection creates a stable environment, helping crops like tomatoes and peppers grow healthier and produce better yields.
ga: Trellis greenhouse ji ŋmɔ mli shĩa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli lɛ ehà nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ hebuu nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Hewalɛ kpakpa kɛ nitsumɔ kpakpa

english: Is it true that building a greenhouse costs much more than regular open-field farming, and is it worth the high cost for a farmer like me?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ maa heɔ shika babaoo fe okwaayeli ni afeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Ni ani ejara wa waa kɛha okwaafoi tamɔ mi?

english: Yes, building a greenhouse requires a bigger initial investment for framing materials and plastic coverings. However, it allows you to grow crops all year round, protects against pests and bad weather, and reduces crop loss, which often leads to higher yields and higher profits that cover the setup costs over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsũ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ maa biɔ shishijee shika babaoo yɛ nibii ni akɛbaafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ plastic ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ mli, shi kɛlɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Hebuu kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii ahe kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ shi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ ni sɛɛnamɔi babaoo hu baa. Enɛ haa shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend starting delicate vegetable seeds under a shaded nursery structure before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ aje aduawai dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashishi yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ashishi dani ajie amɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are like newborn babies—they are easily burnt by strong sun or damaged by heavy rain and pests. A nursery provides a controlled environment with shade and protection so seedlings can develop strong stems and root systems before being transplanted.
ga: Dumɔwu bibioo tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee. Hulu shãa amɛ oya loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ fiteɔ amɛ. Nursery lɛ haa shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ ni hulutsoo kɛ hebuu yɔɔ mli. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi dani adu amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop and drop off when the sun gets extremely hot during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During intense heat, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. To protect themselves from drying out completely, plants drop some of their leaves to reduce water loss and save their remaining energy.
ga: Yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni okɛbu ohe he koni okagbi kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ ato.

english: Why is it bad practice to water my vegetable garden in the middle of the day when the sun is hottest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashwieɔ aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Watering during peak sunshine causes much of the water to evaporate immediately before reaching the plant roots. Additionally, water drops left on leaves can act like small magnifying glasses in hot sunlight, scorching the leaves and encouraging disease.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ ehe lɛ Etswaa baai lɛ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai aba.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages their pollen, making fertilization impossible. When flowers fail to get fertilized due to high heat or lack of water, the plant naturally drops the flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen lɛ. Ehaa enyɛŋ ekɛ fɔmɔ awo mli Beni fɔfɔi ko fɔmɔ bɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo ni mli edɔ fe nine loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Tsei baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: When maize is planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of spending energy to produce thick stems and large cobs, the plant stretches upward quickly just to reach the sunlight.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ hewalɛ najiaŋ koni akɛfee tsei ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛná hulu la lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow while the leaves at the very top stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean the soil is low in nutrients like nitrogen. Cassava plants will automatically pull stored nutrients out of their older bottom leaves and move them to feed new leaves at the top, causing the old leaves to turn yellow and fall.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cassava tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai momoi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more during the wet rainy season than in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: The rainy season brings high humidity and soft, tender plant growth, which creates ideal feeding and breeding conditions for many insects. Warm and damp weather allows pest populations to multiply much faster.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ tsei adalɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo baa. Enɛ haa niyenii kɛ fɔmɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha kooloi srɔtoi babaoo akwɛmɔ. Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ babaoo oya.

english: Why do sweet potato vines spread all across the soil surface, and how does that help the ground around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes naturally grow long creeping stems that cover the ground like a blanket. This ground cover acts as a living mulch, shading the soil to keep it cool, retaining soil moisture, and preventing weeds from growing.
ga: Atomɔ shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ tsei kakadaji ni shwereɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kuntu. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni edɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why do some vegetables grow better inside a greenhouse than in my open farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi-greenhouse lɛ mli fe miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouses protect delicate crops from scorching sun, sudden heavy rains, and insect attacks while maintaining steady warmth and moisture, allowing crops like tomatoes to grow faster and yield healthier produce.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa kɛ kooloi tutuamɔi, yɛ be mli ni ahiɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i mli daa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I nurse my pepper seeds in small nursery bags first instead of planting them directly into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ grow bag bibioo ko mli klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ saatso wulu lɛ mli?

english: Nursing seeds in protected bags gives young seedlings a strong start away from harsh heat, heavy rains, and pests until they build strong roots and are tough enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ kotokui ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ amli koni eye ebua dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli. Kɛyashi ebaafee shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: What does it mean when the lower leaves of my maize turn yellow and dry up?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water, forcing the crop to pull nutrients from its older leaves to keep new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni baai heei akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I plant legumes like beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil and sharing essential nutrients with neighboring crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ jaa niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: Leaves curl and droop in intense midday heat to minimize water loss and protect themselves from sun scorch; they normally bounce back in the cooler evening once water loss slows down.
ga: Ha oyitsɔi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efo yɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Bei pii lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli beni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ eba shi lɛ.

english: Plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, shedding blossoms to save energy for basic survival.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi ni akɛbaatsu nii koni akɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala

english: Why do my crops slow down their growth so much during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daalɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds draw moisture out of plant leaves and soil very quickly, forcing plants to conserve water by slowing down their growth until conditions become humid again.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ oya. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛhaa sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight; fast-growing plantain trees provide broad canopy shade and hold soil moisture to keep young cocoa plants cool and alive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be babaoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni eha cacao tsei bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant my crops very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving no individual plant with enough energy to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why are the bottoms of my watermelons turning black and rotting before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani ekwɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem, known as blossom-end rot, happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or long dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii dani egbiɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf greenness and growth. Rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, so adding balanced fertilizer early helps the leaves stay green and feed the growing corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛfataa he mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni eha niyenii aha abele ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from my bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jwɛi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains beside young cocoa creates a canopy that blocks intense heat, keeps the ground moist, and gives the cocoa time to grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Koo tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni enɛ haa kookoo lɛ be ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: If my cassava grows very tall with plenty of bushy leaves, does it mean I will harvest giant tubers?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava lɛ da waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ manyɛ mahiɛ yitso wulu lɛ mli?

english: Not necessarily. When cassava gets too much leafy food from the soil, it spends all its energy growing tall leaves above ground instead of sending food down into the tubers, which can leave you with thin, woody roots at harvest.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛji akɛ aha cassava niyenii ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee baai ni nɔ kwɔ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛya shi kɛya yitso lɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha oná shishifãi bibii. Be ni esa akɛ akpa

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without forming any fresh tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato hee ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when exposed to extreme afternoon heat or dry soil stress. When the plant feels too hot or thirsty, it drops its flowers to save water and protect its own life rather than using energy to build tomatoes.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo haomɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ kpe. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ edɔ tsɔ loo kumai miiye lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛfee tomato

english: What happens to my corn yield if I plant the seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for soil food and water, while their leaves fight for sunlight. This competition leaves all the plants short and thin, producing tiny, half-filled cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ feɔ kukuji ni amɛhe tseee. Efeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: Why do caterpillars keep hiding inside the small whorl leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai bibii amli lɛ? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Caterpillars like Fall Armyworms hide inside the center funnel of young corn plants because the leaf tissue there is soft, fresh, and full of water. Hiding inside also shelters them from hot sunlight, rain, and surface chemical sprays.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Ejaakɛ baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ amɛhi mli lɛ hu buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food that travels down into the growing tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, prevents rots from wet soil, and exposes every leaf to sunlight and fresh air.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ lɛ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ fitemɔ naa. ni okɛ baa fɛɛ baa awo hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into cups and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips biting the underside of the leaves to drink sap. As the insects suck out moisture and spread plant viruses, the leaves curl up tightly to protect themselves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni ŋmɔɔ baa lɛ shishi koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni kooloi bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ, Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the dirt. When you harvest the legumes, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my main plantain shoot produce small bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigba kɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni kɛji mishi tsei bibii fɛɛ ni miida yɛ ehe lɛ hu?

english: All the small shoots surrounding a main plantain stem share the exact same root system. If you do not prune away extra shoots, they steal food and water from the main mother stem, resulting in smaller, lighter bunches at harvest.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi bibii fɛɛ ni ebɔle Plantain tso lɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ yɛ shishifãi kome pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei niji bibii ni waaa ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing cocoa seedlings with the shade and moist climate they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much sunlight as possible to produce food. Lifting the vines off the ground allows the leaves to get maximum light, which directs energy into building bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aba. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la babaoo. Enɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, prevents the hot sun from evaporating water from the soil too quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the lower parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow strong. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes whatever food it has left and sends it to the upper leaves, turning the lower leaves yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baaye niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ekɛmaje baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is time when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack from the expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ ahe.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts alongside maize naturally enriches your soil. Beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which acts as free natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beans gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the soil. Changing crops each season keeps the soil healthy and starves crop-specific pests.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves, or a plant virus spread by insects like whiteflies. Inspecting the undersides of the leaves early helps catch these insects before they damage the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ he okadi. loo tsei amli helai ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ dani amɛkpãtã tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is scarce, or when there are no pollinating insects around. Without stress relief and proper pollination, the flower cannot set fruit and falls off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu faaa Aloo be mli ni kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ bɛ he fɛɛ he. Kɛji akɛ ajieee nɔnyɛɛ kɛ pollination ni sa lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Young crops are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds. If weeds are left unchecked early on, they steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients your crops need to establish strong root systems.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ mra lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil or when too much standing water is drowning the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its bright green color and energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa amɛhe su kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a natural defense to save water and stay alive. The crop is not dead; as soon as the rains return, it will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Nibii ni adu lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai heei baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but most of the small pods turn black and fall off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii babaoo, shi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a common fungal disease called Black Pod, or by extreme stress from heat and lack of moisture. Clearing weeds, trimming excess shade trees for airflow, and removing infected pods helps protect the healthy ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod loo nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ mli lɛ mli kɛbaa. weeding Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ babaoo ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Ni ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Can I plant my yam directly on flat ground, or must I always build soil mounds first?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo esa akɛ matswa gɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ be fɛɛ be?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to grow long and thick without resistance. Building mounds or ridges loosens the earth and protects the roots from waterlogging, which would otherwise rot the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he. Enɛ baanyɛ aha yitso lɛ agbo.

english: Why does the soil on my farm bake into hard crusts after a few sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves or manure to bind it softly. Covering your soil with dried grass or crop residue keeps the surface cool, holds moisture longer, and stops the ground from cracking.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafi lɛ blɛoo. Jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop and wilt during the hottest part of the day even if the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can drink it up, making the plant temporarily wilt to protect itself. If the plant bounces back by evening, it is normal heat stress; if it stays wilted, it could be a soil disease affecting the roots.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe. Kɛji tso lɛ ku esɛɛ efo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji hulutsoo be ni sa. Kɛji etee nɔ egbo lɛ, ekolɛ eji shikpɔŋ hela ko ni miigba shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: When plants get too much water, their leaves droop, turn light green or yellow, and root tips rot because there is no air left in the soil. Making simple drainage channels helps excess water flow away from plant roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baagbee shi Tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ Ni shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baagboi ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ko eshwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli.

english: Ragged holes inside corn leaf funnels are usually made by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on soft new growth. Checking plants early and applying crushed ash, neem extract, or recommended sprays directly into the funnel kills the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Tso lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni atswa, neem mli nu, loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my pepper plant leaves during humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: White spots are a powdery fungus that thrives when crop leaves are too crowded and moisture gets trapped. Spacing your plants properly and pruning lower leaves lets sunlight and wind dry the leaves and stop the fungus.
ga: White spot ji ŋmei ni tamɔ powder ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji tso baai lɛ mli ewo muji tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ emɔ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha baai lɛ agbi ni etsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why are my sweet potato tubers filled with tiny dark tunnels when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Tiny tunnels are made by sweet potato weevils whose grubs burrow into the stems and roots. Piling soil around the base of the plant as tubers expand prevents adult beetles from reaching underground to lay eggs.
ga: Sweet potato weevil lɛ ji mɔ ni feɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ, he ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni aaabɔle tso lɛ shishi be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ baatsi ŋmeii ni eda lɛ anaa koni amɛkaya shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛyawo amɛwui.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential food for plants. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
