ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices, or by heat stress. Spraying with neem oil or appropriate insecticide and keeping the soil moist helps protect the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie shi ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my okra leaves get a white powdery substance on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ yɛ nɔ ko ni tamɔ powder yɛŋ lɛ?

english: The white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which happens when plants are too close together or humidity is high. Giving plants enough space for airflow and removing infected leaves early keeps it from spreading.
ga: Powda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew ni baa kɛji tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ mli. Ni aha tso lɛ he ko ni sa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli kɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because they cannot breathe when water stays around them for too long. Planting on ridges or raised beds helps rainwater drain away quickly and prevents rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛ nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. kɛha be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo saatso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ehaaa efite.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or heavy dry winds. Regular watering during dry spells and planting windbreaks help the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli, ni adu koni akɛtsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow plenty of lush green leaves but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: When cowpea plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall leaves instead of making flowers and pods. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so they need balanced fertilizers low in nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, tsina tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kakadaji ni amɛdaraa lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni nitrogen faaa yɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow into twisted, strange shapes underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee srɔtoi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni etsake yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when the soil is too hard, clay-heavy, or full of stones, making it hard for the tuber to push straight down. Loosening the soil deeply and making high mounds gives the yam room to grow long and smooth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ shikpɔŋ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa sweet potato yitso lɛ akɛ ebaatsi ehe tɛ̃ɛ kɛya shi. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛyashɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa sweet potato tsu lɛ daa ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves, creating temporary shade that protects young cocoa trees until they grow big enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baada bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even when I plant at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Soil loses its natural fertility over time when crops are harvested repeatedly without replacing nutrients. Rotating crops, adding organic compost, or letting the land rest restores the soil so it can feed future harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ ebɔɔ su ni eyɔɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii shii abɔ lɛ. ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsakeee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he loo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni enyɛ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when light winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that sit near the surface, and heavy fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy. Supporting the stem with strong wooden props or bamboo stakes keeps the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Ni aduawai akui ni tsii baaha tso lɛ atsii waa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa loo ŋmeii ni akɛfee tso lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom upward, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen nutrient. The plant moves its limited food from the old lower leaves up to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen niyenii. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii fioo ko kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo ko lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves usually curl up when tiny unseen insects like thrips or mites are sucking the juice underneath them, or when the plant is trying to protect itself from extreme midday sun and heat.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kooloi bibii ahiɛ. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ Aloo be mli ni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants droop and look dead in the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. They deliberately droop to reduce their exposed leaf area to the sun, and usually recover by evening once temperature drops.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjɛɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the tree trunk without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support as full pods. If too many fall off, it could mean there are not enough tiny midges (insects) to pollinate them, or the tree lacks enough water and nutrients to carry the crop.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ pod ni eyi obɔ mli. Kɛji babaoo gbee shi Ekolɛ etsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ. Aloo tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why is my tomato plant growing big green leaves very fast but producing no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baa baai wuji eŋɔli oya shi ebɛ fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: When tomato plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, they put all their energy into growing tall stem and bushy leaves instead of setting flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my papaya fruits drop off the stem while they are still tiny and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapayai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii ni amɛji ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: Young papayas fall off when the tree experiences sudden changes in water—like a dry spell right after heavy rains—or when the flowers were not properly pollinated before the fruit started forming.
ga: Papaya bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu tsakemɔi trukaa, tamɔ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. aloo be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ.

english: Yam leaves act like solar panels that make food to feed the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward sunlight so they can make maximum food to yield bigger, heavier yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii, ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛkɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛfee sweet potatoes ni dara ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots remain thin if the soil is packed too hard for roots to expand, or if the soil lacks potassium, which is the key food nutrient plant roots need to build heavy starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji akɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei shishifãi koni amɛfee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other underground for food and water, and above ground for sunlight. This competition results in weak plants and small yields compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛwuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. ni amɛwuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baa kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ he ni sa lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my land produce less maize when I plant it on the exact same farm piece every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall with green leaves but fail to produce large, full cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Corn plants often focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leaves when they have too much nitrogen or lack enough sunlight and phosphorus. To get big, healthy cobs, corn needs balanced soil nutrients, proper spacing, and adequate rainfall right when the tassels and silks appear.
ga: Abɛi tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama tsei kɛ baai ni kwɔlɔ ni miida lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛyɛ nitrogen babaoo loo amɛbɛ hulu la kɛ phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ ana ŋmei agbo ni mli wa lɛ, ehe miihia ni Abele lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa beni ŋmeii kɛ siliki jeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Why does the exact same maize seed yield a heavy harvest on my neighbor's farm but produce very little on mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Crop success depends on specific local conditions like soil quality, moisture levels, shade, and field preparation. Even within the same community, differences in how land was previously used, water retention, and weed management cause crops to behave differently.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ omanyeyeli damɔ shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i, bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha, hulutsoo kɛ he ni asaa he lɛ nɔ. yɛ akutso kome mli po Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ tsuɔ nii nu ni akɛtoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli ni haa tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ

english: What happens to my land and crops if I plant corn on the same field every single season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be?

english: Planting corn continuously in the same field drains specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil and allows corn-loving pests and diseases to build up. Rotating corn with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ abele mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Can I successfully grow crops like maize on land that is also being opened up for visitors and non-farming activities?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni saralɔi kɛ nitsumɔi ni jeee okwaayeli nitsumɔi baanyɛ aya nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, combining crop farming with educational visits or tourism—known as agritourism—works well if you set aside clear boundaries. Crops need protected zones away from heavy foot traffic so soil does not get trampled and plants remain undisturbed.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei akwɛmɔ kɛ tsɔsemɔ loo shisharamɔ saramɔ ni akɛaafata he. Ale lɛ hu akɛ okwaayeli he shisharamɔ. Ebaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji oto husui ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Hei ni abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he miihia ni tsɔnei ni hoɔ babaoo lɛ akashɛ he. Bɔni afee ni akanyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tsei lɛ ahi shi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akagbala amɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my entire corn field on one day or to plant small portions bit by bit over a few weeks?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome mli loo fioo ko yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli?

english: Planting in smaller portions over time, known as staggered planting, protects you against unpredictable weather. If a short dry spell hits early, only part of your crop is affected, and it spreads out your labor and harvest times.
ga: dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ fãi bibii amli Beni be hoɔ Ale lɛ akɛ dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ fãi bibii amli lɛ, ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ ahe. Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ba mra lɛ Onibii lɛ fã ko pɛ enaa he sɛɛ. ni ebaagbɛ onitsumɔ kɛ okpamɔ be lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up like tubes during the hottest part of the day when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ paipii yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the crop conserve water and survive temporary heat stress until rain or moisture returns.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. He ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli dɔlɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: If I plant cassava right after my corn starts growing, will the two crops compete and ruin each other?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ŋmãa lɛ ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ, Ani tsei enyɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe baatswa akaŋ ni amɛbaafite amɛhe?

english: Cassava and corn can grow together well if spaced correctly. Corn grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the corn is cleared, allowing you to harvest two crops from the same field.
ga: Cassava kɛ ŋmãa baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kome kɛji akɛ amɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: How can I tell if my soil is fertile enough for corn without buying expensive chemical testing kits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni miheee tsofa ni jara wa ni akɛkaa mɔ lɛ?

english: You can judge soil health by looking at its dark color, rich earthy smell, ability to hold moisture, and the presence of earthworms. Lush weed growth prior to clearing also indicates good natural fertility for crops like corn.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ha lɛ kɛtsɔ esu ni tsuɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni jara wa Hewalɛ ni akɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ dani ajieɔ lɛ hu tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ kpakpa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do fall armyworms suddenly attack my young corn shoots just a few days after they germinate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn shoots lɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Moths lay their eggs on young, tender leaves because early corn shoots are soft and easy for newly hatched caterpillars to eat. Checking leaf undersides early and applying natural or recommended controls right at germination prevents major damage.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii anɔ ejaakɛ mra be mli ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ baanyɛ aye. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ni kɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii loo nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii beni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite nii waa.

english: Why does my harvested corn spoil or get destroyed by insects so quickly inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miifite loo tsɛŋemɔ helai miihe oya yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Stored corn spoils quickly if harvested before it is completely dry or if kept in humid, poorly ventilated spaces where weevils thrive. Drying cobs thoroughly in the sun and storing grains in airtight bags or clean, dry stores prevents losses.
ga: Abele ni ato lɛ baafite oya kɛji akɛ akpa dani egbi kwraa. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii daa yɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛ ŋmeii lɛ to vacuum kotokui amli loo shwapo ko ni mli tse ni egbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from intense sunlight and dry winds. Without shade trees or mulch around the roots to trap soil moisture, the hot sun dries out the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and drop to save the tree.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛhere tso lɛ yiwala.

english: How many shoots should I keep around my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahã ŋmeii lɛ ahi he fɛɛ he? Plantain tso titri lɛ tsei enyiɛ yɔɔ?

english: You should keep only 2 or 3 healthy shoots (suckers) of different heights around the main tree. If you leave too many suckers, they will fight for nutrients and water, causing the tree to produce small, light plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhelɛtemɔ srɔtoi yɔɔ mli lɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ ato tso titri lɛ he. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ woɔ plantains bibii ni tsiimɔ waaa.

english: Yes, you must always plant the cassava stick with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant it upside down, the stems will struggle to turn upwards, producing fewer leaves and smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ehe miihia ni odu ŋmei ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba ni ekɛ ehiɛ baakwɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ faaa kɛ yitsei bibii.

english: Why do I need to stack tall wooden sticks near my yam plants for the leaves to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni baai lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight and produce food. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, protects them from soil diseases, and allows the plant to send more energy into growing large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛwo niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji eŋɔli ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ fe eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build green leaves. Applying organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize turn dark green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni etsɔ oya.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains all the nitrogen from the soil and allows maize-specific pests to multiply. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts puts nutrients back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ fɛɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ ayiɔ babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the liquid from underneath the leaves. Removing infested leaves and applying safe organic or chemical sprays gets rid of the insects so new healthy leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ loo tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ koni baai heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat is too strong or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Watering your plants regularly and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Is it safe to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the ground gets thoroughly soaked by two or three good rains. If you plant after the very first rain, a short dry spell right after can scorch and destroy the newly sprouted seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ kpakpai enyɔ loo etɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ be kuku ni egbiɔ lɛ No sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: When is the best time of day to water or spray my farm crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu loo afɔse nɔ?

english: The best time to spray or water crops is early in the morning or late in the evening when the sun is gentle. Strong afternoon sun can evaporate the moisture quickly or scorch wet leaves when sprays are applied.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu loo awo amɛ nu ji leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu la fioo pɛ yɔɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ oya loo eshã baai ni efɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ ashwie nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct harsh sunlight; they need shade from taller crops like plantain or shade trees to protect their leaves from burning and keep the soil moist while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe koni akashã amɛ. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Excessive moisture and humidity allow fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread rapidly on cocoa pods; clearing weeds and pruning branches helps air and sunlight pass through to keep the pods dry.
ga: Fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya yɛ cocoa pods lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, forcing it to pull stored nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ enɔ koni egbala niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato kɛjɛ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off (around 9 to 12 months); leaving it in the soil for too long turns the roots woody, tough, and less suitable for eating.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi (aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12). Kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei, amɛhe wa, ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot exhausts the specific soil nutrients maize needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmãa he hiaa lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: My tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, so why are the blossoms dropping off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to conserve energy rather than set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tomato tsei anɔ daa Enɛ haa amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking in size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that transmit viruses, which can be controlled by early detection and applying neem oil or insecticidal soap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Abaanyɛ akudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ mra be mli nibii ni ana lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi atsu nii.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dried grass or leaves instead of leaving the ground clean and bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli Moŋ lɛ, shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe atse ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ.

english: Covering the soil with organic mulch retains moisture, protects roots from extreme sun heat, stops weeds from growing, and adds nutrients to the soil as it decays.
ga: Organic mulching baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu shishifãi ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni efiteɔ lɛ

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over before the fruit is even fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be easily destroyed by soil pests like root nematodes or stem weevils, making the plant top-heavy and weak against high winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem weevils baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nyɛɔ etswaa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my plant when I apply it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo mli lɛ?

english: Direct contact with concentrated chemical fertilizer can burn the plant's stem and young roots; it should instead be placed in a circle a few inches away where the root tips can safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ ashã. Mohu ɔ, e sa nɛ a ngɔ kɛ fɔ he ko nɛ e kɛ e he ɔ maa pee inchi bɔɔ komɛ ngɛ he nɛ sisifã ɔmɛ ma nyɛ maa ngɔ lɛ ngɛ he ko nɛ e ngɛ slɔkee ɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and burn when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without enough shade trees or plantains around them, the heat burns their young leaves and dries out their roots, causing the leaves to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni baaha hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition forces them to stretch tall to reach light, leaving little energy for the plant to grow thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛná la. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ahi tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei lɛ amli tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is causing the small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny waste that looks like sawdust inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni fãji bibii yɛ mli Mɛni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the leaves of young maize plants and feed on the soft leaf tissues, leaving holes and sawdust-like waste behind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli ni amɛyeɔ baa bibii amli fãji. Eshiɔ bu kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant cannot support fruit development and sheds its flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. aloo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo ni akɛfataa he Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei nyɛŋ aha aduawai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛfolɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer on my farm when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve so that plant roots can absorb it safely. Applying fertilizer to dry soil leaves concentrated salts directly against the roots, which can scorch and destroy the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ kpaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei

english: Why does adding well-rotted manure to my soil make my green vegetables grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa mi-green lɛ daa oya lɛ?

english: Manure enriches the soil with essential nutrients like nitrogen, which plants use to build green leaves and stems. It also improves the soil's structure, helping it hold moisture and nutrients longer around the roots.
ga: Muji haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ashishifãi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp soil, protecting them from fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are fully grown under the ground and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, the main stem thickens, and cracks begin to form on the ground surface right around the base of the stem as the tubers expand underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ mli tsɔne titri lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni ejeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant immediately, the warm soil and lack of steady follow-up rain will dry out and kill the germinating seeds before they can establish roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo shishifãi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce low yield even when I weed around the plants once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ tsei lɛ ahe shikome pɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and continuously steal light, water, and soil nutrients. If weeds are left unchecked during the early growth stage of the crop, the crop gets starved early on and cannot recover full production later.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishijee dalɛ beaŋ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii mra. ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa aba sɛɛ mli

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rains make the soil waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ midu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is fertile enough for crop farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu nii?

english: Fertile soil is usually dark in color, crumbly when you hold it, holds water well without becoming a muddy pool, and contains plenty of broken-down dry leaves and organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ su feɔ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ kɛji omɔ mli. Ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ sũ ŋmɔtɔ. ni baai ni egboi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ekumɔ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress. Severe heat or dry soil prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to shed flowers to conserve its strength.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Ha tso lɛ afee fɔfɔi koni ehiɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing big green leaves above ground instead of expanding its food-storing roots beneath the surface.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a haa sisifãhi nɛ a toɔ niye ní ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; they have shallow roots that spread near the surface. When heavy rains soften the soil, wind can easily pull these shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than the crops I planted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to local conditions. They can swallow water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds, which need time and gentle conditions to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛye nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. Eheɔ be kɛ shihilɛi ni mli jɔ dani enyɛɔ edaa.

english: Why do my crops dry up during the harmattan season even if I give them a little water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ́ mikɛ nu fioo pɛ ha amɛ po.

english: During the harmattan season, the dry desert air and bright sun draw moisture out of leaves very quickly. Giving small amounts of water only wets the top layer of dirt, leaving deep roots dry while the hot air dries the plant from above.
ga: Yɛ harmattan be mli lɛ ŋa nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Kɛ́ akɛ nu fioo ko fata he lɛ, ebaaha muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ agbi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ gĩɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod disease. The fungus thrives in cool, damp weather with high humidity, spreading fast when cocoa trees are too crowded and sunlight cannot reach the pods.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Mold yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i kɛ fɛ̃i babaoo mli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ mli eyi tsɔ ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are missing nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant make food and regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛná amɛ su eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when rain water collects on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater stays on the land without draining, it suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungi to cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when tiny insects called midges are not available to pollinate them, or when the tree suffers from heat stress and dry weather, forcing it to drop flowers to save water.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ba amɛnɔ. Anyɛɛɛ afee nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ ŋmɔtɔ. aloo beni tso lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahewɔ. Anyɛɔ mɔ nɔ koni ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni akɛhere nu

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down when the fruit bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not grow deep into the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the root base cannot hold the weight against wind unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni edaaa kɛboteɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai akui lɛ miifee shwiili. Shishitoo nyɛŋ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ, ja akɛ tso fiɔ esɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look weak during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very hot, pepper plants curl their leaves to stop water from evaporating too quickly from their pores. Once the air cools down in the evening, the leaves normally spread open again.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu akajɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ gbeleɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with tiny fruits when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ yibii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight and soil food. They stretch tall trying to reach the light, which drains their energy and results in smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ, ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa nitsumɔ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil every season. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do armyworms hide inside the stalk during the day and eat my maize leaves at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli yɛ shwane mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa baai gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworms avoid direct heat from the sun to stay cool and escape birds. They come out during the cooler nighttime to feed freely on young, soft leaves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he koni amɛhi shi ni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ ni amɛjo okpoi anaa foi. Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii bibii lɛ yɛ heyeli mli.

english: Why does removing some side branches from my tomato plant make the remaining tomatoes bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ajie tomato tso ko niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ, ehaa tomato ni eshwɛ lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Every leaf and branch consumes energy from the roots. Removing extra branches forces the tomato plant to send all its water and nutrients directly to growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Baa kɛ tso nine fɛɛ nine kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ enu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ aya tɛ̃ɛ kɛya aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow out of the ground when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mifuɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need warmth, air, and light near the soil surface to sprout easily. If planted too deep, the young shoot runs out of stored food energy before reaching the surface and dies underground.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ dɔlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ la ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, Young shoots lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to stay green. The plant automatically moves its remaining nitrogen from older leaves to feed new top leaves, signaling that your crop needs fertilizer or organic manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni niyenii mli nibii titrii ni he hiaa ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli lɛ yɔɔ mli. Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the ground. Groundnuts and beans are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, naturally restoring fertility for your next harvest without needing costly chemicals.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha okpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni tsofai ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and burn when I remove all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants act like human babies—their leaves burn easily under hot direct sunlight. Taller shade trees keep the soil cool and moist while shielding sensitive cocoa leaves until the plants grow strong enough to bear full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ abifabii. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my yam vines grow bigger tubers when I give them tall sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mihaa amɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum light and keeps them away from damp soil where fungal rot can easily attack them.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni otsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni rot fungus baanyɛ atutua amɛ yɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling up into tight little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny, invisible insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaf undersides. Spraying early with neem oil or recommended insecticide stops these insects from spreading plant diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɔ ni anaaa, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai ashishi lɛ. Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akagbɛ tsei ahe helai amɛshwã.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot, when watering is uneven, or when there is too much chemical fertilizer. Keeping moisture levels steady in the soil helps flowers transform into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tomatoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest when I pack my maize seeds close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmaa bibioo nɔ beni mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures every stalk grows strong and produces full, heavy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la fioo, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ada waa ni ewo ŋmãa toi ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoot suckers growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water and food away from the main plantain tree. Pruning extra shoots down to just one or two leaves allows the mother plant to focus all its strength on producing big, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi kɛyashɛ baa kome loo enyɔ pɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa dumɔwui wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry season, and are they dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops leaves in hot weather to reduce water loss through evaporation. The plant is resting rather than dying, safely preserving moisture in its underground tubers until rains arrive to spark fresh leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miijɔɔ ehe moŋ fe ni eeegbo. Amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ koni baai heei lɛ akpɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the roots of my vegetables help them stay green during sunny weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi shwieɔ shi No hewɔ lɛ mishishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ otsii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli.

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It blocks hot sunshine from evaporating water out of the dirt, keeping the root zone moist and cool longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni jɛɔ muji mli lɛ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look weak and struggle to produce pods even though I weed my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnaa naagba yɛ pods ni amɛbaafee lɛ he eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees extract a lot of nutrients from the soil over time. Without extra nutrients from organic fertilizers, the soil becomes depleted, causing the trees to weaken and produce fewer pods.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ niyenii krokomɛi ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: What signs should I look out for on my farm to know that my crops need fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ okadi esa akɛ matao yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni male kɛji miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yellowing leaves, slow growth, thin stems, and low fruit or pod production are common signs that your crops are lacking essential nutrients and need fertilization.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo, tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, kɛ aduawai loo ŋmeii fioo komɛi ji okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is the benefit of using organic fertilizer instead of just letting my crops grow naturally?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he moŋ fe ni mahã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: Natural soil often lacks enough nutrients for high yields. Organic fertilizer feeds the soil organisms and provides steady nutrients that make crops grow stronger and produce more harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli shikpɔji lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha yibii babaoo aba. Organic fertilizers haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ niyenii ni ehaa amɛ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Is fertilizer made from chicken manure good for my crops, or will it damage them?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii loo ebaaye lɛ awui?

english: Processed chicken manure is very rich in essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. It builds crop strength and helps plants flourish safely when applied correctly.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ mli. Ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa shweshweeshwe kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I apply organic fertilizer to my crops while they are already growing in the field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ organic fertilizer atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, applying organic fertilizer while tending to growing crops gives them a direct nutrient boost right when they are developing leaves, stems, and fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ okɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii beni okwɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai tɛ̃ɛ beni tsei lɛ miikwɛ baai, amɛshishifãi, kɛ amɛyibii lɛ.

english: Why are animal manure fertilizers recommended for long-term soil health in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmeii atsu nii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure and helps the ground hold water better over time, keeping your soil fertile for future farming seasons.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ okwaayeli bei.

english: Fertilizer is best applied during the rainy season when crops are actively growing and the soil is moist enough for roots to easily absorb the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli, be mli ni tsei lɛ miida waa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How does organic fertilizer help my cocoa trees produce better pods?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic fertilizer gives cocoa trees the physical strength to carry heavy pods and reduces pod shedding, leading to healthier and fuller harvests.
ga: Organic fertilizers haa cacao tsei lɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii ni ehaa ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nibii ni abaawo lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaye emuu.

english: Will applying organic fertilizer to my cocoa trees help them withstand harsh weather?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ wo mi cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai anaa?

english: Yes, strong root systems and well-nourished trunks developed through organic fertilizing help cocoa trees stay resilient during dry periods or stressful weather conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni anáa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛhe wa yɛ hɔmɔ loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni haoɔ mɔ lɛ amli.

english: Who can I talk to in my community to learn the right schedule for feeding my crops?
ga: Namɛi manyɛ mikɛ amɛ agba sane yɛ mi akutso lɛ mli koni mikase gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa ni mikɛbaahã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii?

english: You can consult local agricultural extension officers or trained agro-dealers who can visit your farm and advise you on the exact timing and quantities of fertilizer your crops need.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyabi okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko ni atsɔse lɛ ni baanyɛ ayasara oŋmɔ lɛ. ni okɛ ŋaawoo aha yɛ be pɔtɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden poles for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa bo lɛ? Ani obaakwɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso ko nɔ?

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need to lift their leaves up high to catch maximum sunlight. Without stakes, the leaves lie on the damp ground where they rot easily and produce much smaller tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ tso bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ he ni amɛgboiɔ oya ni amɛwoɔ bulbs bibii babaoo.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: If planted too close, the maize plants will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This causes them to grow tall and thin with weak stems and tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build green leaves, or that water is sitting at the roots for too long and suffocating them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli Aloo nu lɛ ehi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni eha amɛmiigbɔjɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing big leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai wuji ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Leaf curling during the heat of the day is a plant's natural defense to protect itself. It rolls its leaves to shrink their surface area so water does not evaporate out of them too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe he. Ekɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni eha baa lɛ hiɛ he lɛ afee bibioo. Bɔni afee ni nu lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ

english: Why can cassava keep growing in dry soil where my maize dies during a drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ he ni mi ŋmãa gboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep underground storage roots that store water and nutrients. During dry periods, it drops its leaves to go to sleep and save energy until the rains return.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ato. Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ baakã shi ni amɛbaakwɛ hewalɛ nɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads very fast in wet, humid weather when there is poor airflow between crowded branches.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ateŋ lɛ

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my field right before a heavy rain or after?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa loo yɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after rain. If you put it down right before heavy rain, the rushing water will wash your expensive fertilizer away into rivers before the roots can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ okɛto dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ baaho o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ kɛya faa lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is ready to harvest since the tubers are hidden underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? Akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cassava is usually mature when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil right around the base of the plant begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. ni sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops, such as plantains or leguminous trees, to act as natural covers that trap moisture and shade the young plants until their roots are well established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo leguminous tsei. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ maa shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over when the bunches start to get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and very heavy stems. As the fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, so strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the soil if the stem is not supported with a sturdy wooden prop.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu tsii waa. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya kɛji akɛ akɛ tso ni mli wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Dropping leaves is a cassava plant's natural way of protecting itself from drought. By shedding its leaves, the plant stops losing water through transpiration and goes into a resting state until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni ŋmei tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akafite nu kɛtsɔ la ni etsɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ, ni ebote hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out in the sun. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food efficiently, which is then sent down into the soil to grow large, healthy tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhoɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. ni abaamaje kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛhe wa

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a essential food it needs to stay green and build leaves, or that the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo baai. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm help my soil for the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer that enriches the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil goes from dry to wet too quickly, or when insects fail to pollinate the blossoms, preventing the fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli fũu oya tsɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ Ehaa aduawai lɛ edaaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into tight wrinkles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without giving good yields when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach light instead of putting energy into building strong stems and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛsɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛshɛ la he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛma tsei ashishifãi kɛ aduawai ni wa.

english: Why does covering the ground with dry grass around my crops help them grow better during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ? So my crops help them grow better during the hot weeks.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from direct heat, traps moisture in the ground longer, and stops unwanted weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: What is the best way to clear my land when it is completely overgrown with heavy bush?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ majie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni jwɛi babaoo eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ?

english: Instead of burning everything, cut down the bush and allow the plant material to rot into the ground. This organic matter protects the soil from drying out under the hot sun and returns valuable natural nutrients to your crops.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, Kpɔ̃ɔ jwɛi lɛ ni oha tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ afite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba onibii amli

english: Should I burn all the trash and cut grass after clearing my farm to make the land clean?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atse?

english: Burning destroys beneficial earthworms and insect life while baking the soil surface. Leaving the cleared grass to decay naturally or using it to cover the soil keeps the ground rich, cool, and moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ yɛ be mli ni shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii, ni edɔ, ni edɔ.

english: Do I need to remove all tree stumps and big roots from my field before planting cassava?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni majie tsei akutsei kɛ shishifãi wuji fɛɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dani madu ŋmei?

english: Removing large tree stumps prevents root rot diseases from hiding in old wood and spreading to your new crop. It also makes land preparation and weeding much easier.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie tsei wuji lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi ni egbo lɛ anaa koni ekatee tsei momo amli ni egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Is it necessary to till or turn over all the soil on overgrown land before I plant my seeds?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ he nii loo atsake yɛ hei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ dani adu dumɔwui?

english: Turning over the whole field breaks up the soil structure and causes moisture to evaporate quickly. Practicing minimum tillage by digging holes only where you plant saves labor and preserves vital soil water.
ga: Kɛ́ atsake ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nitsumɔ ni baa shi fioo kɛtsɔ bu ni oootsu yɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ baaha nitsumɔ akatsu nii ni ebaaha sũ mli nu ni he hiaa lɛ akafite.

english: Why do weeds grow back so aggressively right after I finish clearing my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing away dense bush allows direct sunlight to reach weed seeds sleeping under the soil surface, triggering them to germinate. Planting your main crop immediately or covering the ground with dry grass blocks the light that weed seeds need to wake up.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. wo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ Tso titri lɛ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi la ni he hiaa ni jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ateshi lɛ naa.

english: What can I plant on my cleared land to stop weeds from taking over before the main planting season?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ madu yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ faŋŋ koni jwɛi akaye nɔ dani be titri ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ aba?

english: Planting fast-growing cover crops like Mucuna or cowpea smothers weed growth by stealing their sunlight. Cover crops also capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for your main crop.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ Mucuna loo cowpea ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa kɛtsɔ hulu la ni ejuɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ hu mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei titrii lɛ.

english: Is it better to clear very thick grass using chemical sprays or by using a cutlass?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaatsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi nɔ loo akɛ dagger atsu nii ni ajie jwɛi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Clearing with a cutlass preserves useful soil life and costs less money, but herbicides save time on large farms. Slashing tall vegetation first and applying selective herbicides only on regrowth gives a safe and cost-effective balance.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsu nii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa shika hu baa shi. Shi tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ haa be sɛɛ foɔ yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli. tsei ni kɛlɛ ni afoɔ Klɛŋklɛŋ ni no sɛɛ lɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaa lɛ atsu nii yɛ tsei heei ni eda lɛ pɛ nɔ. Ehaa nɔ ni ja ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he baa.

english: My farm land has been left overgrown for many years, is the soil still good for planting?
ga: Miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ afii babaoo nɛ. Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lolo?

english: Land left unworked for years is usually very rich in nutrients because falling leaves and dying plants have naturally fertilized the soil without interference, making it ideal for strong crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni atsuko nɔ nii yɛ nɔ afii babaoo nɛ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɔɔ mli waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni gbeeɔ shi kɛ tsei ni miigboi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii enaa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I leave cut bush debris on top of the soil, or will it dry up and harm my young crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi jwɛi ni afolɔ mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ? Aloo ebaagbi ni eye miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ awui?

english: Cut plant material forms a protective layer called mulch. Spreading it evenly around your crops cools the ground, prevents rain from washing away the topsoil, and gradually breaks down to feed the plants.
ga: Tso lɛ mli nibii ni afo lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Kɛ́ okɛgbɛ onibii lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni efite fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii aha tsei.

english: Will leaving cleared leaves and bush debris on my farm attract destructive pests to my crops?
ga: Ani baai ni ajie kɛ brɔshi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbala kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Piles of wet, green leaves close to plants can harbor pests, but letting the vegetation dry out and spreading it thinly between plant rows deters insects while feeding the soil.
ga: Baai eŋɔli ni efɔ ni abua naa yɛ tsei ahe lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli. Shi ni aŋmɛɔ tsei lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa fioo fioo. Tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ kooloi anaa be mli ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why is it so important for me to time my corn planting with the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ be ni mikɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ ato nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee he lɛ?

english: Corn seeds need steady moisture right from the beginning to sprout and grow strong roots. Timing your planting with the start of the rains ensures the young crop gets the water it needs without drying out in the sun.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ shishijee koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Be ni akɛduɔ nii kɛhaa nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ana nu ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ ni hulu lɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: If the rainy season starts late this year, should I still plant my maize on the usual date?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ je shishi yɛ afi nɛɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ, ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa lolo tamɔ bɔ ni mifeɔ daa lɛ?

english: No, you should wait for the actual rains to begin before planting. Planting corn seeds in dry soil during a delay will prevent them from germinating and can cause the seeds to spoil or be eaten by pests.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ aje shishi diɛŋtsɛ dani onyɛ odu. Abele dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ mli lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo tsɛŋemɔ helai aye amɛ.

english: What happens to my young corn if I plant too early before the rains fully set in?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmei gbekɛ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu lɛ mra tsɔ, dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ kwraa?

english: If you plant too early, a sudden dry gap after the initial light rain can scorch the fresh sprouts, leading to weak plants or completely ruined crops that have to be replanted.
ga: Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Gbɛ lɛ gĩ trukaa yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui heei ashã. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite ni ehe hiaa ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my corn seeds after just the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is usually better to wait for two or three steady rains to be sure the wet season has truly started, as the very first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I plan my planting date if I want fresh corn ready to eat at a specific time of year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato midumɔ gbi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛji miitao ŋmãa hee ni asaa he koni aye yɛ afi lɛ mli be pɔtɛɛ ko mli?

english: You need to count backward from the month you want to eat or sell fresh corn by the number of months your corn variety takes to mature, making sure that growing period falls within the rainy season.
ga: Esa akɛ okane kɛya sɛɛ kɛjɛ nyɔŋ ni osumɔɔ ni oye loo ohɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa hee lɛ nɔ kɛ nyɔji abɔ ni ŋmãa ni okɛtsu nii lɛ ŋmɔɔ lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akwɛ akɛ dalɛ be lɛ baafee nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to think about when my family wants to eat the corn before I even plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu be ni miweku lɛ miisumɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa lɛ he dani madu po lɛ?

english: Corn matures quickly once it starts growing, so if you do not plan your planting around when you need food or plan to sell, your entire harvest might ripen all at once before you are ready to consume or store it.
ga: Abɛi daa oya kɛji ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ kɛji otooo gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ be mli ni niyenii he miihia bo loo oto gbɛjianɔ ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ. Abaanyɛ ahoo onibii fɛɛ shikome dani ofee klalo akɛ obaaye loo okɛto.

english: How many months after planting does local maize usually take until it is ready to eat fresh?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛyeɔ kooloi niyenii daa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ ehee?
