english: Most common maize varieties in Ghana take between two to three months from planting to be ready for eating as fresh green corn for roasting or boiling.
ga: Abele henɔ ni afɔɔ naa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ dani efeɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ akɛ abele ŋmɔŋ hee ni akɛshãa loo ashãa.

english: Does my corn crop need heavy rain throughout its whole life until harvest time?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni naa wa he miihia mi-ŋma lɛ yɛ eshihilɛ be fɛɛ mli kɛyashi kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Corn needs lots of water when sprouting and flowering, but once the cobs are fully formed and drying out near harvest, too much rain can actually spoil the grains and cause mold.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekwɛ fɔfɔi. Shi kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ egbe naa ni egbi lɛ, no lɛ ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why do my corn plants look stunted if rain stops right after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young corn plants have very small roots that cannot reach deep underground water yet, so a dry spell right after sprouting stops their development and stunts their growth.
ga: Abele tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii waa ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ekpaa dalɛ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if there is enough moisture in my land for me to begin planting corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Dig down a few inches into your farm soil and squeeze a handful; if the soil holds together easily in a ball without crumbling, it has enough water for your corn seeds to sprout.
ga: Tsɔmɔmɔ inchi fioo komɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni okɛ nine awo mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi mlɛo ni egbaaa Etsɔɔ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ni ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their leaves burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight, and the soil dries out too fast. Leaving taller shade trees or planting plantains around them keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ Shimɔ tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo loo duɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cassava alongside maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is ready for harvest within a few months, while cassava grows slowly underground over a year. Planting them together lets you harvest maize for quick food and income without disturbing the slow-growing cassava.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni eshɛɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Beni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ afi kome mli lɛ Companion dumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii ŋmãa oya ni onáa shika ni okɛgbalaaa ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an important nutrient for leaf growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, which means you need to add compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tsei yeɔ baa momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Why do I need to put a strong wooden stick in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso ni wa awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight so their leaves can make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread, helping the plant build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛbaai lɛ afee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in a row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks that produce very tiny ears of corn or no corn at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmãa toi bibii kwraa loo nɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or too much chemical fertilizer. Giving them regular water and mulching the soil helps keep flowers attached so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I buy new certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from previous harvests often lose their vigor and natural resistance to pests, leading to smaller yields. Certified seeds are specially bred to grow uniform, healthy crops that yield far more food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yaa nɔ daa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread diseases, or by heavy heat stress. Controlling whiteflies early and watering consistently keeps the foliage healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa Whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ mra Ni nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial to pinch off the small side shoots on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaamɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tomato tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Removing small side branches forces the tomato plant to send its energy and food directly into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Niji bibii ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ni afoɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii aya tɛ̃ɛ kɛya aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cowpeas grow lots of big green leaves but very few pods during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ dara waa shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water and nitrogen encourage cowpeas to focus entirely on leafy green growth instead of making flowers and pods. They yield better when planted so that flowering happens during moderate rainfall and drier weather.
ga: Nu kɛ nitrogen babaoo baaha cowpea kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ ama baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ lɛ Ewoɔ yibii babaoo kɛji adu lɛ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi aba yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo kɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that scorch easily in direct sunlight. Leaving tall trees or planting shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from harsh sun and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa bushes grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and prevent themselves from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout new leaves and continue growing its tubers under the ground.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars feeding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani ooohi tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by stem borers or armyworms that eat through young maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended pest control methods protects the crop before the worms destroy the whole harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borers loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and turn brown even when I give them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much water can drown their roots by blocking air, causing root rot that makes the leaves wilt. Tomatoes grow best when the soil is moist but well-drained, so you should only water them when the top layer of soil feels dry.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tomato daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ nu awo mli pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ nu he akɛ egbi.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I harvest more food from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Ani manyɛ maná mi nɔ babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow big and produce a fuller harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with lots of green leaves but fail to produce big fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni eyɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo shi ewooo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing leaves instead of flowering and fruiting. Crops need a balanced feed containing phosphorus and potassium to develop strong fruits and grains.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii lɛ, niyenii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia Tsei koni amɛwo yibii kɛ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my farm produce less maize every year even when I plant at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same soil every season exhausts specific nutrients and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating your crops with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts natural nitrogen back into the soil to restore its strength.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ ekome. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb up high to catch as much sunlight as possible with their leaves. Staking helps the leaves make food efficiently, which flows down into the ground to produce large, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛ amɛbaa lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive tough conditions, so they quickly grab available water, fertilizer, and light before your crops can. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops the head start they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni yɔɔ lɛ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa odumɔi lɛ yitso ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and grow white mold when I store it in bags right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa yɛŋ baa kɛji mikɛwo kotokui amli beni mikpa ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly picked maize still contains trapped moisture, which creates heat and mold when locked inside closed bags. Sun-drying your maize until the grains are completely hard removes excess moisture and keeps it safe for storage.
ga: Abɛi ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekã he lolo. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji akɛ awo kotoku ko ni aŋã mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa kwraa lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ehaa ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: I often see people selling soursop in traffic; is soursop a good crop for me to grow on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, minaa mɛi ni miihɔɔ soursop yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he. Ani soursop ji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa ni esa akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Yes, soursop grows very well in Ghana's warm climate. It has a high market demand because people love the sweet-sour fruit for fresh eating and juices, making it a profitable fruit crop for local markets.
ga: Hɛɛ, soursop kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Jarayeli he nibii babaoo yɛ ejaakɛ gbɔmɛi sumɔɔ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha niyenii hee kɛ nu. Enɛ haa efeɔ aduawai ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: What simple steps can I take to process my fresh fruit harvest so I can sell it for more money?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni fata aduawai heei ahe nitsumɔ he koni anyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ shika babaoo?

english: You can wash, peel, and extract the pulp from ripe fruits like soursop to sell as fresh juice, frozen pulp, or dried fruit slices. Simple processing extends shelf life and allows you to target urban buyers and roadside vendors for higher profit.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofɔ, ojie, ni ogbala ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ tamɔ soursop mli koni okɛhɔ̃ɔ akɛ nu hee, ŋmɔtɔ ni afɔ lɛ fɛ̃i, loo aduawai ni egbi lɛ amli fãi. Nibii ni afeɔ lɛ mlɛo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa okɛ ohiɛ fɔɔ maŋtiase mli jarayelɔi kɛ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ jarayelɔi anɔ koni onine ashɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo nɔ.

english: When I want to plant soursop from seeds, do I need to break or open the hard outer seed coat first?
ga: Be ni esa akɛ akwɛ soursop kɛjɛ dumɔwu mli Ani esa akɛ mafo loo magbele dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Soursop seeds have a tough outer shell that slows down water absorption. Lightly scratching the seed coat or soaking the seeds in warm water overnight helps them sprout much faster and more evenly.
ga: Soursop dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa ni haa nu shwieɔ amɛhe fioo. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwie shi blɛoo Loo okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu ni mli edɔ mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛfee ekome.

english: If I save seeds from a sweet soursop fruit I bought at the market, will they grow into a tree that produces the exact same sweet fruit?
ga: Kɛji mibua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ soursop yibii ni ŋɔɔ ni mihe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani nakai dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Trees grown directly from seed can vary slightly from the parent tree in fruit size and taste. To get identical sweet fruit and faster production, many farmers use grafting rather than planting seeds directly.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee srɔto fioo yɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ he yɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ mli. Koni onine ashɛ yibii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni okɛwo yibii oya. Okwaafoi babaoo kɛ grafting tsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui ni amɛduɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do some of my soursop tree flowers fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soursop fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Soursop flowers often drop off due to poor pollination or hot, dry weather. In nature, soursop flowers rely on tiny beetles for pollination, so keeping the soil moist and encouraging beneficial insects helps more flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, soursop fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pollination ni ehiii loo shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hewɔ. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, soursop fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ koni amɛná ŋmeii, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Does soursop need full sunlight to produce good fruits, or can I plant it under big shade trees?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa he miihia soursop koni ewo yibii kpakpai? Aloo abaanyɛ atɛo yɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hɔɔŋ shishi?

english: Soursop trees produce best in full sunlight or very light shade. Planting them under a dense tree canopy starves them of light, reducing flower production and fruit size.
ga: Soursop tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse waa mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha la akafee nɔ ko. Ehaa fɔfɔii ni anáa kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Can I use both the fruit pulp and the seeds of soursop, or is it only the fruit flesh that is useful?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ aduawai amli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ soursop dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii? Aloo aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ pɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ?

english: The soft fruit flesh is mainly used for fresh food and juice. While the seeds are not eaten, crushed seeds and leaves are traditionally used to extract natural oils for insect control on crops.
ga: Akɛ aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsuɔ nii titri kɛfeɔ niyenii hee kɛ nu. Eyɛ mli akɛ ayeee dumɔwui lɛ moŋ, Shi bei pii lɛ, akɛ dumɔwui ni atswa lɛ kɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔji ni akɛyeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know when a soursop fruit is ready to harvest so it doesn't spoil before I get it to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kɛ́ mi-soursop yibii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ, amɛfiteee dani amɛya jara nɔ?

english: Harvest soursop when the dark green skin turns slightly yellowish-green and the sharp spines soften and spread apart. The fruit will still be firm, allowing you to transport it safely before it softens fully.
ga: Kpãa soursop be mli ni hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ-ŋmɔŋ fioo. ni ŋmeii ni naa wa lɛ baafee blɛoo ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Yibii lɛ baakã he ahi shi shiŋŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ amɛ yaa shweshweeshwe dani amɛfeɔ blɛoo kwraa.

english: Why are white powdery bugs sticking to my fruit trees and making the leaves turn black?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda lɛ miikpɛtɛ mi aduawai tsei lɛ ahe ni amɛmiiha baai lɛ miifee ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: These white bugs are mealybugs that suck sap from the tree and secrete a sugary substance where black mold grows. You can manage them early by spraying a mixture of soapy water or neem seed oil on the affected stems and leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii yɛŋ nɛɛ ji mealybugs ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nɔ ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii diji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ kpo. Obaanyɛ otsu he nii mra. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛ samla efutu loo neem dumɔwui amli fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei kɛ baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What kind of soil does a soursop tree need to avoid root rot during the heavy rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ he hiaa soursop tso koni shishifãi akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Soursop trees need loose, well-draining soil rich in organic matter. They suffer in waterlogged ground, so planting on raised mounds or gentle slopes prevents standing water from rotting the roots.
ga: Soursop tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli. Amɛnáa amanehulu yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni ekã shi lɛ naa koni ekafite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Adding compost or the right fertilizer gives the crop the essential nutrients it needs to stay green and produce big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná toi wuji.

english: How can I tell if spending money on chemical fertilizer will actually increase my vegetable farm profits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shika ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha sɛɛnamɔ ni jɛɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer works best when soil has enough organic matter to hold onto it; testing your soil or trying fertilizer on a small test patch helps you see if the extra crop yield covers the cost.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kaa shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ kaa ŋmei bibioo ko nɔ. Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ atsu shika ni he hiaa lɛ he nii.

english: What will happen to my farmland if I rely only on chemical fertilizer every year without using animal manure?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ daa afi ni kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the plants quickly but do not nourish the ground; over time, the soil becomes hard and acidic, making it harder for roots to grow and hold water unless organic manure is added.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya shi amɛhaaa sũ lɛ niyenii. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni acid yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃ ni amɛhiɛ nu mli. ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he

english: Tomato plants lose water through their leaves rapidly in intense sun to keep cool; if they bounce back by evening, it is normal survival behavior, though adding mulch around the stem helps hold ground moisture longer.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. Kɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ lɛ eji wala mlihilɛ mli nifeemɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle The stems lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing lots of tall leafy branches but only small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai kakadaji babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil pushes cassava to put all its energy into leaf growth instead of storage roots; crops need balanced nutrients like potassium to build thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ ŋmei lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeya shishifãi lɛ amli. Niyenii ni ja tamɔ potassium he miihia tsei koni amɛfee bulbs ni mli tse.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive fertilizer, as a protective behavior to save energy for the main plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli Bɔni afee ni akafite hewalɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛha tso titri lɛ.

english: Why do my cabbages get damaged by insect pests more when I grow only cabbage on the whole plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ kaabii babaoo yɛ be mli ni kaabii muu pɛ aduɔ lɛ?

english: Planting a single crop across an entire field creates an open feast for specific pests to multiply easily, whereas mixing different crops confuses insects and reduces pest damage.
ga: Tso kome ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi feɔ niyenii ni amɛshwereɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ futuɔ kooloi, ni ehaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do hybrid maize seeds cost more money than saving seeds from my own last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ jara wa fe dumɔwui ni mikɛbaahere kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are carefully bred to produce high yields and resist local diseases in their first generation, whereas seeds saved from a previous harvest lose that strength and result in smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛha yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni no baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with poor harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo ehiii beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, causing them to stretch upward for light rather than developing strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ koni amɛhe la lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo ŋmeii ni wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why is it better to clear and prepare my land before the rains start instead of waiting for the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ moŋ fe nɔ ni aaamɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ?

english: Preparing land early allows cleared weeds to break down into nutrients, so when the first rains fall, your seeds can be planted immediately to take full advantage of early soil warmth and moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ, abaanyɛ adu Dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shishijee hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my rubber trees are old enough to start tapping them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-gum tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi tswamɔ?

english: Rubber trees are generally ready for tapping when they are between 5 and 7 years old and their trunk reaches a thickness of about 50 centimeters measured at 1 meter above the ground. Tapping trees that are too young weakens them and reduces the total amount of latex they can produce over their lifespan.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔba tsei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaatswa amɛhe kɛji amɛye kɛjɛ afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo, ni amɛtso lɛ shishi lɛ mli tse aaafee sɛntimitai 50, ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he mita kome. Kɛ́ atswa tsei bibii tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ajie yɛ ewala be fɛɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why does liquid latex stop flowing so quickly after I make a fresh cut on my rubber tree bark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ latɛs lɛ kpaɔ oya beni mifo rɔbɔt ŋmɔtɔ hee lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Latex naturally stops flowing because the liquid dries up and forms a plug over the cut to heal the tree's skin. However, if it stops too quickly, it could mean the cut was made too shallow, the tapping tool was dull, or you tapped during the hottest part of the day when the tree is losing water.
ga: Nu lɛ mli nu lɛ kpaɔ shwiemɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni nu lɛ gĩɔ lɛ ni efeɔ plɔg yɛ pilamɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsa tso lɛ hewolo lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ ekpa oya tsɔ lɛ, Enɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. blunt tapping device Aloo ofoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni tso lɛ nu fiteɔ.

english: What causes black rotting wounds on the area where I cut my rubber tree bark?
ga: Mɛni kɛ pilamɔ diŋ ni miifite yɛ he ni afo rɔba tso lɛ he lɛ baa?

english: Rotting on tapped bark is usually caused by fungal infections, especially during humid or rainy weather. Cutting too deep into the inner wood or using uncleaned tapping knives allows fungal diseases to enter and damage the tree's skin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni atswa lɛ baa. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be loo nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo akɛ tsɔne ni he tseee tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ abote mli ni efite tso lɛ hewolo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and burn when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaf surfaces and shallow root systems that cannot handle intense heat. They require shade trees or fast-growing shade crops like plantains to shelter them from direct sun until they grow mature leaves and deeper roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Kɛyashi amɛbaaná baai ni eda kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight. The plants stretch upward as fast as possible to reach light, spending energy on height instead of building strong stems or thick fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei baatswa hulu la he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Tso lɛ baajie ehe kpo oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ la lɛ awo mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa moŋ fe ni eeefee tsei ni mli wa loo aduawai ni mli tse.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip down in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiya shi yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips in a V-shape show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil food for growth. Maize uses large amounts of nitrogen to stay green and produce big cobs, so applying nitrogen fertilizer restores leaf health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo tsuɔ nii koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava crop growing very tall with lush green leaves but producing very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too little potassium, cassava plants spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending starches down to swell the roots into big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo potassium fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu starch kɛba shi koni eha shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop curl up and droop during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense trick plants use to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing water loss through evaporation. If the leaves uncurl and recover by evening, the plant is simply managing the heat.
ga: Baai akumɔ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛba amɛhiɛ he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi ni amɛhe wa amɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miikwɛ dɔlɛ nɔ kɛkɛ.

english: How does covering the soil around my crop stems with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps soil moisture during hot days, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly decays into rich organic fertilizer for the roots.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Will trimming off lower or old branches hurt my crop or help it yield more?
ga: Ani niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo ni egbɔ lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua ni yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Pruning old or shaded lower branches helps the crop because it directs food and energy to the fruit-bearing parts. It also lets air flow through the farm, reducing dampness that causes crop diseases.
ga: Niji ni egbɔ loo ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ejaakɛ ebaatsɔɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛya hei ni yibii lɛ woɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ha hulutsoo ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I start nursing my tomato seeds in a small backyard bed before moving them to my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi tomato dumɔwui yɛ saatso bibioo ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ shia lɛ sɛɛ dani mifã kɛtee miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Nursing seeds in a small, controlled area allows you to protect young, fragile shoots from harsh weather, heavy rain, and pests until they build strong roots and stems for transplanting.
ga: Aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ he bibioo ko. Tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Kɛyashi amɛbaafee shishifãi kɛ tsei ni mli wa ni akɛbaadu.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither when I plant them directly in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct heat and sunshine. They require shade from nurse crops like plantains or cassava to hold moisture and shield them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ tamɔ plantains loo cassava mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi amɛhe ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow even though they get regular rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil has run out of vital nutrients like nitrogen. Applying compost, organic manure, or the right fertilizer restores the plant's health and turns the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, humus, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ abaadu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating crops, especially with beans or groundnuts, restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii komɛi be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ mli, titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Watering early in the morning lets the roots absorb moisture before heat builds up. Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate too quickly and can scorch leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ nu dani latsaa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ ni ebaaha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cover the soil around my plants with dry grass or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, keeps root zone temperatures cool during hot days, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for light, ground water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the food they need to grow robustly.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce very small fruits when I sow many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kwraa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Overcrowding forces seedlings to fight each other for sunlight and root space. Proper spacing allows every individual plant enough room to feed, branch out, and bear large fruits.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛwu amɛha hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii, ekɛ eniji, ni ewoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Why should I trim off extra side branches and lower leaves on my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ sɛɛ niji kɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Trimming excess branches prevents the plant from wasting nutrients on leaves, directing its energy instead into developing bigger, healthier peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi niyenii ni haa tso lɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ naa. ni etsɔ ehewalɛ nɔ ekɛfee chili ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Flowers drop off due to severe heat stress, irregular watering, or insect attack. Keeping soil moisture steady and protecting blooms from pests helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ fɔfɔi ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to extreme heat. Sunlight scorches their young leaves and dries out soil moisture rapidly, which is why shade trees or companion plantains are needed to protect them during their early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa, ni amɛnuɔ he waa kɛ́ edɔ waa. Hulu lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ egbiɔ oya. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni afee nanemɛi tsei loo plantains lɛ shade koni abu amɛhe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when they start bearing heavy fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ebɔi yibii ni tsii womɔ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep, woody roots to anchor them in the soil. As the heavy bunch grows, the top becomes heavy, so strong winds easily push the plant over unless it is supported with wooden or bamboo props.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni kuu lɛ da lɛ Ŋwɛi fã lɛ baafee tsiimɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ tswaa tsei amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. ja tso loo ŋmeii fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is an essential food that keeps maize leaves green and healthy so the plant can feed the developing corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haa ŋmãa toi ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm alongside my maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ ŋmei masɛi?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize naturally enriches the soil with free fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmãa lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam plants with tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atswa mi-sweet potato tso lɛ he adafi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to make food for tuber growth. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground to spread the leaves towards the sun, which helps produce much larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking baawó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni egbɛ efoji lɛ eshwa hulu lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ yitso ni da kwraa.

english: Why does my ginger crop rot easily when I plant it in heavy clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ginger tso lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Ginger underground stems need soft, well-draining soil to expand. Heavy clay soil traps water around the roots, causing the soil to become waterlogged and forcing the ginger rhizomes to rot.
ga: Ginger tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Shikpɔŋ sũ ni mli tse lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu kɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ginger rhizome lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather becomes too hot, when soil moisture changes suddenly from dry to overly wet, or when pests attack the blossoms before bees can pollinate them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fe nine mli lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua fɔfɔii dani ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afee amɛ pollen.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or whiteflies. As they feed on the leaves, they introduce viruses or cause the leaf tissues to grow unevenly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ Amɛjieɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo amɛhaa baai lɛ amli fãji lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal disease that thrives in cold, dark, and damp conditions. The heavy rain spreads fungal spores from the soil onto the cocoa pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are storage organs that peak in starch quality at maturity. If left in the ground past their prime, the plant converts starch into tough plant fibers, making the roots hard and difficult to cook.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji nibii ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe ni starch ni hi fe fɛɛ yɔɔ mli kɛji eda kwraa. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛteke he ni eyɔɔ lɛ, Tsei tsakeɔ starch amɛfeɔ tsei ahe tsɔi ni wa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ wa ni ewa akɛ amɛaakwɛ̃.

english: Cocoa yields drop when soil nutrients get exhausted, when trees grow too old, or when high humidity and poor sunlight cause flowers and young pods to drop off before maturing.
ga: Cocoa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Beni tso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ loo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo ni hulu la lɛ faaa kwraa. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: How many years can my cocoa tree keep bearing good fruit before it becomes too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A cocoa tree usually produces high yields for about 25 to 30 years. After this, fruit production naturally declines unless you prune heavily or replant with new seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afii 25 kɛyashi 30, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, yibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ja ofolɔ tsei lɛ amli waa loo odu dumɔwui heei.

english: Why is it important for me to trim or lift the lower branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mawo mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming low branches lets fresh air flow through the farm and allows sunlight to reach the trunk, which prevents moisture from causing fungal diseases on your pods.
ga: pruning low branches Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eha hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akakɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: My young cocoa trees have just started showing small flowers, so what should I do to make sure those flowers turn into healthy pods?
ga: No mli lɛ, mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ ebɔi fɔfɔi bibii fɔmɔ. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni nakai fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Protect the flowering trees by keeping light shade over them, clearing weeds at the base, and avoiding harsh sprays that might drive away the tiny insects that pollinate the cocoa flowers.
ga: Buu tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni oooha amɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashwie kooloi bibii lɛ ahe. ni haa kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm is getting too much shade from big trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo kɛmiijɛ tsei wuji amli?

english: If your cocoa trees have very dark green leaves but produce very few pods, or if pods rot easily on the tree, the farm is getting too much shade and needs more sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ waa shi ŋmɔtɔi lɛ faaa kwraa. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ oya Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo ni ehe miihia ni hulu la babaoo aba.

english: What happens to my cocoa plants if they get too much direct sunlight without any shade trees?
ga: Mɛni baa mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni tso lɛ haaa amɛ hulutsoo?

english: Without shade, young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn, the soil dries out quickly, and the trees become weak and easily attacked by insect pests like mirids.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya. Tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuaa amɛ oya.

english: Why are some of my small green cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ tsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by black pod disease or natural pod wilt, which happens when there is too much dampness around the tree or when the tree lacks enough nutrients to feed all the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela loo adebɔɔ mli wilt hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni baa beni ebɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ aye abua lɛ.

english: How does clearing tall weeds under my cocoa trees help keep my pods healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-pods lɛ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds hold extra dampness against the lower tree trunks and hide pests; clearing them lowers moisture levels around the cocoa trees and stops fungus from spreading to the pods.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yaa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai teeɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni ebɔle he lɛ aba shi. cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ ni etsĩ ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Apply fertilizer at the start of the rainy season when the soil is wet, as this helps the tree roots absorb nutrients right before flowering and pod formation begin.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani fɔfɔi kɛ pod feemɔ jeɔ shishi.

english: Pods are ready for harvest when their skin turns completely yellow (for green pods) or orange (for red pods). Harvesting at this stage ensures the beans inside are fully mature.
ga: Pods lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhewolo lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ. Amɛji ŋmɔtɔ (kɛha ŋmɔtɔi eŋɔli) loo ŋmɔtɔ (kɛha ŋmɔtɔ tsuru). Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a vital food for growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure helps restore their dark green color and boosts yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is the difference between using animal manure and buying chemical fertilizer for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kooloi aŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahemɔ teŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizer gives your crops a quick shot of specific nutrients right away, but animal manure improves the long-term soil health and helps the ground hold onto water better during dry spells.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi oya, amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Why do you advise me to leave wide spaces between my crops instead of planting them close together to get more plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ owoɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mashi gbɛjegbɛi wuji yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo du mɛ kɛ su he konɛ o ná tsohi fuu.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and produce bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Which direction should I point the buds when planting cassava stem cuttings in my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always plant cassava cuttings with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow downwards first before turning up, which wastes the plant's energy and reduces root growth.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei niji ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni akɛ hiɛ tsɔɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ adara kɛya shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to hide and eat inside the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the center of corn plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended insecticides or neem oil extracts can stop them before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of insect pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and planting at the right time helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ falɛ faaa Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni ehaa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: Weeds act like aggressive thieves that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight to feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni yitsoŋ wa, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa niyenii ni okɛhaa onibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if the ground is ready for planting right after the first rain falls?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain of the season can fool you because only the top surface gets wet while the deeper soil remains dry. Dig down a few inches and squeeze a handful of soil; if it forms a moist ball that stays together without dripping, the ground is ready for seeds.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ alaka bo. Ejaakɛ ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he egbi. Tsɔɔmɔ shi inchii fioo komɛi ni okɛmimɔ shikpɔŋ ni fa fioo. Kɛji akɛ efee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kokroo. Moist ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ.

english: Yam vines dry up early when attacked by fungal diseases like anthracnose or when the soil gets too hot and dry. Staking the vines off the ground and covering the base with dry leaves keeps the soil cool and reduces disease.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose tutua amɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi. Kɛ́ adu wain tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi aha shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support, so they drop extra flowers to save energy. However, extreme heat, lack of soil moisture, or insect pests like mirids can also cause too many flowers to drop.
ga: Kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Shi kɛlɛ, latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni bɛ kɛ Aloo, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afite fe nine.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing small flowers when the plants are still very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi bibii be mli ni tso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants flower early when they feel stressed by dry weather or poor soil nutrients, trying to produce seeds before they die. Plucking off the early flowers and giving the plant water and food allows it to grow bigger first.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔ̃ɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo dumɔwui dani amɛgboi. Kɛ́ otsi fɔfɔi lɛ mra ni okɛ nu ha tso lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eda klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How come my cassava roots are rotting in the ground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays around them for too long because roots need air to breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny whitefly insects spreading a plant virus, or by extreme heat and dry soil. Controlling insect pests and keeping the soil moist helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli loo kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend planting cowpea or groundnuts before I plant my maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii dani adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea and groundnuts are legumes that have special bacteria in their roots which trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that cannot support the heavy weight of big bunches during strong winds. Supporting the stems with strong wooden props or bamboo sticks prevents them from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ tsei niji wuji ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my main crops after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitso titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to local conditions, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops the space they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akpã gbee. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ aná he ko ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do tiny insects attack and destroy my harvested maize grains while they are stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weevils are attracted to moisture inside stored grain. If maize is not completely dried in the sun before storage, or if the storage container is not sealed tightly, weevils multiply quickly and eat the grains from the inside.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛto loo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli kwraa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ faa oya ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: What is Swollen Shoot disease, and why is it so dangerous for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji bud hela ni efuu? Ni mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Swollen Shoot is a serious viral disease that attacks cocoa trees in Ghana. It causes the branches and roots to swell, turns leaves pale or reddish, and eventually stops the tree from producing cocoa pods, causing the tree to die over time.
ga: Tsoi ni efuu lɛ ji hela ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni tutuaa kookoo tsei yɛ Ghana. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji kɛ shishifãi lɛ fuɔ, baai lɛ feɔ tsuru loo etsuru, ni naagbee lɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii feemɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Are there other diseases I need to watch out for on my cocoa farm besides Swollen Shoot?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ akwɛ ehe nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ helai krokomɛi ahe kɛfata tsitsi hela he?

english: Yes, cocoa crops face several diseases in Ghana, such as Black Pod disease and Swollen Shoot. Each disease attacks different parts of the tree, which is why farmers need to keep a close eye on their leaves, stems, and pods.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo tsei kɛ helai babaoo kpeɔ yɛ Ghana, tamɔ black pod hela kɛ bud swollen hela. Hela fɛɛ hela tutuaa tso lɛ fãi srɔtoi, no hewɔ ni esa akɛ okwaafoi akwɛ tso lɛ baai, eshishifãi, kɛ eshishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Can plants get sick from viruses just like human beings do?
ga: Ani tsei baanyɛ aná hela kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ mli tamɔ adesai?

english: Yes, crops can catch viral infections just like people. Plant viruses are usually spread by tiny insects like mealybugs. Once a cocoa tree gets a virus like Swollen Shoot, the virus moves throughout the tree's internal sap and cannot be washed off or killed with regular chemical sprays.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aná helai ni gbeɔ mɔ tamɔ adesai pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs gbɛɔ tsei amli helai. Kɛji hela ko mɔ kookoo tso ko, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, hela lɛ nyiɛɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ fɛɛ mli. ni anyɛɛɛ afɔ he loo agbe lɛ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why has Swollen Shoot disease been affecting farms in Ghana for so many years without going away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bamboo shoot bloat hela lɛ emɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ amli afii babaoo ni ehiɛɛɛ shi lɛ?

english: Swollen Shoot has remained for decades because the virus travels easily from tree to tree through small insects and can hide in wild trees near farms. Because there is no chemical cure for an infected tree, the disease continues to persist unless infected trees are completely removed.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni efuu lɛ hiɔ shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ejaakɛ hela lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii amli kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ mlɛo, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ehe awo koo mli tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛtsaa tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ hela lɛ baaya nɔ ja ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ kwraa.

english: How can I check my cocoa trees to know if they have a virus?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ cacao tsei lɛ amli kɛji amɛyɛ helai?

english: Look out for swollen areas on young stems or roots, strange yellow or red patterns on the leaves, smaller pods, and leaves falling off prematurely. If you see these signs, it usually indicates a viral infection.
ga: Taomɔ hei ni efuu yɛ tso lɛ shishi loo shishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ. Naakpɛɛ ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru yɛ baa lɛ nɔ, pods bibii, kɛ baa lɛ gbee shi oya. Kɛji ona okadii nɛɛ Bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa.

english: What is crop pruning, and why should I do it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei ahe ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pruning means using clean tools to cut away dead, extra, or overgrown branches from your crops. It opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and fresh air can flow through, which keeps the tree healthy and boosts harvest yield.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ okɛ nibii ni he tse baafo niji ni egboi, ni fa fe nine, loo ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛjɛ onibii amli. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ ni agbeleɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ tsei lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How does cutting off branches through pruning help protect my cocoa trees from diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baanyɛ abu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe?

english: When trees are too bushy, water and damp air get trapped inside, creating a humid environment where diseases love to grow. Pruning lets sunlight and wind dry out the branches, making it harder for diseases to survive and spread.
ga: Beni tso lɛ efee ŋmɔji tsɔ Nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ baatsi emli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai srɔtoi baa mli lɛ baa. sumɔɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ Tsoi lɛ ahe niji lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbiɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa hela lɛ akɛ eeehi shi ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Will pruning my cocoa trees reduce the number of pods I harvest?
ga: Ani cacao tsei ni afoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: No, proper pruning actually increases your pod harvest. When you remove unnecessary or weak branches, the tree stops wasting energy on them and directs all its water and nutrients into growing big, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa o-pod kpamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ ojie niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ hewalɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: If a plant disease has no direct cure, how can I protect my cocoa farm from getting infected?
ga: Kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ atsa tso hela lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anaa koni hela akamɔ amɛ?

english: Protection comes down to good farm care: prune your trees regularly, clear weeds where insects hide, plant disease-resistant cocoa varieties, and quickly cut down any tree that shows clear signs of Swollen Shoot before it infects neighboring trees.
ga: Nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ kpakpa nɔ: Kpɔ̃ɔ otsei lɛ daa. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ. Kookoo henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ Ni afolɔ tsei ni jieɔ ŋmeii ahe okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo lɛ oya dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are agricultural officers emphasizing farm hygiene and maintenance so much this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi maa ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ kɛ ekwɛmɔ nɔ mi waa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Good farm hygiene—like pruning, removing bad pods, and clearing weeds—is the cheapest and most effective way to prevent costly disease outbreaks before they destroy your farm's production for the year.
ga: Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ kpakpa, tamɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi Nibii ni ehiii ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ Eji gbɛ ni jara waaa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ helai ni jara wa lɛ agbɛfaŋ. Dani ebaafite oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ afi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take for a plantain crop to start bearing food after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani plantains lɛ jeɔ niyenii namɔ shishi beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: When you plant plantain and take good care of it, it should normally start bearing food from eleven months onwards.
ga: Kɛji adu plantains ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Taakɛ eji lɛ, esa akɛ aje niyenii hamɔ shishi kɛjɛ nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ ekome kɛyaa.

english: What is the expected growth timeline for a healthy plantain farm?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ plantain ŋmɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baadara?

english: If you maintain your farm well and keep weeds away, your plantain plants should be ready to start producing food around eleven months after planting.
ga: Kɛji okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ojie jwɛi lɛ, Esa akɛ Odumɔwui lɛ afee klalo ni amɛje niyenii feemɔ shishi aaafee nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ ekome sɛɛ beni adu lɛ.

english: How do weeds affect the growth and fruiting time of my plantain plants?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa mi plantain tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛwomɔ be lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from your plantains. If you let weeds take over the farm, it will severely slow down the plant's growth and delay fruiting.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ o-plantains lɛ amli. Kɛji oha jwɛi ye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ waa ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is my plantain crop taking over two years to produce food when others harvest earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe afii enyɔ dani ewoɔ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi kpaɔ lɛ mra lɛ?

english: When weeds are allowed to overcrowd the farm and maintenance is neglected, a whole year or two can pass without the plantain bearing food, even though it should normally produce in eleven months.
ga: Beni aŋmɛɔ jwɛi gbɛ ni eyi ŋmɔji amli obɔ ni amɛkuɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛkwɛmɔ nɔ Afi kome loo afii enyɔ baanyɛ aho ni plantains bɛ akɛ niyenii. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ afee yɛ nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ ekome mli moŋ.

english: What will happen to my plantain yield if I leave weeds to grow in my field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantain ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving weeds unchecked starves the plantain of strength. The crop will take much longer to produce food, turning what should be an eleven-month crop into a process that takes years.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ mli awa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani enáa niyenii. Nɔ ni esa akɛ efee ŋmɔshi nibii ni eye nyɔji 11 lɛ ni aaatsake lɛ afee afii babaoo nifeemɔ.

english: Is it really necessary to spend money on maintaining my plantain farm after planting?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni afite shika kɛkwɛ plantain ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, investing money and effort into weed control and general maintenance is essential if you want your plantain to bear food on time without losing years of production.
ga: Hɛɛ, shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni okɛaawo jwɛi akudɔmɔ kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ mli lɛ he miihia waa kɛji oosumɔ ni aha o-plantains lɛ niyenii yɛ be naa ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ akafite afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant plantains but don't have enough money or labor to clear the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu plantains shi mibɛ shika loo nitsulɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa?

english: If you cannot maintain the farm, weeds will overwhelm the crop. The plantain will fail to yield food on time, and years will pass before you get any harvest.
ga: Kɛji onyɛɛɛ okwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Jwɛi lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Plantains lɛ wooo niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli. Ni afii babaoo baaho dani nyɛbaanyɛ nyɛkpa nii.

english: If my plantain plant has not produced food after a whole year, does it mean I bought bad seeds or suckers?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ wooo niyenii yɛ afi muu fɛɛ sɛɛ hu? Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mihe dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni ehiii?

english: Not necessarily. Very often, delayed fruiting is not the fault of the plantain itself, but rather the result of weeds taking over and a lack of proper field maintenance.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ jeee plantain lɛ hewɔ. Shi nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jwɛi ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my plantains standing in the field for a long time without yielding any food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni niyenii ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Plantains need a clean field to thrive. If they are neglected and choked by weeds, their growth stalls, causing years to go by without producing any food.
ga: He ko ni he tse he miihia plantains koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji aku hiɛ ashwie amɛnɔ ni jwɛi ha amɛhe lɛ, Amɛdalɛ baafee mlɛo. Enɛ ha afii babaoo ho ni anáaa niyenii ko kwraa.

english: Can poor field maintenance completely stop my plantain from bearing fruit when it is supposed to?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi mi plantains lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, poor maintenance and weed invasion will heavily delay fruiting. Even though the crop is capable of bearing food at eleven months, neglect will push the harvest back by years.
ga: Hɛɛ, saamɔ ni ehiii kɛ jwɛi ni baa lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ asɛɛ afo waa. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aha niyenii yɛ nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ ekome mli moŋ, Shi kɛji aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni aduɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food corn needs to grow green and strong. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure will help restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots, it suffocates them and encourages fungal diseases that cause the tubers to rot underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, amɛhaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Cowpeas belong to a group of plants called legumes that can trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant matures or decomposes, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas fata tsei akuu ko ni atsɛɔ amɛ legumes ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. Kɛ tsei dara loo amɛfite Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines produce lots of big green leaves but very small potatoes underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi shishigbɛ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes the plant to put all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of roots below. Using balanced nutrients with more potassium encourages the plant to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Niyenii ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early and removing severely infected plants prevents the virus from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ni tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp and overly shady conditions. Pruning your cocoa trees to let in sunlight and air helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars eating the plant. Inspecting leaf undersides regularly and applying biological treatments or natural sprays like neem oil can protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my pepper plants while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Pepper tso lɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients that young pepper plants need to establish strong roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop receives full nourishment to yield plenty of peppers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa pepper tsei bibii koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni yeɔ emuu koni ekɛ chili babaoo aba.

english: Why do my watermelon flowers fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Watermelon flowers need bees and other insects to carry pollen from male to female flowers. If insects are absent or if the weather is extremely hot and dry, unpollinated flowers will simply drop off.
ga: Watermelon fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi. Koni ekɛ pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli lɛ amaje fɔfɔi yoo lɛ. Kɛji kooloi bɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ waa lɛ Fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollination lɛ baagbee shi.

english: How does covering my yam mounds with dry grass help them grow during hot weather?
ga: Bɔ ni jwɛi ni akɛhaa ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) blocks direct sunlight, which prevents water from evaporating quickly. It keeps the soil cool and moist so the yam tubers can grow steadily without drying out.
