ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa ni ekaho oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ aya nɔ ada ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and curling up during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot weather to save water and keep from drying out. If they are also turning yellow, it usually means the plant lacks water or needs nitrogen fertilizer in the soil to grow strong and green.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛkagbi. Kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo tso lɛ mli loo ehe miihia ni akɛ nitrogen awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get too hot, stressed from lack of water, or when given too much chemical fertilizer high in nitrogen, which makes the plant grow extra leaves instead of holding onto its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli loo beni enine shɛɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa baai krokomɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: When plantains are planted too close, their leaves block each other's sunlight and their roots fight for nutrients and water in the dirt. Spacing them further apart allows each stem to get enough sunlight and food to grow big bunches faster.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni kã tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ naa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji oya.

english: Why did my cowpea seeds fail to come up out of the soil after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ ejeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in the soil, if the ground is too dry, or if insects and rot attack the seeds underground. Planting them shallow in moist soil helps them break through quickly.
ga: Cowpea dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii tutua shikpɔŋ shishi dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛboteɔ mli oya.

english: How can I tell if my soil is rich enough to grow cassava without buying expensive chemical tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi kɛ shika bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei nɔ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛkaa mɔ he lɛ?

english: You can judge soil health by looking at it: rich soil is usually dark, crumbly, and holds moisture well. If previous crops grew slowly with pale leaves or the soil is dry and light sandy gray, it needs compost or animal manure to build up nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ha lɛ kɛtsɔ ekwɛmɔ nɔ: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ da blɛoo ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii koni akɛfee niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Is it better for my tomato plants if I water them in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-tomato tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the soil can absorb the moisture before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon watering causes most water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast on my farm right after the first rain season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sleep in dry soil throughout the long dry season or harmattan. As soon as the first rains fall, the combination of heat and water wakes up thousands of seeds at once, allowing them to grow faster than planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo harmattan lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni akɛfee ekome lɛ teɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ shikome. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: What is causing white powdery spots on my tomato leaves, and will it destroy my farm?
ga: Mɛni kɛ powder yɛŋ ni yɔɔ tomato baai anɔ lɛ baa? Ni ani ebaafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: This white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, caused by damp air and crowded leaves. While it can dry out leaves and reduce how many tomatoes you harvest, leaving space between plants and removing low leaves stops it from spreading.
ga: Nɛkɛ powda yɛŋ nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ baai ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ ebaaha baai lɛ agbi ni ebaaha tomatoi ni okpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi moŋ. Shi kɛ́ ashi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ ni ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tomato lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Should I cut off the extra shoots growing on the sides of my cassava stems?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving too many stems forces the cassava plant to send food to leafy branches instead of roots. Leaving only one or two strong main stems encourages the plant to direct its energy underground to grow thick tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ ashi tsei ashishifãi babaoo ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ, ehaa ŋmei tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii kɛyaa tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ shishifã titri kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ amaje shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: How do I know my yam tubers are mature and ready to dig up without unearthing them first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ edara ni efee klalo akɛ mafolɔ ni mikɛfooo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yams tell you they are ready above ground: when the rainy season ends and the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up, it shows the plant has finished feeding the tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato lɛ kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food it needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my okro plant grow very tall with thick leaves but produces no okro fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi okra aduawai ko bɛ?

english: When okro gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, it spends all its energy growing big leaves and tall stems instead of flowers. Switching to a balanced fertilizer that contains phosphorus will encourage the plant to bloom and set fruit.
ga: Kɛ okra nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai wuji kɛ tsei kakadaji amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni phosphorus yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it important for me to rotate where I plant groundnuts on my farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ matsake ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts in the exact same spot every year lets soil diseases and specific pests build up in that area. Moving groundnuts to a new spot starves those pests and allows the plant to naturally add fresh nitrogen to different parts of your land.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii komɛi abua amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii kɛtee he ko hee lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii lɛ, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ nitrogen hee aba shikpɔŋ lɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up like cups and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny invisible insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juice out of young leaves. Spraying an organic neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticide gets rid of these insects so fresh leaves can open normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli Nu ni akɛjieɔ organic neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ. koni baai heei lɛ agbele bɔ ni sa

english: This is black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during rainy, damp weather. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight and wind reach the pods helps keep them dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niji lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant feels stressed, especially during extreme afternoon heat or when the soil gets too dry between waterings. Regular watering and mulching around the base keeps the root zone cool and helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I clear weeds away from my young cassava plants before the weeds get tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei bibii amli dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your cassava. Clearing them early ensures all the strength in the soil goes straight into making big cassava tubers instead of feeding useless weeds.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ o-cassava lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha hewalɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya nɔ afee ŋmei shishifãi wuji yɛ jwɛi ni he ehiaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during rainstorms even when the fruit is not ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ aduawai lɛ efeko klalo lolo lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and struggle to hold the tree when the soil gets heavy with rain and the fruit bunch grows heavy. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden pole or bamboo stake prevents the tree from snapping under the weight.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ tso lɛ he kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aduawai akutsei lɛ amli tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ yɛ muji lɛ shishi.

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the leaves and vines on top of the ground dry up and turn brown naturally. This drying shows that the plant has finished growing and has stored all its energy into the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe edalɛ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly on the floor before putting it into storage sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Wet or moist maize grains easily attract mold and destructive insects like weevils inside storage bags. Drying the grains in the sun until they are hard stops mold from growing and keeps your crop safe for months.
ga: Abɛi ni mli efɔ loo ni mli edɔ baanyɛ agbala ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛya kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ amli oya. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwaa Etsiɔ ŋmeii adalɛ naa ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture so the young cocoa trees can survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ ji koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to heap soil around my yam plants into large mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifeɔ muji agbo ko yɛ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and deep soil to expand downward easily. Mounding loosens the soil, improves water drainage so the tubers do not rot in waterlogged land, and makes harvesting easier.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootswa lɛ baaha egbɔjɔ. ha nu homɔ aya hiɛ Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. ni eha nikpamɔ afee mlɛo

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and pale instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth. It can happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or when weeds steal the plant's food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ daa lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ jwɛi ju tsei aniyenii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to heat stress or irregular watering. When the weather gets too hot or the soil swings between very dry and very wet, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the sap from tender leaves, or by viruses transmitted by whiteflies. The damaged leaf tissues twist and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Baai lɛ amli fãji ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the central growing point of maize plants. They hide deep inside the leaves to eat the tender foliage, leaving behind ragged holes and sawdust-like waste.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ he ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Eshiɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves have powdery white spots all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛhe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: White powdery spots are caused by a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It spreads easily when crops are planted too close together without proper airflow, or during periods of warm, humid weather.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. loo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ

english: How can I tell when my cassava is mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the bottom leaves turn yellow and shed, and the ground around the stem begins to crack open as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko egbɔ kɛji baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why does my soil dry out so quickly even after I water my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ po lɛ, mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Soil dries out fast when it lacks organic matter like compost, or if it has too much sand. Adding well-rotted animal manure or placing dry straw over the soil surface helps trap moisture like a sponge.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli loo ŋã babaoo yɛ mli. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he loo ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ sponji.

english: Why do my harvested maize cobs have missing corn kernels instead of full rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni akpa lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmeii?

english: Missing kernels happen when the maize flowers are poorly pollinated. If there is a drought or severe heat spell when the soft silks emerge from the cob, the pollen dries up before it can fertilize every kernel spot.
ga: Kernels ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa fɔfɔii lɛ efɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji hɔmɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa ba beni siliki ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ jeɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ. Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani enyɛɔ ewoɔ dumɔwu lɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: Is it better for me to plant a small farm neatly or clear a very large piece of land with limited help?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni yɔɔ fɛo loo mafo shikpɔŋ wulu ko nɔ kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ fioo ko pɛ?

english: A smaller, well-managed farm usually produces more food than a huge farm you cannot care for. When a field is too large for your strength, weeds take over and consume the soil's water and food before your crops can grow properly.
ga: Okwaafoi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ niyenii babaoo feemɔ fe ŋmɔji wuji ni onyɛɛɛ okwɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ ŋmɔji lɛ dara tsɔ fe ohewalɛ Jwɛi lɛ baaye nɔ ni amɛbaaye nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does rice require so much water on the field compared to maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants are naturally suited for wet soil because their roots and stems can breathe in shallow water. The water also acts as a natural barrier that prevents land weeds from growing and crowding out the rice.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli. Nu hu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkawo ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell when my rice crop is fully ripe and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Your rice is ready when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the stalks change from green to a golden yellow color and the lower leaves on the plant begin to dry out.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo beni o-rice lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ. ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and stronger than my crop plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants built to survive tough conditions, so they quickly drink up available rain and soil nutrients. Removing them early gives your main crops a fair chance to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya. early removal Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni ekwɛ̃ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do birds suddenly start flocking to my rice field when the crop starts forming grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi bɔi amɛhe buamɔ trukaa yɛ mi ŋmɔji lɛ amli beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi dumɔwui feemɔ lɛ?

english: When young rice grains first form, they fill with a sweet, soft liquid known as the milky stage. Birds love this liquid because it is easy food, so you must protect your farm during these specific few weeks.
ga: Beni afeɔ ŋmãa bibii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ Akɛ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ milk phase lɛ fataa he. Okpoi sumɔɔ nu nɛɛ ejaakɛ eji niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni obu oŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ otsii fioo nɛɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and grow poorly after planting on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Crops eat food from the soil to grow. If you plant the same crop every year without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil runs out of food, causing the leaves to turn yellow and stall in growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baaho yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest on my plot?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close causes plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space makes them grow thicker stems and yield larger grains or tubers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ ni ewo dumɔwui loo bulbs wuji.

english: Why should I buy improved rice seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred to produce more grain, grow faster, and stand strong against local diseases, whereas saved seeds slowly lose their strength over generations and yield less food.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ koni amɛwo dumɔwui babaoo. shwereɔ oya ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafee fiofio Ehewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni ewoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do people say I should plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field after harvesting cereals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take natural food from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, those roots stay in the dirt and fertilize the ground for the next grain crop.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai shishifãi lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha dumɔwui ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested rice turn moldy and get attacked by bugs when stored in my home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ nibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa lɛ kɛ́ akɛto mishia lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested rice still holds wetness inside the grain. If you do not dry the harvested grains thoroughly under the sun before storing them, trapped moisture creates mold and attracts hungry insects.
ga: Omɔ ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ eŋmaa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ogbiiee odumɔwui ni okpa lɛ kwraa dani okɛto lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and burn under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense, direct sunlight, which scorches their young leaves and stops them from growing. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them provides a protective umbrella that keeps the microclimate cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã ni amɛkpa dalɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa shade ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are my cocoa nursery seedlings growing very tall and thin instead of strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ miida waa ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔji najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch out tall and weak when they are kept under shade that is too thick. They are reaching out for more sunlight, so you need to thin out the nursery shade leaves gradually so the stems can grow thick and strong.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be babaoo shishi. Amɛmiishɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okɛtsu nii blɛoo. Fɔlɔmɔ baai ni yɔɔ shade lɛ mli koni eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like drinking straws in the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves inward to protect themselves from losing moisture through evaporation. It is a natural defense mechanism to survive heat and water stress during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ wala kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nu mli haomɔ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my cassava right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji oshara beni miduɔ mi-cassava lɛ?

english: Early rains can be deceiving and may be followed by a long dry weeks period. If the cassava sprouts and the soil dries up completely, the fragile young roots will wither and die before the main rains return.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ, ni otsi kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ Shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baagboi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get more harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak stalks and very small or empty maize cobs instead of a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná nibii babaoo ni afeɔ lɛ

english: Cassava roots fail to swell if the soil is packed too tight and hard for the roots to expand, or if the soil lacks potassium, which is the key nutrient plants use to store food inside tuber roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtoɔ niyenii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: A yellow V-shape on the lower leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant is moving its limited nitrogen supply to the top young leaves to keep growing, leaving the older leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni tamɔ V ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tso lɛ miijie nitrogen fioo ko kɛmiiya baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Kɛtsɔ baai momo lɛ ni oooha amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients like phosphorus. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛyashɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa, nu bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ mli. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies that damages normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ

english: Why do my plantain leaves get dark brown spots that spread until the whole leaf dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyashiɔ baai lɛ egbiɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal leaf disease called Black Sigatoka, which thrives in warm and humid conditions. Removing infected leaves reduces the spread so the plant can keep enough healthy leaves to feed its fruit bunch.
ga: Fungal leaf hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Sigatoka, ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa gbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ abua baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛha aduawai akui lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a living umbrella, protecting the young leaves from burning and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Etsiɔ baai bibii anaa koni amɛkashã ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Extreme heat and irregular watering stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers before pollination happens. Consistent watering and light shade during peak heat can help retain flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves and greenish dirt inside the plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ muji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by fall armyworms, which burrow into the center of maize plants and eat the growing leaves. Early spraying with appropriate bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Efoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui mli ni eyeɔ baai ni miida lɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nibii nɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on the same bed where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize draws a lot of food out of the soil, while cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air and return it back to the ground, restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, cowpea lɛ, ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli emɔɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow even when it rains every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ daa gbi po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential plant food (nutrients) like nitrogen directly from the soil, leaving your crops hungry and unable to stay green despite the rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa (nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ) tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do crops like groundnuts and millet thrive better in the North compared to tree crops like cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Kooyigbɛ kɛ akɛto tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo he lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and millet prefer dry climates and sandy, well-draining soil common in Northern Ghana, whereas cocoa needs heavy rainfall and humid environments typically found in Southern forest zones.
ga: Peanuts kɛ millets sumɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni bei pii lɛ anaa yɛ anaigbɛ kooi amli lɛ.

english: Is it wise to test a small patch of land with a new crop before planting my whole field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooka he bibioo ko okwɛ? kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ dani mikɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ adu.

english: Testing a small trial plot helps you see how the plant behaves in your specific soil and climate without risking your entire labor and financial investment if the crop fails.
ga: Shikpɔji bibii ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ lɛ haa onaa bɔ ni tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. ni ekɛ nitsumɔ kɛ shika fɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ wooo oshara mli kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start growing green shoots before the rain even starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ dani nugbɔ po jeɔ shishi enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy after resting for a few months. Rising temperatures signal to the tuber that it is time to sprout and grow into a new plant.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ tsɔɔ bulb lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei heei.

english: Why do cassava roots get hard and woody if I leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava stays past its maturity date, it loses starch, turns fibrous, and absorbs excess water, which lowers the quality and market value of the root.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei ye afii pɔtɛɛ ko lɛ Ebaafite ŋmei. tsakeɔ efeɔ fiber ni ekɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ kɛ jarayeli jara baa shi.

english: Why do buyers offer lower prices for my fresh peppers if I pick them in the middle of a hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa mi-peppers heei lɛ kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Peppers picked under hot sunlight lose water quickly, soft rapidly, and rot faster in transport, while cool peppers harvested early in the morning stay firm and fresh longer.
ga: Pepper ni akɛtoɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi lɛ nu fiteɔ oya. efeɔ blɛoo oya ni egboɔ oya yɛ gbɛfaa mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni mli ejɔ ni akpaa leebi lɛ baahi shi ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which acts as their main food for foliage growth. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer or well-rotted compost around the roots helps the leaves regain their green color and make food efficiently.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa lɛ bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he fɛɛ he Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa niyenii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts in my field will make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, meaning they have friendly bacteria living on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. After harvesting groundnuts, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to naturally feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ helai ni haa mɔ he feɔ naanyo ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Beni okpa ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many leaves but producing only tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive shade, the plant sends all its energy upward to build leaves and stems instead of underground tubers. Giving the plant full sunlight and balancing soil nutrients encourages food storage in the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo nɔ. Tso lɛ tsuɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛfee baai kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulu la kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni ja ha tsei lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can spread out to catch maximum sunlight for photosynthesis. If vines lay on the hot, damp ground, leaves rot easily and the plant cannot produce large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha fotosintɛsis. Kɛji akɛ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo he ko ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ oya ni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I cut down all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense direct sunlight and hot wind, which cause them to lose water faster than their young roots can absorb it. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains provides a protective canopy until the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Enɛ haa nu lɛ laajeɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ Loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are my growing watermelons rotting on the side that rests directly on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon ni miida lɛ miifite yɛ afã ni miita shikpɔŋ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelon skin absorbs dampness directly from wet soil, creating an ideal environment for soil fungi and insects to attack the fruit. Placing a layer of dry straw or a small wooden board under each melon keeps it dry and safe until harvest.
ga: Watermelon hewolo lɛ ŋmɛɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛtutua aduawai lɛ. Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei bibii ni akɛwoɔ mli Okɛwo melon fɛɛ melon shishi koni eye ebua ni watermelon lɛ agbi ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi kpamɔ be mli.

english: Flower drop happens when pepper plants experience stress, such as sudden hot spells, irregular watering, or lack of pollination by bees. Keeping soil moisture consistent and protecting plants from extreme heat helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ na haomɔ, tamɔ ahum ni mli edɔ trukaa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa Aloo ŋmeii efeee pollination. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I avoid spraying pesticides on my cowpea farm during the middle of the day when flowers are open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi ni fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Friendly insects like bees visit cowpea flowers during the warm afternoon to pollinate them, which is necessary for pods to form. Spraying chemicals during peak daytime hours kills these helpful insects, reducing overall crop yield.
ga: Kplukai ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ ŋmeii yaa cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛyawo ŋmeii. ni he hiaa kɛha pods feemɔ Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mɛi fa babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baagbe nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ ba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly and becoming hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that transmit viruses and drain plant sap. Controlling these pests early using neem oil or insecticidal soap prevents the leaf damage from spreading to new branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Amɛji mɛi ni hiɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni amɛnuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi baa ni efite lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa niji heei amli.

english: How do I choose which small shoots to remove from my plantain mat so the main plant produces big bunches?
ga: Miiya ni mayajie ŋmeii bibii komɛi. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ plantain mat lɛ nɔ koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ awo niji wuji?

english: Plantain mats produce shoots called suckers; 'maiden suckers' with broad leaves and thick bases should be kept, while thin 'water suckers' should be pruned away. Leaving only one strong shoot alongside the mother plant prevents competition for light and soil food.
ga: Plantain tsei woɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii. Esa akɛ akɛ ‘tsobii bibii’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse lɛ ato, yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ afo ‘tsobii bibii’ lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ ŋmei kome pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ akaŋshii ni kɔɔ la kɛ shikpɔŋ he lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plant turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which acts as food for crop growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the plant the energy it needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ daraa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they suffer heat stress or do not get consistent water. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can grow into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo amɛnáaa nu daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni eda ni etsɔ tomato.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when there is heavy rainfall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When too much rain sits on the farm, the roots suffocate in waterlogged soil, making them rot quickly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. ni haa egboɔ oya

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rainy season starts in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until after two or three strong rains have soaked deep into the ground. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to burn in the dry, hot soil underneath.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade cover. It stops sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps the ground cool, and reduces how often you need to water.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or mites feeding on the plant's juices, or a virus spread by insects. Clearing weeds and spraying insecticidal soap can protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni kooloi shwieɔ shi lɛ Jwɛi ni agbeɔ kɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young pods shrivel due to a fungal disease called black pod, which spreads easily in wet, dark shade, or because the tree drops extra pods it cannot support. Pruning extra shade tree branches helps air dry out the farm.
ga: Pods bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ hewɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ko ni efɔ, ni eyɛ duŋ. aloo akɛni tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ hewɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea crop leaves look like someone sprinkled white chalk powder on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ efɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: That white powder is a disease called powdery mildew, which grows when plants are crowded too close together in humid weather. Spacing your plants further apart allows fresh air to stop the disease.
ga: Nakai ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ lɛ ji hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Edaa kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo tsɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Shi gbɛ babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa akpa helai.

english: Yam tubers twist when they hit hard soil, clay, or rocks under the ground. Building soft, deep mounds free of stones gives the tuber room to expand straight downwards.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tsɔɔ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa, shikpɔŋ shikpɔŋ, loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni tɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tuber tsu lɛ mli ashɛ shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on maize to multiply in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts restores soil fertility.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ayiɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight because it burns their leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains gives them living cover and keeps the soil cool so they can survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ ebaashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa loo adu tsei bibii lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ naa he ko ni amɛhiɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is missing nitrogen, which is the food crop plants need to build strong leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plants turn dark green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛdara oya.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves and eating the plant from the inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni oye tso lɛ kɛjɛ emli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest whose caterpillars feed on the tender leaf whorls of maize. Checking your field early and spraying approved pesticides or natural neem mixtures can stop them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni eshishifãi yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli neem ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Growing maize repeatedly in the same spot uses up the same soil nutrients every season and lets pests build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores fertility to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ baatsu nii daa be. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ mafo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy rain because the soil cannot drain properly. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges keeps water flowing away from the roots and stops rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa Enɛ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa fitemɔ kpaa.

english: Why do I need to clear heavy weeds and put tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi babaoo nɛkɛ? ni okɛ tso kakadaŋŋ Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants need their leaves high up in the sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking the vines off the ground keeps them healthy and exposes leaves to full light.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia baai ni yɔɔ hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni wain tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ náa la babaoo.

english: Why does the surface of my farm ground become hard like rock just a few days after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wa tamɔ tɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ lɛ?

english: When bare soil is directly exposed to hot sun, water evaporates quickly and leaves the dirt hard and crusty. Covering the bare ground with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, keeps the soil moist and soft.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ shɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa muji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Atsɛɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛhaa hei ni nɔ bɛ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bɔdɔɔ.

english: Fertilizers need water to melt so roots can swallow them, and concentrated fertilizer on dry roots can scorch and burn the plant. Always apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after rain.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ami lɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi ni egbi lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ni ashã amɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor nutrients in the soil. Regular watering during dry weather and keeping soil fertile helps flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark brown spots and turn dry during rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy and damp conditions encourage fungal diseases that attack tomato leaves and cause spots. Spacing your plants wider apart allows wind to dry the leaves quickly, reducing fungal growth.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa tomato baai lɛ baa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops like maize remove a lot of nutrients from the ground. Beans and groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil naturally, which refreshes the earth for your next crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beans kɛ peanuts kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ehee kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. The plant moves the small amount of remaining nitrogen to its young top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves and tall stems instead of storing energy underground in the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ oyitsoŋ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow better in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from direct sunlight. This keeps the ground cool and retains soil moisture longer so plants do not dry out.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ egbiɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the leaf juices and spreading plant viruses. Removing weeds and protecting plants early stops these bugs from spreading disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ baa nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ mra kɛ tsei ahebuu Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akagbɛ helai amɛshwã.

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Because crops have to share these resources, they cannot grow to their full potential or produce as much harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Enɛ ji akɛ, esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aja nibii amli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he loo amɛwo yibii babaoo bɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat or long dry spells. The plant drops flowers to save its strength until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli kɛyashi shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know my yam tubers are mature and ready for harvest without digging up the whole mound?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up. This sign shows that the plant has finished growing and stored all its energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe edalɛ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo tso lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow fast. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How do I know if weeds are stealing nutrients from my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji jwɛi miiju niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: If your crops are growing slowly, look thin, or have pale green leaves despite getting rain, weeds surrounding them are likely taking the water and plant food first.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo, loo eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ po. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛye nu ni amɛdu niyenii klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop if the tree lacks water during hot dry spells, or if tiny pollinating insects are absent, or if sucking pests are attacking the flower stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ, loo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop young fruit when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden pest attacks as a survival instinct to protect the rest of the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Eji wala yibiiwoo su ko ni haa mɔ buɔ tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: How can I tell the difference between insect damage and disease on my crop leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: Insects usually leave holes, chewed edges, or visible bugs on the leaves, while leaf diseases cause brown or yellow spots, powdery dust, or wilting without any physical bite marks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ bu, ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ, loo kooloi bibii ni anaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni foliar helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ, sũ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the fruit bunches start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over because microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borers eat away the underground roots, weakening the plant's anchor in the soil under heavy weight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ muji ni tsii shishi.

english: How can I check if my crop farm has enough soil moisture without buying tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli sũ lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni miheee nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Dig down a few inches and squeeze a handful of soil: if it holds together in a ball without dripping water, it is ideal; if it crumbles quickly, your crops need watering.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shi inchii fioo komɛi ni okɛmimɔ shikpɔŋ ni fa fioo. Kɛji akɛ ebɔle ehe ni nu shwieee shi lɛ Abuɔ lɛ akɛ esa. Kɛji efo oya lɛ Ehe miihia ni afɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii hu anɔ nu.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops wilt in the afternoon even when the soil feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it up. If they recover by early morning, it is normal heat stress, but if they stay wilted, root disease may be blocking water flow.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛji ohe wa bo leebi lɛ, enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. Shi kɛji egbo lolo lɛ, shishifã hela hu baanyɛ atsĩ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are rotting underground before I dig them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mafo amɛ?

english: Check the stem and leaves above ground: if leaves suddenly turn yellow and drop off or the base of the stem feels soft and smells bad, the tubers below are likely rotting from excess water.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei kɛ baai: Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa ni amɛgbee shi. Aloo tso lɛ shishi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eŋɔɔɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to feed the growing tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread and exposes them to maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. Gbalamɔ ni oná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni obaanyɛ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are completely ripe and ready for harvesting without damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa ni efiteee lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods change skin color when mature, shifting from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange. Looking closely at skin color changes rather than pressing the pod helps you pick them at peak ripeness for optimal bean fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhewolo nɔ su be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛya ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo kɛjɛ etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛya ŋmɔŋ Kɛ́ okwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni hewolo nɔ su tsakeɔ moŋ fe ni ooonyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohala dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: How can I check if my pawpaw fruit is ready to harvest without squeezing and bruising the flesh?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji mipapaya aduawai lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛmiimɔɔɔ mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eko eko eko eko eko?

english: Check the skin color near the base of the fruit instead of pressing it. Pawpaws are ready to harvest when yellow streaks begin to appear on the skin, allowing the fruit to ripen fully without causing internal damage.
ga: Kwɛmɔ hewolo nɔ su ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ shishi lɛ moŋ fe ni ooomimɔ nɔ. Paws lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ je shishi amɛje kpo yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ mligbɛ nɔ ko baaa.

english: Why do my harvested mangoes develop dark soft spots and spoil so quickly after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni mikpa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rough handling during harvesting causes internal bruising that damages the flesh before it shows on the skin. Cutting fruits gently with shears instead of pulling or dropping them prevents rot from setting in.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ekɛ mligbɛ fãji ni fiteɔ loo lɛ baa dani ejeɔ kpo yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ. Okɛ sɛkɛs afo aduawai lɛ blɛoo moŋ fe ni ooogbala loo oooŋmɛɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekafite.

english: How should I handle my harvested yam tubers during harvest so they do not rot quickly in storage?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsu mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ahe nii yɛ kpamɔ be mli? Bɔni afee ni ekafite oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ.

english: Yam skins are delicate and easily wounded during digging. Handling tubers gently and avoiding scrapes on the skin keeps rot-causing fungi from entering the crop while stored in the yam barn.
ga: Sweet potato hewolo lɛ waaa ni efiteɔ oya kɛji akumɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsu nii blɛoo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ hewolo lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ akabote ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli be mli ni akɛtoɔ sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does raw cassava sometimes taste bitter, and is it safe to process directly from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmei ni ahoo lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ? Ni ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaatsu nii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Cassava plants produce natural chemical defenses in their root flesh to protect themselves against pests and wild animals. Bitter varieties contain higher levels of these protective compounds and must be fermented or thoroughly cooked before eating.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui kɛ koo mli kooloi ahe. Nɛkɛ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he nɛɛ fa babaoo yɛ tsofai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni esa akɛ awo mli loo ahoo dani aye

english: Why does the sap from raw cashew nuts burn my skin when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni jɛɔ cashew ŋmeii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ shãa mihewolo lɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cashew nut shells contain a natural defensive liquid that protects the seed inside from insects and animals. Wearing thick gloves when handling fresh raw nuts prevents this caustic liquid from irritating your skin.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nu ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni buɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi ahe lɛ yɛ cashew nut ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ owo glɔvs ni mli tse beni okɛ ŋmeii heei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ nu ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ akawo hewolo lɛ mli la.

english: Why do my cocoa beans lose so much weight after I dry them on the raised mats?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwie shi babaoo beni migbi amɛ yɛ tsɔne ko ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa beans contain high amounts of moisture inside the wet pulp and seed. Drying removes excess water weight until the beans reach a safe moisture level, preventing mold growth during storage.
ga: Cocoa yibii heei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli ni dumɔwui lɛ hu mli edɔ. Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why does my harvested maize weigh less per bag compared to my neighbor's harvest from a similar size field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ tsiimɔ baa shi yɛ kotoku kome mli kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa ni jɛ ŋmɔ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Grain weight depends heavily on plant nutrition during the grain-filling stage. Adequate fertilizer application during flowering creates denser, heavier seeds that yield more weight kilo by kilo at harvest.
ga: Nibii ni tsiimɔ damɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ nɔ waa yɛ be mli ni akɛ ŋmaa lɛ woɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kilogram kome mli tsiimɔ yaa hiɛ kɛ́ akpa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the stem side right before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ tso lɛ fã lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Sudden heavy rain or overwatering causes tomato plants to absorb water too quickly, expanding the internal flesh faster than the outer skin can grow and causing the skin to burst.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa loo nu ni hoɔ babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ fãji lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ada. ni eha hewolo lɛ akumɔ

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi waa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural self-defense response plants use to reduce leaf surface area, conserving internal moisture and preventing excessive water loss during heat stress.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu hetoo ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba baa lɛ hiɛ he lɛ shi. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo ahi mli ni otsi nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides natural shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii ewo mli lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my sugarcane is mature and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sugarcane lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Sugarcane is usually mature when the lower leaves dry up and turn brown, and the stalk sounds solid when tapped. Tasting the juice from the middle of the stalk to see if it is very sweet also confirms it is ready.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni tso lɛ yɛ gbɛɛmɔ ni wa kɛji akɛ atswa Kɛ́ oka nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ okwɛ kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ, emaa nɔ mi akɛ efee klalo.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with lots of leaves but leaves me with very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of roots below. Using fertilizers rich in potassium helps the plant focus energy on swelling its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ anɔ.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season, will it affect my crop yield?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Ani ebaana mi ŋmãa nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil nitrogen and reduces pest problems.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai baa shi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stalks and tiny ears of corn. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to produce large, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants droop in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up from the soil. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the roots cool and holds moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) shwie otsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients in the soil. They also act as hiding places for harmful insects that can spread diseases to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ he ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baanyɛ agbɛ hela amɛshwã onibii amli lɛ ahiɛ amɛhe yɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my maize plants to curl up and develop holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni bulɛ yɔɔ mli?

english: Holes and curling in maize leaves are usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm feeding on the fresh growing leaves. Catching the infestation early and applying approved controls stops the worms before they destroy the crop heart.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Ni aaamɔ helai ni baa lɛ mra Ni akɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsui.

english: Can I harvest my sugarcane stem and let it grow back from the roots without planting new seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa sugar cane tsei lɛ ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni miduuu dumɔwui heei?

english: Yes, sugarcane has the ability to regrow from the leftover stalk stump after being cut, which is called a ratoon crop. Proper weeding and fertilizing after cutting helps the new shoots grow strong for a second harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛjɛ ŋmei ni eshwɛ lɛ mli beni afo lɛ sɛɛ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be mli ni afo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni amɛdaraa waa kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni ji enyɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting due to extreme heat, lack of consistent watering, or insect attacks on the blossoms. Ensuring steady soil moisture and protecting the plants from pests helps the flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa Aloo kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap, or by a virus spread by these insects. Spraying neem oil solution or appropriate organic controls helps get rid of these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛya.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli ewo muji kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ? Yɛ teŋgbɛ kɔni lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central growing leaf funnel to eat young tissues. Checking fields early and applying neem-based repellents or recommended biopesticides protects the crop before damage spreads.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni miida lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ neem mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do tiny insects attack my cowpea pods as soon as they start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔtɔi lɛ kɛji amɛje shishi amɛfee pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers and young pods produce a sweet scent that attracts pod-boring insects. Farmers control them by planting at the start of the rains or applying targeted bio-insecticides during the early flowering stage.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ jieɔ muji ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa kooloi ni ŋmɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Okwaafoi kudɔɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔ ni amɛduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli loo kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or the ground is flooded with excess water, which smothers the roots. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot, when soil moisture changes abruptly, or when the soil lacks key nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent morning watering and proper soil feeding help flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa Aloo beni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa leebi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in soil that traps water without good drainage, allowing waterborne fungi to attack the roots during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
