ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and dry right on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod Disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning shade branches to let air and sunlight through, along with removing infected pods, prevents the spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ hu. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ naa

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade, protecting young cocoa from sunburn and keeping the soil cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Yam vines need maximum exposure to sunlight to create food for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps vines off the wet ground, preventing leaf rot and increasing yield.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa wain tsei ahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my watermelon vines look fresh in the morning but wilt completely in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ feɔ ehee leebi lɛ? Shi ani fɛɛ egbo yɛ shwane ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Watermelon leaves lose water fast through evaporation during midday heat, faster than dry roots can pull water from the soil. Deep watering early in the morning and putting dried grass mulch around plants keeps root zones moist.
ga: Watermelon baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ nɔ, ni enɛ mli edɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ leebi ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi abɔle he. tsei koni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the plant stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee tsei ahe tsei amli lɛ anɔ

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. The caterpillars feed on the young leaves and central shoot of maize, which reduces the plant's ability to grow and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ekɛfee toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi diji ni egboi yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering. When soil moisture fluctuates drastically, the plant cannot absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight and heat without protection. Sunburn and heat stress cause the leaves to turn yellow and dry out, which is why young cocoa needs shade from larger trees like plantains.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛji akɛ abuuu amɛhe. Hulu ni tsoɔ kɛ dɔlɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni kookoo bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds and rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches. If root-eating pests like nematodes damage the roots, or if the stem is unsupported, the heavy weight of the plant causes it to uproot in strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ shishifãi tamɔ nematodes lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ loo kɛji akɛ atswaaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ baaha eshishifãi lɛ ajie ehe yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Yam plants produce larger tubers when their leaves get full sunlight. Staking lifts the vines, allowing leaves to catch maximum sunlight while keeping them away from damp soil diseases on the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛji amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa helai aba shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of maize each year even though I clear and plant the exact same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa kotokui fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie ni midu lɛ nakai nɔŋŋ moŋ.

english: Continuous planting of the same crop without adding manure, fertilizer, or rotating with legumes depletes the natural soil nutrients, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli ni aya nɔ aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli, akɛwooo mli ŋmɔshi nibii, loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ haaa sũ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do weeds actually harm my cassava crop if there is enough space on the land?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight that your cassava needs to build thick tubers. They also harbor insect pests that can spread diseases to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa oya ni o-cassava lɛ feɔ yitsei ni mli tse. Amɛhiɛɔ kooloi ni baanyɛ agbala helai kɛya onibii amli lɛ hu.

english: Why should I avoid planting my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui adumɔ he yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often a 'false start' followed by a hot dry period. If seeds germinate during this dry gap, the young shoots will wither and die from lack of moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ ji ‘Apasa shishijee’ lɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, be ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli egbi lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ baagboi yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the plant reaches 8 to 12 months, lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the stem base begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni tso lɛ eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning rather than in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ aduawai anɔ nu leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering in the early morning gives plant roots time to absorb water before the hot sun causes fast evaporation. Afternoon watering can scorch leaves and encourage wet-soil fungal diseases overnight.
ga: Nu ni afɔseɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ oya. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural way to save water and stay alive until the rains return to spur new leaf growth.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he ni ahiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ koni ewo baai heei hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does my maize crop grow tall tassels at the top and silk on the cobs, and what do they do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛ siliki yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni amɛtsuɔ?

english: The tassel at the top releases pollen that blows onto the sticky silks below, fertilizing the plant so individual maize grains can grow on the cob.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jieɔ pollen ni akɛwoɔ siliki ni shwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni fata he ji tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko anyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full, direct sunlight; they need shade from larger trees like plantains or timber trees to protect their soft leaves and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo tsei ahe. Koni ebu baai bibii ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the bottom tips of my green tomatoes turn black and rotten before they even get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ŋmɔji lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛba po lɛ?

english: This black spot is blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium or irregular watering prevents the fruit from developing properly.
ga: Nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haaa aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my other crops make the soil richer for next season?
ga: Amɛduɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots, naturally adding essential nutrients to the soil that help future crops grow strong.
ga: Peanut tsei gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my plantain tree sprout so many small shoots around its base, and should I leave them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miikwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ mashi amɛ fɛɛ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: The small shoots are suckers trying to grow into new trees, but if you keep too many, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem, making your fruit bunches smaller.
ga: Tsobii bibii lɛ ji tsei ni miitao amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei heei. Shi kɛji okɛto babaoo lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha o-fruit bunch lɛ afee bibioo.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting green shoots in the barn even when there is no rain or dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers ni akpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ loo muji bɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living seed stems with a natural timer; once their dormant period ends, they automatically use stored food inside the root to try to grow new vines.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji dumɔwui ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli be. Kɛji hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Amɛkɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛkɛka wain tsei heei akwɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off to the ground during very hot afternoon weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants drop their blossoms to conserve water and protect themselves from extreme heat stress.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ he.

english: Why do my rice plants fall over flat on the ground right when the grains start to get heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over (lodge) when heavy rain or wind hits stems that are too weak, often caused by using too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes plants tall and soft.
ga: Omɔ tsei gbeeɔ shi (jɔɔ amɛhe) kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ tswa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii, ni haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my garden eggs much faster when I plant them in the exact same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ oya waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ saatso kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting garden eggs in the same spot continuously allows pests and diseases to multiply in the soil over time, so they are ready to attack your new crop immediately.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kɛ helai aba. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaatutua oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under strong, direct sunlight because their foliage is very delicate. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees around them acts like an umbrella, keeping the soil cool and humid so the cocoa leaves do not burn.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ejaakɛ ebaai lɛ waaa waa Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ umbrella Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo baai lɛ akashã.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the middle of the leaf usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or NPK early in the season keeps the leaves green so the plant can grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛfataa he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding in the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds inside the growing point of young maize plants. Spraying the crop early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active helps protect the leaves and save your yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close together, will I get more cassava at harvest?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa Ani maná ŋmei babaoo?

english: Planting too close actually reduces your harvest because the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each cassava stem enough space allows the roots room to expand into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha cassava tso fɛɛ tso he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifã tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I weigh and separate my dried produce into standard bag sizes before selling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu aduawai kɛ aduawai ni egbi lɛ ahe ni majara mli awo baagi dalɛi ni sa mli dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Standardizing your bag weights ensures you receive fair payment based on exact weight and prevents disputes with buying agents. Evenly dividing produce across bags stops bags from ripping and keeps crops from spoiling due to over-compression.
ga: Baagi mli tsiimɔi ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa onine shɛɔ nyɔmɔwoo ni sa nɔ ni damɔ tsiimɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ. ni otsi béi ni baa kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa Kɛ́ aja kotoku lɛ mli nibii lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kotoku lɛ akagbala, ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce lots of lush green leaves but no flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo ŋmeii bɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants grow heavy leaves while forgetting to flower. Balancing your soil with nutrients like phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to stop growing leaves and start forming flowers and peppers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha pepper tsei lɛ afee baai babaoo ni amɛhiɛ akpa fɔfɔii anɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ Ebaaha tso lɛ akpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii feemɔ.

english: Yams need loose, soft earth to push downwards easily. If the soil is hard or rocky, the roots get crushed and turn crooked, so building high, loose soil mounds gives the tubers room to grow straight and large.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni enyɛ eshɛ shishi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ tɛi Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or pest attacks. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather and protecting the plants from insects helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy inside the sacks even after a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Maize gets moldy inside storage sacks when it is bagged before it is completely dry. Moisture trapped inside the sack creates mold and attracts insects, so drying your maize thoroughly on tarpaulins until the grains are hard and dry is necessary before bagging.
ga: Abele baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kotokui lɛ amli kɛ́ awo amɛ kotoku mli dani amɛgbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni agbi ŋmãa lɛ kwraa yɛ tarpaulin nɔ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee shiŋŋ ni egbi dani akɛwo kotoku mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ da lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and weak stems that struggle to hold heavy fruit bunches against strong winds. Supporting the main stem with sturdy wooden or bamboo poles helps bear the weight until the plantains are fully mature.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛwo aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛfi tso lɛ tsiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi dumɔwu lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some farmers harvesting their maize in just three months while mine takes much longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kpataa amɛ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ heɔ be babaoo fe nakai lɛ?

english: Some farmers use early-maturing or improved seed varieties. These seeds are specifically bred to grow faster and produce mature grains in a shorter time, helping farmers harvest early to beat dry spells or food shortages.
ga: Okwaafoi komɛi kɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra loo ni asaa amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui nɛɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni eda yɛ be kukuoo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkpaa nii mra. Koni aye hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni faaa lɛ nɔ kunim

english: What is an improved seed, and why shouldn't I just use the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii?

english: Improved seeds are high-quality seeds developed by scientists to fight off local diseases, withstand dry weather, and produce much bigger harvests. Seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over time and give lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jeŋ nilelɔi fee koni amɛkɛwu amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli ni ebaawo yibii ni baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for soil nutrients like nitrogen. Rainfall gives water, but crops also need plant food like fertilizer or compost to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otsei lɛ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Nugbɔ kɛ nu baa. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu he miihia tsei niyenii, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii. Koni ehi shi akɛ eŋɔli ni eda waa

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly and produce smaller fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛwo yibii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce large yields.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni he wa waa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five seeds in one hole to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: When too many seeds are planted in one hole, the plants fight each other for soil food and water. Spacing them out correctly gives each plant enough space and food to produce bigger, healthier crops.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant the same crop on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating different crops keeps the soil rich and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: You can use simple irrigation methods, like drip pipes or small water pumps, to deliver water directly to crop roots. This lets you grow and harvest crops year-round regardless of the weather.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu shwiemɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ drip hose loo nu pɔmp bibioo atsu nii. Koni okɛ nu aya tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ, ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ ha lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off without forming pods during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat puts severe stress on cocoa trees, causing them to drop flowers to save water. Planting shade trees among your cocoa keeps the soil cool and protects the flowers so they can turn into pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ cacao tsei lɛ ashi amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly eat up my entire maize field in just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ye mi-ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ trukaa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm multiply very quickly and target soft young leaves. Checking your farm regularly lets you catch them early so you can spray approved control products before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ faa oya ni amɛtutuaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ mra. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and turning twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with protective nets or insect sprays prevents the virus from damaging your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Ehe hia ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra. Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akafite onibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient that helps crops build healthy green leaves. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient away from the root zone, making the plant look pale and struggle to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa akɛ eeekwɛ̃.

english: What will happen to my crop if I apply too much chemical fertilizer all at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo tsu nii yɛ be kome mli?

english: Applying too much fertilizer creates high salt levels in the soil that suck moisture out of the plant's roots. This leads to 'fertilizer burn,' where the leaf edges turn brown and dry up, which can stunt growth or even kill the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi amli Enɛ kɛ ‘ŋmei shãa’ baa he ni baai lɛ ashishigbɛi feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tso lɛ dalɛ naa loo egbe lɛ po.

english: Why do fall armyworms always hide inside the center funnel of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-corn tsei lɛ ateŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms nest inside the central leaf funnel because it protects them from birds, hot sunlight, and direct chemical sprays, while giving them access to the softest and most nutritious young leaves to feed on.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ feɔ amɛtsu yɛ baai lɛ ateŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli ejaakɛ ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ okpoi ahe. hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛye.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and drying out during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl during dry periods to conserve water by reducing exposure to the hot sun. However, severe curling is often made worse by pests like mealybugs that suck the sap out of the stems and leaves.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ ni ebaa shi lɛ nɔ. Shi, bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa nɛɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii fe tsutsu lɛ ji kooloi tamɔ mealybugs ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Extreme heat stresses the tomato plant and destroys the pollen inside the blossoms. When pollen becomes sterile, the flowers cannot produce fruit, so the plant drops them to conserve its remaining water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ pollen lɛ bafee nɔ ni fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ pollen koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why does my corn stay very short and produce tassels early when there is a long break in the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ hiɔ shi kuku ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: When corn faces severe drought early in its life, it goes into survival mode and rushes its life cycle to produce seeds quickly before dying, resulting in short stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa na hɔmɔ ni naa wa yɛ eshihilɛ shishijee mli lɛ, Eyaa wala shihilɛ mli ni ehaa ewala shihilɛ yaa oya koni ekɛ dumɔwui awo oya dani egbo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kukuji kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short and bent instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle shi moŋ ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend when the soil underneath is too hard or stony. The growing tip of the tuber cannot push through hard soil layers, so it turns sideways to find softer paths to expand.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ baabɔle amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi tsɔ. Tuber lɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ etsɔ ehe kɛtee afã koni ena gbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni etsɔɔ nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Weeds act like aggressive competitors; their fast-growing roots steal water and fertilizer nutrients from the soil, while their leaves block sunlight from reaching your crops.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa. Shishifãi ni shwereɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout even after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep in the soil where they run out of air, or if the soil stays too waterlogged and causes the seed to rot before it can push through the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ fite dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my paddy rice is fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn from green to a hard, golden-yellow color, and the lower leaves of the plant begin to dry out naturally.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni ŋmaa yitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ ni wa mli lɛ. Ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or has too much stagnant water around its roots. Nitrogen acts as food for green growth, so adding well-rotted manure or NPK fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eyɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from the underside of the leaf, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying neem oil or recommended organic insecticides helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do the stems of my vegetable plants rot at the ground level during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains leave the soil waterlogged, which suffocates the roots and creates a friendly environment for fungal diseases to attack the base of the stem. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or shade trees alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kokoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily burn under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big umbrella-like leaves that shade the young cocoa and keep the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ he feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create food for growing large tubers. Staking keeps the leaves high off the hot soil, reducing disease exposure and allowing the leaves to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo

english: If too many suckers grow around one mother plantain, they fight for water and soil nutrients, resulting in small bunches. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures heavy, high-quality plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, dumɔwu kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui bibii. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni etsii.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the plant rots after harvest, that nitrogen stays behind to nourish your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Beni tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ Nitrogen baakã he ahi shi koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer to my crop when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wooo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so that plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil can burn the roots or sit unused on top until rain washes it away.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuuu nii kɛyashi nugbɔ baafɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are fully grown and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the root base begins to crack open due to the swelling tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbalaa yɛ ŋmeii ni efuu yɛ shishi lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, soil moisture fluctuates sharply, or pollination fails. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps cool the roots and protects the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ oya. loo pollination failure Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ shwie shi pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Which way up am I supposed to plant cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ madu ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You should always plant cassava stems with the small buds or nodes pointing upwards towards the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots will struggle to grow upwards and the tuber roots will not develop properly.
ga: Esa akɛ odu cassava tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nodes. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaawa akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni tuber lɛ shishifãi lɛ hu eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers build high soil mounds before planting yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi maa gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ dani amɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil so their large tubers can easily expand downward without fighting hard ground. High mounds also keep heavy rains from gathering around the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ. No hewɔ lɛ yitso agbo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akawu. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea will turn them green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the land, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull food from the air and put nitrogen back into the soil. This restores your land naturally for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the ground too quickly. It holds moisture near the roots, keeps weeds from growing, and cools down the soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, interplanting them works well because maize grows tall fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly underground over a longer period. They share the space without competing heavily.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Amɛjaraa he ko ni akaŋshii ni mli wa bɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant does not get steady water. Irregular watering causes stress that makes the plant dump its blossoms instead of growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu daa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tso lɛ fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi yɛ yibii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ najiaŋ baa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the middle leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on tender young corn shoots. Clearing weeds around your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or treatments early will stop them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ mra ni awo ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛtsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to remove weeds while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds. Weeds steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients your crops need, so clearing them early lets your crop seedlings grow strong fast.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ. Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaaha otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ adara oya.

english: Why is it important to measure spacing when I plant my crops instead of just scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ he beni miduɔ nii moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui ashwã kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil. When crops are planted too close together, they compete for food and produce very small yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii he akaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin without producing big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo waa ni ŋmãa toi wuji ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops grow tall and weak when they are crowded together because they are fighting to reach sunlight. Spacing them correctly leaves enough room for the plant to use its energy to grow heavy ears instead of tall stems.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daraa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ abua naa ejaakɛ esa akɛ amɛwu amɛha hulu la. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei ahe lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ toi ni tsii ni amɛdaraa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kɛlɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning yellow even though it is raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crops lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is holding too much water around the roots, preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting after the rains begin in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije dumɔ shishi beni nugbɔ lɛ je shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting should begin after the soil receives consistent, deep rainfall. Planting too early after a light shower can burn seeds in hot, dry soil before they fully germinate.
ga: Esa akɛ aje dumɔ shishi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni mli kwɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do some of my crops dry up and die suddenly before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ ekomɛi gbiɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Sudden drying is usually caused by pests attacking the plant stems underground or fungal root diseases. Proper field sanitation and crop rotation help prevent these problems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ashishifãi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa trukaa. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ hetsemɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagbai nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my planted crops, and how do they hurt my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ? Ni te eyeɔ minitsumɔ lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds are natural wild plants that quickly steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer away from your crops. If you do not clear weeds early, your crops will stay small and yield very little.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli oya. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee bibioo ni ebaawo yibii fioo.

english: Is it better to plant only one crop on my land or mix different crops together?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutu mli?

english: Mixing complementary crops, such as planting legumes alongside grains, helps keep the soil healthy and protects your income if one crop suffers from bad weather or disease.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he ni akɛfutuɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ebuɔ oshika he kɛji ŋmãa kome gbo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo hela mli.

english: How does applying fertilizer at specific times actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for your plants at key growth stages—such as root setup and flowering. Giving nutrients at the right time ensures plants build strong stems and produce plenty of fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa otsei lɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ bei titrii tamɔ shishifãi kɛ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtswaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How can I make sure I get a good financial profit from the money I invested in land prep and seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ minine shɛɔ shika gbɛfaŋ sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa nɔ kɛjɛɔ shika ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: Profit comes from reducing seed loss and maximizing harvest weight. Following recommended planting methods, controlling pests early, and caring for crops properly protects your investment and doubles your market yield.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi jɛɔ dumɔwui ni laajeɔ lɛ ni abaaba shi kɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ asɛɛdii Early Pest Control Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ ni sa buɔ oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ he ni ehaa ojarayeli mli yibiiwoo lɛ feɔ shii enyɔ.

english: What is the best way to handle my harvested crops so they do not rot before I reach the market?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsu mikpamɔ lɛ he nii koni ekafite dani eshɛ jara nɔ?

english: Harvested crops must be thoroughly dried and stored in clean, well-ventilated, dry bags. Keeping crops dry prevents mold and insects from destroying their market value.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi tsei ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ amli. Nibii ni adu lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi akafite jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which acts like food to keep them green and strong. This happens when the soil loses nutrients from continuous farming or heavy rain washing the good soil away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli baa lɛ fiteɔ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ laajeɔ.

english: Why is my cassava growing tall with lots of green leaves but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground instead of storing food in its root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ niji kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves. They suck the plant's sap and spread plant sicknesses, which distorts new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa. ni fiteɔ baai heei adalɛ

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium while the fruit is growing. It is often caused by irregular watering or dry spells followed by sudden heavy rain.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo hɔmɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea flowers immediately after they open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpea blossoms produce sweet nectar and tender petals that naturally attract pests like flower thrips. These insects target fresh blossoms to feed, which can prevent the crop from forming pods if not managed early.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ nu kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fɔfɔii a-thrips lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kwɛɔ fɔfɔi heei anɔ koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmeii kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ nɔ mra.

english: Why do the young flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed excess flowers naturally when they experience water stress, lack of shade, or poor soil fertility, as the tree tries to conserve energy to survive the weather conditions.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛkɛ nu he haomɔ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ kpe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli.

english: Why do my crops start wilting in the afternoon hot sun even when it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, crop leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Sandy soils also dry out quickly near the surface where young roots feed.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tse lɛ baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he ni shishifãi bibii yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during windy weather before the bunches mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani panicles lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface and can be weakened by root-eating pests like nematodes or banana weevils. Without deep, healthy roots or soil mounded around the base, the heavy weight of the plant causes it to fall.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ shishifãi tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛji shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa loo sũ ni bɔle shishitoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ haa egbeeɔ shi.

english: Why does my maize grow thin and weak when I plant it too close to my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ mli tsɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ waa kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight like children sharing a small bowl of food. The fast-growing cassava shades the maize from sunlight while its roots take water and plant food away from the maize.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baawuu tamɔ gbekɛbii. Jaa niyenii ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli Kasava ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ haa hulu lɛ shɛɛɛ he. yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots inside the barn before the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living seeds that naturally wake up from their resting state after a few months, especially when stored in warm or humid conditions where air flow is poor.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji dumɔwui ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sun. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make food and stay green. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the root area.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Extreme afternoon heat or a sudden lack of water stresses the plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to save energy. It can also mean there are not enough insects or wind moving to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ̃ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into thin tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural shield against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots very small even though the leaves on top look big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard and compact, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves on top instead of pushing roots outward to store energy underneath.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo ewa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ baai ni tsii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsi shishifãi lɛ kɛya kponɔgbɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shishi.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall and thin when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete fiercely for sunlight. Each plant stretches upward as fast as possible to reach light, resulting in tall, weak stems that break easily in strong wind.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la lɛ he akaŋ waa. Tso fɛɛ tso shwieɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni eshɛ la lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fãa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why does putting dry grass on top of the soil around my vegetables help them stay healthy in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-vegetables lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the direct heat of the sun. It keeps the ground cool and traps moisture in the dirt so plant roots can keep drinking during dry spells.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my yam tubers are mature and ready to harvest without digging them out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mifooo amɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You can judge maturity by watching the leaves and vine above ground. When the leaves turn yellow and the main vine dries up completely, the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber below.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo ehewalɛ kɛtsɔ baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. Beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tso titri lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ hewalɛ eto shishigbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli momo.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster on my cleared land than the crop seeds I deliberately planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ oshara mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted over centuries to quickly capture water and nutrients in local soils, making them grow faster than farm crops that require specific care.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛnyɛ amɛhiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden eggs curling up and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled or wrinkled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids hiding on the undersides of leaves, sucking out plant sap and causing the leaf tissue to distort as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. shwieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni ehaa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni edaa lɛ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient in the soil, or that too much standing water around the roots is preventing the plant from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu yɛ lolo ni ebɔle he Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ena niyenii.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, which acts as natural food to help heavy-feeding crops like maize grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yeɔ loo waa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves curl up and dry out when the Harmattan winds start blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bɔi tswaa lɛ?

english: During dry and windy conditions, cocoa leaves curl up to reduce water loss from their surfaces, saving as much internal moisture as possible to survive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli lɛ, abɔleɔ Cocoa baai lɛ koni nu ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be babaoo hiɔ mli bɔ ni aaanyɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing and look weak during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall fills all the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating pepper roots so they cannot breathe or absorb the nutrients needed to support new growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ehee lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before producing any small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani miwo tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences sudden hot dry spells, irregular watering, or when tiny pests like thrips damage the delicate stem that holds the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips lɛ fite tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ.

english: What causes white powdery spots to spread on the leaves of my garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powder lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: White powdery spots are caused by a fungal infection that thrives in warm, humid air when crops are planted too close together and air cannot flow freely between leaves.
ga: Fungal hela ni yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ mli lɛ kɛ powda yɛŋ baa. Beni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ baai lɛ ateŋ oya

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves start turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack upward due to expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: What makes young plantain shoots grow much faster after I cut down the old main stem?
ga: Mɛni ha dumɔwui lɛ dara oya waa beni mifo tso lɛ yitso momo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cutting the mature main stem stops it from consuming nutrients, redirecting all the food stored in the underground root system directly to the young shoots.
ga: Tso lɛ yitso titri ni eda lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni anáa lɛ kpaa. Ekɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yaa tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds germinate much faster when I soak them in clean water overnight before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya waa kɛ́ mikɛwo nu ni mli tse mli gbɛkɛ kome dani midu lɛ?

english: Soaking softens the hard outer seed coat and allows moisture to enter immediately, which signals the baby plant inside to wake up and start sprouting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛwo nu mli lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ fã ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso bibioo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ le akɛ ete shi ni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why do weed leaves die faster when I apply weedicide in the cool morning rather than at hot noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi baai lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsu nii yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso fe shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: In the morning, plant leaves are fully open and actively taking in moisture, which allows them to absorb the weedicide deeply before the hot sun dries the chemical off.
ga: Leebi lɛ, tso lɛ baai lɛ gbeleɔ kwraa ni amɛmɔɔ nu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsofa lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees to retain moisture and protect them until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli.

english: Why do some of the tiny cocoa pods turn brown and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ etsɔɔ blɔfo ni egbiɔ dani edaa?

english: This is often caused by natural pod thinning, where the tree drops extra pods it cannot support, or by sap-sucking pests like capsids (mirids). Proper pruning and pest control help the tree hold onto healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. He ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni baanyɛ aye abua lɛ. loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids (mirids) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains promote Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning branches to allow sunlight and airflow through the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cocoa trees shed their leaves in dry weather to save water and protect themselves from drying out. Providing adequate shade trees helps reduce water loss and keeps the cocoa trees greener through the dry period.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha lɛ, ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: How do I know when my rubber tree is mature enough to start tapping for latex?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-rɔba tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi rɔba tswaa?

english: A rubber tree is ready for tapping when the trunk reaches a thickness (girth) of about 50 centimeters measured at 1 meter above the ground, which usually takes 5 to 7 years after planting.
ga: Rɔba tsei efee klalo kɛha gbee kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli tsɔ (ebɔle ehe) aaafee sɛntimitai 50, ni asusuɔ yɛ mita 1 nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni bei pii lɛ eji afii 5 kɛyashi 7 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or plantain between my young rubber trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Mi rɔba tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping food crops between young rubber trees is good during the first 2 to 3 years before the tree canopy closes. It provides food and income while keeping weeds down around the young rubber plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ gum tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli dani tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ ŋmɛɔ. Ehaa niyenii kɛ shika kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ejieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ rɔbɔt tsei bibii ahe lɛ.

english: Will cutting into the bark of my rubber tree to collect latex hurt or kill the tree?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt lɛ yibii ni aaafo koni akɛbua latɛs lɛ naa lɛ baaye tso lɛ awui loo ebaagbe lɛ?

english: If done correctly, tapping only removes the thin outer layer of bark to open latex vessels without harming the inner growing layer (cambium). Proper tapping techniques allow the tree to heal its bark while continuing to yield latex for decades.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ Tapping jieɔ kponɔgbɛ fã bibioo lɛ. Ajieɔ koni akɛgbele nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli ni efiteee mligbɛ fã ni daa lɛ (cambium). Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ atswaa tso lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni eyaa nɔ ewoɔ nu afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do rubber trees yield less liquid latex during hot dry afternoons compared to early mornings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ rɔbɔt tsei lɛ jieɔ nu ni mli edɔ fioo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli fe leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Latex flows best when water pressure inside the tree is high, which happens in the cool morning. In hot afternoons, the tree loses water through its leaves, causing internal pressure to drop and reducing latex flow.
ga: Sap hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli wa, ni ebaa yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei baatsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛjie nu. Enɛ haa mligbɛ nɔnyɛɛ lɛ baa shi, ni latɛs ni hoɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: How often should I clear weeds around the base of my young cocoa and rubber trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ mi-kookoo kɛ mi-gum tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ?

english: Weeds should be cleared every 4 to 6 weeks around young trees because weeds steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the crop roots, which slows down the tree's growth.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ daa otsii 4 kɛyashi 6, ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ ada blɛoo.

english: Why do my tree crops grow faster when I leave dead leaves on the ground under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa oya kɛ́ mishi baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ eshishi lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves decay and turn into organic matter, acting as a natural mulch that keeps the soil cool, retains moisture during dry periods, and feeds nutrients back into the soil for the roots.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha shishifãi lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight in their early years. They need shade crops like plantains planted next to them to act as natural umbrellas, protecting the leaves from burning and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the center leaves of my young maize plants suddenly full of tiny holes and green waste?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf funnel. They hide in the center where it is cool during the day to eat the tender growing leaves, which is why treatments must target the central funnel directly.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ teŋgbɛ, he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, koni amɛye baai ni miida ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ helatsamɔ lɛ akwɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow tall with many green leaves but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava plants put all their food energy into growing leaves above ground instead of roots below. Tubers need potassium in the soil to swell and grow large.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Potassium he miihia bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ agbo.

english: Will planting cowpeas between my rows of maize steal nutrients away from my maize plants?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmãa tsei lɛ amli?

english: No, cowpeas actually feed the maize. Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural food source for the neighboring maize.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii yeɔ ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my land give me a smaller yield every time I plant maize on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt and allows pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I stop my fertilizer from washing away when the heavy rains start?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist but not flooded, and lightly buried under a bit of dirt near the plant roots. Covering it prevents heavy rain from sweeping the granules off the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu efooo mli. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop during the hot afternoon even if I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgboi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: In intense midday heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground. The plant droops temporarily to reduce heat exposure and usually recovers by evening once temperature drops.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ajieɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai yɛ be kukuoo mli koni hulutsoo ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds to plant yams instead of planting them directly in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ama gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni akɛdu ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand downwards without obstacle. Mounds also keep water from gathering around the tuber, which prevents the yam seed from rotting in waterlogged soil.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii dumɔwui lɛ akafiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the first rain of the season is strong enough for me to safely plant my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui shweshweeshwe?

english: You should check if the rain has soaked the soil at least finger-deep into the ground. Planting after a light shower leaves seeds trapped in dry subsoil once the sun returns, causing them to dry out and fail to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji nugbɔ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hoo lɛ inchi kome. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi sũ lɛ mli ni egbi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce smaller cobs than the store-bought seeds I used before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ shwapo mli ni mikɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are created by crossing specific parent plants to produce high yields only in the first generation. Seeds harvested from those plants lose those special qualities, resulting in mixed and smaller yields the following season.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei pɔtɛɛ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii srɔtoi ni faaa kɛ yibiiwoo ni faaa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?
