english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Providing shade from taller companion plants like plantains protects the leaves until the tree develops deep roots and stronger leaves.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade ni jɛɔ nanemɛi tsei ni kɛlɛ, tamɔ plantains lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli wa.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the young crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and small yields rather than strong, healthy crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e ngɛ he wami.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil. The plant is pulling nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ miihe niyenii kɛmiijɛ baai bibii lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting groundnuts help improve my soil for future crops?
ga: Te ŋmei dumɔ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that trapped plant food remains in the soil to help crops like maize grow stronger next season.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Tsei niyenii ni amɔmɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛdara waa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds from around my young yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi sweet potato wain tso bibioo lɛ

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food that builds tubers underground. Tall weeds steal sunlight and suck up soil moisture and fertilizer meant for the yam.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ hulu la ni ejieɔ sũ mli nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients. Removing the weak shoots leaves only one strong stem that can produce a heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei krokomɛi kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii bibii lɛ, eshiɔ tso kome pɛ ni wa ni baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before they can grow into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by irregular watering or high heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root zone helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my freshly harvested cassava tubers start rotting just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa ehee lɛ bɔi fitemɔ beni mikɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Cassava roots begin to break down rapidly once cut from the living plant because air causes internal discoloration and decay. They must be processed into foods like gari quickly after harvest.
ga: Kasava shishifãi jeɔ shishi efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ afo kɛjɛ tso ni hiɛ ka mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ su tsakeɔ ni emli fiteɔ. Esa akɛ afee amɛ oya ni amɛfee niyenii tamɔ gari yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava stems are healthy enough to produce big tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo bulbs wuji?

english: Healthy cassava plants have strong, firm stems and dark green leaves without curling or spots. Strong stems show that the plant is efficiently sending sugars down into the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ baai eŋɔli ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ ajie sugar kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I see small holes and chewed edges on the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Chewed holes inside the central leaves of young corn are usually caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworm that hide inside the funnel to feed on tender growth before ears develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii ni dara lɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Dani toi lɛ baadara

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my cocoa farm right before it rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Rain helps dissolve fertilizer so the roots can absorb the nutrients, but heavy downpours can wash it away. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or right before light rain.
ga: Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo kɛya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo dani nugbɔ fioo ko baanɛ.

english: Where exactly around the tree trunk should I place my cocoa fertilizer?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ kookoo awo tso lɛ shishi yɛ?

english: Place fertilizer under the leaf canopy at the drip line—the circular area directly beneath the outer tips of the branches—because that is where active feeder roots are located.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋwɛitsu lɛ shishi yɛ he ni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji he ko ni yɔɔ kokroo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ nine lɛ naagbee shishigbɛ tɔ̃ɔ. Ejaakɛ jɛmɛ ji he ni niyenii ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ shishifãi yɔɔ.

english: Is it safe to put dry fertilizer on dry ground if no rain is coming?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Dry fertilizer cannot be absorbed without moisture and can burn root tips or sit unused, so you should wait until the soil is damp or rain is expected.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã loo amɛfee nɔ ni tsuuu nii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: What happens to my fertilizer if a very heavy downpour falls right after I put it on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-fertilizer lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa waa beni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates surface runoff that washes loose fertilizer away into streams or neighboring land before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa faai loo hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Do my young four-year-old cocoa trees need the same amount of fertilizer as my older ten-year-old trees?
ga: Ani mi cacao tso ni eye afii ejwɛ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ mi cacao tso ni eye afii nyɔŋma lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, younger trees need smaller amounts placed closer to their growing root system, while larger mature trees require more nutrients spread wider under their full canopy.
ga: Dabi, tsei bibii biɔ ni akɛ nɔ ko bibioo ko awo shishifã ni miida lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ niyenii babaoo fe nɔ ni ajaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: At what age should I expect my young cocoa trees to start producing pods?
ga: Mɛɛ afii esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ baaje shishi amɛwo ŋmeii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing pods around 2 to 3 years after planting, reaching solid production by year 4.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, ni afi ni ji ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my ten to fourteen-year-old cocoa trees seem to produce fewer pods than when they were younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-cacao tso ni eye afii nyɔŋma kɛyashi nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe beni eyɔɔ gbekɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, soil nutrients deplete and canopy growth slows, requiring proper pruning and targeted fertilizing to keep pod yield high.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa ni ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ dalɛ baa shi. Enɛ biɔ ni afolɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli jogbaŋŋ koni pod yibii babaoo ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning pale green instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale green leaves usually show that the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, which you can fix by applying the right cocoa fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni obaanyɛ ojaje kɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are actually getting good benefit from the fertilizer I applied?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miiná ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he sɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Healthy cocoa trees respond with dark green leaves, strong new shoots, good flowering, and healthy pod development without early pod drop.
ga: Kakao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ haa hetoo kɛ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Tsofɔi heei ni he wa fɔfɔii kpakpai kɛ ŋmɔji ni mli wa ni haaa ŋmɔji lɛ agbee shi oya

english: Why is it bad to throw fertilizer quickly and unevenly across my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nɔ fɔŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya ni ekɛ nɔ ko akafee ekome lɛ?

english: Uneven application leaves some trees starved of nutrients while over-fertilizing others, which wastes money and damages tree roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛtsuuu nii be fɛɛ be lɛ, ehaa tsei komɛi náaa niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ ekrokomɛi amli ŋmɔshi nii fe nine. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni efiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I know if the corn seeds I saved from my last harvest are good enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: Good seed corn should be clean, fully dry, heavy, and free from insect holes or mold. You can test them by dropping seeds into a bowl of water—healthy seeds that will germinate sink to the bottom, while weak or damaged seeds float.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa kpakpa lɛ ahe atse, ni egbi kwraa, ni etsii, ni ŋmãa loo ŋmãa akafee nɔ ko. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni oooshɛrɛ awo nu tsɛnsi mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji dumɔwui ni he wa ni baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛyashɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo efite lɛ baaho.

english: How should I properly dry and store my harvested corn so it does not spoil before the next planting season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ekafite dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Dry your corn cobs thoroughly in the sun on raised platforms until the grains are rock-hard. Store the threshed grains in clean, airtight sacks or sealed containers kept off the ground in a cool, dry place to protect them from moisture and pests.
ga: Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ tɛi. Kɛ ŋmaa ni atswa lɛ ato kotokui ni he tse, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsɛnsii ni atsĩ naa mli. Okɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Is it better for me to buy fresh seeds from the market every season or save seeds from my own farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ jara nɔ daa afi loo mabua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli?

english: Buying certified seed ensures high yield and disease resistance, but if you save your own seeds, you must carefully select only the largest, healthiest cobs from your strongest plants to keep your future harvests successful.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba ni helai hu nyɛŋ amɔ amɛ. Shi kɛji bo diɛŋtsɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ to Esa akɛ Ohala ŋmeii ni dara fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ amli bɔni afee ni owɔsɛɛ kpamɔ lɛ aye omanye.

english: How do I prepare my land properly before putting my corn seeds into the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Clear the weeds and loosen the topsoil so young roots can spread easily. Preparing moist, rich soil at the very beginning gives seeds the best chance to sprout fast and grow evenly.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ ni ogbɔjɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi bibii lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni baa nii babaoo ha kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my corn seeds when planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for light, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks. Spacing seeds about 25 to 30 centimeters apart in rows gives each plant enough space to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ji aaafee sɛntimita 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops look greener and stronger than mine even though we get the same rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ fe minɔ̃ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ hu?

english: Crops look healthier when a farmer carefully prepares the soil, selects quality seeds, and feeds the soil properly. Observing how successful farms treat their seeds and soil can show you what adjustments your field needs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ fɛo waa kɛ́ okwaafoi lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Halamɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ bɔ ni sa Bɔ ni ŋmɔji yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ mli lɛ kwɛmɔ baanyɛ atsɔɔ bo tsakemɔi ni he hiaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: What are the key stages of growth my corn will go through from planting to harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji dalɛ mli nibii titrii ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ tsɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ mli?

english: Corn goes through three main phases: sprouting and early leaf growth, rapid knee-high stalk growth, and flowering where cobs fill with grain. Caring for your field early on ensures strength through all three stages.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ gbɛi titrii etɛ nɔ: ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ mra. Tsoi kakadaji ni yaa hiɛ oya kɛ fɔfɔi ni baa yɛ hei ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Oshia lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaha hewalɛ aba yɛ gbɛi etɛ lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my corn seeds sprout nicely while others in the same row fail to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔɔ lɛ? Yɛ sɛɛkuu kome mli lɛ, dalɛ ko bɛ?

english: Uneven sprouting happens if seeds were planted at different depths, if moisture was unequal in the soil, or if insects damaged some seeds before they could break through the surface.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ, shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee baa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ jeee ekome loo kɛji kooloi bibii kpata dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ahiɛ dani amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my harvested corn cobs to have missing grains or empty tips?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ bɛ ŋmeii loo naagbee lɛ efolo?

english: Empty cobs usually happen when plants do not get enough water or nutrients during the flowering stage, or when poor weather prevents pollen from reaching the corn silks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ tsiɔ pollen naa koni ekashɛ ŋmãa tsɔji lɛ ahe.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my corn field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Apply a base fertilizer or manure right at planting to encourage early root growth, and add a second application when the corn reaches knee-high height to nourish the plant as it prepares to form cobs.
ga: Kɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii kɛji oodu nii koni eha shishifãi lɛ ada oya. Ni okɛ shi ni ji enyɔ afata he beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ aaafee enaneshi lɛ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii be mli ni esaa ehe koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do people say our climate and land in Ghana are so good for growing mangoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ wɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mango ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees thrive in warm weather and well-draining soil, which Ghana has in abundance. Our distinct wet and dry seasons naturally trigger mango trees to flower and produce sweet, high-quality fruit.
ga: Mango tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. ni Ghana yɛ babaoo Wɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hɔmɔ bei srɔtoi lɛ woɔ mango tsei hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii ni ŋɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is better suited for fruit trees like mangoes rather than seasonal vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sa kɛha aduawai tsei tamɔ mango fe be mli aduawai?

english: Tree crops like mangoes need deep, loose soil where their long taproots can grow wide and deep. If your soil drains water easily and doesn't get flooded during heavy rains, it is well suited for fruit trees.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli, tamɔ mango, biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse. Taproot kakadaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ adara ni etsɔ shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ oya ni nu hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ehi kɛha tsei ni woɔ yibii

english: How far apart should I plant my mango trees when setting up a new farm?
ga: Kɛ́ ato ŋmɔ hee ko shishi lɛ, te esa akɛ adu mango tsei kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Mango trees should be planted about 8 to 10 meters apart. This ensures that mature trees do not block each other's sunlight, allows good airflow to prevent diseases, and leaves enough space for roots to feed from the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mango tsei aaafee mitai 8 kɛyashi 10 kɛjɛ amɛhe koni tsei ni eda lɛ akatsi amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni helai akamɔ mɔ. ni oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Do my mango trees need continuous heavy watering during the dry season to bear good fruit?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni afɔ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ená yibii kpakpai?

english: Young trees need regular water to build roots, but mature mango trees actually need a short dry spell. The dry weather stresses the tree just enough to induce flowering, which leads to a good fruit yield when rains return.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei bibii daa koni amɛfee shishifãi, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, mango tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia be kuku ni amɛgbiɔ. Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ bɔ ni sa ni ehaa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi. Enɛ haa anáa yibii kpakpai kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is an extension officer telling me to cut off branches from a healthy mango tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ mango niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so sunlight can reach the inner leaves. Sunlight and airflow keep the tree healthy, stop fungal diseases, and encourage the tree to grow bigger, sweeter fruits.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. koni hulu la anyɛ ashɛ baai lɛ amli Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Kpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ni owo tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What kind of manure or fertilizer should I feed my mango trees to get high yields?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ akɛwo mango tso mli koni ená yibii babaoo?

english: Young trees need nitrogen-rich compost to build strong branches and leaves. Once the tree starts flowering and fruiting, it needs fertilizers rich in potassium and phosphorus to make the fruits large and sweet.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hia ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ koni amɛná niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ bɔi fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium kɛ phosphorus eyi mli obɔ lɛ aha lɛ koni yibii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do tiny black spots appear on my young mango fruits and make them fall early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi mango yibii lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Black spots are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose or by fruit fly bites. Spraying suitable organic or approved fungicides during flowering and hanging fruit fly traps will protect your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose loo aduawai amli ŋmeii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela diji baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli kɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my mango trees produce plenty of flowers, but very few of them turn into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi fioo pɛ woɔ yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers can drop off due to heavy winds, insect attack, or poor pollination. Keeping bees near your farm helps pollinate flowers, and spraying against tiny pests right before flowering helps the flowers stay on the tree and turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, kooloi tutuamɔi loo pollination ni ehiii hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii kwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Dani fɔfɔi lɛ baawo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to pick mangoes so they don't spoil on the way to the market?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mango koni ekafite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Pick mangoes when the 'shoulders' at the top of the fruit become broad and flat, and the skin turns from dark green to a lighter green with a slight yellowish patch near the stem. Harvesting at this stage ensures the fruit ripens safely after picking.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ mango be mli ni ‘tsitsii’ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli lɛɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni hewolo lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa eŋɔli ni mli tse mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fioo yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Nɛkɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fã nɛɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ shweshweeshwe beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do some farmers get much higher prices for their mangoes even when we grow the same crop in the same village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi naa amɛ mango lɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa eyɛ mli akɛ wɔduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ akrowa kome mli moŋ?

english: Buyers pay higher prices for fruit that is uniform in size, free of insect marks, and properly packaged. Protecting fruit from pests while on the tree and handling picked fruit gently to prevent bruising makes it eligible for high-value markets.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ aduawai ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe, ni kooloi akadi ko bɛ he, ni akɛwo kotoku mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nyɔmɔ babaoo. Yibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe beni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ yibii ni aŋɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii blɛoo koni akafite lɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha jarayeli hei ni jara wa waa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build healthy green leaves and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji aba.

english: Why are there small holes and powdery dirt inside the shoots of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing stem of the maize plant to feed on the soft leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I cut down all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight; they need shade from surrounding trees to protect their foliage and keep the root zone moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ adɛŋ. Koni ebu baai lɛ ahe ni eha shishifã lɛ he afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over when the fruits start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that cannot support heavy weight, so as the fruit bunch grows heavy, the plant needs wooden props to support it against gravity and strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ tsɔne ni tsii nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ dara lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ he miihia tsei ni akɛfiɔ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings rot in the soil when I plant them during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil deprives stem cuttings of air, creating a wet environment where soil bacteria and fungi easily rot the stems before roots can form.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akafee tso lɛ shishi. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa Bacteria kɛ fungi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I train their vines onto tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves up off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight to make more food, which the plant stores underground in the tuber.
ga: Staking haa ŋmeii lɛ náa baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ koni amɛfee niyenii babaoo. Tso lɛ kɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any fruit when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot form seeds, causing the plant to shed the unfertilized flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ ebɔ dumɔwui. Ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the leaves and spreading plant viruses that disrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them stay fresh during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛhi shi ehee yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Mulching with dry grass protects the soil from direct sun, keeping the ground cool and preventing water from evaporating quickly from the plant roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa nu akajɛ tsei ashishifãi amli oya.

english: Why does planting groundnut or cowpea on my land make the next crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnut and cowpea naturally capture nitrogen from the air and add it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct heat and burn easily. Planting fast-growing plantains next to them creates natural shade that shields the young leaves and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ baai bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i baa.

english: When too many shoots grow from one plantain stem, they fight over nutrients and water. Leaving only two or three strong shoots allows the plant to focus its energy on producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantain tsei babaoo miida lɛ, Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tsei niji wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: What are these tiny caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys maize. Catching them early and applying safe treatments, like neem leaf extracts or recommended sprays, stops them before they ruin your entire harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmãa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he ŋaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Is it okay for me to save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant during the next season?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Reusing seeds from high-yielding hybrid maize usually produces weak plants with small ears. Buying fresh certified seeds each season ensures strong growth and a much larger yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni toi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Cassava roots spoil quickly once harvested because exposure to air triggers natural breakdown. It is best to dig up only what you can sell, eat, or process into gari or flour immediately.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsu nibii pɛ ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ, oye, loo okɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofee gari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: Why are my yam tubers very small even though the vines and leaves above ground look large and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes plants to grow thick leaves instead of large roots. Yams need balanced soil nutrients, especially potassium, to feed and expand the tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa baai ni mli tse yɛ shishifãi wuji najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia sweet potato. titri lɛ potassium ni baabote shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli ni egbɛ eshwa

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly dry up and die even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial or fungal wilt living in the soil, which blocks water from moving inside the stem. Rotating your tomato crops to a new plot of land each season prevents these soil diseases from building up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ muawai loo fɔŋi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haaa nu aya tsɔne lɛ mli. Tomato tsei ni atsakeɔ amɛ kɛyaa hei heei yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkaje shishi.

english: Why do holes keep appearing on my pepper leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp conditions and feed on soft leaves. Spacing your pepper plants further apart allows air and sunlight to dry the leaves quickly, making it harder for pests and diseases to spread.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Pepper tsei lɛ amli gbalamɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and encourages crop-specific pests to stay. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts valuable nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ewo tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe hewalɛ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen ni jara wa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I protect my crops from drying out when the rains stop unexpectedly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa?

english: Covering the ground around your crop roots with dried leaves or straw (mulching) keeps soil moisture from evaporating, helping your crops survive short dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oooha Otsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulching) baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ akafo. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture so the young plants can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground onto sticks allows the leaves to catch more sunlight. More sunlight helps the plant produce more energy, which leads to bigger yam tubers growing underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛtee niji lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii babaoo baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know which way to insert a cassava stem cutting into the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmei tsei woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Always plant cassava stems with the small nodes or buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to grow and root development will be weak.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei kɛ ŋmeii bibii. loo ŋmeii bibii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu baagbɔjɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves are usually a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to stay green and build leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ he miihia koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do people recommend planting groundnuts or beans on the same land with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize improves soil fertility naturally without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why is it a bad idea to put fertilizer on my farm right when heavy rain starts falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ ni naa wa jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ lɛ ji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the field before the plant roots can drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist but rain is gentle.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nugbɔ enɛ fioo.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (called mulching) keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from taking over your crop area.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes right in the center of my corn shoots?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest whose moths lay eggs on young corn. They burrow into the growing tips (whorl) of the maize and must be treated early before they destroy the stalk.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli (rings) lɛ mli ni esa akɛ atsa amɛ mra dani amɛfite ŋmãa lɛ.

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain tree, they fight for nutrients and water. Removing the weaker shoots leaves just two or three strong ones, resulting in larger plantain bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ baashwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ agboi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden weather changes. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants developing holes and getting destroyed by small caterpillars?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu ni ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. The caterpillars feed on young leaves, but applying recommended control measures early in the morning or late evening when caterpillars are active helps protect your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai yeɔ baai bibii. Shi gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ he lɛ ni oootsu he nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any tall shade crops nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or bananas gives the young cocoa trees the shade and moist air they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ lɛ haa cocoa tsei bibii lɛ naa shade kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long during rainy periods. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots, keeping them healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crops turning yellow while the rest of the plant stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Mulching around the roots and watering regularly helps keep the soil moist and cool.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space and food to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops slow down their growth?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee tɛŋŋ miigbɔjɔ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures all soil nutrients go directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ tso ko wala shishijee bei amli lɛ, ehaa sũ mli niyenii fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking the vines allows the leaves to catch maximum light, which helps grow larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha sweet potato tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná la babaoo. Enɛ baaha sweet potato ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does heavy rain carry away the good top layer of soil on my farm, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Bare soil washes away easily when heavy rain flows over it. Planting cover crops like cowpeas or building ridges across sloping land slows down running water and traps the rich topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ho kɛtsɔ mli. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ loo ŋmeii ni afee yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans returns nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When I apply medicine to my cocoa trees, should I spray the leaves or focus on the cocoa pods?
ga: Be ni esa akɛ akɛ kookoo tsofa lɛ atsu nii Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔse baai lɛ anɔ loo mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama kookoo lɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ?

english: You should focus on applying the chemical around the cocoa pods rather than on the leaves. The pods are the most vulnerable part that needs protection from diseases like black pod, so targeting them directly ensures your crop stays healthy without wasting chemical on the leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Cocoa pods rather the leaves Pods lɛ ji hei ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ ni he hiaa ni abu he kɛjɛ helai ahe lɛ ateŋ ekomɛi, tamɔ pods diji, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛji okɛ ohiɛ fɔ̃ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ efiteee.

english: Why do my cocoa pods need chemical protection even when the leaves on the tree look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abu mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsofai ahe lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa moŋ, shi.

english: Cocoa pods are rich in moisture and attract diseases like black pod that leaves do not get. Even if the tree leaves look strong, the pods themselves need direct protection around them to prevent decay and preserve your harvest.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbalaa helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni baa bɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ Shi pod lɛ diɛŋtsɛ he miihia hebuu tɛ̃ɛ ni ebɔle ehe. Enɛ haaa fitemɔ aba ni ehaa onibii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: What happens if it rains right after I finish spraying protective chemical on my cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni migbe tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ni mikɛshwie mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naa pɛ?

english: If rain falls immediately after you spray, the rainwater washes the chemical off before it can stick to the pods. This leaves your cocoa unprotected against fungal diseases and pests, meaning you may need to reapply when the dry weather returns.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ tsofai lɛ ahe dani amɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa obu o-cocoa lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ kookoo atsu nii ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How do I know the correct way to apply chemicals to cocoa seedlings without damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ tsofai baawo kookoo dumɔwui amli ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Tender young seedlings can easily be burned by strong chemicals or improper application. Chemical treatments should be applied carefully around the seedling's stem and base rather than directly onto its delicate young leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa loo ni akɛtsuuu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni mli wa lɛ oya. Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi kɛ eshishigbɛ he Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛbaawo baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I pay attention to weather forecasts when planning work on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji anɔ kɛ́ miito mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: Weather forecasts help you know if rain is coming so you do not waste time, money, and labor applying chemicals that rain will immediately wash away. Planning around rainfall ensures your treatments stay on the plants and work properly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa haa oleɔ kɛji nugbɔ baa nɛ loo enaaa. Ehe ehiaaa ni ofite be, shika, kɛ nitsumɔ ni okɛ tsofai awo mli koni nugbɔ lɛ ashwie shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ haa otsofafeemɔ lɛ hiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to spray my cocoa trees with chemical protection before or after a rainstorm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baafɔ cacao nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ loo no sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until after the rain has passed and the crop has dried off. Spraying right before rain leads to the chemical being washed away into the soil before it can protect your cocoa pods.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ eho ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ehaa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛbuɔ o-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ ahe.

english: How does rainy weather affect how quickly diseases spread among my cocoa trees?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ saa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ he oya ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain creates a damp, humid environment that allows fungal spores to spread very quickly from tree to tree. During wet periods, cocoa pods are at high risk, making timely protective spraying crucial.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii yɛ oshara mli waa. Nibii ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ he miihia.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me stay updated about weather changes?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ koni male kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji?

english: Extension officers receive reliable scientific weather updates and translate them into simple farming advice. They can alert you about upcoming rainfall or dry spells so you can schedule your planting, spraying, and harvesting at the right time.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ naa jeŋ nilee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. ni atsɔɔ shishi kɛtee okwaayeli he ŋaawoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo mli Amɛbaanyɛ amɛbɔ bo kɔkɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ loo nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oto be ni sa kɛha dumɔ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ kpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it important for me to build a strong working relationship with my local extension officer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mimaŋ nitsulɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ama nitsumɔ wekukpaa ni mli wa lɛ?

english: A good relationship with your extension officer ensures you get timely warnings about weather, direct guidance on chemical application, and expert solutions to crop health problems before you lose your yield.
ga: Wekukpaa kpakpa ni kã okɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa onine shɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he kɔkɔbɔɔ nɔ. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi tɛ̃ɛ ni kɔɔ tsofai kɛ ŋaalɔi ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsaa tsei ahewalɛ he naagbai ahe dani okɛ onibii lɛ baaje odɛŋ.

english: Do young cocoa seedlings require the same care and protection as mature cocoa trees during rainy weather?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei bibii biɔ kwɛmɔ kɛ hebuu tamɔ kookoo tsei ni eda yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: No, cocoa seedlings have smaller root systems and softer tissues than fully grown trees. While mature trees focus on pod protection, young seedlings need extra care around their stems and soil to prevent heavy rains from beating them down or rotting their roots.
ga: Dabi, Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe tsei ni eda lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii lɛ ahebuu nɔ moŋ, shi tsei bibii lɛ hu he miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite loo akafite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and extreme heat. Shade trees or companion crops like plantains act as natural shields, protecting the tender seedlings from sun damage and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii. Ebuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the bottom up, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. The crop moves whatever nitrogen it has to the upper leaves to keep growing, showing that your soil needs extra fertilizer or manure.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mli.

english: How do cassava stem cuttings know to grow roots downward into the soil and leaves upward toward the sun?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji oofo ŋmei tso lɛ akɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baai lɛ baatsɔɔ hulu lɛ?

english: Cassava stems contain natural plant hormones that react to gravity and moisture. No matter how you plant them, the hormones signal the bottom nodes to push roots deep into the earth for water while the top nodes send shoots up to catch sunlight.
ga: Tso mli tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ cassava tsei lɛ amli. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ooodu lɛ oha. Hormones haa nodes ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ leɔ koni amɛtsi shishifãi lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu. yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi node lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the blossoms drop off without growing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato plants often shed their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when they lack sufficient water. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from stress until growing conditions improve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔi ahe kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb instead of spreading out on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are climbing plants that need their leaves raised high up into the sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves away from wet soil, preventing diseases and helping the plant direct energy into growing large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ ni awó baai anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does planting hot pepper or onions next to my vegetables keep insects away?
ga: Pepper loo onion ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Te aduawai baanyɛ aye abua ni ashwie kooloi bibii lɛ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Strong-smelling plants act as natural guardians by masking the scent of your vegetables. The strong odor confuses pest insects and prevents them from finding and eating your main crop.
ga: Tsei ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli bulɔi kɛtsɔ o-vegetables lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ. Fuumɔ ni naa wa lɛ futuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. ni otsĩ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ni amɛye.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly like tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense against drought and heat. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which traps moisture and stops the crop from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ hɔmɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baaha he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi.

english: Why does growing cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for the next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have friendly microscopic bacteria living in little bumps on their roots. These bacteria grab nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, providing free natural food for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai bibii ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ su ni hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Muawai nɛɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ

english: Why are my sweet orange trees dropping small green fruits before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Dani ebaada kwraa?

english: Citrus trees drop premature fruit when they experience severe water stress—either from too little rainfall or from waterlogged soil during floods—because the tree prioritizes keeping itself alive over growing fruit.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛyibii lɛ oya kɛji nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa kpe amɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa yɛ nu afua be mli jio. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ susuɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala mlihilɛ he fe aduawai ni amɛduɔ.

english: Weeds act like aggressive thieves in your farm. Their roots spread quickly to steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly from your crops, leaving your plants with too few nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my maize plants growing so slowly in the first few weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the first few weeks, a maize plant focuses its energy underground on building strong roots rather than growing tall leaves. Once its root system is established in the soil, the plant will start growing above ground much faster.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Abɛi tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa moŋ fe ni amɛaawo baai kakadaŋŋ agboi. beni eshishifãi lɛ ema shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaje shishi eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why are some of the cassava stems I planted sprouting quickly while others in the same row haven't shown any buds yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi ni miduɔ lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi daa lɛ? Yɛ nɛkɛ sɛɛkuu nɛɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ŋmeii komɛi ekwɛko lolo?

english: Cassava cuttings sprout at different speeds depending on which part of the main stem they were cut from, soil moisture levels, and planting depth. As long as the stems remain fresh and healthy underground, the slower ones will catch up once their roots develop.
ga: Cassava ni afo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Edamɔ tso lɛ fã titri ni afo lɛ nɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ bɔ ni aduɔ lɛ mli kwɔ ha Be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baahi shi ehee ni ehe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Tsoi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baashɛ he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: I buried my seed yams three weeks ago, but no shoots are showing above the ground yet. Have they ruined in the soil?
ga: Mifu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ otsii etɛ ni eho nɛ. Shi ŋmeii komɛi ejeee kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo. Ani amɛgbee shi amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams naturally take time to wake up from dormancy and form a main growing shoot underground before emerging into the light. Depending on soil moisture and heat, it often takes between three to six weeks for new yam shoots to show above ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ heɔ be dani amɛteɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii titrii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛyaa la lɛ mli. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ dɔlɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ otsii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani ŋmeii heei jieɔ amɛhe kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant directs its energy into growing leaves or saving water rather than holding onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei kɛ amɛhe akpɛtɛ fɔfɔi ahe lɛ, amɛkɛ hewalɛ yaa baai ni miida lɛ amli loo amɛbuɔ nu he.

english: Why is my okra growing very tall with big leaves but giving me almost no okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔ okra lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji, shi okra ŋmeii ko kwraa bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen from heavy manure or chemical fertilizer, they put all their effort into leaf and stem growth instead of flowering. Giving the plant full sunlight and reducing nitrogen allows it to shift focus back to making flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ wo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni ajie nitrogen lɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aku esɛɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ni ebaafee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some tomatoes on the same branch turning red while others are still small and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato komɛi ni yɔɔ tso nine kome nɔ lɛ feɔ tsuru shi ekrokomɛi hu hiɔ shi bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Flowers on the same cluster open and get pollinated on different days, so the fruits develop at different rates. This staggered growth allows the plant to share its nutrients steadily over time without trying to feed all big fruits at once.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ kuu kome mli lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa gbi. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai daa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Nɛkɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ waa nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ jaa niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ nɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. ni ebɔɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eye aduawai wuji lɛ fɛɛ shikome.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and look weak in the hot afternoon, even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ

english: In the hot afternoon sun, large plantain leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it from the ground. The leaves curl and droop to protect themselves from drying out, but they bounce back in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Plantain baai wuji lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Shi efoɔ esɛɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why does my young cocoa tree drop its leaves during the dry season, and will the tree die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni ani kookoo tso lɛ baagbo?

english: Young cocoa trees drop leaves during the dry season to reduce water loss and protect their main stems from drying up. If you keep shade around them and cover the soil base with dry bush or leaves, the stems will stay alive and produce fresh leaves when the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebu tso titri lɛ he koni ekagbi. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shade wo shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi ni okɛ tsei bibii loo baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Tso lɛ yibii lɛ baahi shi ni amɛbaawo baai heei kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: When a plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, it automatically pulls nitrogen out of its older, lower leaves to keep the young top leaves growing. Yellowing at the bottom is a natural signal that the crop needs feeding or that excess water is hiding nutrients from the roots.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ ehe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aya nɔ ada. Yellow ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii he miihia tso lɛ. Aloo, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ teeɔ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants remaining tiny and bushy instead of spreading out across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji ŋmɔji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas stay small if the soil is packed too tight for roots to spread, or if the soil lacks phosphorus. Loosening hard soil and ensuring good phosphorus levels helps the root network expand, allowing the plant to branch out normally.
ga: Cowpeas baafee bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni akwɛɔ fɔsfɔs kpakpa nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ amli alɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ atswa niji bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crop roots die when strong winds blow away the plastic covering around their base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa plastic ni akɛha shishitoo lɛ he lɛ?

english: When roots are exposed to direct wind and air, they lose their surface moisture almost instantly. Without protective soil or mulch, fragile feeder roots dry out, preventing the plant from absorbing water and nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ sɛɛ foɔ aaafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni buɔ mɔ he bɛ Shishifãi ni waaa lɛ baagbi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Can I pour liquid chemical or fertilizer directly onto roots that are sticking out of the ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafɔse tsofai ni ji nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shishifãi ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, applying concentrated chemicals directly to exposed roots causes severe chemical burns. You must first cover exposed roots with fresh topsoil before applying any fertilizer or chemical around the drip line of the plant.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha tsofai ashã mɔ waa. Esa akɛ okɛ sũ hee aha shishifãi ni eje kpo lɛ ahe klɛŋklɛŋ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai awo amɛhe. tsei amli nu ŋmɔtɔi

english: Why do my plants wilt and look shocked right after I dig around their base to clear weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni efeɔ tamɔ mɔ ko ni ehiɛ efee lɛ yaa beni mifo shishigbɛ lɛ he koni majie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Digging too close to the main stem cuts off tiny feeding roots and leaves the remaining roots exposed to air. Damaging these water-absorbing roots puts the plant into shock, causing immediate wilting.
ga: Kɛ́ atsa tso lɛ shishifãi bibii ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ, ni ebaaha shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ aya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ afite nɛkɛ shishifãi ni shwieɔ nu nɛɛ, ehaa tso lɛ he feɔ shoo ni ehaa egboɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What happens if I apply chemicals to my soil right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ tsofai wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Heavy rain washes chemicals away from the topsoil or forces them too deep into the ground. This wastes your money and can concentrate harmful chemical runoff around sensitive root zones.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsofai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo enyɛɔ amɛnɔ ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Nakai feemɔ baaha ofite shika, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara aba yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: Why is it dangerous if the rubber nursery bag tears and leaves seedling roots bare during planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji akɛ kɔndom lɛ gbá ni eshi dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Bare seedling roots suffer from transplant shock when exposed to open wind and heat. Keeping the nursery soil intact around the root ball during planting protects the roots until they settle into the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ ashishifãi lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ shoofeemɔ ni akɛwo amɛmli lɛ he kɛji amɛyashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni aaaha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he fɛɛ he Shishifãi bɔɔlu yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaahi ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops scorch so fast when the ground around the stems is left uncovered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Uncovered soil absorbs heat from direct sunlight, heating the soil temperature around shallow roots. When roots get too hot, they stop pumping water to the leaves, leading to leaf scorching.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ shwieɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Ebaakpa nu ni ekɛbaa baa lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa.

english: Why did my crops dry up completely after I sprayed chemical on them when they were already wilting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi kwraa beni mikɛ tsofai lɛ eshwie shi yɛ be mli ni amɛgboi momo lɛ?

english: Applying chemicals to plants already stressed by sun or root exposure overpowers their survival system. Stressed plants cannot process strong chemicals, leading to chemical shock and rapid death.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ tsei ni hulu la loo amɛshishifãi egba amɛnaa lɛ ahe lɛ baaná amɛshihilɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Tsei ni haoɔ amɛhe lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ahe nii. Enɛ kɛ tsofafeemɔ he shoofeemɔ kɛ gbele oya baa.

english: Why do some farmers use rubber sheets or dry leaves to cover the soil around their young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ rɔbɔt loo baai ni egbi tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Ground covers block direct sunlight and wind, keeping soil moisture high and protecting delicate roots from heat stress so plants can grow faster and stronger.
ga: Mulch tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i aya hiɛ ni obu shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Koni tsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛhe awa

english: What should I do when heavy rains wash away the topsoil and leave my crop roots exposed?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni eha mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: You should immediately heap fresh, nutrient-rich topsoil back over the exposed roots. Leaving them uncovered will cause sun burn and allow wind to dry out the root system.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ato shishifãi ni miiba lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ ni amɛgbele lɛ, ebaaha hulu lɛ ashã bo ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why are my crops failing to bounce back after a rainfall, even though the rain was heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If plant roots were exposed to intense heat or burned by wrong chemical use before the rain, the water-transporting cells in the roots may already be permanently destroyed, making recovery impossible.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tso shishifãi lɛ wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo akɛ tsofai ni ejaaa tsu nii kɛshã amɛ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, no lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli wala yibii ni kɛ nu yaa lɛ baanyɛ afite kwraa. ni ehaa enyɛŋ ehi shi ekoŋŋ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under the hot sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create shade, protecting young cocoa trees until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when excessive water in the soil prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing food properly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛ́ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei miida kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmei titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: The first rain after a dry season is often not enough to keep the soil moist for long. Planting too early causes seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows before the main rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Is it beneficial to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is good because bean plants pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize and improves crop growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi ejaakɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when insect pests attack the blossoms during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔii yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted to quickly soak up water and nutrients from the soil, allowing them to sprout and outgrow farm crops that need more care.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni biɔ kwɛmɔ babaoo lɛ.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves high onto stakes to capture sunlight, which gives the plant the energy required to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What causes tiny holes to appear all over the leaves of my cabbage crops?
ga: Mɛni haa buji lɛ feɔ bibii? Ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by caterpillars or beetles feeding on the leaves, which weakens the plant and prevents it from forming a firm, healthy cabbage head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ladybugs ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni baa cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa kabaaji yitsei lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sunlight, keeps moisture in the soil longer, and stops weeds from sprouting easily.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Why do some of my tree crops take up to 12 or 15 years before they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ekomɛi heɔ afii 12 loo 15 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Certain long-gestation tree crops spend their first decade building deep root systems and strong trunks. They need to store enough energy and maturity before they can support heavy, fleshy fruits.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni yeɔ afii nyɔŋma lɛ kɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii nyɔŋma lɛ toɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Ehe miihia ni amɛto hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii.

english: If my fruit tree is already 12 years old and hasn't produced any yield yet, does it mean it will never bear fruit?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mitso lɛ eye afii 12 ni ewooo nɔ ko lolo hu? Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ewoŋ yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Not necessarily. Some slow-maturing crop varieties naturally take between 12 to 16 years to reach full maturity and start fruiting, depending on soil quality, shade, and rainfall.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ heɔ afii 12 kɛyashi 16 dani amɛshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some trees on my farm start fruiting early while others of the same age take many more years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi oya yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni eye afii kome lɛ heɔ afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Variations in individual plant genetics, localized soil fertility, access to sunlight, and root strength cause trees on the same farm to reach fruiting age at different times.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔ yɛ tsei ahe nibii amli Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nakai he lɛ mli nibii ni baa lɛ hulu la ni anáa kɛ shishifãi ahewalɛ Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli.

english: How can I tell if an older, non-bearing tree is finally preparing to produce its first crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ko ni eda ni bɛ bii lɛ miisaa ehe yɛ naagbee koni ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii awo?

english: Trees close to maturity usually show a significant thickening of the trunk, a fuller leaves canopy, and small flower buds forming at the stem nodes long before the fruit appears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni miibɛŋkɛ amɛdalɛ jieɔ tsei ni mli tse waa kpo. Baai lɛ ashishifã lɛ eyi obɔ. kɛ fɔfɔii bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ Feɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be saŋŋ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Is it better to plant fast-fruiting crop varieties or traditional long-term ones on my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii oya loo kusum mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fast-fruiting hybrids give quicker income within 3 to 5 years, but traditional long-term varieties that take 12 to 16 years to fruit often live much longer and resist harsh weather better.
ga: Hybrids ni woɔ yibii mra lɛ baaha shika aba mra, yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli, shi blema tsei ni woɔ yibii be kakadaŋŋ, ni heɔ afii 12 kɛyashi 16 dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ, fɔɔ shihilɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ.

english: How does the fruiting process affect the fleshiness and weight of my produce?
