ga: Te bɔ ni yibii lɛ woɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛtsii ha lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When a mature crop flowers and fruits, it directs stored nutrients into building thick, fleshy pulp and seeds, making the harvest rich in weight and market value.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaawo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii. Ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ dumɔwui. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni anáa lɛ yɛ muji kɛ jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: What can I do to help my mature trees produce bigger and fleshier fruits once they start bearing?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni maye mabua mitsei ni eda lɛ ni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ loo beni amɛbɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Applying potassium-rich fertilizer, keeping the farm free of competing weeds, and ensuring proper watering during flowering helps mature trees channel maximum energy into thick fruit flesh.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ni ahaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ bɛ mli Ni akwɛɔ koni akɛ nu awo mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni eda lɛ ni amɛkudɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli.

english: Why do slow-growing crops that take over a decade to bear yield often produce thicker fruit flesh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo ni heɔ nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋma dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ woɔ yibii ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Because slow-growing crops spend years accumulating minerals and nutrients from deep in the soil, their mature fruits develop denser, fleshier pulp compared to fast-growing crops.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛbuaa shika kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ anaa. Yibii ni eda lɛ yɛ loo ni mli wa ni eyɛ loo kɛ akɛto tsei ni daa oya lɛ ahe.

english: What does it mean to train seedlings in a nursery before transferring them to my main field?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwui atsɔsemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu amɛ awo miŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ shishi?

english: Training nursery seedlings involves gradually exposing them to sunlight, staking weak stems, and managing growth so they develop strong roots capable of supporting future heavy fruiting.
ga: Nɔ ni fata dumɔwui atsɔsemɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ fiofio. Ha hulu la lɛ akpɛ Staking Weak Stems ni okwɛ dalɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aye abua aduawai ni tsii ni baa lɛ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why should I nurse and manually plant seedlings instead of letting seeds sprout naturally on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ makwɛ dumɔwui anɔ ni makwɛ nɔ? Moŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Raising seedlings in a controlled nursery allows you to select only the healthiest plants and train them properly before spacing them in the field, leading to far better crop yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohalaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ni otsɔseɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani oduɔ amɛ srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the essential food crops need to build green, healthy leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to give fertilizer to my crops at specific times rather than all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli moŋ fe ni mawo amɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Crops need different types of nourishment at different stages of growth, so applying fertilizer at the right times ensures the plant can actually use the food rather than letting it wash away in the rain.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii srɔtoi yɛ amɛdalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ atsu nii diɛŋtsɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ mli lɛ

english: Why is it necessary to spray medicine on my cocoa trees before I even see diseases spreading?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo kookoo tsei amli tsofa dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ?

english: Applying crop medicine early acts like a shield, preventing diseases like black pod from taking root in your farm before they have the chance to ruin your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaatsu nii akɛ gãimlibii ni baatsi helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa koni amɛkawo shishifãi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Dani ebaaná hegbɛ ni efite onifeemɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf rolling is a natural protection response where the plant curls its leaves to conserve moisture and stop water from evaporating quickly in intense sunlight.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu hetoo. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun and dry winds, which is why planting temporary shade crops like plantain beside them protects them until their roots are deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Enɛ hewɔ ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to tall, thin stalks with small or missing cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my cassava even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi-cassava lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growing and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your cassava, leaving your crop starved even during good weather.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ o-cassava lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa po yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which prevents the blossoms from turning into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hewɔ. Enɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why does cutting off extra branches from my mango tree help it produce better fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi mango tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so the tree can send its main energy, water, and nutrients directly into growing larger and healthier fruit.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛya tso yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava yields every time I plant on the same piece of soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmei fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients out of the earth without giving the soil time to rest or rebuild its natural fertility.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ekɛsaa ebɔɔ su ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and extreme heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides the necessary shade and humidity needed for young cocoa roots and leaves to establish without burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni kookoo bibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ama shi ni amɛshãaa.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa seedlings when planting them on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo kookoo dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting cocoa trees about 3 meters by 3 meters apart ensures that each tree gets enough nutrients from the soil, sufficient air movement, and light, which keeps them healthy and prevents diseases from spreading easily between overcrowded branches.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni aduɔ aaafee mitai 3 kɛ mitai 3 lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe yɛ jɛmɛ. kɛ kane ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ, ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning completely black and rotting while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and humid conditions. Removing infected pods quickly and trimming extra tree branches helps air circulate, keeping the pods dry and preventing the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Oya ni ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What is causing small dark spots and swellings on my cocoa shoots and young pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? kɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ kɛ mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ fũu lɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by insects known as capsids or mirids that suck sap from young cocoa branches. Applying approved treatments at the right time of year protects the shoots and keeps the tree healthy enough to produce pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo mirids ni nuɔ kookoo niji bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaabu tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds around the base of my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your cocoa trees for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Keeping the ground around the tree clean ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need and eliminates hiding spots for harmful pests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Tsei lɛ ahe tsemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ, ni ejieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Covering the soil around root areas with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a protective blanket. It keeps soil moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat and keeps root zones cooler during dry periods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifã lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ latsaa be mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the straight young shoots growing out from the base of my cocoa trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These shoots, called chupons, drain valuable energy and food from the main tree. Removing them allows the cocoa tree to direct its energy into producing branches, flowers, and healthy pods instead of useless foliage.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ chupon. Ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ, ehaa cacao tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ niji, fɔfɔii, kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ

english: Trees drop flowers when they experience stress, such as severe lack of water, nutrient deficiency in the soil, or excessive heat. Providing adequate shade and rich soil nutrients helps the tree retain flowers and form full pods.
ga: Tsei baajie fɔfɔii kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ nu ni faaa amɛmli waa. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo la ni mli edɔ tsɔ Shade ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do large timber trees inside my farm help my cocoa trees stay healthy for longer?
ga: Te tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mikoo tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Permanent shade trees protect cocoa from strong winds and harsh heat, and their fallen leaves break down into rich natural fertilizer that feeds the cocoa roots, helping the cocoa farm stay productive for decades.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tso lɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli aha kookoo shishifãi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do some of my harvested cocoa pods have flat or sprouted seeds inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ekomɛi yɛ dumɔwui ni etse loo ekwɛ̃ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Flat or sprouted beans happen when pods are left on the tree for too long after ripening, or when the tree suffers from severe water stress. Harvesting ripe pods promptly every two weeks prevents this issue and keeps bean quality high.
ga: Beans ni etse loo ekwɛ̃ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ashi pods yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. aloo beni tso lɛ naa nu he haomɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ oya daa otsii enyɔ lɛ, ebaatsi naagba nɛɛ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is the spray medicine I bought not curing the disease on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni mihe lɛ tsaaa hela lɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Different plant diseases are caused by different issues like fungi, bacteria, or viruses. A medicine made for one specific disease will not work on another, so you must accurately identify the exact problem before buying chemicals.
ga: Naagbai srɔtoi, tamɔ ŋmei, muawai, loo muawai kɛ tsei helai sɔrɔtoi baa. Tsofai ni afee aha hela kome lɛ tsuuu nii ahaaa hela kroko. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ oyɔse naagba lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani ohé tsofai.

english: How do I know the difference between local names for farm diseases and what is actually affecting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli hela ko he gbɛi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ gbɛi ni saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ teŋ?

english: Local names often group several different plant problems under one term based on broad symptoms like wilting or spots. Extension officers look at leaf patterns, stem damage, and root health to give you the precise diagnosis.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akutsoŋ gbɛi lɛ buaa tsei ahe naagbai srɔtoi anaa. kɛtee wiemɔ kome mli Esusuɔ okadii ni mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ he. Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baasusu bɔ ni wolo lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ he. tso lɛ yitso lɛ fitemɔ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ Koni aha bo hela lɛ he tsɔɔmɔ ni ja

english: Are there some crop diseases that cannot be cured by spraying medicine at all?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai komɛi yɛ ni anyɛɛɛ atsa kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa?

english: Yes, viral diseases and advanced viral or bacterial infections cannot be cured with chemical sprays once a plant is infected. In those cases, spraying wastes money, and infected plants should be removed to protect healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛbaa loo helai ni etee hiɛ waa lɛ kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ tso lɛ nɔ pɛ. Yɛ shihilɛ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ mli lɛ, Spray ji shika fitemɔ ni esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni abu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: If a disease medicine fails to work on my farm, does that mean the chemical is fake?
ga: Ni kɛji tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hu? Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa lɛ ji amale?

english: Not always. A genuine medicine can fail if it was selected for the wrong disease, mixed incorrectly, applied at the wrong time of day, or applied after the disease reached an untreatable stage.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsofai diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ ahala hela ni ejaaa, akɛ tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsu nii, akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni ejaaa mli, loo akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ eshɛ he ni anyɛɛɛ atsa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can spraying weed killer or medicine on one crop accidentally harm other crops nearby?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ awui yɛ oshara mli?

english: Yes, chemical drift from spraying can land on neighboring crops. Certain plants are extremely sensitive to specific chemicals, and even a tiny amount carried by the wind can damage or destroy them.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ahe ni ekɛ naagbai aba. Tsofai komɛi nuɔ tsofai komɛi ahe waa. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo po baanyɛ afite nakai tsei lɛ loo egbe amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and die after I spray weed killer around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie ŋmɔ lɛ he fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains are soft-stemmed plants that easily absorb chemicals through their leaves and shallow roots. Many general farm chemicals and weed killers are toxic to plantains and will kill them upon contact.
ga: Plantains ji tsei ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni tsɔɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ tsofai oya. Tsofai kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo ji tsofai fɔji kɛha dumɔwui ni amɛbaagbe amɛ kɛji amɛshɛ amɛhe.

english: What steps should I take to protect sensitive crops like plantains when spraying my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa miifɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Spray only on calm mornings without wind, use a spray hood or nozzle shield on your knapsack, keep a safe distance from sensitive crops, and confirm with an officer that the chemical is safe for intercropped fields.
ga: Okɛshwie nɔ yɛ leebi ni yɔɔ dioo ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli pɛ. Kɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ loo nozzle shield awo sɛɛ kotoku lɛ nɔ. Ha he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ ahe. ni okɛ onukpai lɛ ama nɔ mi akɛ tsofai lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ ni atsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: How can I check if a farm chemical is safe to use around my plantain trees before I buy it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ dani mahe?

english: Read the product label carefully or ask an agro-dealer or extension officer. Labels explicitly list which crops can tolerate the medicine and which crops will be injured or killed by it.
ga: Kanemɔ nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo bi mɛi ni jaa okwaayeli loo mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni aŋmala nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ tsei ni baanyɛ akpɛlɛ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ faŋŋ. Ni mɛɛ tsei tsofa lɛ baapila loo ebaagbe amɛ?

english: Why do plantain trees seem to die much faster than cocoa or wood trees when exposed to bad chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni dumɔwui gboiɔ oya kwraa fe cacao tsei loo tsei kɛji akɛ tsofai gbohii wo amɛhe lɛ?

english: Plantains are giant herbaceous plants made mostly of soft tissues and water rather than hard wood. This structure makes them absorb liquids rapidly, making them far more vulnerable to harsh chemicals and rapid wilting.
ga: Plantains ji tsei wuji ni ji jwɛi ni akɛ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ nu feɔ amɛ babaoo moŋ fe tsei ni wa. Nɛkɛ gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu oya. Enɛ haa tsofai ni mli wa kɛ amɛhe shwieɔ shi oya lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya.

english: Can I safely plant plantains alongside other crops if I plan to use chemical sprays on the field?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe shweshweeshwe? Kɛji mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli

english: Yes, but you must select chemicals that are selective and safe for broad-leaf plants, or rely on targeted manual weeding around the bases of plantain trees to prevent accidental chemical contact.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ ohala tsofai ni ahala ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ. Aloo kɛ ohe afɔ̃ jwɛi ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii, ni akɛ hiɛ fɔ̃ɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ tsiɔ tsofai ni baa trukaa lɛ anaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has too much water, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes tiny holes appear on my vegetable leaves, and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni haa bu bibioo lɛ feɔ? ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Tiny holes are caused by insect pests like beetles or caterpillars eating the leaf. This weakens the plant because it uses its leaves to capture sunlight and make food to grow.
ga: Buji bibii ji nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ejaakɛ ekɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛnáa hulu la ni ekɛduɔ niyenii.

english: Leaves curl and droop as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water and reduce exposure to heat. Once the sun goes down and temperatures cool, the plant usually bounces back.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ lɛ gbɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛbaa dɔlɛ ni baa lɛ shi. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa sɛɛ.

english: If your previous crop grew very slowly, produced pale leaves, or gave a small harvest, it is a clear sign that the soil nutrients are low and need to be replenished.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ da blɛoo waa, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii pɛ. Eji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, sudden dry spells, or a lack of nutrients needed to nourish the developing fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo be ni nu hɔmɔ baa trukaa lɛ. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha aduawai ni miida lɛ aná hewalɛ ni bɛ

english: What happens if I plant my crops too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which leaves them tall and thin with smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that adapt quickly to get water and nutrients before cultivated crops can. Clearing them early stops them from stealing food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Black spots are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in wet, humid shade where rainwater drops spread the fungus from pod to pod.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Nugbɔ nu lɛ gbɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the healthy-looking branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting excess branches opens up the tree so air and sunlight can pass through, which keeps the plant dry enough to avoid fungal diseases and directs power into fruiting.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli egbiɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛtsi ehe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil or get eaten by insects when kept in the storeroom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi yeɔ amɛ kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ?

english: Grains rot or attract insects like weevils if they are put into storage while still damp. Drying them completely in the sun creates a dry environment pests cannot easily survive in.
ga: Ŋmãa baagbo loo ebaagbala kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni edɔ lolo. Hulu lɛ ni egbiɔ lɛ haa ewaa ahaa kooloi ni yɔɔ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ akɛ amɛaahi shi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves are delicate and lose water quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living canopy that protects the seedlings while their root systems grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpee hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ waaa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daa waa lɛ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight. The plants spend all their energy stretching upward to catch light, leaving them with weak stems and no extra energy to form full corn ears.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋshii mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ko ni ekɛbaafee ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is starving for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots and stopping them from feeding properly.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu yɛ he fɛɛ he. shishifãi lɛ ni etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow many leaves but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, legume plants spend all their energy making thick, green foliage instead of triggering the blossoms that turn into bean pods.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Legumes kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo fɔfɔii hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant sap, which distorts the leaf as it tries to expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ.

english: What is the white dust on my garden egg leaves and why does it make them dry out?
ga: Mɛni ji sũ yɛŋ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔŋlooi ahe baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ?

english: That white dust is a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It acts like a blanket over the leaf, blocking sunlight and stealing nutrients until the leaf starves and turns crisp.
ga: Muji yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Efeɔ enii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa ni ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hɔmɔ yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water fills all the air pockets in the dirt, suffocating the roots. This damp, airless environment encourages fungal rot to attack the tubers before harvest.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ ayi obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ dani akpaa amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or when the soil dries out suddenly. The heat and water stress make the plant shed its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi trukaa. Dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to bear fruit when weeds grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni jwɛi miikwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizers from the upper soil before your plantain roots can absorb them, slowing down the plant's overall development.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani o-plantain shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How can I tell if my groundnuts are mature and ready to harvest if they grow underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa kɛji amɛmiida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts show maturity above ground when the leaves turn yellow and drop off. You can test a few pods: mature groundnuts will have dark brown or black markings on the inside lining of the shell.
ga: Peanuts daa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Obaanyɛ oka pods 2-3 okwɛ. Peanuts ni eda lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Leaving tall shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains protects the seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi. tsei ni kɛlɛ ni ashiɔ Aloo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source for crops. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves back their green color and helps form large corn ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua ni afee ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why is it better to push cassava stem cuttings into the soil at a slant rather than straight up or flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu lɛ ja loo ŋmei lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree angle helps roots grow deep into the soil to form big tubers, while keeping the sprouting buds near the surface so shoots can easily reach air and sunlight.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji digrii 45 lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tso ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la he oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and shrink during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips that feed on the plant juice during dry weather. These insects damage the leaves, causing them to wrinkle, stunt plant growth, and reduce fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ tsei amli nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ. kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa lɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry and unviable, preventing pollination. When a blossom fails to pollinate, the plant drops the flower to conserve energy and water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ gbɔfeemɔ. tsiɔ pollination naa Kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ amɛwo pollination. Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Is it good practice to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, legumes like beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize. In return, the tall maize stems provide support for climbing bean vines to rest on.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa lɛ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfiɔ wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhiɔ.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra small shoots growing out from the side of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Nu ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Removing extra side branches—often called suckers—stops the plant from wasting nutrients on leaves it doesn't need. This directs all the food and water straight into growing larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ—ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ suckers lɛ—haa tso lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baatsɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ kɛya aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does maize grown from last year's saved harvest produce smaller cobs than seed bought from the agricultural store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ajie yɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii fe ŋmãa ni aheɔ yɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ?

english: Commercial seeds are often high-yielding hybrids specifically bred for vigor. Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose those special qualities in the next generation, producing smaller stalks and lighter cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jarayeli dumɔwui ji dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akwɛɔ amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni waaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are exceptionally tough and can sit hidden in dry soil for long periods waiting for rain. Because they are native and highly adaptable, they sprout immediately and compete with your young crops for light, water, and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ, ni amɛmɛ nugbɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eji tso ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli, ni enyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛkɛ otsei bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly in the barn if I dig them up right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mifo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Digging yams in wet soil causes wet dirt to cling to the skin and makes the tuber soft and susceptible to cuts. Fungi and rot bacteria thrive in damp conditions and easily enter any bruised skin on the yam during storage.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes wo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha muji ni mli efɔ lɛ akpɛtɛ hewolo lɛ he. ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛji afo lɛ Fungus kɛ bacteria ni fiteɔ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli. ni eboteɔ sweet potato hewolo ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ mli oya yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: The first rain is often a 'false rain' followed by a hot dry spell. If you plant immediately, the young seeds will sprout but then dry up and die in the hot soil before the continuous rainy season actually begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale nugbɔ’ ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of stay dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that your soil is lacking nitrogen. Nitrogen acts as the main food that gives plants their green color and energy; without it, the plant steals green energy from old leaves to keep new leaves alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, tsei juɔ hewalɛ ni ji eŋɔli kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛkwɛ eheei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to grow groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikpa ŋmãa?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Growing them feeds the soil naturally so your next maize crop has free food to grow strong.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛdumɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, o-maise ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the small stems growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Those small stems, called suckers, compete with the main tree for food, light, and water. By cutting most of them away and leaving only one or two, all the soil food goes into making one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tsei bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Amɛkɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, la, kɛ nu. Kɛtsɔ amɛteŋ babaoo ni afolɔ mli ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ nɔ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ atsɔ plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the heavy tuber growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp wet ground where they might rot and ensures they catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akatara hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ, ni ebaaha amɛná hulu la babaoo.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding deep inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ etee amɛhe amɛwo mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. They target the tender inner leaves of young maize because the tissues are soft and rich in moisture, which can destroy the growing point of the plant if left untreated.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni amɛtuɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ ŋmãa bibii amli baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, fãji lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ afite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant juices, or passing a virus to the plant as they feed.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ haa tsei beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep falling to the ground instead of growing into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or when tiny insects attack the delicate flower stems before tiny midges can pollinate them.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ba tso lɛ nɔ. Etutuaa fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani bibii lɛ. lɛ baanyɛ afee pollination

english: Why are my tomatoes developing dark, sunken rotten spots on the bottom side of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni ebote aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil doesn't have enough calcium or when watering is uneven, preventing the plant from building solid skin at the bottom of the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nu woɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Etsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafee hewolo ni wa yɛ aduawai lɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before it is even time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani be po shɛɔ ni abaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them in heavy soil without draining away. Excess water suffocates the roots, allowing soil fungi to enter and turn the tubers soft and watery.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stay small even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii beni nugbɔ enɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn deep green and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on the land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after maize restores nutrients to the farm without buying expensive fertilizers and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do seeds need to be planted at a specific depth instead of just being scattered on top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ko ni mli kwɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds planted at the right depth stay moist and cool enough to germinate successfully. It also protects them from being eaten by birds or dried out by direct sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ni sa lɛ baahi shi ni edɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ebuɔ amɛhe hu koni okpoi akaye amɛ loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akagbi amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants curl their leaves and stop growing during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛkpaa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to cut down on water loss when the weather is extremely hot and dry. Providing temporary shade and watering them at the base helps them recover.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waa.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and top-heavy fruit bunches. Supporting them with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles prevents the trees from snapping or uprooting in high winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishifã yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, and the lower main stem turns thick and woody, typically between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ mli tso titri lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei Enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruits start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when extreme heat or inconsistent watering stresses the plant, preventing successful pollination from taking place.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Etsiɔ pollination naa koni ekaye omanye.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in wet, shaded environments. Pruning dense tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the canopy and reduce fungal growth.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo. Tso niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli gĩɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when the soil stays wet for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and making it easy for rot-causing fungi to destroy the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akɛ amɛbaafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my farm reduce the yield of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, leaving your plants weak and reducing the size and quantity of your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onibii ni okpaa lɛ dalɛ kɛ bɔ ni ebɔi babaoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt during the hot afternoon heat even when the soil is still moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: In the hot sun, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, but usually bounces back by evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often a sign of virus infection spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or a reaction to extreme heat and uneven watering. Stressed leaves roll up to reduce water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ mli baa ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa, loo nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Akɛ baai ni haoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and underground water. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow thicker roots and bigger tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ wuji.

english: Maize continuously drains the same specific nutrients, especially nitrogen, from the ground. Planting the same crop over and over also allows soil pests and diseases that feed on maize to multiply in that spot.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be. Titri lɛ, nitrogen, ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa kɛ helai babaoo yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapted to survive in harsh conditions. They absorb water, fertilizer, and sunlight much faster than domesticated crops, which is why they easily choke out young plants if not cleared.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni amɛfoɔ tsei bibii amli mlɛo kɛji ajieee amɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, dry soil, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɛ́ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava plants have long green stems above ground, but the tubers underneath are tiny and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard and compacted, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves and stems rather than storing food underground to swell the tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi konɛ e ha nɛ ngmami ɔmɛ nɛ a bli.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my high-yielding hybrid maize produce a poor harvest when I plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai beni midu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from two special parent plants to give a high yield only for the first generation. The seeds harvested from that crop lose those special strength traits and produce uneven, weaker crops.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei krɛdɛɛi enyɔ ni ji nyɛmɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai hewalɛ krɛdɛɛi lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa, ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my stored cowpea beans develop small holes and turn to dust after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔɔ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Those holes are caused by bean weevils. The insects often lay invisible eggs on the crop in the field, and after harvest, the eggs hatch inside the stored bag into tiny worms that eat the insides of the beans.
ga: Bean ŋmeii ji mɛi ni kɛ nakai bu lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii woɔ wuji ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ. kɛ beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotokui amli he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why am I seeing tiny dark spots on both the leaves and flowers of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ? Tomato tso lɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ

english: Spots on leaves and flowers are usually signs of fungal or bacterial diseases like leaf spot or blight, which spread easily through water droplets, warm temperatures, and high air humidity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hetsemɔ yɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ ji ŋmei loo muawai hela he okadi, tamɔ baa he hela loo ŋmei. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nui ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli

english: Why do spots appear on the exact parts of the plant where flowers are about to come out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ tso lɛ fãi ni fɔfɔii lɛ miiba lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Emerging flower sites are soft, moist, and rich in nutrients, making them easy targets for fungal spores and insects to attack before the flower even opens.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni miida lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ fungal spores kɛ kooloi bibii baatutua lɛ dani fɔfɔi lɛ afɔlɔ.

english: What should I do if a disease is spreading from the leaves to the new blossoms of my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji hela lɛ gbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fɔfɔi heei lɛ anɔ?

english: You need to apply an appropriate treatment directly to both the affected leaves and the stem areas where flowers are emerging to halt the disease before it destroys your yield.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni sa lɛ awo baai ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishi he ni fɔfɔi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni hela lɛ akpa dani efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Where exactly should I apply liquid crop medicine when my plant starts showing spots?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ nu mli tsei ahe tsofa atsu nii kɛ́ mitsei lɛ je shishi amɛná ŋmɔtɔ?

english: You should apply the medicine directly on the spotted areas, the emerging flower spots, and neighboring healthy leaves to create a complete protective barrier against the disease.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ awo he ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ ni jeɔ kpo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ni yeɔ emuu kɛjɛɔ helai ahe.

english: Is it safe to spray crop medicine directly on the areas where flowers are coming out?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ he ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, treating the stem areas where flowers emerge is critical to protect young buds, provided you apply the recommended treatment gently and according to instructions.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso lɛ he ni fɔfɔi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ tsamɔ he miihia koni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe. Esa akɛ okɛ helatsamɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ atsu nii blɛoo kɛ bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spray healthy leaves that are right next to diseased ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ awo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fungal spores are often invisible and move to neighboring leaves before visible spots appear, so spraying nearby healthy parts prevents the infection from expanding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, anaaa fungal spores lɛ ni amɛyaa baai ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ dani amɛnáa ŋmeii ni anaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ hei ni bɛŋkɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Does spraying only the tops of the leaves protect the whole plant from leaf spots?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ pɛ lɛ baabu tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he kɛjɛ baai lɛ ahe?

english: No, because disease spores hide on the undersides of leaves, surrounding stems, and flower bases, requiring full coverage across all neighboring parts for effective control.
ga: Dabi, akɛni helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi, tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishi hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aha he fɛɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ koni anyɛ akudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to rush when spraying medicine on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikafee oya kɛmiifɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Rushing leads to uneven coverage and missed spots—especially around hidden flower buds and leaf joints—which leaves the plant vulnerable and wastes your chemicals.
ga: Oyaiyeli kɛ coverage ni ejaaa kɛ spots ni elaaje baa. Titri lɛ, yɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efiteɔ tsofai.

english: Why does spraying crop medicine properly take so much time on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani anyɛɔ ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Thorough disease control requires carefully targeting specific plant parts like flower sites and surrounding leaves rather than quick, blanket spraying, which naturally takes dedicated time.
ga: Helai anɔkwɛmɔ fitsofitso biɔ ni akwɛ hei srɔtoi anɔ. ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ fɔfɔi kɛ baai ni ebɔle he lɛ Yɛ oyaiyeli, blanket spray najiaŋ. Nɔ ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ heɔ be.

english: How can I protect my crop's flowers before they even open up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fɔfɔi lɛ ahe dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Inspect the stem joints where flower buds will emerge and carefully apply preventive treatment to those specific spots early to shield them before diseases attack.
ga: Kwɛmɔ stem joint lɛ he ni bud lɛ baaje kpo yɛ lɛ. ni okɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nakai hei pɔtɛɛi lɛ amli mra. Koni atsĩ hela naa dani etutua mɔ

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and lose water quickly. Shade trees protect young cocoa from harsh heat, keep the soil moist, and create a cooler microclimate that helps the seedlings survive and grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ni yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara waa.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and cool, damp air. When heavy rains keep the farm constantly wet and dense tree foliage blocks airflow, the fungus spreads quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɔ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be. Ni tsei ahe baai ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Fuji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient. The plant automatically moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newest top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baajie nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Heavy rains will wash the fertilizer away into streams or wash it too deep into the soil where plant roots cannot reach it. Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is lightly moist so the roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa faai amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same patch of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize consumes specific nutrients from the topsoil every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same place exhausts those specific nutrients, while pests and soil diseases build up in that spot to attack future crops.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii daa be. Kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai be lɛ mli koni amɛtutua wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed. If the tree is stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of tiny insects to pollinate the flowers, it drops the flowers to save its energy.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does cutting off healthy branches from my cocoa tree actually help it produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess branches that block sunlight and drain nutrients away from the main stem. Opening up the tree canopy allows light and air to reach the trunk where pods grow, reducing fungal disease and encouraging fruit development.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni tsiɔ hulu la naa lɛ ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbele tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aba shi ni eha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce low yields when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni yibiiwoo lɛ faaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough resources to grow thick stems and heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are just growing on the ground next to them?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. They also hide dangerous insect pests and diseases that can jump onto your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Ekɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ helai ni baanyɛ atswa onibii titri lɛ anɔ lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Why do I need to wait for the steady rains to start before planting my cassava cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ lɛ ni ebɔi nɛmɔ daa koni manyɛ madu ŋmei niji lɛ?

english: Cassava stems need continuous soil moisture during their first few weeks to sprout roots and fresh green shoots. If planted in dry soil, the stem cuttings dry out and die before root growth begins.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli koni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Niji lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani shishifãi lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that shade the cocoa seedlings and keep the soil moist while the trees are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lolo lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to grow strong leaves, so feeding the soil with manure or compost early helps keep leaves green and cobs full.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni ŋmei lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I plant cassava stems at an angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni adu amɛ shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slight angle spreads the underground buds evenly, allowing roots to grow smoothly in different directions so you get more and larger cassava tubers.
ga: Yucca niji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ jaa pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi. Bɔni afee ni oná ŋmei shishifãi babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die during the daytime even when I water them well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil germ that blocks water from moving up inside the stem. Rotating your tomato crops with maize or cassava helps clean the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaya ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ mli. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ.

english: Yam leaves need lots of sunlight to produce food for growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground to get maximum sun and prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves. Protecting the crop early with neem leaf oil or recommended sprays stops this damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni abuɔ he mra Kɛtsɔ neem baa mli fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akpa nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small shoots growing around my plantain trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nɔ ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantains lɛ ahe lɛ eje kpo.

english: Too many small shoots steal water and food from the main plantain trunk. Keeping only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main plant grows big bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akwɛ plantains babaoo.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers fall off without making pods when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash pollen out of the open blossoms before insects can pollinate them, causing the flowers to drop without forming pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi amli muji lɛ ahe dani kooloi bibii baanyɛ afee amɛ muji. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Groundnuts are mature when the leaves start turning yellow and dry, and when you crack open a test pod, the inside lining has turned dark brown instead of white.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ogbele kaa pod lɛ Mligbɛ tsɔne lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my young oil palm trees make flowers that drop off without growing fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee aduawai akui lɛ?

english: Young oil palms often produce male flowers first to build strength before bearing fruit, and they need helpful insects like tiny pollinating weevils to turn female flowers into fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ dani amɛwo yibii. Ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii bibii ni haa ŋmeii shwieɔ shi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni ekɛtsake fɔfɔi yei lɛ ewo aduawai akui amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up during the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains around them provides critical shade and retains soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or mites hiding on the undersides of the leaves. Spraying early with natural neem oil or appropriate organic insecticides helps clear them and stops leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Ebaaye ebua ni efɔ he ni ekpa baai lɛ afitemɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba emuuyeli mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my maize yield getting smaller every year even though I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil year after year drains specific nutrients and encourages persistent soil pests. Rotating maize with legume crops like groundnuts or cowpeas recharges the soil with fresh nitrogen and restores yield size.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ekoŋŋ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps the soil cool, slows down weed growth, and slowly decomposes to feed the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ oya Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa jwɛi lɛ daalɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants face extreme heat stress or sudden dry conditions, which prevents proper pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular morning watering helps flowers stay attached and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa leebi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo tomato.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall, thin, and fall over easily when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, individual plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each stalk enough room to grow thick, stable roots and sturdy stems.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ehe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shikpɔŋ kɛha mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight to produce energy for heavy tuber growth under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp dirt, catching maximum sunlight and preventing leafy diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ muji ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli. Egbalaa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa helai anaa

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground when heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rain water pools around them without proper drainage, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows extra water to drain away freely and prevents tuber rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo ni ebɔle amɛhe ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Can I use water straight from a nearby river or stream to irrigate my vegetable farm during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa loo faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ awo mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Using river water for irrigation works well during dry seasons, but the water must be clean from industrial pollutants or mining runoff. Clean water keeps crops safe to eat and prevents harmful chemical buildups in your farm soil.
ga: Faa mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shi esa akɛ nu lɛ mli atse kɛjɛ nitsumɔhei amli mujiwoo loo nu ni jɛɔ shika tsuru jɛɛhei amli lɛ mli. Nu ni mli tse haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ. ni otsi tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni abua naa yɛ sũ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why should I buy my crop seedlings from certified places like the Kade Research Centre instead of standard market vendors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe tsei ahe dumɔwui kɛjɛ he ko ni aŋmɛ gbɛ tamɔ Kade Research Centre lɛ? Yɛ jara nɔ nihɔɔlɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Certified research centers produce disease-resistant, high-yielding seedlings bred specifically for local soil and weather conditions, whereas uncertified seedlings may carry hidden diseases or yield poorly.
ga: Nibii amlitaomɔ hei ni aŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ feɔ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni anaaa he odaseyeli lɛ baanyɛ aná helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo amɛwooo yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if a young seedling is healthy enough to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A healthy seedling has dark green leaves, a strong upright stem, well-developed roots without rot or foul odor, and no visible dark spots, holes, or insects.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Tso lɛ damɔ shi ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Shishifãi ni edara jogbaŋŋ ni fitemɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo bɛ mli. Ni ŋmeii diji, bu loo kooloi bibii ni anaa lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to regularly walk around and inspect every part of my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafã kɛya he kroko lɛ? ni okwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã fɛɛ fã daa

english: Regular farm walks allow you to catch pest invasions and plant diseases early when they are still small, making them cheaper and easier to treat before they destroy the whole farm.
ga: Okwaafoi amli nyiɛmɔ daa baanyɛ aye abua bo ni omɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai mra. Beni amɛji bibii lɛ Enɛ haa ejara waaa ni ekwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani efiteɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What early signs should I look for to know if my crops are getting a disease?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ makwɛ mra koni mana kɛji hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Watch out for unusual yellowing or dark spots on leaves, wilting stems when the soil is wet, stunted growth, or strange patches on the stems and leaves.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Tsoi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo okadii ni ejaaa yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: If I notice a crop disease on just a few plants, why shouldn't I just leave those plants alone?
ga: Kɛji mina tso hela ko ni miiba tsei fioo komɛi pɛ anɔ lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ nakai tsei lɛ?

english: Plant diseases spread rapidly through wind, rain splashes, insects, and farming tools. Leaving sick plants in the field allows the disease to multiply and attack your healthy crops.
ga: Tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ okwaayeli nibii anɔ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni etutua onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do plant diseases seem to spread much faster during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rain splash carries disease germs from the soil up onto leaves, and high humidity creates warm, moist conditions where fungi and bacteria thrive and multiply quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ nu hiɛɔ helatsɛmɛi kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ. ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo baa. he ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daa ni amɛshwereɔ oya lɛ

english: If I spray medicine to treat a crop disease, why do I need to treat the nearby healthy plants as well?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa shwie nɔ koni mikɛtsa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ anɔ?
