english: Nearby plants may already be infected with the disease even if they are not showing symptoms yet. Treating the whole area prevents the disease from hiding and returning later.
ga: Ekolɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ená hela lɛ momo kɛji amɛjieee hela lɛ he okadii lɛ akpo lolo po. Kɛ́ atsa he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekatee ehe ni eku esɛɛ eba sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are some seedlings I planted growing fast while others planted at the same time remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi daa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni miduɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Growth differences happen due to variations in seedling seed quality, root damage during planting, uneven soil nutrients, or tall weeds blocking sunlight from reaching smaller plants.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dalɛ mli lɛ baa yɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ahewɔ. Shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ dumɔ be mli Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyaaa nɔ ekome. Aloo jwɛi kakadaji tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tsei bibii ahe.

english: Why do my newly planted seedlings dry up and die even when there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: This is often caused by transplant shock—if roots are damaged during planting or if air pockets are left around the root ball, the plant cannot absorb soil water properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ loo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does clearing weeds around my young crops help protect them from getting sick?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hela he?

english: Weeds trap excess moisture, block sunlight and airflow, and host harmful insects that carry plant diseases. Clearing weeds keeps crops dry, sunny, and strong enough to resist diseases.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni fa fe nine. Etsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa, ni eji he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ tsei ahe helai baa lɛ ahiɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbiɔ, hulu tsoɔ, ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tight like pencils when the afternoon sun becomes intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pɛnsil yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water through transpiration. Shrinking the exposed leaf area helps the plant hold onto its internal moisture until the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite kɛtsɔ la ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie he ni baai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ kpo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ haa edɔɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants turning yellow and drooping after heavy water pooled in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ nu afua ni naa wa ni ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits on a farm for too long, it drowns the roots by blocking oxygen in the soil. Without oxygen, the roots rot and cannot draw up food, causing the leaves to turn yellow and wilt.
ga: Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛto niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before developing into peppers during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When plants face water shortages, they drop their flowers to save energy and water for keeping the main stem and leaves alive rather than spending resources on producing fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ nu ni faaa kpeɔ Amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ahi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii koni ekɛwo yibii

english: Why do my green bell peppers develop dark, soft sunken spots at the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers eŋɔli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: This issue is caused by uneven watering, which stops the plant from absorbing calcium properly. Maintaining steady moisture in the soil helps the plant build strong, healthy fruit skins.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni aaakwɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ahewolo ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava farm produce very bushy leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli baa jwɛi babaoo shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When there is too much nitrogen in the soil, cassava puts all its energy into growing big branches and foliage above ground instead of sending nutrients below to expand the tubers.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei niji kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye níhi kɛ yaa sisi konɛ e ha nɛ ngmlɛfia ɔmɛ a mi nɛ wa.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young maize plants turn purple early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ purple yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize are a sign that the plant is struggling to absorb phosphorus, usually because the roots are still small or the ground is overly wet. As roots expand, the green color typically returns.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eŋɔ fɔsfɔs. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ darako loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ mli gbala lɛ, Green kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my okra plants keep growing very tall like trees but stop flowering and producing fresh pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi gumbo lɛ miiya hiɛ tamɔ tso lɛ? Shi ekpa fɔfɔii ni ewo fɔfɔi heei.

english: Okra plants slow down pod production if old pods are left to over-ripen on the stalk. Harvesting pods frequently while they are young encourages the plant to continuously produce new flowers and pods.
ga: Gumbo tsei lɛ baaha pod feemɔ aya hiɛ kɛji akɛ ashi pod momo ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Pods ni akpaa shii abɔ Beni eji gbekɛ lɛ, ekanyaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ pods heei. daa

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and turn brown after cutting down the surrounding tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mifo tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, shielding fragile cocoa leaves from intense heat and preserving essential humidity around the plants.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni eha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ ahi tso lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain shoots produce small bunches when I leave all the suckers growing together on one root?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ amli fãa bibii bibii lɛ? Beni mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ekome yɛ shishifã kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow from the same stool, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Pruning down to three shoots of different ages ensures the main plant has enough food to grow large bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ ŋmeii kome mli lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni eye afii srɔtoi lɛ amli kɛtee ŋmeii etɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my yam vines wither and dry up long before the expected harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when soil moisture drops drastically or when pests damage the underground root system. Keeping the soil consistently moist and free from root pests allows the vines to stay green long enough for tubers to fully mature.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi kwraa loo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot tolerate direct sunlight or high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a protective canopy that reduces heat stress and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛitsu ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize requires heavy nutrients to grow, so adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsii he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get extremely high or when watering is irregular. Providing steady moisture and mulching the base of the plant helps lower soil temperature and keeps the blossoms intact.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo tso lɛ shishi daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa aba shi, ni ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slanting angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafee nɔ ni ja?

english: Slanting cassava stems allows the roots to spread outward near the surface where the soil is rich, producing larger, easier-to-harvest tubers while keeping the plant anchored against strong winds.
ga: Kasava tso ni etse lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ daraa ni ehaa ekpamɔ waaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, tso lɛ ni aaaha ehi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Yam vines produce energy through their leaves. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground so it gets maximum sunlight for bigger tuber growth while preventing leaf diseases caused by ground moisture.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ aha bulbs wuji ni miida lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsei ahe helai ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas in the same field as my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This enriches the ground, providing free natural fertilizer that helps neighboring corn plants grow strong.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weed seeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akashɛ hulu la he koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I weed my farm right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ waa?

english: Weeding in wet mud damages crop roots, compacts the soggy soil, and spreads fungal diseases easily on wet leaves. It is best to wait until the surface soil dries out slightly.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ muji ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi. Ha shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi fioo.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes right in the center funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the growing point of maize. Catching them early and applying recommended neem extracts or insecticides in the center of the leaves protects your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa shweremɔ nɔ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are the bottoms of my sweet peppers turning black and rotten while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the growing fruit, often due to uneven watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady allows the plant to transport calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing on my cocoa trees instead of letting them grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ agbo lɛ

english: Cutting off extra shoots, or pruning, allows the tree to direct its energy and nutrients into growing healthy pods rather than wasting strength on useless leaves and unwanted branches.
ga: Afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ loo afolɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa kɛ tsei niji ni ataooo lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Is it okay to just leave my cocoa trees to grow naturally like trees in the forest without trimming them?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aha mi-cocoa tso lɛ ada yɛ adebɔɔ naa tamɔ tso ni yɔɔ koo mli ni akpaaa tso lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need active management. If left to grow wild without trimming, they grow too tall to harvest, produce fewer pods, and create dark, humid spaces where diseases thrive.
ga: Cocoa tsei biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ ashi amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni afolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ, Amɛbaakwɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpa. Ehaa pods fioo ni ehaa he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai shwereɔ yɛ.

english: How do I know which branches to cut off when I am pruning my young cocoa tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei niji ni esa akɛ mafo kɛji mifolɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: You should remove suckers growing at the base of the trunk, dead or diseased wood, and branches growing inward that prevent sunlight and fresh air from reaching the center of the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Tso ni egbo loo hela emɔ lɛ Ni tsei niji lɛ daa yɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa akashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa tree take before it starts producing good pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii kpakpai?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa trees usually start bearing their first pods between two to three years after planting if they are properly cared for, weeded, and protected from pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ teŋ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ajie jwɛi ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ,.

english: Why are the pods on my two-year-old cocoa trees very few and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pods ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso ni eye afii 2 lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa ni amɛhe ehiaaa tsɔ lɛ?

english: A two-year-old cocoa tree is still young and building its root system and main structure, so early yields are naturally small before full production begins around the third or fourth year.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eye afii enyɔ lɛ ji gbekɛbii lolo ni amɛto amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishitoo titri lɛ ama shi. No hewɔ lɛ, shishijee nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ji nɔ bibioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa dani eshɛɔ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ he yɛ afi ni ji etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ mli.

english: What should I do on my farm when I see sick or diseased cocoa pods on a tree?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ mina kookoo ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tsei anɔ?

english: You should carefully remove the diseased pods from the tree immediately and take them far away from the farm so the infection does not spread to healthy crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni okɛjie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why does cocoa disease spread so quickly from one tree to another on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many crop diseases are caused by tiny fungi or viruses that travel through wind, rain drops, or dirty farm tools, meaning one infected branch can easily spread sickness to neighboring trees.
ga: Fungi loo virus bibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai babaoo baa. ni tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔshiimɔi, loo okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso nine kome ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela lɛ ashwã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli oya.

english: Can I use the same cutlass I used to cut a sick cocoa tree on my healthy trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni mikɛfo cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ mitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: No, using the same tool can transfer disease spores directly into healthy wood; always clean and sanitize your tools after working on sick plants before moving to healthy ones.
ga: Dabi, dɛŋdadei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ajie helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ etsu nii lɛ, tsumɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ ahe ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ helai awo mli dani oya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Will my cocoa tree give me more pods if I let all its branches grow thick and bushy?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii babaoo kɛji miha eniji lɛ fee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: No, overly bushy trees shade themselves too much and trap moisture, which leads to fungal diseases like Black Pod; opening the canopy brings in sunlight that encourages pod growth.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tsɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba tsɔ ni amɛbaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baa; Kɛ́ agbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa lɛ, hulu la ni haa pod lɛ daa lɛ baa.

english: How can agricultural extension officers help me get better yields from my cocoa farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers provide practical training on proper pruning techniques, early disease detection, soil fertility, and correct chemical application to help maximize your harvest.
ga: Nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ tsɔsemɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii yɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpɛɔ tsei lɛ he hewalɛ. Helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anaa mra kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni anáa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow from the tip along the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green leafy growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps the plant produce food, turning the leaves green again so the crop can yield large ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Ha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ koni eha tso lɛ baai wuji.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer directly into the soil or spray liquid fertilizer on the leaves of my crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji nu baashwie mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Soil fertilizer feeds the roots for long-term growth, while spraying liquid fertilizer on leaves (foliar feeding) acts like a quick energy boost. Using leafy sprays works fastest when plants show sudden nutrient deficiencies or need quick support during flowering.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ niyenii koni amɛdara be kakadaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ (Feeding the leaves) lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli oya. Foliar spray tsuɔ nii oya fe fɛɛ kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli trukaa loo ehe miihia yelikɛbuamɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand properly underground. If the soil is hard, compacted, or rocky, the tubers struggle to push through and become twisted or stunted, which is why making high, soft mounds helps them grow long and straight.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni gɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves during the dry season, and are they dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fite yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli ni egbo lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves on purpose during dry weather to save water and protect themselves from harsh sun. They are not dead; their roots stay alive underground, and fresh green leaves will sprout as soon as the rains return.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ he. Amɛ gboko lolo. Eshishifãi lɛ kã shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant receives irregular water, or when it lacks nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the plant helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ faaa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. They stretch upward to reach the light instead of growing thick stems and big cobs, so giving them proper space produces healthier plants.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight, which scorches their tender leaves. Leaving selected shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool environment that protects them until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. ni haa baai bibii lɛ shãa Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil much faster than domesticated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from choking your crops and starving them of essential nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli oya fe shia tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛkajie niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ amɛdɛŋ.

english: Why do my crops turn pale green and rot at the stem after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When too much water stays on the farm, crop roots get waterlogged and cannot breathe, which causes roots and lower stems to rot. Digging small drainage paths allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping root zones healthy.
ga: Kɛ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ fiteɔ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ mli nubu bibioo ko ni atsaa lɛ Haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifã lɛ he lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Why do my harvested grains get moldy and infested with insects shortly after I put them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikpamɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ebɔle amɛhe beni mikɛwo baagi mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain trapped wetness inside them even if they feel dry on the outside. Drying them thoroughly under the hot sun reduces moisture so mold cannot grow and insects cannot easily multiply inside your storage bags.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni efo mli. Kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi po. Kɛ́ egbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii edaaa ni kooloi bibii nyɛŋ ashwere yɛ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo.

english: Is it safe to harvest and eat my cabbages immediately if I use non-chemical products on them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpãtã ni maye cabbage amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ko ni tsofa bɛ mli tsu nii yɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, non-chemical products are safe because they do not leave toxic residues on your cabbages or other vegetables, so you can harvest without dangerous health risks.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni tsofai bɛ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ amɛshiii nɔ ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɛ kaabɛji loo aduawai krokomɛi anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa ni helatsamɔ he oshara ko bɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, getting too much water, or suffering from root damage that stops it from feeding.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii he miihia tso lɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, ni enine eshɛ nu babaoo nɔ. aloo shishifãi efite ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ niyenii aha.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny instead of bushy when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔji beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they stretch upward to fight each other for sunlight, which makes their stems thin and weak instead of growing strong branches.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Eshɛɔ ehe koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ niji ni he wa.

english: How do weeds hurt my maize crops if they are just growing in the same dirt?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your maize, leaving your crops weak and starving.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi tsei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-abele lɛ. Ha onibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ aye bo.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop and sleep during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Under intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up, so they droop temporarily to save moisture.
ga: yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why does putting dry grass on the soil around my vegetables help them stay alive in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-vegetables lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Dry grass acts like an umbrella over the soil that stops the sun from evaporating water, keeping the soil cool and wet for the roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni tsiɔ nu ni hulu la lɛ shwieɔ lɛ naa koni ekahoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why are my garden egg flowers falling to the ground without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or when it lacks the essential food needed to support growing fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ akwɛɛɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ.

english: What causes holes in my cabbage leaves and will it stop the cabbage head from growing?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bulɛ baa mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli? Ni ani ebaatsi kaabe yitso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃?

english: Insects chew those holes to feed, which harms the leaves that the cabbage needs to capture sunlight and build a big, heavy head.
ga: Kplukai shwieɔ nakai bu lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ baai ni he hiaa ni kaabe lɛ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la lɛ awui, ni ehaa yitsei lɛ feɔ agboi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Hard soil stops tubers from swelling, and giving the plant too much leafy fertilizer forces it to grow big top leaves instead of sending energy to the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa baaha bulb lɛ akafu. Ni kɛ́ akɛ baai babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akwɛ̃ baai wuji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛya shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Will natural sprays burn my vegetable leaves if I apply too much by mistake?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baashã mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ kɛji mikɛtsu nii babaoo yɛ oshara mli?

english: Unlike harsh chemical pesticides, natural and non-chemical treatments are gentle on plants and generally will not scorch the leaves even if applied generously.
ga: Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsuɔ nii lɛ ahe. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa tsei ahe lɛ feɔ mlɛo yɛ tsei ahe. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaaa baai lɛ ashã kɛ akɛtsu nii babaoo po.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut down my cocoa trees when they get sick instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafo cocoa tso lɛ beni hela mɔ mi lɛ moŋ fe ni mawo mi tsofa lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Some diseases, like the swollen shoot virus, live deep inside the tree's sap where chemical sprays cannot reach. Removing infected trees is the only way to stop the virus from spreading through insects to the healthy trees on your farm.
ga: Helai komɛi, tamɔ bud swollen virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ kooloi bibii anɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: How do viruses actually get into my cocoa farm in the first place?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni hela ko bote mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ shishijee mli?

english: Viruses are carried into farms by tiny insects like mealybugs. These insects feed on infected plants elsewhere and then crawl or get carried by ants and wind to your healthy cocoa trees, passing the sickness along.
ga: Koolooi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs ji mɛi ni kɛ hela nɛɛ baa ŋmɔji amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ hei krokomɛi. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ loo ŋmeii baaŋɔ bo kɛya. ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa kookoo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ hela lɛ aha

english: Can I use chemical sprays to cure a cocoa tree that is already infected with a virus?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsa kookoo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ momo lɛ?

english: No, chemical sprays cannot cure a tree that already has a virus. Sprays can kill the insects that carry the virus, but an infected tree must be cut down to prevent it from infecting neighboring healthy plants.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsa tsei ni yɔɔ hela nɛɛ momo lɛ. Spray lɛ baanyɛ agbe koolooi ni hiɛ hela lɛ. Shi esa akɛ afolɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why are ants dangerous to my cocoa trees if they do not eat the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ awui kɛji amɛyeee baai lɛ?

english: Ants actively farm and protect tiny virus-carrying insects like mealybugs because the mealybugs produce a sweet liquid ants eat. By moving these mealybugs from tree to tree, ants accidentally spread crop diseases across your farm.
ga: Akpɔlɔi feɔ ŋmɔ ni amɛbuɔ kooloi bibii ni hiɛ helai, tamɔ mealybugs lɛ ahe, ejaakɛ mealybugs lɛ feɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni ŋmeii yeɔ. Kɛ́ ojie nɛkɛ mealybugs nɛɛ kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛtee ekroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baagbɛ tsei ahe helai ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: What does cocoa rehabilitation actually mean for a farm like mine?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kookoo ni anáa lɛ tsɔɔ kɛha ŋmɔji tamɔ minɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa rehabilitation means removing old, diseased, or unproductive cocoa trees from your land and replanting with fresh, healthy, disease-resistant seedlings so your farm can produce good yields again.
ga: Cocoa sɛɛkuu tsɔɔ kookoo tsei momo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. ni hela emɔ amɛ loo amɛwooo yibii kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni odu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ehee, ni wa, ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ. Koni oŋmɔ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ekoŋŋ

english: If I cut down a sick cocoa tree, can I leave the cut branches on the farm to rot?
ga: Kɛ mifo cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ Ani niji ni afo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbo?

english: No, cut branches from infected trees can still hold live insects like mealybugs that might crawl onto nearby healthy trees. You should collect, dry, and safely destroy infected branches away from your healthy crop.
ga: Dabi, niji ni afolɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ hu baanyɛ ahi kooloi bibii ni hiɛ ka, tamɔ mealybugs, ni baanyɛ atsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ obua tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anaa, ogbi, ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: How long after cutting down diseased cocoa trees must I wait before planting new seedlings?
ga: Kɛ́ mifo kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dumɔwui heei?

english: You should clear all diseased plant material and wait a few months to make sure all virus-carrying insects have left or died before planting new seedlings, ensuring the new plants start in clean soil.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei amli nibii fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni omɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ kooloi ni hiɛ hela lɛ fɛɛ eshi loo amɛgboi dani odu dumɔwui heei. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ajeɔ tsei heei shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ.

english: Has cocoa always been grown in Ghana, or where did it come from?
ga: Ani aduɔ kookoo yɛ Ghana be fɛɛ be loo nɛgbɛ ejɛ?

english: Cocoa is not native to Ghana; it was introduced from Central and South America in the late 19th century and became widely cultivated across the country around the 1930s.
ga: Cocoa jeee Ghana maŋ nɔ. Ajie kɛjɛ Central kɛ South America yɛ ohai 19 lɛ naagbee gbɛ ni adu yɛ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ 1930 afii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my neighbor's cocoa farm getting sick put my own farm at risk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miiye, ni ekɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo oshara mli lɛ?

english: Crop diseases and the insects that carry them do not respect farm boundaries. Insects carrying viruses can easily crawl across farm borders, be blown by the wind, or be moved on shared tools from your neighbor's farm to yours.
ga: Tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ ebuuu ŋmɔ mli husui. Kplukai ni hiɛ hela lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ husui lɛ anɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ atswa amɛ, loo amɛkɛ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ atsu nii kɛjɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli kɛya onɔ̃ lɛ mli.

english: Look out for swollen stems or roots, red veins on young leaves, yellow patterns on mature leaves, and small or deformed cocoa pods. These symptoms show that the virus is weakening the tree.
ga: Taomɔ tsei loo shishifãi ni efuu. line tsuji ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ Line tsuji ni yɔɔ baai wuji kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii loo ni bɛ su kpakpa nɔ. Okadii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela lɛ miigbɔjɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when exposed to full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their leaves lose water rapidly under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective cover that keeps the soil moist and shields the young trees from heat until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be ejaakɛ hulutsoo be lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ nu oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara waa.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato plants in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. Watering during the afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate before roots can absorb it, and hot wet conditions on leaves encourage fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually signals that your soil is running low on nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to maintain green leaves and produce large ears, so yellowing means the plant is starving for nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ toi wuji anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores nutrients to the soil without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: If cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots compete heavily underground for water and soil nutrients. This results in many small, thin roots instead of large, marketable cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo yɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to spread dry leaves and grass around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ashwie mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material (mulching) keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during dry days, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi (mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Ha nu lɛ mli shwiemɔ aba shi yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Should I allow all the new small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree to remain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii heei komɛi ni miida yɛ ehe lɛ? Ani mi plantain shishifãi lɛ yɛ lolo?

english: No, you should cut back extra shoots and leave only one or two healthy suckers. Allowing too many shoots to grow forces them to compete with the main plant for nutrients, leading to smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛkɛ tso ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra foliage and vertical shoots from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie baai krokomɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛjɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning unnecessary branches allows sunlight and airflow to pass through the tree canopy. Good ventilation reduces dampness that causes black pod disease and directs the tree's energy into growing pods instead of excess leaves.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ baatsu nii.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell. If you plant too early, the seeds may germinate and then die from lack of moisture before the regular rainy season fully begins.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni sa lɛ aje shishi kwraa.

english: I noticed small caterpillars eating holes in the leaves of my young maize; how does this affect my yield?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmeii bibii ni miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn baai lɛ amli. Te enɛ saa bɔ ni mitsuɔ nii ehaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Caterpillars like fall armyworm destroy leaf tissue, which reduces the plant's ability to capture sunlight and make food. If unchecked early, this damage prevents the crop from growing properly and drastically reduces your harvest.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ cutworms yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛfee niyenii lɛ baa shi. Kɛji akwɛɛɛ mra Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi waa.

english: How do I know if I am giving my crops too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo mihaaa mihe?

english: If your crop leaves turn yellow and drop off while the soil stays soggy, you are overwatering. If the leaves curl up, wilt, and feel dry during the hot sun, the crops need more water.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ooha nu babaoo. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi, amɛgboi, ni amɛnu he akɛ amɛgbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ he miihia nu babaoo.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land has good soil before I plant on it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa dani madu nii?

english: Good agricultural soil is usually dark in color, crumbly to touch, and retains moisture without turning into a sticky swamp after rain. Soil that supports wild green vegetation often has good nutrients for crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ ata he ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ kooi amli lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What can I put on the ground to keep my crops from drying out during hot days?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass, leaves, or straw—called mulching—keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly under the harsh sun.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo jwɛi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they use up all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil and die before their shoots reach the light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni eto lɛ ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni egbo dani ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ la lɛ he.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, leaving every plant weak and low-yielding.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni fa tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Is it good to split fertilizer application into two or three times instead of giving it all at once?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooja fɔmɔ nii amli awo mli enyɔ loo etɛ mli moŋ fe ni oooha fɛɛ shikome?

english: Yes, splitting fertilizer into smaller doses gives the crop nutrients right when it needs them at different growth stages and prevents heavy rain from washing all the fertilizer away at once.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ agbala ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli bibii bibii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni sa yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ fãi srɔtoi amli lɛ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ shikome.

english: Why should I trim or cut back some of the extra branches on my crops while they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi beni edaa lɛ?

english: Trimming excess or diseased leaves helps the plant focus its energy on growing healthy fruits rather than feeding useless leaves, and it allows fresh air to flow through the crop.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha folier niyenii ni sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under full sunlight. Planting plantain trees alongside them provides living shade that keeps the cocoa seedlings cool and moist until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Kakao jwɛi lɛ baaha kokoo dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a cry for help indicating that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that excessive water around the roots is choking the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu babaoo ebɔle he. Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops stay small and fail to bear fruit even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛwooo yibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Rain provides water, but plants also need rich soil nutrients to build stems and fruit. If your soil is exhausted or overcrowded with weeds, plants remain stunted despite good rainfall.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu taoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ koni amɛfee tsei kɛ aduawai. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ fite loo oyɛ jwɛi babaoo Tsei lɛ baakã he ahi shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do buyers stop buying my produce when the heavy rains start in July and August?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpaɔ minibii lɛ ahemɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ July kɛ August mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains make rural roads difficult to travel, while high humidity causes harvested crops to rot quickly. Buyers avoid purchasing during these peak wet months to prevent losing money on spoiled goods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa akrowa gbɛjegbɛi anɔ nyiɛmɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya. Nihɔɔlɔi tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nihɔɔmɔ he yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɛɛ amli koni amɛkafite shika kɛjɛ nibii ni efite mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil so fast during the peak rainy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Excess rain prevents harvested grains from drying properly in the sun. High moisture levels encourage mold, fungi, and dampness, which quickly destroy crop quality before it reaches the market.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baatsi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ, ni no fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya dani amɛyaa jara nɔ.

english: How does the early rainy season in June affect market demand for my produce?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be ni jeɔ shishi yɛ June mli lɛ saa jarayeli nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: In June, rains are usually manageable, allowing produce to stay relatively dry and accessible. Buyers are eager to stock up as fresh crops enter the market before torrential downpours begin.
ga: yɛ June mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, anyɛɔ atsuɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ he nii. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ he. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miisumɔ waa ni amɛkɛ nibii heei ni amɛwo lɛ ato jara nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do traders prefer buying farm produce in September after the heaviest rains pass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi sumɔɔ ni amɛhe nibii ni amɛdu yɛ September mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fe fɛɛ lɛ eho lɛ?

english: By September, the heaviest rains slow down, drying conditions improve, and transport roads become safer. This reduces crop spoilage risks, making traders more confident to buy in bulk.
ga: Beni shɛɔ September Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa shi. Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ etee hiɛ ni gbɛjegbɛi ni akɛyaa jɛmɛ lɛ hu yɛ shweshweeshwe Enɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa jarayelɔi náa hekɛnɔfɔɔ babaoo yɛ nibii wuji ahemɔ mli.

english: Why do market buyers settle down and buy more predictable amounts of crops in September?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ mli yɛ September mli lɛ?

english: In September, weather conditions stabilize, crop moisture levels drop, and road transport becomes reliable again, allowing market prices and buyer demand to settle into a consistent routine.
ga: yɛ September mli Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tse. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ eba shi. ni gbɛjegbɛ nɔ gbɛfaa ebafee nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jarayeli jara kɛ nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yaa nɔ daa nɔ.

english: What happens to my produce if I store it while it is still wet from the rain?
ga: Mɛni baaba minibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛto be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Storing wet produce creates a warm, humid environment inside bags or storerooms. This invites destructive fungi, mold, and rot that can ruin your entire stored harvest within a few days.
ga: Nibii ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ baa kotoku lɛ mli loo nitoohe lɛ mli. Enɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ akpata onibii fɛɛ ni okɛto lɛ ahiɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ nine.

english: When is the best time during the rainy season to harvest my crops so buyers will accept them?
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baakpɛlɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to harvest during lighter rainfall periods like June or early September when crops can be sun-dried or transported without being soaked, ensuring better quality for buyers.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo, tamɔ June loo September shishijee mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni abaanyɛ agbi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo akɛwo he kroko ni akɛwooo nu mli. Koni aha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aná nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ

english: Why is it harder to sell my cassava tubers during the peak wet months of July and August?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ waa ni ji July-August lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil causes cassava roots to absorb too much water, reducing their starch content and causing them to rot faster after harvest, which deters market buyers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Ni ajieɔ ashikiŋsha lɛ nɔ ni ehaa fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. ni ji gbɛtsii nii ko kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ

english: How can heavy mid-year rainfall ruin the quality of my fruits and vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ afi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baafite mi aduawai kɛ mi aduawai lɛ?

english: Excess water causes vegetables to become soft and prone to fungal decay, while fruits can split open on the stem. Damaged produce rots fast and is rejected by market traders.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha aduawai afee blɛoo ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ baanyɛ agbala yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Nibii ni efite lɛ fiteɔ oya ni jarayelɔi kpooɔ amɛ.

english: Why do market prices drop heavily when many farmers harvest vegetables during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli jara baa shi waa nɛkɛ beni okwaafoi babaoo kpaa aduawai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Abundant rain causes many crops to mature at once. Since wet crops spoil quickly, farmers rush to sell them all at the same time, creating an oversupply that drives prices down.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa dumɔ nii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ shikome. Ejaakɛ tsei ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya. Okwaafoi kɛ oyaiyeli hɔ̃ɔ amɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa fe nine yɛ jara lɛ nɔ, ni no haa nibii ajara baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to build dirt mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shikpɔŋ gɔŋ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil to expand and grow long and thick. Raised mounds keep the soil loose, allow tubers to expand easily, and stop heavy rains from soaking the soil until the roots rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara ni amɛdara ni amɛfee shwiili. Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee mlɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa yitso lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baagboi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow when the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ yɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. This often happens when weeds take all the soil nutrients or when heavy rain washes nutrients away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ gbala niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves. When they feed on the leaf, it twists up and stops the plant from making food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ amɛye baai lɛ Etsiɔ ehe ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot and dry or when the soil lacks moisture. Without enough water and cool weather, the flower cannot form seeds, so the plant drops it to save water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ Kɛji nu bɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ, afɔseɔ tsei anɔ nu koni nu akafite.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over during windstorms even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum be mli eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the top of the dirt rather than going deep into the ground. When heavy fruit bunches grow on top, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs support poles so wind does not uproot it.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akui ni tsii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Tsei lɛ tsii yɛ amɛyiteŋ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei akwɛ amɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akajie amɛ.

english: Is it helpful to plant beans in the same field where I plant my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize helps both crops. Beans naturally take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, feeding the maize while covering the ground to prevent weeds.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my soil work better than burning the bush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni akɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hi fe jwɛi lɛ ni ashãa dani aduɔ lɛ?

english: Burning bush gives a quick burst of ash nutrients, but it wears off fast and burns away organic dirt. Animal manure stays in the dirt longer, holds moisture like a sponge, and feeds your crops throughout the season.
ga: Tsoi ni ashã lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya. Shi efiteɔ oya ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli muji. Koolooi ashishifã baahi sũ lɛ mli be babaoo. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tamɔ sponji ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to crack from the roots expanding underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa kɛmiijɛ shishifãi ni miigbɛ eshwa yɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small green pods during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Yibɔi babaoo yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: The dry Harmattan wind steals water from the trees rapidly. Cocoa trees intentionally drop their smallest pods to conserve precious water so the whole tree does not dry up and die.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ juɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli oya. Cacao tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu ni jara wa lɛ he. Koni kookoo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ akagbi ni egbo.

english: Why is it better for me to raise my crop seeds in a nursery before moving them to my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery protects delicate young seeds from harsh sunlight, heavy rain, and soil pests when they are at their weakest stage. Raising them in a small, controlled area allows you to give them extra care so that only the strongest and healthiest seedlings are selected to be planted in your main farm.
ga: Nursery lɛ buɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ amɛhe gbeyei fe fɛɛ lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ otsɔse amɛ yɛ he bibioo ko ni akudɔɔ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Koni ohala dumɔwui ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ pɛ ni obaadu yɛ oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to move my crop seedlings from the nursery to my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to move seedlings late in the afternoon or on a cloudy day. Transplanting when the hot afternoon sun has passed gives the young plants the cool night air to settle into the new soil without losing too much water and wilting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ eho. Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ hee nɔ ni nu babaoo elaaje amɛ ni ehaaa amɛgboi.

english: How can I protect my newly planted crop seedlings from wilting under the strong sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu tso dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbo yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi?

english: You can provide temporary shade for your fresh seedlings using palm fronds or small leafy branches inserted into the ground next to them. Covering the soil around the stem with dry grass or leaves also keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha dumɔwui heei lɛ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei bibii loo tsei aniji ni okɛaawo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ Stems lɛ he lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my crops instead of planting as many seeds as possible close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni da yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, du dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni ooonyɛ.

english: Crops need enough space so their roots can spread out to find water and nutrients, and their leaves can get sunlight. When planted too close together, crops fight each other for survival, resulting in thin plants and very low harvest yields.
ga: He ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he hiaa tsei bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ agbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. ni baai lɛ hu baaná hulu la Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu amɛhe koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen, an important plant nutrient, or that excessive water in the soil is suffocating the roots. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if I am giving my crop seedlings too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo miiha mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: If seedlings get too much water, their leaves will start turning yellow and feel soft or droopy, and the soil around them will stay soggy for days. Healthy plant roots need air as well as water, so waterlogged soil causes the roots to rot and the plant to stunt.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Ebaai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni enu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo loo ebaagbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ gbii babaoo Tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni tsei lɛ hu agbɔjɔ.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are commonly caused by small insects like whiteflies that carry diseases between plants while feeding on the sap. Removing infected plants early helps prevent these insects from spreading the sickness to your healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni kɛ helai baa tsei ateŋ be mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akagbɛ hela amɛshwã onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantains planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni dumɔwu ko akwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide broad leaf shade that acts like an umbrella, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do farmers plant fast-growing crops like maize together with slow-growing crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa kɛfataa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Combining these crops allows you to make full use of your land. The maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving space and sunlight for the slow-growing cassava to spread out and mature later in the season.
ga: Nibii nɛɛ ni okɛaafata he lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ hulu la baa koni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni eda kwraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the best seeds from my harvest to save and plant for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli koni mikɛto ni madu kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Always pick seeds from your healthiest, strongest plants that produced large, disease-free fruits or pods. Avoid small, wrinkled, or insect-damaged seeds, as healthy parent plants pass their strength on to the next generation of crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ahala dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni woɔ yibii loo ŋmeii wuji ni hela bɛ mli lɛ amli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui bibii, ni egbɔjɔ, loo ni kooloi efite lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ni ji nyɛ ni he wa lɛ baaha ehewalɛ lɛ aha tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa saplings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa lolo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, a main food source maize needs to stay green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What causes small worms to eat holes in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye bu yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli?

english: These worms are often Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the tender growing parts of maize leaves. Checking your field early and applying recommended natural sprays like neem extract can help control them before they cause heavy damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baa ni miida lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ atsu nii. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ dani ekɛ naagbai ni mli wa aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water starves cassava roots of air and encourages soil fungi to attack them. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua amɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans absorb nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. This naturally enriches the land and helps neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ, tamɔ abele, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight on their leaves to make food for the underground tuber. Staking keeps the leaves high in the light and off damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa mli, ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plants do not get consistent water. Keeping the soil evenly watered and mulched with dry grass helps protect the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing pale green spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with light green or yellow patterns are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent this issue.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Amɛji mɛi ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if the ground has enough rain for me to safely sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui shweshweeshwe?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball; if it holds together easily without dripping water or crumbling like dry dust, the soil has enough moisture for seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he mlɛo lɛ, nɔ ko bɛ ni shwieɔ shi loo nɔ ni shwieɔ shi tamɔ sũ ni egbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller yields even when the sun is bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and moisture they need to produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade, protecting young cocoa plants and keeping soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Staking holds yam leaves up toward the sunlight so the plant can make more food, which results in larger tubers growing underground.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔmɔɔ sweet potato baai lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ hulu la lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient for growth. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure will restore green leaves and improve crop yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots, acts as natural fertilizer for crops planted beside or after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi. loo no sɛɛ

english: Why shouldn't I burn the brush on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa miŋmɔ mli jwɛi lɛ dani miduɔ nii?

english: Burning kills good organisms and burns away dark organic matter in the topsoil. Letting cleared grass rot into mulch enriches the soil and retains moisture.
ga: Shãa gbeɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshãa nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ ni yɔɔ diŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni he tse lɛ fite akɛ mulch lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and cracks appear in the soil around the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without making peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni efiteee pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when plants experience stress from irregular watering, extreme heat, or pest damage, preventing the plant from setting fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ amli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: What is eating holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying neem oil or approved insecticides early into the center of the leaves helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Baai lɛ ateŋ shishigbɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp conditions. Pruning shaded branches allows sunlight and airflow to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Shady pruning haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops in the early morning or the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering in the early morning is best because the soil absorbs moisture before heat causes evaporation, and wet leaves dry quickly to prevent fungal rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ baagbi oya koni ŋmeii akafite.

english: How can I get a large harvest if I only have a small piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nikpamɔ babaoo kɛji shikpɔŋ fioo ko pɛ miyɔɔ?

english: You can harvest a lot from a small plot by using proper plant spacing, planting high-yielding seed varieties, and feeding the soil with manure or fertilizer so every single plant grows to its full potential.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa nibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Kɛjɛ he ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ adumɔ Ni akɛ ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tso fɛɛ tso adara kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better to buy certified seeds from agro-dealers or just plant seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ loo madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to resist common diseases and produce higher yields, whereas seeds saved from previous harvests lose strength over time and often give smaller yields.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli, ni amɛfɔɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food plants need to grow green and strong, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
