ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia otso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or pest damage, causing the plant to shed flowers to save its remaining strength.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite Ha tso lɛ agbee shi koni ekɛbu ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when weeds are growing close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo beni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; they steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops, causing your crops to starve and stay small.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, leading to lower yields.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Wait until the rain has soaked deep into the ground at least two or three times so the soil holds enough moisture to help seeds sprout without drying out.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Will adding extra fertilizer make my crops grow twice as big and fast?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni mikɛfataa he lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya fe tsutsu lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: No, giving plants too much fertilizer can burn their roots and damage the soil; crops only need the right amount applied at the correct stage of growth.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛfite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe miihia pɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun, so plantains grow fast with large leaves to provide natural shade umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aha kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: How does planting cowpea or groundnuts together with my maize help my soil?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpea and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting like natural fertilizer that helps the neighboring maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need plantain trees planted right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwu yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and shade-moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing on the main trunk of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, steal food, water, and energy from the main trunk. Removing them ensures the tree directs all its energy into growing healthy flowers and large cocoa pods.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Tso lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the ears are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmã tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that have the special ability to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps your maize grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava stay green and alive even during long dry spells when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ po mli lɛ?

english: Cassava has very deep roots that reach far down for underground water, and it can shed some of its leaves to conserve moisture until the rains return.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa ni baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni obaanyɛ okɛ baai lɛ ekomɛi ashwie shi koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, protecting them from rot and diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite kɛ helai srɔtoi.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small sucker shoots grow around one main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ tso titri kome he lɛ?

english: If too many suckers grow at once, they fight each other for water and nutrients, resulting in thin plants and small bunches. Keeping only one main plant and one or two strong followers gives you larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida shikome lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni kui feɔ kui bibii. Kɛ́ otsa tso titri kome pɛ kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔi ni he wa kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha oná jwɛi wulu.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during peak heat can help flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eha hulutsoo be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper or tomato on the exact same spot of ground every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop family in the same place every year allows specific soil pests and diseases to build up in that spot, while draining the soil of the specific nutrients those crops need most.
ga: Tsei aweku kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai komɛi abua amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa nakai tsei lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my crop yields so much smaller at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. When weeds grow close to your crops, they steal the vital food your plants need to grow large fruits, seeds, or roots.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe Ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ aduawai wuji, dumɔwui, loo shishifãi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help your plants regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli, ni ehi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant groundnuts in the same field with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a plant family that captures nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer for your corn, making the soil richer without buying expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Covering the ground with dry materials—a practice called mulching—traps moisture in the soil so it doesn't dry out quickly in the hot sun. It also suppresses weeds and keeps the soil cool for crop roots.
ga: Nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛha tsei shishifãi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and dry up at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ shãa ni egbiɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants get sunburned very easily when exposed to direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava planted nearby to act as living umbrellas and protect them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hulu shãa amɛ oya waa kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni amɛbu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does it really make a difference if I don't put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ebaaha srɔtofeemɔ aba diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mikɛ tsei kakadaji efɔɔɔ shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking your yam vines keeps the leaves exposed to sunlight so the plant can produce more food. Without stakes, leaves rot on the ground and sunlight is blocked, resulting in much smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ jeɔ hulu la mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hulu la lɛ baatsi enaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest if I can't see them underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? Kɛji onyɛɛɛ ona lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will notice the lower leaves starting to turn yellow and fall off, or you can carefully clear small soil around one plant to check the thickness of the root.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ Obaayɔse akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Aloo obaanyɛ ojie shikpɔŋ bibioo ko. tsɔ tso kome he jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ha

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade trees nearby can reduce heat and help flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa latsaa lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ chili ŋmeii.

english: What are these small green caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji nɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a common crop pest in Ghana. They chew through young leaves and can destroy the plant if left untreated; spraying them early with organic neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides can save your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite tsei kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni akɛ organic neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Aloo, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ehere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why are my green tomatoes rotting and turning black at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miifite ni eyɛ ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often due to irregular watering during dry spells. Keeping the water supply steady and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps prevent bottom rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu jɛɛhe ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ tso sũ loo lime ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishigbɛ sũ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with strong root systems that absorb water instantly, whereas farmed crop seeds need time and special care to establish roots. Clearing weeds while they are small prevents them from stealing water and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ni wa, koo mli ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ agbala nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui biɔ be kɛ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ dani amɛfee shishifãi. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: What can I do to keep my crops alive when the rainy season comes late?
ga: Mɛni obaanyɛ ofee koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bashɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dried grass or plant leaves (called mulching). This acts like a blanket that shades the soil, trapping moisture in the ground for longer so your plants don't dry out quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai akpɛ onibii lɛ. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ gĩii oya.

english: Why do my seeds die in the soil if it rains only once and then stops for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ shikome pɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ ekpa otsii enyɔ lɛ?

english: The first rain tricks the seed into opening and starting to grow, but young sprouts have tiny, shallow roots. If the top soil dries out before the next rain, the delicate new sprout quickly loses water and dies.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ atse ni amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Shi tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ bibii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli egbi dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɛ Dumɔwui heei lɛ nu fiteɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Which crops are best to plant if I am worried there will not be enough rain this season?
ga: Mɛni ji tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kɛji mihao akɛ nugbɔ enɛŋ bɔ ni sa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Crops like sorghum, millet, and cassava naturally require less water than maize. There are also early-maturing seed varieties of cowpeas and maize that grow quickly and finish producing before the water runs out.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa Ekɛ adebɔɔ su biɔ nu fioo fe ŋmãa. Ayɛ tsina kɛ ŋmãa srɔtoi hu ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛgbeɔ nitsumɔ naa dani nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and wilted during the afternoon, but stand up straight again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ.

english: In the hot sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Wilting is the plant's way of reducing leaf size to save water; once the sun goes down and temperatures cool, the plant refills with water.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Withering ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baayi kɛ nu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants before growing into full peppers when it is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ pepper ni eda jogbaŋŋ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or water is scarce, the plant gets stressed and naturally drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive instead of spending energy on growing fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛjieɔ fɔfɔii kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ kɛdu aduawai

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and dry up from the bottom moving upwards during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water is short, the plant prioritizes saving its new top leaves. It moves the remaining water and plant nutrients from its older, bottom leaves up to the top, causing the lower leaves to dry up and die first.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ baama eŋwɛi baai heei lɛ ni eeehi shi lɛ nɔ. Ejieɔ nu kɛ tso mli niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ ashishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why did my cassava produce big leaves above the ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Cassava needs steady soil moisture when it starts forming tubers underground. If the plant gets stressed by dry weather during that critical tuber-forming stage, it spends all its energy surviving on top rather than expanding its roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia Cassava be fɛɛ be kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ. Kɛji akɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ be mli ni he hiaa waa lɛ, Tso lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛhi shi yɛ ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa.

english: Why does rain water make my crops grow much better than when I water them manually with a bucket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ mi nine baawo amɛ nu kɛtsɔ baagi nɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater contains small amounts of nitrogen absorbed from the air, which acts like a mild natural fertilizer. It also soaks the whole field evenly, allowing root networks to expand better than localized bucket watering.
ga: Nitrogen fioo ko yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo Ekɛ he fɛɛ he hu shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ mli lɛɛɔ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ baagi mli lɛ woɔ mɔ he lɛ.

english: Why does hard, sun-baked soil make my crops perform poorly even after the rain starts falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni hulu lɛ etswa lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ po lɛ?

english: When dry soil bakes under the sun, it forms a hard crust. Heavy rain often runs off the surface of hard ground instead of soaking in, making it difficult for plant roots to breath and drink.
ga: Kɛ́ sũ lɛ gbi lɛ, ashãa yɛ hulu shishi. Kpoji ni wa baafee. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ foi kɛjɛɔ hei ni wa lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeeŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛnu nu.

english: How does trees standing in my farm help my crops survive hot dry days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Scattered farm trees act as windbreaks and provide partial shade, which keeps the surrounding air cooler and reduces the amount of water your crops lose through their leaves on hot days.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsii ni amɛhaa hulutsoo fioo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ni ehaa nu ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do wild animals come to eat my cocoa pods mostly early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli kooloi yeɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ leebi bei babaoo lɛ?

english: Wild animals like squirrels, monkeys, and rodents are active at dawn because the air is cool and human activity in the fields is low, making it a safe time for them to feed.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Je kpo kɛyatao niyenii leebi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni adesai anifeemɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Ha be nɛɛ afee be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyeli.

english: What simple methods can I use to stop bush animals from destroying my cocoa pods?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni mafee koni kooloi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ akafite mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: You can clear the overgrown weed borders around your farm to remove animal hiding spots, place physical noise-makers or scarecrows, and harvest ripe pods immediately so animals are not attracted to them.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie jwɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ koni ojie hei ni kooloi kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Okɛ tsɔne ko ni haa gbee loo gbeyeishemɔ ko awo mli. Ni kpamɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ oya koni kooloi akagbala amɛ.

english: How do I know if damage on my cocoa pods is caused by insects or larger animals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi wuji ji mɛi ni kɛ nɔ ni efite yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ ba?

english: Larger animals leave clean bite marks, chewed pod husks, or half-eaten pods on the ground, while insects leave tiny hole punctures, sticky residues, or discolored spots on the skin.
ga: Koolooi wuji shiɔ ŋmɔlɔ he okadii ni he tse. chewed pod shell loo pod ni aye fã yɛ shikpɔŋ Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii shĩɔ ŋmeii bibii, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi loo ŋmeii ni etsake amɛhe yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to inspect my cocoa farm for pests?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana kɛji ŋmeii yɔɔ mli?

english: Early morning around 6:00 AM is the best time to inspect your farm because pests and animals are actively feeding then, making them easier to catch in action.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa aaafee ŋmɛji 6:00 ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ nii waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaamɔ amɛ.

english: How often should I walk through my cocoa farm to check for crop health?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ kookoo ŋmɔ mli koni makwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha?

english: Walking through your farm two to three times a week allows you to spot animal attacks or early signs of disease early enough to act before severe damage occurs.
ga: Kɛ́ otsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ehaa onaa kooloi ni tutua bo loo hela he okadii ni tsɔɔ mra bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ ofee nɔ ko dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ baafite.

english: Why is it important to weed the borders of my cocoa farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Weeding farm boundaries removes the shelter and breeding grounds for rodents and wild animals, making them reluctant to cross open ground to attack your cocoa trees.
ga: Jwɛi ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ jieɔ wɔɔhe kɛ he ni ŋmeii kɛ koo mli kooloi fɔɔ yɛ lɛ kɛyaa. Ha amɛkafee mɛi ni sumɔɔɔ ni amɛfoɔ hei ni agbele naa koni amɛyatutua o-cacao tsei lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting sick with a fungal disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ emɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe?

english: Fungal diseases like Black Pod show up as small brown or black spots on the pod that grow quickly, turning the whole pod dark and powdery if not treated.
ga: Fungal helai, tamɔ black pods lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmeii bibii. Pods ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ ni daa oya ni ehaa pod muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ powder kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: What should I do with cocoa pods on my farm that have already become diseased?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni hela emɔ amɛ momo lɛ?

english: Pluck off all diseased pods immediately and remove them completely from the farm or bury them, so wind and rain do not spread the disease spores to healthy trees.
ga: Gbalamɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ojie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ofu amɛ. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ akagbɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning yellow and shriveling before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' which happens when the tree naturally drops extra pods it cannot nourish, or when the tree is under stress from drought, pests, or poor soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ okadi nɛɛ baa akɛ ‘wilt hela’ ni baa kɛji tso ko da yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmeii amli kɛyashɛ he ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ hɔmɔ, kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ.

english: What immediate action should I take if animals start eating my ripe cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji kooloi bɔi mi-kokoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yeli?

english: Harvest all mature and nearly-ripe pods right away to save your yield, and then set up farm perimeter traps or clearing routine to protect the remaining un-ripe pods.
ga: Kpãa ŋmeii ni edara kɛ nɔ ni eshwɛ fioo ni ebaakwɛ lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni okɛbu onibii lɛ ahe. No sɛɛ lɛ, atoɔ tsɔnei ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he loo ajieɔ nibii ni afeɔ daa lɛ ahe koni akɛbu ŋmeii ni eshwɛ ni ekwɛko lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off whenever heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: When heavy rains submerge the farm, excess water suffocates the roots by removing air from the soil. Unable to breathe or take up nutrients, the cassava plant drops its leaves to survive.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Cassava nyɛɛɛ amu loo eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: If my vegetable farm gets flooded, why do the roots of my pepper plants start to rot so quickly?
ga: Kɛji nu eyi mi-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air pockets in the soil to stay healthy. Standing floodwater fills these air pockets, creating stagnant conditions where root-rot fungus spreads rapidly.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu afua mli nu eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui nɛɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during storms when the ground is very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems. When heavy rains soak and soften the soil, the wet earth loses its grip on the roots, making top-heavy trees easily fall over in strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛtɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and pale even after I put fertilizer during heavy rain periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe tseee yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛmli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash fertilizer away before the crop absorbs it. Additionally, soggy soil stops maize roots from taking in nitrogen, leaving the plants short and pale.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná nitrogen. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ yɛ kukuji ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and damages the pollen inside the flowers. When pollination fails, the plant naturally drops the flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my garden eggs split open on the plant when a big rain comes after a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fãa yɛ tsei anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: After a dry period, a sudden soak of water makes the inside of the fruit absorb fluid and expand faster than the dry outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst open.
ga: Yɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli trukaa lɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli nu shwieɔ nu mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do crop roots grow deeper into the soil during dry weather than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: When the surface soil dries out, plants naturally push their roots deeper underground searching for hidden water, whereas abundant topsoil moisture keeps roots growing near the surface.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛtsiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do black spots spread so fast on my cocoa pods during continuous rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high moisture and humidity, which allows the fungus responsible for Black Pod disease to reproduce quickly and spread easily across trees.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baa. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ fɔɔ oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil before sprouting if rain falls heavily right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly planted seed yams need dry, warm soil to break dormancy. Excess rainwater trapped in the mound causes the dormant tuber to decay before it can sprout new shoots.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni adu ehee lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi koni ekɛfo wɔɔhe lɛ mli. Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni emɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ. Egboɔ dani ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy so fast when stored during wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High moisture in the humid air stops harvested maize from drying completely, creating an ideal damp environment for mold and fungi to grow on stored grains.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ haaa ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi kwraa. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to use dirty or salty water to irrigate my vegetables?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji loo nu ni mli edɔ baawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Dirty or salty water carries hidden impurities and excess minerals that can burn crop roots, stop plants from taking in nutrients, and stunt their overall growth.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji loo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yɛ muji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ minerals ni fa fe nine ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ fɛɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my crops look weak even though I water them every day with river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ faa nu shwieɔ amɛnɔ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: River water often contains tiny dissolved salts or chemicals that block root pores, making it difficult for the crop to drink water and absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni mli ewo muji loo tsofai ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ anaa yɛ faa mli nu mli. Enɛ haa ewaa aha tsei akɛ amɛaanu nu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Will using clean, filtered water help my crop seedlings survive better?
ga: Ani nu ni mli tse ni atsɔ mli lɛ ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Young seedlings have very tender roots that burn easily. Clean water free of harsh dirt and chemicals gives them a safe environment to establish strong, deep roots.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ waa ni shãa oya. Nu ni mli tse, ni muji ni mli wa kɛ tsofai bɛ mli lɛ haa amɛnáa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ.

english: How does muddy pond water affect the soil around my crops?
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ muji bu lɛ mli lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he. Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Muddy water leaves a layer of thick silt on top of the soil that dries into a hard crust, preventing air and fresh water from reaching your crop's roots.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ shĩɔ sũ ni mli edɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbiɔ ni etsɔɔ sũ ni mli wa. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu kpakpa naa koni ekashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashishifãi ahe.

english: Can I use machines similar to the ones for sachet pure water to clean water for my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne ko ni tamɔ nu krɔŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ paketi mli lɛ atsu nii kɛtsumɔ nu kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, water purification machines like reverse osmosis filters can extract dirt, heavy minerals, and bad chemicals from raw water, making it safe and clean for crop irrigation.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nu he nii tamɔ reverse osmosis filta. Ebaanyɛ ejie muji, shika tsuru ni tsii kɛ tsofai gbohii kɛjɛ nu ni mli edɔ mli. Ehaa efeɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehe tseɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ.

english: What actually happens to water when it goes through a filtering machine before reaching my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa nu lɛ nɔ kɛ́ etsɔ filta mli dani eshɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The filtering machine acts like a very fine sieve that traps tiny invisible salts and harmful particles, leaving clear, purified water that is easily absorbed by plant roots.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu mli ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mɔɔ ŋmei bibii. nibii ni anaaa kɛ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Nu ni mli tse ni mli tse pɛ eshwɛ ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ oya.

english: Is clear water always better for crop yield than cloudy water from a pit?
ga: Ani nu ni mli tse lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai be fɛɛ be fe nu ni mli ewo atatu ni jɛɔ nu bu mli lɛ?

english: Clear, treated water is generally better because it does not clog irrigation pipes or deposit harmful substances into the soil that can damage your crops over time.
ga: Nu ni mli tse ni asaa he lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ etsĩii nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ paipii lɛ anaa loo ebuaaa nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I safely reuse wastewater from my house or processing site on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ nu fɔŋ ni jɛɔ mishia loo ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ shweshweeshwe?

english: You should only reuse wastewater if it has been filtered or treated first, as untreated wastewater can contain soap, oil, or pollutants that kill beneficial soil microbes and harm crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ kɛji akɛ ajie mli loo atsu he nii klɛŋklɛŋ pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni mli ewo muji ni asaaa lɛ baanyɛ ahi samla, fɔ, loo nibii ni gbeɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui.

english: How can I tell if the water source on my farm has bad things in it that are hurting my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nibii gbohii ni miiye mitsei lɛ awui yɛ nu jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: If your crop leaves turn yellow at the tips, dry up unexpectedly, or show white crusty patches on the soil after watering, the water likely contains high levels of harmful salts or impurities.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eshishigbɛ ni egbi trukaa Aloo ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nu ni awo lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ ŋmeii loo muji ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo yɛ nu lɛ mli.

english: Does removing salt and dirt from irrigation water increase the quality of my harvested produce?
ga: Ani ŋoo kɛ muji ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, crops watered with purified water grow without stress, leading to healthier foliage, bigger fruits, and better overall yield at harvest time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akɛ nu krɔŋŋ fɔɔ nɔ lɛ daa ni haomɔ ko bɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ. Yibii lɛ feɔ agbo. ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ tee hiɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why are my mango trees struggling to grow in the hard soil on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mango roots need deep, soft soil to grow downwards easily. When the soil is hard and compact, the roots cannot penetrate deep into the ground to find water and nutrients, which stops the tree from growing well.
ga: Mango shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛya shi mlɛo. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi nyɛŋ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ tso ɔ nyɛ we nɛ waa wa saminya.

english: Can I plant mangoes on any piece of land I own in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mango yɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ? Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maná nɔ ko yɛ Ghana?

english: No, mangoes cannot thrive on just any land. They need deep, loose, well-drained soil, so if your land has very hard clay or rocks near the surface, you will need to search for a better location before planting.
ga: Dabi, mango nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo tɛi ni wa waa ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ebaabi ni otao he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ dani okɛdu.

english: Is heavy clay soil suitable for starting a mango farm?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii lɛ sa kɛha mango tso yibii abɔɔi?

english: Heavy clay soil is tough and turns hard when dry, making it difficult for mango roots to spread. It also traps too much water when it rains, which can suffocate and rot the root system.
ga: Shikpɔji ni akɛ shikpɔŋ sũ fee ni tsii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛgbi. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaagbɛ mango shishifãi lɛ ashwã. Ehiɛɔ nu babaoo hu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifã lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha egbo.

english: How can I tell if my soil is too tough for mango trees before I buy seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ kɛha mi mango tso lɛ dani mahe dumɔwui?

english: You can test your land by digging a hole about one meter deep. If you hit hard, impenetrable rock or extremely tough clay near the top, the land is not ideal for mangoes.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ bu ni mli kwɔ aaafee mita kome ni oootsu lɛ nɔ. Kɛji otswa tɛ ko ni wa ni anyɛɛɛ abote mli Loo shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ esaaa kɛha mango.

english: How do mango roots behave when they hit hard rock underground?
ga: Te mango shishifãi lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ amɛtswa tɛ ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When a mango taproot hits hard rock underground, it cannot grow downwards anymore and is forced to spread sideways near the surface. This makes the tree weak, vulnerable to strong winds, and easily dried out during dry seasons.
ga: Beni mango shishifã lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ shishi tɛi ni wa lɛ Enyɛŋ eda kɛya shi dɔŋŋ. ni anyɛɔ enɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa he kroko ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa lɛ oya ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my mango trees look healthy during rains but dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mangoi feɔ fɛo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? Shi egbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli?

english: If the soil composition is hard and shallow, the tree roots cannot grow deep enough to reach deep groundwater. As soon as the surface water dries up during the dry season, the tree suffers from water stress.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli wa ni ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he. Kɛji nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gĩ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli pɛ kɛkɛ ni nu he haomɔ baaná tsei anɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some mango trees take many years to produce fruit while others grow fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei komɛi yeɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni ekomɛi hu waa mra lɛ?

english: Soil condition plays a big role in growth speed. Trees planted in soft, fertile soil develop strong root systems quickly and bear fruit early, while trees in tough, hard soil waste energy trying to push roots through the earth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ tsuɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ ko ni he hiaa he nii yɛ shweremɔ oya mli. Tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa baa oya, ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni wa nɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What should I look for when searching for good farmland for mangoes?
ga: Kɛ́ ootao he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni abaadu mango yɛ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni esa akɛ osusu he?

english: Look for land with deep, loose, sandy-loam soil that allows water to drain easily. Avoid swampy valleys or stony ground where the soil layer is thin and hard.
ga: Taomɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋã yɔɔ mli ni nu hoɔ oya. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ jɔɔi ni mli ewo muji loo hei ni tɛi yɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseee ni wa lɛ he.

english: Is it worth finding a new plot of land if my current farm soil is too hard for mangoes?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ aaana shikpɔŋ hee kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ mli wa tsɔ kɛha mango?

english: Yes, it is much better to search for suitable land elsewhere than to waste time and money planting mangoes on hard soil where they will struggle and fail to produce good yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaana shikpɔŋ ni sa yɛ he kroko fe ni ooofite be kɛ shika kɛdu mango yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ he ni amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ waa shi amɛwooo yibii kpakpai yɛ lɛ.

english: If my soil is hard, can I make the planting holes bigger to help my young mango trees?
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa lɛ, ani manyɛ mafo bu ni da fe nakai koni maye mabua mango tso lɛ?

english: Yes, digging large, deep planting holes (about 1 meter wide and deep) and refilling them with soft topsoil mixed with organic manure gives young roots a soft space to establish before reaching the harder surrounding soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ bu agbo ni mli kwɔ ni aaafo. (aaafee mita 1 lɛɛmɔ kɛ emlibotemɔ) ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli efutu mli lɛ fata he lɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛma dani amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my freshly harvested crop is dry enough for safe storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa ehee lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: You can check the moisture content using a testing machine or meter. High moisture means the crop needs a few more hours of drying, while a low, stable reading shows it is ready and safe from rot.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tester loo mita akwɛ bɔ ni nu lɛ yɔɔ ha. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia ŋmɛlɛtswai 2-3 krokomɛi koni amɛgbi, yɛ be mli ni nikanemɔ ni baa shi ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efee klalo ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Why is it important to dry my grains immediately after harvesting them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ miŋmaa lɛ agbi kɛji mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain a lot of natural moisture. Drying removes excess water so mold and pests cannot grow and spoil your hard work.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ edaaa ni amɛfiteee onitsumɔ ni wa lɛ.

english: What happens to my produce if I store it while it is still warm and wet?
ga: Mɛni baaba minibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛto be mli ni edɔ ni edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Trapped moisture causes produce to heat up, rot, and grow mold quickly, which damages the quality and makes it unfit for sale or consumption.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni atsĩ naa lɛ haa nibii ni adu lɛ mli dɔɔ, egboɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ daa oya. Enɛ fiteɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ni ehaa esaaa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ loo ayeɔ.

english: How often should I check on my crops while they are drying in the sun?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: It is best to monitor your crops every couple of hours because strong sun can dry them quickly, and regular checks prevent over-drying or under-drying.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ onibii amli daa ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo. Enɛ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei agbi oya. Ni kɛ́ akwɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi fe nine loo nɔ ni egbi fioo lɛ naa.

english: What does a high moisture reading on my harvest actually mean?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo ni akaneɔ yɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: A high reading means there is still too much water inside your crops, showing that they need more time drying before they can be safely bagged.
ga: Kanemɔ ni nɔ kwɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo yɛ onibii amli lolo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia be babaoo ni ekɛgbi dani abaanyɛ awo kotoku mli shweshweeshwe.

english: How can a moisture checking machine help me get a better harvest?
ga: Te tsɔne ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpa nii jogbaŋŋ ahaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A moisture meter gives you an accurate measurement of water levels in your crop, taking away the guesswork so you know the exact time your produce is ready.
ga: Moisture meter haa onyɛɔ osusuɔ nu ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. without guessing No hewɔ lɛ ole be pɔtɛɛ ni onibii lɛ baafee klalo.

english: Why do my crops seem to dry faster on some days compared to others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii komɛi anɔ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Crops release moisture faster when the air is hot, dry, and windy, whereas humid or cloudy days slow down the natural evaporation process.
ga: Tsei jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ, edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa, yɛ be mli ni gbii ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli loo atatu yɔɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I tell if my drying crops are releasing water properly without damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi tsei ni egbi lɛ miijie nu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee nɔ ko?

english: By testing sample grains across different hours of the day, a steady drop in moisture without cracking shows your crops are drying at a healthy rate.
ga: Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ akaa yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi be fɛɛ be ni etseee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ miigbi yɛ gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: Is it better to dry my crops alone or work at a central processing area with other farmers?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikome too magbi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo mikɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi baatsu nii yɛ he ko ni atsuɔ nii yɛ mli?

english: Working with other farmers at a shared location allows you to pool labor and share equipment like moisture meters, making harvesting and drying faster and more reliable.
ga: Nitsumɔ kɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi Hei ni ajaa lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nitsumɔ feɔ ekome ni okɛ nibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ mitai lɛ jaa. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ kɛ egbimɔ yaa oya ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I keep testing my produce right up until the final hour of drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya nɔ maka minibii lɛ makwɛ kɛyashi naagbee ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni mikɛbaagbi lɛ?

english: Testing right up to the end ensures your entire batch has reached the safe moisture level before you finish, preventing hidden damp spots from ruining stored bags.
ga: Naagbee-kɛ-naagbee kaa lɛ haa o-batch muu lɛ fɛɛ shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe he dani agbeɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ akafite kotokui ni akɛto lɛ.

english: Why do my carrots grow small and crooked instead of long and straight like the ones in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi karɔt lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja tamɔ jarayeli karɔt lɛ?

english: Carrots need soft, loose, sandy soil that is free of stones and hard clay blocks. If the root hits hard soil or rocks while growing downward, it bends, splits, or stops growing deep.
ga: Karɔt he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ŋã yɔɔ mli. Eye ehe kɛjɛ tɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa he. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi kpe beni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ, amɛbaakumɔ, amɛbaakumɔ, loo amɛbaakpa shweremɔ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant carrots on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ karɔt yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting carrots on the same soil repeatedly allows soil pests like nematodes and root diseases to build up, while constantly draining the specific nutrients carrots need to grow big.
ga: Karɔt ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes kɛ shishifãi ahe helai abua amɛhe naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ mli be fɛɛ be koni eha karɔt lɛ adara.

english: Why do my carrot plants have huge green leaves on top, but the carrots under the soil stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi karɔt tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi karɔt lɛ ji bibioo kwraa?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: What happens to my carrot crops if I do not water them regularly during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi karɔt tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu haaa amɛ daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Irregular watering makes carrot roots crack open or become hard and woody, which spoils their appearance and reduces their selling value.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha karɔt shishifãi lɛ amli agbala loo amɛfee nɔ ni wa ni amɛfee tamɔ tso. Enɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ, ni ehaa jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it important to pull out excess young carrot plants after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie karɔt tsei bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ mli beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When carrot plants grow too close together, they fight for soil nutrients and sunlight, resulting in thin, tiny roots. Thinning them gives each carrot room to swell into a full-sized root.
ga: Kɛji karɔt tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee. Nibii ni afee lɛ mlɛo lɛ haa karɔt tsu lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli lɛɛɔ kɛfeɔ shishifãi ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu.

english: Can I grow carrots in Ghana throughout the whole year or only in the rainy season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu karɔt yɛ Ghana afi muu lɛ fɛɛ loo yɛ nugbɔ be mli pɛ?

english: Carrots can be grown all year if you have reliable irrigation water, but heavy rainy seasons can flood the roots and cause them to rot in wet soil.
ga: Abaanyɛ adu karɔt afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji oyɛ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye shishifãi lɛ anɔ kunim ni eha amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Vegetables lose water rapidly once picked. Harvesting in the cool early morning and keeping the crops in the shade slows down moisture loss and prevents rot.
ga: Nu lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto aduawai amli. Kɛ́ akpa tsei yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ aba shi, ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Is it good to wash my harvested carrots with water before tying them into bundles for sale?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ nu baafɔ karɔt ni akpa lɛ he dani akɛfi amɛ ni akɛfee ŋmeii ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ?

english: Washing makes carrots clean for buyers, but if you bundle and pack them while they are still wet, moisture gets trapped inside the bundle and accelerates fungal decay.
ga: Karɔt ni afɔɔ he lɛ haa mɔ ni heɔ lɛ he tseɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ ofi ni okɛwo tsɔne mli be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ, Moisture baatsi tsɔne lɛ mli ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afite oya.

english: Why do buyers offer very low prices for my crops during the main harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi nɛkɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When many farmers harvest the same crop at the exact same time, supply becomes higher than demand, causing market prices to fall drastically.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ baafee babaoo fe nɔ ni ataoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, jara lɛ ba shi waa.

english: How can I produce carrots that buyers are willing to pay higher prices for?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee karɔt ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo jara ni nɔ kwɔ?

english: Buyers pay more for clean, sweet, firm carrots that are uniform in size. Sorting your harvest by size and keeping them fresh attracts premium prices.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ karɔt ni he tse, ni ŋɔɔ, ni wa ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ he nyɔmɔ babaoo. Nibii ni adu lɛ mligbalamɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ naa ni akɛtoɔ ehee lɛ gbalaa jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant the maize seeds from my last harvest instead of buying new ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ moŋ fe ni mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: Improved or high-yielding seeds lose their vigor and disease resistance when replanted season after season. Buying certified seeds ensures you get strong plants, uniform growth, and maximum yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni etee hiɛ loo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ haa ona tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. dalɛ ni tamɔ ekome kɛ nibii ni anáa babaoo

english: How do new improved seed varieties protect themselves against local crop diseases better than my traditional seeds?
ga: Te dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ baanyɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe helai ahe jogbaŋŋ fe mishishijee dumɔwui lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Scientists breed improved seeds specifically to develop natural resistance to common diseases in Ghana, such as maize streak virus. This means the plant can fight off infections easily without dying or losing yield.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi fɔɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛná helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana, tamɔ corn striped virus lɛ ahewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei baanyɛ awuu ashi helai oya ni amɛgbooo loo amɛbaafee nɔ ko ni baa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying the right fertilizer at the correct time gives the plant the nitrogen it needs to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tsei lɛ amli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa nitrogen ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: How does fertilizer actually help my crops produce bigger grains and tubers?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo dumɔwui wuji kɛ bulbs lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer works like food for crops by giving the soil vital nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. These nutrients give the plant the energy to expand its root system, grow tall, and produce large, heavy fruits or grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei aniyenii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium. Niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ haa tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛ shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ, amɛ kwɔlɛ aya hiɛ, ni amɛ wo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak crops that produce small yields.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Why are weeds able to choke my crops even after I have already applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi baanyɛ agbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will eat up the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. You must clear the weeds early so your crops get all the nutrients from the fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛbaaye ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to plant right at the start of the rainy season in my region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting early with the first steady rains allows seeds to soak up enough water to germinate quickly and establish deep roots before any temporary mid-season dry spells occur.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. ni amɛto shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ama shi dani hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli lɛ aba yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves when there is a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick cassava uses to save water during dry periods. The plant goes quiet to protect its underground tuber until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni ŋmei kɛtsuɔ nii koni eye ebua ni abu nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Tsei lɛ baafee dioo koni amɛbu ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When you plant other crops like maize after them, the soil is already enriched with natural nitrogen.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why do insect pests seem to attack my crops more heavily during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: During dry spells, crops get thirsty and stressed, making their natural defenses weak. Insects travel to these green crops looking for moisture and food, causing heavy damage.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaye kumai ni amɛhao. egbɔjɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hebuu Kplukai fãa gbɛ kɛyaa tsei eŋɔli nɛɛ amli koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. ni kɛ fitemɔ ni mli wa baa

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight; their leaves burn and they lose water quickly. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain protects young cocoa from heat stress and keeps soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shãa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow while the plant is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves near the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food corn needs to grow green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain sits in the soil without draining away, the roots suffocate and soil bacteria cause them to decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ mli Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds after the first rains of the season start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until two or three heavy rains have deeply soaked the soil. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba.

english: Why do caterpillars keep hiding inside the center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm hide inside the central funnel of corn plants because it provides shade from the hot sun and protection from birds, while allowing them to eat the softest new leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni amɛbuɔ okpoi ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: If I plant my crops closer together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my plot of land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani mana yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin plants with small yields. Giving plants proper space allows each one to grow full, healthy produce.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Kɛ́ oha otsei lɛ he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted to survive easily, so they steal water, light, and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops the head start they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe oya koni amɛhi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, kane, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ feɔ klalo koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of tiny holes and dust when I store it in bags at home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ ni mikɛwoɔ kotoku mli yɛ shia lɛ?

english: Weevils lay eggs in grain that has not been dried properly or stored in airtight containers. Drying maize thoroughly in the sun and keeping it in sealed hermetic bags starves insects of oxygen and preserves the grain.
ga: Weevils woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui ni agbiko amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo akɛtooo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ náaa lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra side shoots growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing small side branches forces the plant to direct its energy into developing bigger, healthier fruit rather than spending energy growing extra leaves and stems.
ga: division of small branches Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ehe baahia ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo atsu nii ni ekɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe bɔ ni ebaafite yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my farmland yield less harvest every year even though I plant the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and builds up soil diseases. Rotating different crops, like legumes and corn, gives the soil time to rebuild its nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ helai baa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ lɛ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or the right nitrogen fertilizer will replenish the soil and turn the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmeii ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores your field's fertility for the next season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔji lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why is spreading dry grass and leaves over my crop beds helpful for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ baai ni mikɛshwãa miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, stops weeds from taking over, keeps the soil moist under the hot sun, and slowly turns into rich compost that feeds your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi akaye nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni fiofio lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni okɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the large trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Be ni majie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like young babies and burn easily under full sun. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or forest trees to keep them cool and moist until they are mature enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei amli. Ha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground toward the sun. Staking keeps the leaves clean, exposes them to sunlight so the tubers grow large, and prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking damp leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso ko ni esa akɛ ewó ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Staking baaha baai lɛ ahe atse. Hulu la ni akɛwoɔ mli koni eha bulb lɛ adara. ni atsĩ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua baai ni mli efɔ lɛ

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the very centers of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the fresh inner leaves of corn. Catching them early and spraying recommended neem extract or suitable pest controls will destroy them before they ruin your entire harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa baai heei amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ baakpata amɛhiɛ dani amɛbaafite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap out of the young leaves. Spraying your pepper plants with mild soapy water or neem oil kills these tiny bugs and stops the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem fɔ shwie pepper tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii. Enɛɛmɛi kɛ baanyɛ akpa nɔ ni efite lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked, waterlogged soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: The first rain often tricks farmers, but the ground underneath remains hot and dry, and it may not rain again for weeks. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures your seeds have enough continuous moisture to sprout and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ lakaa okwaafoi. Shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lolo. Ni ekolɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ otsii komɛi. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently damp with regular watering and soil cover will help the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛma shi akɛ tomatoi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is even mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying the right fertilizer, such as NPK or urea at the recommended stages, ensures the plant stays green and develops heavy, full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo urea atsu nii yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni atsɔɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná ŋmei ni tsii kwraa.

english: My cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but why are the tubers underneath so small when I harvest?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus energy on foliage growth instead of root growth. Using fertilizers rich in potassium helps the plant direct its strength into producing large, bulky tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni tsii.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dense shade. Pruning extra branches to let in sunlight, clearing weeds, and removing infected pods helps prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo, hɔɔŋ ni mli ewo muji mli kɛbaa. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu lɛ aba mli babaoo, koni ajie jwɛi lɛ, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when tomato plants experience heat stress, erratic watering, or a lack of phosphorus. Keeping the moisture in the soil consistent and using phosphorus-rich fertilizer helps the flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji tomato tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo fɔsfɔs ni faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap and transmitting viruses. Controlling these pests early with appropriate sprays protects the leaves so the plant can feed its growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Emuɔ mliki ni ekɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ haa Eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ aha eyibii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: If I plant my seeds much closer together, won't I get a larger harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo babaoo nɔ kɛjɛŋ miŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: Planting too closely forces crop plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and smaller yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and nutrition to grow to its full potential.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds each season instead of planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase yɛ be fɛɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from modern hybrid crops lose their vigor and disease resistance in the next generation, leading to smaller yields. Fresh certified seeds guarantee high germination rates, uniform plant growth, and better resistance to common diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo. Dumɔwui heei ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. tsei lɛ adalɛ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant tomatoes on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pest and disease populations to multiply in the soil. Rotating crops like tomatoes with legumes or maize breaks pest cycles and restores soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ayi fa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ, tamɔ tomato ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ewo mli. Efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start sprouting and softening soon after I harvest and store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa ni mikɛto lɛ?

english: Yam tubers sprout when exposed to heat, high humidity, and direct sunlight, as these conditions signal to the tuber that it is time to grow again. Storing tubers in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated yam barn off the ground extends their shelf life.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ amɛ wo dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i babaoo, kɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shihilɛi nɛɛ haa yitso lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ eda ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ to sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?
